Though it succombs into some of the pitfalls of the nickel-and-dime transactions of "free-to-play," WARFRAME is undoubtedly the absolute paragon of "free" games. With just enough plot to make missions feel important while maintaining the feeling of being a powerful hero of a bygone age in an uncertain future and simultaneously maintaining the fun of a well-done co-op game, solo campaign, and online multiplayer all in one. Warframe is a world I look forward to experiencing every time I log in, and the constant updates, rewards, and new and unique missions, characters, and activities endures Warframe will be a delightful pastime for years to come.

This game is literally farmville but its actually enjoyable and isn't like my mom's communist soviet copy. There isn't really a game, its all about grinding (repeatedly, mindlessly doing missions for the sake of an item you want to build) a resource or blueprint and then creating a weapon or warframe. If you enjoy afk farming as Master Yi in league of legends or mining clay in RuneScape then this is for you, but unlike RuneScape you'll be looking up the wiki every 3 seconds to check out what anything actually is since the game doesn't explain anything. Also the whole in game market is a scam, no items there are worth what they are, especially the weapons. Only the cosmetics and the Orokin Catalysts / Reactors are worth it and even then only at a sale. New players can be easily confused and build something completely useless (many weapons are downright worse than the starting equipment or just terrible at the time you get them) and you need to take your requests or questions to the correct channels or else you get muted without being told about these channels and how they work. Overall, great game held back by a really bad start. (like you're on cripple sticks or you're playing S.T.A.L.K.E.R. and wondering why the makarov does as much damage as your grandmother's blins). However, once you get a second or third frame and get to Jupiter the game takes a turn for the better.

ARK is a game which boasts a lot of things and for the most part, lives up to expectation. I've put almost 500 hours into this game and I've enjoyed some of what I've experience. But... there is a side to ark that out shines everything and that's its players.
Do not play this game if you expect to be able to play with players of your own region or balanced pvp. ARK touted a game where one would survive the wilds of the ark and build a base in which they could choose to fight with each other, having epic dino wars or pursuing the true meaning in it's history through the story. However, as it stands, it does not live up to that name.
Your server, should you be lucky enough to find more than one offical server in your region, will be either owned by a 'mega tribe', asian/russian or both. They have numbers, tens of members of members who can start up anywhere and do anything because they have unlimited time and resources. Even better, you won't be able to defend against them, because you'll either be sleeping, doxxed by IP or unable to hit them with their high ping.
WildCard is unwilling and unable to do anything, because there is nothing they can do but take down or wipe servers. New players will find that servers they can't start day one on are either completey owned and they're kicked or made subservent to the Mega Tribe or it will be completely unpopulated and lifeless.
One of the newest additions to the game is the 'Griffin', which has effectively made every land dino in the game utterly useless. New servers right now are a race to see who can get the most Griffins in the shortest time and raid the other base. There is simply no defence against griffins at this point, with over 20k boss like HP, the fastest speed in the game and a dive AoE which can be repeated even in the shortest of movements, no base defence can track them fast enough to stall them before they kill you and your dinos.
Where this game is headed, I have no idea, but it seems that ARK will meet its end in popularity before even the first year of release. I want to see a future where I can play ARK for what it should be, but until things are balanced, until WildCard steps up to the plate to provide for and maintain their game rather than stacking up more content, I know I won't be playing.

I've currently spent on this game 436h (according to steam record). Yet I enjoy ARK:SE, but still "Not recommended", because of Linux/Mac port. Everything below is about that version, and may not be applied to Windows (I don't have one to try it out).
Some major bugs wasn't fixed by the time of release. Most noticeable are opaque dirty-gray water surface (recent bug though) and blinding yellow bloom sometimes on land surfaces, and always in caves, which makes potentially rewarding cave explorations impossible. And also if you installed English version of ARK, you won't be able to see Unicode symbols in chat (as server owner I am forced to ALT+TAB to server logs when playing to see what's going on in chat).
Some issues affect dedicated servers. I've deployed one for myself, and not everything for me goes smoothly.
First is Procedurally Generated Maps. I was really hyped when it was announced, but still not able to create one on my server, because it crashes on each connection attempt. Not a big loss thought.
Another problem is server's remote console (RCON) doesn't support Unicode symbols.
Also server software has some specific dependencies (don't exactly remember), and now I cannot update my major server software normally. Annoying.
Overall impression is still positive. Mystery world and pet dinos is fun, mid-game surviving is not as difficult as early game, but still provides lots of dangers. Huge amount of grind, but it is not a big problem, because there's tons of servers with increased rates (my server is x3 for XP, resources and taming).
It's really unique game environment for me, fun and addictive, but I payed for Linux version of the game, and after official release I still haven't got finished product. If you are Linux or Mac user then don't buy it yet, while major bug is not fixed for this platforms.

If you like to enjoy games, then don't play this. Gameplay is shoddy a lot of the time; combat mechanics use interesting physics; can't swing a 3 foot Warhammer in a narrow hallway but can swing a 12 foot polearm in the same hall, headshot with an arrow is not a 1 hit kill... but sometimes it is. And the only gametype that's worth playing is the siege one; Free-for-all is button mashing, Team Deathmatch is so repeditive, and Last Team Standing is people just shouting "F10" in the chat.
But the real kicker is the community. Horrid attitudes, abusing buggs, spawn camping, teamkilling and banning for no reason. Yes, banning for NO reason. At all. As soon as people see that a vote has been started to ban someone, they automatically assume that the person deserves it and hit "YES". In one of game someone got 4 people banned because they had a higher score than he/she did (someone noticed this in the score screen near the end of the match and brought it up). The community I've experienced is a combination of fools and asses.
All in all...

Warframe has come a long way from when i first started playing, but i can honestly say the majority of it was great! Let me start by describing what warframe is. Its an over the shoulder third-person shooter where you play the role of a ninja warrior in space. The solar system is in chaos, and it's up to you to maintain the balance. With many weapon types to choose from, and different frames to use to suit your playstyle, the possibilities are endless. However there are certain strategies in higher level missions that even veteran players will tell you work. It's pretty much an MMO at this point, so certain "classes" of warframes work better at farming resources on certain missions. The developers also release new content as operations to introduce the new features, for example, the newest addition was corpus dropships that drop squads of enemies into battle. It was introduced as Operation: Ambulas Reborn, which featured a reworked boss that dropped in from the ship with a squad of regular enemies. There were a few bugs at first, but the incredibly awesome support team was very quick to respond to reports and get back within 24-48 hours. All in all, this has become one of the best free to play games i have ever played, and the graphics do an excellent job of immersing you in a living, breathing world that is constantly changing. I have to say that there are certain aspects of the game which require you to pay for features. Such as certain weapons, cosmetic packs, etc. Other than that, if you work hard and spend a decent amount of time on it, everything important is attainable without paying money for it. I do encourage you to support the developers by buying things that you may like, but only at your own discretion. Speaking of which, there is also a thriving market for the ingame currency, platinum, where you can spend platinum to buy parts, weapon mods, and other hard to obtain aspects from other players, as well as selling your own parts and mods to other players to obtain platinum. The prices will indeed vary on the rarity of what you are trying to get, but there is also sites and a wiki for any questions you may have about said things. All in all i have had a great experience with this game, rather than reading my long-winded review about the game, why not try it yourself? It's free! Also feel free to add me ingame and i will do my best to be as helpful as possible, my name is Mix_Masterson. See you on the battlefield, and have fun!

There is no clear objective in Warframe. Warframe is a game where you have to set your own, small goals, to keep you playing. They are consistently adding quests into the game to give it a bit more of a back bone, but besides that, you mainly keep playing through similar missions over and over again, killing similar enemies, in order to level up your Warframe and weapons so that you can eventually kill the same enemies faster or kill them in more interesting ways. With that being the case, Warframe is a grindy game and in order for you to enjoy it, you must enjoy the base feel of the game. If simply killing enemies isn't satisfying for you, then you will likely get quite burnt out on the game.
That being said, Warframe has a ridiculous amount of content such as Warframes (kind of like classes, they have different abilities), weapons, and mods for both your Warframes and weapons, so you are sure to find at least one Warframe and/or weapon that you find very enjoyable to play. For me, I just like to theorycraft and try out different combinations of weapons, warframes, mods, etc. to create new styles of play that can not only be fun, but also very effective.
When you first start out, there is definitely quite a steep grind you have to get through and the starting weapons/Warframes are not all that exciting, but the more you play the game, the easier it becomes to unlock new gear and once you have at least some gear that is high level, it becomes easier to level up new weapons and Warfames you craft.
In the end, I highly recommend trying out the game for a couple of hours and see if you enjoy the feel of the game, actually shooting enemies, using your Warframe abilities, or just cutting them up with melee weapons.
After 1200 hours (plus the number of hours I played before the game was on Steam), I will admit I am burnt out, I know the missions and enemies by heart, not much comes as a surprise, but I always come back to play when they release new content because this game is great for theorycrafting and adding all types of ingredients into a stew and seeing what the outcome is, and lucky for me, they are always adding new ingredients.
Also, their cash shop system is very fair for a F2P game. You can easily trade in-game items for cash currency in order to buy cosmetics and such.

Not as many hours as many others who have played early access but I do have a word to two to say about what's become of the game.
Early access for this game was an amazing journey with what seemed at first like a very reliable and active developer. The developer kept the updates coming like wildfire and it was awesome ... at first.
What happened is the game kept getting more things added but VERY LITTLE optimizations. Not to say there weren't optimizations at all though. They did optimize a lot for sure. However, it ended up turning into what seemed like a rush of content with lower and lower priority for optimizing a very broken game.
People (including myself) forgave those things but it almost seems that the developers took the faithful player base as a justification for keeping things as they are and not feeling pressure to actually FIX anything.
That's what the game is. A very broken idea of a game. It still needs TONS of work on animations, AI, and general game breaking glitches. AI is the biggest downfall of such a game. We're talking about a very diverse family of dinosaurs that fill the world but they still walk around like alpha implemented animations with very limited AI.
I can't say it enough. The most definite daunting task of building AI that fits best for each dino seems completely out of reach but they had a chance to keep the game in early access until that all was fixed and then release a much more completed and ready AAA game. Even if AI itself was the biggest thing they fixed, they could always push out updated Dino animations w/ actual collision awareness.
Dino tails and nearly half of their entire bodies can disappear into walls, cliffs, etc and when they walk up sudden high steps (like big rocks), their body has no bend to look more realistic.
The game had such promise as an early alpha that could have become a true AAA winner of the ages but fails ultimately in every way. I haven't even touched on graphics...
When I play ARK, I imagine a world where I'm out hunting but should be expecting to potentially be actually hunted by preditors - like Raptors. They just have a bigger agro radius and then become dumb attack beasts. This is the same with every preditor - just different agro radii.
At this point, the devs could straight up leave things as they are - no further promises to make. They are saying this game is complete and IT'S DEFINITELY NOT!
I do not recommend buying this game - yet. If they're serious about selling at the current price point, they need to actually fix everything that's wrong with it.

A brilliantly simple hack and slash game, complete with satisfyingly gruesome dismemberment and decapitation. The controls are excellent and provide a fun challenge in mastering the timing of chain attacks with different weapons. The game is online multiplayer only and there are a good variety of game modes, with the objective based games (For example, pushing a cart of corpses into an enemy water supply) being the most fun. The game runs very smoothly even on full servers and the chaos you'll find here is very much like medieval warfare. Teamkilling is practically a part of the game as accidents happen very, very fequently, but its hilarious rather than frustrating (Dont expect to go on a 20 kill rampage, your team mate will probably behead you first lol).
I find this to be a great pick up and play game, and have lost many, many fun filled hours to it. My only gripes would be that the levelling up system doesnt really seem to offer that much advancement or exciting new weapons to use and there could be more maps to play on. Other than that, I'd say grab some frineds and give it a try! Highly recommended if you fancy something a bit different from an FPS or are into the Medieval setting.

Ok, normally I would not leave a review for a game, it's not my style, and I am a horrible writer, but I just have to say this.
If you have put over 500 hours into the game, it should get a positive review, even if it costs 60 dollars unless the game seriously screwed you over.
That being said, a lot of people in the "negative reviews" section are complaining about the game changing for the worse, and that theres no "end game" guess what, there doesn't NEED to be an end game, if you've played for long enough in a FREE, let me repeat that FREE GAME, to reach where the "end game" should be, you got your money out of it. If you buy something from the game, you chose to buy it, in my experience I have never seen anything in the game that you HAD to buy to get it from the developers, you can always grind until you get it. and if you want it enough to buy it with real money, you should want it enough to grind a few dozen hours. if you don't wanna grind, buy it, I wont judge you, I really couldn't care less whether you bought every single warframe and mod you own. if you feel that more should be added to the game, suggest stuff to the developers, maybe they can give you another COMPLETELY FREE update, or patch. Yes, they're not the best at working on the more important issues, but remind me, how many successful free games have you made lately.
Sorry for preaching, that needed to be said for the people with 1k+ hours and complaining their MHMS off, If you don't like the game anymore, feel free to leave a no on the reccomended, but don't whine about the games "golden days" if you liked it better then, just remember your sweet memories. my only personal complaint is the "power creep" as people call it. each new weapon/frame is stronger than the last one, making the old fun weapons obsolete. nidus for example can deal up to 30k+ damage without ANY mods at all with his first ability, that not only costs 40 energy to cast, but restores 1/4th of the energy used to cast it, and people call him balanced. I don't need to repeat more of what has been said about this game and it's developers, pretty much all of what you read here is 100% true and spot on. I really enjoyed this game in the early days, even with all it's glitches, lack of optimization and questionable server community. The idea of taming dinosaurs that were influenced - with artistic creativity to some degree of course - by real life creatures and adding the crafting/survival gameplay mechanics was brilliant and a really fun experience. I'm not sure how many people this will speak for but what ruined the game for me was the addition of the futuristic Tek Tier and silly things like dragons and the various other "lore" friendly creatures and items added. Obviously that stuff will appeal to some people but I wanted a dinosaur survival game, not Lord of The Rings in the year 4000 mixed with Jurassic park. The fact that the Tek Tier is the end game progression tier means that you either use it or become inferior, so you're basically forced to adopt that. I greatly prefer the Primitive Plus mod to the core game now but it's was so under developed and buggy the last time I played that it wasn't worth the time. The original idea was 10/10 but the final product is a 4/10 for me and I definitely would not ever pay $70 for it, let alone any of the ridiculous DLC.

The first time I played this was a week after release. I really liked the game but because I didn't understand most of things and didn't really make progress I stopped again.
Two years passed until a former classmate told me he'd play warframe and was in a clan.
So I reinstalled and joined.
We've been playing Warframe now every week, helping each other to get mods and warframes and all other stuff.
When Second Dream hit, I cried. It was nothing like ever before.
Although I've played for so long I didnt spend so much money on it either. Maybe I should have...
If you like playing a game regulary with some friends, want to come across new challenges every time and like to try out new play styles, new Weapons, new Skills, and Combinations of them to beat these challenges then this game is for you.
It has lore as mysterious as you want. It has emotions. It has detailed NPCs, all with their backstories.
The main game is to get Warframes, Weapons, Sentinels, Pet and other Gear to try them out, have fun, keep those you like, throw away those you don't,
get Mods (which is a really big thing in the Game), upgrade them, put them into your Gear and make you even more powerful. You can play around with the Warframes Skills and the Weapons Stats and find the one Build that suits you and your group the best.
There are many types of Coop-Missions with shuffled "rooms" and many different enemies in the game.
Fashion Frame is also a big thing. You can change out 4/5 colours on any gear or pet, you get to wear shoulderpads, kneepads, helmets, whole skins, some armorplate on your torso, and Syandanas, which are like capes but much cooler.
You can earn points for certain factions to get even more Mods and Weapons and Syandanas.
So the game is about grinding, yes, also you can accelerate building things with real money but that's not the fun way.
It's the hype for the next Weapons or Warframes or Sentinels or Pets that will be ready the next days, that will always have the struggle of leveling up from zero to thirty but may be really powerful, and may or may not be fun to play.
The game is Free to Play but also Free to Master. You can get to the top without spending any money if you do it right.
But also there are many cosmetic things and you wanna look cool while doing cool stuff
so you spend a little ;) not because you need it but because the game deserves it.

This is going to be a more professional review than others I've made.
Gameplay-wise this game is strong. There's a lot of mods on the Workshop, and there's enough vanilla game content to satisfy anyone who doesn't want to use mods.
Graphics wise the game is gorgeous on higher settings, if your PC can handle it. In fact even on lower graphics, it's still beautiful and worth picking up for graphics alone.
Difficulty wise, it's fiendish. You're put into an unbalanced game so the enemies could be completely OP. And I'm kind of OK with that. Games aren't supposed to spoonfeed you victory and this game will for ever make the spoon become decapitated.
Child friendliness. Don't get this for anyone really young, it may give them a heart attack, with the amount of gore.
Storyline: It's a combat game, there is no real story.
Overall verdict: 8.5/10 A very good game with pleasing combat, but the unbalanced fights can be annoying.
Any feedback will be appreciated as this is my first semi-professional review.

There is no clear objective in Warframe. Warframe is a game where you have to set your own, small goals, to keep you playing. They are consistently adding quests into the game to give it a bit more of a back bone, but besides that, you mainly keep playing through similar missions over and over again, killing similar enemies, in order to level up your Warframe and weapons so that you can eventually kill the same enemies faster or kill them in more interesting ways. With that being the case, Warframe is a grindy game and in order for you to enjoy it, you must enjoy the base feel of the game. If simply killing enemies isn't satisfying for you, then you will likely get quite burnt out on the game.
That being said, Warframe has a ridiculous amount of content such as Warframes (kind of like classes, they have different abilities), weapons, and mods for both your Warframes and weapons, so you are sure to find at least one Warframe and/or weapon that you find very enjoyable to play. For me, I just like to theorycraft and try out different combinations of weapons, warframes, mods, etc. to create new styles of play that can not only be fun, but also very effective.
When you first start out, there is definitely quite a steep grind you have to get through and the starting weapons/Warframes are not all that exciting, but the more you play the game, the easier it becomes to unlock new gear and once you have at least some gear that is high level, it becomes easier to level up new weapons and Warfames you craft.
In the end, I highly recommend trying out the game for a couple of hours and see if you enjoy the feel of the game, actually shooting enemies, using your Warframe abilities, or just cutting them up with melee weapons.
After 1200 hours (plus the number of hours I played before the game was on Steam), I will admit I am burnt out, I know the missions and enemies by heart, not much comes as a surprise, but I always come back to play when they release new content because this game is great for theorycrafting and adding all types of ingredients into a stew and seeing what the outcome is, and lucky for me, they are always adding new ingredients.
Also, their cash shop system is very fair for a F2P game. You can easily trade in-game items for cash currency in order to buy cosmetics and such.

This is my second review of Chivalry, now with over 700 hours played in game. I love this game. The fighting is comedic, enjoyable and visceral. The voices of the characters (particularly the Mason Man-At-Arms) are very funny. Nothing like watching a man screaming for help as he appears to demolish his enemies by punching them to death.
The graphics are nice, and the sound effects are neither amazing nor lacking. There is a steep skill-curve with this game. In the low-ranking servers, newbies will fight an easier fight. But this will probably breed a habit of bad tactics and gameplay into them, which they must grow out of to be able to compete against more seasoned players. Much has been made of bizarre spinning tactics and reverse overheads attacks being 'glitch' tactics or somehow broken. It is not. There are ways to combat these, ways you can learn quite easily and then counter them for using. Chivalry is a game that will reward you if you have the guts and iron to stick it out and take the pain for a while.
Chivalry will make you laugh, make you annoyed, and make you feel a surge of victory. One of my favourite games on Steam and I don't really ever see myself stopping playing it.

I had previously written a positive review with strong caveats but am changing it to negative.  At this point I feel that the bugs and the developers' ignoring of said bugs (especially after the release of the DLC) have too much of a negative impact on the game to enjoy anymore.
The game from a design standpoint is fantastic.  They made the best melee combat system I've seen in a game and there's a good variety of maps and game modes to play around with. Unfortunately there are many bugs, some of which completely destroy any concept of class and weapon balance, that have existed since release.  The developers flat out refuse to acknowledge that these bugs even exist, much less fix them.  They have shown themselves to be completely clueless about weapon balance as well, often buffing the stronger weapons in patches and nerfing the weaker ones.  From what I understand the situation has only gotten worse since the release of the DLC.  Every server is pretty much guaranteed to have several people exploiting these bugs and ruining it for everybody else.
So while I did have a lot of fun with the game when it was new, mostly before the bugs were widely exploited, there's no way I can recommend it now.

Okay, definitely one of the better "F2P" titles out there.
I will list the most important pro's and con's that this game has. For obvious reasons I will not write all of them, that'd bring me to the brink of the steam review character limit.
+ Very good Graphics and decent optimization
+ Fast paced action with strong emphasis on movement (stand still and you die)
+ Nice power curve, it takes some time.. but it's really nice to turn yourself and your frames from weaklings to god-like war machines that kill hundreds of enemies with ease.
+ A vast variety of options to choose from for modding and customization
+ Fair microtransaction system, premium currency is tradable
+ Active Community and Devs, it's still being actively worked on and theres like a bazillion people still playing it
+ There's always something to do, with the rather frequent updates, the game always introduces new mechanics, weapons, playstyles and so on
- There's grinding involved. And depending on how good you are, quite a bit, or luck with drops and with trades but yeah you WILL be grinding a bit, but that's never really too annoying for the most part
- WF is a clear meta game, even while playing completely PvE, you still run into people who will expect a certain loadout, especially in late game content.
- Confusing as f***, the game CAN be very disorienting, some things have changed but a few little things are not very intuitive and make you pay the wiki a visit more than once. (or your clan mates)
(when you start playing)
~ Being able to choose freely what to play. Don't get me wrong, you certainly CAN play everything this game offers without spending any money (with founder items being the exception), but some of the things like vaulted primes, questline-tied frames will require a bit of grinding and/or luck and/or prerequisites in form of quests
~ To be able to dish out nearly as much damage as a high leveled/experienced player, every mission shows you how much damage you've done compared to others, so you will most likely run into a few players that will leave your "score" at a few mesely percent
TL;DR: Very good game, that is worth picking up and putting some money and time into, has flaws but very minor compared to all the things it does right.. oh and it's F2P so yeah.. no brainer to at least try it out..

Oh boy, here goes a thumbs down for a game with generally "very positive" reviews.
(In)famous
arrived on Steam in the spring 2015. As ridiculous as I thought the clicker genre was, I found many people in the achievement-hunting community taking it on and I decided it was worth the try. Almost 10 months later I've completed it but unfortunately I didn't like the experience with this particular clicker game.
When I first started the game it was quite fun in a casual way. I found myself farming bosses, building a more powerful build and making giant steps in progress by few critical purchases.
For those of you unacquainted with the genre,
as a clicker game has you training a roster of heroes and beating waves of monsters to get to ever higher waves. Monsters are killed by the static DPS (damage per second) of heroes and your clicks. There is no end, though you can complete the game Steam Achievement-wise and hunt the in-game achievements that require ginormous amounts of time to unlock all.
The artwork is cute and fun, making references to famous JRPGs of olde, like
,
and
. Sound and music is too repetitive to my liking so I kept it muted almost from the start.
After a while you are urged to "restart", i.e. ascend. Only through ascending (well, initially anyway) do you get Hero Souls that are used to build Ancients that are some kind of artefacts or idols that e.g. increase the amount of gold or DPS, reduce skill cooldowns or even increase the number and probability of getting more Hero Souls.
A steady increase in power and things to consider is ensured by collecting artefacts, sending mercenaries to adventures, hero empowerment through gilding and the associated meta-game and even taking part in community-driven clans that fight super-bosses every day for a collective reward of Hero Souls. The latter adds in a multiplayer aspect of sorts.
For a while the game was genuinely fun.
allows for several playstyles. Idle builds concentrate on empowering gold farming and DPS of heroes without interfering with the game, while more active players may opt for increasing click damage, number and power of critical strikes and skills and building huge combos (by active clicking) to keep the run going. Later on a hybrid build supporting both playstyles becomes feasible.
Once everything has been bought, it's only a matter of grinding more and more Hero Souls to be able to beat higher waves. Almost nothing ever changes again. Once in a while a new hero joins the roster, adding a speck of backstory and raising a momentary excitement.
Unfortunately, if you simple farm Hero Souls, the game becomes dull very fast. Playing an idle build, for me the game had come to a point where for months almost nothing interesting happened in the game. I might get one achievement for reaching a certain wave once in two months.
I was looking at years of grinding if I wanted to beat the game by pure idling and farming.
There was one way out: a deep run using the skill called Dark Ritual. There are ten active skills in the game, one of which grants 5% increase to DPS when used. The thing is, through the use of this skill and a couple of others it's possible to retain simple combo that multiplies the DPS by 100 in 24 hours.
After months of stagnation I completed the last few wave-based achievements and apparently one third of the game in a couple of days by using this very combo. Efficient? Yes. But was it fun?
I was appalled and disappointed by how easy it was in the end. What was the grind use for when a simple combo makes all that vain? In my opinion a game design allowing this makes for an unbalanced game.
In 10 months, 1000 hours and 0 dollars used I had completed the game (Steam Achievement-wise) but apparently it could probably be done ten times faster.
In its defense,
has been updated several times during the year it has been on Steam. While originally just a simple clicker, the addition of clans, mercenaries and artefacts the grind has become a lot more bearable and interesting. Someone else might even feel finding the winning combo to be fulfilling.
Would I recommend it though? If your main objective is the completion: not really. While it is fun for a while, the utter grind of Hero Souls and its ultimate futility in favour of spamming a (IMO) boring skill pushes myself to the side of Not Recommended.

Clicker Heroes is essentially the gaming equivalent of pet wheatgrass or a tamagotchi minus the need to participate in its development in any thoughtful or meaningful way whatsoever. It is mindlessness and pointlessness reduced,  distilled  and dripped through a pippette  in the form of inane,  twee monsters superimposed over infinite credit tickers. It is almost impossible to imagine a more meaningless game--Indeed, as I have previously alluded to, it is not really a game at all. Although I haven't tried it, I have no doubt that one could garner the same sense of satisfaction dispensed by clicker heroes by simpling multiplying random sums on a calculator to see how many decimal places you can get to.
It really is very, very ♥♥♥♥ing stupid.
It's also together quite evil, because clearly what the developers intend by this game is to turn people into rats at pellet dispensers by exploiting  human susceptibility to operant conditoning:
"
B.F. Skinner (1938) coined the term operant conditioning; it means roughly changing of behavior by the use of reinforcement which is given after the desired response. Skinner identified three types of responses or operant that can follow behavior."
The particular type of OC driven by clicker heroes is positive reinforcement wed to RNG type drops for items in game ( rubies). Basically, it's gambling. The idea is that you move from something you would consider unthinkable ( spending real currency on rubies in game) to handing over real money to progress in a game which is utterly pointless, requires absolutely no skill whatsoever and is limitless.
This is of course par for the course with clickers ( rat at pellet dispenser games) and to its credit, clciker heroes does offer  means by which to gather Rubies and Hero shards without the use to real currency. Irregardless, it is nonetheless exploitative, boring, pernciously repetitive. It's basically a drag net designed to ensnare those addicted to, or susceptible to, degenerate gambling type behavior.

Gameplay
An unique and intressting concept with increadbly poor execution. The game takes place on what is know as an ARK, why and how is later revealed in the story. The game contains a bucket load of dinos and are very captivating once you get thrown in to this savage and brutal world. In the beginning and at first glance the game is easy to progress in and it feels like you're consitantly moving forward. You get rewarded for exploring the island and looting the sky shards which contains diffrent loot depending on its colour.
After a few hours you should have a basic base up and running and its time to tame your first dino. Diffrent dinos have diffrent abilities and stats, some are tanky and are usefull to farm berries, woods or stone etc. Others are more fighting oriented and some are great for transporting goods or people. The rest of the game is pretty much rinse and repeat, rebuild your base with a higher tier building material which contains more components, tame bigger/better/faster dinos, venture in to more dangerous areas of the map.
So far it's a solid survival/base building experience with many unique mechanics and heeps of content. But after your first 100 hours the game turns into a wierd stat grinder. To keep your dinos relevant you have to breed them by mating two diffrent sex dinos with preferred stats and hope the offspring gains the prefered stats. The later stages of the game turns in to this maintence heavy stat grinder where tribes houses 100rds of dinos just to mate them into dinos with good stats, essentially making it a min/max simultor.
The game heavily favors offline base raiding, its cheaper to get equipment to raid a base than it is to maintain a base. Essentially making offline base raiding the most viable option, promoting a playstyle that rewards avoiding conflicts and just wait until your enemys are offline.
Tech
Game suffers from serious optimization issues, and it does not look like we will see any solutions in the near future or at all honostly.
It looks pretty but even high end riggs consistantly suffers from frame rate issues. Official servers can get really laggy.
TL;DR
Games great to explore as a new player, has much fun to offer in the beginning. The PVP is an offline raid fest, Game gets really stale after a while and turns into a wierd stat grinder min/maxing simulator. Not optimized at all.
5/10 for offline SP.
3/10 for Online play.

I have tried this game during free weekends and finally decided to buy it in the hope that they had fixed the terrible game play. Unfortunately they have not. The core of the gameplay, attacking and blocking the opposition is still broken to the point that the game is not fun, but provides a frustrating experience.
It creates anger every time you play it becuase the game field is not fair. Everything feels slow and clunky becuase all the servers lag so badly. Some are better than others, but in the end, those with the best pings will dominate. It is not uncommon to die 10 times and only get 1 kill becuase the lag is so bad. Your actions on screen are not registered and all you end up doing is getting killed unfairly as hits go through your block. This repeats every match, every game.
If Torn Banner actually cared about the game, they would have attempted to fix it after all these years instead of making a DLC for it. I cannot recommed this game to anyone, not even when it is on sale as I feel like I should be entitled to a refund. It is not fun nor challenging. It just provides hours of frustration while taking your money and wasting your time.

The first time I played this was a week after release. I really liked the game but because I didn't understand most of things and didn't really make progress I stopped again.
Two years passed until a former classmate told me he'd play warframe and was in a clan.
So I reinstalled and joined.
We've been playing Warframe now every week, helping each other to get mods and warframes and all other stuff.
When Second Dream hit, I cried. It was nothing like ever before.
Although I've played for so long I didnt spend so much money on it either. Maybe I should have...
If you like playing a game regulary with some friends, want to come across new challenges every time and like to try out new play styles, new Weapons, new Skills, and Combinations of them to beat these challenges then this game is for you.
It has lore as mysterious as you want. It has emotions. It has detailed NPCs, all with their backstories.
The main game is to get Warframes, Weapons, Sentinels, Pet and other Gear to try them out, have fun, keep those you like, throw away those you don't,
get Mods (which is a really big thing in the Game), upgrade them, put them into your Gear and make you even more powerful. You can play around with the Warframes Skills and the Weapons Stats and find the one Build that suits you and your group the best.
There are many types of Coop-Missions with shuffled "rooms" and many different enemies in the game.
Fashion Frame is also a big thing. You can change out 4/5 colours on any gear or pet, you get to wear shoulderpads, kneepads, helmets, whole skins, some armorplate on your torso, and Syandanas, which are like capes but much cooler.
You can earn points for certain factions to get even more Mods and Weapons and Syandanas.
So the game is about grinding, yes, also you can accelerate building things with real money but that's not the fun way.
It's the hype for the next Weapons or Warframes or Sentinels or Pets that will be ready the next days, that will always have the struggle of leveling up from zero to thirty but may be really powerful, and may or may not be fun to play.
The game is Free to Play but also Free to Master. You can get to the top without spending any money if you do it right.
But also there are many cosmetic things and you wanna look cool while doing cool stuff
so you spend a little ;) not because you need it but because the game deserves it.

There is no clear objective in Warframe. Warframe is a game where you have to set your own, small goals, to keep you playing. They are consistently adding quests into the game to give it a bit more of a back bone, but besides that, you mainly keep playing through similar missions over and over again, killing similar enemies, in order to level up your Warframe and weapons so that you can eventually kill the same enemies faster or kill them in more interesting ways. With that being the case, Warframe is a grindy game and in order for you to enjoy it, you must enjoy the base feel of the game. If simply killing enemies isn't satisfying for you, then you will likely get quite burnt out on the game.
That being said, Warframe has a ridiculous amount of content such as Warframes (kind of like classes, they have different abilities), weapons, and mods for both your Warframes and weapons, so you are sure to find at least one Warframe and/or weapon that you find very enjoyable to play. For me, I just like to theorycraft and try out different combinations of weapons, warframes, mods, etc. to create new styles of play that can not only be fun, but also very effective.
When you first start out, there is definitely quite a steep grind you have to get through and the starting weapons/Warframes are not all that exciting, but the more you play the game, the easier it becomes to unlock new gear and once you have at least some gear that is high level, it becomes easier to level up new weapons and Warfames you craft.
In the end, I highly recommend trying out the game for a couple of hours and see if you enjoy the feel of the game, actually shooting enemies, using your Warframe abilities, or just cutting them up with melee weapons.
After 1200 hours (plus the number of hours I played before the game was on Steam), I will admit I am burnt out, I know the missions and enemies by heart, not much comes as a surprise, but I always come back to play when they release new content because this game is great for theorycrafting and adding all types of ingredients into a stew and seeing what the outcome is, and lucky for me, they are always adding new ingredients.
Also, their cash shop system is very fair for a F2P game. You can easily trade in-game items for cash currency in order to buy cosmetics and such.

Warframe was a game that got hyped up to me by so many people, but ultimately ended up being a huge letdown right out of the gate. The "fluid" combat is nothing more than a slippery, loose mess with little to no feedback whatsoever- if you want to survive, it's a requirement that you keep your eyes glued to the micorscopic health bar 99% of the time.
Missions are repetitive and yawnworthy- once you've played one "defend the thing" objective, you've played them all. There is a miniscule amount of variety in the worlds as well, and it ultimately leads to a feeling of "Oh, I've been here before" on pretty much every level.
The enemies you'll encounter are astoundingly stupid- their strategy is simply to keep shooting and occasionally take cover- or sometimes just stand out in the open and twiddle their thumbs. This strategy works, however, and not because of any true sense of difficulty- it's simply because there's so many of them in each level that their rubber bullets effectively become swarms of bees. The only real difference between enemies is the amount of armor they wear, obviously requiring more shots to take down the larger ones.
The graphics are wonderful, and the atmosphere generally emits the feel that it needs to, but it certainly isn't enough to make up for all of the gameplay issues.
Playing alongside a friend or two does give a slight sense of enjoyment to the game. Being able to tear through the mindless AI does have a certain charm to it; although that might merely be because there's another bullet sponge running alongside you to make the mission end faster.
In summation, Warframe is an unpolished, monotonous, boring mess of a game that I wouldn't recommend to anyone looking for a truly enjoyable experience.

Pitting 6 classes of warriors and raiders against each other; Viking, Ninja, Samurai, Knight, Spartan, and Pirate, this game is such a great idea and fun to play whether in a team or alone.
Each class has a personal set of achievable player titles, weapons, cosmetics, and more which are related to the culture of the class played. The maps large enough to eliminate any monotony and they match the culture and society involved with the correlating class.
Good game mechanics. Though the game might be laggy for some systems after the initial download. If you have this problem, the video "How To Make Chivarly Medevial Warfare Not Lag" from Youtube should help you fix the problem quickly.
A negative criticism would be that there are a few inconsistencies. An example is that two of the weapons of the Viking class are mixed up. The two weapons are the Skeggox and the Dane Axe. The Skeggox is also known as a "bearded axe," which has a longer heel for the axehead and a shorter handle. The Dane Axe has a longer handle (often 5-6 feet in length).
Also, when browsing the server options on the game, many of the "Players" slots will are incorrect (i.e. the slot will show a server is full but when you enter, the number of player slots listed is incorrect. Basically, regardless of the number of players it shows for each server, you should try to connect because it might be in correct.
Overall, I give the game an 8 out of 10 rating.

Excellent concept!
Pitting 6 classes of warriors and raiders against each other; Viking, Ninja, Samurai, Knight, Spartan, and Pirate, this game is such a great idea and fun to play whether in a team or alone.
Each class has a personal set of achievable player titles, weapons, cosmetics, and more which are related to the culture of the class played. The maps large enough to eliminate any monotony and they match the culture and society involved with the correlating class.
Good game mechanics. Though the game might be laggy for some systems after the initial download. If you have this problem, the video "How To Make Chivarly Medevial Warfare Not Lag" from Youtube should help you fix the problem quickly.
A negative criticism would be that there are a few inconsistencies. An example is that two of the weapons of the Viking class are mixed up. The two weapons are the Skeggox and the Dane Axe. The Skeggox is also known as a "bearded axe," which has a longer heel for the axehead and a shorter handle. The Dane Axe has a longer handle (often 5-6 feet in length).
Also, when browsing the server options on the game, many of the "Players" slots will are incorrect (i.e. the slot will show a server is full but when you enter, the number of player slots listed is incorrect. Basically, regardless of the number of players it shows for each server, you should try to connect because it might be in correct.
Overall, I give the game an 8 out of 10 rating.

I do recommend it however, through it all.

It's really worth buying. You know why? Because it's a totally unique game. How often do you see multiplayer medieval FPP/TPP game? It brings very refreshing feeling after all those modern shooters. And it's a really worthy representative of this rare kind of games.
Combat might seem very simple (only 3 kinds of blows: swing, overhead and thrust attacks), but unexperienced people who teamkill and whine about randomness of fighting prove it wrong :). Also, mastering your movement (ducking blows, parry timing, jumping over people's shields to attack them from above, drags, etc.) will take a long time. By the way: what other attacks would you use in real fight? There's nothing to complain about, it's not some kind of Japanese hack'n'slash, for Argon's sake!
There are no killstreaks or perks in this game. Is it a flaw? Not at all. It's an actual advantage! Congratulations to developers for that decision, because efectiveness should be an effect of player's skill, not some buffs which give you supernatural health or damage rate.
Community is generally great, far from typical "CoD kids", people can discuss about many clever topics, you know, like a sir.
I also like high level of immersion: arrows wheezing next to your head, clanging of swords, rustling of hauberk... Imagine this with virtual reality headset...
Just think about one thing: why wouldn't you buy the game that is so immersive and exceeds the boundaries of run-of-the-mill, overhyped productions developed by companies focused on milking money from customers? Many people complain about Battlefield, Titanfall, Call of Duty games. Why aren't you encouraged yet to join the world which maybe doesn't feature tanks, planes or guns, but contains epic, close, often honorable combat and no ♥♥♥♥♥♥s camping in debris, killing you from 1000 m?
10/10, would join the Mason Order.

As far as idle games go, it's not that bad.
Clicker Heroes's problem simply is that it's neither all that good, and it isn't helped by the fact that most people will only need to play a single or maybe two games out of the genre and be done with it.
So before playing this, I'd recommend some better options like Candy Box 1+2, A Dark Room and Cookie Clicker.
Candy Box and A Dark Room both open up to feature highly unexpected and impressive gameplay aside from mere idling, clicking and grinding.
Cookie Clicker on the other hand is fantastically written and has a great flow.
Now, Clicker Heroes on the other hand has lots of text, with lots of it being meant to be funny, but only small parts of it succeeding at it.
It also rarely allows for a good flow, as you'll often bump into bottlenecks, getting up to snuff after an ascension can take WAY too long (also, but not only compared to Cookie Clicker) and you often don't see a particular next goal dangling before your virtual nose.
It also lacks more diverse gameplay with most added features being little more than little treats in the same vein as the rest of the game.
And possibly worst of all: Now I now developers need to make money, but neither Candy Box nor A Dark Room or Cookie Clicker feature any kind of monetization aside from unintrusive ads. Clicker Heroes on the other hand lets you buy jewels with real money and some parts of the game basically beg for your money like when resurrecting a high-level hero for throusands of jewels. Sure, you can just bury the hero and move on, but the game is still trying to push you into spending money.
So, I can already hear some of you murmuring: "Then why did you play it for 500+ hours? Your review is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!"
Three easy reasons:
1. Not all of my "playtime" has been spent as such, as is the nature of idle games. I certainly didn't spend 500+ hours actively playing this.
2. I'm a perfectionist. When I start a game, I finish it. No matter how bad it is. So in this case this meant getting 100% achievements.
3. As I said, it's not a terrible game. I had already finished three other idle games, still looking for more, and Clicker Heroes delivered just that, albeit worse than the other games before it. But as far as idle games on Steam go, this still appears to be one of the better choices with neat visuals and some well-realized ideas such as the various ancients drastically altering your playstyle...until you hit a point where only a certain combination of ancients and actions let you make any decent progress, thus washing away one of the game's greatest strengths.
So, in summary: If you are new to the genre, leave Steam and search for better alternatives elsewhere. Only seasoned genre fans with no better options to take should apply.

Chivalry, slice anyone's head off. Shoot giant arrows into someone's butt. And get a rewarding head explosion when you kill someone with your fists. It's all here in Chivalry.
This game is fun to play, much variety, and a lot of action.
But, chivalry has his ups and downs.
Pros:

+/- The Classes aren't balanced that well, but sure playable
Cons:
- A few bugs you experience through the game are annoying, but there are very few of them.

Verdict:
This game is a big recommend for people who are interested in first person combat (it can be set to 3th person).
Sure, Chivalry has some few bugs and some weapons aren't balanced well, but this is a great expierence. I even recommend you the full Chivalry pack. ( Chivalry: Medieval Warfare + Chivalry: Deadliest warrior which i will talk about in a few seconds)
So I give this game a good rewarding 8.7/10
Chivalry: Deadliest Warrior.
Play as history's greatest warriors. Throw long spears like a Spartan. Stab in someone's back like a Ninja. And die with honor for your family like a Samurai. It's all here to be played.
But it has his Cons and Pros.
Pros:
++++ The combat even got better with more chaos
++++ The new unlocking system got better with individual levels.
+++ The Customisation got upgraded, you can now unlock hats!... HAAAAAAAAAAAAAATS!!!!!!!! (Seriously it's good)
+++ You now have 6 classes instead of 4 with all an unique thing to do.
++ You can be drunk a drunk pirate :D.
++ More maps.
+ A new gamemode called Plant the Banner
+ More everything.
+/- a return of Medieval Warfare's map called Moor (not really a fan of it)
Cons:
--- Where's the team objective game mode? :((((((((((
-- The Spartans and Vikings are a bit Overpowerd which many people don't seem to like
- Some blocking bugs but you'll get used to it
Verdict:
Chivalry: Deadliest warrior is like a whole new game, so do i recommend it? Well, HECK YEAH, but you do need the normal game for it. So, the deadliest warrior offers more variety for less balance. Yeah it's annoying when you get a spear through your head from a Spartan but you'll grow over it.
So i give this DLC (whole new game) a 9/10.
So if you doubt pressing that "buy" button. Click it now before i change my mind about this game.
Have fun with this game and don't forget to play the training.

I can't think of a review, so here's a cinnamon roll recipe:
Ingredients
For the Dough:
1 cup whole milk
one 1/4-ounce packet active dry yeast (2 1/2 teaspoons)
1/4 cup plus 1/4 teaspoon granulated sugar
4 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the bowl
1 large egg yolk
1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla extract
2 3/4 cups all-purpose flour, plus more if needed
3/4 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon freshly grated nutmeg
For the Filling:
All-purpose flour, for dusting
12 tablespoons unsalted butter, softened, plus more for the pan
1/2 cup granulated sugar
3 tablespoons ground cinnamon
For the Glaze:
2 cups confectioners' sugar
1/3 cup heavy cream
4 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted
Directions
Make the dough: Warm the milk in a medium saucepan over low heat until it reaches about 100. Remove from the heat and sprinkle in the yeast and 1/4 teaspoon sugar (don't stir). Set aside until foamy, 5 minutes. Whisk in the melted butter, egg yolk and vanilla.
Whisk the flour, the remaining 1/4 cup sugar, the salt and nutmeg in the bowl of a stand mixer. Make a well in the center and pour in the yeast mixture. Mix on low speed with the dough hook until thick and slightly sticky. Knead on medium speed until the dough gathers around the hook, 6 minutes. (Add up to 2 more tablespoons flour if necessary.)
Remove the dough and shape into a ball. Butter the mixer bowl and return the dough to the bowl, turning to coat with butter. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise until doubled, 1 hour 15 minutes.
Roll out the dough, fill and cut into buns (see instructions below). Butter a 9-by-13-inch baking pan; place the buns cut-side down in the pan, leaving space between each. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise until doubled, 40 minutes. Preheat the oven to 325.
Bake the buns until golden brown, about 35 minutes. Cool in the pan 15 minutes. Meanwhile, make the glaze: Sift the confectioners' sugar into a bowl, then whisk in the cream and melted butter. Transfer the buns to a rack and spoon the glaze on top while still warm.
How to Form Cinnamon Buns
1. On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough into a 12-by-14-inch rectangle with the longer side facing you.
2. Spread with the softened butter, leaving a 1/2-inch border on the far long edge. Mix the sugar and cinnamon; sprinkle over the butter.
3. Brush the unbuttered far edge with water. Roll the dough away from you into a tight cylinder and press on the long edge to seal.
4. Cut the cylinder with a sharp knife to make 6 equal-size buns.

Ok I would like to start off this review with a note: this game was fun for the first couple of hours of playing, after that it felt a bit repetitive and there was no real depth to it. I would only recommend the game if it was on a sale.
Pros:
-The graphics, they seem to be kind of comic styled or cartoon like with something far from realistic but unique and fitting.
-The playerbase, I have played other games similar to this but with limited amounts of players on the servers. Where as this game has plenty of selection with no doubt of finding a packed server with good to decent ping.
-Choice of classes. I believe that these classes are what makes the game what it is, they are all different with their own aspects, such as; the Man-At-Arms has the ability to run faster but to sacrifice this he will have less armor compared to the other classes. It evens out the game making a fair gameplay instead of an archer wth heavy armor, which would be unfair.
-Fast loading time onto the game, compared to some of my other games it seemed to be pretty fast.
-A understandable tutorial which you have the option of selecting, which gives you the indepth tips of perfecting your ability to fight on the battlefield.
-The server filters, which are easy to use. You can create a favorite server list, check what servers your friends are on, view your server history and use the server filter which is mainly used for changing gamemode and ping aswell as the option to search manually.
Cons:
-There was no option to remove the second sword selection, such as the dagger and replacing it with another item such as more throwing knives.
-The actual character response, it feels a bit slow when trying to attack then suddenly block, most of the time resulting in a death.
-It get very repetitive quickly, the only thing that changes is the maps and gamemodes, everything else; weapons, classes, sides, they never change. This game would possibly suit an advanced arcade machine, one of those games which has a limited fun time to it.
-Players in general, some of them will attempt to steal your kill, which you may have been working hard on achieving and coming close to killing them, as I was, this resulted in me launching a fire-pot his way for revenge.
-As far as I am aware, there is no option to join a server to stop the team-kill ability. I understand the developers are trying to keep it realistic, but half of the slashes which I produce will be accidentally focused on a team-mate, this usually happens when a brawl takes place and can be quite irritating.
-Price: I just checked the price to confirm, it is £18.99 here in the UK and currently €23.72 in the EU and $32.48 Dollars. I believe this price is extremely high compared to the amount of fun it gave me. (A couple of hours) Instead I would recommend getting this game on sale, like I did and then it will be well worth your money.

Warframe...where to even begin with this game?
First and most important :
This is not game that is actually P2W hiding behind F2P title like a lot of those games. This game is actually 99% free. That 1% is actually cosmetic and we all know that true endgame is to look fashionable.
Aside cosmetics all other things in the game can be farmed and crafted wothout paying a cent. Also if you want to be part of fashion police do not panic just yet. You can trade for premium currency or platinum.
Now to the rest of the list :
Graphics are amazing for F2P title and is often compared to some of AAA titles and you dont even have to have high end PC. Anything above potato salad will be enough.
Gunplay and melee feels fantastic especially when you can split enemies in bloody pieces.
Parkour is made fantastic. You can roll , slide , double jump , wallrun , wall latch , float like a glider (dont ask how but you can) and even jump like a bullet (surprise oh surprise its called bullet jump) and its not just side thing. Every one of these capabilities are to increase your mobility to the max.
Customisation is done great but it could be better. When I saw what can I do with mods (these are upgrades for your weapons and frames) I was a) Confused AF b) astonished AF. You can build your frames and weapons how you see fit. Want max shield? Done. Want max HP? Done. Want full power strength? It is already done. Or maybe you want full sprint speed build? It was done before you even thinked about it.
Now you are probaly asking : But Vapya this sounds amazing how could it be better.
Well it is true you can build your equipment how you want but to make your weappns deal max amount of DPS it will take a specific build and mods to gain 100% of DPS.
Community
This community is THE best community I have ever seen. To explain this easy way this community is as good as LOL community is toxic and cancerous. If you ask for help you even get to choose who will help you. Imagine that. When you saw that in Lol or CsGo last time?
Devolpers
DE (Digital Extreme) is one of the best companies I have seen. They push out updates frequently , have livestreams once every week or 2 and are actively communicating with playerbase (I mean when they livestream and they do missions you can join them if they need full squad)

Now an honest review. Warframe is probably one of the best free 2 play multiplayer games out there, because it gets updated pretty frequently. However, if you have played it tons and tons of hours, like me, its gets very repetitive. You wil come to the point where it is just grinding and grinding for new weapons to build.
In addition to that, you also have this currency called "platinum". It is used for buying weapons, or cosmetics. You do have to buy that with real money, but there is also a trading system. You can then sell mods, "Prime" stuff, which are basically weapons or warframes with an upgraded look and different stats. If you have those kinds of stuff, you can sell it for some platinum. But do not overprice things!
Finally, you have quests and an ingame lore, which are pretty fun and all, but you will play through that pretty quickly. Now, DE is working on a big new update, called "The Plains Of Eidolon", which will be released this summer, if my intel is correct. When it comes out, there will be a lot more to warframe, than meets the eye.
I will update my review once it gets released. 'Till then, is it worth playing? Absolutely. Its free, and gets updated more frequently than the average f2p game. But if you are looking for an open world game, you might skip this one for now and come back later, because as i said: Plains of Eidolon will be released this summer, so stay tuned for that ;)

As someone who has played Ark probably more than I should,  I can't explain enough how much I love this game. To most of the bad reviews out there, please dont play this game on official servers. Find some friends who play, play by yourself, but dont do official. They lag, have bugs, obviously griefers and cheaters, but thats not the point of this game.
ITS DINOSAURS. Who doesnt love dinos??
Some of the biggest things I LOVE about this game, is the dinos all look so amazing and realistic. Their color patterns are unique, and its not just a copy paste design. There are hundreds of dinos, and so many different things they can do. Doesnt matter if they are useful or not, its just cool to see all of them.
Now here's the big deal for me, is the scenery. This game is so beautiful, both from sunrise to sunset. I love being able to take my griffin out to the grand canyon in the expansion Ragnarok and just enjoy the waterfalls and mountains. It gives me inspiration honestly!
In conclusion, all I can say is don't be so hard on a game if youre playing with the wrong people. If you have griefers and cheaters, thats not supposed to be part of the experience. Find the gameplay that works for you, and adjust settings if you want a difference in gameplay. You do have the ability to make the game easier.
Again, would reccomend to anyone and everyone all ages.

In terms of free to play content, Warframe has a lot to offer. The combat system is fast paced and the lack of a cover system really aids the feeling of intensity. Along with some parkour mechanics and a bit of melee, Warframe's combat is a blast.
There are many different types of playable "warframes", and from the ones i tried, each feels unique. There's even missions set in space, that introduce a whole bunch of new mechanics, and for the first 10+ hours, warframe is a joy to play. Unfortunatley however, it is around this time the game begins showing its "Free to Play" side. While it's true that pretty much all items (besides cosmetics) can be had for free, it is often behind a ridiculous grind wall.
Yes you can trade, but unless sitting in a chat for an hour copying and pasting the same message over and over until someone replies is your idea of a fun gaming experience, this is of little help, though i can imagine this being better in a clan. The truth is, this game expects you to spend an unreasonable amount of time on it, though it is possible you may enjoy the game so much that this is fine for you.
Overall, i will return to warframe now and then, since there is still enjoyment to be had from it, but i'd definitley rather spend a few dollars during a steam sale and buy a game that doesn't drip feed me to keep me hooked.
When you start playing you WILL get addicted.

Possibly one of the best F2P games on the market, it doesn't really force you to partake in microtransactions, but you do end up having to wait around a lot between quests and things. This game is crafting oriented, and it takes time to craft things you really want or need. My experience went a lot like this:
A friend asked me to download this game for a long while, and I never really got around to it fearing it was going to not be that engaging or simply just a low quality F2P game from some developer I've never even heard of. (Oh, was I wrong.)
After downloading it and trying it, I ended up feeling neutral about the whole thing. The entire game just has so much to take in from gameplay, graphics, and lore. It all starts to make a lot more sense around mastery rank 3, which is a little ways into the game. I started to love it as I progressed through more levels and continued on to MR6. I'm only MR8, and there's still a lot I need to learn, especially after the update that removed void keys, but I'm making progress.
TL;DR It takes time and it can be confusing at first, but while it's a good game to play solo, it's a fantastic game to play with friends. I would give it an 8/10.

This game is must-have for people who like fast paced action games. Over the time since this was in beta, it has improved so so much. The bad reviews on this game are from people who don't like the learning curve, and the bugginess of the game in the past. Chivalry does indeed have a big learning curve to become really good at it, but seriously, the more you play the better you get.
Graphics for this game are amazing, and pretty demanding too. You're going to need a mid range or better graphics processor to max out the settings.
Gameplay is a great experience. You can have the most intense fight against your opponents and rise to the top of the player list, or you can constantly mash X2 to say "NO" while you run away from enemies. This game has made me laugh so hard because of the voice commands. I can be♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥if I get killed by some person, but then they say something like "You're welcome" or "The pleasure is all mine" and I can't even be mad. Now onto the few bad things about this game. Some aspects of the fighting are unrealistic, because some people choose to  use these dumb methods of fighting. For example, a knight is facing you and runs right infront of you, turns around, and swings overhead. You take full damage if you don't parry or block fast enough. There are a few other moves like this, but all of them are pretty easy to avoid. Keep your distance from a higher rank player (35-60) It's likely they'll use these moves effectively and put ya six feet under.
Anyway that's my review for Chivalry: Medieval Warfare. I play it all the time, because the community is so great and fun to interact with. I plan on playing for a long time (at least 1000 hours), and you should too. Reccommended game for sure

Almost every child loves dinosaurs, I was infatuated with them.
ARK brought back the days of having your friends over, building dirt and stick forts, making walls so the hungry meat eaters couldn't get in, using GI Joe figures to ride dinosaurs, kill the dinosaurs and have wars between forts.
This game brought back that fun imagination time when you were a wee lad.
Then you play the game.
As a player, you spend time leveling and gathering stuff so you can build a little starter base to store the goodies.  Playing with a friend or two, you can strategically choose what engrams will best help ya along.  You can spend an hour or two doing this, then real life comes along and back to reality and log off.
Now the fun part.  Remember you spent a couple of hours having a blast and taming one dinosaur, ya log back in, and you see the spawn screen.  All the good memories you had as a child just disappear once you respawn and get back to your base and see the walls blown open and your tame missing.  After four days of the exact same thing, the salt sets in and you must question yourself, is rebuilding really worth it?  Is this really any fun?
Even in other games, no one raids a 2x1, it's not worth it.
Should you not like this, the player community will suggest you play on a PvE server.  Well, that's not fun since taking your chances to engage the only animal that can kill from a distance is disabled.
Second option is to rent or host your own server to disable some of the options.  Two problems here.  Renting, the price is insane, hosting your own, you must create another steam account and buy the game and expansions again.
Third option that's recommended by the community is join a large tribe, well then your letting someone else dictate your imagination with the jobs they want you to complete.
TL;DR
The Sandbox is great, concept is awesome.  Having to play on a PvE or your own server and not getting the full game experience due to the bloody community, destroying thatch or wood 2x1's...not fun.
Is there a solution?  Probably not.  So, if you really want to play on an official PvP server, your expectations of playing alone or just with a few friends should be pretty low.  You will never progress in the game and eventually stop playing
These are just my experiences, and based on what I've seen and experienced, I really wish I only had two hours in the game.

Chivalry is the kind of game that is fairly easy to jump into, but has a lot more to it than you'd think.
First, I'll just describe it for you and then I'll share my thoughts on the game:
It's essentially a online multiplayer-only FPS with swords instead of guns. It's a class-based game, with 4 classes to choose from.
There are various gamemodes which you'll recognise if you've ever played games like TF2 or COD before. There's team objective mode, free-for-all, team deathmatch and last team standing modes, among others. Team Objective mode plays similarly to the payload or capture-the-point modes in TF2 in the sense that you run forward from your spawn, complete objective A, then your spawn moves forward, then you do objective B, etc.
Servers generally have a player limit of 32 players, 16 to each team, and the playerbase is quite large so you'll never have problems finding a server to join. There are plenty of "low-level" servers as well if you want a more noob-friendly place to play.
The actual mechanics are very straightforward. Fights consist of hacking and slashing at your enemy, parrying/blocking his attacks and trying not to die first. Or you can be an archer and pick them off from a distance. You can discover all the basic combat mechanics within a couple hours of playing because of how simple it is.
Let me just say this right now: you WILL die a lot at first and you will probably want to give up. There are players who have played for thousands of hours who will kill you over and over, leaving you frusrated and ready to ragequit.
Chivalry is the kind of game you can sink hours and hours into but never really "master". The mechanics are simple, yes, but it takes a lot of time to understand how to play well. There are only a few different types of attacks and the weapons all have the same basic mechanics to them, but it takes a lot of time to get a feel for when to start an attack, when to hold back, when to parry, etc. If you push through it, the game becomes very enjoyable.
I hope that gives you a basic idea of what the game is about. Now I'll put some of my own thoughts out:
As of writing this, I have played over 1000 hours over a span about a year and a half, and I don't regret it at all. It's one of the only games I don't think I will ever truly stop playing. The community is great, the combat never really gets old, and even after all this time I can't say I've gotten sick of it.
I can't say the game is 100% perfect though. The fact that the mechanics are so basic means that fighting higher-level players often boils down to who knows the most exploits. Any swing of a weapon can be parried to do no damage at all, and once you know how to parry the only way you can be hit is by luck, or you somehow screw it up, or the other persons feints to trick you into parrying early, but you can even learn to spot when someone is going to feint, so fighting can just end up swing, parry, swing, parry, swing, parry, etc, until one person slips up. This kind of combat doesn't rely on skill, it relies on one person misclicking and screwing up.
But that being said, even after >1000 hours of play-time I can't say I've really mastered the game. There are heaps of little tricks that people use to break away from the boring "swing, parry, swing, parry" combat which I'll probably never get the hang of, and it keeps me on edge whenever I'm playing.
So would I reccommend this game? Definitely. For all the hours I've spent (and enjoyed), It was definitely worth the ~$5 I paid for it when it was on sale one weekend. I'd probably have paid $50 or so if I'd known how good it was. Look up some videos on the internet of the kind of hijinks you get can up to and you'll see what I mean by how much fun you can have in this game.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare (CMW) is everything that it claims to be and more: "a fast paced medieval first person slasher". It is NOT a simulator. That being said, the mechanics are nothing short of impressive: the weight of the weapon in your hands, solid physics, and top notch sound effects—you really feel a jolt as the weight of your sword is blocked by an opponent's halberd, or the brutal (but oh so satisfying) crisp sound of you shearing off your opponent's head with a perfectly angled swing from your claymore, leaving his head tumbling down the stone steps in front of his slumped body. In a word: Epic.
And also hilarious.
There's something oddly humorous about this entire game. It doesn't take itself too seriously, and the numerous over-the-top voice commands, including screaming battle cries, condescending laughter, and taunts that would make Monty Python proud, make in-game interaction a real treat.
If you've never played a melee FPS before, I would say CMW is comparable to Counter-Strike 1.6 in terms of pacing and "excitement level", but is far more brutal, visceral, and in-your-face. If you are in any way competitive (and let's face it, most FPS gamers are), get ready to be shouting at your monitor in the beginning. You may even rage quit a few times. But it won't be out of frustration from the game itself, but from getting bested by a player who is better than you—and you know it. On the flip side, you'll be yelling in glee when the opposite happens: your opponent overconfidently rushes in with an overhead swing with a sword that's too heavy for his puny little girly arms, and you—gritting your teeth, holding your breath, and sweating profusely—riposte your sword off of his incoming strike in a fraction of a second and plunge 3 feet of cold steel clear through his chest. Victory is sweet.
Chivalry has given me countless hours of enjoyment because it is highly skill based and easy to jump in and out of. If you're busy, you can hop into a public server for 15 minutes to goof around and blow off some steam, or you can spend the better part of an afternoon playing through all of the objective-based maps and dueling high level players, who might just teach you a thing or two.
And finally, purely from a "consumer's point of view", you will get your money's worth from this game, especially if you buy it on sale. I only paid $15.00 for my copy, and Chivalry has given me over 800 hours of enjoyment. You'll notice that a lot of other reviewers here have similar playtimes or even longer. I even saw a negative review by a guy with over 1,000 hours (clearly written by someone who loves CMW so much that he "hates" it).
Simply put, CMW is real bang (clang?) for your buck.
