While ARK is a great concept, and it has a lot of great features, there are just too many issues to justify it being priced like it is. By aiming for that 60$ price point, it, by price association, gets classed with big name titles from big name studios. Compared to games from the likes of Square Enix, Blizzard, and Bethesda, Ark will always fall flat. If you insist on getting it, buy it on sale.
Ark is a fantastic example of an amazing concept gone wrong. Open world survivals are my kryptonite, so when I saw Ark, I knew I had to have it. I looked past all of the bugs and glitches and face-palm-worthy issues because I had so much fun with it. Unfortunately, the new wears off eventually, and rather than continually returning to it time and again with a smile (
), I found myself dreading each time I had an itch that only Ark could scratch.
I looked past its flaws because it was in early access. I knew it wasn't done, and I didn't care how long it took to get to a finished state as long as it made good on its goal of being an epic OWS (open world survival). It never made it there. There are still ridiculous issues, bugs still need to be fixed, performance still needs to be optimized, and yet, it has been released as a "finished" product. It's not.
I got Ark on sale last Christmas for super cheap(base game + scorched earth was like, 10$). I didn't mind paying for the dlc then, and I wouldn't mind paying for a dlc now, but Wildcard's pricing vs their game state is, well, stupid. Here's why:
1) well-done OWS. Hunger, thirst, temperatures, and clothing to combat the elements. Plants to forage from, things to hunt, and the option to self-sustain with your own crops.
2) decent tiers. higher tiers require more and more resources to damage, which adds value to more heavy-duty materials (like stone and metal).
3) dinosaurs. The element I never knew I wanted. Overall, I found I actually enjoyed their presence, which I honestly didn't think would happen.

This game is designed in every way to infuriate you. There's no other way to describe this game besides 100+ GB of sadism. I've played a lot of games in my life, and I can say almost without exaggerating that if I wanted to maintain any form of mental health I'd rather play any of those other game than this one. This game has made me throw my $100 pair of headphones more than any other game, made me utter more foul curses in a louder tone of voice, and made me stay up until 5:00AM swearing to myself that I'd never forgive my brother (sorry brother, I blame it on Ark.)
The game is made to be just fun enough that you think playing it's a good idea, and so that you'll get attached to your dinosaurs, but before you know it the game will ♥♥♥♥ you in the♥♥♥♥♥and kill those dinosaurs, in fact, if you want your dinosaurs to stay alive the only way you could guarantee their safety is to put them in a metal box with another wall around it and two sets of doors so you can make sure no small animals can get into their room behind you when you go in to feed them, and yes, you need to feed your dinosaurs or they will starve to death (though on PVE servers they don't starve while you're offline I think.)
So if you like the idea of spending up to seven hours taming a dinosaur, (not including gathering materials,) naming them, living side by side with them for weeks and getting attached to them, only to have them die because you accidentally let a single ant into your base and didn't set your dino to auto attack, (possibly because your dino has so much AOE that if he attacks he'll kill every other dino in your base,) then you're a massochist and this game is made just for you.
And that's just talking about the DESIGN of the game, I'm not even including glitches, horrible oversights, things I hope are errors, etc.. For example ny time anything important happens, there's a 50% the server will have a several second lag spike: I can't tell you how many times I've lagged and when the spike stopped I had one or more dinosaurs eating me, or I've lagged while outrunning a dinosaur only to have it catch up to me by the time the lag ended, or had lag make me misplace an object so I have to destroy and remake it. One time I actually lost a dinosaur because the game glitched me off of it mid flight and dumped me into a swamp full of giant snakes and I died, the game is just that poorly made.
Another example of poor game creation is that any flying companion will likely fly above the draw distance after you die if it's following you, and that's if you're lucky: if you're unlucky it will fly to some random part of the map and sit there until it starves to death or is killed potentially weeks later, 'cause apparently your character is too dumb to train animals to return home. Even if you're super lucky and a flying animal doesn't fly above draw distance, you can't count yourself too lucky yet because it might still be out of range for whistling and you'll still need a flying mount to recover it.
One of the "best" features of the game is that it feels like the world was designed by a twelve year old due to the fact that it's so densely populated that you're almost always within a meter of at least one animal. Furthermore, carnivores for some reason rarely ever attack other animals, but they will go to the ends of the earth to try to kill you. It's common to see an area populated with a dozen carnivores and a dozen herbivores all just hanging out, but heaven forbid you walk near them 'cause if you do all of those carnivores will suddenly remember they eat meat and won't stop chasing you for half a mile.
And you might think, "Well that's all well and good my fellow reviewer, but what if I don't care about dinosaurs that much and I just want to build things or explore?" Well let me tell you, I initially didn't want to tame dinos either, but if you want to do either of those things you're♥♥♥♥♥♥out of luck as well. If you just want to build things, then you better have a perfect understanding of spatial relations and be good at abusing the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of glitches, 'cause you can't do much of anything interesting without both of those. For example, if you want to build a shack or a wall on uneven ground you're♥♥♥♥♥♥out of luck if you want it at all level, that is, unless you're willing to look up the dumb♥♥♥♥♥♥you need to go through to glitch the game into making something that vaguely resembles what you want. I'd try to explain the process of, for example, building a wall with a level top on a hill, but it's so dumb I don't know if I could do it in text.
. . . and if you want to explore? Good luck. You can't walk half a mile without an extremely high chance of encountering something you won't be able to fight as a human. If you actually want to cover a significant distance on foot be prepared to spend at least ten lives and a few hours doing it, and I don't know what you're expecting to do once you get to your destination but you'll probably die instead and you sure as hell don't have good chances making it back to your base. If you actually want to explore you either A. need to tame a flyer, but this doesn't really work 'cause you're so far up, probably above the treeline, that you can't see anything, and if you're not that high you could always just be killed by some random creature *COUGH*THYLACOLEO*COUGH* that can jump out of the tops of trees and basically kill you instantly or some random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t ('cause we all know cats can jump ten meters off of the top of a redwood and grab you off of a pteradon as it flies at immense speeds through the air, right?) or B. you could spend enough time on the wikis and youtube that you manage to tame several large dinos, say T-Rexes, but by that point you will almost certainly know enough about the game and the world that you don't care about exploring anyway.
And don't even get me started on trying to learn the game, 'cause there's no tutorial or guide. If you want to play this game without looking up on wiki and YT how to do anything you're basically ♥♥♥♥ed. It was a while ago, so I don't totally remember, but I spent probably an hour dying repeatedly from starving, freezing, overheating, and dehydration before I had even a basic grasp of how to gather resources and how to craft items. Do: Play this game if you don't want to have a life.
Don't: Play this game if you want to have a life.
So what's the verdict?
Good concept, poor execution. A half-and-half smorgasbord of good and bad with good PR marred by poor design choices. Interface issues, balance issues and the like all take a while to be meaningfully resolved, and "reworks" don't make things much better.
Although the game is gradually improving, you will find that the only real content it has is of a grindy nature.
If you like that, go right ahead: the community is (mostly) helpful, so it's a good place for making friends, and it is very fun to grind overall for a lot of time. You're just gonna burn out eventually.
If you're looking for a deeply challenging or skill-taxing experience, or something that's content-rich in a meaningful way, steer clear, 'cause the smooth graphics, impressive art-style and flashy (yet horribly balanced) combat are just there to distract you from the fact that you're just going through the motions.
Edit: I guess dressing up is pretty fun after all. All of the problems above still stand, though.

This game said you can do something I always dreamed of doing in a game: Taming massive beasts, with a relatively in-depth system, breeding, individual stats, the whole thing. In fact, that seemed to be the focus of the game. So of course I bought. Only later did I discover that stronger dinos can literally take over a day to tame. I never even went on to the official servers, because I knew from the start how terrible and toxic they were.However, I thought I'd be safe on a private server with a decent owner. There's only problem: The "decent" people on the servers still had virtually no life, and will judge you very harshly if you can not spend 12 or more hours a day in game. People will hunt for bases, and will wait until the few hours when all the tribe members of said base(s) are asleep, then they will outwit your incredibly idiotic dinosaurs, and when you log on in the morning, most of your dinosaurs will be dead, and likely half of your base will be missing. If you live alone, or in a small tribe, the raiders might not even bother waiting until you go offline. Of course, if your tribe is actually keeping up with everyone else on the server, then there will be very few times with no one on, because your tribe members will be taking watches to watch over the dinosaurs you will be trying to tame 24/7. Because yes, it can take over 16 hours to tame a dino. If you can't spend that much time, then you will have to deal with your increasingly insulting tribe members until they kick you for not being hardcore enough. At this point, you should've realized that they all live in their mother's basements, so you really can't compete. Of course, if you choose to go it alone, or form a tribe with some friends who also have lives outside of this game, You will enjoy a day (or an entire two, if you're really lucky) of building, leveling, and trying to tame dinos before logging on the next morning to find... I know I wrote this somewhere... Oh here: "most of your dinosaurs will be dead, and likely half of your base will be missing".
TLDR: Do not buy, unless you live in your mother's basement, and want to play with others in the same situation who think of themselves as "hardcore".
EDIT: Oh wait, the game is $60 now?!? It wasn't worth it at $20 or 30, and it's not like they've actually added anything really good since then. Sure, they added 20-30 new species, most of which use the exact same ai, and almost exactly the same attacks, but it's not like they've actually added new mechanics, or expanded your options in the game enough to justify doubling the price. In fact, I'd still consider this game alpha.

Me personally, I love the concept and ideas of this game. But I do have many things I don't like about this game. If anyone is considering purchasing this game and reading through the reviews (some people do) and want to know more about this game then I can give my thoughts on the game. This is just my humble opinion and some people will disagree with me on some points, but everyone is entitled to their own opinion.
This game used to be a lot cheaper then it is now, rougly £14.99 or roughly $20 for those Americans out there. But now the developers of this game have decided to up the price on steam to £49.99 or roughly $65 which in my opinion would be a perfectly valid thing to do if the game didn't have the following flaws that I will mention later. For most people the current price seems like a massive rip off as not everyone has money just sitting around not doing anything and people who were going to get the game because of the price may not be inclined to do so anymore.
There is a lot to say about the performance and utilization of hardware to run this game. It states under the minimum system requirements that a NVIDIA GTX 670 2GB/AMD Radeon HD 7870 2GB or better and an Intel Core i5-2400/AMD FX-8320 or better will run this game (not very well) and while that may be the case, good luck running this above 30fps on that. I recently upgraded from a GTX 960 2GB to a GTX 1060 6GB and I hope to test run that on this game to get a better understanding of just what will actually run this game properly and smoothly, seeing as the store page does not specify any recommended specs. When I had my old GTX 960 I could not run this game on anything above 'Medium' Preset without dropping down to around 15-25 fps. So for those of you who are using mid spec PC's will most likely not be able to run it.

[Review update - 12/09/2017]
I have changed my thoughts about this game from No to Yes and you will see why if you continue to read, if the previous points have already put you off the game then I'm sorry about that, but I'm being honest here.
So I've had some time to review this game more in-depth and would of updated this review sooner, but I had pc issues for a week or 2 which stopped me from updating this. However, some of my previous points I have made about this game, have changed.
I mentioned that the price was quite unfair for this game, that still kind of stands but I have gained about 25+ hours over the last few days before updating this review, and I found that it was a lot of fun with a friend, I personally like modded servers better then vanilla because there isn't as much grinding, and I know that grinding for good stuff is half the fun, but I enjoy laid back experience on this game as opposed to one where you're worried about losing all your stuff and it taking ages to get back if you can't recover it. I play on a x20 Ragnarok server (Ragnarok is the map name for those of you who don't know) and it's great fun playing with my friend because it's not you just sat there by yourself doing everything solo which can get quite boring, but I do know people who prefer to play these games solo, which there's nothing wrong with. I would say this game is still a bit expensive but if you do have the money or you can save for it, then I would buy it. However if you don't want to pay the full retail price, there is a site that you can use that is 100% safe and secure with great customer support if in the unlikely event that your transaction were to fail, use
Outside:
This game is heavily packed with content,, dinos to tame, loot to collect, areas to explore, bases to build, bosses to beat. All of which is very well structured and very do-able in either vanilla or modded servers. The mods are very extensive as ARK Survival Evolved's community is very dedicated and want to help improve the game in any way they can. I personally love taking my wyvern (Basically a dragon) into the wild to tame dinos and then for it to pick it up and fly it back to my base and add it to the collection. The difficulty of the dinos will vary depending on if the server is a modded server, in which case the wild dinos will be anywhere from level 300 to 3500, where as in vanilla (I haven't really played vanilla enough to know this that well) are probably lower then that meaning that the difficulty will match the server/singleplayer save very nicely so it's not too easy and not too hard, which I like about this game because it offers a fair challenge.
Should you buy this game?
Yes, if you don't mind the price and willing to accept that the performance isn't great on some machines.
Should you play modded or vanilla servers?
It's all down to personal preference, if you like grinding and being carefull with your dinos and loot, then go for vanilla. If you like a laid back but hectic battles and being very powerfull, then go for a modded x5, x10, x20 server depending on which you like the sound of most.
Will you get bored of this game quickly?
Well, some people can spend just a few days playing games where as some people can put thousands of hours into them, it's all down to if you're comitted to the game and want to play it. If you think you will get bored or you are unsure if you should get it, watch some gameplay on youtube because there's some things a review can't give, like gameplay.
Is it worth the money?
Yes and no. I am not sure why the full retail price is so expensive but it is worth the money if you love working for the best stuff, this game is very similar to Rust but with about 70+ layers of content on top of it.

Well, I have been playing for a looooooong time with this game, so here are my toughts on it:
1) It has bugs. Lots and lots of bugs. Some of them get fixed in an update, some of them stay in the game for a month or two. If you wanna play this game you have to take this into concideration.
2) It is an amazing experience. Fighting, goofing around, surviving with your friends is awsome. If you decide to buy this game and play with it with some friends you can watch your little thach house, that can be destroyed by a Rex in half a minute, turn into a gigantic fortress, with autoturrets, metal walls, tons of dinos (literaly), forges, loot rooms, etc. You can watch as your character goes from being a stranded naked guy with a stone pick turn into a god, with TEK powersuit, laser guns, and about 20 imprinted rexes raised by you and your tribe.
3) If you are planing on playing on an official PvP server, best luck to you sir, I salute you. You see in PvP in the ARK every server has a hierarchy. The "Alpha tribe", the tribe who is the strongest on the server, decides who dies and who lives. It will take countless hours and dedication to stand your ground on one of these servers, and you will probably lose it to a random tribe who just happens to be curious what could be behind your walls. The Official servers are nuts.
4) Be prepared to lose everything. Yes, I mean everything. Your tribe can be raided at any time, even if you are in school or work. You will have to begin anew again and again. Each time you will learn what not to do, and go further than before.  That is the essence of ARK.
5) Have fun. I have to recommend it. It is the best game I've ever played (excluding maybe WoW).

This game said you can do something I always dreamed of doing in a game: Taming massive beasts, with a relatively in-depth system, breeding, individual stats, the whole thing. In fact, that seemed to be the focus of the game. So of course I bought. Only later did I discover that stronger dinos can literally take over a day to tame. I never even went on to the official servers, because I knew from the start how terrible and toxic they were.However, I thought I'd be safe on a private server with a decent owner. There's only problem: The "decent" people on the servers still had virtually no life, and will judge you very harshly if you can not spend 12 or more hours a day in game. People will hunt for bases, and will wait until the few hours when all the tribe members of said base(s) are asleep, then they will outwit your incredibly idiotic dinosaurs, and when you log on in the morning, most of your dinosaurs will be dead, and likely half of your base will be missing. If you live alone, or in a small tribe, the raiders might not even bother waiting until you go offline. Of course, if your tribe is actually keeping up with everyone else on the server, then there will be very few times with no one on, because your tribe members will be taking watches to watch over the dinosaurs you will be trying to tame 24/7. Because yes, it can take over 16 hours to tame a dino. If you can't spend that much time, then you will have to deal with your increasingly insulting tribe members until they kick you for not being hardcore enough. At this point, you should've realized that they all live in their mother's basements, so you really can't compete. Of course, if you choose to go it alone, or form a tribe with some friends who also have lives outside of this game, You will enjoy a day (or an entire two, if you're really lucky) of building, leveling, and trying to tame dinos before logging on the next morning to find... I know I wrote this somewhere... Oh here: "most of your dinosaurs will be dead, and likely half of your base will be missing".
TLDR: Do not buy, unless you live in your mother's basement, and want to play with others in the same situation who think of themselves as "hardcore".
EDIT: Oh wait, the game is $60 now?!? It wasn't worth it at $20 or 30, and it's not like they've actually added anything really good since then. Sure, they added 20-30 new species, most of which use the exact same ai, and almost exactly the same attacks, but it's not like they've actually added new mechanics, or expanded your options in the game enough to justify doubling the price. In fact, I'd still consider this game alpha.

Me personally, I love the concept and ideas of this game. But I do have many things I don't like about this game. If anyone is considering purchasing this game and reading through the reviews (some people do) and want to know more about this game then I can give my thoughts on the game. This is just my humble opinion and some people will disagree with me on some points, but everyone is entitled to their own opinion.
This game used to be a lot cheaper then it is now, rougly £14.99 or roughly $20 for those Americans out there. But now the developers of this game have decided to up the price on steam to £49.99 or roughly $65 which in my opinion would be a perfectly valid thing to do if the game didn't have the following flaws that I will mention later. For most people the current price seems like a massive rip off as not everyone has money just sitting around not doing anything and people who were going to get the game because of the price may not be inclined to do so anymore.
There is a lot to say about the performance and utilization of hardware to run this game. It states under the minimum system requirements that a NVIDIA GTX 670 2GB/AMD Radeon HD 7870 2GB or better and an Intel Core i5-2400/AMD FX-8320 or better will run this game (not very well) and while that may be the case, good luck running this above 30fps on that. I recently upgraded from a GTX 960 2GB to a GTX 1060 6GB and I hope to test run that on this game to get a better understanding of just what will actually run this game properly and smoothly, seeing as the store page does not specify any recommended specs. When I had my old GTX 960 I could not run this game on anything above 'Medium' Preset without dropping down to around 15-25 fps. So for those of you who are using mid spec PC's will most likely not be able to run it.

[Review update - 12/09/2017]
I have changed my thoughts about this game from No to Yes and you will see why if you continue to read, if the previous points have already put you off the game then I'm sorry about that, but I'm being honest here.
So I've had some time to review this game more in-depth and would of updated this review sooner, but I had pc issues for a week or 2 which stopped me from updating this. However, some of my previous points I have made about this game, have changed.
I mentioned that the price was quite unfair for this game, that still kind of stands but I have gained about 25+ hours over the last few days before updating this review, and I found that it was a lot of fun with a friend, I personally like modded servers better then vanilla because there isn't as much grinding, and I know that grinding for good stuff is half the fun, but I enjoy laid back experience on this game as opposed to one where you're worried about losing all your stuff and it taking ages to get back if you can't recover it. I play on a x20 Ragnarok server (Ragnarok is the map name for those of you who don't know) and it's great fun playing with my friend because it's not you just sat there by yourself doing everything solo which can get quite boring, but I do know people who prefer to play these games solo, which there's nothing wrong with. I would say this game is still a bit expensive but if you do have the money or you can save for it, then I would buy it. However if you don't want to pay the full retail price, there is a site that you can use that is 100% safe and secure with great customer support if in the unlikely event that your transaction were to fail, use
Outside:
This game is heavily packed with content,, dinos to tame, loot to collect, areas to explore, bases to build, bosses to beat. All of which is very well structured and very do-able in either vanilla or modded servers. The mods are very extensive as ARK Survival Evolved's community is very dedicated and want to help improve the game in any way they can. I personally love taking my wyvern (Basically a dragon) into the wild to tame dinos and then for it to pick it up and fly it back to my base and add it to the collection. The difficulty of the dinos will vary depending on if the server is a modded server, in which case the wild dinos will be anywhere from level 300 to 3500, where as in vanilla (I haven't really played vanilla enough to know this that well) are probably lower then that meaning that the difficulty will match the server/singleplayer save very nicely so it's not too easy and not too hard, which I like about this game because it offers a fair challenge.
Should you buy this game?
Yes, if you don't mind the price and willing to accept that the performance isn't great on some machines.
Should you play modded or vanilla servers?
It's all down to personal preference, if you like grinding and being carefull with your dinos and loot, then go for vanilla. If you like a laid back but hectic battles and being very powerfull, then go for a modded x5, x10, x20 server depending on which you like the sound of most.
Will you get bored of this game quickly?
Well, some people can spend just a few days playing games where as some people can put thousands of hours into them, it's all down to if you're comitted to the game and want to play it. If you think you will get bored or you are unsure if you should get it, watch some gameplay on youtube because there's some things a review can't give, like gameplay.
Is it worth the money?
Yes and no. I am not sure why the full retail price is so expensive but it is worth the money if you love working for the best stuff, this game is very similar to Rust but with about 70+ layers of content on top of it.

Over my last couple years of playing, first on pc, then on xbox, then back to pc, I have encountered a multitude of victories and failures. This game was headed for greatness when it first released and honestly could still see greatnesss and amass many new players if not for WildCards main problem. WildCard as many experienced ARK players will attest to, is the fact that Wildcard rarely listens to their dedicated player base when imposing new things or even fixing various problems within the game. For the last couple of years I've seen a lot of bugs come and go but the one thing that still remains is the poor server connection that plagues multiple servers that wildcard fails to address. They'll say something to drive oblivous or naive gamers into being content but for those of us who put in considerable time it's hard to ignore the fact that these server issues still exist. The average ping on my server for the last 4 months has held itself at 255+ ping failry consistently with small breaks every now and again of a reasonable 50 ping. I will note that trying to play this game on 255+ ping will drive the average person to madness. If you however can deal with the small bugs thst still exist I would recommend getting the game, just stay to the original map as it's the DLC that tends to suffer from the netwrok issues.
TLDR:
Great Game, not worth 60$, wait for a sale and pick it up. I purchased this game for 15$ and I would say I more than got my money out of this game but 60$ is insane support for a company that pushes it's playerbase to the backburner.

Chivalry is a really fun game in my opinion. Granted the path to victory in this game is piled high with your own corpse and the bodies of your fallen comrades that you just accidentally killed. This game will feel brutal and cheap until you figure out how to fight like a real man. After learning to fight with one weapon you'll gain access to a few more, allowing you to pick and choose what killing tool to bring to the battlefield. You can also dress yourself up and change your appearance too.
This game can feel like hell alone, but with teamwork you can be an unstoppable force. Objective based modes feel the most fun, despite many matches turning into straight up brawls instead of someone trying to acheive the objective.
A big point to keep in mind about this game is to make sure to have a decent computer and a good internet connection. Lag kill, literally. Having a good framerate and connection can be crucial to your success in this game, failure to having either will result in you never killing and only ever getting killed.

In terms of free to play content, Warframe has a lot to offer. The combat system is fast paced and the lack of a cover system really aids the feeling of intensity. Along with some parkour mechanics and a bit of melee, Warframe's combat is a blast.
There are many different types of playable "warframes", and from the ones i tried, each feels unique. There's even missions set in space, that introduce a whole bunch of new mechanics, and for the first 10+ hours, warframe is a joy to play. Unfortunatley however, it is around this time the game begins showing its "Free to Play" side. While it's true that pretty much all items (besides cosmetics) can be had for free, it is often behind a ridiculous grind wall.
Yes you can trade, but unless sitting in a chat for an hour copying and pasting the same message over and over until someone replies is your idea of a fun gaming experience, this is of little help, though i can imagine this being better in a clan. The truth is, this game expects you to spend an unreasonable amount of time on it, though it is possible you may enjoy the game so much that this is fine for you.
Overall, i will return to warframe now and then, since there is still enjoyment to be had from it, but i'd definitley rather spend a few dollars during a steam sale and buy a game that doesn't drip feed me to keep me hooked.

Possibly one of the best F2P games on the market, it doesn't really force you to partake in microtransactions, but you do end up having to wait around a lot between quests and things. This game is crafting oriented, and it takes time to craft things you really want or need. My experience went a lot like this:
A friend asked me to download this game for a long while, and I never really got around to it fearing it was going to not be that engaging or simply just a low quality F2P game from some developer I've never even heard of. (Oh, was I wrong.)
After downloading it and trying it, I ended up feeling neutral about the whole thing. The entire game just has so much to take in from gameplay, graphics, and lore. It all starts to make a lot more sense around mastery rank 3, which is a little ways into the game. I started to love it as I progressed through more levels and continued on to MR6. I'm only MR8, and there's still a lot I need to learn, especially after the update that removed void keys, but I'm making progress.
TL;DR It takes time and it can be confusing at first, but while it's a good game to play solo, it's a fantastic game to play with friends. I would give it an 8/10.

Do: Play this game if you don't want to have a life.
Don't: Play this game if you want to have a life.
So what's the verdict?
Good concept, poor execution. A half-and-half smorgasbord of good and bad with good PR marred by poor design choices. Interface issues, balance issues and the like all take a while to be meaningfully resolved, and "reworks" don't make things much better.
Although the game is gradually improving, you will find that the only real content it has is of a grindy nature.
If you like that, go right ahead: the community is (mostly) helpful, so it's a good place for making friends, and it is very fun to grind overall for a lot of time. You're just gonna burn out eventually.
If you're looking for a deeply challenging or skill-taxing experience, or something that's content-rich in a meaningful way, steer clear, 'cause the smooth graphics, impressive art-style and flashy (yet horribly balanced) combat are just there to distract you from the fact that you're just going through the motions.
Edit: I guess dressing up is pretty fun after all. All of the problems above still stand, though.

I have a little over 1k hours on this game in EA and as I have read in a lot of reviews already the mere fact that WC took a dump on its seasoned players on legacy servers is very dissapointing.  Prior to full release i enjoyed the game greatly even with all its flaws for pc gaming. (i.e. rendering large scale bases with high dino pop)  I played on an official pve server and my tribe became alpha and most progressed on the server.  After seeing the list of server wipes and our SE server along with allies of ours Rag and Se servers being wiped it was very upsetting, upsetting enough for a lot of us to never want to play again after losing so much time invested in dinos and wyverns on other servers.  To top it off WC saying that legacy servers will no longer recieve tech support just made things worse.
The overall concept to this game is genious and is what truly brought me to play this game.  The difficulty to survive when starting made the thrill that much rewarding especially when fending of Allo's or Rexs when your only lvl 50 fighting from a window in a stone structure.  The breeding was probably the most exciting part of the game.  To make it so realistic almost as if your raising something in real life with the imprinting and feeding was very daunting but at the same time it gave a sense of achievement when you got the best stats you can possibly get post imprinting.  (Like a basilo i raised to 430% melee 20k health pre imprint and 480% melee 25k health post).  With imprint bonus and those stats i ran east water cave solo fighting 3 Alpha megalodons simulataneously along with dunkleo's and other megalodons.
Overall a fun and enjoyable game just wish WC had taken better care of its seasoned EA players, and allowed more time for transferring to new servers before the wipes.  Giving us 5 days to transfer hundreds of dinos, when there is irl things happeing such as work, school, family, etc, is un realistic and almost impossible for smaller seasoned tribes.  Especially considering they would most likely have to start a whole new base to store these dinos.  To those seasoned EA players that continue to play  hats off to you and good luck.  And to the new players I hope you get the same enjoyment I got and hopefully wont have to deal with a server wipe in your future.

I personally do very much enjoy the game.
At first I didn't. One of the biggest things was FPS issues. Don't be an idiot like me and have these really nice graphics but forsake gameplay. The gameplay really is very fun, and you can't let looks stop you.
Next off, one of the things I do enjoy about this game is that each class is different, and has a different playstyle. Would you like to be a knight? Lots of health and a few nice shields, and you'll be able to take a few hits, but nowhere as strong as the vanguard, and nowhere as close as able to avoid attacks as a man-at-arms. Like to run in swinging, dealing as much damage as possible, with little to no regard to your own safety? Take a vanguard.
The man-at-arms and archer both feel a bit underpowered for me, a little weak, if you will. First off, archers are slow, but have low health, low armour, are incredibly weak at anywhere close to short range, and distance can be closed in moments. While they do apparently do more damage if they can stab someone in the back, no one plays a sneaky type character on this game because they are utterly ineffective, as you can see someone twenty miles away, and if they have to approach head on and try to get around to the others' back, they can't move quick enough to do so. They should bemade slightly faster, because of all their other cons.
The man-at-arms just has low health and low offensive capabilities. Make it so that they have one or the other - The inability to be anything more than a nuisance, is, to me, stupid. Their shields don't count for much, and their famous fire pots can only be used once. Please, make it so these guys actually stand a chance. Shouldn't be that I can literally rush in with a vanguard or knight and absolutely dominate 4 or 5 of these guys and take little to no significant damage.
All in all, a good game that GENERALLY rewards you for skill.

You know, I like this game.  Deep down, there's nothing more fun that shouting aloud and running into the fray.  However, I had to agree with others that this game seems to have been produced, popped out and quickly forgotten by the devs.  For example -- there has been a bug that shows all servers as full that has been around for at least two months, when they are maybe at half capacity.  I would think 2 months should be enough time to fix this.
Specifically for the DLC -- If you liked the original Chivalry, then you'll probably get a kick out of this well enough, though  I would not purchase it for more than 5 bucks.  If you never played the original, then you may be frustrated pretty quick as the game does have a learning curve.  However, there are balance issues among the various classes that can lead to that added contempt.  Also, there are playstyle issues (example: using 3rd person and high mouse sensitivity) that allows people to move their player models in unnatural ways, making it less of a move/counter/riposte sort of fight and more of a fight of who can spin their screen faster.
So all-in-all, I wouldn't recommend this game unless you really enjoy the style.  For the average gamer, take your money to some of the other games out there.

This game is potentially one of my favorite competitive games that I've played in a while. Dismembering your foes in this game is extremely satisfying. Each class in game has a different playstyle, so you have to change the ways you fight when you meet them. An example would be if you came across an Archer, you could probably just swing wildy if they had their bow out before they could react. If you tried the same thing on a Man at Arms, he could probably dodge your attack and lunge at you after you swung so you couldn't block. Blocking in this game is quite easy and not hard to use like Mount and Blade: Warband's blocking system. (Although I do like that game.) There are a variety of different gamemodes to suit different types of players. These gamemodes are King of the Hill, Last Team Standing, Team Deathmatch, Free For All, Duel, Capture the Flag, and Team Objective, which has you doing certain objectives according to your team and the map. While the base game is fun in it's own, the Deadliest Warrior DLC adds so much to the game class-wise. Instead of fighting as just medieval warriors, you can fight as 6 different classes, all from different time periods and regions. There is a Samurai, Spartan, Viking, Ninja, Pirate, and Knight, as well as their class specific weapons. The normal game, with only the four classes Man at Arms, Vanguard, Knight, and Archer, had much less variety than this DLC. So if you have played Warband's fighting system, than this might be a good game for you, and I recommend everyone else to try this game out and see if you like it.

This game may seem like a dream come true. A medieval-style Battlefield game. Endless hordes of footsoldiers charging a stronghold; arrows flying; blood and glorious combat every direction you look. something straight out of Stronghold Crusader. And this game certainly has some of that. The combat system is heavily skill-based and well done for the most part. Surprisingly, the pinnicle of this game is the battlecries- extremely well done and hallarious. However, this game just feels like it's not as big as it could be. You will participate in a charge of maybe a large squad of 12 soliders, but not a small army of 30 (at least not on any servers i played on). There are large battles, but not enormous ones. And also, another minor complaint is the maps. They may get repetitive after a while. The glorious charges and whatnot can eventually become slightly predictable. I only recommend this game with an almost reluctant 7.5/10, only due to the slightly disapointing replay value. With friends, 8/10. If you aren't in a rush to chop off some heads, maybe wait for a sale. If you are, then please go ahead and yell out some battlecries. Or wicked laughs. Or taunts.

First off i wanna say is that the idea to make a game like this was awesome. The Dinos,The terrain, The weather effects,Water, etc were just truly amazing. Everything about the game in terms of content has been spectacular.

2) Secondly, and i feel this issue every Ark gamer has is the optimization issue! The optimization is just pathetic! My 2015 version of this game looks much better than the updated 2017 version! So are they actually improving the game or are they destrying it deliberatly? No Idea!
So to conclude,
If you're looking for a game jam-packed with content,Fantastic scenery and lovely dinos to see,,, but the only problem is that it working on a broken engine, don't wait a second longer, BUY IT NOW!!!

I've thought long and hard about this.  I love this game.  I own multiple servers (Grakor) and have thousands of hours.  I'm actually a little embarrassed about the time I've spent.  I enjoy every minute, but the fact is I've had to adjust the game (vis a vie my own server) to make it playable.
Problem is, and I truly hate to say this, the game isn't finished.  The optimization is bad.  They've finally dropped all pretense of using Windows 10 DirectX, which is honest but not a good thing.  (Full disclosure, I only have Win7 anyway, but it is the attitude I'm addressing here).  I have a massive rig (multi SLI Nvidia), and I still get lag just by turning around.  Graphics are great, but at a performance price.  And in this instance, there is a very very steep grade to the quality settings.  Even a minor reduction effects things exponentially.  Simply put, their reach exceeded their grasp.
This game is not a AAA title, as it currently sits.  The DLC is not worth the cost, and they've messed over the long-time pre-release audience with the marketing.  I truly hope they continue to expand and improve, and there is no real reason to think they won't, but the industry is generally not heading that way so I find it hard to be positive.  When you consider the "other release" that is basically a copy of ARK, but with Magic, I'm just not overly hopeful.
On the positive, the concept is terrific.  Riding and taming dinosaurs?  Really?  OMG!  As always, improvements can be made of course.  We can disagree about some of the direction and whether WC has gone astray with something here or there.  Choices were made, and you can't fault them for that.  But the overall direction is great.
On the negative, the stock servers are not acceptable unless you are used to a Half-Life type situation.  You just can't play the game because of the time required to learn the necessary skills and tame the dinos you need to be successful.  Playing PVP is virtually impossible because of the huge advantages groups have over servers.  If you insist on playing ARK (and I frankly wouldn't blame you if you did) and are too stubborn to heed the warnings, then be sure you are playing on a modded server that shortens the time required to make this a functional experience (or just quit your job and play full time, which I recommend but is undoubtedly unfeasible).
Bottom line, wait a while.  I hope in a just a couple months I can upgrade this recommendation to be more positive.  I truly believe WC allowed circumstance and scope creep to overwhelm their production schedule.  I only hope they will hold out long enough to fix the mess they've created and expand the ARK universe to something long lasting.

Now that the game is released and official I won't feel bad going all out with this.
TL;DR
ARK didn't deliver on the hype, and very thinly met on it's promises. It's selling double the price for what is barely the game. And it suffers no more (Sometimes MUCH more) than any other game in the Survival-Building-OpenWorld-Shooter genre set.
It's better you save your money. Unless you have friends to help, unless you have more money to spend on a private server, unless you have a lot of patience, or unless you absolutely cannot find another game that fits your desires for entertainment.
But if you cannot resist buying this game because it's 'the only one of it's kind', I think you're in the exact trap the devs want. And they know it. Why else raise a price on a mixed reviews game?
---For More Detail:---
For starters, the game fails to achieve what we first heard (And continue to be told) the game would be about. ARK is a game about dinosaurs and survival that hopes to put you to scale with a thriving prehistoric world with building elements and interactions between players. I was hoping that much like the trailers I too would be part of a thriving community of players participating in events in this theme.
Instead what I found was a odd game. Character customization feels like a joke, moreso than say Dark Souls. At least with Dark Souls you can viably CHOOSE if you want to be a grotesque horror with cartoonish proportions or a actual human being with meaningful customization. (In fact, Dark Souls has the ability for both quite well. Monster characters are hilarious and outright unreal while the system still allows you to make meaningful and delightfully varied Roleplay characters.) ARK doesn't let you do this nearly as much as it lets you become some freakish vaguely human creature thing. It doesn't feel finished, and that carries on well outside of the character creator.
Gameplay suffers from many of the problems of the Four Horsemen of the Apocolypse Survival-Shooter-Openworld-Builder genre. Guns exist but are hard enough to come by that a small group can grief a whole server and deny everyone time to build and catch up. Survival is a joke in some cases and as simple as walking up to a open water source and pressing the interact button and that's the entire worry for dehydration covered; It is implied more that players and dinosaurs are a threat but with dinosaurs being run by particularly butchered dumb AI the only real threat is players and that just makes the game feel like a terrible idea for a indefinite arena-shooter.
I feel like the only purpose this game serves is not to actually be a fun game, but to be the game you -have- to play if you have specific desires. Dinosaurs are a niche that some people can't find in other games, certainly none as popular. Survival is not uncommon but ARK gained popularity enough that most people feel to indebted to it to try others that aren't as strong in playerbase. The world building aspect is a curse that few games have pulled off well and ARK doesn't either, but the point is that it 'may be one of the best' which in this case is to have base building even mean anything.
I don't get to play as the guy that rides a dinosaur with his clansmate in this game, and when I do its so brief that by the time you realize you might be there the world wipes you clear off the map and starts you right off from scratch; Whether it be a enemy clan or other misfortune. This game is a great despairity between having fun and not having fun, and the having fun in this game doesn't feel valuable enough. This game costs more frustration to play then it gives happiness, and that's counter to what a game should be. I'm all for games making me work for my reward, as some of the greatest games are all about the massive payoff whether it be ingame or from personal "Awww yeasssss!" But in this game it takes a certain kind of person to justify retrying again and again and again and again just to succeed in a ideal they likely had to compromise for because the game isn't built to allow for what they really wanted. (Example: Building a private farm with massive walls, a task made difficult by hostile neighbors and limited resources. The reward is just pulling it off, when you really wanted to make it public and create or join a town. But you can't, because doing so has costed you several farms before and you need to spend money on walls because the enemy will offline raid you if you don't.)

Clicker heroes is the game you play while playing other, better games ( ACap's line, yeah I know). But then, that's what all Idle games are. The game is rarely fun for extended periods of time, but it makes up for it by being strangely satisfying to open up first or second thing in the morning. Nothing like finding out you have 98 octovigintillion gold to get your day going, eh? no one? Okay.
You can't go wrong with Clicker Heroes (it is free after all!), and it gets strangely addictive over time. It scales infinitely, so you never get bored either. It's basically the same thing, day after day, apart from improving your heroes and seeing a different letter after the huge number at the top of your screen, but it
. The initial setup clicking and bossfights aside, Clicker Heroes plays itself. All you do is watch as the goons you hire beat up stronger monsters.
And that's basically it. Hire peeps, fight monsters. Fight tougher monsters, hire new peeps. Run out of peeps to hire, ascend the world and start all over again.

And in that way, it's like a drug. You feel terrible for enjoying it, but you love it to bits anyway.  You need your daily shot of Clicker, and you need to experience this game. Whatever you do, don't uninstall it. If you don't like it, just leave it to play itself for a couple months, then try again. You'll fall in love all over again.
You have 50MB of Hard Disk space to lose, and a lot of fun(?) to gain. Make the decision yourself.

TL;DR
ARK didn't deliver on the hype, and very thinly met on it's promises. It's selling double the price for what is barely the game. And it suffers no more (Sometimes MUCH more) than any other game in the Survival-Building-OpenWorld-Shooter genre set.
It's better you save your money. Unless you have friends to help, unless you have more money to spend on a private server, unless you have a lot of patience, or unless you absolutely cannot find another game that fits your desires for entertainment.
But if you cannot resist buying this game because it's 'the only one of it's kind', I think you're in the exact trap the devs want. And they know it. Why else raise a price on a mixed reviews game?
---For More Detail:---
For starters, the game fails to achieve what we first heard (And continue to be told) the game would be about. ARK is a game about dinosaurs and survival that hopes to put you to scale with a thriving prehistoric world with building elements and interactions between players. I was hoping that much like the trailers I too would be part of a thriving community of players participating in events in this theme.
Instead what I found was a odd game. Character customization feels like a joke, moreso than say Dark Souls. At least with Dark Souls you can viably CHOOSE if you want to be a grotesque horror with cartoonish proportions or a actual human being with meaningful customization. (In fact, Dark Souls has the ability for both quite well. Monster characters are hilarious and outright unreal while the system still allows you to make meaningful and delightfully varied Roleplay characters.) ARK doesn't let you do this nearly as much as it lets you become some freakish vaguely human creature thing. It doesn't feel finished, and that carries on well outside of the character creator.
Gameplay suffers from many of the problems of the Four Horsemen of the Apocolypse Survival-Shooter-Openworld-Builder genre. Guns exist but are hard enough to come by that a small group can grief a whole server and deny everyone time to build and catch up. Survival is a joke in some cases and as simple as walking up to a open water source and pressing the interact button and that's the entire worry for dehydration covered; It is implied more that players and dinosaurs are a threat but with dinosaurs being run by particularly butchered dumb AI the only real threat is players and that just makes the game feel like a terrible idea for a indefinite arena-shooter.
I feel like the only purpose this game serves is not to actually be a fun game, but to be the game you -have- to play if you have specific desires. Dinosaurs are a niche that some people can't find in other games, certainly none as popular. Survival is not uncommon but ARK gained popularity enough that most people feel to indebted to it to try others that aren't as strong in playerbase. The world building aspect is a curse that few games have pulled off well and ARK doesn't either, but the point is that it 'may be one of the best' which in this case is to have base building even mean anything.
I don't get to play as the guy that rides a dinosaur with his clansmate in this game, and when I do its so brief that by the time you realize you might be there the world wipes you clear off the map and starts you right off from scratch; Whether it be a enemy clan or other misfortune. This game is a great despairity between having fun and not having fun, and the having fun in this game doesn't feel valuable enough. This game costs more frustration to play then it gives happiness, and that's counter to what a game should be. I'm all for games making me work for my reward, as some of the greatest games are all about the massive payoff whether it be ingame or from personal "Awww yeasssss!" But in this game it takes a certain kind of person to justify retrying again and again and again and again just to succeed in a ideal they likely had to compromise for because the game isn't built to allow for what they really wanted. (Example: Building a private farm with massive walls, a task made difficult by hostile neighbors and limited resources. The reward is just pulling it off, when you really wanted to make it public and create or join a town. But you can't, because doing so has costed you several farms before and you need to spend money on walls because the enemy will offline raid you if you don't.)

Chivalry: Medieval BOREfare. Hehe.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare is exactly what it sounds like, medieval warfare. Swords, shields, bows, there is a good selection of weapons to choose from, and each one is fun. Whether you're stealing a kill with a crossbow, or decapitating your enemy with a greatsword, you'll often find yourself chuckling at the truly graphic and gory visuals of the game. The unlock system keeps you coming back, but doesn't make it difficult to earn new weapons. The customization of your character is a nice extra feature, and lets you add your own personal spice to your characters.
The Deadliest Warrior DLC only makes the game better. The classes are similar enough to the original ones that you'll know how to play them, but it will still feel fresh. Of course, they have all new weapons, and each class has it's own special feature. For example, a viking can throw all of their weapons, or even their shield, and pirates get an entertaining arsenal of firearms and explosives.
When it comes down to it, Chivalry: Medieval Warfare and it's DLC content makes for a fun combination of features and weapons that will make you want to keep playing. You may find some balance issues with certain weapons, but there is nothing that seems too difficult to counter.

Two words:
Warframe is by far my favorite FPS, not that I've played many compared to most people. While I haven't played it for very long, only around 12-or-so hours collectively, Warframe is ridiculously hard to put down. It's got great graphics, it's easy to run on my PC, which isn't in any way meant for games (I can run it on High with little to no lag at all), the movements of the NPCs and warframes and fast-paced combat are to die for, and the UI is super sleek and nice to look at.
And for all that, it's
!
Granted, you do have to pay for extra stuff, like certain skins, color palettes, etc. All the more advanced customizations and weapons. But to me, that's perfectly fair. It's not P2W, nor is it P2P like most games of the same style are, but instead it's P2-look-prettier/get-upgrades-quick. So long as you aren't salty when someone who spends money on a cooler-looking weapon looks better than you, it's a pretty good deal.
So yeah, I'd recommend Warframe to anybody and everybody. DOWNLOAD IT. You'll never be able to stop playing once you do.

This game tries to do too much. All through Early Access they were announcing new features, but never dealing with existing issues. I took a break for a while and decided not to install the game on my new computer until it came out of Early Access, which was last week. It's crashed on my 4 times in as many hours and all the gameplay clunkiness remains.
The most annoying gameplay element for me is the combat. It's unclear when you're hitting something, friend or enemy. I've killed pets because I thought I was cutting down a tree near my mount. The feedback from hitting something is often missing. So when fighting an enemy, you don't know if you're in a good position or if you need to get closer.
I like that you can adjust the settings to give you pretty fine-grained control over the difficulty, but it makes weight management difficult if you set the resources higher to speed things up. You end up with enough wood from one tree to make you over-encumbered, and yet it still takes a while to find enough metal for anything useful.

Incredibly rewarding combat is a phrase I hear thrown out a lot with this game, and I'm inclined to agree. All projectiles, melee weapons, and parries/blocks must be aimed appropriately and timed appropriately. Yes, just like real life, if someone comes crashing down on your head with a overhead swing and you don't hold your weapon up above you, you're probably dead, if not seriously wounded.
Choosing positions is incredibly strategic; trading attacks and parries, using more advanced rotation and feint techniques to get your opponent to waste a parry, jumping over horizontal attacks, sidestepping vertical one, ducking headshots to counter with taking someone's legs off, aiming projectiles at someone's feet to cirumvent shields; there are just so many options available to you at any given time, it's almost impossible for every scuffle to even be a little alike(unless of course they let you pull off the same combos and refuse to learn).
Plus you can use a sling to throw rocks at people's heads. So many rocks.
If you like swords and strategic real time combat with hilarious warcries and a usually great(occasionally toxic individuals) community, then this might be the game for you. I've had so many matches where my teammates ask questions and answers happen(this doesn't happen in lots of team-based competitive games).

ARK is an epic game, that borrows an idea here, idea there, and then adds in its own wonderful content, and mixes it all together for a game that is truly unique when looked at as a whole. Despite performance issues, I have seen improves, and it's well worth putting up with for the range of sandbox content this game has to offer. Building, taming, fighting, PvP, medival, modern, sci-fi, dinosauars, mythological creatures, this game blends it all beautifully. It has minimal, but interesting, story, revealed through notes and endgame content. The music is very well done, and the graphics are stunning -if- your rig is able to handle it, through limited optimizaiton. But even at lower settings, this game is a sight to behold.
P.S. I feel as though I've recently rediscovered the game in a new light. I was a diehard official server player, enjoying the game as it was orginally designed by the devs. Now I'm loving it all over again, as I've started playing on an unofficial server, with accelerated progression. This allows me to bypass what might be an excessive grind for some, and get more of an enjoyable casual experience, and hopefully allow the exciting sci-fi endgame content to finally be reachable. Even with accelerated progression, the game should prove to be a fun challenge.
I hope you all enjoy the game as much as I have. =)

This is my first negative review and hopefully my last.
Is this an excellent game, with a great concept, content and potential? Absolutely. I could never disagree with that. From an official standpoint and also the work that the community has put forth through the workshop.
I won't say I have not had my monies worth considering I bought this game when it first came out 2 years ago. However, as it currently stands I am unable to recommend this game to potential buyers. Not because I dislike the game, I think it's great, but the Wildcard Team are not letting this game shine to the best of its ability.
Things are delayed, bugs happen,♥♥♥♥♥♥happens and things will go wrong. That is understandable and I take no issue with that. That said, the complete lack of communication towards the playerbase is something that is becoming more and more ridiculous, even more so now that we are out of EA and they're already annoucing new DLC.
There are still no new Ragnarok PVE PC servers. There is no information, there is no update, there is no communication from anyone at Wildcard. Not even a tweet of an ETA, a confirmation or simply declining new servers for us PC users. This is what is irritating. The fact they do not care. Period.
You can say "oh well go play single player or rent a server", but my friends did not purchase this game to do that. They bought it under the premise of being able to play PVE online through official servers. That is what they purchased for and that is what is advertised.
I will happily retract not recommending this game once Wildcard acknowledges the issues at hand. Until then, I cannot in all good conscience give this game a positive review, despite the fact it deserves one, your total neglect of your playerbase outweighs all the pros you can, do and possibly will have.
You have an excellent product, Wildcard, please respect your customers who purchased it and regain some faith from your playerbase. Quality over quantity.

This is my first negative review and hopefully my last.
Is this an excellent game, with a great concept, content and potential? Absolutely. I could never disagree with that. From an official standpoint and also the work that the community has put forth through the workshop.
I won't say I have not had my monies worth considering I bought this game when it first came out 2 years ago. However, as it currently stands I am unable to recommend this game to potential buyers. Not because I dislike the game, I think it's great, but the Wildcard Team are not letting this game shine to the best of its ability.
Things are delayed, bugs happen,♥♥♥♥♥♥happens and things will go wrong. That is understandable and I take no issue with that. That said, the complete lack of communication towards the playerbase is something that is becoming more and more ridiculous, even more so now that we are out of EA and they're already annoucing new DLC.
There are still no new Ragnarok PVE PC servers. There is no information, there is no update, there is no communication from anyone at Wildcard. Not even a tweet of an ETA, a confirmation or simply declining new servers for us PC users. This is what is irritating. The fact they do not care. Period.
You can say "oh well go play single player or rent a server", but my friends did not purchase this game to do that. They bought it under the premise of being able to play PVE online through official servers. That is what they purchased for and that is what is advertised.
I will happily retract not recommending this game once Wildcard acknowledges the issues at hand. Until then, I cannot in all good conscience give this game a positive review, despite the fact it deserves one, your total neglect of your playerbase outweighs all the pros you can, do and possibly will have.
You have an excellent product, Wildcard, please respect your customers who purchased it and regain some faith from your playerbase. Quality over quantity.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare has many interesting traits.
Pros:
First, its fighting mechanics are outstanding and really feels like you are in the combat.
Second, the people fighting in game are always kind and helpful. Unhelpful people are rare.
Third, it is very much a skill based game requiring lots of effort to learn how to fight and to fight proficiently. Once you learn how to fight it becomes very fun to get into 1v1 battles, 1v2 battles, 1v3 or more.
Lastly, the sounds and graphics are well made and immerses the player into the game.
Cons:
If you get easily angered and frustrated this is definitely not your game. In the beginning you will die quite a lot and it will be very rage inducing; I know I have ragequit this game multiple times.
The archery mechanic is very difficult to get the hang of and if you like sniping like me you will be disappointed quite a bit in the beginning by not getting those headshots.
For younger players be informed now that the gore cannot be turned off.
Tips:
I recommend watching or reading a few tutorials on combat to begin with. After that, practice practice practice. Nothing is more satisfying in the game then when you perform a combo and decapitate a few knights and vanguards.

Two words:
Warframe is by far my favorite FPS, not that I've played many compared to most people. While I haven't played it for very long, only around 12-or-so hours collectively, Warframe is ridiculously hard to put down. It's got great graphics, it's easy to run on my PC, which isn't in any way meant for games (I can run it on High with little to no lag at all), the movements of the NPCs and warframes and fast-paced combat are to die for, and the UI is super sleek and nice to look at.
And for all that, it's
!
Granted, you do have to pay for extra stuff, like certain skins, color palettes, etc. All the more advanced customizations and weapons. But to me, that's perfectly fair. It's not P2W, nor is it P2P like most games of the same style are, but instead it's P2-look-prettier/get-upgrades-quick. So long as you aren't salty when someone who spends money on a cooler-looking weapon looks better than you, it's a pretty good deal.
So yeah, I'd recommend Warframe to anybody and everybody. DOWNLOAD IT. You'll never be able to stop playing once you do.

When it comes to medieval games, this is definitely one to have in your library. It goes on a cheap sale price so be sure to keep an eye out for it!
This game literally throws you into action and provides you with more than a simple swing the mouse and chop someone. The game has an awesome fighting engine. It's accurate and very rewarding while playing. What sets this one apart from other hack and slash's is the way you have to be facing the enemy to block or attack (and even dodge). On top of that, there are variances in the swings you can engage in. Rolling the mouse wheel backwards allows for a heavy overhead swing, while rolling it forwards provides a front poking motion extending your reach. Left button allows for a swing left to right while right mouse button is to block attacks. There are other swing variances that you should look into as I've set one of my extra mouse buttons as a side swing from right to left. Swing types matter as it could be the difference between hitting an opponent and accidentally hitting your own team-mate (which can be a regular occurrence given the right ignorance). Alternative attacks and different classes mix the game up and can really halt your strategy after receiving an arrow or axe to the head. The best game mode would be Team Objective (raid the castle) as being able to use some of the in game props like throwing torches or using a giant mounted crossbow can be just as fun as the modern day shooters.
Objectives also change as you may be trying to free prisoners one game, another game you may be trying to slay the King's family. Just make sure you don't get a dimwit using the catapult or you and the enemy will go flying. Other modes include team death match, which is two teams going straight for one another, free for all, dual mode (where people go one on one), king of the hill, last team standing and capture the flag. Different classes are also available. There is man at arms, who is the fastest but least armor. Vanguard, who when he sprints, raises his sword over his head and can do a lunge jump attack unlike any other class. Knight, who is the slowest but has the most armor and does the most damage. Last but not least, the archer, who can still fight with a dagger but is better off shooting arrows. Swords can also be swapped in for maces and axes. There are other variances available as well for your other weapons such as throwing axes or mini-explosive fire bombs that burn enemies.
Graphics and sounds are phenomenal. Everything seems to be given a realistic touch and levels take places from beautiful rolling hills to being on top of a volcano. If you get hit, you will see blood. Sounds of metal clanging together or being blocked can be heard throughout the game. When running, players are given the option of pressing "C" to make their character yell. It can get intimidating when 15 players are running after a few guys all yelling at the top of their lungs.
Really fun to play for a while or simply drop in for a quick game. It's learning curve at first is a little difficult but after realizing how the game works get ready for flying vanguard sword attacks.
RATING : 8.3/10
For future Chiv games : adding horses or some sort of vehicle system may be appreciated for a Chiv 2 or some sort of update. There is a nice big open map available, why not make it complete chaos with more disposal or fixed mounted weapons.

TL;DR It's not worth it at it's current price. Wait until it's cheaper before buying it, I'd suggest $20 or lower.  Bring friends if possible.
To start off with, I have no experience with public servers, only private ones where I played with a group of friends on, where the server hosts changed some settings, so you may have a different experience.  The settings I know of in specific are no crosshair and a drastically increased level range in any area for dinosaurs.  There are also going to be spoilers if you want to discover mechanics and how various things work for yourself.
The performance in the game is terrible.  People love to say "Get a better PC," all the time but I have no need for a better PC considering I have a GTX 1070.  Sure it's not top of the line, but it's still better than what many other people are going to have.  For those that aren't too keen on computer parts, that can run most games at 1080p resolution at the minimum 60 fps when at maximum graphics settings, but will usually be able to go to 120 or higher for many games.  However, in ARK, I get a solid 50 fps at near max graphics settings when I turn down the render distance to be something more reasonable.  Closer to 30 fps if I set the graphics to max.
To me this isn't acceptable but I can bear with it if the rest of the game was good enough to overcome it.
It doesn't look terrible for the most part.  Some things could stand to be improved.  There were a couple small areas where you were able to see some texture overlap slightly, but it otherwise looks fine, in some places even great.  No major gripes about the graphics in particular other than how certain things in the technology tree look but that's minor.  Overall not the best looking game ever but far from the worst.
As with graphics the sound design isn't super bad, offhand I cannot think of anything that would lead to bad sound design.  For the most part everything sounds like you could imagine it sounding, with the exception of some dinosaurs sounding similar.  Honestly though some dinosaurs are going to start sounding similar if you're trying to make something unique for every single one.  Sound in my opinion is pretty alright.
Now my experience may be slightly different from other people due to the settings changed in the server but it shouldn't be too different.
You're thrown into the world at a spawn point.  There's many on the entire map, some much easier than others.  I like this because you can choose a harder spawn as a veteran player to push yourself more.  The developers heard that in Minecraft you punched trees to get wood for your first set of tools so they took that quite literally.  You punch the tree with bloodied fists and your tools.  Simple enough.  Practically everything in the game can be learned without looking up a walkthough, which is very good. Many things explain themselves such as pickaxe mines stone and ore, axe for wood, campfire to cook and provide heat.  Overall the crafting works fine, some things can be slightly difficult to grind for though when starting off.
Slaying dinosaurs is as expected, slaying a large carnivore can be difficult and feels great for your first few times.  Many dinosaurs are going to be quite deadly if you're alone, especially most carnivores.  You need to bring some allies of some sort.
Through taming you can get those allies you need to defeat more powerful dinosaurs.  With taming you can tame nearly any dinosaur.  There are very few exceptions.  The bad thing about taming is that without decreasing time to tame, it is very much a grind.  Especially if you have dinosaurs be any level within the possible range like my server had.  This leads to level 120 dinosaurs in the easiest starting zones, which can take upwards of 4 hours to tame.  Larger and more dangerous dinosaurs require longer.  Considering you need to check back to make sure they're still unconscious it can be very time consuming.  Luckily they have option to decrease tame time, but it doesn't quite feel like a proper fix in my opinion
Taming could stand to improve by being more engaging, since as it stands it's mostly jam food and narcotics into dinosaurs then you sit back and watch Netflix.  I'd prefer an engaging minigame, if it was a well made minigame.  It could use the same amount of resources right now it would just eat them up right away upon a successful tame.  This would lead to lower tame times and would allow inexperienced players to venture farther faster because they won't have that fear of "Is it going to just run away with my narcotics and food?" for an hour while they tend to various resources such as barries and among others closeby.
There are pet commands which let you command your tamed dinosaurs in various ways.  They overall help control your dinosaurs.
Breeding dinosaurs is a bit odd because it's much more simple than I would expect.  You have two uses for the eggs.  Making a new dinosaur, which is more difficult, or using it to make kibble for a specific dinosuar.  This kibble lets you tame dinosaurs MUCH faster than with with basic taming materials.  It's fair that kibble exists, but some kibble can be very difficult to get.  It does encourage you to tame multiple types of dinosaurs since finding eggs in the wild is uncommon.
Combat itself is very basic.  It doesn't need to be super engaging combo based combat but it could be improved slightly since it reminds me of skyrim combat, with melee weapons.  With a bow it gets much better because it has some nice arrow drop.  It works well for what it is.
I know some people might complain that I'm a casual or whatever for saying this but I do wish there was an option to allow people to keep their inventory upon death.  It would make dying less stressful, especially if you just want to sit back and relax without having to worry about dying.
Something that might worry people is you can come across various bugs that may or may not be able to be replicated.  There was a single instance where I could not feed a dinosaur food, which led to it's death.  I could not replicate the bug so I could not submit it as a bug report.
Exploration is fine for the most part, there's some more hidden areas and plenty of places to go, plenty of dinosaurs to see.  Some dungeons too, but they can prove a challenge if you're undergeared.  In my opinion it's much better and more enjoyable to explore on foot than in the air, but it's also more dangerous.  I would like for there to be more little things but the default island is already pretty packed as it is.
I do not recommend this game because there's been a few bugs that have affected the game enough, taming is a pain without modifying the setting, the performance issues, but most importantly the price.  If the performance was much better I might consider switching to to recommended.  But for $60 you get something that doesn't run well on even systems with a great cpu/gpu, has various bugs, and feels similar to a Korean MMO with how much time you may have to dedicate at a time (without increasing tame speed)? Not at that price is it worth it.  If you have some friends to play with get it with the season pass for $40 or less.  Maybe $25 or $30 for the base game if it really appeals to you, and you especially love the concepts.  Wait until winter sale if you can't wait for the price to drop significantly, it's only a couple months out and will hopefully save you a fair chunk of money.

Considering performance and price I rate it 4/10.
