ARK has to be one of the most intriguing and interesting games Ive played to date. Ive clocked almost 400 hours on this game and have yet to even begin exploring the options that it has to offer, I still know very little about taming and breeding/hatching.
This is a game that will immerse you fully in either an advanced world of high tek dinos and structures, or take you back to your primitive nature with bricks and mortar (depending on the game mode of your choice).
With literally thousands of hours of content currently available on the game as-is; its definitely worth the money that you will spend on it. I have had my ups and downs thus far and can only imagine the roller coaster ride for legacy EA players who have stuck with WC from the beginning, and I honestly have to say that i rather envy those people as they were able to watch this masterpiece unfold before their eyes.
WC has made some mistakes and their communication skills aren't always the best, but lets be real and look at the quality of content they have brought to us and just be happy that a company was able to produce such an immensely detailed game with thousands of options rather than your generic point and clicks.
The game could still use some serious optimization; but thats not an easy task for a game of this magnitude, especially considering the content involved. There are dozens of kilometers of open world to render and explore and that doesnt come without taxing any rig, the fact that you can play well on bottom consumer grade hardware is an amazing level of optimization by the WC development team.
I can say that I look forward to peaking thousands of hours of gameplay and Im sure I will get frustrated and annoyed with decisons the CC makes for this game, we all will and this isn't new for any game. It happens.
I only hope that ARK will find a way to sustain a recurring financial model that benefits them so they can continue to explore this game and not lose the financial capability to develop it further.

This is, in my opinion, the ultimate LAN game. You get a bunch of your buddies together, split into teams (or do a free-for-all), get down to first-person slashing, and hit the "yell" button liberally. That's right, there's a button to make your medieval warrior yell battlecries.
A lot of games get first-person slashing wrong. I've played a lot of those games, and this isn't one of them. It's easy to launch attacks with reasonable chances of hitting, it's reasonably easy to block or avoid them, and the various weapons handle quite differently. It's tons of fun, and there are unlikely to be accusations of cheating, lag, or hitbox issues.
It's a good game (no, really), and there's a battlecry button!

WC has made some mistakes and their communication skills aren't always the best, but lets be real and look at the quality of content they have brought to us and just be happy that a company was able to produce such an immensely detailed game with thousands of options rather than your generic point and clicks.
The game could still use some serious optimization; but thats not an easy task for a game of this magnitude, especially considering the content involved. There are dozens of kilometers of open world to render and explore and that doesnt come without taxing any rig, the fact that you can play well on bottom consumer grade hardware is an amazing level of optimization by the WC development team.
I can say that I look forward to peaking thousands of hours of gameplay and Im sure I will get frustrated and annoyed with decisons the CC makes for this game, we all will and this isn't new for any game. It happens.
I only hope that ARK will find a way to sustain a recurring financial model that benefits them so they can continue to explore this game and not lose the financial capability to develop it further.

First off I will say I DO NOT recommend this game at a full retail price. I got Ark back in early access for around $30 and I have gotten my money's worth in enjoyment. This game has a lot of fun things to do and I always find myself going back to it. I really really enjoy the solo play and PvE aspects of this game a lot. Unfortunately, this game has plenty of bugs/glitches and is still poorly optimized. That plus the amount of time and energy it takes to get Dinos tamed, PvP can be really frustrating sometimes and I don't particularly enjoy it (but I know a few people who do). Like any building/survival game you will reach a point where you have too much and there is no longer a challenge so replayability can be an issue. Ark's visuals are also beautiful but you'll need a very strong video card to see it because of the optimizations issues.
No developer in their right mind would consider this a polished game for launch so don't be fooled by that. The game still needs more content (like additional maps), bug fixes, and some serious optimization. 7 Days to Die, for example, is in much better condition, is still in early access, and only cost $25. However, if you are like me and get burned out on other games like this after awhile (and you love the idea of Dinosaurs instead of Zombies) then you'll probably enjoy Ark  but wait for it to go on a Steam sale. I wouldn't pay more than $30 for it in its current condition and the developers should be ashamed asking for full price.

At more than 1,000 hours logged this is the single game I play most frequently. It is fun, but not overly complicated. There is a lot of variety in gear. It's free to play. There is no pay 2 win, and the majority of game modes are a lot of fun to play. You can go for the team experience by playing with others, or you can solo to content when you don't want to engage in team play. Has an easy to use trade system for tradable items. Also, the graphics are stellar.
That being said, the biggest negative is that the game is very grindy. If you hate having to repeat the same mission multiple times to aquire the exact drop you're looking for, then this game probably isn't for you. As an example, say you want the super shiny warframe. Well, you have to repeat a regular mission to acquire the keys to get to the special mission which drops the shiny warframe. Then you repeat the special mission ad infinitum until you acquire all the parts for the shiny warframe. It's largely RNG based, so you can luck out and get what you need in the first run or you can go for hours without acquiring a single needed drop. Drop tables can be real confusing and useless too. Drop tables can be frustrating. Not game breaking frustrating, but definately frustrating.
They do have real world currency, like all free MMO's do these days, and you can use that currency to purchase the equipment without grinding for it. There are no stat boosts to bought equipment, it's literally only to save you time. You can also use said real world currency to purchase things in trade chat that you don't want to grind for.
Most players only use the real world currency for cosmetic items. Which there is a large selection of cosmetic items to purchase. This brings up another draw back, cosmetic items are only available for real world currency. They do some charity cosmetics for the poor players on holidays. Like holiday themed color pallet's, but it's basically all gonna cost you real world money. If you're cool not looking awesome then you don't need to worry about this. Also, they usually have a sale on cosmetics once a year. So it's best to save your real world currency till the sale hits.
Don't lose hope though. You can earn the real world credits through trading. You can't trade with in game currency, only in real world currency. So if you spend a lot of time grinding, you can essentially earn your cosmetic items by trading the weapons/parts/blueprints you don't want on the trade chat. I've heard of serious traders acquiring a couple thousand real world currencies per month. It does require an investment of time, but the option is available if you decide you don't want to invest cash into the game.
Overall, I would recommend the game. I find it fun to play. Plenty of acheivements to unlock. Lots of content to go through. Typically it's decent writing and it's a great looking game. Very active community. So give it a shot. It's free, so you really only will lose a bit of time if you decide you hate it. =)

I've been a long time player and fan of Warframe. I has been one of my favourite games.
The Pros:
Combat can be insanely fun
There's a lot of freedom with movement
It's not nearly as pay to win as everyone says.
Every weapon, and frame in the game is available to you, you just have to farm and earn it.
DE even leaves it open to earn cash shop currency through farming and trading mods/ prime parts/ special weapons.
There are around 851 mods give or take some due to development: this means almost infinite possibilities to customize your frames and weapons to suit you and your play style.
It's rewarding watching yourself progress.
It's an amazingly well done game for being self funded, and it's come a long way
Diverse community
Neutral:
It's a grindfest. There's a lot of repeating missions, farming and grinding. For some this can be a turn off. For others, like myself, it's enjoyable. It can get monotonous though.
The Cons:
(okay this will get a bit whiny but it's a growing concern of mine) There's listening to your player base, and acknowledging their concerns; then there's bending over backwards to pander to them. I don't know what it is with DE but recently I've often been wondering if they almost fear their player base. There's many different desires from the Warframe player base, and DE bends over backwards trying to please each and every single one of them. It's almost like the community is divided into three camps. Nerf It, Leave It As It Is, and Buff It. I tend to fall under the mostly leave it, but make some balancing efforts to players and enemies to keep the game fun, exciting, and challenging. Yes, if you are a developer it's a great Idea to listen to the feedback from your players, but in most other games only a small percent that of complaints get implemented. With Warframe... it seems like they're both selective and all inclusive, over which squeaky wheels they grease. Players whine constantly to either buff or nerf something and DE just does it, but then the more neutral members of the community that say "leave that as it is but make these changes for over all better game play for everyone," are left unheard.
If you look at the early on weapons from three years ago, weapons that were meta then have absolutely horrendous stats compared to the weapons they've been releasing. Not many want to sit there with a level 100 eximus bombard and pump clip after clip of head shots into it for a minute and a half to kill it. And the newer weapons reflect a desire from the player base for options that are fun, exciting, creative, but also scale well. But, in some cases those weapons are WAY too strong, and need a slight slight nerf.
For example take two weapons called the Synoid Simular, and the Tonk. In all honesty these weapons were stupid strong and needed a small nerf to bring them back down to appropriate levels.  But these weapons were immensely fun and exciting to play, and that was key.
My first time using a tonk I was like "HAHAHA! HOLY S***T!" and knew I had something. But, being able to do a mission and get 700 kills to everyone else's 45... yeah admittedly that's a bit ridicules. So, on the other side of the coin people were crying for it to be nerfed.
The nerf came in the form of a 10% crit chance deduction from 35% down to 25% which is a considerable damage deduction. What ever, Tonk can still hit like a truck. But what made the weapon unusable is the self damage was increased by a lot. So now that stray erratic grenade that bounces back in your face kills you. And that killed the fun (and me).
Ultimately though here's what we had: Two weapons that were fun and exciting to play and that's what it's all about. Keeping those "HAHAHA! HOLY SH*T!!" moments coming, and that is why I say these were good weapons. Not cause they were  OP or their stats. They were fun to play, but needed a slight nerf. Instead, of balancing them, they changed their mechanics and nerfed them so far into the ground they were useless and no longer fun to use.
DE doesn't seem to understand  the concept of balancing. Pleanty could have been done to make changes to these weapons. For the Tonk there could have had a 12% chance that your grenade could just be a dud. But the changes made are the exact same changes screamed about by more spiteful critics of the weapon. "Add full self damage then no one will use it." DE pandered to a sect of the community, rather than imagine a more creative solution, or at the very least went with the lazy solution of altering preexisting code."
I'm not upset about the Tonk nerf. It needed to happen, just not to the extent that they did it. My concern is that as newer and cooler weapons and frames come out, there's these AMAZING ideas that DE implements. They do exactly what you want in a game. They keep it fresh, fun, exciting, and challenging. Then ultimately a group of people cry for a buff or a nerf (usually a nerf) DE changes it and it's no where near as rewarding to play. At that point, what's the point in implementing these incredible new ideas for weapons and frames if it's just going to get changed to something blase and underwhelming? It's almost like DE is having fun dreaming up these concepts trying to progress the game forward and then parts of the community cry over it and for what ever reason DE acts like they're forced revert the concept back to the mundane.
Part of the issue is that there's toxic mentalities with in the community such as this casual gamer, Call of Duty-esk ideological. "That frame or weapon needs to be nerfed because my build is OP and they got more kills than I did." It's always been that 75% of Warframe has been thought and strategy. It's required of you to think, research and look at your options and find out how to make your build better for YOU. Everyone has their own frames they prefer and even if you don't think highly of lets say, an Oberon, and someone with one gets more kills than your "totally op, no one can beat whatever it is you play build," then that's on you. Because just as you are proficient with your build so are they with theirs and at that point it's time to stop being salty. It's up to you to adapt. Just because someone's researched, experimented, knows what they're doing and has come up with a strategy that works better than yours, does not mean that it should be nerfed so it's more fair to you. Especially in a PVE based game.
I'm of the opinion that DE should just worry about DE, instead of worrying so much about what the player base wants. Just let DE do their thing. All the the player base wants is something fun and intriguing. I have seen them publish new content and gone "OMG I LOVE THAT THEY DID THIS." Come back a week later and it's been nerfed or changed and then you go to the forums or the wiki and you find fore every person crying over it, another was saying leave it alone.. If their efforts are allowed to blossom then over time the game will balance itself and progress, and then you would revisit these ideas to level the playing field. It's these toxic mentalities, and constant changes to either buff or nerf things to pander to those mentalities that are slowly driving alot of the long time fans like myself away.

Over and all, I can't recommend this game enough! Come on, it's free!

What to say about Warframe?
Quite a bit and perhaps some not to nice but I will say one thing, Warframe even after four years of playing it. Been playing since open beta literally as soon as it popped up.
I still enjoy the game, even if the grind is rather immense.
You must grind quite literally for everything and I do mean everything.
New Frame, grind.
New Weapon, grind.
New Resource you need, grind.
Need Experience, grind.
This shouldn't put you off.
There are some good well a lot for the most part.
The graphics are really stunning, the lore is coming together and turning out rather good.
Unlike Blizzard the lore remains the same.
Several hidden things, like Oro-Kitty statues.
The clans are good as long as they remain active.
You can actually make some good friends here.
About the Devs, I'm fairly sure their attitudes reflect the hate they receive daily.
They can sometimes do kneejerk reactions which always open the floodgate.
But they are human, so it's expected.
Now events aren't as great as they used to be. If they release a weapon in the event, it'll show up in Sorties eventually. Sorties are for those that enjoy pain, they start out as level 100's.
They've introduced some interesting things over the years.
They have done some unfortunate things, but nobody's perfect.
In short, it's a grindfest of a game, but it is still rather good.
Enjoy it but don't burn yourself out as I have.
See you within the Origin System, Tenno.
-End of Line-

I'm a casual gamer.  What that usually means is that, while I might play the living daylights out of a game for a month (around 30-40 hours a week), at some point I'll get bored and not be interested any more.
While there is some "grind" to this game, it is minor.  The extent of "grind" that you need to do in this game is really "Level up weaspons, level up frames" - once they hit level 30, you can dump them or keep them, as you choose.  Level 30 on a frame is not difficult or even time consuming.  Level 30 on a weapon is not difficult or time consuming.  The only thing that could be difficult is the trial to rank up, but that's not a grind, that's a one-time quest to achieve the next rank.
This game is pretty darned good.  This is like Destiny, only WAY better.  More classes, more weapons, better storyline, more skill to play.  If you like Destiny, you'll love Warframe.

The game has potential.
The mechanics are well thought out, but could be better executed. It has a different kind of combat, the weapon swings are realtime, and the point of impact follows the swing, but the precision needed to properly set up a good stab is ♥♥♥♥ed over by the lag and lack of polish, meaning you'll be killed over and over by thinking, SEEING your opponents swing miss, but then see your head roll around on the floor.
You'll see a bunch of people oneshotting you with a massive hammer, and people swinging nonstop while you can't even set up a simple 1-2 combo... It has a learning curve that I find steeper than Dark Souls, which isn't a bad thing, but as the tutorial sucks, and the playerbase by now has advanced as much as it has you'll find a lot of the time excrutiatingly horrible, the game is simply not fun for a new player at all.
BUT I will still recommend this game for anyone who likes melee combat, as the times where you're lucky and don't end up with horrible lag and players far more skilled than you, the game is very fun.
If you can manage to git gud and get through the hours of gitting rekt over and over (which I haven't yet) you will probably find a fully entertaining game

Since this game is my 2nd most played game with so manny hours (2nd to league of legends, which I quit after what is prob something like 3k-5k hrs) I suppose I could write a review. Warframe is a game that you need to expect to pour your time into. This is not the game for you if you dont have atleast a little free time. You will be grinding in this game an insane amount. Even for an MMORPG. I play quite a lot of mmo's and this one is definetly within my top 3, maybe even my favourite. This game isn't exactley an mmorpg, and I would say it fits more into a third person shooter, but it definatley has a lot of aspects from an mmo. If you are sick of TF2 and only play for the economic standpoint, warframe has a very nice trading system. Also, just a heads up trading is a big part of this game so expect to at the very least to a little bit of it. I'm running out of mental power to continue a descriptive review so here is this for you.(This is all personal opinion dont flame) Graphics 8/10: I love em. Gameplay 9/10: Who doesn't want to be a space ninja? Customization 5/10: Ok so here's the thing, it would be an 8 but in order to do a large amount of customization you need platinum, so get ready to trade or spend money. Story/Lore 8.5/10: Early on it's like blehhh but once you get to the second dream things start to really heat up. F2P value 9/10: So many people mistake warframe as a pay to win, but it really isn't. The only thing you HAVE to use plat for is cosmetic purposes, and you don't even NEED to spend money for that since trading exists to get you plat for free. You can use plat to speed things up too, but all that is doing is decreasing the amount of time you spend on warframe, but time is monney so this game is insanely expensive.(was that too bad of a joke? ;-;) Well that concedes my first game review and my only one for a long time. Have a good day. Blehhh

I recommend this game because I have managed to spend 900 Hrs playing it so it was worth $25.00 USD at the time and remains recommended because it was also gifted to me, however for reasons explained below you may want to consider if its the game for you and why I would reconsider my own answer of "Recommended" knowing what I know now.
Reasons why you
buy the game are simple, it offers a interesting melee combat system in really simple FPS style mechanics, but it can also delve into much much deeper mechanics not limited to a single play style. Infact without the developers intention  the possibility for play styles and combinations of play styles can be very advanced. There are a number of good players I know who have mixed variations of advanced mechanics into their play styles, and its quiet interesting. Its easy to pick up and kill some time playing Chivalry if you can get past the steep learning curve and these are the primary reasons I would suggest buying the game, but
at full price.
Now to review my disappointments and reasons of regret that I pass onto you in your moment of consideration.
Torn Banner studios is the primary reason I am disappointed with the game, not because they have a bad game in their hands but because they have a great game that screams competitive gameplay with practically zero outlets to portray and express competitive play.
The closest thing to competitive play you are going to get is Duel mode, and all Duel mode will do for you is randomly select someone for you to 1v1 for no real particular reason beyond to keep playing the game and not quit to desktop. My 900hrs game time exp will randomly be queued into someone with 2 hrs in a duel server of 15  people of which 10 are over 500hrs, and because it is literally just a random generator and it can't que me into people already dueling I will constantly get queued into this poor guy with 2hrs experience vs my 900 and ruin his experience forever never to return.
The ranking system in the game only really takes into account how many hours you have invested, I remember when I was rank 30...something long ago I actually lost rank for having a bad ratio, but they changed that and now I am pretty positive you can't even drop ranks.
The game needs more competitive play, arena 2v2, 3v3 other game modes, maps arenas that make the game what its clearly calling out for but I doubt this will ever happen, at least directly from the Torn Banner team, maybe someone on Steam Workshop can iron out the kinks.
This image took Torn Banner over a year to fix, its simple they were aware of it and it took one Earth revolution around the sun or more to fix, and this is the kind of neglect you may feel from your Dev team if you purchase this game.
So in closing.....buy at a reduced price, expect the game to have limited things to do and you will more then likely get what you consider
its always fun to log on hack and slash and log out.....Or buy at full price expect things to be done, stuff to get released and the game to offer ever evolving gameplay modes, and competitive challenges and be disappointed.

I feel I should write a review about this game now I am I quitting from official servers. I bought the game on March 2016
Just to clarify, I played the game mostly on PvE Official servers as my experience on PvP was very bad and on private servers was bad. I clearly understand that the business model of Wild Card is hosting private servers as main source of revenue, so they do not really care about the player base on official servers. The developer’s main focus always has been private PvP servers.
I love the concept of the game, being a survival, open world, multiplayer and with some dinosaurs. The original map was very fun to explore, there were some new biomes, like snow, swamp and red wood during the years. During most of the development of the game, they were adding creatures, new stuff and even new game mechanics (like kibble, breeding, fishing, end bosses, ascension, Ark transfer, etc) with each mayor revision of the game; they also hosted events, which were really fun. The graphics, sounds and music on the game are great and well done. You can play the game on local host (it requires a powerful system) if you like to test something on a controlled environment, or try building something cool just for fun. You can also run the game on your own server.
The game suffer from lag, this is because the way the game is coded, you just need one player with bad Internet connection to have lag on the server, which affects everybody playing there. There are still some bugs in the game, some as dangerous as making you lose your character, which means, for people who plays solo on official servers, starting over again. Some as annoying as getting your tamed creatures stuck and having to kill them on some cases. Because I played on PvE, we were forced some balancing changes (mostly know as nerf by the community) made for PvP to various exploits and mechanics on the game, like flying creatures, caps on items stats, offline raid protection, and now a timer for transferring items between server. From time to time they added creatures with features that broke the way we played the game.
Well, this is the hardest part to write about. I won’t go into details, the foremost, main complaint is support, or better written, lack of it. Game has almost no support on the free, official servers, if you open a ticket you will have to wait from 2 to 8 weeks to get an answer, and most of the time they will do nothing for you. Did you lose your character? Well, sit and wait a few weeks, they will not recover it for you as there is not such mechanism on the game, create a new one and they would give some Exp, forget about achievement as they will not grant you that. Complaining about griefer or cheater? Good Luck with it. Second, the idea of a game on early Access is to allow input from the community to make a better, more enjoyable game, well, from some unknown reason the developers started to make a lot of “balancing” and “fixes” on the game this years, most of these changes cause outrage on the game community as it made changes no one asked while ruined the fun factor of the game.  The community’s moderators are also famous by deleting post that points out obvious flaw in the game, try to find out any complain about the transfer timer, or people complaining about the support, to give you some examples.
Well, I wouldn’t as the game is no longer fun for me, I would love to be able to play version 256 of the game instead of the broken version we have now. I strongly disliked the changes they made on the last six months; I even tried to get a refund as this was not the game I bought.
Also, they released a paid DLC last year while the game was still on Early Access, most players, like me, bought it, the DLC is mostly dead and worthless as they released another free map which includes some of the same content.

I remember in my younger days flipping through my father's books on dinosaurs, fascinated by what I saw and trying to imagine what it would be like to live amongst such strange, giant beasts. Since playing Ark im glad to say I feel, in way, like a child again. Seeing these creatures so beautifully rendered is magical, to say the least.
I nearly passed the game by due to many of the reviews. So many negative, or mixed reviews. Then I began noticing.... these people not reccommending the game. Many were putting in hundreds, or even thousands of hours. It made me think of the person who sits in a restaurant, eats a whole steak, then at the end refuses to pay because they did not enjoy it. Im glad I ignored these reccomendations, but also glad I noticed they seemed to have something in common. Issues with multiplayer. Having played both singleplayer and multiplayer, I can safely say, singleplayer mode is where this game really shines.
In singleplayer you wake up on a huge island, covered in strange prehistoric creatures. You are free to do as you wish, whether it be try to tame your first dodo or start gathering materials to make your own clothes and shelter. Ark, in true survival fashion, starts out difficult. I died many times in my first few hours, and can see how one would get frustrated. But each death taught me a little more. Not to get close to this dino, it isnt as friendly as it looks. Dont go in the rivers, piranhas will swarm you. Watch your back in the swamps, the boas are stealthy and silent. Each time I lived a little longer, knowing better how to steer clear of the dangers the Ark had to throw. Eventually, as you learn and tame more dinosaurs and creatures, you will stay alive longer and lose fewer animals.
Each dinosaur has its own unique quality to help you survive. Some are excellent at harvesting wood, or stone, and in one strike can gather more than you could by hand. Others can quickly carry you out of harms way. I know many people complain of taming and breeding times. I understand how in multiplayer, when someone has to be on watch at all times, this can get maddening. But in singleplayer if you get tired you can simply leave, take a break, close the game and come back refreshed. Your dino will be waiting right as you left it.
I personally have not encountered any issues with performance. I built my first gaming system with Ark in mind. Its a large game, ambitious in its amount of content. It does take a powerful system. Having made sure when I put my system together it would be able to run this game easily I have only seen smooth frames and no lag, no stuttering. All settings on epic.
For price, I remember going to the store on release days, anxiously giving $60 for a game I had preordered, only to have completed about 20 hours later. This game, having a startling amount of play time and content to explore, is a great value for its $60 price tag. It has more content than most any game I have picked up off a store shelf in the past.
The only fault with the game I have found so far is the multiplayer aspect. Any online game will have abusive members, those who dont wish to play by the rules, or cause grief to others. I expected this when I went in. What I was surprised about was how the whole feel of the game had changed..... I know longer felt I was working to survive on a deserted island....I was living amongst a well populated 'town' of sorts. Too many players in one area ruins the magic for me.
In conclusion, yes, I whole heartedly recommend Ark. Its fun, beautiful, challenging.... Especially in singleplayer, where this game shines. Play at your own pace, your own set rules, master it. I have not brought friends in for a private session, but I can see that being great fun, jsut a few people against a whole island. Hundreds of hours of fun await with more content on the way. Take the plunge into another time; its well worth it.

Regretfully, I'm going to jump on the negative bandwagon. I have 190 hours, so I'd say I got my money's worth back when the game was still in beta playing on private servers with friends, and before the Scorched Earth controversy. I bought the game for $30 USD though. My gripe with the game is not the same as others who are upset about price points and business practices, although Wildcard has displayed highly questionable buisness practices a number of times, especially in late development.
As far as gameplay goes, the grind is real, as in really pointless. Beyond dying from being eaten by a giant crocodiles or raptors on spawning (which I found to be entertaining really), the default settings for this game are absurd and unplayable. Very little to nothing has been done to balance the game in this regard. The player is then left to experiment with the game's meriad settings to find an optimal amount of challenge without too much grinding. This might take a long time to find something that works for you and your friends.
Thinking of playing this game on your own? Don't bother. I came to this game hoping to have an experience as a small, cooperative group on an island where we are constantly at odds with the environment. But the A.I. is predictable, clunky, and fairly easy to exploit.
You'll get to a certain point with the game where you start to feel accomplished and then realize "What's the point?" This is because the game is designed from the ground up to be an online battle survival game. Not really my bag, because what this really means is that you will feel obligated to sign on every day and spend hours collecting resources and making sure your dinos are fed, and your base hasn't been trashed while you and your team was away. Baby sitting, basically. No thanks.
The direction it has gone through in development leaves VERY much for players like myself to be desired. The best moments came from awesome team planning where you work hard to knock out this T-Rex together... to spend the next 30 minutes babysitting it while you wait through the taming process. It had it's thrilling moments where you were worried you might lose everything. Where you managed to escape the clutches of death or came in for the rescue. This isn't what the game is about though. It is about endless grinding on a grind tredmill. It is about poorly designed mass-multiplayer mechanics where your base is vulnerable to attack while you are offline and you have to login every day to perform base maintenance. I would not go back and buy it at it's current price, and especially not with this season pass nonsense.
If you don't have a GeForce 9xx or 10xx series GPU or better, don't put yourself through the frustration.

After around 3000 hours of playing Ark I have decided to write this review, especially now that it is released.
The length of time I have played Ark has definately been an experience I have enjoyed, purchasing it on release to EA (or near as possible) purely because of the Jurassic World movie and game release timing (them WildCard tactics though). As with every game of this magnitude and online multiplayer style there will always be ups and downs. You will have seen a large variety already from the other reviews so I will attempt to sum up a fair amount of them in my own review and potentially credit/discredit them. I will in particular highlight the downsides at the bottom or what other people would claim are the downsides.
The game itself allows you to play from a basis of primitive gameplay where the hunt is real, predators are always out to get you and inexperience will haunt you for a great many hours. My first experience was this harsh world where I would keep taming low level Parasaurs because back then this was the 'in thing' - quick(er) tames so you could go around and survive. The word 'quick' is used in respect to that period of time, where we had twice as long taming times to what you do now, three or four times longer than the evolution events and you hand picked your berries.... we were grateful for those sweet sweet mejoberries. Every time I would log off I would come back to find my dinosaurs dead, repeatedly and never understood why - then one time I log in to see a spino looking through the roof of my wooden cabin with my friend and our immediate reaction is to run as far down the beach as possible, which we later renamed Spino Beach (because of the frequency of those spawns at the time).
The lesson to be learned from this? Your initial hours on Ark are going to be DIFFICULT. It really pressures you into understanding why it is called a SURVIVAL game. You will also find it is a lot easier now than it was when it was originally set up and a hell of a lot less of a grind, but we'll get back to that later.
The creatures that you can tame are numerous and varied and will have defining attributes and roles given to them. Any day you play you can tame a new creature and learn about your setup, what can perform certain activities quickly and what role they should play within your tribe. Gatherers, combat mounts, flying mounts, tanks, mobile bases, exploration - there are so many varieties that when you think you've got what you really need to say you're done, you really aren't. We used to have a lot more imbalances in the dinosaurs that we tamed and used, where health and damage were so ridiculous you could one shot nigh on everything with the raptors, the developers then fixed issues like these so that dinosaurs could have more of a 'tier-system' such as raptor-carno-rex-giga (from weakest to strongest) and then alongside this tier system each had a more unique role (raptors were good for hit and run tactics, rex's for tanking, carnos for knockback whilst fighting and giga's because they are death machines).
To more customise the dinosaurs to specific stat requirements that you set you are now able to breed them as well! When you breed dinos for their specific roles you often find yourself nigh on constantly using them for a period of time. My personal favourite is an anky we named Scuba Mallet, he had high physical damage and a decent oxygen stat, so shallow water oil nodes etc were easy to harvest for us and when taking the anky up a mountain we could harvest superior amounts of metal to what we could with just a tamed ankylo. Best of all, with imprinting you were able to increase its stats further and also form your own fist-bump buddy bond with your dinosaur. When imprinted to the full 100% you could dish out roughly 2.4 times as much damage before your dinosaur got killed as compared to when it has no imprint. That is huge when you find yourself in a predicament you didn't expect to occur.
Ontop of all of this, you get to move through different tiers of equipment and buildings. Starting from thatch beginnings hoping that no dinosaurs nearby would target you to building stone castles and then metal monster buildings, capable of holding back all but well armed players and the mighty raid creatures (titanosaur). Each tier of building and equipment gradually builds up as you play, allowing you to truly experience your own development and power increments. Primitive weapons can become a thing of the past when you move forwards, beginning to create firearms and eventually end-game futuristic lasers, special featured armour pieces... a true reward for those who survive that far, against beast and man alike. The amount of content overall will bring you extreme amounts of hours of enjoyment, progression and self back-patting with each achievement.
The game is truly one of a kind and something I would highly recommend to anyone looking for a survival game to play. However, I have kept the pros of the game short so that you could make up your own mind, and will now lead on to further points that may back-up or dispute certain 'cons' of the game.
1) The Alpha-Mega-Tribe crisis.
Now this is often featured in reviews as a standing issue that will remove playability and break the game. These are larger tribes that often dictate power struggles because of sheer PLAYER NUMBER and therefore MAN HOURS and by smaller, more toxic behaviour tribes considered 'UNFAIR'. All of this is solveable - form a larger tribe, make alliances, play on an unofficial server. This argument for this making the game bad is void.
2) Legacy Server/New Server Argument
Slightly more understandable, those whom have survived this long and have made serious progress will be upset by their servers getting wiped especially when they shouldn't have been (15-20 people still playing on the server at every moment in time). The limited time frame to move their stuff was definately a horrid factor. However, the new servers present a solution to problem one - no alphas and megas moving their stuff across to new servers and if they are in clusters, no mega-tribes period. So some pros and some cons with this.
3) Optimisation
A lot of people will tell you the game is as poorly optimised as it was 1 or 2 years ago. It really isn't. Sure the optimisation could have been done a lot better before the game is released, but it is nowhere near the problem it was when the game first came out and through a lot of the time after that. Some duping bugs may need to be fixed and the transfer system will cause some lagg... but with 30-40 people online all forcing a server to do math across tames, crafting, resource checks and updates, transferring dinosaurs (which will cause the most issues) you can expect some lagg and some crashing. As for the people giving their specs on their PCs and saying you can't get a solid framerate... I'm running a laptop with a GTX 860M, 8gig RAM and I7 4710MQ @ 2.50ghz, and getting 40-50 fps on a mixture of medium and low settings pretty much solidly... I can't understand why you can't get a 50-60 fps on a PC with much more capable hardware and higher graphical settings.
4) Pricing of £50 and sale of DLC during EA
This one is possibly the most logical of the arguments presented so far. The pricing is a bit steep for it's current state - even under the excuse of Retail Parity. I would suggest this game is more worth £35-40 with the scorched earth DLC included. The optimisation isn't what it needs to be to have the price tag it currently has. The paid-for DLC during the EA was also a bit of an uncool move... but is a lesson learned and not to be repeated.
5) Few dinosaurs are obselete
Despite having the tier system in place for some dinosaurs, there are a few which become obselete very quickly in my opinion as they don't have any advantages over some counterparts (parasaur/trike < iguanodon for example).
Definite Recommendation for this game.

Oh boy.. It's been four years, I'm not sure if I'm ready to do this yet.
Okay, well, enough is enough.
Warframe, why or why not?
Well, first of all I will tell you to anyone who has never played FTP, there are advantages and disadvantages to having this system.
GRAPHICS: Warframe is an astounding looking game, since DE's Engine 2.0 way back when, the game is absolutely mesmerizing with the multitude of lights and colors. You personally will never find a better looking FTP, and I am willing to challenge that.
GAMEPLAY: While missions in Warframe, being located on the nodes of each planet in our system (and moreso) are a bit tedious when you've come to learn which ones are the best for grinding gear, but Digital Extremes I believe understood this prior to a couple years with the introduction of their new quests, which feature characters, emotion, and a load of different activities that change the style of the game.
PROGRESSION: Warframe has a system called "Mastery Ranks", maximum highest level for those overachievers is MR 31. Mastery Ranks in Warframe are achieved the same way most other games have, by enemies which give affinity. Unlike most games though, at the end of each Mastery Rank, the player has to complete a specific test to ensure their ability to move on. If players fail the test after 3 tries, then he/she/it will be prompted to try again in 24 Hours time, counting down from the time that the player ended the failed attempt.
GEAR: While playing warframe, players will be collecting not only be collecting frames themselves, but as well as three main classes of weapons. (Below)
Primary: Assault Rifle, Bow, Shotgun, Sniper Rifle, Explosives, & Energy Based Weapons.
Secondary: Handcannons, Crossbows, Explosives, kunais, shurikens, etc.
Melee: Fist weapons, 1H Swords, 2H Swords, Hammers, Sword & Shield, Nunchucks, etc.
Typically, weapons and frames in Warframe must be built through the foundry system in-game which takes time to complete, but by throwing a bit of money at their screen, they can get the weapon instantly.
FREE-TO-PLAYNESS?: Yes, it is completely possible to grind every piece of equipment in the game (with an exception to some timed exclusives) completely without spending a dime on the game. However, if players desperately want to make their grind faster, which believe me, it becomes tempting from time to time, then they can give money to RNGesus for the ability to buy gear. However, being around for awhile, I've learnt how crappy the USD to Platinum rate is, and this game, if you really aren't willing to play it at all, will suck up money like a vacuum.
That's basically my overall for Warframe, feel free to PM me with questions that I will answer back in moments notice because I don't have a life.

I'm a firm believer in the fact if you spend hours and hours on a game you are getting your money's worth so therefore you would think after 312 hours I should give it a Yes as I've clearly gotten my money's worth. Unfortunately, this game is nothing more than a time vampire, it is so badly designed in terms of leveling and crafting I've never gotten to the final tier legitimately (w/o using single player multipliers).
When the game first came out in early access I jumped right onto it and me and a couple of friends spent hours building crafting, taming, but we never really got far, at least nowhere near as far as others on the server. It simply got the point the grind was far too much and we got bored. 2 of us then tried again not too long ago on a server with multipliers and STILL the same thing happend, we got bored, trying to reach a tire so far even with multipliers.

The only realistic way of playing this game is to have a dedicated team of 6+ players on every day, still however you will spend most of your time gathering resources, taming dinosaurs to gather resources faster, building machinery to process resources, in order to build better items for gathering resources so you can build better machinery to process resources and only then you are about 1/2 way to building what you want to build. the entire game is just gathering resources to help you gather resources faster!

The trailer is so misleading, yes, what you see is in game and possible but it NEVER HAPPENS, these giant battles in the trailer of tek dino vs tek dino, any players in a battle like that, should it ever happen would last about 5 seconds. Some dinosaurs are so unbelievably powerful it makes other dinosaurs obsolete, the trailer shows tek dinos fighting each other I know would be over in seconds.
I wanted this game to be good i really enjoyed this game but I simply dont have the time and patience to spend days and days reaching the final tek level having as base and an army of dinosaurs knowing it can all be taken away from me in minutes when a player who has more free time then me attacks while I'm offline.

As for PvE what's the point on building 1/2 of the stuff available if you are not fighting other players? I wanted to love this game it had so much going for it, sadly in my view, the developers instead of trying to re-balance the game to fix issues like this, they just add more and more content. More maps, dinos, weapons, all pointless if the game itself is fundamentally flawed.
If you have a LOT of free time and a group of people to play with, maybe host your own game for yourselves and have play fights with each other. PvP online is brutal, days of work gone in moments. Otherwise just save your money, it's not worth the price tag anymore now they jumped it up to £50!

At more than 1,000 hours logged this is the single game I play most frequently. It is fun, but not overly complicated. There is a lot of variety in gear. It's free to play. There is no pay 2 win, and the majority of game modes are a lot of fun to play. You can go for the team experience by playing with others, or you can solo to content when you don't want to engage in team play. Has an easy to use trade system for tradable items. Also, the graphics are stellar.
That being said, the biggest negative is that the game is very grindy. If you hate having to repeat the same mission multiple times to aquire the exact drop you're looking for, then this game probably isn't for you. As an example, say you want the super shiny warframe. Well, you have to repeat a regular mission to acquire the keys to get to the special mission which drops the shiny warframe. Then you repeat the special mission ad infinitum until you acquire all the parts for the shiny warframe. It's largely RNG based, so you can luck out and get what you need in the first run or you can go for hours without acquiring a single needed drop. Drop tables can be real confusing and useless too. Drop tables can be frustrating. Not game breaking frustrating, but definately frustrating.
They do have real world currency, like all free MMO's do these days, and you can use that currency to purchase the equipment without grinding for it. There are no stat boosts to bought equipment, it's literally only to save you time. You can also use said real world currency to purchase things in trade chat that you don't want to grind for.
Most players only use the real world currency for cosmetic items. Which there is a large selection of cosmetic items to purchase. This brings up another draw back, cosmetic items are only available for real world currency. They do some charity cosmetics for the poor players on holidays. Like holiday themed color pallet's, but it's basically all gonna cost you real world money. If you're cool not looking awesome then you don't need to worry about this. Also, they usually have a sale on cosmetics once a year. So it's best to save your real world currency till the sale hits.
Don't lose hope though. You can earn the real world credits through trading. You can't trade with in game currency, only in real world currency. So if you spend a lot of time grinding, you can essentially earn your cosmetic items by trading the weapons/parts/blueprints you don't want on the trade chat. I've heard of serious traders acquiring a couple thousand real world currencies per month. It does require an investment of time, but the option is available if you decide you don't want to invest cash into the game.
Overall, I would recommend the game. I find it fun to play. Plenty of acheivements to unlock. Lots of content to go through. Typically it's decent writing and it's a great looking game. Very active community. So give it a shot. It's free, so you really only will lose a bit of time if you decide you hate it. =)

The game is very grindy, RNG heavy, and requires a shtload of investment if you wanna make any real progress. So if you have a life then avoid this game lol. There's been times where other players have p*ssed me off (which is any online game really) but I'll get to that at the bottom of this review.
You are a Warframe, aka "Tenno" (think of a space ninja lol). There are enemy factions at war with each other. Your job is to fight them. You can do spy missions, defense missions (defend cryostasis pod), exterminate missions (kill all enemies), etc. At the end of these missions you get rewards like blueprints to make weapons and new warframes, component parts, credits (in-game currency), mods (which you can equip on your weapons and warframes.... mods like Melee damage +90%, etc). You can customize the colors of your weapons and warframes, customize the interior of your spaceship, you can have a sentinel or pet to assist you in battle, just all kinds of cool stuff here and there. Then there's this other currency called Platinum, which you have to buy with real money, or another way to get Platinum is to farm for prime parts to sell to other players. You need this if you run out of space to use weapons and warframes, or if you want to buy accessories for your appearance, speed up the building process of weapons, warframes, etc.
Personally what I think is a pain in the az, are the wait times you have to endure when building sh*t. OH WHAT'S THAT? You FINALLY got all the parts to build the warframe or weapon you've been wanting? It'll only take 3 f*ckin' days to build it :D Don't like waiting that long? Spend some plat to speed it up! Don't have plat? Welp..... guess you'll just be waiting then :D ....... or you can.... you know, buy some plat? :D Oh and don't forget to take your Master Rank test to increase your rank to use better weapons, etc! Oh you failed? Welp...... 24 hour wai..WHAT THE F*CK!!!
Then of course before you can even build your stuff you need the parts first, which requires mindless grinding and a chunk of time. And there's no guarantee you'll actually get the specific parts you want because of the RNG system. Like for example, there's Prime versions of Warframes and weapons you can get, and in order to get them you need to get relics (objects that you obtain from doing missions which hold specific prime parts within them). To get the prime parts from the relics you need to do Void Fissure missions, which is basically you fighting these holy looking azholes and getting them to drop this stuff called reactant which will crack open the relic once you have 10 reactant. Sounds easy, but the problem is that there are 6 prime parts in the relic, and the game randomly picks an item out of the relic. Or if you're playing with 3 other people the game will randomly pick 1 prime part from each persons relic, thus making farming a bit easier. So that gives you an idea of how time consuming this process can be when you're trying to farm for something specific. This game is nothing but poke and hope and saying "Hey guys look at this stuff I have that you don't have", and definitely isn't for the impatient lol. That's all I've been doing for almost 700 f*ckin hours, not that I'm complaining but yeah this will suck the soul out of you and possibly turn you into a Warframe crackhead.
As for the Warframe Community, this game surprisingly has some really nice people that are willing to help you out if you're not afraid to ask. And in a way I guess it makes sense considering this game literally doesn't teach you sh*t, doesn't handwalk you at all, barely gives you any instructions as to what the f*ck is going on and how to play the game. I had to look up most information on the internet, the Warframe Wiki and a bunch of YouTube videos. I think the developers need to step it up in that department as well as other aspects. As mentioned above, I'm very asocial and hate people but this game kinda' showed me that not everybody on the planet is a d*khead with the mindset of a 12 year old. One random guy saw me asking for help in the region chat, decided to personally message me, and spent like 400,000 credits to upgrade some mods for me and spent a bit of Platinum to help me out. Completely shocked me I'll be honest. ALTHOUGH, some of the players on here are big babies.... like actual manchildren no joke.
There are warframe players in this game with Elitist mentalities that will throw fits when you don't play the game the way they want you to play, the "hardcore math on paper tryhards" and it's quite annoying... especially for someone like me. It's very rare that you encounter these turds, but every now and then it happens. Like this one time I was playing as Valkyr Prime (a very melee heavy warframe) and was doing a Sortie mission called Mobile Defense, where you have to go to a spot and kill the enemies and keep them from destroying data you're protecting. I was playing with 3 other randoms and this guy was btching because I was getting most of the kills, said he can't stand Valkyr and told me I need to pick a better warframe lol. I'm sorry but last time I checked I thought it was Valkyr's job to go around and tear sh*t apart? lol I mean honestly it's not my problem if you're slow at killing enemies, but I'm the one that needs to pick a better frame? Don't whine and b*tch to me, go cry to the developers and tell them to nerf Valkyr if you don't like it lol. On that note, I think I need to take a break from this game, because f*ck anxiety XD
I do enjoy the game though, I'd be lying if I said I didn't, so thumbs up.

One of, if not the best first person "melee fighting", middle-ages game you'll find.
If you like games like Dark Messiah Of Might And Magic, The Elder Scrolls for their level of immersion during combat, you might like this game. Chivalry delivers this even better by making the slashes, thrusts and blocks feel very powerful.  The swinging feels just right, while a game like Skyrim can feel kind of slow.
There is a lot you can do with the mechanics. You have about seven ways to attack your foe but combined with the right mouse-motions and timing the opportunities are larger than you might think.
There are the basic game-modes(FFA,TD,D,CTF,HTF,a rush(complete a task to go further) like mode and dueling("1on1"), and enough maps for some diverse fighting. Sometimes you can use your surroundings(catapults, pits, spikes) to your advantage. A lot of the European weapon types of the middle ages are to be found. I would have loved to see more Arabic, African and East-European weapons.
Of course this game is purely multiplayer, there is some kind of story, told through events and maps(and the tutorial), but that's just a reason for the action.
There are some minor silly things like very slow swinging stats on the greater weapons.
Playing this game can be quite aggravating, especially with bad performance or a high ping. The community is not the best either, if you are the kind that stays away from popular games because of this, you might look elsewhere.
I have some minor performance issues on my machine(which runs other games of this generation without complaint).
The graphics are well enough for a game like this. There is a lot of gore which fits the setting.
The audio adds to the high level of immersion, but does not stand out to me.
The DLC makes the mechanics even better, but feels not as balanced and is even worse in performance. And of course there is not much of a “setting”.

This is probably the best MMO currently on the market, but it's certainly not your traditional MMO. If you've played Spiral Knights it may not look similar, but it surprisingly is the best replacement if you want an MMO that's still getting.. y'know.. content that's not just cosmetics? Sure the gameplay and combat is different, but the system itself is very similar, play it and you'll see what I mean.
So, why do I call this the best MMO currently on the market? Simple, the community is active and passionate and rather friendly (ignore the occasional troll on the region chat almost everyone's been friendly to me), the developers are also passionate and release quite a bit of content rather frequently, as I'm typing this it's been less than a week since we got an update and they already announced the next one saying it should be out by the end of the year, not to mention it'll contain a lot of content a lot of players including myself have been wanting.
The gameplay feels like a mix of a third person shooter such as Gears of War and a hack and slash game like Devil May Cry, and it works really well, the enemy veriety is decent and is still being added to, environments also work like Spiral Knights because there are multiple presets for individual areas that are then stitched together to randomly create a massive map, and then there's the Plains of Eidolon, the first open world section to the game, and I've basically done all there is to be done there so I can guarantee there's a lot of stuff there for you to enjoy. Plus the game look reeaally good, like, AAA game good, and when it comes to quality overall looking at today's AAA games I'd say it's even better.
Now I've been spouting nothing but pros so far, so let me get into some of the problems I have with this game: THE ♥♥♥♥ING MASTERY GRINDING... I swear, there's been no level system that has frustrated me this far, because it doesn't have to do with skill, nor experience, not even familiarity with the game.. it literally is how many weapons you've leveled, and trust me that is NOT fun to level up a bunch of kinda crappy weapons compared to your main just to be able to have a few more in game bonuses. Also there is a lack of balance in the game too, I have mentioned a bunch of kinda crappy weapons just now, and t hat's because most of the game's weapons are useless unless you're playing on Earth (the lowest level area) which sure would make sense for new players, but you'll always go to the best weapons even if there's other supposedly "best" weapons, the best scythe in the game right now for example is pretty♥♥♥♥♥♥compared to say the best greatsword, sure there's a large selection of good gear, but most of the gear is just mastery fodder once you really start getting further into the game, which sucks. Then there's items such as Nitain, my gosh is this the worst ♥♥♥♥ing game design I've ever seen, not everyone can play all day every day, some later game items require this resource to craft but you can only get it from alerts which are basically temporary missions that pop up and give special rewards that change every couple of hours/minutes depending, people say you can get Nitain from another mission type but I've tried for hours and didn't get♥♥♥♥♥♥ and there's only like 4 Nitain every 24 hours supposedly that is just terrible.
But now let's compare to other MMOs I've played in recent years and I'll explain why I love this game the most, although some of this will be very opinionated: First there's the combat, so many MMOs resort to you just clicking on an enemy to auto attack, or having to focus on an enemy and press a button to attack them specifically, or maybe press number keys to trigger anythingother than a regular attack. Warframe has a detailed and intense combat system that may not be perfect but it doesn't make me want to go to sleep, it's active combat, seriously I'd prefer menu based combat rather than most MMOs' half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥combat system that's just boring to me. Then there's setting and lore, so many MMOs I've played have a rather boring or traditional setting, whether sci fi or fantasy, Warframe is indeed sci-fi but it's different, maybe on the surface you can already tell but it goes even deeper, and I just find that they really put a lot of effort to make this world feel unique despite it still technically being the world we live in in a way, just many years in the future. Then there's the community, and let me tell you OHH BOY IS IT ACTIVE! Seriously, there's so many MMOs with such a small amount of players still playing, this game doesn't seem to be running out any time soon.
Overall this game isn't perfect, but as for MMOs like I said I think it's the best option on the market right now, it has quality, it's fun, it has a passionate and active dev team and community that just fuel the awesomeness nonstop, and hey it's free, so you have nothing to lose by giving it a shot <3

Ok, It staggers me that this game gets so many negative reviews based on the price.
Yes, the full sale price is high, but conisdering the amount of game time people have in it, thats hardly unreasonable. The majority of people writing the reviews already bought the game at Early Access, therefore didnt pay that price. So why complain?

For those with a lesser PC, dont expect graphical miracles, but for those who do, the scenery in this game is stunning. There are building bugs yes, there are random moments where its apparent the laws of Physics havent been taken into consideration, yes, but then there are Dinosaurs, Wyverns and Griffins ... so you take the rough with the smooth.
I play solely on an Unofficial modded server, with an amazing community and some awesome people. And *that* is where the enjoyment comes in for me.
If you dont want to pay £50 for this game, then dont. But, given that the majority of people I play with have upwards of 1500 hours, i think that speaks volumes about the depth and playability of this game.

I'm a little bit confused about all the reviews - positive and negative - that refer to this game as something outside of, beyond, or somehow different than a game. What makes Clicker Heroes so great is that, despite the reputation of the genre it is placed in, it is very much a game. Perhaps it's a very simple one in that you only click or buy auto-damage upgrades to defeat enemies, but you still defeat enemies. There is still a concept of bosses, difficulty, and progression. It's unlike other "idle games" I've played in that you can't really leave it idle, because if you do, you simply won't win. You have 30 seconds to beat a boss, and if you can't do it in 30 seconds, you can't move on, and eventually you WILL hit a boss you can't beat. So right there we have a sense of a "video game" and I don't agree that it's just repetitive work. There is much repetition to increase your levels and when you boil the game down to its core, it really is just about increasing levels, but the diversity of the upgrades and the added gilding, ancient, mercenary, and relic systems create an engaging experience beyond just leaving a window closed and letting it count a number up for you.
Anyway, I personally love the game. Nice balance and great features, all for free. It's a pretty crazy good deal.

Ok, for all you people complaining that Clicker Heroes sucks because it requires active playing: First of all, once you get far enough in the game, you can choose to do an Idle Build or an Active Build. And if you do an Idle Build, you wont have to participate nearly as much as with an active or no build (assuming progression mode is on). So if you're saying activity in the game is a bad thing, you haven't played enough and/or you're just being r00d. And second of all, why would being active be a bad thing? I mean, 99.99% of clicker games out there DO require a ton of idleness, but clicker heroes doesn't.  Complaining about this difference is like saying Undertale sucks because it's unique.
Another thing people complain about is that there is no point to the game. This is actually true for a lot of idle games, but again, clicker heroes gets special treatment. Clicker Heroes seems boring at first, but once you grind past level 120 or so and ascend, the action starts to pick up, and it becomes really fun really fast. Additionally, almost all games get boring at times, so you can't really say this boringness is unusual.
HOWEVER, there are a few bad things I have to say:
Firstly, the mobile version. The mobile version of this game is... just... unbearably unsatisfying and dangerous. I say 'dangerous' because people all over Reddit are saying that a recent update has a trojan in it. Not 100% sure if this is true or not, but I imagine so since the game crashes when I start it on my phone. Another thing is that people are losing their save files left and right because the save system in the game is so messed up, and either can't read the data properly or the data is written incorrectly. I know this review is supposed to be for the PC version, but the mobile issues need to be mentioned!
Rubies. 'Nuff said.
So overall, I recommend this game, just be sure to stay away from the mobile version and to not get tempted to buy the timelapse, since it's the single dumbest way to spend rubies. I hope you found this helpful!

The game moves blazingly fast, but is nearly infinite, if not actually infinite.
There are a few slow points during which the gold required to purchase the next tier of heroes suddenly increases exponentionally, which can cause frustration.

If you're a fan of medieval combat, then this game is already starting out in your good graces. If you're also a fan of nuanced yet simple combat mechanics which are easy to learn, yet hard to master, then you're on the right track here.
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare is an epic first-person (though you can change to third-person in some servers) melee-centric multiplayer game of battle. Ranged options are available for those who wish to use them, though they do not fare well at close range. There are a few modes included for the multiple maps, such as Team Deathmatch, Arena, King of the Hill and Objective. Team Deathmatch and King of the Hill are your standard fare modes, being basically just what you'd expect. Arena mode pits players on two teams against each other in a fairly small, trap laden arena with no respawns in a fight to the last side standing. Objective mode, as its name suggests, tasks teams with various objectives to complete, such as one team assaulting a village and killing its civilian population while the other team must push back and defend them.
All of the modes are fun to play, and the rewarding combat mechanics really pay off with practice, giving victories against other skilled players a satisfying feeling rather than a sense of simple quick reflexes. A raise of the sword may deflect an incoming blow, while a perfectly timed deflection leaves your opponent staggered and defenseless. Feint an attack, stopping just before you connect, to proc an opponent's parry before going in with a true, fatal blow to the head. Relish in the gurgling death cry as you stand victorious, then move forth to a new foe. Death from a far away arrow or a tossed tomahawk can seem a bit cheap at times, but no kill is an unearned one, as archers are constantly exposed and throwable weapons are limited in supply and simultaneously hard to aim under duress.
It's hard to beat the adrenaline rush of a small army, iron-clad and weapons raised, sprinting forth and shouting their battle-cries before two sides clash together in a mess of steel and blood. If you're willing to put in the time to learn the strategy and rhythm of combat, and don't mind a relatively small pool of maps, then Chivalry: Medieval Warfare will prove to be a rewarding and exhilirating experience, and is definitely a must-buy. However, if you are looking for a reflex based game of twitchy-madness, look elsewhere.

I got Ark: Survival Evolved back in June, 2015. At a first glance, this was going to be an interesting game, and I thought that perhaps I could persuade my friends to join me in my adventure. Boy was I wrong, they hated survival games.
So I set off alone, discovering the vast island that was back then, running from low-level hostile animals or just preying on the usual berry-bush occasionally. I met some people in the game who quickly realised I were new, and invited me to their tribe. I joined them, and they taught me all the basic game mechanics that was available back then. Sooner or later, I lost contact to them, but they hooked my interest for the game itself.
Fast forward, through multiple updates and now, finally, the actual release of the game, I can say its been two enjoyable years. Yes, there has been times where I stopped playing altogether, all stemming from different reasons.
Those reasons include;
Cons;
No Friends Available, and most servers being hostile-themed PvP.
Sheer lag and overall bad optimization. You have probably seen this by now if you're roaming the reviews. Ark needs better optimization.
Growing bored of it, but I would quickly return after a few updates where the new animals would appear.
---
However, the game also have some beautiful, and amazing pros;
An exquisite
, with the devs being active and events (Such as tournaments or competitions)
Amazing possibilities when it comes to building, or taming your newfound army of animals.
As mentioned, frequent updates. (This also includes nice DLC)
Community Mods.
I could go on and on, theres so many aspects that could be discovered, but, I will leave that to you, the person reading this review.
If you are still unsure whether you should buy this game, go ask yourself some things first?
If you answered yes to most of these, go on ahead. I'm sure you will enjoy Ark: Survival Evolved
If you are still not sure, go read more reviews on this page, or ask somebody you know who have tried it before.
Thank you, for reading this review.
I hope you may have a wholesome and unique day,

I think it is finally time for me to write a review of this game after about 300 hours of gameplay (some are played while offline so didnot count)
This game had and still has a a ton of potential, with it's nice graphics and very good sound design that complement the good features in gameplay. It has a lot of dinos to kill or tame (definitely kill for me) and you can play pvp for the complete live or die experience against other players. It worth noting however that everything in thing (And I mean literally everything) has something bad attached to it.
Let's start by what is good about the game:
- Graphics are awesome if you crank them up to high or epic and the sounds are very good in the game. Every dino has it's own distinguishable sound which is very nice.
- The systems in game are good. Food and thirst are good in adding depth to the survival element of the game along with the stamina meter that limits the actions that can be done.
- I am especially fond of the construction system that enables the construction of all sorts of amazing structures and large fortresses.
- Combat in the game is acceptable but there is definately a lot of room for improvement.
- The maps are varied and nice to travel and explore by air.
- The crafting is nice and offers the chance of making a ton of cool stuff.
Now that I made an impression let's start with the bad stuff:
- This game requires a computer straight from the future to be able to hit 60 fps on high and it looks like garbage on low which still runs in a very bad state on low end computers. And why did the performance on my old computer increase when I increased the graphics? I will never know. This is not a good example of a well optimized game and gave me a very bad impression of unreal engine 4 to be honest but gears of war 4 was quick to fix that.
- About the food, thirst and stamina. While good on paper and good in early gameplay. They are an absolute annoyance in late game and during combat. And since temperature affects food and water consumption, some areas in game are an absolute no no for new players due to the high consumption of food because of the extremem cold for example which is a real shame since the cold regions have a lot of cool stuff. The stamina meter is very annoying because it depletes really quickly and even after leveling ti up, there will still be a lot of sticky situations.
- While I like the construction in the game, I have to admit that there a lot of wierd things about it. Why can't I pick up a bed after I placed it for example? and what is up with the materials required for construction, they make no sense sometimes. Why does a gate that is around 24 meters high need to be made in a smithy (a table with a hammer)? and why the hell does it weigh less in my pocket than a metal pike?.
- Let's talk about the combat a little bit here. The combat is barely passable and early game can be considered good. There are no heavy attacks here, it's all bash bash bash. And why does the sword make the same sound a club while attacking?. A lot of times, you can't tell if your attack actually hit or not specially with the large creatures with all the camera shake. Small animals are knocked back with each hit which make it extremely annoying in some cases. Sometimes when dinos hit, they can molecularely bypass the wall I am standing behind and hit me for some reason. The hit detection is extremely wierd and I once got hit from a dino that was underground (I could only see it's name under me).
- Whiel the maps are varied and nice to explore, this only applies if you are exploring by air or on a strong dino. These devs made sure to include everything possible to be able to kill you when on foot, it is extremely dangerous. There are dinos that make you sleep with around 2-3 hits (really hate them), there are dinos that steal from you, there are dinos that attack your tamed dinos and can easily kill you on top of them, there are dinos that take you for a ride in their mouths, dinos that drain your stamina, too maky to count. And at night you can not see anything and it is extremely dangerous to do anything alone.
- I like crafting but the material requirements are absurd. 95 iron ingots (weight is 95 units) are required with other stuff to make a simple rifle (weight 15 units)?? and don't even think about adventuring with all the nice weapons and armor like in the videos on official servers, when you die you lose everything and these stuff takes ages to make on the normal gathering rate. And why the hell does 900 stone (weight 450) + 900 wood (weight 450) + light stuff = a gate that weight only 4 units in my pocket???? Why does a raft weight more than a whole small hut made of metal in my pocket?? how can a lathing machine make an assault rifle? (engineers will understand) there a lot of logic problems in the crafting.
Speaking of logic, This game murders physics and brutalizes logic, For example, I can punch a dino to a pulp and then force feed it for a while and suddenly it's loyal to me, I can also build a whole structure made of stone on a bloody raft, and that structure was two stories high. For some reason there are stone pipes that float in mid-air. There a lot of logic problems in this game but in the right sontext, it could be fun.
There is still more to say but here is the summary:
Game can be extremly fun specially with friends. community can be very aggressive in game and there is a 100% chance to be raided every day. Be prepared for bad performance and know that the game will feel very unfinished. Tons of small problems and some bugs. Developers keep adding new stuff but for some reason ignore the optimization and performance. This is a game that had DLc while in ealy access (keep that in mind). Sweet deal for 10-20$ but a slap in the face for 60$.
