This game had a lot of promise when I first heard about it - Decided I wanted to get hold of it and see what it was like - Waited for the sale and picked it up for £11.49 - I was first met with the horror of the game's size at the time - If memory serves correctly it was arround 100+GB. I installed it anyway accepting that it was a large game.
Started it up, made a singleplayer game to see how it runs to which I was met with a fixed 15fps on the recommended settings. Dropped all the settings from the recommended "very high" down to medium with no change, moved them to very low; fps got worse. Thought "Okay, maybe everyone plays it like this?"
Tried to join a server with no idea what was happening, murdered by a giant bird of sorts around 10 minutes in, followed by players murdering me instead  before I gave up.
Proceeded to make my own SP server to just get to grips with the game, learn how to do things and so on - Found a Triceratops stuck in a tree (Bug) so i hit him with a hammer until he fell unconscious then tamed him. Feeling proud of myself I thought I'd leave it there for the day assuming I could just hit load it all up again to go back to my old game.
All my data was gone, assumed I'd done something stupid or missed a large save button - I couldn't find any explanation
I gave up trying by this point, the poor optimization, large size, vast bugs, awful framerate were just irritating me,
I kept an eye on the content of the game to see if they were adding any new dinosaurs/beasts, fixing bugs and doing anything else that a player would be happy to hear. I then find they were adding *sigh* Power Armor and laser weapons, I thought this had to be an April Fools joke but it wasn't and the content just looks like it's getting more and more ridiculous. The developers don't seem to have a specific direction and just seem to be vomiting ideas into the game after one of them watches a C-List creature feature film on the SciFi channel or something.
I understand that some people are into the whole power armor and laser rifle ideas but it's not really what I wanted out of this. Having a suit with a built in jet pack that you wear while wildly reenacting a 90s rave with a weapon doesn't really speak the word "survival" to me.
Overall I'd give this a 5 or 6/10 - I'm in shock that the developers are gouging customers with a £50 price tag without including Scorched Earth and then following up with a £35 Season Pass? I'd say to people thinking about getting this to wait some time for the game to be properly optimized as well as for the console-like price to go down.

I have barely scratched the surface of things this game offers, but if you're looking for a good mideval sword fighting game, then look no further. 8/10

This is a tough game to review.
Pros:
It's free.
It is an excellent time killer.
It's something to do to entertain your brain when you don't have the time or energy for other options.
It plays itself 90% of the time even when it's closed.
There's more to it than just clicking. There is some strategy to it in selecting Ancients, pursuing achievements for boosts, selecting mercenary quests, which heroes to "gild" (level up), and how to spend your hero souls and rubies in general.
It's mezmerising to watch everything on your screen continously explode in fast succession.
Cons:
There's really no point to it other than wasting time. There's no story. It's endlessly repetitive. And it slows down signficantly once you pass the e100 cost level. Even switching all my "gild" levels to the highest level character and noticing an extreme dps boost, the game still progressed excrutiatingly slow. It's a disappointment after how quickly you can sprint up to a point where things move to a crawl. I'm finding it to slow dramatically around level 1300+. I've spent a lot of souls leveling up ancients as well. I basically only didn't get the clicking-related ones. I just let the DPS heroes play for me to avoid wrist damage.
I had fun figuring out all the angles but eventually I had to question what I was doing with my time.

Some paid games have them but generally these purchases are not too prevalent, in FTP's however these purchases are at the forefront. Logistically this makes sense, a game has to make money somehow right, so the question becomes how many in game purchases is too many? and that's where warframe comes in.
Let me start by saying that warframe is probably the best FTP game that I've ever played on steam, it is one of the only games that i know of that has such an intricate combat system and grandios maps for the player to use/explore all for free. In and of itself that, for me atleast, takes this game to a 8/10 already.
That being said the in game purchases take it back to a solid 4/10. If you want anything new, guns swords skins warframes etc. it can be purchased for the in game currency of platinum, however unlike alot of really bad free to plays this game offers another option. Instead of buying the actual equipment, you can buy the blueprint of the equipment; gather the necessary parts from different areas (certain resources are limited to certain planets but for the most part everythings eventually accessible)(there is however ALOT of grinding/farming to be done as is the case for most FTP's) and then combine them in your foundry. The one drawback of this is that everything and I mean EVERYTHING takes time.
Yes theres the time you take to find the resources or to save up the credits for the blueprint (some bosses also have a chance of dropping certain blueprints) but on top of that there are literal time requirements for every crafting item. this wouldn't be so  bad if we're talking achievable in a day at max but no; at minimum equipment is 6 hours, at maximum so far I've had 3 days, most of the equipment falls into the 12 hour category which isnt overkill but is still annoying. Of course you have the option to rush this process but thats done with, you guessed it, platinum. this becomes even more infuriating in the specific case of crafting a warframe. Instead of using hypotheticals I'll give you an actual example from my gameplay: on venus there's a boss called the jackal, after defeating him you have a 33% chance to be dropped the chasis of the warframe rhino, a 33% chance for the neuroptics of the rhino, and a 22% chance for the systems of the rhino, all three are required to craft the actual warframe the rhino. Now it took me 12 playthroughs of this mission for me to actually acquire all 3 parts, so about 2 hours give or take. Then after gathering all the parts I realized i didn't have enough plastids (a resource i had previously never seen) to craft the systems. So after looking up where to get plastids i found that I needed to go to the planet/moon phobos which was several missions away. after about another 3 hours of completing missions on mars (which unlocks phobos) and actual mission playing on phobos looking for plastids, I had enough. So 5 hours give or take to collect all the ingredients. Now I have to craft all 3, ONE GREAT ASPECT THIS GAME HAS OVER MOST FTP'S IS IT ALLOWS YOU TO CRAFT MULTIPLE THINGS AT ONCE, this cut my waiting time for each object down to 12 hours. Once those 3 were finished I'm able to assemble the rhino, which will take 3 days (all warframes I've seen so far take 3 days to craft). As I type this I still have 24 hours left to complete the crafting of this warframe. In total itll be about 90 hours of time just so I can get a SECOND warframe. The ingame purchases mainly come down to would you rather spend your time or your money, as they always do. There are other things you can do with the plat, for one you only get 12 base colors for your warframe all of which are god awful, and for some price of plat you can buy the rest of the colors in that pack, or one of the other 4 packs. Again this isn't saying i completely deplore this system, as this is a FTP so I understand it's neccesity, I just personally wish they'd toned it back a little.
My next problem is a smaller one, simply put if you have the ability to purchase something right off the bat (not plat but with credits earned in game) then you should be able to access the necessary ingredients. If the game gives me a sword blueprint I shouldn't have to progress 2 planets just to get the stuff for said blueprint. I'm going to leave it at that.
As far as the story goes the voice acting is bland and they reuse one boss 3 times in the first 6 main planets, so that should give you a good idea of what you're dealing with.
All in all if you're looking for a game that costs no money and that you can enjoy thats not TF2 this is an ok choice. Just look at the wiki alot and try to sell stuff to other players at the bazaar.

I think the best place to start is to simply state that I love this game, there are good and bad things about it though.  Over all, the graphics are wonderful, and running around in a variety of worlds filled with dinosaurs you can tame is exciting for sure.  Building a base, and carving out a piece of that world for yourself is difficult, yet rewarding.
That being said I do have a couple of complaints, one of which is the tribe system.   Once you join a tribe they own everything you build, which is hard if you decide you dislike the tribe and want to leave.  It also uses a lot of resources, and can be a bit laggy.  Taming dinosaurs can be super time consuming, as can raising offspring, which makes it all the more frustrating when they can so easily be killed by other dinosaurs, and players if you're on a PvP server.  And lastly, on the public servers it can be extremely difficult to find a place to settle due to so many abandoned projects by other players, some of which quit the game or transferred servers.  In the end though, it's easy to look past those things and really sink your teeth into the game.
My 11 year old nephew who likes watching me play says it's like, "Minecraft with better graphics, and dinosaurs!"  My suggestion is get this game, and get some friends, and pool some money for a private server so that you can control how difficult you want the game to be, and who you have there.  This game is really defined by the people on the server, and having a server full of good friends is a treat.

That said the game is still incredibly accessible and I'm almost finished with a couple prime items myself.
8/10 all around good time. Can recommend.

AGATHAAAA!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
First Person Medieval combat? Done right? Javelins and quarterstaves? Count me in. Chivalry: Medieval Warfare is a brilliant idea actually done right. Setting: It's 1500. Agatha doesn't like The Mason Order. War! And that's about it. 2 teams of feudal infantry face off in free for all, deathmatch, or objective game modes. Players choose from 4 classes.
Vanguard: Polearms and two-handed weapons, meant entirely for brutal banzai charges.
Archer: Fires arrows, fights with a wimpy dagger. No armour; dies quickly. (Doesn't wear a Ghillie suit, thank god)
Man at Arms: Light and nimble: one sword, one shield fighter. Quick, and lightly armoured, dances around enemies.
yooouuuu gguuueeessseeeddd iiiitttttt
Knight: BIG. ARMOURED. SLOW. STRONG. BIG SHIELD. BIG AXE. BIGGER SWORD. BIG ARMOUR.
Choose a class, customize his weapon loadout (axes, throwing knives, swords, smoke bombs, pikes, spears, long swords, broad swords, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ swords, maces, mauls. battle axes, little hields, big shields, slings, bows, crossbows, dagggers.) And enter the fray.
Comabt is first person, based off of blocking, and hitting. Blocks, be it with weapon or shield, must be in ther general direction of the opponents attack, the larger the object, the more room for error. Kicks and shield bashes wear down opponents stamina, ad open up opponetns for cheeky stabs. Attacking is based on a directional slash, swing, or stab; all with varying speeds and damages. This simple yet intuitive system creates complex and intense dulas mano-et-mano, as well as hectic stab-fests in large group melees. Arrows must be drawn back and aimed, flails don't give a rip who they hit, and quarterstaves are useless. All together, you get a hectic and distinct melee combat game which can be described in one word:
FUN!
Simple enough, Chivalry rocks. How does it perform? Textures are quite good, though nothing special. Vistas are well lit, well colored, and quite beautiful. Simply; the game looks great. Frame rate is a bit... meh. In accordance to the graphical fidelity, they seem a bit low. Lower end systems should only expect 30 FPS, and even higher ends can barely scrape 60. Combat is intensive, but not THAT much. Regardless, you can run the game fine, even if framerate occasionally gets a bit wierd. (On a GTX 760, I'm averaging 45FPS in heavy combat. I get almost 90FPS in Battlefield 4.) Opponents' limbs fly off spectacularily, blood splatters, and sowrds clang very pleasingly. Furious war crys, crackling fires, painful screams, it all sounds great.
Overall: A quick, brutal, and FUN hack and slash first person melee fighter, with well thought out sword fighting mechanics, tons of weapons, engaging game modes, and a whole lotta happiness for $20. Get it, on sale; $8 is well worth this joyride.

There is no relevant consequence to something so irrelevant as having to beat anyone in a place that is not real and does not have any bearing in our day-to-day lives.
However, what is really disturbing is that there are droves of these people who do take this game seriously, or even gaming seriously.  I do not think I will even make one dent in their hearts and minds, but I think this effort will somehow affect something.  Their reactions to others to this place of irrelevance who are not on par with their mindset and skill is not merely discouraging, but amazingly violent given the place they are in.  So what?  They are in the heat of the game.

There is nothing important that needs to be achieved.  No one to impress. Nobody, and nobody gives a care about something irrelevant to life like this albeit great, but psychologically exposing game like this or any other competitive game.

Warframe gets by on style alone. Keep that in mind when you fight a boss or clear a mission 20 times in a row to get that one weapon part that won't show it's face. This game is grindy and tedious and repetitive and even a bit glitchy at times. But why do I, as well as millions of other people enjoy playing it so much? Style. Any other game would pull the aforementioned grind off horribly. It takes a team like the one at Digital Extremes, the developers of Unreal Tournament, to make this work. Warframe is one of the only games where you can front flip forward and land on your sword lodged in a space nazi and pump his buddies full of shotgun shells that explode. The combat is fast fluid and fun. The graphics are marvelous even on the lowest settings possible, and it's free to play. The words Free To Play usually has a stigma behind it, as it usually can mean, "Pay-To-Win". Warframe is more along the lines of "Pay-To-Win-Faster", as nearly everything in the game can be acquired without spending real money. Sure, you can buy one of the best guns in the game, but then you still have to level it up, fit it with the appropriate mods, level up the mods, and learn how to use it to the best of your ability.

I gave this game a positive review at one point. That was years ago, when I was new to the game, and legitimately enjoyed playing it now and again.
I recently decided to return to the game, as I'd set the game aside after having to wade through a number of matches where people would do what is called 'dancing': Manipulating the dragging mechanics for weapons, while moving their character around in a way that added extra speed, strength, and ridiculous levels of lexibility to attacks. This meant that players could, effectively, land a one-hit kill on a player behind them, by performing an overhead attack, and then quickly forcing their charcter to look stright up.
Anyway, upon my return, I still found that players were, of course, dancing their way up the scoreboard. Certain weapons, of course, were also insanely overpowered, and certain classes were of course, completely underpowered.
What was once a great game is now sitting here, in my library stewing in its own rancid juices right now. The devs, as well as many moderators, have defended the use of mechanic exploits, and repeatedly say "Dancing is easy to counter, just walk backwards and let your opponent wear themselves out." Easier said than done, as servers have issues with lag, and some players have also been using speed hacks to keep pace with backpedaling players.
My time here was fun while it lasted, despite that time being so short. But I seriously can't recommend this game anymore.

I want to like this game. Heck, I want to love this game. Alas, I simply cannot.
ARK: Survival Evolved has everything to satisfy the survival RPG enthusiast inside anyone. Dinosaurs make up a huge amount of gameplay but when it comes down to it, you can play this game without doing a thing with them and simply treat the beasts as if they were merely apart of the world.
The leveling system is good so long as you know what upgrades and items you are needing next. As a new player I found I was wasting quite a bit of my earned engrams "exp".
Adventuring is fun and risky. Dungeon diving is fun and riskier. My overall experience of ARK, risky if I daresay I had fun. Once you've mastered the basics, everything becomes a chore and on servers with "normal" times for taming dinosaurs and farming materials, you find yourself waking up a week later in♥♥♥♥♥♥stained underwear with your neighbour checking to see if you're still alive all because you wanted to hatch some babies and build a solid defence on your base.
The investment of both money and TIME is ridiculous. It's all the terrible time building applications of a pay to play game with all the best elements of a "you're free to do whatever you want" RPG. (Yes you can change all the settings to speed up all farming elements, but un official servers are another headache)
When you read the other comments on "UNoptimized" and "Price too high", they're not wrong. Don't bother building a rig and spending half an hour changing all your computers settings to make ARK run both smoothly and beautifully. You can run this game as a stable frame rate with playdo graphics, or you can make this game look like real life and enjoy your new screensaver.
I do recommend TRYING this game (get it for free or just watch a lets player) as it is one of a kind and super fun with friends. However I no longer support the developers because they have stayed far too long in early access and now with the "full release" onto consoles and all their new content being spewed out, one must ask..... "Where will they find the time to go back and fix the basics"? and "If mods make this game better, why would I bother with the original"?

Oh ARK, what a wonderful game this was... Before Studio Wildcard decided to become a walking cancer of gaming developers...
To go over the numerous issues, firstly, paid DLC (Thats right, paid DLC in an early access game, what a joke...) but I thought, hey, maybe they're just trying to raise money to focus development, so I gave them a chance... Then they launched it on console.... In Early access ?? Finally, they decided to basically TRIPLE the price before the game launched, claiming it was almost finished. Around this point, and also around the point that they decided to conveniently put the game on sale right as people started quitting because of the HORRIBLE flyer changes and transfer system, I knew this company was becoming awful and to be honest... This game is less refined than when I first bought it about 2-3 years ago.
They kept slamming in content, then never actually refining that content. I'm glad they kept adding in new dinosaurs and stuff for us to play around wth, but then you encounter horrible parts that just ruin the entire game... For starters, the transfer system was added, never really refined. They put a cap on it, woop dee doo, a whole tribe will still show up on your server, and raid everything you spent so long making with their super high level gear and dinos, then just leave after having ransacked everything. That's the transfer system in a nutshell... The main servers are basically unplayable because of this, not even to address the rubber-banding and just general horrible lag you will experience. Dinosaur AI is pretty dumb as well, generally taking stuff down involves "How can I get it stuck into a rock best"?
For balance sense well, they added in boss gear... This♥♥♥♥♥♥in my opinion, is stupid as ♥♥♥♥, I already absolutely detested the Gigas (I would play on private servers with no Gigas to avoid server lag and to have balance) Gigas basically took all the other dinos and said "Lol naa, all of you are now redundant for combat", and then to make this worse they added in boss gear, and basically everything was made redundant because you can rocket jump all over the map, and just one shot punch♥♥♥♥♥♥ or, alternatively, get a rex and equip it with  a ♥♥♥♥ing laser that does a million damage because why not? Starting out new and becoming alpha is basically impossible at this point, because if an Alpha feels threatened, they'll just destroy everything you own in about 4 seconds. The balance in this game is non-existent.
Actually, I say "The alpha will destroy you" actually no, the Alpha will just block off all the caves usually so that you can never access the boss gear without basically paying huge tributes to them for each trip, making grinding the stuff (Which isn't hard, just requires access to the caves and some good sabertooths to farm the caves and dinos to be able to take on the bosses) basically impossible.
The sad part is, this game had so much potential, and at one point, I loved this game, but after all the scummy moves by this company and a game that isn't finished, horribly unbalanced, buggy and generally just price hiked from when it was early access and with more broken content, I fully cannot recommend this game, despite having poured so many hours on it and having loved this game before. £50 is a pure rip off. If I could get back the £15 I paid for it at this point, I would. Had I known what kind of company I was giving that £15 to in the first place, I never would have, giving them money feels the same as if I were to buy an EA game, like I'm giving money to the Devil. Don't buy this game. Let the developers have their game tank, and finally address the community after ignoring every outcry from it, and then buy it after they do fix their act and their game, but for now, don't buy it.

Clicker Heroes is a fun, laid back game, but in my opinion, quite generic.
Allow me to explain.
When I say generic, it doesn't really bring anything NEW to the table. Like most other clicker games, it's "Spam your mouse button, buy some auto-clickers, boom bada bam." Which I'll admit, kind of disappoints me. Now I know that's sort of the point of clicker games, but I would rather spend an hour on a game I like instead of 5 minutes each day, getting on to upgrade a few things and then waiting tomorrow for more currency.
I will admit however that clicker heroes does have its pros. A level system, where you'll fight stronger monsters as you continue through them. It's got a sort of storyline once you piece together the character's little backstories, you can sort of see how they connect to one another, which I always enjoy a good read. Other games like cookie clicker and adventure capatlist don't really have much insight or backstory.
In any case, I do recommend this game for when you're bored and/or have a few minutes to spare and can just drop by and see how everything is going. It's a good game for a laid-back and patient person.

I have a love/hate relationship with this game.  I don't have ANY experience with PVP because i have avoided it from the start due to secondhand experiences of this game's PVP from friends.  Anyway, PROS:
-great variety of dinosaurs, each with unique purposes and roles from penguins that keep you warm  to warpigs that have a healing AOE buff and beyond.
-LOTS of good mods to enhance gameplay to choose from, you can really customize this game to suit your playstyle.
-stunning graphics and incredible, fantastical landscapes.
-Unpredictable and dangerous world to explore, with several large, unique maps to choose from.
-This game will keep you busy. there are several tiers of weapons, armor, mechanisms, etc to explore as you progress further into the game
-a promising storyline that continues to be developed and fleshed out that is akin to something out of a science fiction novel.
-more content is added regularly, almost weekly.
and now the part you've been waiting for, CONS.  now having not much experience with pvp firsthand I only have what i've heard from friends on that matter, although that is most people's biggest gripe.
-The game is horribly optimized with memory leaks and many bugs.  Fatal errors are a common occurance and, as it goes, as of writing this review I cannot join any server due to a fatal error.  High end computers can get 20 fps and stuttering, this game eats through RAM, often in excess of 6gb (even in the low memory 4gb mode).
-the devs have terrible support service. Going through both the steam forums and ark community forums I have seen dozens of different fatal errors posted with only one thread I saw actually receiving moderator/dev attention while the rest are pushed under the rug.  I have heard of many users personally posting support tickets to the devs only to be ignored or set aside for months before receiving any answer.
-The devs are hellbent on balancing pvp to the detriment of all other playerbases be it PVE, private servers, or singleplayer.  this happened with several nerfs and rebalances most notable the dreaded flyer nerf and nerfing many stats like movement speed.  This, of course does nothing to address the underlying issues of PVP and why it is un-FUN.  Players will always find exploits and ways around whatever you remove and it will just make players who appreciated that content disheartened.  Instead, you need to protect new players somehow until they are at a level to fight back against more established players or else many new players simply get frustrated and quit.
-This game vanilla is a GRINDFEST and a half, taking over 100 real-life hours to raise a dragon, for instance.  That to me obviously means those high level types of things are meant to be done in a tribe of multiple players, but still that is 100 hours just to acheive one thing and not everyone has a tribe of teammates to help or that want to help.  Resources are scarce and take much too long to gather on vanilla settings.  It also takes far too long to level up and earn XP on vanilla settings unless you exploit the game and only do the few things that earn the most XP.
-There is nothing to do once you reach end-game unless you PVP.  You get very neat sci-fi tech after beating the bosses, but what do you do with that tech?  go beat the bosses again?  Maybe once you reach that level, it takes you to an even more challenging world where you feel vulnerable even with that high level stuff. So really there is no motivation to attain the end-game stuff other than "WOAH, COOL".
-The bossfights, at least from what I have experienced, have been made ridiculously hard due to the devs response to people exploiting the bosses pathing, etc. to kill them.  Yes, they should be challenging, but you should be able to beat the bosses with a modest investment of time. but how it is currently you have to grind for 100+ hours in many cases in order to put the odds as much in your favor as possible and stick to very few limited meta options to even stand a chance against the bosses.  Of course on your own server you can tweak the settings to make these bossfights as easy or challenging as you like.  I just don't think the end game content should be locked behind such a distant, unmoving wall, or at least give new players a taste of this gear to entice them towards working towards it more.
all in all, This game can be a beautiful experience when you know how to set it up right, leading to unforgettable close-calls, hilarious antics, and intense, frantic fights with or without friends.  But at the same time, good luck with PVP and that whole mess, and beware the many bugs! They will come for you eventually. (and i don't mean the bees).

My Not Recommended is based on playing about 100 hours SINGLE PLAYER (vanilla settings) followed by 1000+ hrs SOLO PVE on official servers. Since there are several modes of play available my recommendation is directed at like-minded individuals. A pvp focused player in a tribe would naturally have different goals and experience the player interactions quite differently.
My rig: i7-4770, GTX 970 4Gb, 16 Gb ram, 500Gb SSD, game settings such that I get 40-70fps depending on in game environment. I also played on a wimpy laptop when away from home with 15-25fps with low, low, low settings. I called it crayon mode.
Pros:
Dinos are awesome, good audio, improved graphics over time, almost too much stuff to do - explore, tame dinos, hunt dinos, build, breed, trade, collect, meet new people, help noobs, join in rescue missions, help find lost tame dinos, etc., etc.
The game design is such that you need to see how to use all the resources at your disposal in an integrated way that results in the efficient production of higher level/quality weapons, medicines, buildings, clothing and so on. Some of these paths to the end game are quite challenging - it's like running your own company.
ORP, Offline Raid Protection, helped prevent a dino disaster due to the occasional wild dino spawning inside your base while you were logged off. While logged off nothing of yours can be damaged. Although your tame dinos can be set to defend themselves it can get complicated and messy depending on what wild dino shows up. The Alpha version of wild dinos can slaughter a lot of your tames before being neutralized. The more common thing ORP prevents in pve is keeping a passive-aggressive neighbor from provoking a wild dino to come crash your base while you're not logged in.
Cons:
1. Up to the Aug. 29 release server lag/rubber banding/hiccups was a real and constant issue. I played on The Island map (na pve official 35) and it occured the whole 6 months I was on that server. Player complaints about these problems were common in the global chat. Pings would go all over the place, global chat would have 6 people complain about it at the same time, etc., etc. I also played on Scorched Earth (na pve SE 794) and at first it was almost lag free but started to exhibit that problem more and more. The reasons people claimed it happened included high player count, high building count, high dino count, bad server programming, bad internet link to the servers, blah, blah, blah. Not fixed as of Aug. 28
2. The grind - it can take quite a bit of time to step from hand collecting materials to taming high level & helpful dinos plus upgrading crafting tools. Solo playing an official vanilla server, which had the desired social environment, was at times a form of self-induced sweatshop labor. There is more to the grind than just mining and building though. Tending crops, feeding your tames and breeding all have strict timing requirements as does the life of any structure you build. For a solo player on official servers that pretty much means logging in every few days without fail. Before I started using that low end laptop on business trips I lost an entire base and my tames on the SE server - missed the deadline by a couple of hours. Poof. Since then I've found myself almost obsessively orchestrating my life to make sure I can get on frequently enough to avoid a reoccurance. My bases (3 of them) and tames (120-ish) represent hundreds of hours of activity. ARK is crack and if time is money then it is the most expensive crack around.
3. Customer relations management is the final negative in my review. The devs have had a checkered history and a good portion of that can be attributed to ARK being an early access game up to now. However, my own decades of experience in the corporate world let me recognize a troubling trend. WildCard seemed to repeat certain errors in dealing with their paying customers. The decisions their management made led me to believe they were trying to work at a level beyond their abilities. This is a sadly common event in businesses undergoing growth - the very good college team is not replaced with a pro team when it's time to do so. This puts the future of ARK at risk for all the playing modes.
Once again, this review is directed at solo playing on pve official. Due to the master/slave relationship of the grind I'm not going back to solo pve play on official servers even though it is my preference for the social interactions. I haven't played since mid-Aug and may never play again.

Beautiful game with a talented modding community. Fortunately, Wildcard realizes that the lifeblood of this game lies with the modding community. They've made some mistakes and delays with the dev kits, but overall, they seem supportive of them.
Ark can be a fun game for exploration, discovery and building bases with your friends. Finding and taming dinos so you can find even more locations and resources to not only survive, but thrive, is rewarding. Adding mods to mix to get even more creative and present more challenges has been great because there's always been something new to check out.
The developement of this game has had some pretty bad misteps for the PvP communities. Wildcard's communication regarding PvP content was few and far between. When they did communicate, it was frequently cryptic and sometimes open to interpretation. This led to a lot of upset players and understandably so.
Personally, I never saw this game as being a successful PvP title. Open-world games that allow you gather, craft and build usually have mechanics that leave too many openings for players to find exploits to abuse. Some of these included duping, spawn-trapping, blocking, wall glitching, duping, duping, duping... If there's a way to screw other players by abusing a mechanic in a way that was never intended, some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is gonna find it and grief you with it.
I learned pretty early on that PvP wasn't going to be my reason for playing since too many other games have tried and failed at that in this particular genre and I didn't think it was going to be fixed by a game that let's you mount and control dinosaurs and sharks that can shoot lasers.
That said, if you're looking for a game that has huge gorgeous environments along with multiple maps that are fun and rewarding to explore and build in, this is a solid choice. If you're looking for a well balanced PvP game, you should probably keep looking until some miraculous fixes come through which may not happen for a while, if it ever happens.

There are many bad things about ARK. The official servers are terrible, the game itself is a total grind fest, there are numerous performance issues that have still not been addressed (any never will). I've been through a bunch of wipes and glitches, and I've had justified support tickets knocked back for no reason but 'early access'.
BUT I have to still highly, HIGHLY recommend ARK. I paid $30 for it years ago, and I've played for more than 300 hours. Most of my friends have 1k+ hours. I base my games on the cost per hour formula - I understand not everyone does this, but personally if I'm comfortable spending $5 an hour in the cinema (more with popcorn and the rest) then I don't see how I haven't got my money's worth of entertainment here at 10c an hour.
And I have definitely enjoyed it - maybe not every minute, but overall I look back on my experiences with fond memories. There are still many things to like. Gorgeous visuals, heaps of content, complex breeding and levelling systems, base building, online multiplayer.
My suggestion is to skip the official servers. Skip PvP and go straight to PvE, on a private server with accelerated taming rates and reduced feeding rates, or anything that accentuates the positive aspects and reduces the negative, grindy ones. Enjoy taming beautiful dinosaurs and have fun setting up your base and dinosaur farms with your friends.

The more common thing ORP prevents in pve is keeping a passive-aggressive neighbor from provoking a wild dino to come crash your base while you're not logged in.
Cons:
1. Up to the Aug. 29 release server lag/rubber banding/hiccups was a real and constant issue. I played on The Island map (na pve official 35) and it occured the whole 6 months I was on that server. Player complaints about these problems were common in the global chat. Pings would go all over the place, global chat would have 6 people complain about it at the same time, etc., etc. I also played on Scorched Earth (na pve SE 794) and at first it was almost lag free but started to exhibit that problem more and more. The reasons people claimed it happened included high player count, high building count, high dino count, bad server programming, bad internet link to the servers, blah, blah, blah. Not fixed as of Aug. 28
2. The grind - it can take quite a bit of time to step from hand collecting materials to taming high level & helpful dinos plus upgrading crafting tools. Solo playing an official vanilla server, which had the desired social environment, was at times a form of self-induced sweatshop labor. There is more to the grind than just mining and building though. Tending crops, feeding your tames and breeding all have strict timing requirements as does the life of any structure you build. For a solo player on official servers that pretty much means logging in every few days without fail. Before I started using that low end laptop on business trips I lost an entire base and my tames on the SE server - missed the deadline by a couple of hours. Poof. Since then I've found myself almost obsessively orchestrating my life to make sure I can get on frequently enough to avoid a reoccurance. My bases (3 of them) and tames (120-ish) represent hundreds of hours of activity. ARK is crack and if time is money then it is the most expensive crack around.
3. Customer relations management is the final negative in my review. The devs have had a checkered history and a good portion of that can be attributed to ARK being an early access game up to now. However, my own decades of experience in the corporate world let me recognize a troubling trend. WildCard seemed to repeat certain errors in dealing with their paying customers. The decisions their management made led me to believe they were trying to work at a level beyond their abilities. This is a sadly common event in businesses undergoing growth - the very good college team is not replaced with a pro team when it's time to do so. This puts the future of ARK at risk for all the playing modes.
Once again, this review is directed at solo playing on pve official. Due to the master/slave relationship of the grind I'm not going back to solo pve play on official servers even though it is my preference for the social interactions. I haven't played since mid-Aug and may never play again.

Beautiful game with a talented modding community. Fortunately, Wildcard realizes that the lifeblood of this game lies with the modding community. They've made some mistakes and delays with the dev kits, but overall, they seem supportive of them.
Ark can be a fun game for exploration, discovery and building bases with your friends. Finding and taming dinos so you can find even more locations and resources to not only survive, but thrive, is rewarding. Adding mods to mix to get even more creative and present more challenges has been great because there's always been something new to check out.
The developement of this game has had some pretty bad misteps for the PvP communities. Wildcard's communication regarding PvP content was few and far between. When they did communicate, it was frequently cryptic and sometimes open to interpretation. This led to a lot of upset players and understandably so.
Personally, I never saw this game as being a successful PvP title. Open-world games that allow you gather, craft and build usually have mechanics that leave too many openings for players to find exploits to abuse. Some of these included duping, spawn-trapping, blocking, wall glitching, duping, duping, duping... If there's a way to screw other players by abusing a mechanic in a way that was never intended, some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is gonna find it and grief you with it.
I learned pretty early on that PvP wasn't going to be my reason for playing since too many other games have tried and failed at that in this particular genre and I didn't think it was going to be fixed by a game that let's you mount and control dinosaurs and sharks that can shoot lasers.
That said, if you're looking for a game that has huge gorgeous environments along with multiple maps that are fun and rewarding to explore and build in, this is a solid choice. If you're looking for a well balanced PvP game, you should probably keep looking until some miraculous fixes come through which may not happen for a while, if it ever happens.

Closing on 2000 hours with this gem I figured it was time to finally write a review.  As a long term player (since the now ancient 'update 7')  I've seen the game change a lot, mostly for the better.  And since it started out really well, that's saying something.  TL:DR - Well worth downloading to see if you like it!
---
I can say a lot of great things about Warframe:  The visuals are great, the gameplay is slicker than an ice rink and the game world is steadily becoming one of my favourite sci-fi settings ever.
But the real magic here is that it's free to play done well.  There are issues, sure, but I've never felt like I HAD to spend real money to progress.  Don't get me wrong, I've poured a fair bit into Digital Extremes' coffers over the years, but it's never left me with a bad taste.  As an added bonus, a good 80% of the game can be played entirely solo, removing that need to polish your epeen with premium stuff (or deal with asinine team-mates), which is compounded by the fact that some of the best weapons and warframes are easy to aquire early on.
Lastly, and perhaps most importantly, the game is still very much ALIVE at time of writing.  Devs keep the updates coming thick and fast, and there's a large, vocal, diverse community supported by an exceptionally well maintained wiki.
If procedurally generated co-op space-ninja sci-fi loot-em-up sounds like something you at least MIGHT want to try?  I highly suggest you do.

you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

Coming from an Age of Chivalry background, long time player, I've recently decided to purchase both the original and the expansion. The time I've spent on this game, it was an awkward trade of fun and frustration, the only fun I had was when I wielded a 2 handed spear, how it provided me with enough distance to poke enemies to death easily, yet what I really looked forward in this game was being an archer, or for the expansion, being a pirate.
If you purchase this game, don't bother much with range weapons, either you're good enough to hit a human with an ant-size bullet/arrow, or be killed easily by a spear and shield Spartan, given the reason that range classes have poor melee weapons, pirates have a default short sword which is not going to save you from a 2 handed sword landing a building breaking smash over your defenseless head. Not only I find it rather annoying and difficult to land a shot, but reloading takes all of your patience, especially crossbow, the character would bend over, spending about 3 seconds to reload and when the character gets up, you only see the tip of a spear ramming down your eye, nonetheless whether you score the shot or not, it only takes about a few percent of life, you still need to draw your safety-precaution approved sword and land a few hits.
I feel the game is unbalanced, for that reason, you barely see range weapons, just Spartans, Knights, Vikings, and some Samurai around. Because people like to win easily, they would rather sprint towards you, slice you in half before you even get a chance to respond, given the fact that it takes time to swap weapons and mispressing would lead to swapping back to another weapon, not to mention if you are reloading and get hit, your weapon remains unloaded. My biggest complaint is with range classes, they are plain hard to use, forcing most people to for the easy win classes. I wouldn't recommend this game if you like pirates, playing as one, or unbalanced games.

Pretty fun concept of Medieval Times Warfare hacking and slashing one another and dismemebering heads, legs, and arms for a prety long match time for each battle. However it is far fetched as when i had the oppurtunity to play the game for free, you must realize that this game is not worth 25.00$ bar-none imo. First the off the lack of a story really brings down the purpose for this game its basically random medieval knights fighting one another because they feel like it. Second the multiplayer is fun and sometimes inventive but if you're a newbie trying to get into some newbie combat you're going to have a bad time. Almost every match is filled with at least 4 try-hard douches that ruin the experience and force you to randomly click the right Mouse Pad in hopes of getting a kill when suddenly you're struck in the head with a ballista or an arrow. Third the combat is fun but it feels innacurate and doesn't flow very well. The movements feel sluggish and off at the most and it sometimes feels like im fighting an inflatable punching bag rather than a heavily armored knight. The game is great to play especially if you have friends as well, but some of the content does drag on and it becomes a tedious task of just slashing random knights that doesn't give you enough reward or effort for progression and just getting better in general. A 6/10 at most. Wait to get it on sale for 6$ again, or have a friend thats dumb enough to gift it to you as a present or if they owed you 25$ at one time in your life.

You can basically run through the game using only melee if you really desired. The parkour is fun, but could definitely use some work. It doesn't feel 100% polished up, never did, but it's what we have. The boss fights are fun, but most are difficult on your own at the start and you should get some help from a public match or with some more experienced friends.
I love the combat in this game. It feels great firing your weapons at all enemies, or stabbing them to death. There are tons of weapons to use! Every one of them can be obtained in the game legitimately, but most of them can also be paid for. I will explain more of this in the free-to-play model.
The parkour is fun, but not completely polished. For one you can't grab ledges, which definitely needs to be added. However, I also feel like that could hinder the experience and get you caught in ledges where you didn't want to. In the game you can Wallrun, double jump, bullet-jump, slide, ninja spin slash, etc. It's fun once you get used to it.
In my opinion this game has the best free-to-play model I have ever seen. If you want everything in the game you do not need to pay at all. However, it will take you a lot of work. But the amount of work you have to do is completely worth it for most items. All you have to do is go to planets and grind for resources to build different items. This is, however one of the problems I have with this game.
Everything that is put out ends up becoming a grind-fest. This just makes the game boring at long periods of time and you have to put down the game after being bored of it, and then pick it back up at a later date. This goes on for the entire game. The game, however, feels incredibly fun when you do get back into it.
Overall, this game is one of my favorites with the amount of fun I've ever had. I give it a 8/10. The issues it does have does not outweigh my experiences, and thus I feel like the grade I gave it serves well.

I have had a great deal of fun in this game. Over 700 hours of fun at the time of this review. The idea behind the game is brilliant and it had the potential to be an absolutely awesome long term project, but unfortunately I have come to realise this will not happen. Multiple bugs that remain for extended periods of time despite patches claiming to have fixed them. The patches themselves are big, sometimes in the multi gigabyte range and almost daily.
However, the biggest problem is that the devs do not seem to care about the customers. Upon launch it was announced that the 'legacy' servers, the servers that existed during their beta testing time would have all customer support axed from them. That was a huge "screw you" to the bulk of their customer base. Because with the price increasing 4 fold I don't think they will be getting a massive increase in customers any time soon.
Prior to that, any tickets I did send in were responded with "We are sorry but our customer service team is unable to assist you with this issue. Below is a link to the forums that may have details on how others solved this or a similar problem..."
Because of the coding issues and the lack of customer consideration I will not recommend this game. If you enjoy survival games with dinosaurs and such then go for, but don't expect anyone at Wildcard to help you if something goes wrong, you're out of luck there.

It's a clicker/idle game. Some might argue that it stands at the top of the genre, and I would be inclined to agree.
If you like feeling a sense of progression and can get that from watching numbers go up, or getting to bigger numbers than you did before, then Clicker Heroes just might be the idle game for you. It was for me.
Some other nice points:
-Idle, Active, Hybrid are all perfectly comparable and viable playstyles.
-Overall progression always continues to increases. It doesn't slow down to a crawl. If you feel like you're progressing very slowly, you may be doing something wrong. (Try ascending!)
-Decent sized community depending on where you look.
-Lot of resources out there due to the above point. Calculators, scripts, clans, trackers, guides, etc.
-I have never once felt compelled to do microtransactions. Microtransactions get you rubies, but you can also get them naturally in the game by clicking (woah!) certain objects that appear reasonably often. And I honestly haven’t felt a great need to use them anyway.
Con:
I definitely feel like the startup was a little slow, and it’s hard to see at the beginning what seperates Clicker Heroes from the other idle games. But once you start with the Ancients, well, then the progression really begins. I wasn’t too big of a fan before, but I really started to like the game after that.

There are no characters to love. There are no beautiful envoirments. There is no epic music score. And for that matter, there is no end.
People are joking about how addicted they are to this game. About how this game has consumed their life and how they can't stop playing it. This is not something to joke about. Take a moment and think about what you could have done instead in those 50 hours you've spent clicking a monster. Just think of the new hobby you could have found instead. Or all the beautiful cakes you could have baked instead.
Funny thing is that there are so much better things to do regarding both clicking and idling (is that even a legit word? xD) Want to train your clicking finger? Play Torchlight or Diablo. Want to play a good idle game? Play Fallout: Shelter on your mobile - it's on par with Fallout 4, not even joking. Just whatever you do, don't waste time on this or any cheap copycat of it.
This review - or angry rant, philosophing, thingythingy whatever - is the final ounce of my time I'm wasting regarding this game (read "scheiße"). I stopped playing it before it was too late and can proudly say that I've uninstalled it from my computer never to return to it.
I encourage you to do the same.

Early Access doesn't make sense for this type of game, we've learned that over the past few years.  Games like PUBG are perfect for it, games that have a set time limit and follow a repeatable pattern.  Games that you invest HUGE amounts of time into, like this, are generally not that great for Early Access.
Now, with that said, would this game be where it is if it weren't for Early Access?  No, not even close.  So, I think what we really need is something like Steam Alpha or something.  A game like this just can't work with thousands of players playing, investing huge amounts of time.  It could work with a handful of players, where the devs actually spawn stuff, or alter level rates, etc, to test things.  As it is, this is a fully released game, that isn't ready.
This game is something special, but it's also an example of why not all games make sense for Early Access.

Now I want to begin by saying ARK has some weird place in my heart. From the week it came out I fell in love with the game. A few weeks later and here I was, my excited self rearing to start the game. I spend my first IRL night playing the game casually, browsing servers, having a bit of fun. I then joined upon a server which would take up around 400 hours of my life. The server WAS my life... I had a mentor in a tribe and I moved around a few tribes, becoming a member of the community which was the server. Then my broken computer hit and I stopped playing. I returned to it a year later, thinking back to all the people I had just left on that server, months of talking and making friends and building a foundation for a community was gone. I then decided to try out unofficial, yet again servers came and went. I then found a server which occupied another 100-200 hours of my time, then we got wiped and my tribe kind of broke apart, I was yet again a leader who lost many friends. This game actually gives me memories, I am partly in love with this game and it legitimatly hurts me to see negative reviews. I decided to finally take out my rage for the hatred upon the game. For any of you wondering I dont have the time or the courage to start playing ARK again, which is also tearing me apart for the fact I really do miss this game.
Mending the misunderstood issues:
Cost - The main stick for all of the hate recently is for the games up in price. This is an eventuality, they have just made it the cost of a main game on any console. Early access was cheaper because the game wasn't what it was today. Quit your complaining, I have had so many hours of fun and a lot of people have had ever more hours of fun. You can even buy it (fairly certain) for cheaper on♥♥♥♥♥anyway.
Paid DLC - Well the rest of ARK DLC have been free, but people complaining about the state of the game (which was fine for me)  being bad and why bring out a paid DLC. Truth is Scorched Earth was planned to be around the release time as a DLC anyway and was virtually finished. So they didn't make a DLC for a cash grab while the game was in a "bad state" they just released it a bit later.
Optimisation - Yes, this game needs optimisin BUT that does not mean they don't care for it. The game is beautiful and is still going to be a heck of a game to run. A well built PC for £500-600 will do the job on high settings. Which is less than most people actually spent on their overpriced laptop.
This game has made me laugh, made me friends and has entertained me. This is what all games should be like and granted they are. But what makes ARK special, is the memories which its given me, the undiscribable feeling of love and sorrow at the same time. I really wish I could go back in time, grab those memories back and hold on to it, hold on to everyone who I left not by choice. And if I could regain that my life would be amazing.
If you were to ask me negatives about the game, I would say to you :-
The main negative is that it makes me angry when people diss and insult such a good game, saying "They HAD the principle they HAD the idea but the money pigs went and ruined it" and I just get so annoyed over it.
The other side negative is the fact I long for the days back. My old ARK friends dont play anymore, and any others dont play it, or with the passion at which I do. Which means I am stuck in a massive nostalgia and brilliant memories, and everything there to allow me to continue, apart from other people. It kind of makes me depressed in a light way.
In the end my conclusion is, I may be sensitive and biased over the game, but this game gave me something to look back and have a next level nostalgia over, and I could never put a price on that. I could go on for ages about how brilliant the game is and how not to listen to the haters. But just please, I beg you to give the god damned game a chance! It is worth every bit of money.
EDIT:
I have decided to give haters a solution for their problems.
Optimisation: A Nvidia 1050/1050 Ti can run ARK on high, A 3GHZ overclocked to 4.1GHZ is also plenty and 8 GB of ram should do you just fine.
This solution kind of solveds 2 in one : For people complaining about massive tribes coming over and taking over masses of servers AND people who complain about how grindy and long the game process is, PLAY UNNOFFICIAL. You can have the rates higher, tames take less time, you can join PvE either way if you are tired of PvP servers wiping you out. The problem is people who dont want to play PvE because there isn't enough actual action and goal to it when they then complain about people wiping them out on PvP! Come on! These people are wiping you because they are people banding together to have fun and kill people in PvP just like you exept they are more prepared and doing a better job than you. I have seen loads of videos on youtube of people in 2/3 man tribes who survive and then manage to destroy other people. Nooblets built a solo base once and took on a whole tribe and won and that was on a PvP Official server! So man up and if you are not going to get better at the game and start actually battling against these big tribes, then you can shove a stick up your♥♥♥♥♥♥and play PvE. OR maybe ARK just isnt the right game for you, because you lack the skill or otherwise the patience and intelligence to get better. So stop giving this game negative reviews because it doesnt suite me. Its like me playing My Little Pony and then giving it a bad review because it was a little too pinkish and was too difficult... Just accept the fact ARK isnt the game for you.

Now I want to begin by saying ARK has some weird place in my heart. From the week it came out I fell in love with the game. A few weeks later and here I was, my excited self rearing to start the game. I spend my first IRL night playing the game casually, browsing servers, having a bit of fun. I then joined upon a server which would take up around 400 hours of my life. The server WAS my life... I had a mentor in a tribe and I moved around a few tribes, becoming a member of the community which was the server. Then my broken computer hit and I stopped playing. I returned to it a year later, thinking back to all the people I had just left on that server, months of talking and making friends and building a foundation for a community was gone. I then decided to try out unofficial, yet again servers came and went. I then found a server which occupied another 100-200 hours of my time, then we got wiped and my tribe kind of broke apart, I was yet again a leader who lost many friends. This game actually gives me memories, I am partly in love with this game and it legitimatly hurts me to see negative reviews. I decided to finally take out my rage for the hatred upon the game. For any of you wondering I dont have the time or the courage to start playing ARK again, which is also tearing me apart for the fact I really do miss this game.
Mending the misunderstood issues:
Cost - The main stick for all of the hate recently is for the games up in price. This is an eventuality, they have just made it the cost of a main game on any console. Early access was cheaper because the game wasn't what it was today. Quit your complaining, I have had so many hours of fun and a lot of people have had ever more hours of fun. You can even buy it (fairly certain) for cheaper on♥♥♥♥♥anyway.
Paid DLC - Well the rest of ARK DLC have been free, but people complaining about the state of the game (which was fine for me)  being bad and why bring out a paid DLC. Truth is Scorched Earth was planned to be around the release time as a DLC anyway and was virtually finished. So they didn't make a DLC for a cash grab while the game was in a "bad state" they just released it a bit later.
Optimisation - Yes, this game needs optimisin BUT that does not mean they don't care for it. The game is beautiful and is still going to be a heck of a game to run. A well built PC for £500-600 will do the job on high settings. Which is less than most people actually spent on their overpriced laptop.
This game has made me laugh, made me friends and has entertained me. This is what all games should be like and granted they are. But what makes ARK special, is the memories which its given me, the undiscribable feeling of love and sorrow at the same time. I really wish I could go back in time, grab those memories back and hold on to it, hold on to everyone who I left not by choice. And if I could regain that my life would be amazing.
If you were to ask me negatives about the game, I would say to you :-
The main negative is that it makes me angry when people diss and insult such a good game, saying "They HAD the principle they HAD the idea but the money pigs went and ruined it" and I just get so annoyed over it.
The other side negative is the fact I long for the days back. My old ARK friends dont play anymore, and any others dont play it, or with the passion at which I do. Which means I am stuck in a massive nostalgia and brilliant memories, and everything there to allow me to continue, apart from other people. It kind of makes me depressed in a light way.
In the end my conclusion is, I may be sensitive and biased over the game, but this game gave me something to look back and have a next level nostalgia over, and I could never put a price on that. I could go on for ages about how brilliant the game is and how not to listen to the haters. But just please, I beg you to give the god damned game a chance! It is worth every bit of money.

Warframe is basically a collecting (a la Pokemon) game.
Every few months, a new frame/weapon/mod/cosmetic appears and players start grinding for it. It will be a lot of fun in the beginning, as you spend all your time collecting everything. But it will get dull quickly once you get almost everything and you find that there is a lack of reason to play.
There is little to no group dynamic and as with alot of multiplayer games out there, it grapples between being solo-friendly and encouraging group play. If you are looking for a good social experience, your mileage may vary depending on the clan and people you meet.
It has kept me occupied for more than 1000+ hours and I am glad with the money I have spent on this game for platinium (in-game currency), though I ended up with a surplus in the end.
I would recommend people to try this game, but not to be too heavily invested in it. Playing casually is the best way to enjoy this game. However if you are a hardcore player looking for the next mmorpg to invest in, you will be sorely disappointed.

I think it's come time to change my review. I used to enjoy playing this game, but I just can't anymore. There are too many things wrong with it for me. For starters, the community is pretty cancerous from what I remember. You can be vote-kicked for almost literally any reason, or no reason for that matter. Anyone can start a poll to kick you, and from there people vote pretty randomly. Furthermore, the combat is terrible. It started off pretty good and straight forward, where you could have an honest duel with someone and win if you utilized most of the combat mechanics, but that didn't last long. What passes for skill now is winding up to swing a maul overhead and then turning around with extremely high mouse sensitivity so that the hammer hits your head while it's still behind the other guy's head, which happens much more often than I care to admit. Another example would be the guy who runs away when you come after him but then starts thrusting his spear and turns a perfect 180 to hit you in the face; good luck catching up to him. It's not even really combat anymore, it's seeing who can have the strangest, most unpredictable or broken fighting-style in the game. If you like traditional medieval games, then you're probably going to think this is garbage, and in my opinion it is. To top it off, the dev team has gotten pretty bad too. They've started selling character and weapon skins in game for real cash, some of which are even created by the community, which is just unforgivable.
At it's best, I can only give this game a 5/10. There are times you'll have fun, but there will be even more times you just end up feeling frusterated.

I bought this game when it first released back in 2015 for the introductory price of $25, and I don't think I could possibly be any happier with my purchase!
ARK is much more than "just another survival game" in my opinion....... This game has so much more to offer.
> Massive beautiful landscapes to explore.
> A comprehensive building system that can be used to create some amazing architecture,
> Explorable caves, huge oceans filled with deadly creatures.
> A host of tamable and breedable beasts.
> Several teirs and types of weapons and armor..... you can begin the game as a caveman and work your way up to a teched out sci-fi super hero!
> A good selection of bosses to keep you busy, from mini bosses like the Iceworm Queen in Ragnarok to ascension level bosses like the Broodmother or the Megapithicus on the island.
> Oh and did I bother to mention Ragnarok? It's only one of the most amazing maps ever released in any game, and it was community created, the ARK devs liked what they seen and arranged an agreement to pay the creators of this map to continue to develop it.
> Which brings me to the awesome modding community and capabilities...... a mod can range from a simple reskin of an item up to and including a complete total conversion of the game into something else entirely, pretty much limitless from what I can tell.
This game to me is everything an open world sandbox should be..... is it perfect and completely without its problems? Nope.
Optimization can be a bit hit and miss for some, you do need a beefy enough gaming PC to maintain good framerates at higher visual fidelity..... and even then that framerate can tank when around large complex player bases with lots of tamed dinos.
A good gaming rig for high settings in this game would look like this
CPU - Intel 4th gen I5, or AMD Ryzen R3 or better.
RAM - 16GB or more of DDR3/DDR4
Graphics - Nvidia GTX 1060 6GB, or AMD Radeon RX 480/580
Storage - 100GB with mods and maps, a large SSD would be a really nice option here.
The above rig should give you a very nice playing experience in ARK without really being super overkill or super expensive.
Another downside that deserves mention is the official servers themselves..... they can be a mess at times, unstable, prone to hacks and exploits, slow, laggy, crowded..... the other players can be extremely toxic on some, and, as we've seen, there's no guarantee that your server will not be wiped if it's population drops below a certain level, meaning much of your hard work could be lost.
Fortunately though, ARK offers some alternatives to official servers, such as, single player, peer to peer coop, rentable dedicated servers, a dedicated server that you can host for free on your own hardware....... if you wish to avoid the aggravation which can the Official servers can be, any of these options are far more recommended.
All in all, ARK easily goes down probably as my favorite game bar none, and probably one where I've sank the most time into...... I can't recommend it enough!

Warframe, one of the best games I have ever played on steam!
The game is basically a third person "shooter". However, there is more to it than just shooting, the melee combat is incredibly fun! You can basically run through the game using only melee if you really desired. The parkour is fun, but could definitely use some work. It doesn't feel 100% polished up, never did, but it's what we have. The boss fights are fun, but most are difficult on your own at the start and you should get some help from a public match or with some more experienced friends.
I love the combat in this game. It feels great firing your weapons at all enemies, or stabbing them to death. There are tons of weapons to use! Every one of them can be obtained in the game legitimately, but most of them can also be paid for. I will explain more of this in the free-to-play model.
The parkour is fun, but not completely polished. For one you can't grab ledges, which definitely needs to be added. However, I also feel like that could hinder the experience and get you caught in ledges where you didn't want to. In the game you can Wallrun, double jump, bullet-jump, slide, ninja spin slash, etc. It's fun once you get used to it.
In my opinion this game has the best free-to-play model I have ever seen. If you want everything in the game you do not need to pay at all. However, it will take you a lot of work. But the amount of work you have to do is completely worth it for most items. All you have to do is go to planets and grind for resources to build different items. This is, however one of the problems I have with this game.
Everything that is put out ends up becoming a grind-fest. This just makes the game boring at long periods of time and you have to put down the game after being bored of it, and then pick it back up at a later date. This goes on for the entire game. The game, however, feels incredibly fun when you do get back into it.
Overall, this game is one of my favorites with the amount of fun I've ever had. I give it a 8/10. The issues it does have does not outweigh my experiences, and thus I feel like the grade I gave it serves well.

Pros
-	No P2W.  A microtransaction based cooperative online RPG, this game has a robust and generally fair economy.  Players trade using the cash shop currency (plat) for common goods (weapon/frame components, mods etc), which is so far probably the best system under any F2P scheme.
-	Not a lot of other games let you play a space samurai/ninja and use overpowering ability to mow down enemies in masse.  The aesthetics are quite unique and draws a lot from East Asian cultural themes, along with Digital Extreme’s own twists.
-	Although not a single-player game, I was pleasantly surprised by the amount of lore and backstory the game’s universe contains.  I read every text in every quest while I playing games, no matter it’s an MMO or a single player game, so I have to commend the devs for trying.
-	Being a cooperative game, vast majority of the game modes and maps are enjoyable with random groups, a feat which has to consider the fluctuating quality of the players in said groups.
Cons
-	All games eventually run out of fresh content; this game is no exception.  After unlocking all the star chart (equivalent of finished mapping the world), done all quests (meaning all main and sub stories are experienced), the remaining highly repetitive contents may not be suitable for everybody, but are still far from the worst I've seen in online games.
-	There is an insane amount of blinding “eye cancer” graphical effects in this game that can’t be turn off despite having set lowest to relevant options.  Depending on each person, your eyes may be severely strained if you keep playing the game for a few hours.
-	The game is no MMO, but it’s still way too sharded.  Game sessions are hosted on the “host” player’s PC, and is subject to wildly fluctuation of network and other constraints.  If your internet is bad, not only you are extra vulnerable to incurring issues, but your issues will become your team’s issue, especially if you are the host.
-	Given the huge arsenal of weaponry and warframes, balance is a challenge.  I don’t feel the devs are doing a passable job on making sure all weapons have some uses.  Quite a lot of them fell to disuse because other more “meta” weapons are simply stronger.
Is Warframe a game that you’d want to spend 800+ hours playing like I did?  It depends.  If you feel this game is something within your taste after watching its gameplay videos on YouTube, then don’t hesitate and try playing it yourself.  My only advices to newcomers are: choose Excalibur as starting frame because it’s superior to the other two, and don’t spend your plat buying weapons and frames form the cash shop without a bit research, because chances are their Prime versions (better, upgraded version) are likely to cheaper buying from other players.  Use the plat on unlocking weapon/frame slots instead.
