Considering the recent cancellation of refunds, decided I might as well write this.
ARK: Survival Evolved is a very fun game at its core, but it's plagued with issues that keep me from fully enjoying it. The potential for an amazing survival experience is definitely there, but the game doesn't actually seem to do anything with it.
For starters, simply getting into the game for the first time is a massive pain. While the leveling system is a nice touch, the ability to craft almost every item is locked behind what's known as an "engram". The engrams are essentially the crafting recipes for items, but engrams can only be obtained through the leveling system itself. While it can feel like your character does learn how to survive and better equip themselves, the issue lies that
are locked behind this system. Until you manage to pick enough berries and grass and punch a couple dodo birds, you're not able to properly collect supplies or defend yourself. In short: you're going to die at first.
While death in survival games is very common and the point behind said games is avoiding it at all costs, I've never had a survival game force death this much upon me before. I completely understand that the player is essentially stranded on an island by themselves (or with some other people) that happens to be filled with dinosaurs, but doing something as simple as taking a wrong turn almost means certain death and disembowelment via Raptors. Survival games are perfectly allowed to have a learning curve but in ARK it comes down to pure trial and error and RNG at times.
Secondly: Most systems within the game play out in real time. The most noticable of the two that use this are food spoiling and the taming system. The food spoiling is a lot easier to control thankfully do to craftable refridgerators (which again, are locked behind the engram system meaning that your berries and meat are gonna go bad pretty FAST), the taming system is simply painful. Aside from one or two animals that can be thankfully be tamed by befriending them, taming for most animals requires beating up said animal until it passes out, cramming berries or narcotics down its throat, and then waiting for it to eat the meat you put out for it enough until it likes you. While already a poor system, the problem lies that the taming can take a very long time for the bigger dinosaurs, which unless you're playing singleplayer, requires that you
I shouldn't have to constantly devote my time to the game in order to get AND keep my tames, who also starve in real time (although thankfully there are feeding stations you can create to keep them alive which you guessed it, are ALSO locked behind engrams). A game should be consistently fun to keep players coming back to it, NOT forcing them via poorly thought out gameplay mechanics.
Third: The game's optimization is beyond♥♥♥♥♥♥poor. I can't believe I'd say it, but even Fallout 4 is a very nice pc port if you compare it to this game. While not the absolute best, my pc is pretty far beyond the minimum requirements and I STILL have trouble getting above 30 fps on the lowest settings possible AND some fps fixes. There's not really much to say about this part, but considering that this game was originally designed for PC you would think they would at least put slightly more effort into optimization.
Fourth: The devs themselves have been making extremely poor decisions when it comes to the health of their own game. Instead of fixing the content they currently have, they add even more dinosaurs and maps. Instead of improving performance, they raise the price from $30 to $60 when the game isn't even properly finished. Instead of balancing the game out, they
The game is advertised as being out of early access, yet with the poor ai, performance, and bugs galore, it almost feels like it just released, which is especially embarassing considering the game started development in October of 2014.
This game is definitely not worth $60. This game was barely worth $30. If you're looking for a fun survival experience, you're better off buying The Forest or Subnautica. If you're looking for a game with dinosaurs, you're much better off purchasing one of the Turok games or Dino D-Day.

Warframe is basically a collecting (a la Pokemon) game.
Every few months, a new frame/weapon/mod/cosmetic appears and players start grinding for it. It will be a lot of fun in the beginning, as you spend all your time collecting everything. But it will get dull quickly once you get almost everything and you find that there is a lack of reason to play.
There is little to no group dynamic and as with alot of multiplayer games out there, it grapples between being solo-friendly and encouraging group play. If you are looking for a good social experience, your mileage may vary depending on the clan and people you meet.
It has kept me occupied for more than 1000+ hours and I am glad with the money I have spent on this game for platinium (in-game currency), though I ended up with a surplus in the end.
I would recommend people to try this game, but not to be too heavily invested in it. Playing casually is the best way to enjoy this game. However if you are a hardcore player looking for the next mmorpg to invest in, you will be sorely disappointed.

If you are a young person who has more time than money this is the perfect game.
If you are an older person with more money than time, this is maybe a bad option.
I am the latter, and spent hundreds of dollars on the free to play game! with over 330 hours played, I  have spent more than a dollar an hour. I won't say i regret it, as it was fun. But unless you are a completiontist, you may find the lack of proper challenging "end game" content an issue. I  got bored fast seeing as I had 4-5 frames and 4-5 weapons that were all just as strong as they could possibly be. My friends were the same. Between us we could dominate any challenge the game had. The only challenge came in the form of endless modes where the enemies would scale infinitely and eventually you cant win. But it didnt become challening for over an hour of being in the map!
That all being said though, there are hundreds of weapons, and many frames. If you were to play with them all, than you would have a lot more content. As leveling weapons and frames takes a great deal of time investment. Personally I just stick with what I like. And as such ran out of challenging content. But I am somewhat spoiled for choice at my age. I have more games than I could ever hope to play. 10 years ago I would have been much more willing to spend time collecting and grinding in Warframe.
Still a solid recommendation. Try not to spend all your money on platinum and frame/weapon packs! I would encourage you to buy $50-60 worth of things to support the great dev team. But maybe stop there!

It is a very hard game to explain but here we go.
You are a space ninja who runs around killing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ clones, interstellar miners and their laser ostriches, gold robots, random viscious animals, and even other ninjas.

TL;DR: Too expensive, unbalanced/buggy.
I played this game during the free weekend and everything about it feels like it was meant to be that way. I believe that if you're already paying for a game then anything else ingame should unlockable by means of progression. If you want any customization beyond the generic armours (as in 3 different sets of each item) expect to pay around 10 bucks for that.
You unlock weapons as you progress and while there is some variety depending on your class you will get stuck playing with whichever weapon you find you have the cheapest kills. For me that was the knight with the broadsword, which is the first weapon you start with. 9 out of 10 games I completely dominated just by using a simple "overhead and slash" combo
As far as the actual gameplay you will run into plenty of texture clipping, game crashing, disconnecting servers, and a community that will try to kick you out of every game you try to play while screaming hacks.

This game is fun at first but you will loose that feeling of simulation once you start disecting the bugs and unbalances. If it were free I would say sure, but for what you get its not worth sinking your time and money into.
*EDIT*: I'm a hypocrite and bought this game but waited for a 4.99 sale. After going through swordplay withdrawl I realized that their are unfortunetly far too few games with this type of gameplay and combat. Mount and Blade: Warband is the only close competitor, at least that I have found, and looks fun being able to mount horses and having much larger scale battles but also looks very old and doesn't seem to have the same depth and weight to combat as this game. Kingdom Come: Deliverance looks very promising but is still in development and will be single player only. So until another game comes around, and I really hope one does come soon, this is in my opinion the best option right now for this particular type of game :|...

So after playing the game since the early days of its release, I must say, that the game itself didnt get much better than in the beginning. Sure they added a ton of stuff, which on one side allows for more content und fun, but on the other hand makes a game that is buggy/laggy as hell, much worse.
Reaching out to the modder community was the biggest and most important step they could ever take, as they are the ONLY reason this game is still alive today and has so many players. Without mods, this game would be in EA hell forever. So goodjob here, to get willing workers to fix your game, that you dont need to pay a dime.
The graphical and fps lags this game has since its arrival on steam are just horrible. They simply dont get better, nothing gets fixed in this matter here, the game is a complete lag fest, if you dont own a absolutly hardcore mashine, but even then you prob will still have lags/stuttering and ocasional freezes. If you play on cancer mode (very low settings), the game is kinda stable, so still have some lags and some freezes, but its as frequent (maybe 2-4 per hour, on high up to 20...).
Its so sad, that you guys only want to milk money out of the people, you have the time to work on pay dlc( 1 in EA, 1 1-2 months after release and the 3rd roughly 6 months after), when you could finaly ix the stuttering & lags.
People have been very patient with you guys, but absolutly nothing happened.
On the loading times... well yeah you did improve them, but only the loading times for vanilla. If you mod the game or play on a dlc map, and you dont have it on a ssd,where it can easy take up to 150GB of space (mods+game(around 70)), you basically spend up to 20 minutes and more waiting to connect to a server. And dont blame this here on the mod devs guys, as it is simply not their fault. It makes no big difference, if the mods loaded are just some new armor/wep pieces or big maps and overhauls.

Oh boy, chivalry. One of my favorite multiplayer games I've ever played, and if you're into hacking,
slashing, and decapitating, this will be a favorite too. So lets begin, shall we?
To start, I'll explain the story behind the entire game. Contrary to the belief of other reviewers, there actually is a story to this game. The land of Agatha is ruled over by king, Argon. He rules over the land and commands an army of loyalists, the Agathian army, and according to the wiki, controls the northern half of Agatha. Their faction's colors are gold, and blue, and their symbol is a lion. Southside, there is the Mason Order, commanded by Lord Malrik locked in a civil war with the Agathians. They don't believe in the way King Argon rules over Agatha, and their goal is to crush any loyalist thoughts under their boots. They want to make the people of Agatha harder and stronger, and use fear and intimidation to increase their ranks while providing vast promises for a better tommorrow. Their faction's colors are black and red, and their animal symbol is an eagle. For the rest of the story, you'll simply have to play the game for yourself by playing team objective maps, the story is driven by whoever wins these matches. Could agatha defeat this mighty force of mercenaries, or will Malrik rise
as the new king of Agatha?
If you're considering buying this game, please heed my warning:Don't dive into this game headfirst, you will die.To start, play the damn tutorial if you want to atleast learn the basics. The learning curve is ridiculously high, and if you're playing against competent players in your first matches, it can get extremely frustrating when their swinging their sword across your face before you know what hit 'ya. But don't give up, find what you're good at, stick to it, and sooner or later you'll find glory on this virtual battlefield. With the variety of four classes, with about 20-25 weapons.(With the more weapons mod, this number will be increased.) You'll find your niche in this crazy environment of swordplay. And with the many mouse techniques and crazy swings you'll be swingin', the gameplay is very satisfying. Want to storm castles with your buddies, you can do that. Want to just kill, kill, and kill some more in a small arena with about 15 other blokes wanting to rearrange your face into the greek alphabet, you can. Hell, with the steam workshop, the amount of gameplay is tripled. Only blemish I can see are the common exploits/glitches with hitboxes and such.

Warframe is one of the best games you will ever play. When I first played it, I didn't know what to expect since someone had recommended it to me, but after the first few hours, it got me hooked. It was a little hard at first to get enough material to craft some of the better weapons, but once you're past that point, the game has a lot of variety.
Now it's come a really long way ever since I joined in, with lots of amazing things such as the missions, the characters, the mechanics, the gamemodes and the quests (specially the cinematic ones, which are my favorite).
The game has ingame paid currency, which is platinum, and is required for some stuff like more weapon slots, cosmetic items, etc. It is, however, relatively easy to pile up once you start getting the more valuable loot thanks to ingame trading, so you could get all of the more fancy things without paying a dime with enough dedication (although the discounts you can get for the platinum are pretty good too).
Overall, this game is a must have, and anyone can have it since it's free!

*Variety of ways to play.  Animal tamer/collector.  Builder.  PVP'r.  PVE only.  Whatever you want to do, there is sure to be a server out there to fit your needs.

*Achievements to get and funny holiday events (same every year though, but still nice to have them back)
*Extensive mod collection so that you can customize your game as you want or, change the ark experience into something totally new
Cons:
*Weird things still happen, usually around patch times.  Best not to log in on patch day XD
*Very hard on your rig.  Not all computers can handle this game
*official servers are super grindy with low rates on tame/xp/harvest.  Many trolls play on the official servers, and whether pve or pvp, can make your game time frustrating, especially if you are months in at those low rates only to have it be for nothing.  Recommend playing on unofficial servers as the admins are usually quick to get up to speed on your situation and come up with a resolution.

Ark is pretty solid survival game but it suffers from the same toxic playerbase that  games like Rust suffer from. Games like this are great in concept and ideology but when it comes to actually executing that idea and making it real, the game falls flat.
You can be in a tribe of 20+ or even larger, which is great. However, the moment you have your whole tribe go "offline" for what we call "going to bed" in the real world, this is when it becomes the worst. All that time you spent building and farming, wasted. Sure you can go play Single Player, play PvE or rent a private server, but why would I want to build a base alone on a large island that is meant to have a living breathing world with the threat of other survivors?
I'd say overall I'd give this game a 6.5-7/10 because the game is feature rich, and does look great, however I just feel that the whole "Survival" genre of games really suffers from the whole "offline raiding" issue that we all have come across one time or another.

I will say this: Yes the game has a bit of grinding
However it handles it in such a way, that the game is overall always fun. Slaying hundreds of around 10 types of enemies of a faction is still fun every time. Flying around as some robot ninja with 3 different weapons makes this a very fun hack, slash, and shoot grind.
I remember playing this back in closed beta, when there were around 5 to 6 Warframes.
Now theres 42, all with different unique designs, abilities, customizations, and cosmetics if you're into Fashionframe. To see how far this game since then is actually insane. The developers are extremely friendly, active, and pay attention to what the people want. Easily the most attentive and interactive developers I have ever seen; even their server posts in chat are funny before they do a Hotfix.  They even will answer you directly if one is online and you post a question, almost instantly.
You can play up to with 3 other friends, as it is a 4 player co op each mission, however sometimes there are 8 man raids. You can also join up with an active clan, where you open up new opportunities to more warframes as well as weapons of 3 factions: Corpus, Grineer, and Infested
The story is actually very well done and polished, the cutscenes are pretty top notch, the graphics in general are really good for a free-to-play. Playing through the story gives a good amount of lore throughout it on the whole Tenno/Warframe race, but it can easily get confusing if you don't pay attention.
Overall this game is incredible, watching it blossom into this amazing interactive kill fest was a damn good journey and I can not wait to see more of what they do in the future. Please try this game; starting off early is always a little difficult, but the payoff later when you get your bearings  makes you see how well made the game really is and how much effort was put into it since that closed beta I played.

WELL then, so I gave Warframe and DE a terrible review and I apologise for giving DE a hard time... For no simple reason, being the ignorant fuss-rocker that I am. 'Twas uncalled for, 'twas immature and I meant nothing by it.
Right, now to the review. I must say I'm quite fond of Warframe now. First of all, let me praise DE for developing a free to play game that, for once, lives up to the f2p genre unlike many of these generic military-twitch-shooters nowadays, wich has ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥te rental weapons, forced microtransactions and advertisements and rather awful balancing in terms of pvp multiplayer that grants p2w players the upper hand. In Warframe, it says "let us give you the ability to play SINGLEPLAYER and CO-OP multiplayer as well as PvP with no expense. We give you an arsenal of a variety of weapons that actually HANDLES DIFFERENTLY and OTHER WARFRAMES with different abilities that YOU, yourself, can choose. How 'bout that, sounds good yes?" - SIncerely, Digital Extremes.
Warframe does everything that Destiny's already been doing, only one million times better. In this game, you get to explore not just Earth, Mars and Venus... but the entirety, but only, a miniaturized version of the Milky-Way. You acquire weapons and other warframes in wich they all act differently. You can craft them by buying blueprints, either through your arsenal, the market or by doing certian missions. You can also customize them to your liking. Wich is a win-win for all of us.
So how does Warframe play? Good, bad or terrible? On my potato pc, it's stable since it's well optimized, though I'm sure that you with your beast pc can run Warframe without a hitch. The controls, however, are a dream! Not once have I complained about them. They're responsive and fast. Nothing more. How much content does Warframe have? There's so much in this game that I can't count, but I can say it's enough to keep you playing for a while and DE let's you play for a great portion of the games content. Continue to make Warframe better... Yes, I'm serious. Continue to make it better, DE.
Now, if you're looking for something more in the sci-fi-third-person-shooter genre, Warframe's the game for you. 'Tis worth your time and eventually your money. The developers are constantly working to add more updates and good content for you to drool over.

get the desired or needed item.
3. The people, who play this game seem really friendly and not toxic, which is also a great factor.
Getting to the point now why I recommend this game is, because I pesonally had great fun into it. The game is really chill and you just sit and start doing things: farming for resources, completing some missions, crafting items, upgrading items, crafting "warframes". The reasn is that everything you do in this game in some point of time into it, it pays of. You play a lot to gather resources to build an item, which you desire and after crafting it you are feeling like: yaaaas.
Warframe is pretty neat well optimized game, which I totally recommend.

Well here I am finally reviewing this game. The amount of hours my steam shows Ive logged into this game is very misleading, as I was playing this game on a friends copy for the longest time before making the purchase (which is a questionable one for sure). So here it goes:
I love this game, really. Its gorgeous, the controls and interface are intuitive, at least for me they are, and the scope and scale combined with the high level of detail is unlike any other game ive seen. The amount of content is overwhelming and all in all its one of my favorite games to play... WITH MODS.
For starters, Ark SE is notorious for its horrible performance even on high end gaming PC's. That's just not acceptable for its player base. The price for this game is more than its already exhorbenently high steam price. you gotta take into account the hundreds of dollars you will sink into your PC just to be able to run this game marginally well. Im not even joking. My goal with my latest PC build was to be able to max out Ark's in-game settings just so I know I could run any other game I wanted. Kinda sad, I know, but Ark does make a pretty mean benchmark.
Performance aside, I will argue thats its second biggest fault is how unforgiving it is to players who dont have time to spend 4+ hours taming a dinosaur, or spending 4+ hours getting the start of a decent base going. Just the shear amount of time you have to take out of your own life to have fun in this game is ridiculous. I'm all for a challenge, which this game definitely provides, but sometimes (a lot of times) its not even fun to play because of the required effort. I have a job man. School. Kids... okay I dont have kids thank god but if I did I'd have to neglect the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of them to put decent progress into this game. It is however, easy to circumvent this by playing on modded servers where level progression is tremendously faster, but then there are many other hurdles that follow in regards to maintaining progress.
This review is sloppy, I know, but I felt compelled to get my voice out there. I just cant recommend this game even with all the fun I've had on it. Studio wildcard does not cater to gamers with live's outside of the dark depth's of their home offices and they sure as hell dont cater well to people who dont want to spend their hard earned cash on DLC for an imcomplete game with the hard earned scathing reviews that follow. Typing this very review makes me feel more productive than meeting my in-game goals... and that really is sad.
Conclusion: Get it on sale, with a $1200+ gaming rig, and a good paying work-at-home job where you don't mind if your girflfriend starts cheating on you because of how important that Giga is to tame.

This isn't a super extensive review, just my personal opinion about some certain things. I don't have hundred of hours in this, but i feel like you've played enough after 30+ game breaking crashes. :D
Good game for the early access price. Do NOT pay 60 dollars/euros for this, although the graphics look good, and gameplay is vary different from a normal survival game. I think this has been said before, ALOT, but releasing DLC is not even close to okay when your base game is not finished! (In Early Access). A season pass aswell?!? You're not EA, you can't get away with that, especially with a survival game! And if anything, learn from their mistakes... Somethingsomething... splitting community...somethingsomething.
+ The amount of dinos you can ride, tame and breed is amazing, and alot of them do different things from all the others. Vary different, and a vary interesting system!
+ You havn't settled in a place that has every resource around? (Vary rarely will) Well, time to go on a journey across the world to get yourself some pearls, cement, obsidian etc! Or even items to summon bosses and receive TEK blueprints! This is usually not a big thing, but i find that it realy pushes people out into the world and doesn't leave them cramped up in their bases like in Rust for example.
+ Crafting system is very extensive! It can be realy hard to just get mid-tier gear for the reasons explained before. It vary much so depends on where you have settled, or if you have a flying/climbing dino! (Tame a Thylacoleo and you'll understand) The amount of crafting "stations" in this game realy gives you goal upon goal to follow.
- So, this is an up/down depending on the person. For me it's a meh, realy frustrating at times. Starting in this game is fudging hard as nails. Even in the "easy" spawn locations, you can easily get killed by a single raptor (or such) in under 30 sec. It's realy satisfying when you find a nice place to settle.
- Server list shows about 10% of all servers. This is realy frustrating when you know there are almost full, 120 slot servers out there and you only see 12/60 once at max.
-One crash every 2 hours is not justifiable. Maybe it's my system, but i've seen alot of people with the same issues and crashes.
I've had a good enough amount of hours in this to give it a rating of... meh. Solo is a good place to start, but i can't imagine it will take you less then 30 hours to get high-end items on Vanilla servers. And i'm not including TEK stuff in that list. With a friend it would probably go alot faster, and that is of course highly encouraged.
As much fun as i've had, this game can't be justified at 60 Euros/Dollars. An example for saying this is these "Story notes" in urns, boxes or crates you could find around the map. (Not sure if this is still happening, but this was in the last version before "full release") I tried to pick up several of these, and sometimes by mistake broke the item that contained this note. This caused a fatal error to the game EVERY TIME... This isn't to bad in multiplayer, but when playing SP, the load time for your save/map can take up to around 30min depending on your system, and the rollback can be 10-15 min before the crash. I personally had alot more game breaking errors, and during a time, this game even made my graphics card shut off.
But don't worry about all these flaws. You can put bunny ears on your T-Rex...
At the moment, there's alot of content, and you should try it out if you see it on sale. It's worth 60$ as much as No Man's Sky is tho.

I will say this: Yes the game has a bit of grinding
However it handles it in such a way, that the game is overall always fun. Slaying hundreds of around 10 types of enemies of a faction is still fun every time. Flying around as some robot ninja with 3 different weapons makes this a very fun hack, slash, and shoot grind.
I remember playing this back in closed beta, when there were around 5 to 6 Warframes.
Now theres 42, all with different unique designs, abilities, customizations, and cosmetics if you're into Fashionframe. To see how far this game since then is actually insane. The developers are extremely friendly, active, and pay attention to what the people want. Easily the most attentive and interactive developers I have ever seen; even their server posts in chat are funny before they do a Hotfix.  They even will answer you directly if one is online and you post a question, almost instantly.
You can play up to with 3 other friends, as it is a 4 player co op each mission, however sometimes there are 8 man raids. You can also join up with an active clan, where you open up new opportunities to more warframes as well as weapons of 3 factions: Corpus, Grineer, and Infested
The story is actually very well done and polished, the cutscenes are pretty top notch, the graphics in general are really good for a free-to-play. Playing through the story gives a good amount of lore throughout it on the whole Tenno/Warframe race, but it can easily get confusing if you don't pay attention.
Overall this game is incredible, watching it blossom into this amazing interactive kill fest was a damn good journey and I can not wait to see more of what they do in the future. Please try this game; starting off early is always a little difficult, but the payoff later when you get your bearings  makes you see how well made the game really is and how much effort was put into it since that closed beta I played.

WELL then, so I gave Warframe and DE a terrible review and I apologise for giving DE a hard time... For no simple reason, being the ignorant fuss-rocker that I am. 'Twas uncalled for, 'twas immature and I meant nothing by it.
Right, now to the review. I must say I'm quite fond of Warframe now. First of all, let me praise DE for developing a free to play game that, for once, lives up to the f2p genre unlike many of these generic military-twitch-shooters nowadays, wich has ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥te rental weapons, forced microtransactions and advertisements and rather awful balancing in terms of pvp multiplayer that grants p2w players the upper hand. In Warframe, it says "let us give you the ability to play SINGLEPLAYER and CO-OP multiplayer as well as PvP with no expense. We give you an arsenal of a variety of weapons that actually HANDLES DIFFERENTLY and OTHER WARFRAMES with different abilities that YOU, yourself, can choose. How 'bout that, sounds good yes?" - SIncerely, Digital Extremes.
Warframe does everything that Destiny's already been doing, only one million times better. In this game, you get to explore not just Earth, Mars and Venus... but the entirety, but only, a miniaturized version of the Milky-Way. You acquire weapons and other warframes in wich they all act differently. You can craft them by buying blueprints, either through your arsenal, the market or by doing certian missions. You can also customize them to your liking. Wich is a win-win for all of us.
So how does Warframe play? Good, bad or terrible? On my potato pc, it's stable since it's well optimized, though I'm sure that you with your beast pc can run Warframe without a hitch. The controls, however, are a dream! Not once have I complained about them. They're responsive and fast. Nothing more. How much content does Warframe have? There's so much in this game that I can't count, but I can say it's enough to keep you playing for a while and DE let's you play for a great portion of the games content. Continue to make Warframe better... Yes, I'm serious. Continue to make it better, DE.
Now, if you're looking for something more in the sci-fi-third-person-shooter genre, Warframe's the game for you. 'Tis worth your time and eventually your money. The developers are constantly working to add more updates and good content for you to drool over.

A really good game!
The most important thing, there is a really great and friendly community.
The game is nicer when playing with friends, but also really enjoyable alone or with random people.
There is a big weapon/mod/character diversity.
Talking about mods, they add a lot to the game since you are always trying to find better one to upgrade your skills. They are really important to level up compared to other games where they are completely useless.
The gameplay is really reactive, dynamic and fast wich is really interesting to play with. It's really innovative with all the jumps, dashes and moves possibilities. Honestly, its one of the best gameplay (of this type) i had so far.
Finally, for the good points, I think it's really great to have that much characters. They all have their own skills and it's really important to have some of them while building a team for a mission. It will be really helpful.
Graphics are really good and there are updates and dlc (most of the time free) really often. The game is not forgotten by his developpers and there is always new content.
The only downside I can note is that the missions are almost the same every time even if there are many events.
I recommand trying many gamemodes and playing with friends or a group so you don't get bored of the game.
Anyway, we should not forget that it's a "free to play" and more than that, not a "pay to win" so everyone can have the same content even if you have the possibility to get it faster if you pay. It's really rare to have such quality games that are free and I think it's normal for a free game to have paid content considering that keeping a game updated cost a lot of money. Even just paying the servers can cost more than 100$. Anyway, I think it's the most complete "free to play" game there is actually on the market for this type of game.
So thank's to the developpers, keep up the good and active work !

The progression is invisible. I can't tell if I'm getting better or not. Gear? Classes? Item upgrades? New abilities/spells? I never saw it in the time I put in. I stopped pretty quickly because most games have some kind of "hook" by the first 30 min or so of game time, and if I didn't make some notable progress by 4.5 hrs, I forsee this game having a loooooot of grinding. It's also worth mentioning that I couldn't find anyone to run any content with. Is this community that dead, or what?
What really hurt the fun was the level design was dreadful. While beautiful and detailed, the graphics only do so much to mask the corridor shooter that this game is. No interesting puzzles, no platforming that takes advantage of the game's unique mobility mechanics, no notable scenery, and nothing really memorable at all, but it
pretty.
I'd give it a 5/10. The setting and art style are very, very unique and refreshingly creative, and the game runs smoother than any other PC game I've ever played in my life, but with the grindy combat and lack of any notable progression, it lost me rather quickly.
After almost 5 hours of saying "It will get better", I said "It won't get better."

I'd like to say what got me into Warframe to begin with.
The actual gameplay itself is super fun and very smooth. Not to mention, the preferred way of moving around quickly in this game is straight up torpedoing yourself through the air. Can't complain about that! (As many other reviews have stated - you're basically a space ninja with special powers.)
So along the lines of the gameplay - this can be changed by which Warframes and weapons you choose to equip. The underlying gameplay will always be there, but you can change it up how you see fit.
(After a ton of grinding for said Warframes and weapons, of course! All drops in this game are RNG - unless stated otherwise.)
The other thing that really made me love this game is the community. Warframe honestly has one of the friendliest, non-toxic and most helpful communities I've seen in a game in a long time. If you have a question, it will most likely get answered, and answered well. (The chat usually has a ton of people talking at once, you may have to make yourself be seen. But it WILL get answered.) I've even had a couple random people give me things to help me out (blueprints) and ran missions with me (carried me).
For questions that don't get answered, you will have to head to the internet. The wikia page has the most up-to-date information.
Unfortunately, one of the biggest problems I've had since returning to this game, is trying to find information online and most of it being years old. It's been very frustrating as a semi-new player..
Warframe doesn't really thrive in the tutorial department. You really have to learn things on your own after learning the VERY basics of the game. There is still a ton that I don't know.
To help any new players, my most used sites for information have been: warframe.wikia (most up-to-date information, somewhat lacking on more needed information), tennodrops (shows location for drops of items), and deathsnacks (keeps you updated with alert missions [alert missions reward random loots, such as blueprints for weapons, aesthetic helmets, crafting components, and more]).
All in all, it's a great game. There's always more stuff being added to it, and the devs seem to be pretty active. As with any game that is constantly updated, there will be some issues every now and then, and sometimes the community's wishes aren't granted. But that isn't enough to make this a bad game.
I recommend  trying it out if you enjoy torpeoding around, slashing enemies to bits, and using random powers to crush the souls of said enemies. :D

The game has a variety of problems that not even started worked on, part of which became even more troubling thanks to devs efforts. So here they are:
GRIND
Game is about grind. When I saw Farming Simulator 2016 cover with warframes all around it, it only caused me a faint sad smile, because it's literally the truth. There is nothing wrond with a grind being a MMO game element, because there wouldn't anything to do in this kind of games without it. But this game takes it on whole new level. Grind new equipment, grind expendables for it, grind resources for new equipment to be made, repeat. Only point of getting stronger ingame is to farm more and farm faster. DEVS
I do not know such insult, what could fully and completely describe Digital Extremes. Started as shy and humble studio on the edge of bunkrupt, they've lost their mind after Warframe being such a successful game. They care not about players desires and adding new interesting content to the game. Yet, that isnt the worst part. The worst part being the fact, that they silence critisizing people, ban their accounts, even banning them on support forums after their logical question "Why my account permabanned". The only answer, beside ban on support forums, that you may be getting is "You were banned with reasons". Btw EULA says, that YOUR account isnt in fact yours, but it belongs to DE, who make a great act of beneficence, giving you the right to use it for free for a time being. No matter how many cash you've poured in this game. Damn, RevxDev, the youtuber, that suffered everything I listed above buyed every single prime access (there was 5 of them before he got banned), that costs, like 80-120 bucks each. And only thing he've done to deserve such a thing is simply critizising the game. Not hating and lying about the game, but fairly pointing on all good and bad sides of the new updates and etc. Btw prime accesses were created to support dying company. But after 4 years of constant money pumping they are still there. Guess why?
NO ENDGAME CONTENT
That's it. When you have all most useful warframes, guns and companions, you may think "it's time to finish farming and roll into some more serious bisness this game has to offer". But there is no such a thing in Warframe. You farm new equipment to farm again. Fighting system may be at first glance interesting and facinating, but all you going to do with it is spam 1-2 skills that your warframe being valued for and nothing more. PvP is foking and boring♥♥♥♥♥♥ Archwing, which I, unlike the other welcomed and liked, is not being developed further 5-6 different missions and 3-4 weapons for each of slots.
NERFS AND BALANCE
So, mostly every multiplayer game has a meta. When DE do something with game balance, they never try to foresee what's going to happen with meta. That leads to constant buffs, nerfs, rebuffs and renerfs. If literally anything becaming too popular among the players, as for example former Mesa, being primary damage source on defence type missions, it's going to be nerfed at the level that you'll never seen it again, like Mesa today.
Suggestions?
Someone said that gold rule of critisizing is suggesting better things. Right now what game is lacking is good competent developers that should've taken this game 2-3 years ago, when it was gold time of it. But since that is alredy impossible, I would suggest at first not to try to invent a wheel by♥♥♥♥♥♥like Riven mods and just buff or recall nerfs on warframes, literally noone plays on.
Then as endgame content, I would recommend adding something like global war between Tenno, Corpus and Grineer for control on map sectors, giving opportunities to use different sectors like trading hubs, that allow Tenno place different parts and resources for sale for desired price without need of trading for >1 hour in trade chat or without trading restrictments and pays, a sectors that contains different types of forge-like facilities, that allows creating things with lesser material requirments or almost immediatly and a sector that allows breeding kubrows and kavats with increased speed, a sectors that allows to refill their loyalty and health for free. Each captured sector would provide opportunity to all Tenno to use it, but other fraction would try to fight it back or capture it, with players required to defend it.
To improve clan and archwing elements, I would suggest creating mobile orbital bases like stations and ships that clan alliances must build by combined efforts of it's players, and this things should be defended with combined archwing/land missions, that allows boarding attacking capital ships to kill their crew instead destroying the ship itself. This mobile orbital bases would be required to lauch an assault on planet sector and each of additional base would ease the situation on planet, calling people to rise against tyrans and etc. To addition, making missions like stopping the train full of resources on shipyards of Cerera or robbing space trade caravans of Corpus with Archwing would bring diversity in ways crafting materials can be achieved, further reducing grind by giving an opportunity to go on dangerous and hard mission instead of it, increasing game freshness overall.

By getting account levels, you will get the possibility to get more influence points so you can trade it for more items, more trades will be available daily.

I wanted to take a moment to state that this game has its ups and its downs. Overall I would say the multiplayer is glitchy yet addictingly fun (Always fun to yell AAAAGAAAATHAAAAA when running in there). The weapon variety is lacking and any server lag can make the game nearly impossible to play legitly without just swinging wildly. I host my own server with my friends and face bots when we want to have a nice day of carnage. I just wish that the server software had more options and possibly more spawn-able bots (or difficulty levels on them)
A few more details:
The game is 100% multiplayer and due to the nature of the game you tend to get a good deal of people frustrated at each other with at least 1-2 attempts to kick a player every match. Although the controls are rather simple there are a good number of moments where the reach of a weapon isn't clear nor are the enemy's "telegraphed movements" acurately portrayed so you never really know who is swingging their weapon first and if you're in range of the hit. On that same note, be prepared to be yelled at as friendly fire is a common theme in the game as well as attempts at stealing kills. I can't count how many times I've been fighting a guy one-on-one only to have a teammate run in there lobbing off my head in an attempt to steal my thunder. Yes, you can kick someone for friendly fire (its a nice touch that they include the amount of damage dealt to teammates in the voting window) but I've had matches where people are voted to be kicked due to friendly fire that was clearly on accident and let's be frank here- when a skirmish happens EVERYONE has a little friendly fire.
On the note of multiplayer- the different game modes are refreshing. It's great to go from a free-for-all mass chaos match to an object oriented map or a team battle to a duel arena. The variety is nice but the game feels like it could use more support from the developers- the content is lacking for the price tag and you would think there would be more weapon variety or at least some more 'unlockables' or something a little 'flashy to earn'.
Final notes:
The game is a lot of fun to play but keep in mind that the $25 price tag is a little steep given the amount of content you receive. If the game is on sale for $10 or under however- pick it up and enjoy a weekend of bloody murders!

Awesome game, hours of enjoyment for a low price. This is about the only game that makes my heart pound. When you earn your first triple kill you'll be giddy. It's a game of skill, it doesn't take a long time to learn how to play but it takes a long time to get good at.

You will die a lot unless you are a prodigy, don't be surprised if in your first dozen games you get a 1:4 k:d. I've been playing for a little while and I can generally get up to a 1:1 or a 1.5:1. The weak players drop out before they get good, and this leaves the average players pitted against the experts.
Overall though, an excellent game with minor weaknesses. Enjoy!

This review is for the new players ONLY, you may have a totally different or opposite opinion that is totally fine but please no rage arguments here.
I see the main reason people dislike about this game is the amount of grinding and lack of main story quests (only a few such as Second Dream and The War Within). I totally get that and I do agree that those two are major cons that are enough to outweight the pros to some people.
So if you are looking for the answer whether this game is good or not please keep in mind for some stuffs of this game:
1. This is a free-to-play game, meaning that the budget and staff the dev has are much limited compared to major companies like Square Enix or EA. Making a story quest with cutscenes, dialodges, and other fancy stuff costs A LOT especially for a free-to-play game since the money only comes from people who buy plat with their cash.
2. Well this is a free-to-play game so of course there will be pay-to-win stuff right? I have a good news for you: even if you don't spend a cent for this game you can still literally get access to everything (excluding the cosmetic items). The only main difference between a pleb and a rich person is the rich person can RUSH things. If you don't mind letting the crafting table spending 12 hours or a few days to craft your items then you basically have the same access to a paid person.
3. Enough of those free-play stuff, what's the pros and cons of this game?
Pros:
Lots of weapon choice
Lots of warframes (classes), each of their unique abilities.
Freedom of your movement such as jumping, sliding, rolling, you can even climb walls with your 2 feet
Positive and active community
Great graphics without requiring high level specs (mine is Raedon HD 7750 and it works without lagging)
Cons:
Very few central story quests
VERY HUGE amount of grinding NECESSARY
Some special modes like Archwing need to be reworked
Please note the pros and cons are from my opinions based on my experience with the game.
So, should you get this game?
Only if you don't mind the grinding and main story part. Otherwise in terms of mechanics this game is great (in fact the closest to my ideal video game)

This game is one of the only online, multiplayer games that not only have I enjoyed but found myself returning to time and time again.  Cyborg ninjas in space, it's a hard thing not to have fun with and many of the new features have been great!
The game modes consist mostly of: kill all enemies, hold points, stealth missions, escorts (though not as bad as in other games) and specific target captures or assassinations and I have to say that each of these feels pretty good, doesn't waste much of your time and will get you used to the gameplay quickly.  Teaming up with up to three of your friends is easy and plenty of fun.  Ranking up consists of skill-based challenges and joining factions can unlock exclusive weapons and gear as well as make a few enemies the more you participate.  Joining a dojo will also grant you the ability to trade items with others (though items have to be unranked and unmodified, fair warning) and there's even some PvP elements, though it's not its strongest feature.
All of this being said, it has hang-ups.  For starters, the new navigation map is terrible compared to the simple one we had before.  It very much feels like a case of aesthetic over-design conflicting with user friendliness.  The new system for acquiring prime items is simple enough, but you have to wait on the right kind of mission you want for the right relic to unlock, there's still a huge RNG factor (though you can opt to get the same reward of a friend instead of stick with your own, which is great when four people are hunting for a particular thing) and really the process seems to have reduced our chances of getting what we want in the end.
The rail network can jump into a blackhole!  I had every region of the star map unlocked prior to its integration and though I can still travel to all of those places, it's locked a particularly big portion of the main story arch behind those rails which aren't completed for me (some of which have some pretty steep requirements that I just don't have the time for).  It's a shame, because Waframe has a storyline that I'm very into and want to progress to the next portion of, but I've been hard-stopped by this rail system thing that I just can't invest the time and effort in, rather than being it's own, separate questline like the previous arcs were and it was annoying enough to get through the whole Second Dream phase back then.  You shouldn't hide your plot behind your new gimmicks, it just sours the experience for me.
All that being said, I still recommend this  game, there's plenty to do and you really don't have to spend a penny on it!

My first negative review. I look for the best in games, and rarely do I dislike a game more than like it, but ARK is the first. I wholeheartedly do not recommend this game for any reason. I decided to wait until the game's full release to weigh in on whether or not this game is recommended, as a lot was promised by the developers upon release.
Yes, you're not reading wrong. I have nearly 1000 hours in the game. All but 20 or so of them were played before Patch 246 or thereabouts (Redwoods) which hit last year sometime. I believed in the game and the devs back then. I recommended it and ran my own private server. Up until then, I had overlooked a lot of the smaller red flags with the company's behavior.
It changed when the Scorched Earth was released. Up until then I'd supported the developers. Maybe I was naive, but I can say for certain, the release of the paid DLC, on the heels of a lawsuit, when there were so many issues that needed resolving  drove the nail in the coffin. Mr. Stieglitz's smug reply to the outcry over this, gave me a pretty clear idea of the lead dev attitudes. Watching everything unfold from the dishonestly about his involvement in the company, to the lawsuit, to the DLC fiasco, Clearly Mr. Stieglitz was more interested in money than integrity. I uninstalled the game, removed any trace of it from my PC and moved on to other games.
With the announcement of Ark leaving early access, I still refused to purchase the DLC but I  came back to see if perhaps things had moved in a better direction. Sadly I find that nothing was improved at all. There were more dinos, more cosmetics and more weapon tiers, but the foundations of the game were still utterly broken. Performance is spotty, bugs are rampant and cheating is commonplace. The toxicity on the forums is unreal. Everything but the newest, shiniest toys are neglected. A few examples of things that have affected my player group specifically:
- The Center map has been all but abandoned
- Primitive plus is full of issues that have yet to be solved
- TEK is now the be all, end all of the game. Everything below it has been neglected
- New dinos are being announced and implemented, Yet the older ones are ignored.
- The pushing of transferring around between ARKs when they still haven't solved base game issues
Their quality is all over the place. some things are polished, but a lot feels like an after thought. There is no real cohesiveness to the game. It went from a survival game with PVP, dinosaurs, and weapons and structures that made sense, to a rush for space tech gear, to raid each other, ignoring the dinos. it honestly feels like a case of developers not having a clear picture of what they want to do, and simply throwing in things that 'look cool'. They've lost sight of what is they are trying to make. It's sloppy all around. Beautiful graphics and high def textures can't hide a bad foundation.
This isn't a game that can be played for an hour a day and left, so it's imperative that players can be assured that game breaking bugs aren't going to destroy all that hard work. Players want to know that the devs won't decide on a whim to introduce something to the game without regard for it's effect on the community. (I'm looking at you, handcuffs, and heavy handed nerfs taken too far.) The game itself has potential, but not in the hands of the current team. So no, even after 800 hours pre patch 246 and 16 hours in the last few weeks, I do not recommend it.
At this point, even if the game was completed to utter perfection, the head of the company himself has tarnished the reputation of the game and the studio. With him at the helm, and others on the team condoning this behavior, ARK is a ship with no sails. There is no telling what kind of reckless direction it will set sail in. The increase to $60.00 didn't do them any favours, nor did bragging that they were a 'AAA quality studio'.
I don't agree with Wild Card's ethics. I don't agree with the way they treat their players. That is as important to me as the gameplay itself. As my library illustrates, I've contributed to a lot of Early Access games. And none of them have been as much of a heartache as this one. As much as my friends and I love dinos, and as much love and effort as I have poured into this game in the hopes that it would triumph, this won't be a game we'll be supporting in the future.

I'd like to say what got me into Warframe to begin with.
The actual gameplay itself is super fun and very smooth. Not to mention, the preferred way of moving around quickly in this game is straight up torpedoing yourself through the air. Can't complain about that! (As many other reviews have stated - you're basically a space ninja with special powers.)
So along the lines of the gameplay - this can be changed by which Warframes and weapons you choose to equip. The underlying gameplay will always be there, but you can change it up how you see fit.
(After a ton of grinding for said Warframes and weapons, of course! All drops in this game are RNG - unless stated otherwise.)
The other thing that really made me love this game is the community. Warframe honestly has one of the friendliest, non-toxic and most helpful communities I've seen in a game in a long time. If you have a question, it will most likely get answered, and answered well. (The chat usually has a ton of people talking at once, you may have to make yourself be seen. But it WILL get answered.) I've even had a couple random people give me things to help me out (blueprints) and ran missions with me (carried me).
For questions that don't get answered, you will have to head to the internet. The wikia page has the most up-to-date information.
Unfortunately, one of the biggest problems I've had since returning to this game, is trying to find information online and most of it being years old. It's been very frustrating as a semi-new player..
Warframe doesn't really thrive in the tutorial department. You really have to learn things on your own after learning the VERY basics of the game. There is still a ton that I don't know.
To help any new players, my most used sites for information have been: warframe.wikia (most up-to-date information, somewhat lacking on more needed information), tennodrops (shows location for drops of items), and deathsnacks (keeps you updated with alert missions [alert missions reward random loots, such as blueprints for weapons, aesthetic helmets, crafting components, and more]).
All in all, it's a great game. There's always more stuff being added to it, and the devs seem to be pretty active. As with any game that is constantly updated, there will be some issues every now and then, and sometimes the community's wishes aren't granted. But that isn't enough to make this a bad game.
I recommend  trying it out if you enjoy torpeoding around, slashing enemies to bits, and using random powers to crush the souls of said enemies. :D

When I was younger(I'm 18 at the moment), I had a♥♥♥♥♥load of free time on my hands. And I was struggling about what to fill it with. Warframe seemed a decent game then. And I dont know is it me getting more mature or is it game becoming worse, but I fear the last. The game has a variety of problems that not even started worked on, part of which became even more troubling thanks to devs efforts. So here they are:
GRIND
Game is about grind. When I saw Farming Simulator 2016 cover with warframes all around it, it only caused me a faint sad smile, because it's literally the truth. There is nothing wrond with a grind being a MMO game element, because there wouldn't anything to do in this kind of games without it. But this game takes it on whole new level. Grind new equipment, grind expendables for it, grind resources for new equipment to be made, repeat. Only point of getting stronger ingame is to farm more and farm faster. And Devs, yet saying, that they'll reduce the grind in game, only make game more ♥♥♥♥ing grindier, adding more weapons and warframes, yet creating absolutely nothing new. Why bother fixing something, that works and gives a ♥♥♥♥♥on of money, right?
DEVS
I do not know such insult, what could fully and completely describe Digital Extremes. Started as shy and humble studio on the edge of bunkrupt, they've lost their mind after Warframe being such a successful game. They care not about players desires and adding new interesting content to the game. Yet, that isnt the worst part. The worst part being the fact, that they silence critisizing people, ban their accounts, even banning them on support forums after their logical question "Why my account permabanned". The only answer, beside ban on support forums, that you may be getting is "You were banned with reasons". Btw EULA says, that YOUR account isnt in fact yours, but it belongs to DE, who make a great act of beneficence, giving you the right to use it for free for a time being. No matter how many cash you've poured in this game. Damn, RevxDev, the youtuber, that suffered everything I listed above buyed every single prime access (there was 5 of them before he got banned), that costs, like 80-120 bucks each. And only thing he've done to deserve such a thing is simply critizising the game. Not hating and lying about the game, but fairly pointing on all good and bad sides of the new updates and etc. Btw prime accesses were created to support dying company. But after 4 years of constant money pumping they are still there. Guess why?
NO ENDGAME CONTENT
That's it. When you have all most useful warframes, guns and companions, you may think "it's time to finish farming and roll into some more serious bisness this game has to offer". But there is no such a thing in Warframe. You farm new equipment to farm again. Fighting system may be at first glance interesting and facinating, but all you going to do with it is spam 1-2 skills that your warframe being valued for and nothing more. PvP is foking and boring♥♥♥♥♥♥ Archwing, which I, unlike the other welcomed and liked, is not being developed further 5-6 different missions and 3-4 weapons for each of slots.
NERFS AND BALANCE
So, mostly every multiplayer game has a meta. When DE do something with game balance, they never try to foresee what's going to happen with meta. That leads to constant buffs, nerfs, rebuffs and renerfs. If literally anything becaming too popular among the players, as for example former Mesa, being primary damage source on defence type missions, it's going to be nerfed at the level that you'll never seen it again, like Mesa today.
Suggestions?
Someone said that gold rule of critisizing is suggesting better things. Right now what game is lacking is good competent developers that should've taken this game 2-3 years ago, when it was gold time of it. But since that is alredy impossible, I would suggest at first not to try to invent a wheel by♥♥♥♥♥♥like Riven mods and just buff or recall nerfs on warframes, literally noone plays on.
Then as endgame content, I would recommend adding something like global war between Tenno, Corpus and Grineer for control on map sectors, giving opportunities to use different sectors like trading hubs, that allow Tenno place different parts and resources for sale for desired price without need of trading for >1 hour in trade chat or without trading restrictments and pays, a sectors that contains different types of forge-like facilities, that allows creating things with lesser material requirments or almost immediatly and a sector that allows breeding kubrows and kavats with increased speed, a sectors that allows to refill their loyalty and health for free. Each captured sector would provide opportunity to all Tenno to use it, but other fraction would try to fight it back or capture it, with players required to defend it.
To improve clan and archwing elements, I would suggest creating mobile orbital bases like stations and ships that clan alliances must build by combined efforts of it's players, and this things should be defended with combined archwing/land missions, that allows boarding attacking capital ships to kill their crew instead destroying the ship itself. This mobile orbital bases would be required to lauch an assault on planet sector and each of additional base would ease the situation on planet, calling people to rise against tyrans and etc. To addition, making missions like stopping the train full of resources on shipyards of Cerera or robbing space trade caravans of Corpus with Archwing would bring diversity in ways crafting materials can be achieved, further reducing grind by giving an opportunity to go on dangerous and hard mission instead of it, increasing game freshness overall.
If you wonder why I'm writing all of these here, and not on Warframe forums, well, it's because noone there cares about what I have to suggest. And as long, as people waste money on this game, they never will.
OVERALL
At the moment the game is dull. It's not that bad that one can imagine, but playing it really resembles work. It has it's pros, but atleast for me, at this point cons overweight all of them. Yes, the visuals are good, yes, the fight system is good, but that's all there is good in this game, really

When push comes to shove I feel that I should write a review about any game I have over 100 hours in and at this point in my life I have wasted a grand total of 822 hours in this game. So, uh yeah, I'm going to give it a review,
This is an overall description of the game but it's quite long and quite detailed and if it's TL feel free to DR.
You click, a lot, you level things up and you advance zones, it's a sort of different spin on the clicker genre. The original clickers are all about production, and in that respect this game is different but simular. You want to produce DPS, instead of a resource like money or cookies(...cookies...).
This game restricts you a little more by the way of making it so that you need to use your DPS to kill enemies and get gold from them. So there's a middle step between resource and spending.  These enemies are divided into zones, with each zone's enemies having higher health and giving more gold.
Every fifth zones lies a boss zone, a time restricted zone that requires you to beat an enemy more powerful than all other enemies before it. This means that you can genuinely get stuck, without the DPS and you have to grind gold before you take on a boss. That sort of thing is quite new to this genre and instead of waiting for a new unit, a new goal or something you're blocked by a boss, which is a little different.
After you hit Amenhotep and you can ascend you get these neat little things called hero souls. They are mainly used to feed to the insatiable ancients, which give you awesome buffs in exchange. It's like the clicker game on top of the clicker game. Unlike games before it it pretty much requires you to ascend on a daily basis for the amount of souls you need.

They're like ancients in their effects, but you can only have four at once. Any more need to be scrapped before an ascention. The scrapping gives forge cores which can be used to upgrade your main 4.
Not as cool as it sounds to be honest. You can send them on quests to get you gold, souls etc. Resources you could get elsewhere but getting more is always nice, right? They're ok and they sort of add a different flavour to the whole game, which is nice.
Yeah, you heard me, Clans. Multiplayer in a clicker game. It's crazy, you can be a member of a clan and do amazing things with people. There is a daily boss fight where you use your DPS to fight a boss, who then in turn gives you hero souls as a reward. Though, in my opinion, the best part about clans is watching as you destroy other people's highest zone, or compete with someone else to get higher first. It genuinely makes you want to play more and is my favourite part.
If I left something out it's fine, I can always edit more in but I get the feeling you get the point. This game is massive for a clicker game, it's so big and detailed. The community behind it is weirdly close and awesome. There is a subreddit:
in which the developers listen to players, have polls on new hero names, ancient powers etc to add to the game. The openness and willingness to listen to the player base(especially when naming heroes like Orncha Gladeye Didensy Bananna) is just excellent and is the reason this is potentially one of the best clicker games around

This game is one of the only online, multiplayer games that not only have I enjoyed but found myself returning to time and time again.  Cyborg ninjas in space, it's a hard thing not to have fun with and many of the new features have been great!
The game modes consist mostly of: kill all enemies, hold points, stealth missions, escorts (though not as bad as in other games) and specific target captures or assassinations and I have to say that each of these feels pretty good, doesn't waste much of your time and will get you used to the gameplay quickly.  Teaming up with up to three of your friends is easy and plenty of fun.  Ranking up consists of skill-based challenges and joining factions can unlock exclusive weapons and gear as well as make a few enemies the more you participate.  Joining a dojo will also grant you the ability to trade items with others (though items have to be unranked and unmodified, fair warning) and there's even some PvP elements, though it's not its strongest feature.
All of this being said, it has hang-ups.  For starters, the new navigation map is terrible compared to the simple one we had before.  It very much feels like a case of aesthetic over-design conflicting with user friendliness.  The new system for acquiring prime items is simple enough, but you have to wait on the right kind of mission you want for the right relic to unlock, there's still a huge RNG factor (though you can opt to get the same reward of a friend instead of stick with your own, which is great when four people are hunting for a particular thing) and really the process seems to have reduced our chances of getting what we want in the end.
The rail network can jump into a blackhole!  I had every region of the star map unlocked prior to its integration and though I can still travel to all of those places, it's locked a particularly big portion of the main story arch behind those rails which aren't completed for me (some of which have some pretty steep requirements that I just don't have the time for).  It's a shame, because Waframe has a storyline that I'm very into and want to progress to the next portion of, but I've been hard-stopped by this rail system thing that I just can't invest the time and effort in, rather than being it's own, separate questline like the previous arcs were and it was annoying enough to get through the whole Second Dream phase back then.  You shouldn't hide your plot behind your new gimmicks, it just sours the experience for me.
All that being said, I still recommend this  game, there's plenty to do and you really don't have to spend a penny on it!

I feel like...  this is a little bit addictive.  There have been many, many psychology papers and articles written about constant micro releases of dopamine for doing practically next to nothing.  It's essentially what put Zynga on the map monetarily.  To paraphrase one of the best descriptions taken from a psychological evaluation from the effects of World of Warcraft:  "It's like a cup and ball game.  If you had a thousand hands and a thousand cup and balls."
You're never *not* doing something.  Even if you leave it on in the background like I did and come back to it periodically.  And as long as you're checking back periodically, you're making "progress".  Progress to what, however...  Nowhere...  Everywhere...  There is no actual logical ending to this.  It spans infinitely.  There was a soft cap not to long ago where you ran out of achievements to obtain, but they just recently added a significant amount of extra content and achievements.
I'm conflicted as to which button to press on the recommendation though.  To say nothing of whether this can actually even be considered a game as much as a vehicle simply to reprogram us to be addicted to constant input and giving us something to always be doing in between every single tiny nook and cranny of our time between loading screens, commercial breaks, and waiting for telephone calls.
Am I truly having fun, or am I addicted?  Either way...  come join me down the rabbit hole and the adventure into madness.

The anxiety before the next kill. The stress before being killed yourself. Any dedicated player of Chivalry: Medieval Warfare knows these two bitter feelings well.
Although its price may bring a sizeable punch to your Steam Wallet (when it isn't on sale/for those who must choose their games wisely) this competitive game offers a chance at glory and mayhem.
+ Hours of play can allow you to watch your own skills strengthen. (Nothing beats the satisfaction of victory)
+ Combat is - often - precise, yet simple.
+ The Mayhem of Free for All and Large Team Deathmatches makes for some memorable hilarity.
+ Rather acceptable visual quality for those who want it.
+ Hysterically comical voice-acting.
+ Laughable gore.
+ Great (official) servers for beginners.
+ Excellent variety between classes.
+ Weapons and statistics differing between classes makes players capable of adopting their own playstyle.
+ Intruiging enough customization. Sigils, colors.
+ Yelling.
+ Worth its selling price.
+ Effective DLC.
- Server lag and latency issues can take away from the game's precision, causing frustration.
- Some - although excusable - unnecessary clipping goofs with models and environments.
- Potentially severe difficulty spike for newer players.
- Additional (but optional) costs for customization. (Some costing nearly half of the game's selling price [Depending on bundle])
- Blocking system is difficult to perfect. + But a blast once perfected.
- Third Person Perspective is lacking. + First Person Perspective is spot on.
For its moderately cheap price, any FPS enthusiast or Medieval Fanboy should own this game, without a doubt. It's fun, hilarious, pretty, and worth a thousand deaths to gain skill. Once skilled enough, duels with equally matched opponents and rallies with lesser foes are a true experience. But, prepare for hours of suck, beforehand. Trial by error is the key to learning in this innovative First Person Slasher.
An Easy 8/10
Enjoy!

This is an unbiased, devil's advocate kind of review.
Acknowledge the bugs. Step 1 to fixing any problem is admitting you have one.
Unfortunately ARK does a horrible job of recording and properly linking patch notes, much less tracking a bug list and addressing the issues the community complains about head on.
Publish a Trello board or something!
Step 2 would be to actually fix the issues. Various fixes that were needed over a year ago only recently got pushed, and we are still encountering bugs that cause entire tribes, dinos, bases, hundreds of hours to just go poof. I can't count the number of times I've had to restore backups, copy files, essentially fix issues with my servers that shouldn't even exist. I've even had to learn about the file structure at a depth that only a developer should have to.
Now, all of this being said, I've played over 2000 hours, and I can say that the game is definitely worth playing. I bought it when it was less than half of what it costs now, before there was even a season pass. I paid for Scorched Earth and I can say that I don't regret it. We had many hours of enjoyment and struggle, which made it totally worth it.
The bosses still need a LOT of work. The balance simply isn't there.
90% of the work done in the last year has been to add dinos, to add items, add the tech cave, redesign the already functional UI, and essentially rework a ton of issues that should have been addressed on release day. What is obvious to most of the players of ARK after some time, is that the developers don't spend any real time actually playing their own game.
Roughly 20% of the features added recently were actually mods at one point, which tells everyone we pretty much need outside developers to give us features we already expect from the game. That's almost sad, but it also means that the community wants the game to succeed, which is critical for any successful title.
Optimization needs a lot of work. It's playable but keep your drivers up to date.
Now for the upside.
The game puts you in a completely up-side-down world where dinosaurs are everywhere, you start from barebones nothing. You have to go find rocks, sticks, plants, and make everything from scratch. Build a base, tame a triceratops, and defend yourself by any means necessary. You start with sticks and stones, and eventually, after a lot of effort, build up to energy weapons and power armor that gives you superpowers.
The PVP is definitely fun, but there are some serious bugs when it comes to damage, hit boxes for headshots, and bullet drop for some weapons either doesn't exist, or bugs out. With that in mind, and some patience, you can score some serious loot when raiding.
This game offers the most out of any survival sandbox I've ever played.
Build a base, tame a wyvern (tiny dragon), fight king kong, install a few mods and do even more. Write your own lore, do some role play, Sniper rifles, assault rifle, shotguns, pistols, there isn't much in the way of sub machine guns or grenade launchers, two very important weapons classes, but you'll make due. The concept is that all of these weapons were fabricated from scratch, so you get what you get and you don't pitch a fit, so the song goes.
You can expect a few rough starts, especially on servers with higher difficulty. We're talking about unofficial servers of course, because official servers are all pillar spammed to hell, making it impossible to build or do anything really. Unoffiical servers can have boosted rates, but also increased difficulty, so the tradeoff can be either fun or painful depending on your outlook. The challenge can be rewarding.
Don't play this game alone. Going solo on a server where there are tribes of players is going to frustrate you quickly.
If you want to start your own ARK server, I can recommend a fantastic and inexpensive ARK host. 60 slots for 15 bucks, with scalable resources (RAM). Hit me up and I'll share the link.

I'd like to say what got me into Warframe to begin with.
The actual gameplay itself is super fun and very smooth. Not to mention, the preferred way of moving around quickly in this game is straight up torpedoing yourself through the air. Can't complain about that! (As many other reviews have stated - you're basically a space ninja with special powers.)
So along the lines of the gameplay - this can be changed by which Warframes and weapons you choose to equip. The underlying gameplay will always be there, but you can change it up how you see fit.
(After a ton of grinding for said Warframes and weapons, of course! All drops in this game are RNG - unless stated otherwise.)
The other thing that really made me love this game is the community. Warframe honestly has one of the friendliest, non-toxic and most helpful communities I've seen in a game in a long time. If you have a question, it will most likely get answered, and answered well. (The chat usually has a ton of people talking at once, you may have to make yourself be seen. But it WILL get answered.) I've even had a couple random people give me things to help me out (blueprints) and ran missions with me (carried me).
For questions that don't get answered, you will have to head to the internet. The wikia page has the most up-to-date information.
Unfortunately, one of the biggest problems I've had since returning to this game, is trying to find information online and most of it being years old. It's been very frustrating as a semi-new player..
Warframe doesn't really thrive in the tutorial department. You really have to learn things on your own after learning the VERY basics of the game. There is still a ton that I don't know.
To help any new players, my most used sites for information have been: warframe.wikia (most up-to-date information, somewhat lacking on more needed information), tennodrops (shows location for drops of items), and deathsnacks (keeps you updated with alert missions [alert missions reward random loots, such as blueprints for weapons, aesthetic helmets, crafting components, and more]).
All in all, it's a great game. There's always more stuff being added to it, and the devs seem to be pretty active. As with any game that is constantly updated, there will be some issues every now and then, and sometimes the community's wishes aren't granted. But that isn't enough to make this a bad game.
I recommend  trying it out if you enjoy torpeoding around, slashing enemies to bits, and using random powers to crush the souls of said enemies. :D
