New features and interesting mechanics; awesome. I don't think this is neccesarily a Steam problem, having allowed this to run early access for so long. It's pretty normal for these things to happen in the service industry, we just aren't used to being served code yet. Plus, because of the mere token equivalent money you gave them for the game, they're just as happy as the restauraunt owner who decided to install a random toys dispenser by the front desk. A studio is much more akin to a restauraunt in my opinion. And anyone who's left with a sour taste, well, its their fault for continuing to eat (play). If you break down everything, and you can, its all math. You could calculate absolutely everything in official servers, thus how much time its going to eat if you really want to do it. So again I say, for those who took  bites too large and are suffering from indigestion now... sorry man, you should have known better.
Ultimately the reason I only have 260 hours to date is becaues I'm fully aware of the breakdowns for video games. It is how I decide whether I want to play something, or even if I can play it through the end. This has been one giant fiasco of pampered gamers who don't know when to step out of a consumerism trap and an experimental studio who knew how to make and spend money.
Would only reccomend for a large group of friends with short minded goals of exploration and community to eliminate the constant grind upwards. Its hard to trust others, or find a tribe. I was never able to join any tribes (that would be worth joining) to date. I can almost compare this game to Eve. There's a right way and a wrong way and a better way to do almost anything, and consequences can be dire, causing you to become more serious than you may have wanted to be. Groups of players only work best when operating like a beehive out of their base and pvp will never be worth it because of pre-established super powers aka Alpha Tribes.
Edit: Think about WoW. Think about reaching end game. How satisfied are you gonna be after hundreds of thousands of hours working your way up with your friends just to watch a health bar reach 0 on every boss. And then what? If you're in a PvE server, you ain't got a thing left to do but mess around. If you're in a pvp server, you start wrecking everyone you can. Both of those gets old fast. In the end, all you're left with is mindless dino-breeding-grinding (SFW).
Conclusion: The "Journey" is the only thing that makes this worth playing. Replayability is dictated by maps, of which there are 3. Three Ark experiences. Who the f**k has time for that?!

I have played more then 150 hours already.. thats not much for a grind game, but.. what can i say about it? - The game is Very Good! I am not sure if you will even find another Free game of such a great quality!
Not more.. not less. You will really feel what your character is doing. You can run fast, climb on walls, snake and do high damage backstabs. There are ranged/melee weapons in game. Is melee viable? Sure! Block the ranged projectiles and use powerful special abilities of your warframe.
And even more, you can experience full 3d space fights, by fitting your wings on, and flying like a rocket :)
There are some quests to do, but basically, i dont feel like living in the story. Its kind of separate little stories about the world, and you will unlock some content by doing them. The game is a grind basically, we are playing to unlock new warframes and craft new weapons to try and find the one you will like most. I love grinding games, but you see, you will not get tons of equipment like in other games on every run, its just very few of it.
No dialogs and other♥♥♥♥♥♥. no decisions to make.. Just kill them all :) But thats not bad.. isnt it?
What is it about in this game? There are two types of levels: Account level (you will get it by leveling other stuff), and items levels (mastery).
By mastering the item, you will unlock additional slots in the item, where you can put "Mods", and the mods basically are the reason of damage and defense. How long will it take to master one? (Max level 30) Later on, its possible to master the item by doing even one defense mission, if you are good enough, or if you have really good party :) Ah yah, you can upgrade the mods too...
By getting account levels, you will get the possibility to get more influence points so you can trade it for more items, more trades will be available daily.
Leveling system is really good, it gives the new players a possibility to dive in the game from the very start!
Definitely Not! You can get everything without paying a cent, and getting the item will not take ages of farming :)
Thats it for now :) Maybe i will upgrade the review in another 150 hours of playing. I am definitely recommending this game to play for people who like to fill the collections and love the action! Dont hit me hard if you dont like the review ;)

1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

I can't think of a review, so here's a cinnamon roll recipe:
Ingredients
For the Dough:
1 cup whole milk
one 1/4-ounce packet active dry yeast (2 1/2 teaspoons)
1/4 cup plus 1/4 teaspoon granulated sugar
4 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the bowl
1 large egg yolk
1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla extract
2 3/4 cups all-purpose flour, plus more if needed
3/4 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon freshly grated nutmeg
For the Filling:
All-purpose flour, for dusting
12 tablespoons unsalted butter, softened, plus more for the pan
1/2 cup granulated sugar
3 tablespoons ground cinnamon
For the Glaze:
2 cups confectioners' sugar
1/3 cup heavy cream
4 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted
Directions
Make the dough: Warm the milk in a medium saucepan over low heat until it reaches about 100. Remove from the heat and sprinkle in the yeast and 1/4 teaspoon sugar (don't stir). Set aside until foamy, 5 minutes. Whisk in the melted butter, egg yolk and vanilla.
Whisk the flour, the remaining 1/4 cup sugar, the salt and nutmeg in the bowl of a stand mixer. Make a well in the center and pour in the yeast mixture. Mix on low speed with the dough hook until thick and slightly sticky. Knead on medium speed until the dough gathers around the hook, 6 minutes. (Add up to 2 more tablespoons flour if necessary.)
Remove the dough and shape into a ball. Butter the mixer bowl and return the dough to the bowl, turning to coat with butter. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise until doubled, 1 hour 15 minutes.
Roll out the dough, fill and cut into buns (see instructions below). Butter a 9-by-13-inch baking pan; place the buns cut-side down in the pan, leaving space between each. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise until doubled, 40 minutes. Preheat the oven to 325.
Bake the buns until golden brown, about 35 minutes. Cool in the pan 15 minutes. Meanwhile, make the glaze: Sift the confectioners' sugar into a bowl, then whisk in the cream and melted butter. Transfer the buns to a rack and spoon the glaze on top while still warm.
How to Form Cinnamon Buns
1. On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough into a 12-by-14-inch rectangle with the longer side facing you.
2. Spread with the softened butter, leaving a 1/2-inch border on the far long edge. Mix the sugar and cinnamon; sprinkle over the butter.
3. Brush the unbuttered far edge with water. Roll the dough away from you into a tight cylinder and press on the long edge to seal.
4. Cut the cylinder with a sharp knife to make 6 equal-size buns.

Good, visually appealing game that can almost run on a potato because despite it's nice visuals it's not as demanding. Like pretty much all MMOs, this one is also victim of the holy grind and RNG sickness. But at least the game mechanics overall set it way apart from anything else out there. This is an instance based melee and third person shooter game that also offers parkour moves and stealth play. Can be played solo or with up to 4 players (more in certain missions)
The game has a high skill ceiling and from mid game onwards, a very high skill demand as well. Simply put, this game is not for the casual nor the faint of heart, as even pre-end game content will be way too difficult for the non dedicated. So you either play and learn or leave and move on. No middle ground here. But if you decide to stay, you will see all the love the developers have invested in the game's stages and overall creativity of the warframe suits and weapons to be obtained, and all the lore hidden away behind challenging stages, enemies and bosses.
The game offers a good deal of customization as well. There's a lot of cosmetics to wear and all warframe suits and companion pets can be recolored.
On the off side, this game is not for the completionist. As of this date, I doubt more than 2 people can obtain everything in the game, as many things have been permanently locked behind either past event prizes or founder exclusive stuff, and even stuff added for this or that special player. So those coming to try and complete a collection of things, know there's some permanently unobtainable stuff. Also, again, the difficulty in this game can be rather high if you don't have the right gear for the stage. And getting the right gear can take a long while as RNG is tossed at you relentlessly. Not even the real money shop has everything you will need to deal with the harder stages, as much of that gear must be earned through repetition and RNG, or by trading with other players if you get your hands on stuff they may want.
In short, this is a good game to pass some time, but it's not too welcoming of the lazy.

I'm going to write a review as I feel that the current, especially recent reviews are unfair to the game & developers.
Pros:
- Constant updates
- Developers support modders (yay)
- Hours worth of content
- (In my opinion) enjoyable gameplay
- Decent visuals
- Developers have a bounty system for bug reporting on official servers (yay)
Cons:
- Performance can be choppy on slower systems particuarly
- Bugs are somewhat frequent (Although they're usually fixed fast from what I've seen)
- Community (Althought subject to change between servers) is commonly quite unfriendly
- Some strange decisions, such as raising the price drastically, which really does feel a bit out of place, and then immediately releasing a fairly expensive season pass.
Currently, at the time of writing this review I have 441 hours in the game, which is more than some and less than many. I've had alot of fun playing ark, with friends or alone. The developers have made more progress than basically any other early access game developer can claim they have. Rarely games even make it out of early access, but ark has a large or impactful update every week or so, and I think that's great. Changes that are made that are not widely accepted by the community are sometimes reverted, or stay for the sake of the greater good for the progress of the game. For example, the flyer nerf that almost everyone hates. Yes, flyers are slower, but it's not like it will now take you AGES to cross the map anyway as theyre not THAT slow. However, the advantage of this nerf is that it helped revert the "ride pteranodon pick up player drop player at the speed of sound" pvp, which is literally the only PVP I experienced on every official server I played on, which isn't very fun gameplay.
New additions to the game via dinos, progression or quality of life updates are fairly frequent, which I enjoy, albeit sometimes pointless.
I think it's important to note that I play on high or epic settings the majority of the time, and pull 60 or so FPS, running on a GTX 1060 with a 3560k CPU (Not over clocked) and 8gb DDR3 ram, without any issues. My system is in no way top tier and I'm really not experiencing the "God awful" optimisation that everyone seems to tag the game with. I rarely crash on vanilla, and by rarely I mean I've crashed maybe twice in total.
I play on modded servers, most of the time which use core mods that add content to the game, and I enjoy every bit of it. The modding community for ark is fairly diverse and add some great additions to the game, which is made even better by the fact that the developers support the modders for their game that are making good progress.
Overall, I just think the game is fairly good, and I really enjoy it. Those who aren't a huge fan of survival games probably wont get as much of a kick out of it. Developers make alot of progress and have some good habits, but also have a strange marketing scheme. Try it out, you'll probably enjoy it.

I can't believe this game is free to play. And unlike most free to play games, it is NOT pay to win!
I give this game 8/10.
Pros:
You can unlock everything in the game for free.(sans some cosmetics)
Very large player base, ranking in the top 10 on steam for player count every time I check.
It has a very large amount of customization, allowing you to tailor design your own strengths to make your play style.
The dev team is very active and still years after release they are releasing more and more content!(for free!!! Did I mention that yet?!?!)
Shots fired are calculated client side, meaning if your connection is slow that if you hit something on your screen, it stays hit!! Lag is a thing of the past!
With seemingly endless amounts of things to do, it's very hard to put it down... there are so many players with literally thousands of hours of play time! That alone is a testament to how enthralling it can be!
Cons:
The in-game tutorial is not the greatest. Also despite the massive wealth of knowledge available to draw from online is partially outdated.(this is due to the dev team constantly updating and adding content)
It can seem to be a daunting grind fest.
I am yet to sink my teeth into the end game, but from the onset this game is just so well finished. The graphics are silky smooth, the theme song just keeps reminding me of stranger things! I completely forgot that I was playing a free game! The gameplay is incredibly versatile, if you feel like being a ninja you can do crazy parkour and stealth kills with one of the many melee weapons available, or if you are channeling your inner leeroy you can charge in guns blazing raining down mayhem against streams of enemies. If you feel like exploring and opening chests and collecting resources the maps change every time, meaning even playing the same mission over and over will not feel too repetitive. If speeding runs are your thing, you can move incredibly fast if you put your mind to it, it seems to always make me smile when I successfully parkour through a stage like lightning.
The only things you can't get for free don't really have much importance to gameplay, new colors for your character and ship, and speed up things you are building. If you have the time, you can be just as strong as someone who spends hundreds of dollars! But like all free games, it is a lot faster to spend money to unlock things than it is to earn them... because of this it can become just a grind fest after a while. That's the only reason I have not given warframe 10/10.
All in all, warframe is thoroughly entertaining. The price tag means you have nothing to lose in trying this out! There is a certain game that got released, which shall be referred only to as "D.....y", that is just a bad and limited copy of warframe. The similarities are endless but after playing both I have to say warframe has far more to do and seems to just exceed D.....y in about every aspect!

I'm going to write a review as I feel that the current, especially recent reviews are unfair to the game & developers.
Pros:
- Constant updates
- Developers support modders (yay)
- Hours worth of content
- (In my opinion) enjoyable gameplay
- Decent visuals
- Developers have a bounty system for bug reporting on official servers (yay)
Cons:
- Performance can be choppy on slower systems particuarly
- Bugs are somewhat frequent (Although they're usually fixed fast from what I've seen)
- Community (Althought subject to change between servers) is commonly quite unfriendly
- Some strange decisions, such as raising the price drastically, which really does feel a bit out of place, and then immediately releasing a fairly expensive season pass.
Currently, at the time of writing this review I have 441 hours in the game, which is more than some and less than many. I've had alot of fun playing ark, with friends or alone. The developers have made more progress than basically any other early access game developer can claim they have. Rarely games even make it out of early access, but ark has a large or impactful update every week or so, and I think that's great. Changes that are made that are not widely accepted by the community are sometimes reverted, or stay for the sake of the greater good for the progress of the game. For example, the flyer nerf that almost everyone hates. Yes, flyers are slower, but it's not like it will now take you AGES to cross the map anyway as theyre not THAT slow. However, the advantage of this nerf is that it helped revert the "ride pteranodon pick up player drop player at the speed of sound" pvp, which is literally the only PVP I experienced on every official server I played on, which isn't very fun gameplay.
New additions to the game via dinos, progression or quality of life updates are fairly frequent, which I enjoy, albeit sometimes pointless.
I think it's important to note that I play on high or epic settings the majority of the time, and pull 60 or so FPS, running on a GTX 1060 with a 3560k CPU (Not over clocked) and 8gb DDR3 ram, without any issues. My system is in no way top tier and I'm really not experiencing the "God awful" optimisation that everyone seems to tag the game with. I rarely crash on vanilla, and by rarely I mean I've crashed maybe twice in total.
I play on modded servers, most of the time which use core mods that add content to the game, and I enjoy every bit of it. The modding community for ark is fairly diverse and add some great additions to the game, which is made even better by the fact that the developers support the modders for their game that are making good progress.
Overall, I just think the game is fairly good, and I really enjoy it. Those who aren't a huge fan of survival games probably wont get as much of a kick out of it. Developers make alot of progress and have some good habits, but also have a strange marketing scheme. Try it out, you'll probably enjoy it.

I wanted to love this game so much.  I picked it up almost day 1 early access and played it mostly singleplayer on and off for months, primarily waiting for new dino's and features.   I didn't dedicate myself to the game as much as I would have liked simply because I was waiting for the expanded content, improvements and optimizations, occasionally coming back to test the waters with each new update.
Unfortunately , despite it's promises and massive potential, ARK has gone down hill on a bike with no brakes for months now, to the point where the dino filled survival crafting fun it used to have has been drowned beneath a tide of game breaking bugs, hideously bad optimization and bafflingly atrocious development decisions.
It is a worse game now than it was the first few months of it's early access life.
Let's break it down.  This game has been released now. It's no longer early access and that can no longer be used as an excuse for poor performance.  The game's optimization is nothing short of broken.   I began playing ark way back on an old 660gtx.  Over time I upgraded to an 850 ,  970 and 1080 and the game has run progressively worse and worse with lower resolution and framerates regardless of the grunt I put into my gaming rig.  It runs worse now on release than it did on my ancient 660 back in the first month of early access.
Worse still, the developers have really dropped the ball on community concerns and made bad decision after bad decision.
Releasing a buggy , unfinished, unpolished early access title as an AAA release complete with obscene price tag , and ludicrously overpriced season pass?  Check.
Remove fun, key features and mechanics and replace them with clunky, boring, time consuming nonsense all in the name of 'balance'?  Check.
Take a plain but sevicable UI and interface and replace them with a nausea and eyestrain inducing cluttered blue on blue mess?  Check.
Outright lie to the playerbase about server support and continuation thereby screwing over your loyal customers with potentially thousands of hours in your product leaving them feeling betrayed and ripped off?  Check.
It's really sad that I game I had been eagerly waiting to spend my own thousands of hours with when it was properly released turned out so poor.  Ark now reeks of cash grab when it should have been so much more.  In it's current state for it's current price as a fuly released game, I cannot possibly reccomend it.

If you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

On higher levels you will need more rare ingredients which takes even more time to farm.
2. You can't go on vacation IRL
If you are offline for certain amounts of time your things despawn ingame. Making all your efforts nulled.
I for instance had built a large stone base on an unofficial server, which had increased timers for everything so I could actually play (faster farming, taming etc.) However, I learned that when I would go on a 2 weeks+ vacation to Spain all would despawn. Making all my previous build and grind null. That's a total game breaker for me.
3. Bugs.
Quite so often, too often, you get an error when you try to enter a server. It says 'Failed to install Mod Map' and then you have to alt+f4 out of the game. I had it once, Googled and managed to fix it by manually deleting all mod files one at a time from the bottom of the hierarchy and up. If i try to delete a folder with other folders or files in it, I got a access denied error. VERY time consuming.
About 1 week later, I got the error again. Yet again the game got too time consuming, not to play - but to fix so it can be started, to ruin my preparations for my vacation mentioned in number 2. Therefore, my last chance to try and save my stuff from despawning and my dinos from starving to death during my vacation was ruined by a game bug/error.
It IS a quite fun game, but know what you buy before you buy. Especially now that they bumped up the price!
All things considered, I can't really recommend it.

The concept for the game is great! Unfortunately WildCard's treatment of users time and time again have shown once they get their money from their Early Access buyers like myself they'll screw you over in every way possible, just like the people in PvP.
My experience is as follows:
My clan had a good spot on a Center map. I went through a lot of days where the game constantly crashed on startup or crashed during flight which was frustrating but generally it was fun while it lasted.
WildCard then said (I'm paraphrasing) "you got a week to switch servers and take your stuff or it'll get shutdown".
We transferred over to a new server, but then WildCard initiated a rollback of everything on the servers that should've only set us back a few hours but instead set us back a FULL WEEK with only a few hours to get our dinos out. Why? Apparently some timer bug. I don't really understand the details but when I tried to put in a ticket for it the site wouldn't even let me create an account (confirmation email never got sent).
Out of our clan only two members including myself were active, so we attempted to get the dinos transferred only for ARK to crash on me several times, crash my sound card and constantly freeze for many seconds at a time while being attacked by Dillos. We lost some dinos to that, and lost all of our blueprints and resources to the server shutdown.
Then the timers for the ARK CrossTransfer units kept rolling while the servers were shutting down so we lost even more of our dinos. Great.

Then to add more salt to our wounds, then the person I gave the dinos to when I got what's left out of the Cross transfer pods killed me with my own dinos on the spot instead of inviting me to his clan and providing the metal flak jacket he promised
- but alas, this is the way of PvP, freedom to be a c^&* without consequences, I knew this when I signed up and the Game of Thrones-like betrayal grinded my gears but didn't really shock me much. Joke's on him, WildCard said the server we transferred to was a "Legacy" server and the new servers wouldn't allow transferring from there anyway so he's stuck with a bunch of dinos he can't manage.
At the end of the day, uninstalling this game gave me more time for my real life pets and for other games I can play and develop for. I expect I'm not the only person who suffered at the hands of WildCard's poor customer service and won't be the last. Damn shame.

After about 300 Hours of Gameplay i decided to write a review about this game. I kinda wanted to give a negative review, but i still had a lot of fun with this game so think i'm not in the position to do that. Too bad you cant give a neutral one. Anyway i will go through Pro und Contra Points either way:
Pro:
- A LOT of dinosaurs and prehistorical creatures. And you can tame and ride them. What else do you want?
- Ark looks gorgeus. Even with lower settings (tried high and low ones) the world still looks amazing
- A lot of content (e.g. dinos, structures, tools, weapons) keeps getting added for free
- The Mods the community has developed are very useful (e.g. Structures +) though normally you HAVE to use them because building in ark can be a real pain in the... you know what i mean.
- There are a lot of private servers which are open to everyone. Most of them have some reasonable rules (e.g. don't build in caves or on big resource spawns) and the majority of them use mods which are very useful and fun as i mentioned above. Try it!
Contra:
- The optimization of this game is just horrible. I buyed this game in EA in 2015 after i got myself a new PC with the newest specs on that time. Was still not able to play this game on "Epic" without problems. After 2 years, almost nothing changed. Instead of working on the optimization the dev's are only working on the content. A bit sad in my opinion.
- Bought this game for like 20€ in EA. Good Price, can't complain. Now it's gone up to 60€?! What the.... I really don't think this is reasonable if you consider that this game still has a lot of problems and bugs (e.g. Dinos disapperaing, glitching trough structures when you log out and log in again the next day. Just to mention a few. These are problems that exist since 2 damn years!)
- I don't think i know a game that releases a DLC in EA-Phase. Do you? Once again i think that they should work on optimization instead.
- A Season Pass. Wow. I mean really? After all the things i mentioned above?
Ark is still a lot of fun especially with friends. Makes things also a lot easier ;)
At last i have to mention that all my experince was made on the PvE servers - official and private ones - so i can't speak for the PvP experience.
Hope i could help you all.

Clicker heroes is an incremental clicker/idle game. Click to deal damage to enemies. Earn gold. Spend that gold on upgrades to your click damage. Purchase automatic damage over time, and upgrade that. Unlock special skills and use them to defeat enemies faster, or earn more gold per kill, and invest that gold into more upgrades so you can kill faster and get more gold to invest so you can kill faster and get more gold to invest so you can kill faster and get more gold to invest so you can kill faster and get more gold to invest so you can kill faster and get more gold to invest so you can kill faster and get more gold to invest...
Yep. It's one of these types of games. There's a prestige system that gives you bonus dps whenever you reset, and you can give up some of this bonus dps to purchase various powerups that do a lot of things, such as decreasing skill cooldowns, increase gold dropped, increase dps (more than the dps you lose from buying this).
To many people, this type of game seems boring. To those people, I'd suggest peeking at a few games like this to see what the appeal is. It's basically a distillation of most game genres that have some form of upgrade system, such as obtaining better gear or gaining levels and powerful perks.
Personally, I like these types of games. They satisfy that reward center in the brain. It's a perfect example of the Skinner Box.

Clicker heroes is an incremental clicker/idle game. Click to deal damage to enemies. Earn gold. Spend that gold on upgrades to your click damage. Purchase automatic damage over time, and upgrade that. Unlock special skills and use them to defeat enemies faster, or earn more gold per kill, and invest that gold into more upgrades so you can kill faster and get more gold to invest so you can kill faster and get more gold to invest so you can kill faster and get more gold to invest so you can kill faster and get more gold to invest so you can kill faster and get more gold to invest so you can kill faster and get more gold to invest...
Yep. It's one of these types of games. There's a prestige system that gives you bonus dps whenever you reset, and you can give up some of this bonus dps to purchase various powerups that do a lot of things, such as decreasing skill cooldowns, increase gold dropped, increase dps (more than the dps you lose from buying this).
To many people, this type of game seems boring. To those people, I'd suggest peeking at a few games like this to see what the appeal is. It's basically a distillation of most game genres that have some form of upgrade system, such as obtaining better gear or gaining levels and powerful perks.
Personally, I like these types of games. They satisfy that reward center in the brain. It's a perfect example of the Skinner Box.

I'll start off by saying that at this time, I still actively play this game and still find it to be enjoyable and at times challening.
I'll break this review into sections.
Gameplay
For a third person melle/shooter mmo, Warframe's gameplay is simple and still leaves little to be desired besides perhaps more in depth melee combat systems. The standard gameplay switches between gun driven batrles, to power fights, melee slashing, and stealth combat as well as fully covert operations in the standard gameplay modes. The only flaw within the gameplay itself is with the Arcwing combat systems, and while clunky, can be enjoyable.
Customization
If you're as vain as I am about your characters, Warframe offers some actual customization options that leave most satisfied. However, it should be noted that the color modification in game comes with a single, very basic color palate. Any others must be purchased via differing methods (mostly premium currency).
Community
With most mmo's there is always the risk of idiocy and rude people within a community. Warframe for the most part seems to have enough of a learning curve and time based limitations to seed out the majority of cancerous players. In addition, considering the economy within the game is entirely community driven, it not only pushes the community to be far more polite, but also allows all players access to 90% of the preimium content with little more than time invested.
Story
The story is still sort of in development. The way DE has given us the various story points so far with The Second Dream and The War Within have been less difficult challenges and more cinematic story explanations as to what the Tenno are, where they fit in to the universe and what their relationship to the various factions within the game as well as The Lotus and the Warframes.
Premium Content
There is, so far, only a very small number of items that require a direct cash exchange to attain and none of these effect gameplay ever. The in game premium currency, Platinum, is attainable in varying amounts through community trading that is entirely unregulated by DE. Any and all items besides some asthetic armor that is attainable with platinum can be gained over time via the community. In addition, save for Excalibur Prime and the weapons released with his pack, all other equipment in the game is attainable through trade or via other means in game that do not cost actual money.
In summary this game is quite literally the best free to play, freemium MMO available that I have come across. While it's story is still in development, new content is released very often and it's development team is active within the community, hosting events, giveaways, and podcasts regularly.
Personal Rating 8/10

Listen my review is intended for the player who only wants THE ACTUAL GAMEPLAY AND NOT BE RANTED TO ABOUT THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ DEVS AND THEIR MISTAKES. With that out of the way we can begin.
Now I fully understand compared to most other players my play time doesn't even compare. People are diehard for this game for a reason, and I want to share that reason. The gameplay is just addicting, especially when done solo, or with a couple friends in a private server -that can be for free and without much hassle through the game in my experiences- which leads to an overwhelming positive amount of experiences. Now going onto public Wild Card hosted multiplayer servers is a whole other monster entirely. Expect giants tribes with mega dinos, ghost servers that have been wiped, and hella chinese/korean farm tribes that just wipe underdeveloped servers. Although now compared to the start of the game most underdeveloped servers are now just ghost servers. So expect your time to be spent on friendly community private hosted servers, or some of the modded ones. Doing anything else with the public servers is just a waste of time, and will lead to all your work being wiped out overnight.
Now the fact of the matter is that the game is VERY GRIND HEAVY and is a large commitment if you want to go far. Now while this may sound tedious, its actually very rewarding. You can build large customizeable bases, breed, tame, and ride your favorite dinosaurs, and experience a curve of progression where you feel rewarded for grinding. I mentioned the multiplayer aspects of this game first due to the clear fact that this game is made infinitely better by playing with your friends, or friendly randoms. Now the game is buggy at times, and the Dino AI can go full boosted ape mode. Every game has its shortcomings, but the dinos are truly -starting off, and mid game- far scarier than players. The modding community also makes up for Wild Cards short comings and helps you customize the game to your preferences, and fix the AI. Its a grind game that makes your time invested feel worth it, if you don't believe me look at the play time of many of the reviews left.
In terms of optimization the game has come a far way, but I will warn you that it takes a beast of a rig to play this game fully maxed out. I HEAVILY and again HEAVILY emphasize you do your research to make sure you can run this game before purchasing. Wild Card kinda threw optimization at the fan and hasn't fixed everything so its up to your discretion.
As a final note I want to say that looking towards many of the negative reviews, the criticism is more towards the company rather than the game. While I am in no way claiming their reviews are not valid -as if we are being honest Wild Cards has made lots of questionable choices that are horrible and unacceptable, and their anger is 100% understandable- its more for me about the game rather than the company. What they made is something that is very enjoyable in the right circumstances as I have mentioned. While I understand that the face of a company is represented onto the game they have created, I feel that in this instance it should be more about the gameplay. The ability to become absorbed into this games world is there, you just have to look past Wild Cards boosted♥♥♥♥♥choices, and accept the charm the game can offer you.
Please leave any comments or points I missed -positive or negative- in a comment. Helping people decide whether or not they should buy this game is my only purpose, not flame Wild Card further as its been beaten to death at this point. Thanks.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare, in a nutshell, is a great game about medieval warfare via swords, hammers, bows & crossbows, flails, etc. and etc.
There are 7 Gametypes, consisting of Team Objective, King of the Hill, Free-for-All, Team Deathmatch, Capture the Flag, Duel Mode, and Last Team Standing. Within those 7 Gametypes are the 2 Teams, the Agatha Knights (Blu) and the Mason Order (Red.) On both of these teams, there are 4 Classes, the Knight, Vanguard, Man-at-Arms, and the Archer. Within these Classes, there is a total of 55 Weapons (including fists), 5 Shields, and 9 Extra Items (Bodkin + Fire + Broadhead Arrows for Bows, Lead Balls + Pebbles for the Sling, Crossbow Bolt + Extra Ammo for the Crossbow, a Smokepot, and the Torches for some maps on some gametypes.)
From what I've experienced, the combat and blocking are great, but they might fail a bit sometimes (not occasionally.) You unlock weapons via rank, but this is a bit difficult for 2 reasons. 1 is that some weapons are just hard to use (to the majority), like the Archer's weapons), and 2 is because the ranking system might whack out, or your progress on a weapon might set back a bit. However, graphics are great, but they require a well-off. If there is every any Lag in the game, be it from graphics or ping, it is very noticeable. However, when your weapon meets its target, it is very rewarding and satisfying. The ambience and screaming is great.
Overall, I give this game a 9/10, and I highly recommend that you buy it. It's worth every penny.

Warframe is a great game if you just want to sit down and shoot some mindless enemies with ridiculous weapons for a few hours. Here's a few things you should know about it:
-Weapons include: throwing stars, dual smgs, sniper rifles, bows, grenade launchers, shotguns, grenade-launching shotguns, harpoon guns, a chunk of mutated flesh attatched to a scyth that spits at enemies, flamethrowers, a blender on a string that can pass through walls, a boomerang that can launch enemies out of the map, and swords taller than you are.
-You can play as a dragon, a mummy, a fairy, a magician, and there's a DJ being worked on right now with their own step sequencer.
-I highly recommend approaching the game with a casual mindset, or else you're likely to get frustrated with the grinding and wait times for item crafting.
-Item crafting usually takes 12-72 hours. You can rush things with premium currency, but I implore you not to do that.
-The only thing you NEED premium currency for is item slots. These are cheap though, and you can trade for premium currency fairly easily. Just be patient.
-The most you should ever spend on this game in a year is about $30 if you care about making your gear look pretty.
-If you don't play for about a week you have a VERY high chance of getting a 75% off coupon for premium currency. If you like the game enough, go ahead and buy some to support the devs.
-You get some sweet free gear on March 24th for the game's anniversary, so if you're considering playing and reading this around that time I recommend downloading it ASAP.
-The community is A+ and full of great, funny people and talented content creators. QuietShy and MGLBlaze are some personaly favorites of mine.
If you just want a casual, free game to play every now and then, Warframe is a great pick. It won't keep you sticking around for hours on end though, so don't expect it to become your one true love of gaming.
Best game I have ever played!

Warframe, oh gosh, where do I start?
Okay, so this game has some positives. The weapons are pretty neat, and have a good amount of diversity and there are an absolute ton of Warframes, all of them having fairly different play-styles. Also, the multiplayer co-op is pretty good. I rarely experience connection issues. When you start this game you'll have plenty to do, and will probably be in awe at all there is. You'll be able to play this game for a pretty long time before things get boring.
Now on to the bad stuff about this game...
1) The grind is absolutely disgusting. I get that everyone's always talking about the grind and it may seem like an overused complaint, but it isn't. People have plenty reason to be complaining about it. Almost every single thing you do in this game is going to be a grind. Want to get Nova? Gotta fight Raptor over and over and over and over until you finally get all of her parts. But here's where it gets good: it's all RNG. You could very well just get her chassis 3 times in a row. You could get her chassis 10 times in a row. Everything is RNG. It would already be bad enough if you had to fight bosses 3 times to get all the individual blueprints (systems, chassis, and neuroptics), but you also have a chance of getting some part you already have. What's even worse is the Warframes you don't get from bosses tend to also have RNG-based aquirement. It's the same with prime gear. All prime gear is able to be gotten with void relics, but here's the catch... It's (once again) all RNG-based! As if ALL of this isn't bad enough everything else requires grinding. Want to max out your health-boosting mod? Gotta spend a few weeks worth of credits on it. Now if you want to get your mod maxed out faster, don't worry, you can just spend 12 hours a day on Warframe for a week and hopefully you'll have enough credits then, no promises though. Oh, wanna hear a secret? Leveling up your mastery rank is also a grind. To increase your mastery rank you have to level up warframes and weapons, but since there's a maximum level on weapons and Warframes you have to get more weapons and Warframes. Y'know what that means? More grinding. I could keep going on and on, but I think I've made my point.
2) There's a tremendous amount of waiting. After you've spent hours farming the parts necessary for your new weapon you have to wait 12-24 hours for it to finish construction. People can call me impatient all they want, but in general this system is stupid. If I spend lots of time getting lots of stuff I should at least be able to use my new item right away, but nope! I gotta wait. Awesome.
3) Forma. This stuff is evil. The purpose of Forma is to add or change a polarity slot on a W/W (Weapon/Warframe), which means you can store more mods on your W/W, but there's a problem... Adding this thing to your weapon resets it to level 0, which means (you guessed it) MORE GRINDING. On some W/Ws you may even need to add a minimum of 3 or even 4 Forma to fit all the mods you want on to it.
4) W/W capacity. Yup, there's a maximum capacity to how many W/Ws you can have. After all the grinding and waiting for your item you have to do more grinding to get the platimum required to increase your maximum capacity, which means you either have to trade for the platinum or buy it with real money. Trading's great and all, but you may not find anyone looking for your items, so you either gotta go through a long tedious process of negotiating (if people are willing to negotiate at all) or you gotta send the game developers your cash.
5) Lack of map variety. Some planets are completely identical. Like, COMPLETELY identical. The maps are systematically generated, but there's a heavy lack of rooms for the system to generate, so after a few levels you'll realize you've seen the room you're in 10 times already.
6) Pay to accelerate. I won't say this game is pay to win, because it's not. You can get as far as someone who's spent a lot of money on this game without spending a dime on it yourself, but it's gonna take you a dang long time. If I hadn't spent $40-$60 on this game I would be significantly lower level, no doubt about it.
That's all folks! If you want to have some fun and maybe play this game a little bit then go ahead, but if you're considering playing this game really hardcore DON'T. All in all I wouldn't recommend this game to a friend.

Digital Extremes has accomplished a rarity, building a free-to-play massively-multiplayer-online game rich in variety. My primary use for the game is as an excuse to game on-line with my brother who lives 5 hours away. We've enjoyed discovering the various tilesets, mission types, gear loadouts, and quest story-lines.
By avoiding the open-world fetch-quest model and focusing instead on 10-20min combat missions, Warframe presents easily digested chunks of gameplay. Meanwhile, rich layers of customization (see Mods) exist for those who want to improve their in-match performance and unlock new play areas.
Less about where you're going (the story is fairly thin) and more about what you pretend to be (a space ninja turning the tide in a battle for the solar system), Warframe entertains while rewarding each player's evolving skills. Five stars.

NOTICE: I actually like this game and I plan to continue to play it, however I cannot recommend it right now.
Pros:
ARK is a game that was first introduced to me by a friend and to be honest, this game, to me, is a lot of fun to play with a group of friends. The game concept is simple, tame dinos, fighting each other and try to survive. Personally this is something I tend to enjoy in games. I love other survival games like "The Forest," and "7 Days to Die," so this one was one I naturally started to take a liking to immediately. It was similar to those types of games, but you got to tame and ride dinosaurs.
Cons:
This game currently has far too many cons for me to even remotely consider recommending it to a friend or anyone else considering buying it. For starters, the game hashad 3 years in early access with a (previously) strong fan community. The game looked cool and was a fun idea that people wanted to see grow, but its all being thrown away slowly but surely.  The  game itself has had a lot of bugs with it and it needs a LOT of refinement. One of the largest problems with ARK is the way the game is updated. Literally every day or every other day there is a new update for the game. Now this wouldn't be so bad since it shows that the developers are still working on the game, but they rarely tell the community what they are updating. Not only that, but on many occasions the game has updated and I have had to go through an overly complex number of steps to fix it including uninstalling ALL my current mods to the game, uninstalling the map I have in the game (in this case Ragnarok), rebooting my computer in safe mode and then deleting all the reminent files from said mods (I'd think this was a personal problem if not for the fact that my friend also experiences this problem).
Another problem with the updating system is how its set up. The game thinks you need to have up to the amount of space the update takes EXTRA on your computer before it can start (it installs the new "fix" and then uninstalls the old stuff). This means that if there is a rather large updates (say 3 GB) and your computer is low on space, then you can't even play the game until you make space for the update. My last complaint about the update system is similar in that many times the game will give you a "MISSING FILE PRIVLEDGES" error while updating which forces you to restart before it can update any more.
Conclusion:
ARK is a game that is fun to play and has potential, but is extremely infuriating based on how the developers treat their fan community. Its a game that I wish I could write a positive review for, but due to the doubling of price, poor communication with the fanbase and terrible updating process for the game, I cannot recommend this game right now. If you do decide you really want to get it, AT LEAST wait until it goes on sale.

This game is extremely addictive.
A Medieval FPS set in the fictional land of Agatha, you can choose from four different classes - the ranged Archer, who specializes in ranged support and sneak attacks with his 50% damage bonus to exposed backs; The lithe Man At Arms, who has a variety of quick and speedy one-handed weapons and is the fastest class in the game; the DPS Vanguard, whose giant-sized weapons one hit kill the previous two classes; and the tanky Knight, who has less OP two-handed weapons and a shield the size of Coventry.
The combat is quick, and relies on a combination of speed, luck, and skill - if you manage to dodge a Vanguard's jump attack you have the perfect opportunity to slide your dagger in between his ribs before he can finish the compulsory screaming. Did you know? Pressing C will make your character scream like an eight-year old on fire. Do it.
However, the combat has its flaws, which l33t pro tryhards take advantage of - for some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t reason, looking up while preforming an overhead attack with your target behind you will inexplicably connect without any chance at blocking it. Everyone - and I do mean everyone - has the opinion that they are better at fighting than William Wallace himself. Lots of tears in this game - best to take your "butthurt" bottles along with you!
The gamemodes are similar to the standard gamut of shooters - Deathmatch, Last Team Standing, Team Deathmatch, Free For All, 1v1 duel. However, the best gamemode is Team Objective - where you recreate famous battles and engagements within the fictional setting created by the devs. Have you ever wanted to massacre an entire village of defenseless serfs? This game lets you!
Finally, the mods for this game are hilarious. Thanks to Steam Workshop, the modding community has exploded with such gems as "Giant Slayers" (grow in size per kill, become literally unstoppable!), "Black Knight" (lose limbs and your weapons!), and the infamous "LASERSWORD" (Disney will hurt me if I give an explanation). Once you eventually tire of historically accurate medieval combat, give these exciting gamemodes a spin!
Despite numerous shortcomings in the game, the game remains fun. I give it a hearty 9/10. GG TB nerf zwei

I'll preface this review by saying this: the review section of this game is filled with a lots of very, very stupid ♥♥♥♥ing people.
The game itself is good, it is fun to play once you start to settle in and there is a LOT to get through for max level. You start with spears and bows and work up to guns. The core mechanics work really well, you need to make risks to tame big dinos and you need to be careful when moving around, get careless and a carnovore will be on your tail seeing you as spaghetti. Progression requires activity, you need to be doing something always and it's a nice change from other survival games which have downtime between activities.
The game does have its cons, though. Dying can be unpunishing at times, especially when you die near a large amount of beds you own. At the same time, it can be excessively punishing as predators can spawn right next to the spawn areas leaving you dying 1/4 the times to a Raptor or something similar eating your♥♥♥♥♥before you even finish the waking up animation sequence. PvP can be a mess on vanilla, unchanged servers where you wait for the player to go offline where you then break into their base and steal their things and cheese their dinos. Another problem is taming, it can get really, really stupidly long. Some dinos can take an entire day IRL to tame. The only solution they have is to reduce the tame times for ALL dinos.
Something I'd like to point out as a side flaw of the game- the developers. There is little to no communication between the devs and the players. Is it a problem? Moderately. Is it something to cry over and write negative reviews about? No. They made a great decision and wiped the characters currently existing, letting new players avoid the absolutely cancerous alpha-tribe gankers who would destroy any tribes other than themselves with overwhelming force. The devs, however, have made some horrible choices like implimenting character transfers, allowing alpha-tribes to spread server to server easily.
Overall I give the game 8/10. The devs are bad, yes, but the game is alright. It could use major optimizition improvements as well as some tweaks to character transfers and tribe sizes as alpha-tribes are a problem. While the game has problems, the game is a unique, interesting, and fun game to play with friends. To boot, I've gotten my 1$:1H money-to-time ratio so I'm happy. $60 game for 60 hours of fun, with many more on the horizon.
Tip: Do not start on Scorched Earth, it is a traumatizing experience for new players and should be kept for later once you have gained more experience.

Well, I wanted to see what all the fuss about Warframe was, see why it's so addictive besides the usual FTP daily grind cocaine. Now that I'm 50 hours in and I've finished most of the newbie stuff, leveled up a bit, and asked some questions.... I think I've got the gist.
First, it's farming and grinding exactly as people say. That's basically the whole point of the game. Sure, as you go along you're unlocking new content, characters, and gear, but it's all from and to the grind.
Second, it's all about gear. In a sense, you don't have a character strictly. Your account Level, the Mastery Rank is really just a measurement of how many items you've leveled up to unlock more items, content, etc. So you grind to get MR, MR unlocks more grind, so you can get more MR. Though apparently when you reach MR 8 or 11 you don't have to worry so much about it because you've basically got everything you might want unlocked.
Third, there is no "end-game". I mean, sure, eventually after a few hundred hours I suppose you run out of content to play, but the game doesn't REALLY change as you go along, from the impressions I've gotten by higher level buddies. It's all the same PvE crap just with different color palettes and abilities as you go up.
There is PvP, but I haven't tried it and I only heard bad things about it. The game is almost entirely 4-8 play coop, but you can solo it up forever if you really wanted to I suppose. Talk about lonely autism. This damn thing is tweaking my completionist disorder, so I'm going to try to quit sometime soon..... It's burning a bit too much time with too little actual "fun".

One should not be intimidated by CMW. Nor should one prejudge, despite the fact that CMW is non-vintage and comes in such large containers. Do not be fooled: this is not a AAA game. I always find it important to taste games using high-quality stemware -- this is a game deserving of something better than a Flintstones plastic tumbler. One should pour just a small dollop and swirl it in the glass -- note the coating and look for clots or discoloration. And the color -- it should be opaque, and very, very white. Now, immerse your nose in the glass and take a whiff. CMW transports you instantly to scenic hill towns in central Italy (is that Montepulciano I detect?) --- there is the loamy clay, the green grass of summer days, the towering cypress. And those gentle hints of Italian flowers -- wild orchids, sunflowers, poppies. Then, one takes in the thick liquid and lets it roll across and under the tongue -- what is that? perhaps a hint of a nutty Edam cheese? With CMW, you feel the love of every developer involved -- from the somewhat sad and deranged farmhand shovelling steaming cowpies to the bored union milk maiden dreaming of leaving this soul crushing life behind for a job waiting tables for obnoxious American tourists in Siena. But not too fast -- sip gently, slowly, or one is in danger of not only missing the subtleties of the game's texture and its terroir, but -- if chilled too long -- also of giving oneself a blinding ice cream headache. Nay, savor the goodness that only developers working at the apex of their craft can deliver. CMW is best drunk young -- no, no, don't cellar this gem -- I guarantee you'll be sorry if you do. I recommend pairing with freshly baked macadamia nut scones. I gives this one a 92.

So, first of all, the short TL;DR part is down; also, don't pay attention to the Metracritic score, the game has evolved a lot since its inception.
The game's a third person shooter that isn't based on covers but on your actual skill dodging and jumping around, it has an AWESOME combat system, very unique in its own way, and a lot of RPG elements (weapons strong against X but weak against Y, etc.). The art direction is plain amazing; this game has style, simply put. It has a couple of story mode missions that are actually well put, but the narrative itself is kind of "meh", if you're looking to Metal Gear-Witcher-Bioshock levels of storytelling, this is NOT your game; but, the thing is, I like the atmosphere, setting and lore, which is a distant solar system engaged in a not-so-cold war between a couple of factions.
The game has had a lot of criticism because of the grinding, but if you enjoy the polished combat by itself "grinding" just becomes normal gameplay. In my opinion, usually the people that say that is a grinding fest and that it lacks content are just mmo-obsessed guys that have already poured HUNDREDS OF HOURS and demand more; like, c'mon guys, it gave you HUNDREDS OF HOURS. AN ACTION GAME. A normal AAA fifty bucks game won't give you that insane amount of gaming, except competitive multiplayer games or maybe Bethesda games/Witcher 3/etc.
And, about DLCs and stuff... I spent like 15 bucks on it with a discount of 75% plus extra money, so I got around 50€ worth of ingame currency, and I don't think I will ever need more (in fact, with 5 bucks could have been enough). I agree there shouln't be expensive or RNG stuff ingame, that is an evil move of the gaming companies to keep gambling-addicted people paying, but the important things (forma, orokin cells and reactors, mods,. etc.) are actually very cheap or can be found playing (and you can get ingame currency by trading, a lot of people do it). Just DON'T buy characters (Warframes) or weapons with real money, and you'll be good.
TL;DR: All in all, I'd give it around 8/10, it's an EXTREMELY funny and long coop TPS game to play with a great artistic direction. Play it if you liked Borderlands o The Division, for example. Just don't expect top-notch narrative; just well designed gameplay, like e.g.: Doom 2016.

Warframe, oh gosh, where do I start?
Okay, so this game has some positives. The weapons are pretty neat, and have a good amount of diversity and there are an absolute ton of Warframes, all of them having fairly different play-styles. Also, the multiplayer co-op is pretty good. I rarely experience connection issues. When you start this game you'll have plenty to do, and will probably be in awe at all there is. You'll be able to play this game for a pretty long time before things get boring.
Now on to the bad stuff about this game...
1) The grind is absolutely disgusting. I get that everyone's always talking about the grind and it may seem like an overused complaint, but it isn't. People have plenty reason to be complaining about it. Almost every single thing you do in this game is going to be a grind. Want to get Nova? Gotta fight Raptor over and over and over and over until you finally get all of her parts. But here's where it gets good: it's all RNG. You could very well just get her chassis 3 times in a row. You could get her chassis 10 times in a row. Everything is RNG. It would already be bad enough if you had to fight bosses 3 times to get all the individual blueprints (systems, chassis, and neuroptics), but you also have a chance of getting some part you already have. What's even worse is the Warframes you don't get from bosses tend to also have RNG-based aquirement. It's the same with prime gear. All prime gear is able to be gotten with void relics, but here's the catch... It's (once again) all RNG-based! As if ALL of this isn't bad enough everything else requires grinding. Want to max out your health-boosting mod? Gotta spend a few weeks worth of credits on it. Now if you want to get your mod maxed out faster, don't worry, you can just spend 12 hours a day on Warframe for a week and hopefully you'll have enough credits then, no promises though. Oh, wanna hear a secret? Leveling up your mastery rank is also a grind. To increase your mastery rank you have to level up warframes and weapons, but since there's a maximum level on weapons and Warframes you have to get more weapons and Warframes. Y'know what that means? More grinding. I could keep going on and on, but I think I've made my point.
2) There's a tremendous amount of waiting. After you've spent hours farming the parts necessary for your new weapon you have to wait 12-24 hours for it to finish construction. People can call me impatient all they want, but in general this system is stupid. If I spend lots of time getting lots of stuff I should at least be able to use my new item right away, but nope! I gotta wait. Awesome.
3) Forma. This stuff is evil. The purpose of Forma is to add or change a polarity slot on a W/W (Weapon/Warframe), which means you can store more mods on your W/W, but there's a problem... Adding this thing to your weapon resets it to level 0, which means (you guessed it) MORE GRINDING. On some W/Ws you may even need to add a minimum of 3 or even 4 Forma to fit all the mods you want on to it.
4) W/W capacity. Yup, there's a maximum capacity to how many W/Ws you can have. After all the grinding and waiting for your item you have to do more grinding to get the platimum required to increase your maximum capacity, which means you either have to trade for the platinum or buy it with real money. Trading's great and all, but you may not find anyone looking for your items, so you either gotta go through a long tedious process of negotiating (if people are willing to negotiate at all) or you gotta send the game developers your cash.
5) Lack of map variety. Some planets are completely identical. Like, COMPLETELY identical. The maps are systematically generated, but there's a heavy lack of rooms for the system to generate, so after a few levels you'll realize you've seen the room you're in 10 times already.
6) Pay to accelerate. I won't say this game is pay to win, because it's not. You can get as far as someone who's spent a lot of money on this game without spending a dime on it yourself, but it's gonna take you a dang long time. If I hadn't spent $40-$60 on this game I would be significantly lower level, no doubt about it.
That's all folks! If you want to have some fun and maybe play this game a little bit then go ahead, but if you're considering playing this game really hardcore DON'T. All in all I wouldn't recommend this game to a friend.

Digital Extremes has accomplished a rarity, building a free-to-play massively-multiplayer-online game rich in variety. My primary use for the game is as an excuse to game on-line with my brother who lives 5 hours away. We've enjoyed discovering the various tilesets, mission types, gear loadouts, and quest story-lines.
By avoiding the open-world fetch-quest model and focusing instead on 10-20min combat missions, Warframe presents easily digested chunks of gameplay. Meanwhile, rich layers of customization (see Mods) exist for those who want to improve their in-match performance and unlock new play areas.
Less about where you're going (the story is fairly thin) and more about what you pretend to be (a space ninja turning the tide in a battle for the solar system), Warframe entertains while rewarding each player's evolving skills. Five stars.

Well, I wanted to see what all the fuss about Warframe was, see why it's so addictive besides the usual FTP daily grind cocaine. Now that I'm 50 hours in and I've finished most of the newbie stuff, leveled up a bit, and asked some questions.... I think I've got the gist.
First, it's farming and grinding exactly as people say. That's basically the whole point of the game. Sure, as you go along you're unlocking new content, characters, and gear, but it's all from and to the grind.
Second, it's all about gear. In a sense, you don't have a character strictly. Your account Level, the Mastery Rank is really just a measurement of how many items you've leveled up to unlock more items, content, etc. So you grind to get MR, MR unlocks more grind, so you can get more MR. Though apparently when you reach MR 8 or 11 you don't have to worry so much about it because you've basically got everything you might want unlocked.
Third, there is no "end-game". I mean, sure, eventually after a few hundred hours I suppose you run out of content to play, but the game doesn't REALLY change as you go along, from the impressions I've gotten by higher level buddies. It's all the same PvE crap just with different color palettes and abilities as you go up.
There is PvP, but I haven't tried it and I only heard bad things about it. The game is almost entirely 4-8 play coop, but you can solo it up forever if you really wanted to I suppose. Talk about lonely autism. This damn thing is tweaking my completionist disorder, so I'm going to try to quit sometime soon..... It's burning a bit too much time with too little actual "fun".

Ok so here is what I think about this game after many hours put into it.

Obviously for me the pros are outweighing the cons but I will say abit about both. And bare in mind that the game offers so much that I still havent experienced it all so I am speaking based on my experience only.

Now that that is out of the way, I will start with the pros. For me, the best thing about this game is its versatility, it has SOO many diffrent things to do, game mechanics and content in general. Wether it be, collecting and trying all the weapons, frames, sentinels, etc. and making them look amazing in your own way(since looks are quite customisable in warframe) or making an awesome clan with a majestic dojo or maybe going questing or unlocking all the planets and all the missions, or maybe you want to grind the hell out of the fissure missions and make a killing in trade chat (some people practicaly live for that), what would you trade for you ask? Well this brings us to the second thing I absolutely adore about this game, its that you can get ALMOST EVERYTHING in the game, because you can trade with other people for the currency that is bought with money, yes thats right you can get it just by playing the game and trading! And if that is not enough there is the other thing that makes you game experience unique from that of all other players(except if you like copying others` builds), its the mods. Mods are a BIG part of this game as they pretty much make up how strong you or your weapons or anything you can mod will be. And I put them separately because they are the core of the game and I want to stress that you can make alot of diffrent choices as to how you want something to function(example: slow nova/speed nova|you will understand what i mean if you play the game). The last thing I want to mention is certainly not the least important and its that the community of the game is LEAGUES above alot of communities out there in terms of being friendly and helpful to each other.
Now about the cons, I myself don`t find alot of bad things about the game. One thing for me is that it tends to get quite grindy in moments, but I think that is inevitable in this kind of games. Also there is the fact that the players that have been playing the game longest start quitting because there isnt much to do after you reach the "End game"(which by the way is very hard to reach, atleast for me). And thats about all I can think of, nothing really major...
All in all, this is one of the best FREE TO PLAY games out there, with one of the best communities and awesome versatile content. So if you actually really read all my gibberish and stuck to the end.. The universe needs you Tenno, so get out there and kick some a$$. :)

Clicker Heroes is, in my eyes, the pinnacle of the idle/clicking/incremential genre.
This is not a genre for everyone, it's for those of us who have compulsive loot-chasing instincts.  The goal is pretty much the satisfaction of faster and faster progress, and bigger and bigger numbers.   The game starts off incredibly slow, you click hundreds of times, and if you only play for half an ahour, that's what you'll think it is.
You click and click, and then you get enough money to buy your first hero, Treebeast.   When you hire treebeast, the enemies will start taking continious damage over time, and the higher you level your heroes, the more damage they do.
Eventually, you make your way up to Amenhotep, and you can buy his "Ascension" skill.  What this does, is it takes away all your hero levels, and plops you right back at level one.  WAIT, COME BACK
When you get to the higher levels, you start aquiring 'Hero Souls', and for every hero soul you hold on to, all damage by you and heroes is increased by ten percent, so you'll start progessing faster, further, and deeper.
Once you get enough, you can start spending those hero souls on 'Ancients', which are extremely beneficial passive effects, and the game will shift to leveling up the Ancients, and less about the heroes.
The developer has been shooting updates and patches practically bi-weekly, and they've added incredible content.
*Relics (Loot that drops once per ascension that grants additional passive benefits)
*Clans (up to 10 players, a message board, and daily 'Raids', which are incredibly tough bosses that last 24 hours, and will give everyone who participates in killing them hero souls based on their participation and damage done)
*Holiday events
*Followers (Think WoW's garrison quests)
There will be those who are turned off just because it's a free to play game, but there is literally no pay to win, everything you can buy is stuff that you get in game extremely easily.  The developers also clearly love this game, they can't stop adding stuff to it.
This is an incredibly insidious game, and it's very, very addictive if you have the patience to learn it.  When I'm not playing it on Steam, I am also playing it on my phone.
I highly recommend this to all fans of loot based games such as Diablo, WoW, etc, as it will really, REALLY scratch that gear grind itch.

So, first of all, the short TL;DR part is down; also, don't pay attention to the Metracritic score, the game has evolved a lot since its inception.
The game's a third person shooter that isn't based on covers but on your actual skill dodging and jumping around, it has an AWESOME combat system, very unique in its own way, and a lot of RPG elements (weapons strong against X but weak against Y, etc.). The art direction is plain amazing; this game has style, simply put. It has a couple of story mode missions that are actually well put, but the narrative itself is kind of "meh", if you're looking to Metal Gear-Witcher-Bioshock levels of storytelling, this is NOT your game; but, the thing is, I like the atmosphere, setting and lore, which is a distant solar system engaged in a not-so-cold war between a couple of factions.
The game has had a lot of criticism because of the grinding, but if you enjoy the polished combat by itself "grinding" just becomes normal gameplay. In my opinion, usually the people that say that is a grinding fest and that it lacks content are just mmo-obsessed guys that have already poured HUNDREDS OF HOURS and demand more; like, c'mon guys, it gave you HUNDREDS OF HOURS. AN ACTION GAME. A normal AAA fifty bucks game won't give you that insane amount of gaming, except competitive multiplayer games or maybe Bethesda games/Witcher 3/etc.
And, about DLCs and stuff... I spent like 15 bucks on it with a discount of 75% plus extra money, so I got around 50€ worth of ingame currency, and I don't think I will ever need more (in fact, with 5 bucks could have been enough). I agree there shouln't be expensive or RNG stuff ingame, that is an evil move of the gaming companies to keep gambling-addicted people paying, but the important things (forma, orokin cells and reactors, mods,. etc.) are actually very cheap or can be found playing (and you can get ingame currency by trading, a lot of people do it). Just DON'T buy characters (Warframes) or weapons with real money, and you'll be good.
TL;DR: All in all, I'd give it around 8/10, it's an EXTREMELY funny and long coop TPS game to play with a great artistic direction. Play it if you liked Borderlands o The Division, for example. Just don't expect top-notch narrative; just well designed gameplay, like e.g.: Doom 2016.
