I've had this running for over 1200 hours in the background as I did other things. I've been playing it for roughly half a year. And it's free.
Those facts make it pretty obvious that I like this game, but I'll list some reasons. Once again, it's completely free. You can buy rubies, which let you do various useful things, but those are basically just for speeding up the game. The only reason to buy those, other than being impatient, is to support the devs. They give you plenty of them as-is, which is great. It's one of the better free-to-play models I've seen from a consumer standpoint.
The game balances idle play and active play quite nicely. If you want to let it sit in the background and just pop in now and then to buy upgrades, the game will let you do that, no problem. It even has upgrades in the form of Ancients (more on that later) that let you make idle play more efficient. But if you're the sort who just can't sit there and watch the game go by, or if you get impatient when your progress hits a wall, active play is also good, and is more effective in the long run. Once you buy Juggernaut, an Ancient who creates click combos that boost your DPS, it can addicting to watch the numbers climb higher and higher with each click.
Like most clickers, this game has a "soft reset" system to keep things from getting stale. In exchange for resetting your world, you get Hero Souls, which can either be stockpiled for a boost to DPS, or they can be spent on Ancients, statue-like things that provide various boosts to make future runs more efficient and help you go to higher and higher levels. There are enough Ancients, with enough different useful boosts, that it takes a long time for this mechanic to become boring. Some are geared toward active play, some are geared toward idle play, and some are useful in both, so this still encourages the full spectrum of play styles.
There are other mechanics--Relics, Clans, and the newly-introduced Mercenaries--but I don't have much to say about those. Those are more for poking at now and then, rather than actively fretting over. They make the game slightly more like a Facebook game, but they're not integral enough for me to really mind it. (Clans introduce a social element where teams of players take down a monster each day for a certain number of Souls, and Mercenaries are sent out on "missions" for various loot, which can be sped up via Rubies. They also die, and can be revived with, you guessed it, Rubies.)
Overall, this game suffers from most of the problems typically seen in free-to-play clicker games, but to a lesser extent than most of them. It's free, and spending money is in no way required to advance, which is nice. Basically, if you like the clicker genre, and you got over Cookie Clicker long ago, this is one of your best options.

Graphics are excellent (make sure that your machine can handle them).The game has benefited well from updating: animations now are smoother than ever before, and the customization feature allows players to change helmets (and also to raise their visors or remove them altogether), logos (on shields an armor), and the colors of clothing and shields. Expect more top-notch content as fans in the Steam community submit new maps and modifications. With battle experience ranging from massed infantry confrontations to careful skirmishing and even one-on-one duels, the game delivers thrills on every front. Each fight is a confrontation of different play styles and loadouts, each with advantages and disadvantages. Team play is just that: don't expect success taking on the enemy team by yourself. In all, Chivalry has a lot to offer the casual player and even more for those who like to put time into mastering the game. A must-buy for anyone interested in the Medieval ages or archaic combat in general. Did I mention the voice acting? "You rapscallion, I'll tickle your catastrophe!"

As someone who is very asocial and not a team player, I can honestly say this game kinda' broke me out of that shell. I'm not one for online games that requires social interaction, but this game becomes so addicting that it makes you wanna work with others to get sh*t done. Though you don't necessarily have to play with other people if you don't want to, but it's a lot faster trying to get things accomplished. The game is very grindy, RNG heavy, and requires a shtload of investment if you wanna make any real progress. So if you have a life then avoid this game lol. You are a Warframe, aka "Tenno" (think of a space ninja lol). There are enemy factions at war with each other. Your job is to fight them. You can do spy missions, defense missions (defend cryostasis pod), exterminate missions (kill all enemies), etc. At the end of these missions you get rewards like blueprints to make weapons and new warframes, component parts, credits (in-game currency), mods (which you can equip on your weapons and warframes.... mods like Melee damage +90%, etc). You can customize the colors of your weapons and warframes, customize the interior of your spaceship, you can have a sentinel or pet to assist you in battle, just all kinds of cool stuff here and there. Then there's this other currency called Platinum, which you have to buy with real money, or another way to get Platinum is to farm for prime parts to sell to other players. You need this if you run out of space to use weapons and warframes, or if you want to buy accessories for your appearance, speed up the building process of weapons, warframes, etc.
Personally what I think is a pain in the az, are the wait times you have to endure when building sh*t. OH WHAT'S THAT? You FINALLY got all the parts to build the warframe or weapon you've been wanting? It'll only take 3 f*ckin' days to build it :D Don't like waiting that long? Spend some plat to speed it up! How do I describe Chivalry? Well it's sorta a First Person Melee game. I can honestly say that this is the first and only game I've played that can make that sort of claim. It's a blast to play either alone or with friends. In the stock game without the Deadliest Warrior DLC, you choose between being an Archer, Vanguard, Man-at-Arms, or a Knight. Each one has their own strengths and weaknesses.
The archer has decent speed, but low health. However, they have weapons that allow them to attack from range.
Vanguards have medium speed, higher health than the Man-At-Arms and Archer, but lower health than the knights. They're equipped with excellent melee weapons, and can do a sprinting charge attack. This comes at the cost of not having any real ranged attacks, and not having a shield.
Man-At-Arms class has the fastest speed, as well as the ability to quickly leap out of danger. They're equpped with shorter range weapons than the Vanguards, and they also have less health. They also can carry fire pots, which you can use to set your enemy on fire, as you listen to them scream for mercy. A good Man-At-Arms can be very annoying to beat.
The Knight is slow, has high health, and can carry a shield. There's not much to say about him, really; he's a tank. He's very vulnerable to the fire pots that I just mentioned, however.
I've gotten more enjoyment out of this $25 game than I have out of any of the Call of Duty games past MW2; and those games cost $60 at launch. Do yourself a favor and buy this game.

While the trailers are actually much more entertaining than the game itself, you'll find hundreds of hours worth of interest in a game like this.  It's another addiction like Minecraft that will have you coming up with cool ideas to attempt provided you have the friends required to not have it be a slog.  Singleplayer it's relatively uninteresting.  You definitely want people to play with because you'll easily dominate dinosaurs after a while and be left with nothing but a castle building simulator.
Some people will complain about FPS, and while it was a problem for me as well, it's merely an issue of a person's personal perception of what "high-end gaming machine" actually means.  People with cards three or four years old think they have high end machines just because they can run some other game that looks cool and released in 2007.  ARK is unoptimized some would say but actually it's optimized for higher end devices.  If you have a cutting edge PC worth thousands of dollars, you're probably going to be alright.  Just remember technology becomes obsolete every six months and you either keep upgrading or begin to fall behind.
ARK is demanding.  Of specs, of time, of patience, of social skills, of server bandwidth.  If you have what it takes, you'll be rewarded with hours upon hours of enjoyment that puts to shame that 8-hr singleplayer thriller you devoured in a single night for the same price.

I need to first warn anyone that wants to try and run this game on a budget build: It's entirely possible, I come from that experience myself. I managed to get it running on a gtx 670 and an older i5 with mixed results at first, but persevered nonetheless. I really did start to enjoy the game a whole lot more when I got the build I'm currently using (GTX 970 and an i7-5820k ).
Ark is a very time consuming Spacey-Dinosaur jamboree, complete with technology ranging from the basic sharpened stick to high powered rifles and more. If you enjoy farming and building with a side of making friends with dinosaurs, then this game is for you.

Breakdown of Pro's and cons:
PROS:
-Beautiful game, makes use of the Unreal 4 engine
-Lots to do, especially with the addition of ascension
-Ragnarok: A free DLC that includes assets from a paid DLC as well as a gorgeous yet daunting map to play on.
-Otters. Need I say more?

CONS:
-Setting up a dedicated server can be a bit of a hassle
-It's extremely taxing on hardware to budget machines

FINAL NOTE:
I've been with this game off and on during it's development cycle. I started following its development during closed alpha and beta days and picked it up as soon as I had the money to do so while it was just entering Early Access. My friends kept me up to date with its development while I was unable to play, and I got to experience the evolution of ARK as it marched through Early Access. And while it's releasing a year behind the first time they announced a full release, I am more than pleased to see it finally hit the store without the Early Access tag. Other people can vote with their thumbs and their wallets as I vote with mine - ARK gave me some of my fondest memories in gaming, and I hope it does to anyone else that decides to play it.

(This is specifically about the Deadliest Warrior DLC.)
Pirate vs. Ninja? Knight vs. Viking? Spartan vs. Samurai? Astronaut vs. Caveman? You'd be hard-pressed to find someone that hadn't at one point engaged in the pointless discussion of "Who would win?" out of two seemingly equivalent groups. It's a fun and addicting conversation, but it ultimately leads to nothing except frustration. That is a feeling that Torn Banners managed to accomplish with the "Deadliest Warrior" DLC for its "Chivalry: Medieval Warfare" game. While may not quite quite have cavemen and astronauts yet (though points to you if you got the reference), the other factions do make a grand appearance.
If you're unfamiliar with "Chivalry: Medieval Warfare," which is the base game for this DLC, it is essentially a "Counterstrike"-esque death match game between two opposing medieval forces. The game varies from straight team deathmatches to more complicated game modes involving objectives (essentially various capture/defend scenarios). While that seems rather standard, what sets "Chivalry" apart from other games in the genre is how beautiful the game looks all the while maintaining an air of silliness.
The "Deadliest Warrior" DLC acts as a separate game from the title "Chivalry" (though the base game is still required to play) and introduces six factions: knights, vikings, Spartans, samurai, ninjas, and pirates. You start out in each faction using the most basic equipment, but as you practice and rack up experience, you have the ability to unlock the faction's more advanced weapons. You are also able to unlock different accessories, but these just provide a custom appearance and does not award the player with special bonuses.
"Deadliest Warrior" differs from "Chivalry" in that it does not have special story maps/missions. Each game is a deathmatch with a wide variety of scenarios; sometimes its a free-for-all while other times it is a team deathmatch. Sometimes it divides the players into faction vs factions matches, limiting choice but providing a more stable sense of balance.
Each game itself is very frantic and exciting. People (especially those new to the game) sprint towards their opponents, spamming the war-cry button ("C" if you're interested), and then it's mostly a LMB fest. Sure, sometimes people use their ranged weapons or use the other attacks besides whatever their primary attack is, but what you'll see 80 percent of the time is people spinning around enemies hitting the LMB and then complaining that that is all anyone ever does. You can't argue with results, though. The game does a great job of making combat very satisfying. You can stop off heads and limbs. Arrows and spears stick into people's bodies. Finishing blows can leave deep gashes that expose bone, muscle, and blood.

The different levels of the game each have their own stylized beauty to them - not nearly to the level that the base "Chivalry" game has, but they come close. The Spartan level, for instance, has an impossibly deep well (ala the movie "300"), into which you can kick foes that aren't paying attention to their environment. The pirate level has cannons that you can hit and fire. The Japan level has spike traps placed at certain key points. Just about every map has something special to it to make the game just a little more diverse and frenetic.
Each faction has different strengths and weaknesses that provide an extra level of strategy to the typical LMB fest that makes up most combat. The knights, for instance, are slow but heavily armored, allowing them to take a lot of punishment before going down. Pirates have access to guns and can drink rum to restore their health (at the cost of getting drunk). Ninjas are fast and run silently, giving them the opportunity to sneak up on people. Samurai and Spartans are both armored, have access to ranged weapons (bows and spears, respectively), and maintain a decent movement speed.
Vikings are my favorite class in the game. While when dual wielding, they can get into a combo in which their attack speed becomes faster and faster until they either run out of targets or exhaust themselves. That is not my favorite part, however. My favorite bit is the viking's ability to throw ALL of their gear. Swords, hammers, axes and even their shield can suddenly become a ranged weapon until the viking is left with nothing but their fists to attack their opponents. One of my favorite memories of the game is when I was charging three samurai on a staircase. They were shooting arrows at me, and I was dodging while I advanced. One steped forward to meet me, drawing his katana. I responded by throwing my shield Captain America-style right at his face, which made his head explode. I celebrated by spamming the war-cry button (as you do) and then being sliced to death by the remaining samurai that expertly outmaneuvered me. I died, but seeing that first swordsman's head erupt into goo was just too fantastic.
"Deadliest Warrior" is filled with those types of experiences that keep you coming back to the game despite the little bugs and often frustrating matchups. As a pirate, I've thrown a bottle of burning grog and lit a group of ninjas on fire. As a Spartan, I've "THIS IS SPARTA" kicked a dumb knight into the well on the Greek level. As a knight, I've swung my mace and exploded two viking skulls. The game is still fairly new and has its share of issues, but it also has tremendous potential to grow into something as polished as the base "Chivalry" game. And if it continues to follow the footsteps of the "Deadliest Warrior" TV show, then there is definitely a chance that we'll see more factions added to the game (Shaolin monks? Maori? Zulu warriors?), which will only add to the insane experience that make the game so memorable.
Currently, "Deadliest Warrior" is available on Steam, but in my opinion as a fan of the game, it is also a little too pricey for what the game is right now. I recommend keeping an eye on the game and waiting for a sale to snag it. It doesn't look like much, but I was definitely surprised at how addicted I became to it. It has a long way to go before looking as polished as the base game of Chivalry looks, but even as it is now, the game is a great deal of silly fun and if you like unlikely matchups, you should definitely give 'Deadliest Warrior' a chance.

I've been playing Ark for a decent time, I've been playing for 300 hours and none are fake hours.  You don't need any more than that to make a desicion about the game. The graphics are absolutely splendid, but if you want to play it on your Mac, forget about it.  In Ark, you can play on your Singleplayer server (you can make it a non-dedicated multiplayer server whenever you want), you can play on an Official server (I only reccomend this if you are willing to put in lots of hours into Ark because it's extremely hard to get by on Official servers), and Unofficial servers (a lot of people prefer this mode because you can chose a server with easier settings and less people will try to raid your base).  I play in Official Servers but it took me SO much hard work just to get into the stage where your base doesn't get raided every night.  You can also play in PVE (player versus environment) mode, but I think that it's boring because there is no risk or challengenge in it.
Ark is a game with tons of possibilities.  Just so you get the idea I will tell you some of the things that have happened to me in Ark.
Bad things
1. Finally built my first base in Ark! I spent hours on it.  It was thatch and it was huge.  I was adding the finishing touches when a man with a griffin knocked me out and put me in a cage.  He then made me watch as he smashed my poor base to the ground.  He didn't take me out of the cage and I starved to death.
2. I got my first "friend" in Ark and we made a tribe together.  The next day he killed me, left my tribe and stole all my stuff while I was logged off.
3.  I did not know about auto-decay and when I went on a vacation, my 5 bases and all my dinos were auto-decay destroyed.
4.  I finallly got a fertilized wyvern egg and I was flying the heck out of there on my Pteranodon when the game crashed and me and my ptera died.
5.  I was travelling across the valley, looking for a nice spot to relocate with my friend and 7 horses when 3 wyverns swooped down from out of nowhere, killed us, and stole everything we had.
6.  I raided my first base! I spent a VERY long time hacking down a reinforced stone door with a metal sickle.  The base was empty except for a bed (which I destroyed) but it was worth it!
7. Me and 3 of my friends were sailing around the island with a raft containing all the stuff for a new base when someone with a Pteranodon dropped another guy who had a C4 attached to him and he exploded our beautiful boat.
8.  I was flying over a beautiful canyon when I was sniped off my Argentavis.
9.  I tamed my first Brontosaurus on Official servers! I was so proud of myself and I stampeded around with my giant tank machine and I killed EVERYTHING in sight.  He was able to get me to raid lots of bases and I had lots of fun.  A guy with a rocket launcher shot us to the ground after a few hours of wrecking havoc, but I had lots of fun and I would do it again (if I were at that level)
10.  Someone left the door of their big metal base open.  All I can say is, I made them regret that.
Lots more cool things happened to me on Ark and I really had fun.  Thumbs up, it's worth it.

The game is fun yet much harder as single player. I recommend multi-player PvE on a private server with friends.

The worst of these being weapon kills not counting, making it impossible to get new weapons, the kills will count occasionaly it will just take longer to level up.

However if your not with a good group of players you will get the occasional (censored) on your team, who thinks it is funny to sneak up behind you while your fighting and stab you. Fortunately there is a nice ban system to get rid of these trolls.
Overalll this game is well worth the 8.50$ i spent on it after using a coupon. I would really like to see a healer or mage class though this probably wont be implemented, seeing as this game is medeival, not fantasy medeival.

The vanity system is also a nice feature to help stand out on the battlefield, and its free...currently.

However the amount of time you have to commit to this game is ridiculous and will quickly ruin the fun of the game for most people. If you plan on playing in a public server then you should be prepared to play for a bare minimum of 10 minutes every day (this si assuming you are playing on a pve server and have a rather small amount of creatures to look after). If you decide to play on a pvp server you will have to check frequently every day to ensure all of your stuff is still there. And yes this is usually standard for these types of games. But in this game everything you attain is much harder to get back. Most dinosaurs take hours to tame. You have to micro manage them the entire time to ensure they aren't killed, wake up, or run out of food all of which will reset your progress. The game simply makes everything take much longer then it should. This would all be fine if the tasks that took long periods of time didnt become so repetitive so quickly. DON'T let the negative reviews and rants throw you off your possible purchase. Seriously. Take a step back and take a constructive view on things. I'd concider myself a "relative" casual player. I rented a private server to play with a handfull of friends and we choose the server settings we felt enjoyable and acceptable as a small group. We have had alot of fun since. No drama. No major time sinks. Just fun. How a game should be.
My recommendation is simply NOT to play on official servers. Unless you really have no life and sadomasochistic pixel pushing, alpha tribes raiding you, PVP grief and and an elitism player base is really your thing. On official, dino taming and breeding takes far too long and can go very wrong at any minute. Costing you alot of time and effort. Bringing in disapointment, saltyness, then complaints and negative reviews.
Single play is fun to mess around with god mode and spawning stuff in etc... but without any quest system or anything equivalent to keep you going in the long run, it get's very boring alone. ARK is meant to be played with freinds. Personaly I'd say with a minimum of 3 people. 4 or 5 preferably. With some decent server settings and a few QoL mods, you will be busy enough taming, building and breeding away until you have good enough dinos to face the boss arenas on a casual difficulty.
Start on the basic map "The Island" to get you acquainted with the basics of ARK. Without rushing it, you should be very well geared and have some solid dinos within a month or two. Then either move along to another free map, like "The Center" or even "Ragnarok". Good thing about renting your private server is, on Ragnarok you will have access to all the "Scorched Earth" items without owning the expansion. This does not go for official servers though.
I think it's safe to say that, if you enjoy the game at a good pace, play all the maps, you should be able to get at least a year of playtime out of ARK. Of course it depends alot if all of your friends will stil be around to join you, but thats just my estimate. And with the game out of Early Acess now, we can expenct more DLC's, gear, dinos, maps and such to keep us busy in the long run.

A lot of variation in terms of frames and weaponry although when it comes to end game missions and events, it does narrow to a select few of the aforementioned. There is a handful of quests, a few pertaining to the game's lore and centers around the "Operator" and other quests revolving around frames in the game's universe which you can get the blueprints for as reward for completion.
Only real issue of contention is the RNG of which you can either be blessed or cursed and believe me if you are the latter then prepare to grind yourself silly. I'm not particularly opposed to RNG, you work to get the space cabbages (relics) and you refine them and venture to fissures to hopefully get the part or blueprint you need but doing the same thing ad infinitum can be a pain in the backside.
Unfortunately I've gotten to the point where the game has gotten a little dull but considering I've almost got every frame and I've sunk a substantial amount of time into this game I'm not surprised and I certainly not going to hold it against Warframe.
Should you buy it? Yes absolutely, for a F2P game you've got not much to lose.

Been a part of this journey since near the beginning of it. I wouldn't say ignore the people who say that they're penny pinching, or money driven. Though, those are defensible positions, I feel they are ones driven by frustration in the fact that they didn't get a finished product so near to the moment of conception. Very rarely do things exist in it's apex of opperation from the get go. So, keeping in mind that in buying this product (before it's official release today (super happy for the developers, by the way)), you purchased a work in progress that you pledged patience to, this game is very much worth "it". As you can see, I have dedicated some time to this game and refrained from submitting a review until release, for I felt it was unfair to review a product that was unfinished. My review should carry some weight with your decision to purchase, though, be aware, my unwaivering biasees do exist in it, do to the fact that I have been enamoured with the concept of this game since it's blip appreared on my radar.
We have seen many dinosaur survivals pop in and out of existence (or maybe just concern) many times in the past, but this is one of the few that released fully and, in my humble opinion, is worth it. The modding community is highly active, giving you many hours of dynamic game play and challenge to keep you interested. That is, not to say that base game isn't fun and challenging on it's own; need I remind you that you exist in a world where ♥♥♥♥ING DINOSAURS all band together to make your life, in it's entirety, a living hell.
All in all, the abition behind this product is immense. If you like rewarding, stunningly beautiful and immersive, challenging, ambitious, massive, and thoughtful open world survival sand box games, this this game gets a 10/10 from me. God damn, i've been wating a long while to review this game and I have to say, it feels good that we made it here. Thank you, Studio Wildcard, for giving me the best gaming experience I have ever had.

I've played this for around 400 Hours and i'm gonna clarify this now, I do not like the original game, I do not play regular servers, I play modded servers with Upped rates and Lots of overhaul mods, The reason for this is that i enjoy A more "wacky" experience when playing this. The regular game is still lots of fun but is harder and takes a long time, and i don't have too much time on my hands to do that..
My experience with ARK (modded) has been amazing, most points where i havent could most likely be due to bugs with the mods or the main game, none the less you will always get them, Communities are usually really nice, friendly and usually welcoming to newcomers.
I had very basic knowledge of ark at the time, But mostly got a hang of it, whether that was googling things, asking the communities on servers, or just through the rather basic tooltips.
The mods I've used mainly are; Extinction core, Annunaki and ARK Eternal, All 3 have been a blast and i've always gone back to them after playing them, depending on the other mods can make it easy or hard, you can also just play at your own way to make it easier or harder either way.
The Pros: A really enjoyable Co-op experience on servers, Active modders, Lots of servers with friendly communities, PVE and PVP for the prefered playstyles, A good steady increase from early game to late game, Plenty of dinos to capture, A big map to build Different bases and get immersed in.
The cons: A recent increase of price to £50 , Bugs, Not very starter helpful, mostly reliant on youtube or google when starting, sometimes starting out generally is a pain, There are some performance issues for Mid-end pcs.
The performance issues shouldnt be much of an issue for someone with an good processor and okay graphics card, Me personally can run it on 100 fps with:
GTX 1070
Ryzen 5 1600
MSI B350 Tomahawk
8 GB DDR4 RAM
I think thats all thats neccessary...
TL;DR:
Modded is reccomended from me, but play at your own pace, play and expect performance issues, excellent with friends, very difficult for starters but you will get the hang of it...

I'd recommend this game, As long as you like enjoy doing things. First of all, I want to say that this game will look like repetitive grinding, if you havent understand it's core. Because from my 300 hrs, I realized that this game mimics the style of "trying every stuff until you found the one that you really love". Sure, trying to farm 300 weapons just for 300.000 exp are not enjoyable to some, But don't think about it like that, because you will get burned very fast.
Think about this game as a playground. And sure, Everybody knows a MK1 vs Prime even on it's base stats are different. But it's kind of a reward of your hard work, grinding to get relics, then grind the parts, then grind the material, then wait countless hours, and all of it before you know how it will works. Forget youtube. Try it for yourself, and you can see that there's still a lot of things to do.
Doesn't meant you can ask for help. This game's community playerbase is Amazing, yeah sometimes toxic, but you can't really avoid that, like in most games in the world. But this game was actually designed to "make yourselft at home" style, And you know what ? you can actually make your own home in the game.
The Devs, are supportive either, watch the game when it's released, and watch it now. The difference, I could say, is a BIG one. The mechanics, the system it self were changed, adjusted towards the playerbase. Archwings are bad. For me ? It's just a refreshing playground. Tired of pressing 1-2-3-4 to win ? Play the Archwing Rush mode. It's too easy ? Sometimes. but you can get to Lv 9999 solo if you want to, no one's stopping you.
For a F2P ? It's amazing. You can trade for basically everything. Except Anniversary Items and Prime Accesories Bundles. Even cosmetics in game, you can buy with your free plat. But I'd recommend to spent at least a few dollars into this game, just for a little thank you to the devs.
This is even more enjoyable with friends. Doesn't meant by your friends doing all the hard work, but doing as what I stated above, with friends. Still bored ? Poking fun at the bot, also works. But don't do it too much, or you will lose your account pretty fast. Still bored again ? Play Conclave. Try to win those oro and place it on your Orbiter.

Though probably you'd get sick of hearing the same praise over and over again for 5 million times throughout the course of the game, but it's still enjoyable. Or having a zombie dog that has the enemy head tilted upside down just cause it's a placeholder, Cool. Loved to get attacked by the unknown ? It happens often. But all I gotta say, is that this game's story is shine it's masterpiece when it's on the start of "Natah" quest. The first few quest is a common drift, but it's unique feelings starts when you play Natah.
It's a totally mixed review, but if you had gone through almost everything solo like I did, Like losing those potato because I can't finish the mission solo... you'd pretty much get what I meant.
PS: But yeah, like most games out there, there is always something that overpowered af.

Destiny x Diablo, but free and with more content.
Pros:
*Constant updates and additions to the game
*Excellent and helpful community
*Good variety of mission types
*Ridiculous catalogue of weapons and classes
*Multiplayer recommended, but not required
*Runs well on lower end computers if you optimize for it, and looks great on higher end PCs
*Parkour system is incredible
*Gorgeous level, sound, and art design
*"Paid" currency can be traded with in game items
*Responsive and active dev team
*Good variety of play style due to large range of weapons/classes
Cons:
*HEAVY grind.  There is a lot of farming and waiting to get what you want
*Very high entry learning curve.  There's a lot to figure out at first, especially alone
*PvP is unpolished and fairly underpopulated
*Some parts of the game do become repetitive
*Archwing is not a favorite of many.  Improvements coming soon™, but it's worth noting
Real talk though, I think Warframe is F2P done right.  Everything can be farmed in game, and you can even trade in game items for the "paid" currency.  You can spend money to speed up the process if you want, but there's no hard need to.  Nothing is "Pay to win," only "Pay to rush" or "Pay to look pretty."  The devs are also fantastic people, very personable and responsive to the community.
There is a fairly high entry learning curve, and it may take a few weeks of learning to get a decent grasp of it, but I recommend reaching out to the community and other players.  Warframe has a fantastic community, and that's one of the things that keeps me coming back to it.  That, and the constant updates and additions of weapons and frames.
There is a lot of grinding and farming.  A lot.  Like a lot a lot.  If that's your deal though, it can be a ton of fun.  I'd recommend checking it out at the very least.
After all, it's free.

TL;DR: A great idea and initial development quickly turned into a cash-grab. Not worth the price. Un-optimized game.
They lost a $40 million lawsuit, which probably was the main reason for switching to a "cash-grab" development style. After the loss, they stopped fixing and optimizing the game to perform reasonably, and instead they released a DLC (more money for them) while still in Early Access. Their next move was releasing more content and ultimately pushing the "Full Release" of the game, which (who knew) raised the price per copy up to $59.99.
In the end, you have (in my opinion) an overpriced, un-optimized game, with the majority of the focus from the developer on money rather than the player. I think most people would agree that the game performs less-than-optimal on most modern PC setups. And to further prove my point about their focus on money, they are already selling a "Season Pass", which (as of now) only gets you the expansion "Scorched Earth" and promises 2 additional expansions that haven't been created yet.
Boooooring !!!

Warframe: A game where you grind so you can grind some more. I will warn you of that right now! If you hate those types of games best get off the boat now!
It's repetitive, it can be tedious and as I just said it's a hell of a grind to acquire the stuff you want. There now that we got that out of the way lets move on, this is a positive review after all. So what makes it good?
The combat is ohhhhh so satisfying! Everything is so fluid and well animated and executed. The game is challenging, there is no mercy for the unprepared. The game looks amazing with beautiful graphics and it runs like a dream, even on a potato machine. The lore and story is interesting enough to keep you interested and there is an abundance of side quests to do. The upgrade system is well done, you feel yourself getting stronger which is always good. The mods you equip to your weapons and Warframe are varied so you can build up your character in a number of different ways that feels unique.
Plus the game is free... And you don't need to spend a penny to get everything in the game, this goes back to the whole grinding thing, but paid currency is avaliable for those who want fast access to what they want. The Devs are very active and updates are regular and meaty.
Give the game a try you have nothing to lose, except maybe hours and hours of your life if it tickles your taste buds!

Warframe is a pretty neat game. I mean, it combines two of the best fiction genres (ninjas and sci fi) in a game with amazing graphics, incredible detail, and fairly straightforward concepts. It does, however, have major flaws that make it in my opinion unplayable. They are as follows:
First: The combat system, while easy to use, is terrible. You literally have to shove yourself in the enemy's face in order to use most melee weapons, and shooting is also nigh-impossible at long range. Why? Because the guns are inaccurate, which is especially annoying since in a third person shooter you miss more shots than you do in a first-person game, and the weapons do piddly amounts of damage on top of all that. Imagine playing a convential mmorpg like SWTOR or WOW. Remember how long it takes to kill enemies in those games? Compare that to, say, an fps like Halo or BF4 or a good 3ps like Battlefront. Huge difference in how long it takes to kill even the simplest of enemies. Well, in Warframe all of your weapons except for the melee weapons do so little damage that it is like playing one of the aforementioned shooters, but it takes as long to kill one enemy as it does in one of the aforementioned mmorpgs. I.E., imagine if SWTOR was more like a shooter, but without the stat changes. Also, the characters tend to move REALLY QUICKLY, which means that it is extra-difficult to aim or even melee.
Second: Warframe designers would probably argue that, as a ninja, one should be stealthy instead of getting into full on combat. However, the stealth system is even worse than combat. First of all, it is impossible to get somewhere without at least one enemy noticing you - not only do you move really quickly, meaning you often move past the cover you were using to hide or alternatively overcompensate and don't move far enough, but for some reason enemies can see things in their periferal vision really easily and they can sometimes see through corners and spot you. Killing these guys, even with a supposedly stealthy weapon such as a bow, oftentimes leads to the alarm being tripped anyway. Either someone sees you kill that enemy or they hear a supposedly silent weapon. Similarly, there is no way to outmanuever your foes. There is simply too little cover, and the enemies rarely move anywhere except in groups - which again prevents stealth kills. Finally, in most stealth games there is some kind of gimmick you can use to distract enemies or confuse them. Unless you have a particular suit (called Warframes, which is where the name of the game comes from) you don't have anything like these abilities. There's also no method of hiding bodies, which means that you have to wait to make sure no-one walks in on a body before it despawns - although to be fair this is usually fairly quick.
Third: In order to get new Warframes, or new weapons, consumables, etc. one must grind for hours and hours. Also, you have to wait until the parts you are looking for are available in events, as this is where they usually appear. This can take anywhere from days to in fact months for the piece you need to be available. Also, unless you log in daily to check, the only way to find out when the piece is available is via the app, which I have heard has issues.
Fourth: The game is based almost entirely around what are essentially supposed to be campaign missions. These can be played coop or solo. However, there are only a handful of instanced regions that they are based in, based off of which type of enemy you are fighting. They also have a set mission type, i.e. eliminate all troop types, etc. Going back to the stealth aspect, many of these types are impossible to do via stealth (such as the defend area/machine missions) which forces you to rely on the terrible combat system. There are only a few enemy types, which between the limited settings and the handful of mission types makes the game terribly repetitive.
Fifth: The community is terrible. They are unforthcoming about where to find materials, parts, etc. forcing you to go through the poorly written wiki (which also hasn't been updated in many cases, and is thus inaccurate) to find answers. There are very few friendly players out there to do missions with, unless you join a clan. The players that are willing to play with you, regardless of whether you are in their clan or not, are ultracompetitive. If you are then this should not be a problem, but for a casual like me this is a huge downside. I play for fun, and I don't mind losing if I had fun doing so. However, these guys do not, and they aren't even willing to account for new players who haven't ground their lives away to get good gear.
I would like it noted that, while I am a casual, I usually do very well at both shooters and stealth games. I can't complete some missions in Warframe due to the terrible mechanics and the unfriendly community. I also hate grinding, so I will probably never get the good gear even though I have now figured out how everything works. If you are looking for an mmorpg to play, go play an actual mmorpg. If you're looking for a shooter, go play an actual shooter. This is a terrible attempt at combining the two genres. It's not even worth the price (yes I know it's free).

I haven't played on the PC since the game was relatively new (or on Steam), but I play almost every night on the Xbox One now. For anyone worried about the grind, all I can say is... honestly it's complete bull, there is no grind. I had my first Prime frame on my first week. I'm on week three and I have four primes (Trinity, Ash, Nekros, Valkyr) and numerous prime weapons. I didn't get handouts. I didn't pay for items. The only thing I've ever spent real money on are cosmetics and frame slots.
I will say this. The game does get extremely repetitive at times. But. It only really gets boring if you're playing alone/with PuGs, or are doing a hardcore farm. Most of the turn-off comes from the initial illusion that everything worthwhile costs money or is a million miles away. The game doesn't really give much of a sense of direction to a new player. In reality, once you realize what you have to do, and start leveling a bunch of different things up, everything gets so streamlined and put into perspective.
The gameplay is fun. The graphics are beautiful. The narrative is deceptively amazing. The game is FREE! There's no reason not to pick this game up.

So, my views on this game have shifted from right to left to right to left. I love this game. I hate this game. It's a unique and troubling experience. Here's the run down.
This game has some of the coolest, smoothest, and most epic sword play I've seen in a FPS game. It's hectic, and the timing and skill it takes to successfully take down an opponent is immense at first, and remains immense even after hundreds of hours of gameplay.
There are still issues with the combat though, often times I'll take damage despite my shield being raised and they are standing directly in front of me, and this is a little annoying, but forgivabel in the grand scheme of things.
The community is as varied as it can get. I've played games with the meanest, saltiest, most profane group of internet bred scum. But I've also played games with interesting, intelligent, and competitive opponents. There have been games where it's just chaos and everyone is pressing only the LMB. But there have also been games where we'll strategize in the chat box and discuss how best to over throw the enemy team, or how and when to flank them.
Nothing is more satisfying than when someone suggests in the team chat that everyone should gather at the spawn point and charge out together at the same time all the white screaming their battle cries. It's an awesome experience and is definitely fun to be apart of.
You die a lot.
More than Dark Souls.
The game is multiplayer only, but there is a vague, and loose narrative tied to it through the training session (which is highly recommended for new players).
This game is worth the twenty bucks I paid for it, and if they figured out how to get it onto console I'd pay another twenty bucks for it there too. It's a lot of fun. There is an intense learning curve. I've only just now gotten good at the game in first person mode after 115 hours of playing it.

DONT BUY. HERES WHY.
1) CRASHES STOP GAME FROM RUNNING: Check the forums for people who simply cannot play the game at all after purchase.

3) TEAM CONFUSION: The added "player customization" actually allows you to color you're character's clothes like he's on the other team! Sure it's a great trick, but that's a problem the devs simply should not be ignorant about.

I tried to make the game fun, but it just became a technical battle of who had the most free time to figure out exactly what the developers overlooked. I actually had a guy shoot me with an arrow thru a fence, telling me I was stupid for not know that there's a 1 pixel space between the posts. Really, like I'm gonna look that up somewhere?
A common bizarre tactic is for players to reduce the speed of their blade to being almost motionless while still delivering full damage. While their claim it requires skill may be true, it over looks the fact that it has nothing to do with enjoying a good swordfight.
The game is defined by a poor game mechanic which creates a whole slew of bizarre game tactics that take the enjoyment out of the sword fighting gameplay. It could be good if the devs worked it all out, but they say whatever people can figure out is "acceptable" within the game. So yeah, might want to avoid this one.

If you're someone like me who loves online games that are filled with adrenaline, excitement, rewards, bonuses, etc, then this is an amazing game! I personally love this game because it's a sci-fi shooter that allows players to interact with one another and take each other head-on in plenty of different competitions and events. You can even battle for items, platinum, and mods (which is really fun). Overall, the game is incredible when it comes down to making you feel entertained and the admins never fail to let us know when an update is available and what we should expect in the future. I like the story with Tenno and how you need to defeat several bosses in order to return the solar system to it's healthy state and I love how the game tells you how far players have gotten at beating the infestation. I also love the different ways of trading, whether it's through a trading post, bazaroo's (and other trading areas), or through the chat, you can always find someone who's willing to buy or sell items.
Another great aspect of the game that I shoud mention is the graphics (cause who doesn't love those?). Despite it being a free game, the graphics and overall programming of the game is magnificent. The details and sound are really well done and even though there are a few glitches every here and there, if you have a stable operating system, everything looks beautiful! The quests are also very interesting and they're always coming out with new ones! One of the newer quests (The Glast Gambit is what it's called I think), has everyone excited as always! I also like the fact that you have a wide variety of warframes to choose from. It's kinda boring just sticking with one all the time so switching to a new warframe always feels refreshing so I'm always thankful for that.
One more thing is that everyone in this game is usually very respectful of one another. Although there is a bit of drama here and there, everyone tries to respect one another's opinion and are simply there to enjoy themselves (which is nice considering that a lot of players in online games tend to be a bit rude to one another). Unlocking and exploring the different planets is always a lot of fun and even though a lot of people feel embarrassed when they have to admit to being new to the game, newbies are welcomed here and everyone is usually very kind to people who are playing for the first time!
In fact, they're so kind that they often try to help them out and give them advice! I was kind of shocked when someone helped me out as a new player on how to finish a mission and I now see other people doing it as well all the time. It's really helpful and kind of everyone.
If you're also a sci-fi weirdo who loves sci-fi stories and themes, then you should definitely play this game because it has A LOT of that in it! I sincerely recommend this game for all of it's beautiful aspects! Bravo!

I'd recommend this game, As long as you like enjoy doing things. First of all, I want to say that this game will look like repetitive grinding, if you havent understand it's core. Because from my 300 hrs, I realized that this game mimics the style of "trying every stuff until you found the one that you really love". Sure, trying to farm 300 weapons just for 300.000 exp are not enjoyable to some, But don't think about it like that, because you will get burned very fast.
Think about this game as a playground. And sure, Everybody knows a MK1 vs Prime even on it's base stats are different. But it's kind of a reward of your hard work, grinding to get relics, then grind the parts, then grind the material, then wait countless hours, and all of it before you know how it will works. Forget youtube. Try it for yourself, and you can see that there's still a lot of things to do.
Doesn't meant you can ask for help. This game's community playerbase is Amazing, yeah sometimes toxic, but you can't really avoid that, like in most games in the world. But this game was actually designed to "make yourselft at home" style, And you know what ? you can actually make your own home in the game.
The Devs, are supportive either, watch the game when it's released, and watch it now. The difference, I could say, is a BIG one. The mechanics, the system it self were changed, adjusted towards the playerbase. Archwings are bad. For me ? It's just a refreshing playground. Tired of pressing 1-2-3-4 to win ? Play the Archwing Rush mode. It's too easy ? Sometimes. but you can get to Lv 9999 solo if you want to, no one's stopping you.
For a F2P ? It's amazing. You can trade for basically everything. Except Anniversary Items and Prime Accesories Bundles. Even cosmetics in game, you can buy with your free plat. But I'd recommend to spent at least a few dollars into this game, just for a little thank you to the devs.
This is even more enjoyable with friends. Doesn't meant by your friends doing all the hard work, but doing as what I stated above, with friends. Still bored ? Poking fun at the bot, also works. But don't do it too much, or you will lose your account pretty fast. Still bored again ? Play Conclave. Try to win those oro and place it on your Orbiter.
Story, pretty good considering it's an online game. It has a great depth, even though it still revolve on the classic (It's all about the origin of us, the player). Though probably you'd get sick of hearing the same praise over and over again for 5 million times throughout the course of the game, but it's still enjoyable. Or having a zombie dog that has the enemy head tilted upside down just cause it's a placeholder, Cool. Loved to get attacked by the unknown ? It happens often. But all I gotta say, is that this game's story is shine it's masterpiece when it's on the start of "Natah" quest. The first few quest is a common drift, but it's unique feelings starts when you play Natah.
It's a totally mixed review, but if you had gone through almost everything solo like I did, Like losing those potato because I can't finish the mission solo... you'd pretty much get what I meant.

So, it is free and it can be finished. Yet I despise it much more than other clicker games I've tried so far. Yeah, I know "Clicker Heroes" is still in beta, and will be improved in some way. But from my point, it is beyond help. And no, it is not about broken mouses and/or fingers due this process.
You see, all clickers in general seems to me much like facebook games ala "Farmville" - you redistribute some resources, closing the window and returning to it after some time, to collect more resources and expand a bit. So on and so forth, you do your things, and your clicker game living its own life, killing some monsters, collecting gold and precious achievements for your profile... Generally, I don't mind, I have more time to do my things, while my profile expanding with help of that freeware stuff. But all that is not about Clicker Heroes.
While at start it looks just like other clickers, after some progress you facing the fact that you need more and more time in game. Without your guidance, the game will be stucking in one place for too long. After 1000+ completed levels, it is getting even worse, as you need to wait more and more for the next "Hero" to unlock. Gaps between normal playing, where the game can play itself, to some freaking grindfest, where you sitting by hours, making all that clicking by yourself just to get over one boss level... It is not Farmville anymore, it looks like those self-proclamed RPGs (you can find those in Facebook as well), where are no story, and so much grind, that you eventually catching yourself installing some third-hand script, which is presumed to get your hands free, at least for some time.
I hate games like those. They are not giving you fun, they do not entertain or educate you. Quite opposite, they make you dumber. To the point, where you starting to pay up with your money for some "boosts", which gives you a freedom of 2-3 minutes to not proceed with all that clicking by yourself.
So yeah, love yourself, stay away from Clicker Heroes. If you still want to see that, "just with one eye, just for one minute", I suggest you to look for another clicker game. Tap Tap Infinity, for example, is much alike Clicker Heroes, but it stays in Farmville pattern, not morphing into timetrap like Clicker Heroes.
My mark is 4/10. It is playable, it is free at start, and it is still possible to get all achievements... But you will do yourself a great favor with not getting into that.
PS Am I have to remind someone that third-party scripts that supposed to "help you with the game", can do some other things on the way? Like collecting your data and passwords, for example? If you can't beat the game without such scripts, maybe it is not worth it, how do you think?
ver.1 update: so they added much more levels, and few more mechanics to spend your clicks on. Still boring and freaking unrewardable, even with those Ancients to swing by. Took me a hundred of hours to beat that thing... again. Wish I never started it, sigh.

Disclaimer: This review is done by me after returning from not playing for two years. So I am writing a new review to adjust to the new changes.
Do you like good quality games that are enjoyable and keeps your butt in the chair playing? Then go no further.
However if you don't like having to earn everything, you don't have any patience, you want a bland, predictable, experience that has been spoonfed to you, and you don't like an open free trading market then plenty of other games have you covered. Maybe try anything made by Valve, Blizzard, Ubisoft, Activision, or EA. This game is not for you. Don't come in here complaining that something takes longer than 30 minutes to finish. Just move along.
Warframe is very well optimized. 200 enemies on the screen with all sorts of particle effects and my game never drops a frame. Controls are very tight and feel tight, you feel in control of your warframe at all times. A huge variety of gameplay style choices which come from varieties in warframes, weapons, mods, and more that offer endless possibilities. Many different tasks and goals to accomplish in this game along with many planets, quest types, mission objectives, clans, customization, and many more. Warframe is really about you creating your own goals and experience and then following through on it. Nothing is really spoonfed to you except some quest rewards that serve as a tool to teach you how to play the game.
That being said: there are flaws to this game. I personally don’t have a problem with the grind since I have played games with far worst grinding but some people find it demanding. You can always opt out to paying for plat to skip grinding but I would not recommend that since it would take away from leveling up your gear and slow down your progress in general. If you enjoy grinding like me, then this will not be a flaw for you. Another flaw(which unfortunately has no positive to it) is glitches. I encounter annoying HUD bugs every now and then and a few game breaking glitches that required me to restart the mission. Maybe DE will fix those, maybe they won’t. Host migrations are a pain in the butt and often are the source of the bugs that occur. No dedicated servers? That’s a HUGE flaw. Also DE has a habit of introducing new content and then abandoning it to pump out more new content. Not enough optimizing the content and making it a core aspect of the game.
All the flaws being considered this is still a great game and most of the time you are not even going to notice this because the game is just so addictive and triggers the “fun” in my brain even after running a mission for the 200th time in a hope of getting a rare drop. I think this will easily be my next game with 5k hours in.
Hopefully DE continues to release new content like their recent open world addition and they made this a core aspect of the game rather than an afterthought. If they do that, this game will not die for a LONG time.

Destiny x Diablo, but free and with more content.
Pros:
*Constant updates and additions to the game
*Excellent and helpful community
*Good variety of mission types
*Ridiculous catalogue of weapons and classes
*Multiplayer recommended, but not required
*Runs well on lower end computers if you optimize for it, and looks great on higher end PCs
*Parkour system is incredible
*Gorgeous level, sound, and art design
*"Paid" currency can be traded with in game items
*Responsive and active dev team
*Good variety of play style due to large range of weapons/classes
Cons:
*HEAVY grind.  There is a lot of farming and waiting to get what you want
*Very high entry learning curve.  There's a lot to figure out at first, especially alone
*PvP is unpolished and fairly underpopulated
*Some parts of the game do become repetitive
*Archwing is not a favorite of many.  Improvements coming soon™, but it's worth noting
Real talk though, I think Warframe is F2P done right.  Everything can be farmed in game, and you can even trade in game items for the "paid" currency.  You can spend money to speed up the process if you want, but there's no hard need to.  Nothing is "Pay to win," only "Pay to rush" or "Pay to look pretty."  The devs are also fantastic people, very personable and responsive to the community.
There is a fairly high entry learning curve, and it may take a few weeks of learning to get a decent grasp of it, but I recommend reaching out to the community and other players.  Warframe has a fantastic community, and that's one of the things that keeps me coming back to it.  That, and the constant updates and additions of weapons and frames.
There is a lot of grinding and farming.  A lot.  Like a lot a lot.  If that's your deal though, it can be a ton of fun.  I'd recommend checking it out at the very least.
After all, it's free.

Warframe: A game where you grind so you can grind some more. I will warn you of that right now! If you hate those types of games best get off the boat now!
It's repetitive, it can be tedious and as I just said it's a hell of a grind to acquire the stuff you want. There now that we got that out of the way lets move on, this is a positive review after all. So what makes it good?
The combat is ohhhhh so satisfying! Everything is so fluid and well animated and executed. The game is challenging, there is no mercy for the unprepared. The game looks amazing with beautiful graphics and it runs like a dream, even on a potato machine. The lore and story is interesting enough to keep you interested and there is an abundance of side quests to do. The upgrade system is well done, you feel yourself getting stronger which is always good. The mods you equip to your weapons and Warframe are varied so you can build up your character in a number of different ways that feels unique.
Plus the game is free... And you don't need to spend a penny to get everything in the game, this goes back to the whole grinding thing, but paid currency is avaliable for those who want fast access to what they want. The Devs are very active and updates are regular and meaty.
Give the game a try you have nothing to lose, except maybe hours and hours of your life if it tickles your taste buds!

I would recommend this game to people mainly because the game itself is absolutely amazing! There are bugs, as to be expected from a non-Triple A company making a Triple A type game. The Price is a bit too high in the ranges, it used to be $30, now it's $60. I understand the reasoning behind it, being that they wanted to keep it on par with the console version, though they could have just raise it by like 10-15 dollars, and set that same price on console versions as well and still kept the majority of their potential customers.
My second gripe with the game is the lack of size optimization! I downloaded the game at a little over 12 Gigs, now it's around 115 Gigs. Every update, whether a minor patch containing bug fixes or an update adding a few dino's or maybe some texture updates, or even a major patch containing a huge amount of bug fixes, ranges from 50MB to 7GB!!!!!!!!!!!! I understand the dino additions and the major patches for texture additions/fixes and bug fixes, but for the minor patches to be from 50MB to 1.5GB is utter hogwash!! Recently there were a couple of 2gb updates where the only description they gave were "Some Minor Bug Fixes". What does that mean?! How many were "Fixed", what bugs were they, and why did they consume so much space?!
Also there needs to be a better way of getting off Bronto's. That and it'd be nice if dinos could turn while backing up. As far as I know, they're just Mobile Forks. They can only more backwards in a straight line, and forwards in a straight line or left or right, most dino's can't turn around when standing still.. I think the Two-Legged ones can, and maybe some four-legged dinos, but it's really the ones that need to, can't.
But other than those gripes, it's pretty fun, can be difficult, and annoying at times. Compies will be your main source of levels and death in the beginning, that and fish. Raptors will murder you, well until you're higher in levels.

I haven't played on the PC since the game was relatively new (or on Steam), but I play almost every night on the Xbox One now. For anyone worried about the grind, all I can say is... honestly it's complete bull, there is no grind. I had my first Prime frame on my first week. I'm on week three and I have four primes (Trinity, Ash, Nekros, Valkyr) and numerous prime weapons. I didn't get handouts. I didn't pay for items. The only thing I've ever spent real money on are cosmetics and frame slots.
I will say this. The game does get extremely repetitive at times. But. It only really gets boring if you're playing alone/with PuGs, or are doing a hardcore farm. Most of the turn-off comes from the initial illusion that everything worthwhile costs money or is a million miles away. The game doesn't really give much of a sense of direction to a new player. In reality, once you realize what you have to do, and start leveling a bunch of different things up, everything gets so streamlined and put into perspective.
The gameplay is fun. The graphics are beautiful. The narrative is deceptively amazing. The game is FREE! There's no reason not to pick this game up.

I've been playing Warframe since 2013, and still do today.
A bad thing about Warframe -> people are lacking creativity. Most of the players seem to play like blind people, since almost every player is focused on ONE thing... Leveling up, and when they've reached the current max lvl they complain about a lack of content and nothing more to do...
Warframe is a game of customization, filled with opportunities to make every player fit in. Every weapon, Warframe, Archwing etc. can be good. People often seem to think that the prime/stalker weapons are the only thing to use, and that the "how to mod: ____" videos on YouTube is the only well working option to make a weapon good. But that is in most cases a big mistake from the players. Sure a starting mk.1 weapon is not as good as the prime one, and of cause there is nothing bad about getting modding inspiration from videos. The thing is, if you put enough effort into a Weapon/Warframe/Archwing/Companion, then that might just work just as good. Why try to make the Ignis good, if you don't like the way it's shooting, why not go for an old school Burston if that's what you prefer?
A lot of people seem to only focus on those things: ranking up and getting good loadouts. It's like people seem to forget what the game is trying to offer you. Try to do something different if you don't like the game. Join a clan, do some Archwing races, finish the quests, challenge yourself like how long can you defend the objective and even better, how long can your squard which you currently are chatting with, having a good time, laughing together about how stupid and yet addorable Clem is, defend the objective!
Don't be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and join a clan because they've got full research and no taxes. When you join a clan, think of it as you join a community, sure some clans are only out there because of the remaining items they need to reach max lvl.
Do yourself a favour and look for a clan with a great working community, it doesent have to be a big clan, it can be even more exiting to help a clan grow from the bottom, reqruit players, and experience how a community can be made from a single free to play game.
And don't come and say the game is pay to win, because it's not... As they added trading in Warframe, every player is able to get as much platinum as they want. The only thing they can't get without paying is the steam workshop items, and the prime access accessories.... But those are all cosmetics... So let's just forget about the whole P2W thing people are complaining about.

I'm going to try to keep this brief since I've played this game for a long, long time that I could probably write a ten page essay talking about its pros and cons in detail.  Warframe is basically a highly mobile third person shooter with powers.  It's also free to play where most in-game affecting stuff can either be bought or earned.  The only things you can't earn in-game, except through rare events like anniversaries or logging in for a hundred days, are inventory slots.
Now, I'd divide the game into two parts:  star chart and post-star chart.  The star chart is insanely fun to play through.  Granted, the new player experience is rough since so much isn't explained clearly, or not at all, in-game, pretty much forcing you to use the community (which is actually a pretty good one, IMO) or the off-site wiki.  For example, things it doesn't mention are that most regular Warframes drop from specific bosses, most weapon blueprints are market and clan tech rather than drops, and Prime stuff, which is upgraded regular stuff, comes from fissures.  There's also the early resource and credit grind being a big pain, especially without access to some of the planets that drop specific resources.  But get past that, as well as past the long craft times, and playing through the star chart and exploring the confusing and non-chronological storyline is great fun.
Then you clear everything and what's left?  Grinding.  For grind's sake.  I eventually got to the point where I started to wonder "Why am I still grinding?  To what end?"  I could do most Sorties, solo even if I didn't feel like rushing.  Few enemies were challenging and the ones that are were the ones with bullcrap mechanics (hello Scorches if they've STILL not been fixed yet!)  Basically, it was grinding up incremental power to make me kill stuff faster, or get mastery rank points from leveling weapons and warframes I didn't care for, to kill stuff even faster when I was already killing stuff fine.  This game is fun when you go through a mission at a reasonable rate and the enemies are a reasonable threat:  not too squishy and weak and not too ridiculously OP or bullcrappy.   But in the end game, it's either one or the other and you're speedrunning because it's easy and boring and you just want the reward or you're speedrunning because holy crap this is bullcrap end it now.
So if it becomes that, why am I still recommending this?  Simple:  it's worth picking up for the Star Chart experience.  Early days are a pain, but the amount of fun playing the regular content is worthwhile.  Once you've seen and done all the non-repeatable stuff is when you should consider whether or not you enjoy replaying randomly generated missions with the same enemies over and over enough for the sake of it.
I had a lot of fun with this, but I'm done.  I've probably put way too many hours in as is and I've bled this game dry of everything it has to offer me.  DE's decisions over the past few months have also left me doubtful for the future of the game (hello Hema and Nidus), especially since they seemed focused on rushing to new and shiny stuff while leaving a trail of broken and unpolished content in their wake since they aren't putting enough time into anything, so I don't ever see me coming back to this except to casually mess around.  But most of my time with the game was still fun, worthwhile, and I don't regret it.
So, give the game a shot and get your fun out of it.  Just keep an eye on your wallet and how much time you're spending grinding.  And ignore the prime access and stuff, just wait for a 75% off platinum log-in reward if you want to dump money on the game.  I grabbed the $100 one for only $25 and, between that, trading for some more, and conservative spending and it lasted me through my entire excessive number of hours.

A bloody and violent first-person action game, yet amazingly and outstandingly constructed. With ice cold steel swords, mountain-heavy blunt weapons, or feather-light yet devastating daggers on hands, one may find skull decapitations and limb dismemberments rather interesting and enjoyable in skirmishes during the medieval era. As detestable as it seems, Chivalry: Medieval Warfare exaggeratedly illustrates the gore and bloody scenes of medieval warfare through explicit digital renderings, yet accurately expresses the involvement of the very bloodsheds during the devastating era of unstoppable religious warfare. Not only are the historical accuracies well done, but the language styles of which the various characters in the game use are also as plausible and humorous as they can possibly be. The complexities of how to approach in a combat in the game are by far - in my opinion - the best designed, comparing to that of other first-person action games (Call of Duty); Players utilize parries (to block incoming attacks), psychological trickeries (feint attacks), and other various methodologies of melee combat. Players utilize these methods, often in a heterogeneous and complex manner, to pursue a glorifying victory from their opponents. Warm approvals should be awarded to the crews of Torn Banner, for their most diligent and quality efforts have allowed users of Chivalry: Medieval Warfare to rejoice in gaming experiences.

TLDR: A great game which I cannot recommend until significant - very significant - bugfixes are complete.
ARK is a fantastic game that should have spent at least a full additional year in development.  The amount of bugs still present in the game is staggering, despite voluminous communication from the early access community over a series of years.
Bugs which were identified years ago, and deeply affect the major game systems, are still very much present.  The building systems, mating, breeding, kibble (early raising), pathing, collision, creature spawning, terrain/mesh, ascension (end game), are all suffering from fundamental flaws in both design and execution.
Worse, the game has an enormous number of very well-publicized cheaters who destroy their local servers' economy by duplicating items, DDOSing rival servers, and manipulating the cross-server system, significant problems which have been around for over a year - since the introduction of the cross-ARK system - and still have no adequate resolution, or even an (announced) plan to fix it.
That said, the core of this game really is fantastic (over 2k hours logged) and in terms of value, you will undoubtedly get your $60 worth.  Just expect that at that price, you will also be paying for quite a lot of frustration.  The core survival elements of the game are incredibly compelling, if you enjoy a steep difficlty curve.  The world(s) are vast and feature-full, and you will not lack for interesting, challening objectives to complete until the endgame.  There is no questing system; it is an open world where your intentions and interests form more of your experience than a traditional MMO, and this is very welcome.  Like raising animals?  Building? Hunting? Teamwork? Boss fights?  The game has them, and generally, they're all pretty fun, although often with a very serious grinding component. It's hard to overstate how much fun riding a huge dinosaur into an epic battle is.  Or even picking up dodos and throwing them at your friends. The basics are great!
The frustration many of us feel is that, with so many deep and engaging systems, the numerous bugs are like giant worts right on the face of the game.  And they don't feel like true technical hurdles; they feel like oversights and poor development prioritization.  Almost like, "you guys are engaging a lot with the game so we're going to ignore your complaints because clearly they aren't stoppping you from playing." But, the issue is, people are willing to forget this junk in EA under the expectation that it will get fixed before release.  To find so many fundamental bugs still present in the game is just inexcusable, despite how good the good parts can be.
Personally, I would love to return to this game on a subscription basis that also included much needed development.  Here's hoping that with the release of the game, they'll be able to devote the kind of development resources that should have been brought to bear on the project long ago.
I plan to install the game again after I see some significant progress on the system bugs and widespread cheating, and will update this review accordingly.

up to the days when the mechanic changed, with a lot of new gamemodes & frames come, I still played them

I would love to play warframe

up to the point where you reach some high-end missions....

Grinding is the real problem for you....

keep grinding....and....no.......

This game is psychologically complicated. It's entertaining, it's rewarding, but I'm not entirely sure that I would describe it as fun. It might also be mildly addicting. Probably has badly as World of Warcraft is, but not in the same way. It is rewarding when you get your heroes to a high enough dps (damage per second) that you don't have to click anything. I have delayed going to bed for more than a few minutes to make sure that I farmed gold most efficiently while sleeping. I would liken the experience to grinding levels in an rpg like Final Fantasy or farming materials for the Ultima Weapon in Kingdom Hearts. You don't play this because it's super fun. You play it because of the reward of reaching a boss you can't kill, starting over with more damage and getting a little further next round.
You can reach a point where you can play the game without clicking the monsters (being idle). So you don't have to really pay that much attention to what's happening. I usually "play" while browsing the internet and leave it running while I sleep or am not at the computer.
This is probably everything that is right and wrong with casual gaming. It's rewarding without putting forth any real effort. The game requires patience, an addiction, or indifference.
