There are a lot of mixed reviews for Ark, and after so long playing it I thought I'd add my own two cents. The biggest sore point recently is the price, so I'll start there. Personally... I would never have paid £50 for this game – that's just far too much. If I could have known without a doubt that I would spend 1000+ hours on it? Bargain!... but no one can be sure of that before a purchase. Setting the price so steep is basically Wildcards way of cutting its nose off to spite its face. I've no doubt that the price will drop again, even if only in sales. Therefore, if you're unsure about it, I would recommend waiting for that price drop.
I bought it for around £15, I have never regretted it, and if I had been daft enough to pay the £50 back then... I still wouldn't regret it now, not after getting so much out of it. It really annoys me to see all these negative reviews from players with 100s+ hours played....

OK now I've got that over with. next point: Wildcards second biggest mistake after this price change is the release of a paid expansion during early access. It's just not done. There are people who refuse to even try the game because of that. I think that's when most of the reviews started to drop from positive and I can't blame them … but it's time to get past that. The game is now fully released, and with a further two expansions promised in the future.
Bugs. I haven't suffered any problems that make the game unplayable. I don't have a top of the line PC. The most annoying thing is having to change the gamma between day and night... that's what torches are for, I suppose, but I just don't bother with them, and to be honest it's either too bright or too dark. The graphics are beautiful.. anyone who says they're rubbish needs glasses or, most likely, a new toaster.
This is one of those games that takes time... about 500 of the hours I've played have been setting up a base with my friend, getting an egg farm together etc before we could start thinking about taming any strong high level dinosaurs. All these games are about grinding, about slowly working towards something – if you don't have the patience for that, go play Minecraft.
Every game has its bugs, and quite a lot of them nowadays have problems on launch – its disappointing, sure, but not a good enough reason to mark the game itself down.
I play on an unofficial server that suits me, so I cant speak much for the official servers. I know, however, that I hate pvp and in all the hours I have on this game, not once have I been forced to partake in it. I will agree that the devs seem blissfully ignorant of their player community – they're more interested in putting out the game they want, not what their players are asking for. That's a big no no in this day and age, but... Ark is exactly what is says on the tin. You know it, you want it, you buy it and you play it.
To round things up – I got a bit sidetracked and ranty there – if you like survival games and all that comes with it – food, drink, temperatures, things that go bump in the night and tear your face off, then this is for you. You can build a base as large or as small as you like – depending on your server choice. You can tame a HUGE variety of dinosaurs, virtually all of them useful – and anything you don't like? There's probably a mod for it. I definitely recommend the game.

I'm going to try to keep this brief since I've played this game for a long, long time that I could probably write a ten page essay talking about its pros and cons in detail.  Warframe is basically a highly mobile third person shooter with powers.  It's also free to play where most in-game affecting stuff can either be bought or earned.  The only things you can't earn in-game, except through rare events like anniversaries or logging in for a hundred days, are inventory slots.
Now, I'd divide the game into two parts:  star chart and post-star chart.  The star chart is insanely fun to play through.  Granted, the new player experience is rough since so much isn't explained clearly, or not at all, in-game, pretty much forcing you to use the community (which is actually a pretty good one, IMO) or the off-site wiki.  For example, things it doesn't mention are that most regular Warframes drop from specific bosses, most weapon blueprints are market and clan tech rather than drops, and Prime stuff, which is upgraded regular stuff, comes from fissures.  There's also the early resource and credit grind being a big pain, especially without access to some of the planets that drop specific resources.  But get past that, as well as past the long craft times, and playing through the star chart and exploring the confusing and non-chronological storyline is great fun.
Then you clear everything and what's left?  Grinding.  For grind's sake.  I eventually got to the point where I started to wonder "Why am I still grinding?  To what end?"  I could do most Sorties, solo even if I didn't feel like rushing.  Few enemies were challenging and the ones that are were the ones with bullcrap mechanics (hello Scorches if they've STILL not been fixed yet!)  Basically, it was grinding up incremental power to make me kill stuff faster, or get mastery rank points from leveling weapons and warframes I didn't care for, to kill stuff even faster when I was already killing stuff fine.  This game is fun when you go through a mission at a reasonable rate and the enemies are a reasonable threat:  not too squishy and weak and not too ridiculously OP or bullcrappy.   But in the end game, it's either one or the other and you're speedrunning because it's easy and boring and you just want the reward or you're speedrunning because holy crap this is bullcrap end it now.
So if it becomes that, why am I still recommending this?  Simple:  it's worth picking up for the Star Chart experience.  Early days are a pain, but the amount of fun playing the regular content is worthwhile.  Once you've seen and done all the non-repeatable stuff is when you should consider whether or not you enjoy replaying randomly generated missions with the same enemies over and over enough for the sake of it.
I had a lot of fun with this, but I'm done.  I've probably put way too many hours in as is and I've bled this game dry of everything it has to offer me.  DE's decisions over the past few months have also left me doubtful for the future of the game (hello Hema and Nidus), especially since they seemed focused on rushing to new and shiny stuff while leaving a trail of broken and unpolished content in their wake since they aren't putting enough time into anything, so I don't ever see me coming back to this except to casually mess around.  But most of my time with the game was still fun, worthwhile, and I don't regret it.
So, give the game a shot and get your fun out of it.  Just keep an eye on your wallet and how much time you're spending grinding.  And ignore the prime access and stuff, just wait for a 75% off platinum log-in reward if you want to dump money on the game.  I grabbed the $100 one for only $25 and, between that, trading for some more, and conservative spending and it lasted me through my entire excessive number of hours.

This is basically a grind/waiting simulator and has been for over 4 years.
I first played this game when it came out some time ago and back then it felt like a genuine game. The combat was fun, gruesome, and all-around it felt like there was a huge variety of things to do in the world itself. You could sit down for an entire day and just play the game and unlock all the systems, do some quests, and maybe during that time you found some warframe parts you could make and everything was awesome. At first it did seem really grind-y and that was really the only part that threw me off plus the fact I had to wait 4 days for a new warframe, but that was mostly it. I stopped playing for a while, played it senior year of highschool, and when I came back I did't even recognize the game I had once loved.
The new system for doing side-quests to unlock planets/systems was a horrid idea and never should have seen the light of day. All 100+ hours I had put in before became meaningless and I had to start from scratch to get anywhere further in the game. But no, I couldn't do that, because somehow every weapon, Warframe, and Mod I had had been reset. Said ♥♥♥♥ this, I'm making a new account. Probably the worst decision I had made. The new grind for everything was SO ATROCIOUSLY BORING I couldn't play the game for more than 1 hr at a time. I kept logging on every day to get my daily reward, grind some more, build some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ weapon, level it up, log off, and do the same thing over and over again for over a month. The bosses don't even feel unique or satisfying to battle anymore. Theyre just another enemy you need to kill to POSSIBLY get a part that you need for something but then you gotta fighr them 12+ more times just to get the same part 6 more times over. The RNG in it is so infuriating I couldn't help but buy platinum just so I could play the game the way I wanted to play it.
And to make matters worse, all the new content is just terrible. Nothing feels unique anymore, nothing feels special or really satisfying to use, it's just all numbers ona screen that let you know how much faster you can farm. Even getting all the new content is nigh impossible because you need to do 1,000,000 things before it to even think about getting any of it becuase the new pre-requisites for getting anything in this game is just complete utter BS. For anyone new looking to get the cool new weapon that they really want to see in action, nope, sorry, play 400+ hours and you'll maybe get it.
As you can see, I've played over 300 hours in this game and have nothing much to show for it and honestly, I wish I could buy my time back that I wasted on this game.
DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME PLAYING THIS GAME.
Go do something, literally anyting else. Go even play ARK Survival Evolved or run around for 7 hours in DayZ. The communitty for this game is dying and everyone knows it.
TLDR; This game is hard for beginners, is really grindy, and takes lots of time and effort to really get anywhere in the game itself. Also the pre-requisite system is BS

Warframe is a game I have left and returned to many times over the course of 4 years. I began my journey as a lowly console player with 30 frames per second and terrible resolution in a completely different game. Now, on PC and after years of development, I have to say I'm very impressed with the sheer amount of improvement.
The combat is very fluid and easy to master, but each weapon has little nuances that will improve your efficiency as you use them more. And there is endless variety in the weapon selections. From a bow that can cleave enemies in two, to a jet powered hammer that will send enemies flying. Each melee weapon has multiple stances that will change the way you wield it and what sort of combos can be achieved with it. Furthermore, each warframe has 4 unique abilities, and most have augments that will change their effects in some way.
The movement system when I started was clunky and awkward (maybe just because I was on console), but since the Movement 2.0 update, everything flows together nicely. The movement system seamlessly integrates with the combat to create a fast paced and high flying experience, but also encourages you to move slowly and stealthily in certian missions.
Now on to the grind. I once thought that grinding in this game was terrible, slow, and not rewarding enough. Then I realized that I was missing out on the cooperation. Simply playing with a squad will increase your gain of resources dramatically. I left a 20 minute mission yesterday with 1000 Endo (The resource used to improve mods), which more than enough to improve many mods to max rank. I recommend joining a clan as soon as possible and asking your new clanmates for help.
Which brings me to my next point. The community is wonderful. I had been farming for an essential mod, but had no luck getting it. So I took to the chat and voiced my complaints about my bad luck. Within seconds I had almost 20 people offering to give me the mod for free! People are always willing to help or answer questions you might have. Anything from helping you aquire the resources you need, beat a challenging mission, all the way up to forming groups to take on the Sortie's (High level missions with big rewards).
Overall, this is a completely different game than it was when I first started playing. I would argue that it has done nothing but improve. Some people complain about the grind and feel that they need to spend money in order to get the items they want, but simply asking for help from the community can expedite your process greatly.
If you decide to play Warframe, come in with a willingness to learn, because there are thousands of things to do and millions of enemies to slaughter.

The explosion took me by surprise, one moment I was bracing myself against the door leading into my King's throne room, supported by my men. The next I was flying accross the room. I hit the wall and I felt my body give. My lungs were failing. I was struggling to breath. I did not register the sounds of battle, or the screams of the mortally wounded until all went silent. I looked to my weapon just inches from my side as I reached for it I noticed my arm was a bloody stub.
Before I could go into shock I heard footsteps approaching me keeping my mind focussed on surviving the couple moments. They were heavy steps from large metal shoes.
As I looked up to face what I was sure was my death, I saw instead the familar face of my Sergeant. A man who has campainged with me for nigh on 20 years.
There was sadness in his eyes.
Why is my Sergeant so distraught?
Have I not led him through the most desparately dark campaigns, wherein our ONLY hope for survival lay in the flesh of our dead brothers. What has managed to *cough* make him despair so badly that he would openly weep--
My mouth moves but I cannot seem to force any sound pass my lips. My vision starts to blacken. The last thing I feel is my sword being place in my good hand...

So I'm 1050 hours in warframe, bugs come and go but theres a new terror coming and I hope it never does. Now I'm going to begin this review with a note: If you are a lover of warframe or a hater of warframe, make your opinions true and not false don't defend warframe souly because you love it at least point out it's issues before attacking a hater or a destiny player because it makes us as a whole look stupid the white knights of warframe open your eyes because warframe isn't a perfect free to play game, far from it actually. So let's get to the review, warframe is a free to play game with you a badass space ninja fighting off 3 enemy factions corpus, grineer and infested. The game starts you off brand spanking new and explains some of the mechanic's but not all of them, I am glad that Steve played through it and thought it would be nice to add more explanation's for the game itself so the devs are constantly trying to make the game better for the new players but it's still rather hard to get invested in warframe when you're a new comer. Warframe is a great third person shooter with awesome parkor mechanics and beautiful visuals for a free game, their gun designs are nice but some them just look disturbing like the "Hind". Warframe is buggy but not all players run into them but the Devs make quick fixes and stay active when they make new content like during christmas they got updates out left and right fixing things quickly before they left for vaction which is fantastic they risk vacation time for their community. Some of the parkor can be glitchy at times and sometimes get you killed for example jumping towards a box at a certain angle stops your character so he latches on and does a cool spin flip on it but it wastes time when you're doing a survival. The Lore is kinda lackluster with a lot of the story locked behind symaris targets as one youtuber of warframe had to do them all just to get the lore since he's like a lore channel or something? Warframe also has a vast amount of melee weapons that each have their own animations and badass take downs which is always refreshing to watch. The warframes themselves aka your character a lot of them are well balanced and fun to play with but others are just lack luster and need some good reworks to em like Mag, Hydroid and oberon but oberon is nice where he is at. The quests in warframe in the beginning were freaking amazing! a new character after you finished a certain characters quest teaching us his history and how became the thing he was it was so well done. But recently their quests have been getting lack luster and reptitive and don't even give you the full character instead it was a pay wall or farm for the character but you didn't know where you got the parts until it was data mined. We have been getting some really weird power creep weapons as well lately with tigris prime and galatine prime being a thing. Warframe Isn't pay 2 win but it almost feels like it when they give out weapons like those because the new relic system is nice in some ways. But the fact that there are just so many relics make's it a tedious job to get the stuff you want so they have a prime access which costs 40 to 60 dollars for everything that's just mental it's like purchasing a new game when all you bought was just 1 weapon and a character. But everything is free if you're willing to farm...well not everything is sadly. Warframe has awesome events from time to time but if you miss them as a new player you can't get the rare mods or event specfic mods that came out during that event, and if that event doesn't come back you will never be able to enjoy the event and the mods in it. Which is honestly rather sad because maiming strike is one of most useful mods for a lot of crit melee builds and its locked behind a event or 1000 platinum the in game currency(trading of course). The community in warframe is always willing to help out new players espeiclaly me so add me if you want help! Warframe also has raids that are alright I guess but the rewards you get for completeing them is just sad. You get credits and 1 arcane and it can be a crappy one or an amazing one but you can play the game just as well with out em so Raids are pointless besides the amount of credits you can get. And credits will be the one thing you need the most resources to craft weapons are easy to come by. Also if you hate waiting to use new gear when you get it well you have too, it's not long usually a day or less but wanting a new character you need to wait 3 days. Not in game time btw an actual 3 day wait or pay for them to get done faster. One of the most time consuming characters to get is equinox because shes a 9 day wait basically because she has 2 seperate bodies that take 3 days each. Warframe has also been getting a lot of weapons recently that are just reskins of others or are just worthless like dark dagger and dark split sword, the jet kusar has the same crit stats as the atterax and so on. But recently we got the best weapon pack I have ever seen the Arca pack, they're badass and powerful and entierly free like everything in the game! But be warned if you like costmetics you better have the money because you need to fork up some good old green to be beautiful in this game. So on a last note, warframe has gotten a lot better over the years and I wish people wouldn't be hypocrits about it because warframe back then during first release was just meh and now look at it! it's amazing in all these different ways but also bad in different ways, like most games no game is perfect unless its KNACK 2 BABY BEST GAME 10/10 JUMPING CUT SCENES! But on a serious note open your eyes people and stop defending stuff that doesn't need it because if we constantly do it, things will get worse. Look at the nidus quest! Also yeah this game is super grindy, like really grindy.

The game runs fine, despite what people say.  I can run this on Epic (their version of ultra settings) at 1080p with an older graphics card, the Titan X, and get smooth frames.  Anyone with a lesser card just needs to upgrade their computer or NOT complain about performance above Low Graphics Settings.  The system requirements listed on the store page are not for running at Epic, so if you have the bare minimum (GTX 670) don't expect great performance.  I cannot run this at 4K resolution on Epic, but that is because I don't have to GTX 1080's SLI running this. I'm not going to complain I can't run it at 4K, because I have not upgraded my rig to do that.

Let's get some things out of the way:  This game may or may not cause you to break your mouse.  There, I've said it.  I doubt they're getting kickbacks from Logitech but you never know.
The visuals are good for what they are, and the UI is pretty clean.  The menu system could use some work, but for something that is also a browser game and has mobile ports it isn't horrible.
Now, for the game itself- there's a surprising amount of strategy for what amounts to a self-playing game.  You kill creatures for gold to purchase heroes that automatically do damage so you can kill more creatures to get more gold to buy more heroes to do more damage to get more gold- you get the picture.  The strategies that come into play are based around the fact that you can upgrade your heroes- both in level and with abilities.  Eventually, you will "Ascend", which resets you back to the first stage, forcing you to start over, but provides you with "hero souls", that can be traded for a variety of things.
Randomly there are "clickables" that show up, offering bonus loot or activating an ability without needing to worry about the cooldowns.
So, each ascension should allow you to buy better stuff and make it further in the game, faster than your last round.  There are a LOT of combinations to work with, and you can experiment or do some research on the 'net for some optimal paths.

Welcome to Chivalry: Medieval Warfare, evidently you're looking for a review that's explains to you whether you should or shouldn't buy this game. Well look no further, I have taken some time and wrote a decent review on the game which you can find down below, enjoy!
Chivalry is a game that truly lives up to it's ESRB rating, if you are not prepared to see body parts being hacked off and heads being decapitated then I don't recommend playing this. With a cutting edge gore system, Chivalry delivers a realistic experience that feels genuine and you actually feel a form of accomplishment when you run up on an enemy player and successfully cut off his head, legs, arms etc.
Chivalry can be played in either third-person or first-person, it delivers realistic weapons to the point where you actually need to consider which one you want to use instead of the typical FPS route where it generally doesn't matter what weapon you use.
Stunning visuals, rich in-depth detailing and textures are just some of the graphical enhancement's this game has compared to most of it's genre. Now speaking of the medieval first-person genre, there is really only a few and they would have to be Chivalry: Medieval Warfare and War of the Roses, if you like Vikings then there is another title called War of the Vikings which is very good as well.
With the addition of the Deadliest Warrior DLC, it's a match made in heaven. No longer are you restricted to Medieval Knights and Templars, you may now play as a Gladiator, Viking, Ninja, Samurai and so much more. Compared to the usual $60 price tag on an FPS, this game is well worth the purchase and I highly recommend buying the DLC.

Sigh. I'm no sure why I'm doing this. I usually have an urge to write a short review on this game every few hundred hours I spend in it but usually give up because I get angry at words...Well my inadequacy to accurately portray what I feel about this game.
Seeing that steam shows how many hours I logged on in this game I'm err no stranger to it I suppose. I've been playing this game on and off since around update 7. I started literally on the cusp of closed beta, the week it went into open beta, and ♥♥♥♥ me for not logging on that weekend and getting my vandal items (this sort of behavior ends up problematic as you will undoubtedly understand as you read on).
There isn't really a neutral button for this game. I can't in my right ♥♥♥♥ing mind recommend this to general public, but obviously there is something to it otherwise I wouldn't have logged few thousand hours into it (its more than what steam says, game had its own thing before steam). Anyway for new players. If you are going in and you aren't very social, you will either get really frustrated with this game, or you will spend more money on it than you could probably find sensible. I've spent a great deal of money on this game, to support it because I felt it was worth it, and I sure as hell got my money's worth, I also get a shiny Excalibur variant people can't get anymore.... That being said, this game is NOT new player friendly. No it isn't eve online level of harsh, but unless you have people helping you a great deal at the start you are going to have a very bad time, unless you absolutely love grinding until your eyeballs bleed out. For majority of established playerbase when new content comes out, it isn't too overwhelming to get it by free means. Even if it is grinding intensive if you stockpiled on something you can sell or trade you can usually acquire it without much fuss. If you are in there with nothing and plan on getting somewhere solo, you are in for a bad day.
Deep breath. Game is complex. You 'can' haphazardly hop in shoot and mod stuff on a whim, but when it comes to the harder content you will end up annoying those who might need you to contribute, or you simply won't be doing the very end content at all. Now even the hardest content in the game is relatively easy, but only when you understand the game mechanics and apply the knowledge accordingly. You might as well bookmark the wiki and have it up on all times fo reference. You will need it, be it too look up damage values, resistances, builds, or find out what drops where. Now here I'm talking high end content. If you are new you have one HELL of a ladder to climb to do it, and most of it will be dumb♥♥♥♥♥♥like leveling mods, getting mods, getting mastery rank to be able to equip weapons, and so forth. Usually really tedious crap.
As a newcommer you have three options. If you plan to trek it solo you can either grind your eyeballs out, and do minimal amount with other people for when you have to (some sorties like interception or so), you can dive in the community and hope to find folks who can help you (plenty of them btw, don't be discouraged), or if you have a friend with an established account have them bring you up to speed. When you have someone to help you, it will save you months of work. I'm not kidding. I gave my friends maxed mods like Serration or Redirection, which to a new player is a damn tall order to have. As well supplied them with spare nightmare/corrupted mods which can take time. Or give them some spare prime set of a warframe I have stocked etc. In short having a friend who is willing to help you bring you up to speed will help with the biggest shortcoming this game has. The eye gouging tedious grind. It's always gonna be there, but thankfully the core game is fun. Shooting♥♥♥♥♥♥is awesome, melee mechanics are satisfying as all hell, and when you get your hands on top tier gun (like say Tigris Prime) you will laugh maniacly as you chunk lv 100 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s by the hundreds and thousands.
So far I said very little on the actual game itself. In short it is simple. It's mission based co-op game. Each mission is usually randomly generated level with pre-set tiles (like diablo esque games are). With exception of defense type missions, where map is always gonna end up the same with several variants. You either play solo or with up to 4 people(Raid missions are up to 8 people, and are generally pretty fun to play). Enemies are usually plenty, either endlessly spawning, on a timer or numbered. You have one primary weapon,one secondary and melee. Each warframe gets four unique active abilities, and its own stats, bonuses etc. Here you go.It's simple, controls are tight and responsive, guns feel amazing, melee feels amazing, sense of power you can get is overwhelming at times, but you will work to get it. Everything will take time in this game. Learn to try to do multiple things at the same time. If you are farming for something, try to level something at the same time, and so forth.
This is a free to play title. So question is, is the 'free' part fair. Err yes, and no. For a new player I'd say you have months of work ahead if you wanna be up to speed, or at least on the current edge of things. For current players, absolutely. While DE does do unreasonable crap from time to time, they usually get it right and I don't have *too* many complaints. There are 'timed' exclusive content this game has. Bunch of it usually repeats (eventually), but time windows for some things tend to be tight. So say there is an event at one weekend, and you are too busy geting wasted in Vegas, your options are either trade for the item (and the warframe trading is no simple thing, economy exists in this game like many others like it), or you can hope the item gets reintroduced in the game at a later point. In very rare cases it doesn't (like Excalibur Prime).
In my case the game caused some compulsive hoarding behavior. New prime frame? I need to have it, because at some point it's gonna be taken out of circulation. New prime weapon? Oh snap it's amazing, I need it? New Stance? New Mods? Next thing I know I'm putting cosmetics on my warframes and playing fashionframe. Compared to the usual $60 price tag on an FPS, this game is well worth the purchase and I highly recommend buying the DLC.

So I've put a good 70+ hours into ARK, but wanted to wait for the launch version to give a review, and as such here it is.
So ARK as a game in and of itself is actually pretty good. It's your usual Survival formula with a dinosaur ecosystem around it, and it does the overall formula quite nicely for the most part.
The only downside to the formula is the developers seem to want to turn it into an ultra grindfest, with resource collection and anything related to the dinosaurs being *EXTREMELY* slow on official servers. It's tough to find any non-official servers that use the same rates, because they are so widely detested for the most part.
speaking of servers and content, the modding support seems to be impressive. There are developer-approved maps made by the community that are integrated into the game now, and they seem to want to pay modders to provide regular content to the workshop overtime, which is interesting and a good thing potentially.
For performance, I have to say the game has come a long way, though only very recently. It *was* a massive slugfest for performance but now, whilst still very intensive, it has become far more stable for framerate and it's overall system demands have come down somewhat. I run a GTX 1080 and i7-6700k / 16GB DDR4 setup, and at 1440p this game can hold a permanent 60FPS now with close-to-maxed settings, but it does sit at 90% GPU usage at almost all times.
On official servers, you also have a problem with Alpha-tribes; groups of players in large numbers who farm entire servers and force everyone else off regularly by destroying what little they can build (due to the aforementioned horrendous gathering rates). It's effectively impossible to play solo or in small groups on official servers, though unofficial does mitigate this I suppose (I'd say this is a bad thing because overall you are forced to ignore official content to get around problems it brings, which isn't a good thing imo).
There's also a singleplayer version, and it works quite nicely as you can edit any server stats to your liking, but there's also a "singleplayer settings mode" which makes solo-play far more user-friendly. The downside though is you will have to go file-editing to actually play the game properly, as you cannot actually unlock everything on your own otherwise.
Now, from everything above I'd probably give this a decent 7.5/10 worth it review, listing it as positive and that there's definitely good gameplay there. But there is simply one thing that brings this to a negative, maybe 4/10, review:
The Price.
I picked up ARK and its official DLC together whilst they were on sale. It cost me around £20 / $27.50 overall. At that price, it is totally worth it. The amount of content, the quality of the content, and now the performance too, made that pricing worthwhile.
At the non-sale old price of about £30, it was struggling to be worthwhile a little more, mainly due to performance, but overall it could be worth it.
Now the developers have raised the price to £50, and I for one can find no justification for it in terms of the value of what you will get. Given that the £50 does not incorporate their early-access DLC, and even if it did, there is no way the game has enough content and outright polish to be worth it.
You are getting a good game in this product, but it's a £30 good game, not a £50 good game. This game is as if Terraria wanted £34.99 for it's version 1.0 (Which is severely weaker than its updated versions after it went viral at £7.99).
Not here to hate, but I don't see this game *Ever* being worth that price, and it's a real shame.
Get it on sale and sale only.
UPDATE: I would like to add that on top of EARLY ACCESS DLC, they have added a $45 Season pass as well. You now pay over $130 to get all the content of this game, and $70 is basically the base-game and the early access DLC. Although the season pass is on sale for launch-day, it seems those of us who supported them by buying that DLC will not get any discount at all even though the EA DLC is in the season pass. Congratulations on throwing away consumer trust.

I played this game years ago. It was simple and fun. If you wanted something, all you had to do was devote a little time to farming it or pay money for it. I was a decent Mastery Rank when I quit. Enough to know that I'd done well with the time I spent. I would have highly recommended it back in the day. The lore is interesting and the weapons and warframes are very unique. Now, however, I'm telling you to pick a different game.
I recently created a new user and logged on. Now it's much more complicated and difficult to get anything you need. If you're up for a game that sucks the life out of you, this is perfect. You can't pick a weapon blueprint at random and know you'll get the materials in a couple hours. It could be a long time before you get to the planet that drops the resources requied. They've put a large number of warframe primes in the vault, which means you will never be able to build them ever again, unless the developers decide to put them back out for a bit.
Don't worry though, there are plenty of "common" warframes and "rare" ones out there that aren't primes. Of course, if you don't want to farm or brave the in-game economy, you can just pay more than a full game's price for a prime. No big deal there.
The community is great. It's fun to send enemies flying with explosions, pin them to the walls with bows, or just shred them with some AR you picked up and hopefully were far enough along in the game to not have to buy platinum to obtain it.
If you're into a game who's pros will never outweigh the staggering cons, then go for it. As for me, I've seen enough.

Initially, I downloaded this game out of pure boredom at five in the morning after I noticed a friend playing it. I looked at it, I laughed, and then just shrugged and hit download. I thought it would be stupid and something I would throw away after ten minutes, like most F2P games.
And here I am, over 100 logged hrs. later, still playing, and with no plans of stopping.
As boring as it looks at the start, it really does grab you and hold you to it. It farms gold for you when you log off, allowing you to go to work and come home to a nice boost to speed up your first playthrough, which is really convenient.
The mechanics (what few there are) are done exceedingly well. There's really no endgame but the drive to get to higher levels and unlock more heroes is extremely motivating.
Another aspect I love is the paid currency that every game has (rubies in this case). Its possible to get them simply through playing and purchase upgrades without spending any real money.
Overall, I'd say at least give the game a chance.

I'm going to try to keep this brief since I've played this game for a long, long time that I could probably write a ten page essay talking about its pros and cons in detail.  Warframe is basically a highly mobile third person shooter with powers.  It's also free to play where most in-game affecting stuff can either be bought or earned.  The only things you can't earn in-game, except through rare events like anniversaries or logging in for a hundred days, are inventory slots.
Now, I'd divide the game into two parts:  star chart and post-star chart.  The star chart is insanely fun to play through.  Granted, the new player experience is rough since so much isn't explained clearly, or not at all, in-game, pretty much forcing you to use the community (which is actually a pretty good one, IMO) or the off-site wiki.  For example, things it doesn't mention are that most regular Warframes drop from specific bosses, most weapon blueprints are market and clan tech rather than drops, and Prime stuff, which is upgraded regular stuff, comes from fissures.  There's also the early resource and credit grind being a big pain, especially without access to some of the planets that drop specific resources.  But get past that, as well as past the long craft times, and playing through the star chart and exploring the confusing and non-chronological storyline is great fun.
Then you clear everything and what's left?  Grinding.  For grind's sake.  I eventually got to the point where I started to wonder "Why am I still grinding?  To what end?"  I could do most Sorties, solo even if I didn't feel like rushing.  Few enemies were challenging and the ones that are were the ones with bullcrap mechanics (hello Scorches if they've STILL not been fixed yet!)  Basically, it was grinding up incremental power to make me kill stuff faster, or get mastery rank points from leveling weapons and warframes I didn't care for, to kill stuff even faster when I was already killing stuff fine.  This game is fun when you go through a mission at a reasonable rate and the enemies are a reasonable threat:  not too squishy and weak and not too ridiculously OP or bullcrappy.   But in the end game, it's either one or the other and you're speedrunning because it's easy and boring and you just want the reward or you're speedrunning because holy crap this is bullcrap end it now.
So if it becomes that, why am I still recommending this?  Simple:  it's worth picking up for the Star Chart experience.  Early days are a pain, but the amount of fun playing the regular content is worthwhile.  Once you've seen and done all the non-repeatable stuff is when you should consider whether or not you enjoy replaying randomly generated missions with the same enemies over and over enough for the sake of it.
I had a lot of fun with this, but I'm done.  I've probably put way too many hours in as is and I've bled this game dry of everything it has to offer me.  DE's decisions over the past few months have also left me doubtful for the future of the game (hello Hema and Nidus), especially since they seemed focused on rushing to new and shiny stuff while leaving a trail of broken and unpolished content in their wake since they aren't putting enough time into anything, so I don't ever see me coming back to this except to casually mess around.  But most of my time with the game was still fun, worthwhile, and I don't regret it.
So, give the game a shot and get your fun out of it.  Just keep an eye on your wallet and how much time you're spending grinding.  And ignore the prime access and stuff, just wait for a 75% off platinum log-in reward if you want to dump money on the game.  I grabbed the $100 one for only $25 and, between that, trading for some more, and conservative spending and it lasted me through my entire excessive number of hours.

This is basically a grind/waiting simulator and has been for over 4 years.
I first played this game when it came out some time ago and back then it felt like a genuine game. The combat was fun, gruesome, and all-around it felt like there was a huge variety of things to do in the world itself. You could sit down for an entire day and just play the game and unlock all the systems, do some quests, and maybe during that time you found some warframe parts you could make and everything was awesome. I stopped playing for a while, played it senior year of highschool, and when I came back I did't even recognize the game I had once loved.
The new system for doing side-quests to unlock planets/systems was a horrid idea and never should have seen the light of day. All 100+ hours I had put in before became meaningless and I had to start from scratch to get anywhere further in the game. I kept logging on every day to get my daily reward, grind some more, build some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ weapon, level it up, log off, and do the same thing over and over again for over a month. The bosses don't even feel unique or satisfying to battle anymore. Theyre just another enemy you need to kill to POSSIBLY get a part that you need for something but then you gotta fighr them 12+ more times just to get the same part 6 more times over. The RNG in it is so infuriating I couldn't help but buy platinum just so I could play the game the way I wanted to play it.
And to make matters worse, all the new content is just terrible. Nothing feels unique anymore, nothing feels special or really satisfying to use, it's just all numbers ona screen that let you know how much faster you can farm. Even getting all the new content is nigh impossible because you need to do 1,000,000 things before it to even think about getting any of it becuase the new pre-requisites for getting anything in this game is just complete utter BS. For anyone new looking to get the cool new weapon that they really want to see in action, nope, sorry, play 400+ hours and you'll maybe get it.
As you can see, I've played over 300 hours in this game and have nothing much to show for it and honestly, I wish I could buy my time back that I wasted on this game.

Go do something, literally anyting else. Go even play ARK Survival Evolved or run around for 7 hours in DayZ. The communitty for this game is dying and everyone knows it.

So here we are on launch day, and I have to say Ark is... ok, first you need to know a few things.  I've never had any interest in playing on official servers.  I don't enjoy PVP enough to deal with strangers and trolling and so on.  I played single player, then about 5 months on a private server with friends, then more single player.  If you play on official servers, you're going to have a very different experience.
The second thing - I bought this game on a whim.  It didn't really appeal to me, but I was bored so I gave it a shot.  And it took over my life for the next few months.  It's huge.  Sprawling map, diverse creatures, secrets and tips and so on.  I fell in love with it and it's a great place for me to explore, build, grow, breed and have adventures in.
But your mileage may vary.  It's a huge game, so there are bugs.  Less than there were when I bought the game, but bugs.  The building system is incredibly powerful, but it's also painfully fiddly.  At this point I see the Structures + mod as essential.  There *is* an endpoint, but mostly you can ignore it.  Some things take a huge amount of time to accomplish, though most of those can be tweaked with server settings (assuming you're not on an official server).
Will you love this game?  I have no idea.  Plenty of people don't.  Some fall for it, play for hundreds or thousands of hours and then flip the table.  But I've had a really good time in Ark.  It's more fun with friends, it's a great place to set long term goals and massive projects.  But it works perfectly well solo.
And again, I've never felt any inclination to go near the official servers. I have some students who do, and their favourite moments sound like horror stories to me.
Is it worth the price increase?  To me, sure.  I've got 500+ hours on it, so if it's a pretty good investment.  Is the Scorched Earth pack necessary?  Probably not, but I love it (and plenty of my friends hate it).  The community at large is pretty passionate, sometimes toxic, often supportive.
So... should you buy it?  If you want to know if you should buy this game, first be sure what you want out of it.  find the right community (or start a private server with friends.  Or host games on your machine and have friends join you).  Do you want the thrill of starting as the always hunted underdog on a PVP server as you gather allies, make a huge guild and stomp on anyone who gets close to your resources?  Go official.  Do you want to have adventures with some friends? Do you want to find a roleplay community and build a life?  All of these are good reasons.
And ask yourself, are you ok with a game where everything is going to take time?  Where you have to set your own goals that may take weeks of real time play to achieve?  Where there may be bugs or the building system sometimes feels obtuse?  Where you might be eaten by a dinosaur you didn't see or fall off a cliff and have all of the things you were carrying be the other side of the map where you may not get to them?  Are you ok with breeding a high level mount only to watch it get killed on your first time out?  If this sounds frustrating to you, you probably won't enjoy Ark.  If it doesn't, give it a shot.

I take this game for what it is, a survival sim. You may die to a random dino, or some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ toxic player, or some problem with the server or game engine, or your internet may simply dip into slow enough speeds to dc you while youre flying 20 feet off the ground and you fall to your death and lose all your items. But that's life, both real and virtual. Everything is random and very seldom is it in your favor, but when it is, when you've established your base and have a group of dinos waiting to defend or gather or transport you by air or land or water to where ever you wish, there's no better feeling. Sure it's quickly replaced by anger and frustration when you get raided, but then you find a new, more secluded place to make your base that you can set up with better countermeasures, both offensive and defensive. You change your tactics and learn and survive, and I believe that this is the point of games like this. You either survive, or you die (or uninstall), and it truly is survival of the fittest. I've never been part of any alpha tribes, but i've spent several nights running around with 1 of my buddies, living under the shadows of giant metal bases, stealing from them when we could and hiding when we couldn't until we could take to the seas and start raiding the smaller shore bases with our two man pirate crew and c4. These were some of the best gaming experiences I've ever had and I'll never forget my times in early access. I look forward to launch and hope that the betas stop flooding ark with negative reviews because this game should not be punished because some players either don't have a rig that can run this game the way it should be, or simply can't survive. We'll see you guys out there, even if you don't see us.

So I'm 1050 hours in warframe, bugs come and go but theres a new terror coming and I hope it never does. Now I'm going to begin this review with a note: If you are a lover of warframe or a hater of warframe, make your opinions true and not false don't defend warframe souly because you love it at least point out it's issues before attacking a hater or a destiny player because it makes us as a whole look stupid the white knights of warframe open your eyes because warframe isn't a perfect free to play game, far from it actually. So let's get to the review, warframe is a free to play game with you a badass space ninja fighting off 3 enemy factions corpus, grineer and infested. The game starts you off brand spanking new and explains some of the mechanic's but not all of them, I am glad that Steve played through it and thought it would be nice to add more explanation's for the game itself so the devs are constantly trying to make the game better for the new players but it's still rather hard to get invested in warframe when you're a new comer. Warframe is a great third person shooter with awesome parkor mechanics and beautiful visuals for a free game, their gun designs are nice but some them just look disturbing like the "Hind". Warframe is buggy but not all players run into them but the Devs make quick fixes and stay active when they make new content like during christmas they got updates out left and right fixing things quickly before they left for vaction which is fantastic they risk vacation time for their community. Some of the parkor can be glitchy at times and sometimes get you killed for example jumping towards a box at a certain angle stops your character so he latches on and does a cool spin flip on it but it wastes time when you're doing a survival. The Lore is kinda lackluster with a lot of the story locked behind symaris targets as one youtuber of warframe had to do them all just to get the lore since he's like a lore channel or something? Warframe also has a vast amount of melee weapons that each have their own animations and badass take downs which is always refreshing to watch. The warframes themselves aka your character a lot of them are well balanced and fun to play with but others are just lack luster and need some good reworks to em like Mag, Hydroid and oberon but oberon is nice where he is at. The quests in warframe in the beginning were freaking amazing! a new character after you finished a certain characters quest teaching us his history and how became the thing he was it was so well done. But recently their quests have been getting lack luster and reptitive and don't even give you the full character instead it was a pay wall or farm for the character but you didn't know where you got the parts until it was data mined. We have been getting some really weird power creep weapons as well lately with tigris prime and galatine prime being a thing. Warframe Isn't pay 2 win but it almost feels like it when they give out weapons like those because the new relic system is nice in some ways. But the fact that there are just so many relics make's it a tedious job to get the stuff you want so they have a prime access which costs 40 to 60 dollars for everything that's just mental it's like purchasing a new game when all you bought was just 1 weapon and a character. But everything is free if you're willing to farm...well not everything is sadly. Warframe has awesome events from time to time but if you miss them as a new player you can't get the rare mods or event specfic mods that came out during that event, and if that event doesn't come back you will never be able to enjoy the event and the mods in it. Which is honestly rather sad because maiming strike is one of most useful mods for a lot of crit melee builds and its locked behind a event or 1000 platinum the in game currency(trading of course). The community in warframe is always willing to help out new players espeiclaly me so add me if you want help! Warframe also has raids that are alright I guess but the rewards you get for completeing them is just sad. You get credits and 1 arcane and it can be a crappy one or an amazing one but you can play the game just as well with out em so Raids are pointless besides the amount of credits you can get. And credits will be the one thing you need the most resources to craft weapons are easy to come by. Also if you hate waiting to use new gear when you get it well you have too, it's not long usually a day or less but wanting a new character you need to wait 3 days. Not in game time btw an actual 3 day wait or pay for them to get done faster. One of the most time consuming characters to get is equinox because shes a 9 day wait basically because she has 2 seperate bodies that take 3 days each. Warframe has also been getting a lot of weapons recently that are just reskins of others or are just worthless like dark dagger and dark split sword, the jet kusar has the same crit stats as the atterax and so on. But recently we got the best weapon pack I have ever seen the Arca pack, they're badass and powerful and entierly free like everything in the game! But be warned if you like costmetics you better have the money because you need to fork up some good old green to be beautiful in this game. So on a last note, warframe has gotten a lot better over the years and I wish people wouldn't be hypocrits about it because warframe back then during first release was just meh and now look at it! it's amazing in all these different ways but also bad in different ways, like most games no game is perfect unless its KNACK 2 BABY BEST GAME 10/10 JUMPING CUT SCENES! But on a serious note open your eyes people and stop defending stuff that doesn't need it because if we constantly do it, things will get worse. Look at the nidus quest! Also yeah this game is super grindy, like really grindy.

I will start with this: If you don't have this game, get it. With the exception of maybe Dota 2, its without a doubt the best F2P game on Steam. You're missing out.
Nearly 1.5k hours in (some of it was logged before it was added to Steam) and I feel like its finally time to write a review.
I've been with DE/Warframe since the very, very early beta, and god damn they have come far. I am so proud of them as a developer, actively listening to the community and constantly updating the game with new features and eye candy to spend your hard (bought) platinum on. Of course, its not all sunshine and kubrows. There have been a few 'questionable' choices made to the game, but with community feedback (totally not screaming and cursing on the forums) and hard work, 99% of the nonsense has been fixed. The game it has become is barely recognizable from when I first started playing, and thats a good thing.
The business model is absolutely fair, you don't have to buy a single thing at all (apart from Tennogen fan created skins, which are purely cosmetic). You can instantly unlock in-game items and cosmetics with 'Platinum' which is bought with real (Steam) money, but you can also obtain that in game for free, albeit more slowly. There is a daily chance to get a 20%, 50% and 75% discount though, which is quite frankly amazing. Some people will argue and say that the farming is ridiculous, but it really isn't. Once you have max level gear, which takes about 2 hours give or take, you can do almost anything, farm anywhere and get as many resources as you need. My only qualm would be the things you can only get from time-limited alerts (Nitain Extracts, Vauban, etc.) but if you play, they will appear more often than you think.
At the end of the day, I don't regret a single dollar or hour I have spent on this game.  I actually wish I had've spent more at the start to get Excalibur Prime, who was only available for beta players that pledged a certain amount, kinda like a Kickstarter. I can see myself playing this for many, many more years and I can't wait to see what DE have planned in the future.

The best way to sum this game up is to say that its primary function, melee combat, is buggy beyond repair. Blocking is utterly useless; coming off of a block if you attempt to strike you will almost always do so at a slower rate than your opponent whom you just blocked. For this reason it is more feasible to just use the light clas with dodging and use something like a dagger the entire time. That dagger will block even the hardest of two handed weapon strikes, and then you can dodge and stab them while they recover. All of the weapons all also have roughly the same range regardless of what it actually says. Countless times I have swung my spear and missed only to be hit by the very person I missed who is using a short sword. To even get a hit you also have to sprint as you swing or you basically might as well go home. Stabbing is also probably the slowest attack method. A thurst is always faster than a swing, but not in this game. While using a spear it is easier to swing it like a baseball bat than it is to stab with it. The game is just overall bad, and it's poorly executed. It is also very poorly optimized and probably won't run very well for you.

I looked back on this review and, I was wrong. I've been playing Warframe for nearly 3 years now and I have to say, it's better than what it was. The Plains of Eidolon update made the normal objective cycle feel interesting, splashing in a different objective into each bounty! I take issue with Focus 2.0 though, it just feels lacking. But my absolute favorite part of Warframe now is that you can build your own melee weapon with the new Zaw mechanic. In Ostron, you can purchase blueprints using standing you gain from bounties with a merchant to build pieces of a Zaw, you can choose almost every detail of the weapon! From making a Speedy status weapon well suited for Condition Overload or having a Berserker Build on a fast Zaw meant for criticals! The possibilities are (nearly) endless!
Customization used to be my favorite part of Warframe, it let you change the way your Warframe looks to differentiate you and another Tenno using that same Warframe. Digital Extremes, while their policies are garbage, try their best to make a fun and enjoyable experience. They've worked almost as tirelessly as the TF2 team to make the game as bug free as possible and that's something I respect.
If you enjoy Destiny or Destiny 2, You'll absolutely love Warframe. It's story and lore are interesting and it's gameplay is mobile, unless you're defending a stationary objective, you're always moving about. Bullet jumping across large gaps to reach an enemy just out of melee range. Getting to a vantage point to make Sniping actually half decent. Running across the battlefield in Hysteria as Valkyr clawing through every enemy that gets in your way. It's all an enjoyable experience. You may get burnt out after the grind but come back in another month and You'll probably be ready for whatever new content DE decides to put out.

I have put in almost 1000 hours at the time of writing this, and I have read other's reviews on DE's game.  I have seen people complain about it being pay to win, that it is grindy, and there is not much variation in gameplay.  This game is not perfect, and if you're looking for a perfect game, go screw yourself. You will literally NEVER find a perfect game.  This game very much does have its flaws, but despite those flaws I still really enjoy playing this game.  It is not a pay to win. You can get everything in game if you are willing to put in the work, but this does mean you will have to grind.  Each weapon and Warframe has its own feel and playstyle, so people that complain about it lacking variety are just using the surface mechanics of the game.  There is PvP for those of you that enjoy it, it isn't perfect, and I prefer the PvE, but that's just me. But if you play this game and focus on the mechanics of play, you are missing a large portion of the game. There isn't much in terms of story, and for most people that is fine, but the lore runs deep, and the story, for what little there is, is spread amongst several important NPC's as well as the Tenno. This is a great example of throw some vauge stuff against the wall and let the player's minds fill in the blanks working.  But even that is not what keeps me coming back day after day.  I have made friends playing this game, and the community will welcome anyone who needs help with open arms.  There are a few people that "forget" that they communicate with other people, but every game does. When you first find that person that you just click with in play, and then you get into a clan and all of a sudden you have people that care if you are having fun and what your in game goals are.  The majority of the people I have met playing this game still don't know anything about my life, but they are there if I come in and play more aggressivly. And they will know that something is wrong. Yes the gameplay is fun, I mean YOU ARE A FREAKING SPACE NINJA, and there are a variety of weapons and frames, but you won't come back to that after nearly 1000 hours if you can't enjoy the people and the world.

I've been playing Ark since Early Access release way back in 2015. To be honest, the reason I haven't written a review over the past two years is because I've had very mixed feelings about the game. Sometimes I would love it, and other times I would feel like I've just been wasting time in an unfulfilling way. I think a lot of people flip back and forth with these feelings, and that reflects quite strongly in the reviews. I'd like to shed some light on how the game really is from the perspective of someone who has been playing for over two years now, and I want to elaborate on both the good and bad points.
Ark is for better or worse a first-person multiplayer survival game in a persistent world. The core of the game is to survive, build, and thrive in a prehistoric and alien ecosystem. That sounds incredible on paper, but the entire core of the game relies on two frequently contrasting conditions...
1: The game needs other human players to have prolonged enjoyment.
2: The game's biggest fun-killer is other people.
To clarify, the game on its own will quickly grow stale when playing solo. The enviroment (for all it's dangers) eventually becomes docile once the player has tamed enough high level dinos and progressed far enough in building/items. At that point, the game grows stale very quickly. By playing multiplayer, other players fill that void by providing both good and bad interactions. Trading, player made server events, mutual goals, PvP, etc all make the multiplayer great! On a good server, you will literally have fun for hundreds if not thousands of hours played.
That all sounds great, but why #2 you might be asking? Why all these thousands of negative reviews? Well... that's because this is a first-person multiplayer survival game. Unfortunately, this sort of game tends to bring out the worst in people. A tribe that has grown to a certain point is basically unkillable by small/new tribes to the server. This tribe is called the Alpha Tribe, and every server has one. Some alpha tribes help new players out, but most will not. As they say, absolute power corrupts absolutely, and in a game that's this longterm, people take their powers a bit too seriously.
You'll find tribes that threaten, pressure, and destroy other tribes who don't stroke their egos. Sometimes you might play somewhere for months, and then one slip of the tongue causes these power tribes to destroy all your progress while you're offline. It's frustrating, and the constant push/pull of server politics can add so much stress that you stop enjoying the game. It becomes a second job that doesn't pay, and it can make you more stressed than a real job!
It's very hard for new (or even many experienced) players to tell the difference between a good tribe and a bad one. Most think of themselves as just and merciful too, which makes it hard to judge them at their word when scouting for a good server. The game is very fun, but new players need to find mature/established tribes to play with before jumping onto an official PvP server to truly have fun. The game's server politics rival Eve Online in many ways, and like Eve, you'll need people with experience to really help you get off on the right foot.
I hope this helped people! Good luck surviving!

I just want you to remember this while you read my review. I've never really enjoyed shooters (first person views aren't my thing) and I though this genre was boring (yea yea, hate me for this). I discovered Warframe through a friend and an article on PC Gamer. Because of its humble origins, I decided to try it nonetheless, even though it is a shooter game. I thought the game would be boring... I was wrong. Here are my pros and cons:
Pros:
The customization is insaaaaaane. There are a whole lot of warframes, weapons, and companions to suit your personal style. For example, I'm sticking to warframes that give me a lot of shield and armor stats, and I like to use a sword as a melee weapon, a machine gun as a primary weapon, and a silent range kunai as secondary weapon. Only thing that may irk you is the fact that to level up, you need to master EVERYTHING. This forces you to change your style a lot. This can be a good and a bad thing, depending on what you like to do. It's possible to keep the same configuration, but you'll never rank up (ranking up allows you to access to different armors, weapons, etc. and the community considers you a vetera if you hit 7-8 and upwards)
The community is nice. Everyone is there to help you and I haven't seen yet a person spamming - hating etc. another newcomer.
Missions are different. There are a few planets out there that offer you different types of missions with different types of objectives. You'll end up having your favorite and those you dislike a little more (Ex. I enjoy Excavation missions and dislike Survival missions). You can also participate in cooperation missions (alerts, fissure, etc.). There's got to be something that you'll enjoy.
The game is free!!! For what Warframe offers, compare to its nonexistent price, this game is by far one of the best F2P shooter - sci-fi game out there.
Cons:
New player experience sucks. I'll be honest about that and say it bluntly. When I first started, I found it a bit difficult to know where to go and what to do. I had to read a lot of guides (Warframe Wiki was so useful!) and ask around. Although, I had the help of my friends, I did spend hours studying what I wanted and what I had to do and where to go.
The P2P aspect of the game. You don't need to spend to enjoy the game. There are some things which irk me, though. You'll end up collecting a lot of warframes (the game's armors), weapons (melee, primaries and secondaries). You only have limited space (open slots) to keep them in your inventory. The game gives you 50 Platinum (the game's currency) at the start of the game, which you SHOULD spend for a warframe slot and a (few) weapon slots. For the beginning, the starting Platinum is enough, but as you get more hours in, you'll want to spend money. Now, I know the game needs money to maintain everything, but making slots exclusively P2P irks me personally.

Ark Survival Evolved:
I have finally decided to review this game after 8400+ hours of gameplay in early access mode.
Positives:
The game is a great idea. The way the game begins is tough… I mean really tough. It is a challenge to get started and anyone without any patience is going to struggle but I do have patience and to me the hard difficulty of this game was a real refreshing eye opener… but be warned it is not for the feint hearted. The best part of the game is the idea that you can breed your dinosaurs. This has been implemented in a really interesting way, where you can pool your breeding into achievable goals and breed out your favourite dinosaurs to have the stats that you have always wanted… but all this comes after you have set up a kibble base, and tamed great level versions of your favourite dinosaurs. I personally play on PVE and as you can see, for over 8K hours I have had a great deal of fun and I have met some fantastic friends in the community… This ought to be a great game, but there is another side to it that I have to address…
Negatives:
I am so sad to say this, because I have put so much effort into playing this game legitimately and have done my best to help create a wonderful community and support network on a great PVE server… however, the developers of the game have treated us long serving players with utter contempt. We have been completely mistreated, taken for granted, unrewarded, lied to, mis-sold to… under a cloak of awful communication and absolutely brutal and dire decisions that have kicked the games player base in the teeth. The scenario now is that the devs were going to cull the lowest 10% of ghost servers… and instead have decided to wipe over 33% of servers with medium traffic to consolidate their server lists and re-use these to plonk new servers on that do not have the same issues that the old servers had, and then to cap it all, any support for the old servers and the long serving players who play on those servers is to be canned so that we are on our own if we lose a character or experience any technical issues… This is a huge let down of the Ark gaming community, and sadly it is pretty irrelevant, because any support I have needed in my 8K+ hours has been utterly non-existent anyway. I reported a serious harassment case and followed every single instruction to the letter, and no action was taken against the wrong-doers. This was a shameful let down and completely spoiled my enjoyment of the game… The devs carried on doing little tiny favours for a select few gamers whilst most tickets were left completely unattended. I have colleagues who lost their level 100 character in transit and not a single effort to answer the ticket was made, that was over 2 months ago now. The sad truth is, that this team of developers and community managers, is sadly the most useless and incompetent and uncaring team that I have ever experienced in a game… so if you have any issues playing this game… do not even bother to report it… nothing will be done… this Dev team do not care. They care that they receive your money… they will go on to look after the new servers and make things look as though they are prepared to provide support there… but it is as many things are in ark… it is lies and false promises.
Conclusion:
This game had SO much going for it… it was a fantastic idea but the execution of the game and the choices made by the developers has left a bruised gaming community feeling ripped off and mistreated, un-respected and un-supported… and sadly their actions and incompetence in how they run their business has led to this review being a vote of no confidence. The way the legacy servers are setup now means that over-time the old servers will lose players and get wiped, so either old players stick around on current servers and wait for the server to die, or we start afresh on a new server and wait to be lied to and sit having no confidence that one day these new servers wont be wiped themselves… and that is the finding of this review… that ultimately, there is no point in playing this game, because it provides 10% fun, 80% grief and trolling and a final 10% of crying into your coffee as you hope your dino baby survives over the next ridiculously badly timed update that takes away something else that used to be a good idea.
Do not buy this game… do not play this game… go and play something similar where the developers actually deserve your money.

Just a short simple review. Im not an expert >.>
+Game is fun, seriously you guys.
+Takes skill.
+Graphics are good, but still tolerable at lowest settings (IMO)
+There is a learning curve, and a "meta-game" (learning more "advanced" techniques), can clearly see the difference between Pros and Mediocre players (experience really shows)
+Variety of weapons and 4 classes to tweak gameplay
+DLC (that you sort of want but dont need.....no it's not free -_-)
+Community is good (the occassional idiots comes along & stands out, but they're few & far inbetween)
+Friendly Fire on (makes for more dynamic gameplay)
+Id imagine that, even after unlocking all weapons, you'll still play (at least casually) for fun or to better youself as a player
+Rank provides a sense of progression, abliet a weak sense of progression....
+User generated content...I think
+Music isn't annoying, repetitive maybe, but it's appropriate to the point where you don't notice it (which is a good thing) so it wont hamper gameplay, and you also wont be playing in dead silence.
+Can chop or smash certain body parts of enemies and comrades alike (even if they're dead and it's just a ragdoll). Note:If you wanna disrespect a fallen foe, bash his ragdoll's head in
+Hey look a beta
+(Moderately detailed) votekick to punish unruly players
+Well optimized
+ Ideal matches determined by collective skill & teamwork of the team
+Acceptable variety of game modes
+Not pay to win (microtransactions seem to be limited to cosmetics)
+Really easy to find a (near-full) match
+Can freely switch between 1st-person and 3rd-person view (So it isn't strictly first person)
+Classes & Weapons are balanced.
-Occassional abuse of Friendly Fire
-As with many games, players with higher FPS have a huge advantage (this is worth noting)
-Story only exists as an excuse for fighting (IMO)
-Bugs & Glitches, that you figure the developers are working on to fix (and trying their best, as far as circumstance allows) but will♥♥♥♥♥♥you off anyway.
-Small playerbase (IMO......at least at the time of my typing this)
- Maps & Game Modes can be repetitive (you'll probably still play, but just less, or in short bursts)
-Practice makes perfect, but ♥♥♥♥  "practice" is hard
-There is a chat function, but it's not the best, texts can obscure gameplay at times (though I suppose this is subject to change)
-Votekick prompt "can" obscure gameplay for 30 long seconds (also probably subject to change if Tornbanner wanted to)
-Matches sometimes determined by "who has the most players" (although this is expected, yet still annoying)
-Lot's of emtpy servers, combined with small playerbase (as I mentioned) can decrease your morale if you think too hard into it for too long.
-Community not very organized (likely due to size) so finding information, active clans, detailed guides, decent gameplay, or just socializing with community can prove to be difficult (relative to other MMO's)
-The "Chivalry:Deadliest Warrrior" DLC is ambiguos (again probably due to small player base).What little information you will find on it is either discouraging, or encouraging. Such contrast makes it tough to decide if you should buy it or not.
-Although there is technically what can be called a "meta-game", not much depth to gameplay, I think this is why most players don't seem to have a lot of hours on the game. Even dedicated players seem to end up playing casually. IMO
Well that's my simple review, this is all I can think of, will edit if neccessary (If I'm still alive when neccessary that is)

It's an idle/clicker game. You spend time either clicking, or not clicking, and have numbers go up. Then you reset to get bonuses and do it again for bigger numbers.
So why do I recommend it? Out of all the idle games, I like the fact that this one gives you more to do (if you want to click, there's ancients that give bonsuses to click power and skills, and if not, there's ones that give bonuses to idle mode), there's relics, and gilding (which give particular heroes a bonus to make their numbers bigger) so if you like min/maxing, there's a ton of math to do for it.
I like the cartoony art style, and I like some of the humor bits in the game. I like the fact they have seasonal events.
If you want an idle game to run while you're doing something else, this is a decent choice.

This game is my all time favorite. If you like ninjas in space, fighting, slashing and dashing, with amazing graphics and animations, then it's for you. The game has everything: great graphics, action all the way, amazing music and of course the incredible storyline. Although it's not a mmo in the traditional way, there's still a lot going on. The game is being constantly updated and fixed, you can also expect new content every month. People who love grinding and farming for weapons or warframes will love this game. There is a ton of customization for your warframes and weapons, too. It's a game that you have to give a shot, at least play through the first main quest of the game, because that's what really makes the game so special and makes you love it even more. That's at least how I got hooked, because the story is fantastic. If you ask if it's p2w, it's not. The only thing you really need to spend your money on are the cosmetics. I think a lot of players would agree with me. The game is perfect for beginners, because you have a lot to do, and I mean A LOT. The only downside is the endgame, because nobody really knows what it is or what it will be in the future, for me it is fashion, making your frames look badass, others like raids or sorties, which are daily quests that reward you with a lot of stuff. If you want a game that has a lot of action in it, just go for it. You won't be disappointed.
To sum up:
Pros: Fast-paced
Beautiful graphics
Not p2w
Awesome lore and storyline
Constantly updated, new content every month
Cons: What should I do in the endgame? (A question always being asked)
