So I'm 1050 hours in warframe, bugs come and go but theres a new terror coming and I hope it never does. Now I'm going to begin this review with a note: If you are a lover of warframe or a hater of warframe, make your opinions true and not false don't defend warframe souly because you love it at least point out it's issues before attacking a hater or a destiny player because it makes us as a whole look stupid the white knights of warframe open your eyes because warframe isn't a perfect free to play game, far from it actually. So let's get to the review, warframe is a free to play game with you a badass space ninja fighting off 3 enemy factions corpus, grineer and infested. The game starts you off brand spanking new and explains some of the mechanic's but not all of them, I am glad that Steve played through it and thought it would be nice to add more explanation's for the game itself so the devs are constantly trying to make the game better for the new players but it's still rather hard to get invested in warframe when you're a new comer. Warframe is a great third person shooter with awesome parkor mechanics and beautiful visuals for a free game, their gun designs are nice but some them just look disturbing like the "Hind". Warframe is buggy but not all players run into them but the Devs make quick fixes and stay active when they make new content like during christmas they got updates out left and right fixing things quickly before they left for vaction which is fantastic they risk vacation time for their community. Some of the parkor can be glitchy at times and sometimes get you killed for example jumping towards a box at a certain angle stops your character so he latches on and does a cool spin flip on it but it wastes time when you're doing a survival. The Lore is kinda lackluster with a lot of the story locked behind symaris targets as one youtuber of warframe had to do them all just to get the lore since he's like a lore channel or something? Warframe also has a vast amount of melee weapons that each have their own animations and badass take downs which is always refreshing to watch. The warframes themselves aka your character a lot of them are well balanced and fun to play with but others are just lack luster and need some good reworks to em like Mag, Hydroid and oberon but oberon is nice where he is at. The quests in warframe in the beginning were freaking amazing! a new character after you finished a certain characters quest teaching us his history and how became the thing he was it was so well done. But recently their quests have been getting lack luster and reptitive and don't even give you the full character instead it was a pay wall or farm for the character but you didn't know where you got the parts until it was data mined. We have been getting some really weird power creep weapons as well lately with tigris prime and galatine prime being a thing. Warframe Isn't pay 2 win but it almost feels like it when they give out weapons like those because the new relic system is nice in some ways. But the fact that there are just so many relics make's it a tedious job to get the stuff you want so they have a prime access which costs 40 to 60 dollars for everything that's just mental it's like purchasing a new game when all you bought was just 1 weapon and a character. But everything is free if you're willing to farm...well not everything is sadly. Warframe has awesome events from time to time but if you miss them as a new player you can't get the rare mods or event specfic mods that came out during that event, and if that event doesn't come back you will never be able to enjoy the event and the mods in it. Which is honestly rather sad because maiming strike is one of most useful mods for a lot of crit melee builds and its locked behind a event or 1000 platinum the in game currency(trading of course). The community in warframe is always willing to help out new players espeiclaly me so add me if you want help! Warframe also has raids that are alright I guess but the rewards you get for completeing them is just sad. You get credits and 1 arcane and it can be a crappy one or an amazing one but you can play the game just as well with out em so Raids are pointless besides the amount of credits you can get. And credits will be the one thing you need the most resources to craft weapons are easy to come by. Also if you hate waiting to use new gear when you get it well you have too, it's not long usually a day or less but wanting a new character you need to wait 3 days. Not in game time btw an actual 3 day wait or pay for them to get done faster. One of the most time consuming characters to get is equinox because shes a 9 day wait basically because she has 2 seperate bodies that take 3 days each. Warframe has also been getting a lot of weapons recently that are just reskins of others or are just worthless like dark dagger and dark split sword, the jet kusar has the same crit stats as the atterax and so on. But recently we got the best weapon pack I have ever seen the Arca pack, they're badass and powerful and entierly free like everything in the game! But be warned if you like costmetics you better have the money because you need to fork up some good old green to be beautiful in this game. So on a last note, warframe has gotten a lot better over the years and I wish people wouldn't be hypocrits about it because warframe back then during first release was just meh and now look at it! it's amazing in all these different ways but also bad in different ways, like most games no game is perfect unless its KNACK 2 BABY BEST GAME 10/10 JUMPING CUT SCENES! But on a serious note open your eyes people and stop defending stuff that doesn't need it because if we constantly do it, things will get worse. Look at the nidus quest! I also feel like the Raptor boss on Europa is too difficult for players when they first meet it. They have no easy access to plastids, and often are only Mastery Rank 4-6. It is a huge steep curve in difficulty, that only rockets back down to the same consistency the player is used to as you progress onto Saturn and beyond.
Otherwise give this game a try, play solo or in public matchmaking. Even better if you have some friends to play with.

ARK has everything, what makes a great game in my opinion.
It has a very cool setting, you as a player wake up, completely naked at a beach, not knowing whats going on. It reminds me of the last Predators movie. The atmosphere is really intense, especially at the first couple hours before you manage, to get a decent mount. The survival aspect of the game diminishs over time, although it alters from hostile dinos to hostile players on pvp.
There are many cool features integrated, which helps, keeping the movitation at top level, from the ways to travel arround all the maps over the traversing between the maps, caves, bosses, lots of loot, , many dinos to discover and tame, an interesting, although very thin story which is intended, to keep things together. Overall a great game, especially if you bought it prerelease price with the downside of many bugs and a not optimized game.
The negative aspects are, that the game in its actual state has not gained a lot of performance. The rise of performance was directly consumed by all the lightning and graphical effects on the new items, so it stays almost the same as it was at the beginning of ark. Next and most important thing, that cannot be stressed enough. Noone in the dev team plays their own game. It sounds ridiculous, but I and many others have no other explanation, why most of the recent decisions where made contrary to the by far bigger part of players opinion. They are completely out of touch with their playerbase, let alone their game. There is a suggestion thread that rarely gets attention. Doesn’t matter, if ist about basic issues like linux / mac clients, balance issues, bugs, balancing decisions ranging between ‚worthy a discussion‘ and outright stupid, hardhanded cuts of game mechanics, finding silly excuses for design flaws and programming skills, the list goes on and on.
TL;DR: Great idea and in the beginning a great game, but an awful dev-company, which tries to cover their lack of proper community managers, soft skills and bad decision with events. Also very bad: the companys idea, of the free time, average bob has to spend for games per day/week/month.
All in all, it was a great game once, but not at the current state.

I love the game and really appreciate that they are trying to keep the Linux version up w Windows.
Many servers online if you prefer that kind of play. I prefer private server as I am not interested in competing against others for building locations, resources or physically.
I find the depth of detail in the world amazing. The physical features of trees, water, cliffs, caves, deserts, forests... Huge range in scope of the biomes. Sometimes I just turn on "leavemealone" (cheat so the dinos do not see you and therefore don't attack) and just wonder around the map. Jump on a flyer and you can do it quicker but you miss all the ground level items and details.
Its a lot of found exploring the varied personalities of the different dino species and learning what they can do. Some are rideable, some are great at collecting resources for you, others are good to protect you, others are just big carry a lot and don't die as you try to get back to base.
I have been using the early access version for close to a year. A few quirks over time, but mostly all are fixed. Any "saltwater" currently looks gray from above in Linux. That glitch started early June and doesn't seem to have been worked on.  You physically can not see down through the water. This is a pretty big problem when you are near the water. Once under the water, it looks great. You can even look up through the water and see the sky. I guess the water surface is like a one way window. The fresh water rivers and lakes do not have this issue.
Setting up and running a dedicated server was easy. A GUI to do more would be nice. I do not play w any mods. I had the dedicated server running on a core2 Quad 2.73mhz, 10 gig ddr3 ram and a gtx 1050ti video card. I would also play on that same computer w my son (hours of father son building and exploring). I was worried that old CPU and small amount of ram would cause performance issues, but it did not. The gtx1050ti gave me roughly 30fps on medium at 1080. If near a large base w lots of dinos, it would dip below into the 20's. It was more than adequate for me.
The other maps really add to the variety. Certain critters are limited to certain maps. Same for some of the items you can craft (boomerang) and the resources you can find (cactus sap).
I'm really looking forward to the release and hopefully the Linux water glitch fix.

Got a lot of good and bad to say about ARK: Survival Evolved. We'll start with the pros first.
Pros:
+Absolutely beautiful game. The graphics on the landscape, the oceans, the sky, everything is just wonderful.
+The crafting system is really quite neat and can keep you going very long into a playthrough of ARK.
+The sheer number of different dinosaurs and animals on the island is staggering.
+The biomes are really quite nice and each comes with a challenge if you intend to build there.
+Exploration is always fun, finding all kinds of nooks and crannies, caves and ruins. There's a lot to explore.
+Fantastic to play with friends. Anywhere from one other person to ten others. It's just a load of fun.
Cons:
-Networking needs a lot of work done. FPS lag and connectivity issues are commonplace and can very well get you killed.
-Pathing for the animals is atrocious far more often than not. It can lead to cheesing some, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t from others.
-Exploration, while fun, is not very rewarding unless you are in the artifact caves.
-You can spawn and be killed before the screen is finished loading.
-Building needs some serious work to be done. It's clunky at the best of times, downright frustrating and difficult at the worst.
-The biomes are unbalanced. While some are full of infuriating and dangerous threats, others are marginally empty save for a few "smaller" predators, such as the Redwoods.
-$60 US for this game is a super hefty price tag considering the bugs, glitches, and networking problems.
Overall, it's a fun game. I'm glad I had gotten it a long while back when it was far cheaper. I cannot recommend anyone buying it with a $60 price tag, however, unless you've literally just got the cash to throw around.
Buy it at your own discretion. I'd highly suggest waiting for a sale to lower it again, even then I'd not spend more than $30 on it.

ARK has everything, what makes a great game in my opinion.
It has a very cool setting, you as a player wake up, completely naked at a beach, not knowing whats going on. It reminds me of the last Predators movie. The atmosphere is really intense, especially at the first couple hours before you manage, to get a decent mount. The survival aspect of the game diminishs over time, although it alters from hostile dinos to hostile players on pvp.
There are many cool features integrated, which helps, keeping the movitation at top level, from the ways to travel arround all the maps over the traversing between the maps, caves, bosses, lots of loot, , many dinos to discover and tame, an interesting, although very thin story which is intended, to keep things together. Overall a great game, especially if you bought it prerelease price with the downside of many bugs and a not optimized game.
The negative aspects are, that the game in its actual state has not gained a lot of performance. The rise of performance was directly consumed by all the lightning and graphical effects on the new items, so it stays almost the same as it was at the beginning of ark. Next and most important thing, that cannot be stressed enough. Noone in the dev team plays their own game. It sounds ridiculous, but I and many others have no other explanation, why most of the recent decisions where made contrary to the by far bigger part of players opinion. They are completely out of touch with their playerbase, let alone their game. There is a suggestion thread that rarely gets attention. Doesn’t matter, if ist about basic issues like linux / mac clients, balance issues, bugs, balancing decisions ranging between ‚worthy a discussion‘ and outright stupid, hardhanded cuts of game mechanics, finding silly excuses for design flaws and programming skills, the list goes on and on.
TL;DR: Great idea and in the beginning a great game, but an awful dev-company, which tries to cover their lack of proper community managers, soft skills and bad decision with events. Also very bad: the companys idea, of the free time, average bob has to spend for games per day/week/month.
All in all, it was a great game once, but not at the current state.

This is a very fun multiplayer game. It's a first person slasher set in a medieval setting, with two rival factions battling over a fictional kingdom, the Agatha Knights and the Mason Order. It offers a variety of game modes such as Deathmatches, Duels, Last Man Standings and even Objective based modes.
There are 4 character classes that you can select from and level up by scoring kills. As you level up you will unlock more weapons for each class and some neat armor customization options that unfortunately are pretty limited. A problem I had with the game is that the archer class is way underpowered compared to the other three and requires a lot of skill and effort to be able to compete with the others
The gameplay is fun, accessible and really violent. Nothing's better than charging and beheading the guy that stabbed you in the back before. Each weapon is also very authentic and realistic so you can feel the weight and power of each hit. Also, unlike other multiplayer only games like Counter Strike, Chivalry is a lot more easier to get into and you won't always be dominated by more skilled players since the game is fast paced, wild and unpredictable.
While the game offers a decent tutorial to make you familiar with the combat mechanics. The single player modes where you can pit yourself against bots for practice are really lackluster. Not all maps are available and the bot AI is terrible. Also sometimes the game may present some annoying bugs but luckily Torn Banner Studios updates the game constantly and is quick to fix any major issue
Finally there is Steam Workshop integration for the game so you can download extra maps, skins and modes created by the community
If you want a fun multiplayer game that doesn't require hundreds of hours to be put into it just to feel competent, Chivalry is strongly recommended.

The Good:
Since I am not recommending this game, I'll start with the good.
- The Team Objective game mode is simply great. Lot of fun and it's possible to contribute even if you are completely new.
- The combat mechanics are pretty good.
- Overall not a bad game IF you manage to overlook the BS.
The Bad:
- The aforementioned good combat mechanics also introduces some problems. Firstly, it is just too heavily dependent on ping. Normally it is not such a big deal but you'll know when the servers start drying up. And then there is something which is known as "exploiting" to some, while the others call it "taking advantage of the mechanics". Eitherway, it is rather irritating to see someone move in the most unnatural way possible and hit you before you even see the weapon move.
- The archery is the the weakest part of the combat, if we exclude the javelins.
- The community is not all that great. Now it's in no way the worst out there, but it's still pretty bad. I am not talking about the team kills and such but when you hear "You are being kicked because you are a n*gg*r", you know you have a problem (DISCLAIMER: This was not directed at me and this is not the only basis of my opinion, just an example). I have never seen a veteran player give any constructive advice to newer players except the occasional "stop hitting me noob". Some may argue that i was just unlucky with my choice of servers but hey, random sampling is a legit method of statistics.
The Ugly:
- OMG THE BUGS.....This game is broken to the point that the two methods of character progression DONT WORK. The two being unlocking weapons and leveling up. When i say they dont work, i mean they literally dont work. If you gain a level or two in a match, you'll see that number reset back to where it was in the next one. You may be lucky enough to unlock a weapon or two but the counters just give up after that. I know there are way to edit some files and stuff but that should never be the case for a game that is over a year old. There a hundred other bugs from the mildly annoying to game breaking, but i would rather not go on a rant.
- Identification of Friend or Foe (IFF). In a game where your allies take the same damage as your enemies, this feature is rather important. You have a small dot at the centre of the screen which if exactly place on another player will turn BLUE (friend) or RED (foe). Also at the bottom of the screen you will see the name of the player in BLUE (Agatha) or in RED (Mason). Keep in mind that the two colours are unrelated. Given that you may get autobalanced to the other team more than once in a match, all this is a recipe for some nerd rage. And dont come at me with "you're just a noob", I have seen veteran players making the same mistake.
- FInally the worst thing that can be said about an online competitive multiplayer, THE DEVS DONT SEEM TO CARE. In spite off all the problems, the devs blessed us with new helmets which cost about  $4 or something. THe amount may or may not be accurate but there is certainly a real money value to them. I personally couldn't care less. These kind of things make some sense in a game that looks good.
You can hear more about the good thing and the not so good things on the steam forums, which you should definitely check out if you want to buy.
TL;DR: Buggy as hell. Buy if you own a couple oil wells or something (or wait for heavy discounts XD)

Short Version: Warframe is a good Third-person Free to play with great combat and decent variety, fair business model but can suffer from grind and repetitive gameplay. Still worth your time and you’ll get some fun experiences and moments out of it.
Long version: I don’t like usually playing online but this game intrigued me enough from some videos and looked cool plus I can play solo. I will say the learning curve and experience was quite the challenge. A LOT of game mechanics and other items were not explained or mentioned in the tutorial like Mod Fusion and it took wiki searches and youtube videos to figure out aspects of the game. Also after the tutorial was done I didn’t know quite what to do or if this was just a system of open gaming that I’m not used to.
The combat is fantastic. Weapons have different feels to them, and different characteristics. You can combo different movement and melee strikes to perform multiple and different attacks which especially with a stance can be a great pleasure to watch and experience (Nothing like smashing everything with a mace or spinning around slicing up foes with dual swords).
Also for a good portion of the missions while the objectives are simple you can decide if you want to go stealth or with guns blazing or a combination of the two. Most mission objectives involve you killing enemies and performing variations of tasks such as taking a component to specific locations, protecting points on the map or eliminating targets. You can decide how you want to approach a mission depending on your warframe choice.
There is also a flight mode called Archwing which is neat but is not as polished as the rest of game and doesn’t get updated very often. The missions and alerts are far in between and would like to see this updated and expanded as it shows promise.
The games sense of progression is decent as you can accomplish a fair amount if you sink in the time with getting new upgrades to customize your warframes, weapons and companion units. There are also quests and some lore options they added to help you explore the universe that reward exploration.
Almost everything in the game you can get for free if you put in the time. Warframes, weapons, companions, mods everything. The only thing that you’ll need to pay for are cosmetics, or community made content. It can take a LONG time to get a warframe depending on the one you want so be sure to look up where you need to get parts for it via the wiki. Otherwise if you really want it now you can just buy it outright.
My griefs about the game is that it can be bit repetitive with certain quests and missions asking you to perform similar to the same tasks over and over again. This can be frustrating if the task is a long one and you’re doing it solo. You can get far  on solo but there are some modes and quests that are better with a team. Often you’ll have dome something 3 times to get the reward or the option to build the reward wether it be a weapon, a component or a quest item. I feel like the Titania Quest was the best compromise on this and while it had repetitive tasks I always got the sense of progression instead of being stopped doing the same mission over and over to get a part or a blueprint.
I’ve recently slowed down my play and actually taking a break from it. Which after the amount of hours and a 1 year for a free to play game is actually really solid. The developers are always updating and applying fixes so I easily see myself coming back for the new content. They have greatly improved the new player experience so the issues I mentioned earlier have been made easier for players to understand and more obvious.
I would say if the game looks cool to you and fun, it is and it is worth your time. Even if after first quest or couple of planets is all you play the environments and levels are fantastic (Uranus I think has the best in terms of level eye candy and reminds me of  Bioshock). They’ve added a LOT more content to the game since I started so as this continues this game has a greater and greater value especially for the price of a free online account.

This is the best game that gets worse with every upate.
When I first purchased this game, it was amazing. Didn't run well on my machine because of poor optimization, but it was a lot of fun. A friend made a server for a few of us and we went around taming everything that the devs added to the game. It was a joy and a challenge to grow our collections and obtain the highest-level and coolest looking of our most favored beasts. We built bases in hard-to-live-in locations, relying on our teamwork and our tamed dinosaurs to keep us safe from increasingly deadly predators. It was gloious and so, SO much fun!
But times have changed and ARK has changed with it. The developers have decided to focus on the PvP aspect rather than having fun with friends. This is in spite of the fact that ARK isn't even a blip on the eSports radar right now, and to my knowledge never has been. Creature balance is determined by compeditive advantage rather than what makes for an enjoyable experience in the survival game. Sadly the devs can't bring themselves to just make two different stat blocks, so those of us who enjoy going out and taming dinos with our friends are feeling slighted that things are getting frustratingly difficult in places. Just ask anyone who's tried to obtain a wyvern both pre- and post-flyer nerf. ARK was always challenging, but the nerfs have turned that into almost punishing in places.
Other changes have likewise taken a lot of the fun out of the game. Taming the newer creatures is frequently frustrating as many of them are tamed using the exhausting and aggrivating 'passive tame' method. This method means that hours of work can be destroyed by seconds of server lag. This is the antithesis of fun. To add to this, the wonky and horribly unintuitive building system hasn't been improved or expanded on since the early versions. If you came to this game from something like Minecraft, which was popular at about the same time this was intitially released for public Beta, you were in for a world of hurt trying to make a half decent base. It's sad that this game's development has strayed so far from what made it fun in the first place.
If you DO decide to purchase this game, make peace with the fact that you're going to be using mods. The modding community for this game is FANTASTIC... and kinda has to be. There are a lot of glaring defficiencies in the vanilla game that need to be addressed, and the modders have done a spectacular job. While there definitely isn't a mod for every problem, it's pretty close. There's very little that I've really wanted to change that I can't find a decent mod for, which is excellent.
It wasn't long ago that this game was one of my favorites. I stopped playing it as much during the past year, and now I don't know if I'll ever play it again unless I get a WAY better computer (the optimization issues have never been fixed or addressed, even though it's close to release at the time of this writing) and even then I doubt it unless I can find a very well modded server to play on since the devs of the vanilla game seem to have no interest in improving the PvE experience I grew to love so much.
It's sad to see how things have gone for this once-beloved title. I pray that one day I'll be able to re-write this review just as I re-wrote the original in favor of this updated one. I'd love to be able to recommend this again some day. :)

On a serious note, this is one of the best free to play games I have ever played. You can aquire everything in the game (including Platinum) without spending any real money at all. The platinum you purchase with real money can get your access to certain items in a shorter amount of time, but by no means is it necessary.
My only suggestion for the game is a little more information from the game itself about the various currencies, mods, junctions, relics, mission types, etc. New players are often very lost as to what to do, or where to go or even how to do it. I also feel like the Raptor boss on Europa is too difficult for players when they first meet it. They have no easy access to plastids, and often are only Mastery Rank 4-6. It is a huge steep curve in difficulty, that only rockets back down to the same consistency the player is used to as you progress onto Saturn and beyond.
Otherwise give this game a try, play solo or in public matchmaking. Even better if you have some friends to play with.

This review is not based on the official servers, but rather on private servers where one can tweak the game to your own liking.
This is a really great game and has delivered hours of fun and despair. While the game can be fun, it can also be frustrating, but overall it is most enjoyable. The game delivers a brutal survival experience where everything is trying to kill you once you spawn, and at the early levels one really has to think about surviving.
The game has a great modding community where one can find lots of great mods. So if the base game feels empty and less challenging, one can get mods which enhances gameplay and increases difficulty. The opportunities become infinite with mods.
Combat can be both fun and frustrating. The mechanics aren't bad, but doesn't feel too realistic when you are being thrown around when attacked by a pack of wolves. The combat does feel somewhat balanced, and if not, one can simply just adjust the difficulty and damage to your own liking.
When it comes to graphics and performance; The game looks amazing with all settings maxed out in a 4K resolution, but performance could have been better. It does feel like the game is a bit too demanding for certain players, but this hasn't been a huge issue for the community on my servers.
While this review might be short and lacking at certain subjects, I would definitely recommend this game. I do not recommend playing on the official servers, but I do recommend playing on unofficial modded servers. Everything about the game can be tweaked if you're not happy with the standard settings.

so, here we are. a few years (i think a bit less than 2?) since the announcement, no longer in early acces (i will refer to this as EA) and yet something feels off...
oh wait, i know.
the price.
and yes, this is one of the (2, maybe more in the future) main points i will discuss here, so buckle up.
price
at first i belive it was about 30 euros? i think i bought it for less but i can't remember because it was such a long time ago. it was hardly worth the 30 at the time. at this point it would be kinda worth it, but they decided that instead of doing the rational thing and dropping the price like most games do when they come out of EA it goes up to double that. somehow they think that while this game still has many issues (mainly revolving around hitboxes and graphical glitches) yet they still thought it'd be okay to hang a larger price tag on it.
Content
So, contentwise it's more than worth it. 3 massive maps (4 if you include Scorched Earth) each filled to the brim with life, detail and graphic nerdgasms. it looks fantastic [note: i think they optimalised ark massively?] the dino's look full of life and when it comes to crafting and building oh boy is it deep. games like NMS are "vast like an ocean but deep as a puddle" meaning that they're large in size but lacking in content or things to do. ark is vast like an ocean and digs straight down to the planet's core (and claiming they've only scratched the surface i think you can see where this is going so i'll stop). most mechanics are well-thought out, work together (albeit still a bit glitchy) and feel right (even TEK feels fitting considering the alien nature of this game)
misc
something that i didnt feel like it fit in in any of the above is that dinos that are big feel big. if they walk, the earth shudders, if they roar, you get goosebumps and if they die you cry.

Clicker heroes is a game that seems worthless on the surface.  Pretty soon after you start, you don't even have to click, the heroes do all the work with their damage over time.  But then, they stop doing much damage, and the game reveals its gleaming hidden self.
This game is all about optimization.  What character do you level up, when?  Do you save up for a new hero, or do you put a hundred levels into one of the early level heroes?  Do you sacrifice your DPS to purchase passive buffs that will pay off later, or push to maximize your DPS now?
This game is addictive, but also doesn't swallow your life (at least it hasn't swallowed mine).  I leave it running while talking with friends, watching anime, even playing other video games.  It works in the background, and every few minutes (or even 20), I return, select new hero upgrades, and let it go back to killing bucketfulls of monsters.  Or, it can just be good for killing some time.
Even the paid content isn't bad, since the in-game purchaseable currency (rubies) can be acquired regularly.  (I've found over 300 rubies, where the most expensive things are 50 rubies).  I've started my own clan, purchased double damage forever, and purchased plenty of upgrades, and all without actually paying anything.
So overall, I definitely recommend this game, and am even playing it as I write this review.

Ark survival evolved had me at the start.  When it first arrived on early access, I got it primarily to try my DK2 out on, and the fact that they were supporting VR supposedly from the ground up, filled me with anticipation.  Many people will have shared my frustration and dissapointment, when the game turned out to be so poorly optimised.  However i struggled on when most people gave up, and upgraded my pc to monstrous proportions to continue playing.
The huge amount of money I spent eventually paid off and i actually played ARK survival exclusively on my dk2 totting up a total of 350 + hours entirely in VR!   So i think it's fair to say i gave it a fair crack of the whip!   Then disaster, they stopped supporting VR properly and in any case I sold my DK2 in preparation for the CV1 coming out.  Since buying my CV1 and upgrading my PC yet again, I waited and waited until the recent news that support for VR was back.  However re-installing and playing today dealt me a final insult.  It's still totally (and i mean totally) VR broken.  Like many other gamers have already said, the resolution in the hmd is screwed so i get a vomit inducing wavy line down either side of my peripheral vision.  The blinding sunlight which plagued the game since early on is still there!!! I mean WTF??   How many people need to complain about this before they do something and fix it?  There are still glitches everywhere and the game seems no more fixed (or VR ready) than it was years ago when it was first up for early access.
I have been a dedicated fan of this game, and supported it when nobody else would but now I think its time to throw in the towel.  Come on guys really!  How is this game ready to be released? and how can you say it's VR compatible? I work as an application developer and if i released something as broken as this I would be out of a job!
So much of this game is still broken, and not just the VR side of things.  What's worse about this though, is that everything that was broken when i stopped playing it about two years ago is still broken today!
Do yourselves a favour folks.  There are many survival games out there, and plenty of developers listening to their community.  Leave this one on the shelf and try a game that actually works properly.....

The most fitting way to describe Warframe to me is 'wasted potential'. It's tragic that this review is negative, since I don't dislike the majority of the game itself. The lore is quite interesting, the weapons are unique and varied, and the system with which you upgrade them leaves for a lot of tinkering and whatnot to fit your playstyle. The game itself isn't anything revolutionary, but you play as a robot ninja, and it usually feels as awesome as it sounds. This game has a lot going for it, so why would I condemn it with "No, I would not recommend"?
The heart of this game's progression is equal parts grindy tedium and RNG. You can circumvent this with in-game currency that you obtain with grindy tedium and RNG. Alternatively, real money. That said, you're doing yourself a disservice if you pay real money to skip the annoying grind, because the annoying grind is basically the whole game. It's grinding for things so you can grind for more things. Even if you somehow stick with it until you have everything you could ever want, the end-game content is, for the most part, exceptionally disappointing.
All in all, if you don't mind relying on repetitive slog and RNG for the vast majority of your progression, you will certainly enjoy this game more than most. Its own community is usually complaining about the design choices throughout, after all. On the other hand, if you were to spend thousands of dollars on this game, you'd be done and sick of it within a week or two. As for me, this game gets an unfortunate thumbs down.
As a side note, the devs for this game have been compared to the likes of Ubisoft for several instances of moneygrubbing scumbaggery that really shouldn't be present in any sort of self-respecting company, but that's a seperate issue.

Get. This. Game.
If you're into Medieval Warfare, like the title says, then you should definitely get this game. Archery, fencing, everything. This game is -the- game of the games. F*ck Skyrim, F*ck Mount&Blade. This game has the most realistic and perfect combat system I have ever witnessed. You can hit in five different ways; each attack and each weapon takes different damage, different stamina and different speed, so there are many alternatives to how fast/strong/lasting you want to be. You can block as much as you can with shields, but they lower your mobility, and the enemy can still attempt to sneak his sword around your shield, which you must try to prevent. You can also block with weapons, but only for a short second, which means you have to time it perfectly.
You constantly use fingers on your left hand, you constantly use fingers on your right hand, and you constantly have to be focused, have quick reaction and quick judgement as to what should be your next move. One second of hesitation, and you're dead meat.  It's not all bashing your way through the enemy; this game has some serious tactics. And all the while, you can have fun with guts and blood splattering around as you chop your enemy's heads and limbs off while using ridiculously awesome voice-commands.
I'm mostly into linear games, but considering that this game is only a competitive game.... 9/10.

Short Version: Warframe is a good Third-person Free to play with great combat and decent variety, fair business model but can suffer from grind and repetitive gameplay. Still worth your time and you’ll get some fun experiences and moments out of it.
Long version: I don’t like usually playing online but this game intrigued me enough from some videos and looked cool plus I can play solo. I will say the learning curve and experience was quite the challenge. A LOT of game mechanics and other items were not explained or mentioned in the tutorial like Mod Fusion and it took wiki searches and youtube videos to figure out aspects of the game. Also after the tutorial was done I didn’t know quite what to do or if this was just a system of open gaming that I’m not used to.
The combat is fantastic. Weapons have different feels to them, and different characteristics. You can combo different movement and melee strikes to perform multiple and different attacks which especially with a stance can be a great pleasure to watch and experience (Nothing like smashing everything with a mace or spinning around slicing up foes with dual swords).
Also for a good portion of the missions while the objectives are simple you can decide if you want to go stealth or with guns blazing or a combination of the two. Most mission objectives involve you killing enemies and performing variations of tasks such as taking a component to specific locations, protecting points on the map or eliminating targets. You can decide how you want to approach a mission depending on your warframe choice.
There is also a flight mode called Archwing which is neat but is not as polished as the rest of game and doesn’t get updated very often. The missions and alerts are far in between and would like to see this updated and expanded as it shows promise.
The games sense of progression is decent as you can accomplish a fair amount if you sink in the time with getting new upgrades to customize your warframes, weapons and companion units. There are also quests and some lore options they added to help you explore the universe that reward exploration.
Almost everything in the game you can get for free if you put in the time. Warframes, weapons, companions, mods everything. The only thing that you’ll need to pay for are cosmetics, or community made content. It can take a LONG time to get a warframe depending on the one you want so be sure to look up where you need to get parts for it via the wiki. Otherwise if you really want it now you can just buy it outright.
My griefs about the game is that it can be bit repetitive with certain quests and missions asking you to perform similar to the same tasks over and over again. This can be frustrating if the task is a long one and you’re doing it solo. You can get far  on solo but there are some modes and quests that are better with a team. Often you’ll have dome something 3 times to get the reward or the option to build the reward wether it be a weapon, a component or a quest item. I feel like the Titania Quest was the best compromise on this and while it had repetitive tasks I always got the sense of progression instead of being stopped doing the same mission over and over to get a part or a blueprint.
I’ve recently slowed down my play and actually taking a break from it. Which after the amount of hours and a 1 year for a free to play game is actually really solid. The developers are always updating and applying fixes so I easily see myself coming back for the new content. They have greatly improved the new player experience so the issues I mentioned earlier have been made easier for players to understand and more obvious.
I would say if the game looks cool to you and fun, it is and it is worth your time. Even if after first quest or couple of planets is all you play the environments and levels are fantastic (Uranus I think has the best in terms of level eye candy and reminds me of  Bioshock). They’ve added a LOT more content to the game since I started so as this continues this game has a greater and greater value especially for the price of a free online account.

This is a game that rewards patience, because there's no way to lose... there's just no way to win until you can.  That is, until you have the DPS needed.  You acquire damage per second based on the heroes you recruit, which you get by buying them with gold, which you earn by defeating monsters.  You get one gold per monster in the first level, and the first hero costs 5 gold, so you only need to kill 5 monsters.  However, each hero gets more and more expensive.  Fortunately, the amount of gold per monster killed goes up rapidly as you ascend the levels.  Unfortunately, every 5 levels is a boss level, and here is where you need DPS, because you only have 30 seconds period to kill the boss.  No matter how quickly you click, if you don't have the DPS, you don't have it.  It's never close: you either don't have it or you slaughter the boss with 10 or 15 seconds to spare.  All in all, this is a fun and highly addictive 'Idle' game.

The best recommendation I can give for this game:  This will quickly become my most played game.
From the Atari 2600 to today I have always been a fan of games.  In particular I love MMOrpgs and Rpg's as they tend to offer some of the best value (Money invested into hours of fun played).  This game has elements of Raiding, micro and macro management with a nice level up system.  There are three ways to play this game: Active (You click a lot or use a clicking program), Inactive (You let burn damage kill creeps) and hybrid (Inactive on mobs, active on bosses).  If you like a game you can get satisfaction from while multitasking, watching tv etc etc then this is possibly the best game you have never tried.  The game is cute and satisfying as you make deeper and deeper runs.  The game uses a soft reset mechanic where you go as deep as you can (As fast as you can) then reset and repeat with bonuses you can from varius level ups.  The best thing about this game is it is 100% FREE and you get rubies (In game currency you can pay for but do not need to at all) for buffs VERY fast.  The best way I can describe this game is a Raid game like wow mixed with a monster mashing slasher.  Without the aggrivaiton of playing with others =).  Even the guild system ONLY helps you never causing headaches.  If you are on the fence about this game I hope this review helps.

An impressive multiplayer game that throws you into chaotic medieval combat utilizing very satisfying fighting mechanics.
One of most entertaining melee games that I have had the pleasure of playing. You have the
choice to pick from four classes (archer, man at arms, knight, vanguard) with a variety of
weapons for each and sent to battle the evil mason rebellion or the noble agathian knights.
Now what makes this game great is the fightning mechanics. There is very steep learning curve in this game butincredibly rewarding once you start getting the hang of it and see the different strategies players use to win a fight.
The typical multiplayer game modes are utilized in this game including King of the hill, Team deathmatch, duel and Team objective. Team objective places you in war with one side defending and the other attacking by reaching objectives. The game packed with chaos and happy accidents (catapults wiping out an entire platoon) which makes
its replayability quite high.
The only negatives I can come up with are some issues with certain weapons and overhead swing that hurt you without completing the animation (only happens on occasion, the developers patch bugs) and a very limited amount of maps.
This indie project is a very impressive entry with good visuals and hilarious voice acting. If you enjoy epic battles and swordplay I highly recommend this game. I keep coming back to it even after investing hundreds hours into it!

There really is something incredibly satisfying about the look on an enemy's face after your bardiche comes down on his shoulder and he's left standing there minus one sword arm. Even more satisfying is subsequently planting a Sparta kick solidly on his chest and leaving him on the ground. Most satisfying is finishing him (at this point, he's already long dead, but this last step is absolutely vital) by using your sidearm mace to turn his head into a mushy pulp.
I only have a few problems with this game, mainly relating to armour being incapable of completely deflecting blows and a two-handed battleaxe being unable to chop through a wooden weapon handle, but overall this is a great game; lots of fun, lots of blood. Did I mention the blood? It goes everywhere. Your clothes get more and more bloody as time and murder goes on, and incidents of blue guys mistaking other blue guys for red guys and lopping their heads off are common. Still fun.
One thing though:
DO NOT buy this game if you experience more than 300ms of LAG on other multiplayer games. LAG SCREWS YOU OVER.
"Oh, well I live in ♥♥♥♥ing Antarctica, and I totally play CoD on the North American servers all the time despite my 1200ms of lag and I'm prestige 12 andblahblahblah" NO. YOU. WILL. DIE. That axe will be coming for you, you'll block it well within time, it'll magically phase through your block, and you will lose limbs. Check to see if your country has any local dedicated servers running before you buy this.

I have played this game off and on for the last couple years.  SO much has changed since I first started.  The dev time is excellent at making strides forward with Warframe. Something that impresses me alot is how they keep working on improving their current content while they make new content.  Whether they are polishing and improving the graphics, or sound, or reworking boss fights and making them more interesting, it seems like they work hard to improve what they have instead of ONLY focusing on new content.  The Dev's are VERY open too in their streams, discussing much of what they are working on.
This is my favorite free to play game, and if some other game catches my interest I always find my way back to Warframe and getting back into it.  The in game store doesn't feel pay to win AT ALL, especially since the best versions of things are recieved from farming (or buying off of other people).  The only thing you might have difficulty with if you choose not to spend any money, are extra Warframe and Weapon slots.  But there are ways that you can get items to sell players that will allow you to open up more slots, so you don't have to spend any real money if you choose not to.
Besides the awesome dev team, another thing i like is that they have been doing a REALLY good job adding story to this game. However, in practice it falls flat on the archery side of things.  The one thing that ruins this game for me and makes me feel as though it was a waste of my money is the fact that archers are at a HUGE disadvantage.  The horribly slow draw animation coupled with sometimes unplayable connection issues (players lagging all over the place and instadeath from people who were 20 feet away from me) make this game almost embarassing from an archery standpoint.  Where improvement could be made is to better balance the bows to make them a little more useful in a world predominantly populated by headless chicken like players running around swinging their axes wildly. The most fitting way to describe Warframe to me is 'wasted potential'. It's tragic that this review is negative, since I don't dislike the majority of the game itself. The lore is quite interesting, the weapons are unique and varied, and the system with which you upgrade them leaves for a lot of tinkering and whatnot to fit your playstyle. The game itself isn't anything revolutionary, but you play as a robot ninja, and it usually feels as awesome as it sounds. This game has a lot going for it, so why would I condemn it with "No, I would not recommend"?
The heart of this game's progression is equal parts grindy tedium and RNG. You can circumvent this with in-game currency that you obtain with grindy tedium and RNG. Alternatively, real money. That said, you're doing yourself a disservice if you pay real money to skip the annoying grind, because the annoying grind is basically the whole game. It's grinding for things so you can grind for more things. Even if you somehow stick with it until you have everything you could ever want, the end-game content is, for the most part, exceptionally disappointing.
All in all, if you don't mind relying on repetitive slog and RNG for the vast majority of your progression, you will certainly enjoy this game more than most. Its own community is usually complaining about the design choices throughout, after all. On the other hand, if you were to spend thousands of dollars on this game, you'd be done and sick of it within a week or two. As for me, this game gets an unfortunate thumbs down.
As a side note, the devs for this game have been compared to the likes of Ubisoft for several instances of moneygrubbing scumbaggery that really shouldn't be present in any sort of self-respecting company, but that's a seperate issue.

Let me start at the very core thing of the review for the mass who are lazy to read an entire text: the game is good, but not amazing as it used to be a long time ago.
I shall start explaining it further on by zeroing in on the fact that the grind (except for prime part grinds) got worse by the years. It's easier to farm a primed item than to farm it's normal counterpart which makes it a hella less enjoyable for new players to get into the game. Sure they improved the gameplay by a lot, by introducing riven mods, renewing the movement system for normal gameplay and archwing (for others it's a minus point, but for me a plus)
Gameplay wise it's great if you're someone who doesn't mind playing the same thing over and over again because of the challenge it creates as difficulter it over time, but even people like me tend to get tired of the game after a long while. I've been in the game since the alpha when the founders pack was still available and i will say that it's more focused on the action than on the actual farming part of the game.
The community is one of the best i've ever encountered in any game. Warframe is like the Canada (ironically DE is centered in Canada) of MMO's. You just join a clan and they'll all be helpfull to you and even tend to give you mods and primed stuff if you're nice like them. You can just chat with a random stranger in an interception run and add him at the end of the game. I think that that's the best part of Warframe and the main part that kept me going on in the game for 1.6k+ hours (call me addicted, but i see it as a good investment in a good mmo with a fun playerbase)
Now let me start with the movement mechanics. They're amazing to me. You just latch on to a wall and shoot up a bunch of enemies with your crit modded weapon (since critical chance is too valued in this game) or just jump over a group over enemies with your firewalker equipped warframe and run away from them while doing a roll mid-air that makes your warframe go like the flash. It's really fun and makes the game feel really high paced.
Now about the warframes. The warframes have been buffed and nerfed (or as DE calls it: "reworked") all the time such as Mag who has been turned into utter crap (except for her second ability). They are plenty powerful with the right setup, but you'll always have people crying for nerfs in the power struggle for the most kills in the game (i'm looking at you Ash). It has all been good up to the part when they randomly figured to mess the idea of "ninjas" up with a bard type warframe.
If you're someone who'd want to play this game for a short time between games to blast off some steam then i'd say "go for it", but as long as the grind is bad i'd recommend not putting all your time into this game despite it's amazing community and gameplay.

All in all, I can't recomend this game. I'm not gonna say I never have fun with this game, because I do sometimes, but most of the time its just annoying. It has potential, but thats not enough. Most of the time it just isn't fun at all, for me. I don't know of any other games quite like this one so I still play it, but I usually leave it in a bad mood. I don't know why I do this to myself.

I myself, wouldn't have started playing this game if I hadn't have a friend helping me and showing me around.
Pro:
+ Free.
+ Easy to install.
+ A lot of content, weapons, "warframes" and the such.
+ Good asthetics.
+ Good storyline.
+ Trading between players.
+ Good communication system, easy to leave a note to your friends.
+ A lot of customisations, weapons and other stuff can be unlocked through Alert-missions that usually have a lot of other players that can help you get them.
Contra:
- Archwing missions (Space and Water).
- Hard to learn without help.
- Slow progression without any help.
- Stuff locked behind a paywall.
- Stuff locked behind the requirment to join clan.
- Missions and enemies that require you to team up with players, unbeatable in solo. (Unless you're some kind of level 25+ Which will take ages to get there.)
- Everything requires in-game money to upgrade, trade or advance. Trading has a tax/fee on it and upgrading mods requires you to grind through hours and hours of gameplay to get enough resources together.

TL;DR: if you really want to play the game, stick to single player or unofficial servers, where you aren't held hostage of WildCard's terrible decisions.
The game itself is amazing, the problem starts, however, if you want to play online, specifically at Official servers...
I'd have recommended the game if it wasn't for the extremely terrible PR and Customer Service "provided" by WildCard, not even Brazilian phone companies are this bad, and they suck A LOT
Of course, the game was at Early Access, bugs are expected, and we expected them to be fixed, which they weren't, dinos fall through the map, you submit a ticket reporting it, they never get back to you and then, approaching release, when they needed good PR the most, they simply decided to wipe out every support ticket submitted by "Legacy" Servers (a.k.a. the servers prior release), without ever addressing most of them, and basically say "F**k You" to everyone who supported the game through Early Access.
Let alone that, they act like a "Fun Police", where fun isn't allowed, it takes you 11 real life days to raise a Mosasaurus, Tusoteuthis or Giganotosaurus, 11 real life days for a virtual pet, it takes 28 hours to make them feed from feeding troughs, alleviating some of the stress, and almost every dino in the game takes days of care to become adults.
Then you might say "well, tame them instead, takes less", sure, and they are extremely weak compared to bred dinos with good imprinting (oh, yeah, there's that as well, every 3 to 4h you need to give some attention to your virtual pet, so it gets imprinting bonus, which then makes them far stronger and far more resistant than, say, the wild parents of said bred dino, even if they have the exact same stats, the bred one will be much stronger)
Ok, so now, in order to have a really strong dino you need to either not work, or do it on free days, nice, then what's next?

One of said nerfs was to the Therizinosaur, a dino meant for harvest which is very hard to tame, which, everyone agreed it was OP, but what was their solution for that? nerf it so it is either slightly better or worse than other dinos who aren't meant for harvest as the Theriz was (Theriz has a special ability which allows you to allocate special harvest points to two abilities, power harvesting or delicate harvesting, which buffs a specific resource group output, no other dino has that, and after the nerf, in practice, there was no difference between delicade and power anymore, a farming session would be, in practice, the same with the two). Another nerf was the so called flyer nerf, which they set the movement speed for flying dinos to be static, you can't increase or decrease, no matter what, not even imprinting helps there, and that made moving across the map an extremely boring task. A third nerf example was the fishing nerf, where they reduced the loot from fishing, and limited the size of fishes that can be catch, fishing would yield rare blueprints to craft saddles and other gear, and they nerfed it to the point that it became quite pointless to even bother.

Another reason to avoid Official servers, is the fact that you need to abdicate from life, or allocate some time to do choirs, I mean, play Ark, because your dinos can starve to death, or, which I consider even worse, if you play PVE, they can be gone in 8 days if you don't log-in and visit these structures (be within render distance) to reset the timers. Same goes for structures, but they have different timers, with thatch and greenhouse/glass being 4 days, wood and adobe 8, stone 12, metal 16 and tek 20 days, the last 3 doesn't even make sense, because you build bases to secure your dinos, but what's the point of having 12, 16 or 20 days for the base to expire, when your dinos inside only last 8 days, and after this period they can either be claimed by someone else, or simply automatically disappear from the server if no one claims them shortly after the timer has expired.
And this is where the complaints about steam review system comes in place, because I do recommend this game if you avoid official servers, but WildCard and their PR and Customer Service forces me to check the "Not Recommended" button

A huge part of me want's to recommend this game, but I just can't bring myself to do so. Having over 1100 hrs it may seem strange that I'm not recommending this game but that's part of the problem. Having spent all that time in alpha and beta I expected their to be issues. These are things you have to accept with early access and I have spent many fun filled hours in this game. Everything in the game screams for you to enjoy it from the beautiful landscapes, the taming of dinosaurs and exploring of the world to find the perfect place to build your base. The modding community have only added to the game and there are many many great mods currently available. So why can't I recomment this game? Well various reasons. Firstly still after all this time the game is nowhere near optimised. Even on a super fast machine with lots of memory and a great graphics card the FPS can be terrible. The graphics are great but when you either have to run on terrible settings or wait for things to load in it looses so much of the wow factor. Secondly the community...yes I know I'm setting myself up for backlash but hey ho. Finding a server that isn't dominated by several toxic alpha tribes is hard. Yes its a PVP game and you can't control the game base but it seemed like for a long time every patch the developers have done has actually encouraged this style of play and level of toxicity. Alpha tribes moving from one server to the next dominating, destroying the player base of the server and moving on became a staple for the game for far to long. I feel like the developers really let the decent community down on this one and having played almost 1500hrs of Rust I know what a toxic community looks like. OK the final and most important reason I can't recommend this game. The developers decisions themselves. For a game that still has so many issues for them to sort out the developers appear to have taken the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of the consumer far too often. As I said as a gamer buying a alpha or beta product I expect issues in the game and thats why playing them is helping to give feedback so the developer can produce the game they want to bring you and the game you want to play. Likewise playing modded games you know you are taking the risk to the stability of your game. I have no problem with that at all. Getting 'The Center' was fantastic but I would have been happier if they had ironed out the bugs in the original map first. Getting a paid for DLC in 'Scorched Earth' maybe could have been reasoned as the developers claimed it was to enable them to invest the money back in to getting that final game we all wanted, a reason I never fully agreed with or brought as it did sting a bit of a being a cash grab and paid DLC on a game not completed just doesn't seem right. OK so the developers learnt their lesson and once again gave Ragnarok as a free DLC but then, and this is why I'm writing this review now after so long playing the game, they then hiked the price of the base game up to £50...I mean wt actual f. OK so some will say what do I care, I got the base game on sale for £10 years ago and maybe thats my reward for helping with alpha and beta. Fair point. But this review is for people thinking of buying the game now. So is the game worth £50....not by a long way. I would struggle justifying any game at a £50 price tag but no way could I recommend for someone to spend that money on a game that is still so far from a finished article. Optimisation issues asside, (which are great and many), the past record of the developers and the way they have so far progressed this game would make me reticent to where they are going. Yes it has so many things going for it, yes I have spent many happy hours in the game, yes it does look beautiful when looked on from the outside but no I don't have faith the developers will ever produce the final game I want to be playing and that is why I simply couldn't recommend to anyone to buy this game. As sad as that makes me feel to say so. To me the dlc's and new dinosaurs etc have become a way for the developers to try and distract us from the real issues of the game with new toys, maybe looking at these new toys transfixed whilst in a zombie like trance and saying 'shinny' is enough for some gamers. Me... I would have just been happy with a perfectly running, smooth base game. Even then £50...........really......really really?

Well.......to start off, Warframe is a game with a lot of potential, even though I'm not recommending this game......for now at least, why do you ask? Well, to start off, a few years back, DE was quite known for hearing out the community and offering good support to their players, offering us interesting quests, frames, a very pleaseant player base abd other features, however, around 2016, things has started to.....change, to start off, the new relic system......while it allows us to tip the odds a tiny bit to our favor, I didn't quite agree with it being an effective solution to reduce the grinding, being pretty much the key system with pretty much increased grinding due to the void fissure farming, not only that, but the feature to only get rewards if you bring a relic is in theory a good idea, it starts to make it harder to find a good party to play casually, back with keys, you could choose between a keyshare or just a relaxing void run with randoms who needed help, the prime part just being a bonus, now? It's almost Impossible for me to go on a multiplayer Void run without being pestered to bring a certain relic with the current meta weapon, what was that? Play with friends? Oh, I would love to.........if they hadn't stopped playing for the exact reason that troubles me now, clan mates? Not an option either, the veterans all quit after these last few updates. In theory, this system would also makes things cheaper, right? I mean, prime parts would sell for cheaper between players, and everything would be merry forever and ever right...? Well, sadly not so much, ever since the relic system was impanted, the prices for the prime weapons sure decreased, but for some reason many greedy players seem to have taken some interest in the market and overpricing things, in an effort to ensnare a helpless newby who just started......that and since the increased power creep, it is quite hard to sell or find an item for a reasonable price, earning platinum for that shiny new Valkyr Prime...? Well, good luck with either the farming with void fissures & relics, or earning the 160 - 200 platinum you need for it....that is, if someone doesn't charge you way more than that, speaking of newer prime frames, its resource requirements compared to the older frames simply don't stand, while back then the worst we could face was, for instance, getting 600 of a somewhat rare lightweight material (oxium) and 2000 of those resources that comes in clusters (e.g.: Polymer bundles), now? well, I hope you are ready to farm the 20 nitain (a resource only found on alerts, which are some sort of "event" missions, which usually are tedious and only come 1 each!), over 6000 of oxium, and more for a frame called Vauban Prime. Want that shiny Valkyr Prime to have a better looking Valkyr or a slightly more powerful version? Well, while not as absurd as the previously mentioned Vauban prime, I hope you are ready to spend some hours farming polymer bundles without buying (or dropping if you're lucky) a resource booster (you need 15000 to build one, and usually each run without the mentioned annoying players, nets you around 3000 bundles per run........in a survival mission where you most likely will spend 20 or more minutes at least before leaving). Sure, some players complained to DE about the absurd farming or resource cost (Hema research and Mutagen sample drop, anyone?) and while I'm NOT interested on the new meta, I find it ridiculous the clear lies regarding reduced grinding they promissed the players, while ignoring the players that are unhappy with it or any other features (for instance, the Frost Deluxe skin, which DE changed slightly and made many players who bought it before the change unhappy, or the Tennogen Syandana, Sari, where many loved their open wings design all the time and folding when shooting or looking the menu, and yes, while they now stay open in the liset,dojos or relays, they stay closed within a mission, which makes it look unimpressive and almost the same as the other capes, taking away its charm), all things considered, Warframe IS a good game with potential, that is if the developers start hearing out their players like before and stop presenting us with solutions that do nothing to fix the problem, unless that happens, I suggest you to stay away from this game for now.

Intensly brutal in your face combat that you'll get nowhere else. The Massive, teamwork focused objective modes are well thought out and immersive with boulders impacting castle walls while you mercilessly fight to the death with your enemy.  Though the game includes the typical multiplayer maps of team deathmatch CTF etc. the team objective modes truely sold this for me. The classes are well balanced and feel unique, all requiring a good level of skill. You may think wildly swinging your sword will earn you kills but once you bump into a skilled player you'll find yourself in pieces until you adapt. Make sure you go through the tutorial first, it covers all the basics very well. Then the game's duel mode will teach you quite a bit about the nuances of swordplay. There's nothing quite like the first time you trick your enemy into lowering his guard as you lop his head clean from his shoulders. Though into the negatives of this game you need to take where a server is hosted seriously before you jump into a fight. Lag is a much bigger issue for a melee game than a shooter. Secondly the chat function, I suppose this is just a symptom of online gaming but dear lord does this game's community turn into crap flinging monkeys quick. If WoW's old tbc era barrens chat means anything to you, you'll understand the level of stupidity and trolling quick. Overall though it doesnt ruin the game even slightly, I am very happy i found this gem. I really recommend this game.

"Welcome to the grind," we tell the newbies who cry foul at the awful amount of effort it takes to acquire anything.
I last wrote my review 7 Mastery Ranks ago. I am now MR8, well on my way to veterancy among the community. I gave it a glowing review. A few strangers helped me out in the early game. The combat is fast and visceral. The movement is clean and natural. At the time I had no complaints.
At the time, I gave it a thumbs up and a "You can't go wrong."
Over the last four months of on and off play I can finally take off the rose-tinted goggles and see the game clearly. What I see is not as perfect, not as shiny and new, not as well thought out as I had thought at first glance.
The progression takes center stage as the driving force for the player. Some, perhaps most, of the systems in place for progressing are elegant in many regards. It suffers from a slowly growing number of currencies, but otherwise, from the midgame onward, getting new items comes fairly regularly. The farming system for Prime items is actually rather clever, encouraging open co-op and rewarding organized farming attempts.
Ultimately, the whole thing is not too bad even if getting basic frames is an insipid, unecessarily difficult affair.
Why, then, has DE gone out of their way to sabotage their own system? Between Prime weapon/frame parts getting randomly yanked into an unreachable "vault", and the prominence of "common Primes" (Primes considered much easier to gain than others), the economy becomes wildly inflated.
DE's got you covered though. For more than the price of a full game you can gain a few vaulted Prime weapons and a Prime Frame. From their perspective, your money is more valuable to them than it is to you.
Players now trade those vaulted parts at high prices. Players who only gathered some of the parts and are left with incomplete sets are forced to either keep useless parts, sell them for platinum, or buy the rest of the parts from others (which is a bit difficult since many people collect and sell only full sets).
The clever system of Prime part acquisition is rendered less effective (moot in some cases).
In fact, many systems in the game seem intentionally counter-intuitive and damn near outright hostile to new players. Others are only technically functional, being poorly thought out and even less well implemented (Dojo construction).
Ultimately, DE seems to only patch these problems, when they address them at all. It ends up being up to old veterans to try and care for and educate newbies. Though this, on paper, creates a sense of community, in reality new players will leave even if they receive help for the sheer amount of information that must be absorbed.
If THAT doesn't turn them off, taking 4 days to make a Warframe IF you have all the prerequisite blueprints and materials (another week or two of straight grinding in some cases) will. Not to mention the Mastery Rank system locking out many items in the game. Not to mention some items only being grindable at the LATEST of planets, or requiring access to multiple planets.
Yeah. Yes, indeed. Hope you got the money to drop on Platinum if you want to avoid that slog.
With the game being almost entirely cooperative, there IS a strong community of players, many of whom will go out of their way to help others. Ask for help or knowledge and you're nearly guaranteed to get it. When I first started I was asking where to farm for the mandatory Power mods like Flow and Continuity.
A player at MR20 said "You don't," invited me to trade, and gave me all four that I was looking for, and then started listing off mods to see if I had them so he could give them to me. For nothing! Amazing. I've heard a staggering amount of stories of players helping players.
It is online, it is public, and so there is always SOME trolling and toxicity. To say its absent would be a lie, but poor sportsmanship is a rarity for this game.
You can hit things with an exploding sword, causing them to fly across the map at comical velocities. You can wade through a crowd with a machine gun, ripping foes in half and blowing off limbs. You can cover 100m in seconds with almost no effort. Whip out a glowing energy blade as Excaliber. Ignite enemies by walking by them as Ember.
Summon the freakin' Kraken as Hydroid.
Though progression is a miserable time, and much of the game is shrouded in overt complexity, its raw gameplay is top-notch. Gratification is abound in a game where your starting weapons can turn bodies to mush.
Challenge, however, scales unevenly. Sometimes you'll expect a hellish fight but end a boss solo without hardly a twitch of the trigger. Sometimes you'll fight the same enemy twenty times wondering where you've gone wrong, how something could possibly be this difficult.
In general you'll want to join a clan to ease the pain of the more absurd missions. Luckily, there are clans abound. My own clan is AEDC, by the way. Research at max. Always looking for new members.
What makes this game fun, the community, the impressive combat, the aesthetics and unique setting, cannot carry it.
It is hostile to new players in all the wrong ways and demands a grind like few games demand. The economy is exploitable, and despite being a "free" game, Platinum can do everything. You can buy weapons, rush construction times, acquire Primes from other players, and basically solve (i.e. cut corners) every problem the game has with Platinum. In fact, you can't even keep a decent amount of weapons at the same time without spending platinum to boost storage space.
And there's no way around that.
Why play the game when you can pay the devs instead? Why suffer the torture of crap RNG rolls if you can "earn" your imaginary weapons with a little scratch. To sell this game as having a fair business model, where everything can be earned, is only technically true.
I've got another 16-ish Master Ranks to go. Its too late for me.
But you can save yourself.

I don't know why? Maybe it is because of the great and fluid combat? The cool looking characters? or maybe the massive plethora of weapons? Anyway, I always return to it. And that has a reason. But not only that, The graphics look great, there are quite some planets to explore, you can customize everything (literally everything from your warframe, weapons and companions to your ship and your playstyle), you can make your own guild (with a dojo as base), easily play with friends thanks to the nice matchmaking system, there are multiple PVP modes and there are story missions that you can play. Overall a whole lot of fun things to do in warframe, which is why I do recommend it! The thing is to get all of these awesome warframes, weapons and companions, you have to go through a long proces of grinding missions over and over again. And when you finally get that nice looking gun, you can do it all over again to get the next one. This makes it very boring and repetitive after a short while.
But of course this is my opinion. And I do like warframe a lot which is why I recommend it. Plus, it's free, so even if you don't like it in the end, i am sure you'll get some fun moments out of it!

At the start, it's very frustrating, and rage enducing, but you'll eventually get the hang of it. Then it's slightly less punch-a-hole-in-your-computerly difficult. So if have ever broken anything out of rage and anger, Chivalry isn't for you. Don't get me wrong, it is a great game, it just takes practice. Once you get on a role, it's great, you'll have the time of your life. I give Chivalry: Medieval Warefare, 8/10.

In case anyone is confused, the single most important attribute of an action game is tight controls, especially in pvp.  Chivalry fails this basic test in spectacular fashion, considering your input as more of a suggestion to be considered in time rather than an instruction you'd very much like it to do right now before that other guy chops off your head.
Being a male, I spent almost all of my childhood swinging sticks, pvc pipe, cardboard tubes, and anything else that could conceivably substitute for a sword at other people...I know there's a bit of a lag before swinging something and the moment you give your best friend a concussion.  That lag is not nearly as long as the lag in this game.  Of course, managing to swing is only half the battle, the hit boxes in this game are all messed up.  I hacked away at a helpless archer for a full 10 seconds without registering a single hit, presumably because he was standing sideways.
It's a pity the controls are so bad, because there's some real potential here.  Siege combat is not something that's gotten a lot of attention in video games, and I don't understand why.  This game makes it seem like it could be fun.  There are a variety of other mission types available (mostly ripped off from Team Fortress 2), and they all look like they'd be entertaining if the game would just do what I told it to.
