I wanna get a few things off my chest in this review of Warframe, as someone who has been playing for over 550 hours, for those who are new to the game so they don't goof up as much as I did. First off, the game WILL take up space on your computer, so this isn't for the weak ones that crash easily either, and will also take up a portion of your time if you decide to play this.
Second: this game is not something you can play for 8+ hours straight a day. Unless you have a clear objective of what it is you're gonna do when playing, be it alert missions that crop up with your desired rewards, missions, farming resources and prime items, etc. then you WILL get bored easily. I say this because of the hours I've wasted in indecision of what it is I wanted to do, and its just easier when you plan out what you want to work on.
Third: Be prepared to grind the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of the missions when collecting resources or trying to rank up. You will not get far simply blitzing through each mission, and searching areas for much needed loot will help you later. Do not listen to those complaining about not getting enough loot when they go grinding, they make the mistake of speedrunning instead of being meticulous. That said, this leads me to my next point.
Fourth: this IS a genuine F2P, and although real currency CAN (not WILL) be used, it is not necessary to advance at all. Using platinum (this is the currency you do exchange your real money into) is completely optional, and there are multiple tips I'll give on the use of it for newcomers:
1. Spending platinum is optional
2. don't use it on frivolous things like credits (the game's other currency that you can earn in any mission) or resources as it is NOT WORTH IT IN VALUE
3. save it for big purchases like colours, hard-to-obtain warframes or accessories. Trust me, you'll want to be stingy
4. There are ways of gaining plat WITHOUT spending real money, but it does involve grinding specific items and finding willing trading partners. These items are called 'Prime' items, and hold onto as many as possible - you do not want to be selling them for credits even if you cannot use them. Trade them as 'prime junk' with other items to gain platinum, just be patient when looking for partners.
Finally, Each warframe has a set of abilities connected to them that you can use. buttons 1-4 on your keyboard activate them during missions. It took me ages to realise they were even there, so I figured its best to tell you upfront to avoid my ignorance happening to you.
Its entirely up to you on how you play this, and yes there will be tech issues as addressed by other players, but otherwise its a fun way to spend a few hours of your day as well as be a paradise for hoarding and collecting. Or hell for the recovering ones, anyway. In short, good luck grinding the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of this game.

I have almost 3k hours in this game at the time of writing this. I have done just about everything from collecting end-game items to raids to collecting cosmetics to becoming rich with in-game currency. So here is a pretty comprehensive review:
Graphics
This game was created in 2013, yet still holds up really well in 2017. There are many different tile sets such as deserts, icelands, futuristic buildings, ruins, and a moon-like planet. The warframes each come with several abilities. Many look awesome and baddass. For e.g. when activating Volt's speed ability alot of electricity eminates from his body. Banshee's quake creates a massive dust/energy cloud around her. The nidus warframe can create an area of infested vegetation and fill the screen with various colors sometimes luminescent.
Controls
Honestly, this game is top-notch in the controls department. Not many games will compare. You'll be zipping around in your warframe and have complete control over it. How efficiently one moves from point A to point B really depends on player skill. There's a parkour system. There's bullet jumping which allows you to jump several stories up or in any direction. You can wall-latch, double jump, roll, and kick in midair. The parkour physics can be used to maximize travel speed. If you end up missing jumps, or falling off the map, you have only yourself to blame.
Sound
This game has a coolness factor. In some of the quest cut scenes, the music goes well with some of the epic lore. The gameplay music, weapon and ability sounds are good and nothing to complain about.
Gameplay
This game isn't highly skill based. Although you'll still need to be able to aim to kill enemies. Also headshots do more damage. For the most part the game is about collecting items and powering up warframes and weapons. The game offers a ton of variety. There are many warframes and each warframe comes with four unique abilities. Each warframe has their uses except for a couple that are arguably underwhelming. However, that still leaves many to choose from, and I recommend collecting them all. There are hundreds of weapons to choose from. Each weapon comes with a set of unique strengths and weaknesses. There are accurate automatic rifles, automatic shotguns, double barrel shotguns, sniper rifles, laser weapons, flamethrowers, grenade launchers, throwing knives, and bows. There are also many strange weapons that are hard to explain. For example, there's a javelin you throw that explodes, a weapon you shoot twice in order for its energy orbs to explode, a laser weapon that shoots cubes made of lasers, and a pistol made of infested bio material that changes shape when you land critical hits. There are large and small swords, double swords, sword and shield combos, staves, daggers, whips, axes, hammers, and more.
There are several mission types: assassination, capture, defense, exterminate, interception, mobile defense, rescue, raid, sabotage, spy, and survival. Without giving long explanations, sometimes you'll have to defend a position. Other times you'll have to infiltrate a base to hack for information or destroy a high priority target. The raids are special missions and are pretty detailed requiring a coordination of button presses, hacks, and bomb deliveries. A raid needs 4 to 8 players to start. The players really need to know what to do in order to succeed. If not, raids can be pretty painful and can result in mission failure or long completion times. The raids should take less than 20 minutes, but for the inexperienced, raids can take 40 minutes to 1 hour. Ouch.
Loot
As said earlier, there are many warframes, their prime variants, and hundreds of weapons to collect. Each of which isn’t actually powerful until they are properly modded out. These mods are like cards you collect and installed onto warframes and weapons. Builds in this game are formed by a specific combo of these mods of your choosing and there are hundreds if not thousands+ mods. There are also arcanes gotten as rewards from raids. These give additional boosts such as health regen per second, heightened critical hit chance, increased fire rate, additional revives and more.
In order to build warframes and weapons, you’ll need credits and various resources which require farming. Many warframes and weapons have prime variants (superior versions) and are farmed via the relic/fissure system. First you need to farm relics and which relics you get are based on RNG. You then use these relics in fissure missions. Each relic has a unique reward table, so the chance of you getting the item you want is again based on RNG. You can heighten your chances of getting the item you want using traces and traces need to be farmed. The good news is when joining pub fissures, you may get lucky if a party member receives the reward you want. You can then choose their reward instead of yours.
The grind in this game is probably the biggest complaint among players. Mostly what you’ll be doing is farming for the next best thing. However, there are strategies for more efficient farming that can cut a serious amount of time and effort.
Content
This game is only going to get bigger and bigger. This game receives continuous updates adding new warframes and weapons, new quests, and new mods. There is so much to do in this game, that in 300 hours a player still has experienced only a small portion of the game.
For New Players
This game does not hold your hand. Having an experienced friend who can help you is HIGHLY recommended. I’ve asked thousands of questions playing through this game. I had to find answers from friends, random players, warframe wiki, forums, and google. As said earlier, building warframes and weapons requires credits and resources. You’ll need to unlock all the planets and junctions. With your unmodded and underpowered warframe and weapon, this is a daunting and time consuming task. A friend will ease this initial hoop.
Free To Play Aspects
The big question: Is this truly free to play? The simple answer is yes. All items can be farmed or traded for. The in-game currency is called platinum which you will no doubt need. There are only two ways of getting platinum: trading and buying with real money. I personally have not spent any real money but I’m not going to lie because I was tempted to especially in the beginning. Platinum can be used to buy time cutting resource, affinity, and credit boosters. Platinum is needed to buy warframe and weapon slots. Warframes take 3 days to build and weapons take 24 hours. Platinum can be used to rush building. Platinum can be used to skip farming and directly buy warframes and weapons off the market. As you can see there is incentive to buy platinum with real money especially in the beginning, but you don’t need to. You can farm items and trade for platinum which of course is more time consuming. From another perspective, farming and trading for platinum can be fun.
I give this game a 9.5/10. Half a point taken off for certain items (not all) requiring an absurd amount of grinding for.

I was very hopeful after reading the description and then watching the video for this game.  Fortunantly the game delivered on my expectations!  This game is insanely fun.  And it works well.  It is, I believe, described as a first person brawler.  That is the same as a first person shooter, but with close combat.  Whether you use swords or spears or axes or bows the combat is always exciting and thrilling.
There is no peeking around a corner and suffering a headshot from a sniper.  It is constant old fashioned hand to hand combat.  Block with your shield and then thurst back with your sword.  Sneak behind an enemy while they battle an ally and stab them in the back.
The game is very thrilling with large groups.  It always feels like an epic battle.  There are mission objectives that make the combat very engaging as opposed to pure deathmatch.  You can even use catapults and ballistae to help defend your domain.  I've experienced players do interesting things like surround the last surviving opponent in a circle and allow that opponent to take on the remaining enemy in one on one in hand to hand combat.  Very Awesome! Character customization is pretty weak, and the grahics are nothing to write home about, but the glory of battle makes up for the shortcomings.
I would highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys epic medieval battles from a first person perspective.

Let me start at the very core thing of the review for the mass who are lazy to read an entire text: the game is good, but not amazing as it used to be a long time ago.
I shall start explaining it further on by zeroing in on the fact that the grind (except for prime part grinds) got worse by the years. It's easier to farm a primed item than to farm it's normal counterpart which makes it a hella less enjoyable for new players to get into the game. Sure they improved the gameplay by a lot, by introducing riven mods, renewing the movement system for normal gameplay and archwing (for others it's a minus point, but for me a plus)
Gameplay wise it's great if you're someone who doesn't mind playing the same thing over and over again because of the challenge it creates as difficulter it over time, but even people like me tend to get tired of the game after a long while. I've been in the game since the alpha when the founders pack was still available and i will say that it's more focused on the action than on the actual farming part of the game.
The community is one of the best i've ever encountered in any game. Warframe is like the Canada (ironically DE is centered in Canada) of MMO's. You just join a clan and they'll all be helpfull to you and even tend to give you mods and primed stuff if you're nice like them. You can just chat with a random stranger in an interception run and add him at the end of the game. I think that that's the best part of Warframe and the main part that kept me going on in the game for 1.6k+ hours (call me addicted, but i see it as a good investment in a good mmo with a fun playerbase)
Now let me start with the movement mechanics. They're amazing to me. You just latch on to a wall and shoot up a bunch of enemies with your crit modded weapon (since critical chance is too valued in this game) or just jump over a group over enemies with your firewalker equipped warframe and run away from them while doing a roll mid-air that makes your warframe go like the flash. It's really fun and makes the game feel really high paced.
Now about the warframes. The warframes have been buffed and nerfed (or as DE calls it: "reworked") all the time such as Mag who has been turned into utter crap (except for her second ability). They are plenty powerful with the right setup, but you'll always have people crying for nerfs in the power struggle for the most kills in the game (i'm looking at you Ash). It has all been good up to the part when they randomly figured to mess the idea of "ninjas" up with a bard type warframe.
If you're someone who'd want to play this game for a short time between games to blast off some steam then i'd say "go for it", but as long as the grind is bad i'd recommend not putting all your time into this game despite it's amazing community and gameplay.

I've owned Ark since Day 1 (June 2, 2015) and although I have had a lot of fun, the BS that the developers have put us through is enough to give it a negative review.
The only time my tribes have been wiped in this game has been due to cheating. Hackers are frequent and Wildcard never takes the claims serious, even when there is proof (search youtube for Official server 16 Jane Cheating).  You will tear your hair out when you tames begin dying for no reason while they're safe in their pens, only to be followed by a wave of hacking players who take over the server.
The last straw came in the form of taking away everything that Beta players have made for themselves, packing them up and moving to already populated servers to try to get a foothold in a landscaper filled with other players and broken buildings from the past that prevent you from building in that area until you destroy all of the foundations. The biggest slap in the face is preventing players from the old "legacy" servers from transferring anything to the new servers at all.
Basically, they're rewarding long time players by making all of the hours we've spent absolutely meaningless.  It wouldn't be nearly as bad if they'd let us transfer our characters at least.  If you take anything away from this, take this: Wildcard does not care about you or your complaints (especially about optimization over new creatures).
Also, Wildcard never officially announced this in game.  I had a friend tell me about it since they read the list of servers being taken down, but no one else in the tribe was aware and now we have less then a week to scout for new homes on new servers, pack up dozens of tames, hundreds of stacks of items and resources and do this all with a server transfer limit that will have you transferring, then looking for a drop to unload your stuff, build a small base. go back to your old server, find a drop, transfer, go to new server, find a drop, etc.
The amount of time that this will take is not available for smaller tribes with a lot of stuff to transfer, who still have lives and jobs outside of the game.  Wildcard messed up big time.
I won't even go into optimization because if you're reading this, then you've already seen everyone else who complains about it.

A brilliant meta-satire on skinner box games, but not really much of a game itself. Clicker heroes is a game where you grind, so that you can grind faster, so that you can grind, so that you can grind faster, etc. in a never ending cycle of grinding. But what is the actual grind? Nothing. You just sit and watch as numbers get bigger. You have no real choices to make. You earn gold to spend on upgrades to earn more gold so that you can spend on upgrades to earn more gold and there are no wrong choices, only slightly inefficient ones. You can do some clicking as well but 99% of the time you don't need to. If you ever played a game like Diablo, any kind of loot game or RPG where you grinded to level up, you get the exact same experience, but here you don't have to do anything at all. It's brilliant how they distilled the essence of an entire genre into its bare components and showed how pointless and stupid Diablo-esque or any game with grinding in it is. Even though I didn't recommend it, because the game is shallow and pointless, you may as well at least try it, since it is free, and think of this brilliant game when you play other skinner box type games.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare was released almost simultaneously with
, which offers a similar experience to some extent.
What Chivalry aims to do, it does very well. The melee combat is the primary focus of the game and that really shows, as the other possible method of engaging the enemy, ranged combat, isn't as well fleshed out. The close combat is some of the best, most visceral action out there. The pace of the fighting is great and really makes it feel like every blow counts, as a missed or parried strike can be the end of you. As brilliant as the melee is, the ranged combat is in no way unique and feels quite mediocre. The mechanics are very simple and it doesn't feel that satisfying.
Chivalry's offering of game modes is very good, it has the standard deathmatches and also some more unique modes like it's asymmetric Team Objective which is arguably the best mode in the game. Team Objective pits 2 teams against each other as one takes on the role of the attacker and the other the defender. The objectives vary from map to map, at times you're supposed to take a siege engine to the gate and then on the next map you might be there to curb a peasant uprising.
If you have to make the choice between Chivalry and War of the Roses, Chivalry is your pick if you are there for the brutal, unrivaled melee combat and that's all you need to be satisfied. Both are great games and if you can afford picking them up, I recommend you do.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare was released almost simultaneously with
, which offers a similar experience to some extent.
What Chivalry aims to do, it does very well. The melee combat is the primary focus of the game and that really shows, as the other possible method of engaging the enemy, ranged combat, isn't as well fleshed out. The close combat is some of the best, most visceral action out there. The pace of the fighting is great and really makes it feel like every blow counts, as a missed or parried strike can be the end of you. As brilliant as the melee is, the ranged combat is in no way unique and feels quite mediocre. The mechanics are very simple and it doesn't feel that satisfying.
Chivalry's offering of game modes is very good, it has the standard deathmatches and also some more unique modes like it's asymmetric Team Objective which is arguably the best mode in the game. Team Objective pits 2 teams against each other as one takes on the role of the attacker and the other the defender. The objectives vary from map to map, at times you're supposed to take a siege engine to the gate and then on the next map you might be there to curb a peasant uprising.
If you have to make the choice between Chivalry and War of the Roses, Chivalry is your pick if you are there for the brutal, unrivaled melee combat and that's all you need to be satisfied. Both are great games and if you can afford picking them up, I recommend you do.

This review only covers the base game Chivalry: Medieval Warfare, not the DLC Deadliest Warrior.
Prior to playing Chivalry, I never really had played a game that had deep, tactical hand to hand/ sword fighting. This is where Chivalry delivers. Chivalry is a multiplayer experience in which the combat is extremely brutal (heads and limbs can be dismembered), but very satisfying. When you hit someone with a mace, the character actually reacts the way they should. The sound of steel on steel and the two factors in the game screaming "FOR AGATHA," or "FOR THE RED AND BLACK," is great. The maps are very diverse ranging from castle sieges to fighting in wooded areas to a Roman Arena (just like the movie Gladiator). The game also provdes your standard nultiplayer modes in addition to Duel mode (self explainatory). With four different classes (Archer, Man-at-Arms, Vanguard, and a Knight) and roughly 10 different weapons to unlock for each class, this game can keep you occupied for a pretty long time. This game is a blast to play with friends, and I highly recommend it to anyone (especially any FPS fans in need of a game to respark there interest).
Pros:
+ Excellent, tactical combat. This game actually takes skill to be good - something you don't see very much.
+ Graphics - The game looks pretty good on the Unreal 3 Engine. The weapons and characters really stand out.
+ Controls - The controls are responsive and work great.
+ Sound
+ Map Design
Cons:
-  Customization could have been a little better (not a big deal though)
Overall, this game is a breath of fresh-air coming from a seasoned FPS fan. I highly recommend it!

I bought Chivalry within a few days after release looking for something fresh and different. I've begun to turn a blind eye to big developers these days, they simply don't release any new, fresh material and you always find "mods" that are community made actually have better gameplay and better ideas than those of big developers. And so, this contributed towards my decision to buy this game. Now, believe me, it's the best couple of quid I've spent on a game for as long as I can remember.
I wouldn't say this game is a flawless masterpiece. It has its downfalls and "wtf" moments, but if you look past these minor errors then it's absolutely a must buy if you like anything medieval. Or gore. This game definitely doesn't fall short on the gore side of things and hell, I love gore. Screw rubber bodied enemies, this is realistic, gritty yet glorious and only an indie company would have the balls to put this extreme gore into a game (because they care more about the product than the money, *cough cough*). But there is nothing more satisfying than chopping your opponents head clean off with one mighty vanguard leap and watching the blood spurt out from where the head once sat, or setting your opponents on fire and hearing them scream as they run round like a human torch amongst the cries of the battlefield. Then, as they lie groaning on the floor, using your weapon to decapitate their body while taunting with the hilarious voice commands you have in your arsenal. Have I tempted you to buy this yet? No? Read on.
The positives definitely outweigh the negatives to this game and if you have a buddy to play with then I advise you jump in together. It's much more fun running around shouting stupid things at each other, using your fists to overwhelm a big dumb zweihander wielding vanguard, aiming for that explosive headshot (yes, the heads explode when punched. Realistic? No. Hilarious? Yes.). Or you could try being a big dumb zweihander wielding vanguard yourself, using the vanguard leap to your advantage to fly halfway across a map (try it out for yourself) or just running around messing about, jumping to your death in a lava pit shouting "help me" with multiple enemies chasing you both. That said, you can easily have fun playing by yourself and I've spent the majority of my play time playing without friends. It simply heightens the playing experience having a friend.
The combat system can seem flawed at times and the learning curve can be steep, or at least I found it to be. I have watched as my ax passes through an enemies head, I have been killed hundreds of times as enemy swords pass right through my shield, I have dodged attacks with MAA, only to have the attack register when it shouldn't have because of lag compensation, I have seen bigger, heavier weapons be swung faster than small, light weapons, and daggers blocking MASSIVE swords or poleaxes (seriously, a 5 inch blade cannot defend against a god damn claymore, get it right Torn Banner.) Oh, and by the way, those archer spears SERIOUSLY need to be nerfed.
I have taken collateral damage from being hit in the foot, which bring me to my next point. You'll find the highest level people aren't even fun to play against since they exploit the game engine like mad. Watch for those vanguards who swing their sword at the floor which manages somehow to hit you while they run in circles and kill you super fast without you even getting a single hit on them (this happens a lot, BELIEVE ME NOW, there is a massive skill difference between new players and vets, even mid tier players like myself still get smacked up by lvl 40+). But don't let this deter you, the skill curve is high but you will improve with time. The fighting system is more intricate and well designed than one may think. Little things like moving your mouse into the direction you are swinging to hit the oppenent faster is what make the fighting much less animated and 2 dimensional than say, Elder Scrolls: Skyrim. Saying this, of course, there is no shortage of LMB spammers and I'd like to point this out now: You're gonna get lots of team damage and die by your team mates hands many times. It happens. This is Chivalry in all its glory.
Quickly focusing on the negatives now, there are only 3 real things that bug me about this game. First, I really REALLY wish Torn Banner would sort this stupid weapon unlock glitch out. This has been here for TOO LONG and they are losing Metascore because players are tired of not being unable to unlock certain weapons which has been here basically since launch. The worst part? They had the audacity to release an expansion and 2 updates with buyable helmets
As a result, many people have been giving them negative metascore because they are fed up, and rightly so. Second, the chase/running system in this game is TOTALLY broke. Many a time I have had a head start of 10 feet or so running away from a knight or vanguard as a man at arms, only to have them catch up with ease. This really rubs me the wrong way and I know it annoys other players too. Thirdly, and this isn't really much of a bad point, but rather something I should make a note of for people wishing to play, the archery system in this is very primitive. To understand what I mean by this.. Well you'll just have to pick up a bow and some arrows as an archer and find out for yourself.

I've been playing this game on and off for over 2 years. I left for a little while (basically bored with survival gaming) and came back. Since I've come back, I've never left. This has got to be the BEST survival game I've ever played. Nothing compares to ARK: Survival Evolved. I play PVE. I don't really like PVP gaming. It's not too fun when you've spent hours or even days building a nice area for yourself only to have it raided or destroyed. Not to mention being on the constant look out for thieves and such. I prefer PVE and this game delivers 100 fold. The key is to find a good PVE server that has the game play you prefer or (As my brothers, friends and I have done, start your own unofficial dedicated server and password protect it. This way YOU control the players you want and how the server is run. The game play is intense. The scenery and graphics are amazing. The crafting is easy to understand and the coolest part is the dinos and the taming aspect. My brothers and friends and I get so into this game we are constantly either cheering something we've accomplished or yelling at each other for screwing something up. It's not a cake walk. There is a slight learning curve but once you get it? The game will engolf you and transport you to a world that is truely breathtaking. You not only can tame wild animals and dinos but you can also breed them. The Wyverns can't be bred so imagine having to sneak into a dragon's (Wyvern's) lair and steal one of their eggs (that you have to hatch btw) to be able to have a pet Wyvern. Imagine the adrenaline rush you'd get when once you get one, you are being chased by a fire breathing, poison or frozen breath Wyvern. You'd have to play the game to experience what it's like to go from a naked, weak, primative character, to building an army of loyal tamed dinos on land and sea and having your own empire. Not sure why this game is labeled "mix reviews". It's too bad because it really is not fair. This game ALL ROUND IMHO is the best servival game out there. Try it. Be a little patient. YOU WILL DIE A LOT in the beginning. If you persevere though, the rewards will be immense.

It pains me a lot to downvote this game. However, the story is mediocre and the game itself, while fun, gets boring after a month or so. And I don't really care how many Warframe fanboys I♥♥♥♥♥♥off.
You are basically a god, and the enemies are the puny mortals that can't even aim half the time. Difficulty is infrequent. The AI can be braindead sometimes. The story is basically there to keep you entertained when you have nothing to do in the game, and the writing can be really cringy sometimes.
After the first few months of playing, you start to realize how flat Warframe is. The characters are not compelling. Ordis is not funny. Lotus just basically lies to you for the whole game; it's really obvious sometimes, the devs weren't really trying with the plot twists, but she keeps lying for the sake of plot progression.
And DE turned it into a microtransaction moshpit, too, even worse than Team Fortress 2.
The bulk of the game is just grinding for a while in boring side missions. It was fun at first, but now it's too much.
The final verdict for Warframe is a 4/10. The only thing that keeps it from being any lower is that it's occasionally fun with friends. Warframe also has a lot of potential, but for now, it's just potential. If you do subject yourself to this game, don't expect any deep stories like you would in Call of Duty.

I got into playing warframe a bit later than all the cool kids but It quickly became my favourite free to play game of all time. There is no denying the value you are getting in this package without having to pay a thing upfront. The game does however have a few minor issues which, however insignificant, should still be mentioned.
Pros:
The game has a intricate and interesting lore which is just ripe for exploring. Whether thats done via scanning different things in mission or completeing the various quests there is always more to learn about this world. That said you won't be running out of content any time soon. The variety when it comes to weapons, warframes and equipment is truly amazing and they keed adding to it constantly. Furthermore the extensive customization and upgradability of different items provides even more depth,
My personal reccomendation for anyone is to play with a group of friends because that's when this game really shines. The public matchmaking isn't too bad either however you may encounter lag as well as AFK playes which are to be expected.
Cons:
Playing this game alone can sometimes be extremely boring and on higher tier mission it is directly discoraged as the game can get pretty difficult and going solo will just be a pain. The higher level equipment often requires a fair bit of farming which can quickly get repetitive and what doesn't help is that the rng sometimes seems utterly broken. And don't get surprised if it actually is broken as the game does suffer from its share of bugs and connectivity issues. Oh yeah and everytime you launch the game prepare yourself for 15 minutes of downloading new content....but maybe that's just me.
Overall I think warframe is a stellar example of how ftp games should be done. Whilst having microtransactions most of the high tier equipment isn't actually purchasable so forget about the ''pay to win'' strategy. There is no denying the ammount of content, lore and hours of fun you can have with your friends without paying a dollar.

I would suggest taking Excalibur as your starter frame, as he is a very good offensive monster. His Ultimate can punch through walls, obstacles and enemies, hitting everything in his path. Then aim for Loki and Rhino parts. You will have to grind missions several times to get the parts... I had to kill Jackal probably 30 times before I obtained all the parts I needed for Rhino. Like people say, This is a grind but with no pay wall.(You can, if, again... you're lazy)
There are 4 Rotations for Excavation, Defense, Interception, and Survival endless fissures, and go A A B C. Every 5 minutes in Survival is a rotation, 5 waves in defense is a rotation, and every 2 Excavators(in Void Fissures) is a rotation, and every time you decode a message in interception is a rotation.
Fissures are life. Always do endless fissures as long as possible. You get Credit, Experience(Affinity) and Resource boosts for every rotation by 25% for the game. These endless missions are THE best way to level up your gear.
Need relics? There are 4 types that drop from different areas with a wide range of difficulty.
Lith Relics - Spear, Mars (Defense) these can drop from every rotation. So play lots and get lots of relics.
Meso - IO, Jupiter (Defense) the first two rotations(10 waves) drop Meso relics. You can simply leave after the 2nd rotation and repeat, or stay for a chance at a mix of Endo, Meso/Neo relics, and Mods
Neo/Axi - Xini, Eris (Interception) the first two rotations drop Neo Relics, the second two rotations drop Axi. Another good spot for these relics is Heiracon, Pluto (Excavation) which has a chance of dropping Endo, Relics, and Mods. Be weary, Neo/Axi relic farming missions AND fissure missions difficulty scales quickly, so come prepared.
If you're leveling a frame, do not take any weapons that are not Mastered(rank 30). As Experience(Affinity) is split among everything you have equipped. Taking multiple items that require Affinity to level will make leveling the frame/weapon longer. If you're leveling melee weapons, find your way to Kappa, Sedna with Loki or Ivara and assassinate everyone(using a charged assassination by holding down the left mouse will increase damage and cause the body to vanish). Stealth kills give an experience multiplier up to 500%. Some primary weapons can be leveled this way too, granted you use Silencing Mods/Frames to give you stealth abilities.
Need Platinum? Plat is mega easy to come by.. Do fissures, open those nifty relics you got, sell the parts(or craft your weapons). Simple as that. Don't forget to check your Void Traces often at lower Mastery Ranks, as you can only hold so many until you level up more. I personally only spend my void traces on making Relics become Radiant by spending 100 traces, and crafting Derelict keys. If you can open enough relics to find whole sets of frames/weapons that can substantially increase your Plat generation.
There are plenty of guides online. Try to find a decent clan to join, as they can be a big help. Some people may even be nice enough to "Taxi" you to places. When googling things, try to stick with "Players Helping Players" Warframe forums and Reddit. Most everything else isn't kept up to date.

I can neither recommend this nor fully condemn it. It's a PVP hack and slash whereby you face off against opposing players (duh, PVP) You can decimate your opponents by means of blocking, feigning attacks to get your opponent to block and then striking him as he lowers his guard. Pros:
-You'll have a few good chuckles at the hilarity of your kills. Some of them are really satisfying
(I seriously didn't find many things that I liked about it. Overall it was frustrating to maneuver and felt like I was constantly trying to wade out of mud)

Pretty, mindless fun as long you don't care about balance or fairness, and aren't bothered by a community that thrives on grief.
Classes that utilize slow weaponary are at a clear disadvantage to those with a faster weapons. Traits meant to offset the loss of speed, such as damage mitigation or weapon reach, are not implemented well and ultimately do not factor into balance. This leads to most matches being populated by the "man-at-arms" class - wielding a starter sword or mace and choosing to forgo a shield, they're capable of effortlessly decimating heavier classes even when outnumbered. It completely trivializes melee combat, makes itemization pointless, and negates any reason to play the more cumbersome classes.
Archery can be rewarding once one unlocks better weapons and becomes accustomed to the cadence of movement and combat. It's the only balanced aspect of the game.
Griefing is rampant by abusing map layout, game mechanics, and the vote kick system. One common example: other players will block doorways and force team mates to assault them so that they can exit the spawn area. TL;DR: Nausea-inducingly poor performance, developers don't have their priorities in order, still has glitches from day one, devs ignore basic optimisation tips from players.
Before starting, here's what you need to run the game smoothly at 1080p on 'high' settings.
GTX 1080 or similar, with 6Gb-8Gb VRAM
A CPU around the i7-6000+ range. Not too clear on this one.
16Gb of DDR4 RAM
An SSD with spare space for the 100 gigabytes Ark will take up.
Good internet.
And patience.
Content warning: salt.
As I write this, the game is less than 8 days from release. Apparently. Might be pushed back for the 4th (or is it 5th?) time.
And, as I write this, the game still looks like an early access game in the first year of development.
Don't get what I mean? Let's expand:
- Content promised long-ago is still missing, despite it being so close to their "launch". Meanwhile, a lot of less-than-necessary content has been thrown in instead of focusing on more important issues.
- Pathfinding is broken. Your tamed dinosaurs will get stuck on every rock, tree, and eachother no matter where you go. Tames also tend to not follow you until you stop walking and look back at them (presumably sternly) so that they can promptly (give or take 3 seconds) begin running into you or the tree that's 30 metres behind them.
- Random crashes because haha screw you. May or may not be the broken engine. May or may not.
- Developers have taken the idea of optimising their game and pushed it off the table like an angry bubba. But they swore they'd clean it up. Swore on it, they did. But children also don't have a firm grasp of language, and that may be why they never cleaned up the mess.
- Furthering on the above, players have both delved into the code and even just looked at config files in an attempt to fix the saddening performance. What did they find? Something about every rock loading its texture 8 times as you get closer, I guess. So they fixed this and other bad moves by the devs, and ended up fixing most of the issues the game has. An extra 20 FPS here, 90% less loading stutters there... What did the developers do when sent these fixes? They said "Oh, cheers, we'll look into that.", then printed out screenshots of these tips for the sole purpose of crumpling them up and proceeding to throw them in the bin.
- Devs added BattleEye so any self-modification you do to make the game smooth gets you permanently banned from all official servers. Meanwhile, it did nothing to stop hackers (despite them not being a problem to most players in the first place).
- Something something you still fall through the ground like it's 2015.
I know it only says I've played 32 hours of the game. That's not counting the ~100 I've spent testing it on a friend's PS4, launching it outside of Steam because you're not allowed to play until those generally useless daily updates get downloaded, and on a laptop that got to 85 degrees Celsius at 15FPS before blue-screening (rip Betty).
Right now, I can't recommend this game. I probably won't be able to any time soon. The gameplay itself is only fun alone depending who you are, and usually requires playing with friends on a server for it to be fun. But the performance stops you from accessing most of the enjoyability of the game, coupled with every official server being owned by toxic "alpha tribes".
Also, I'd like to make a passive-aggressive memorial to all the dinosaurs I've lost to the game glitching out.
Rest in many pieces, my many raptors Harry, Larry, Barry, Raptor, Raptor, and Lucy.
To my beloved herbivores, Parasuar1, Parasaur2, Parasaur that died before the naming menu popped up, Trike-cle, and a few dozen dodos that all went MIA at once because the dodo army crashed the engine and the lack of a manual save option meant the game loaded the last autosave... Which was 30 minutes ago.
Oh, and to my lumbering, useless mass of love, the T-rex Bitey McBiteYourFaceOff.
You'd all be here with me if not for... some... developers.

I got into playing warframe a bit later than all the cool kids but It quickly became my favourite free to play game of all time. There is no denying the value you are getting in this package without having to pay a thing upfront. The game does however have a few minor issues which, however insignificant, should still be mentioned.
Pros:
The game has a intricate and interesting lore which is just ripe for exploring. Whether thats done via scanning different things in mission or completeing the various quests there is always more to learn about this world. That said you won't be running out of content any time soon. The variety when it comes to weapons, warframes and equipment is truly amazing and they keed adding to it constantly. Furthermore the extensive customization and upgradability of different items provides even more depth,
My personal reccomendation for anyone is to play with a group of friends because that's when this game really shines. The public matchmaking isn't too bad either however you may encounter lag as well as AFK playes which are to be expected.
Cons:
Playing this game alone can sometimes be extremely boring and on higher tier mission it is directly discoraged as the game can get pretty difficult and going solo will just be a pain. The higher level equipment often requires a fair bit of farming which can quickly get repetitive and what doesn't help is that the rng sometimes seems utterly broken. And don't get surprised if it actually is broken as the game does suffer from its share of bugs and connectivity issues. Oh yeah and everytime you launch the game prepare yourself for 15 minutes of downloading new content....but maybe that's just me.
Overall I think warframe is a stellar example of how ftp games should be done. Whilst having microtransactions most of the high tier equipment isn't actually purchasable so forget about the ''pay to win'' strategy. There is no denying the ammount of content, lore and hours of fun you can have with your friends without paying a dollar.

text: Clicker Heroes is a very unique idle game. This game has many things other idle games dont have, for example, gilded heroes which actually focuses on the heroes instead of ignoring them like other games do. Also ancients, each are unique to help you play and there are even some who gives you a bonus for just idling and doing nothing for 60 seconds! Clicking? Get tired. breaking your fingertips? NO WORRIES! YOU CAN GET BOTH MORE DPS AND GOLD FOR LIBERTAS AND SIYALATAS! But because of that making you restart the game is actually much more worth it. You get hero souls which buy these ancients. Heck with it! Everyone in the game have a storyline as well! The heroes actually talk about one another like Bobby and Natalia! May be uselesss but they're actually quite fun to read, you should check it out if you haven't, even ancients have a story that connects to heroes! The game also includes bosses, and unique primal bosses which adds up the hero souls for the ascension by 1 or 2, you can also level up 2000 times to increase it by one. What? Too hard for that? No worries! It's actually incredibaly easy! There are also a kind of multiplayer function for the clans which allows you to chat with others, see others highest zone lvl, and fight bosses as well which allows you to gain hero souls without acsension! There is a bit of p2w for rubies and gileded heroes and such. However, there isn't much p2w since the orange fish things appear quite frequently to give you rubies or gold which comes in handy. In addition, you also get gilded heroes by going level 100-110-120-Etc and there are 34 heroes so go nuts. Plus, there are relics which allows skills to be extended which are useful but you can only get it after acsension. Oh, did I mention skills yet? Yep there are skills! For instance clickstorm (10 clicks per sec), powersurge (100% dps), etc. Also, I just described the whole game for you. It's amazing, go check it out if you haven't and it's my fav idle game and the best in my opinion. Trust me, I played 73 hrs, just check it out. I have legitemately only spent around 600 hours on the game, the rest has been idling to prevent item degrading.
Warframe gameplay is nothing short of amazing. Movement is fluid, animations don't conflict, and the ability to vault and barrel roll through countless maps is nothing short of amazing.
Weapons handle amazingly, and melee combat, for the first time I've seen in a shooter to date, is fully fleshed out as not only a potent alternative to gunplay, but a tool to use alongside it in more ways that a simple destiny-style quick strike.
The plentitude of both co-op and PvP game mods makes gameplay versatile and fresh. However, Archwing missions are tedious, and I wish that submersible missions would simply cease to exist entirely, as there is nothing more annoying that trying to control a spacecraft in viscous water.
Each planet is unique, and locations are semirandomly generated, with set sections combined in diffrent ways, so that locations are both familiar and new
As for plot....I'm not going to lie. Up until about halfway through the game, you will not see almost any plot. The game makes you be devoted enough to famr your way through abut half of the planets before the plot appears, and when it does, it just seems like pointless lore at first...Until the quest called the Second Dream. Now, I will say nothing about this, as the game does a good job of keeoing it secret, but this quest arc not only provides quite a bit of lore, but one of the best twists that lead to a whole new gameplay mechanic that I have ever seen.
For a game that never makes you pay for literally anything, this is a must have. It runs well, has innovative mechanics,and is all together one of the most enjoyable games I have ever played.

A really fun and unique medieval slasher game in both first and third person. It comes with 8 official gamemodes, Team Objective being the most popular and 4 classes; The archer (ranged), man at arms (light melee), vanguard (medium melee) and the knight (heavy melee). It has a very unique and humorous voice acting along with unique combat system which is bascily one of its kind.
- Mostly sieges and raids.
- Capture mode.
- Last man standing.
- Earn enough points to win over your team.
- Control an area for a specific amount of time to win.
- A co-op PVE mode where you defeat AI controlled minions. Each kill gives XP to unlock gear.
- Kill everything you see.
- 1v1 mode.
Do not expect too much realism since big part of the combat is about manipulating the swings with movement. (Visually game breaking for the realism searcher).
Community is extremly toxic but very nice and enjoyable in the right company. (Rude behavior. teamkilling and votekicks).
Developers don't work much on the game and it has alot of bugs and glitches. Only releasing skins and such at the moment. (Still playable though).
Only a basic tutorial, so new players will have a rough time to get into the game (Can and probably will take thousands of hours to become good).
Steam workshop is supported and you can make your own mods for the game with the developers tutorials online.

The game shows great promise but in it's current state it's unplayable unless you play solo and mess with all the server settings.  Also the build system is horribly broken, the walls and other items don't snap quite where you want them to when you encounter uneven terrain, and you will.  Domesticating dinos and using them is an awesome idea but the progression path is unclear and you'll eventually hit some dinos that just wipe the floor with you.  The grinding is too much for too little.   I personally love the graphics in this game, others will disagree there, but I think they're great, in fact it's one of the aspects that drew me to the game.  The game is horribly optmized thou and the load time at least a few minutes (with a 1080 card, longer with less than the best hardware) every time you enter the world, although I've found it does tend to load faster on linux than windows.  The crafting system is cool but the game forces you to play online where you can get ganked easy because they don't give you enough points to learn all the things you'll need to be self sufficent ... of course you can tweak the server settings and run your own server for single player if that's your thing.
I don't know why but for some reason the focus seems to be on adding new dino's rather than focusing on balancing the game and fixing the frequent crashing issues.
This game is both awesome and terrible.  I'm not sure how else to put it.

It is recommended whenever it goes on sale. Maybe when it becomes fully released it will go on sale. Do not spend the 60 dollars for early release, this is steam after all so patience is worth it. You feel like you can lose everything, but as long as you level up it gets better. I have been wiped before in pvp, but me and my brother found ways to survive them. We hide our important stuff in places that keep them from getting it at once. That way we can recover and rebuild. It's cruel and unforgiving, but I played Dark Souls so i'm no stranger to an unfair world. It does become enjoyable and the idea of getting sweet revenge on griefers is great (I said idea, i'm still getting to that part). I got this game for 15 dollars, it is worth that money. Not 60 dollars for a game that suffers problems with glitching and well it's tough love attitude. It's not for everyone, but for the hardcore survivalists it definitely is.

This game is a game I would reccommend to people who like the grind and the satisfaction of getting new things such as weapons and warframes. No this is not one of those p2w games. I think its a play 2 win type of game. The only way to acutally get good is to play the game. Which takes a HELL A LOT OF TIME (unless you buy stuff).
PROS:
There are many different types of warframes, and they all have a unique features. There's also a lot of weapons, guns, kubrows, missions, etc. It's a game where you can team up and play with your friends and have a great time. It's a very satisfying game and burns time FAST. The price for the plat isn't that bad, 20 dollars for 370 plat isn't that bad tbh. And there's trading too, so you can trade stuff with other players to speed things up. Another pro is that all the missions aren't on land. There's archwing missions, where you can fly around space and kick♥♥♥♥♥and it's soooo cooool.
CONS:
Too much grind. The grind is literally unreal. Students like me wont be able to catch up to what's going on and play. The missions are repetitive, and they're all pretty much the same, but on different planets. The Warframes are hard to get without paying money, but even with paying money it's still hard because all the good primed warframes are in the vault so you have to wait till they release it from the vault. Another con is THE LAG. This game is NOT suitable for people with really weak and cheap PC's. If you try to run it on a really horrible and cheap PC, it's only gonna go 10 or 20 FPS max, maybe even 5 FPS, especially in infested missions since there's so many graphics involved with it.
Overall, I think this game is pretty good. I would give it a 8.5/10

TL:DR- Essentially, whats good and bad point by point, use the parts below to help + i have no idea how to do the text formatting so deal with it. If you can't decide on if you want to play the game or not, read below.
Straight up, either you will like the game or you will hate it, it is the nature of the game. So I have played this for 49 hours and I loved it until now, there is some variability in the weapons and gear however most of it is locked behind platinum or end game tier planets. Now with some obvious stuff out of the way;
The good stuff;
1.The not one size fits all idea behind it
2. The variation (what little there is) in the map design
3. Good with or without friends/other players and how seemless it
4. The part where you can set up your own "shop" and trade
The bad stuff;
1. The huge amounts of platinum required for certain in-game items ie. warframes
2. The grinding
3. Some incredibly difficult enemies/bosses
4. That most of the content required to deal with certain things early on, is locked on higher tier planets
Those were the main things I could think of
Now the longer version of the points above
The good stuff;
1. So there is something like 32 different warframes, which is like 32 diffferent classes. This allows players (later on) to change how they play for different mission types however, there are only 3 available to new players (I'll finish this with the paywall part). The weapons seem to me to be highly diverse also promoting different playstyles such as stealth or just really offensive or maybe a hybrid inbetween, whatever you choose to play. Also with every weapon is like 200 different mods for them, all with varying amounts of upgrade space.
2.  With the maps, from what I learned, they bring them out in "tile sets", each with their own enemies and enviroment, which is great. The problem is that there just isn't (imo) enough difference in some maps on planets, as I have done three different types of mission on a single map, some even at the same start point. I can't say much more except that it does get boring after so long.
3. I have played mostly by my self and have done many a co-op mission, and it does help to have more people on certain mission types, such as survival or defense where it can be difficult to defend all sides of the object (such as infestation reactors). Sometimes in missions, if you haven't completed an objective yet, you can invite allies/friends to help you in the mission. I have not experienced the conclave nor random people helping me so I can't say much there but I have experienced the clan (kinda) , it does require alot of resources and usually would be best to set up late game due to most things requiring nano-spores.
4. OMG, I have to say if you have surplus resources (which are rare), you could go into a relay (or Maroo's Bazzar idk) and there is a person you speak to and they allow you to set up a shop, where you can trade for items or grab a bargain on a resource you have been hunting for a while. Not much else to say there
The Bad bits;
1. So to get most items in game, you have to grind your butt off, however there are some resources which can only be obtained either late game or by completing alerts. Warframes are incredibly expensive to craft (still haven't been able to craft one yet :( ) and on the market, they cost near stupid amounts of platinum (the purchasable currency) to buy whole which usually comes to a price of something like £20 (no idea but it is close) for the warframe. Not to mention that colours and decoration for your warframe isn't free, oh no, if you want colours you need to pay, same with changing your armour or helmet.
2. Holy crap, out of my 49 hours played, at least 15 of it has to be grinding due to just doing missions again and again for that rubedo/plastids/gallium/neurodes, it is insane that I had to do a mission at least 20 times to get a single neurode. It is a huge part of the game and unless you are willing to spend hours killing bosses for blueprints or doing random missions for a specific resource, then this isn't your game mate. (don't talk to anyone about grinding if they have the equinox warframe unless they paid for it)
3. The worst by far for me has to be the midgame point at Europa, and the boss that resides there. The raptor/s, which are giant versions of the ospreys, but their gun has a volley of shield devouring aoes followed by precision explosive rounds. I play a volt and I find that I hate shield devouring enemies due to the fact that I am shield (mostly) but this boss takes the biscuit for me, I changed my main weapon twice to combat this boss and my friend managed (somehow) to get a frost warframe and it still proved too much. If you thought that was it, you'd be wrong as a second one follows soon after with 5-6 small drones which never fail to kill me immediatly upon contact because I cannot deal with them as a Volt. Imo, the worst boss so far. About the worst enemies thou, Bursas, they are like tanks with groundpound set to max. My friend who is playing Excalibur, dies to them like a hot knife through butter, but I as a Volt with melee only, wipe the floor with it. This is why I think the game is at somepoints extremely unbalanced.
4. So for an example a weapon called the Drakgoon (or something close) is a fairly good shotgun, but requires a material only known as nano spores, which are on Saturn. Most blueprints for weapons that are useful early on require nano spores, and that I see is the only resource which is locked off but almost everything needs it to be built. Nuf said
Conclusion; If you feel like grinding your fingers and brain to the point where your gloves have more fingers (and brains) than you, then good, play to your heart's content. Whereas the opposite, if you hate grinding, please never touch this game ever. By the way, I am expecting "git gud" comments so I'll say I have gotten good and have been for at least 20 hours now.

Ok, so I've been playing this game pretty heavily for the last few weeks, including the Deadlis Warrior mode and I must say  I'm really enjoying it!  it's  a huge breathe of fresh air.  A first-person  melee combat game (with some ranged stuff thrown in) with a variety of classes each with thier own play style.  From the heavily armored knight and his poleaxe, mace, swords or crossbow;  to the lighter more trickster implied classes like the ninja and pirate with thier merried of annoyances and traps they have at thier disposal.  Of the ranged options its all fairly standard:  Knight can get a crossbow, samurai can get a large "Yumi Bow",  Spartans can hurl thier spears at people,  ninjas get things such as shuriken/blinding powder and the like and pirates get flintlock firearms and a molotov cocktail type thing....and the viking can hurl pretty much anything it gets its hands on.
What suprises me the most about this game is the attention to physics and colision,  especially when it comes to how you play defensively.  some  classes gain varing shapes nad types of shields which can be held up and interposed between atttackers and yourself (or an ally if timed right) whos effectiveness is based on the size of the shield. while most classes get a blocking naimation that not only needs to be timed well but also has specific strikes or somes of atacks its good at repelling.
For instance, the ninja and samurai have a horizontal almost shoulder height block that makes them excelelnt at deflecting vertical attacks while leaving its lower body incredibly vulnerable to low attacks.
All in all this game (especialy deadliest warrior, which features the classes I've mentioned and is the version I have the most experience with) is very engaging and its a proper fun time mashing peoples faces in with my mace.  For anyone looking for a good semi-competitive game to play where you go at it like manly men from the middle ages  this is definetly something you should check out.   There is hilarity in combat and sweet sweet viceral carnage to be had as you mete out your honor and prowes over the internet.  Just be carefull,  you will be suprised during yoru first couple of sessions  with things like being hi by random blinding powder  or watching a one on one fight in a 30 man free-for-all quickly turn into a massive melee in the blink of an eye as more and more people find you and enter the fray.

To preface, I've never reached the endgame bosses. Regardless, I've had alot of fun in this game, and have put in more hours than I'm proud to admit.
The game definitely plays best with friends / tribemates, not necessarily for PvP. The game can be buggy at times, and though it looks beautiful, that also means its a resource hog and it will demand much from your PC.
The game's progression systems can be manipulated by your server admins to suit the likings of the players. On top of that, the mechanics themselves, while sometimes very demanding especially when you're new to the game, always feel like they justly reward the player's efforts. This game has a long lifespan if you don't mind the grind.
There're alot of things in this game that a survivor has to deal with: violent dinos, needing food and water, weather conditions, the dreaded fall of night. Encountering new biomes and new dinosaurs is always thrilling and exciting.
A drawback to the game is it's obtusity: I always have Ark Wiki open on my phone in order to quickly research what I'm doing no matter what I'm doing - I seriously couldn't imagine playing this game without external resources. It doesn't spoil the game entirely, but it is erksome when you have to stop playing so you can read up on how to obtain Wyvern Milk, or how Moschops taming is supposed to work, or how knocking out a dino with a Narcotic Trap will make it untamable - and because of how the game is structured (ie. it isn't), I can't think of an organic way to implement these things into the game itself.
Even the Recipe notes that infrequently drop as loot can have their own measurements which aren't intuitive (eg. "18 dallops of Narcotic"). There's even a note that can drop which helps translate these measurements, but looking it up on the internet is always far easier since you should be doing that incessently. Playing this game would be frustrating otherwise.
The progression system for crafting is through "Engrams" of which you can spend points to unlock - these points obtained through leveling. I love base-building in games, which is a large part of the crafting system in this game, but beyond that the Engrams have alot of variety that give you several avenues of accomplishing your goals as you advance in the game. In the early parts of the game, killing minor dinos like raptors or crocs will feel like major accomplishments and survival can feel genuinely satisfying. Later on, you'll have big bad dinos of your own that can shred through nearly anything the game tries to throw at you.
I would suggest to anyone going into this game to research quality-of-life mods (S+ is almost a must if you like base-building like I do) and admins to look into server settings that will make the game more enjoyable (the base taming and baby-raising mechanics are painful and can take hours, detering casual play).
I received this game for free, but as a Steam gift from my friend who insisted that we play together. This was a year or so ago, before the price shot up. I left that box unchecked for my review here, but I wanted to disclose that anyway. I wasn't given this game from any official source, unless my friend isn't telling me everything about himself.
Overall, I would recommend this game, but bring or make friends, do your research and have alot of time. Still, at 60$ USD, I want to say to new players to hold off on their purchase in the chance that the price might go down. Do I think the game could definitely be worth that much if it was completed? Yes, absolutely. It's a big project packed with alot of fun content and you can tell that the game creators have a passion for the game and churning out tons of fun and interesting content, but it is unfinished and charging this much for the game feels a bit unwarranted at this point, especially since many of the troublesome aspects -
the game's obtusity;
finding a suitable server and group of friends;
the time commitment - or learning to change the settings in order to avoid such long time commitments;
choosing between official or non-official servers;
bugginess (which I don't think will be 100% solved, as even AAA titles don't bother to catch everything);
- all act as a barrier-to-entry for the game to new players. And, while it might be easy to say, "Well, those players should just get over it and learn all that stuff if they want to play ARK properly," the truth is, you can spend your 60$ somewhere else with a game that won't ask this much from you and have a good time there too. There are plenty of games for 60$ and under that can offer you as rewarding a time while asking you to bring nothing else to the table.
In closing, the most difficult aspect is the time commitment and tribemates. This game benefits from sinking in alot of hours and reaping the rewards of your labors with others. Short review:
Fast paced and fun medieval combat game. This game good and enjoyable but not as good as Mount & Blade: Warband.
Full review:
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare should be considered as Call of Duty of Medieval combat games. This is both good and bad thing. The game is fast paced, fun and very casual (which can be considered both good and bad thing). It also has nice visuals compared to Mount & blade Warband.
Now to the bad things that being Cod like causes. Like CoD the game focuses on infantry and does not have drivable vehicles (in this case horses). The lack of horses backfires as a lack of variety and even though the horses aren’t that realistic in Mount & Blade: Warband, riding the horses is one of the most enjoyable things in that game. Small maps and focusing on infantry combat is also seen in the fact that ranged weapons are very unrealistic and bland to use in Chivalry. Infantry combat on the other hand is fun, but not as fun as in Mount & Blade: Warband, because the directional attack of mount & Blade Warband is more immersive once the player learns to use it compared to Chivalry’s choice of attack methods.
Despite these weaknesses the game is fun nevertheless. The only real problem of this game is that Mount & Blade: Warband beats Chivalry in everything else but graphics and being more fast paced. The latter of these is also an opinion not a thing that is objectively good or bad.
My recommendation for customers is to buy Mount & Blade: Warband, because it is far superior to Chivalry: Medieval Warfare and it has both Single and Multiplayer. Buy Chivalry Medieval warfare only if you consider yourself extremely casual player or if you already own Mount & Blade Warband and would like to try something a bit different.  I have no experience on War of Roses but from what I have heard, it sucks so Chivalry: Medieval Warfare is your best alternative in the rare case that you would not like Mount & Blade: Warband.

I have legitemately only spent around 600 hours on the game, the rest has been idling to prevent item degrading.
Warframe gameplay is nothing short of amazing. Movement is fluid, animations don't conflict, and the ability to vault and barrel roll through countless maps is nothing short of amazing.
Weapons handle amazingly, and melee combat, for the first time I've seen in a shooter to date, is fully fleshed out as not only a potent alternative to gunplay, but a tool to use alongside it in more ways that a simple destiny-style quick strike.
The plentitude of both co-op and PvP game mods makes gameplay versatile and fresh. However, Archwing missions are tedious, and I wish that submersible missions would simply cease to exist entirely, as there is nothing more annoying that trying to control a spacecraft in viscous water.
Each planet is unique, and locations are semirandomly generated, with set sections combined in diffrent ways, so that locations are both familiar and new
As for plot....I'm not going to lie. Up until about halfway through the game, you will not see almost any plot. The game makes you be devoted enough to famr your way through abut half of the planets before the plot appears, and when it does, it just seems like pointless lore at first...Until the quest called the Second Dream. Now, I will say nothing about this, as the game does a good job of keeoing it secret, but this quest arc not only provides quite a bit of lore, but one of the best twists that lead to a whole new gameplay mechanic that I have ever seen.
For a game that never makes you pay for literally anything, this is a must have. It runs well, has innovative mechanics,and is all together one of the most enjoyable games I have ever played.

Not my favoite clicker game on Steam, despite the fact it is one of the most popular, Clicker Heroes is about as basic as it gets. You click on enemies to deal damage, collect cold, and repeat. Every ten enemies gets you the next area, and after so many areas you get a boss. The farther you go, the tougher the enemies get and the more gold they drop.
You use said gold to upgrade your clicking damage and to hire allies who will do DPS, essentially playing the game for you. It's at this point you go attend to life in general, or play another game, whatever; you come back to heaps of gold, which you spend on new heroes or upgrades to the existing ones, which in turn lets you get farther and farther.
Eventually one of your heroes, Amenhotep, will learn the ability "Ascension" which resets everything but rewards you with Hero Souls, which give you a whopping 10% increase in DPS each. You can keep these to get through the game faster, or spend them on bonuses, the downsides being you lose the DPS in the process.
The game is good, don't get me wrong. But if you want a good clicker game I'd recommend Time Clickers instead. No micro-transactions, and in that game, when you spend its equivelant to Hero Souls, you don't lose your bonus DPS.
If you take this game seriously, you're an idiot.

I would suggest taking Excalibur as your starter frame, as he is a very good offensive monster. His Ultimate can punch through walls, obstacles and enemies, hitting everything in his path. Then aim for Loki and Rhino parts. You will have to grind missions several times to get the parts... I had to kill Jackal probably 30 times before I obtained all the parts I needed for Rhino. Like people say, This is a grind but with no pay wall.(You can, if, again... you're lazy)
There are 4 Rotations for Excavation, Defense, Interception, and Survival endless fissures, and go A A B C. Every 5 minutes in Survival is a rotation, 5 waves in defense is a rotation, and every 2 Excavators(in Void Fissures) is a rotation, and every time you decode a message in interception is a rotation.
Fissures are life. Always do endless fissures as long as possible. You get Credit, Experience(Affinity) and Resource boosts for every rotation by 25% for the game. These endless missions are THE best way to level up your gear.
Need relics? There are 4 types that drop from different areas with a wide range of difficulty.
Lith Relics - Spear, Mars (Defense) these can drop from every rotation. So play lots and get lots of relics.
Meso - IO, Jupiter (Defense) the first two rotations(10 waves) drop Meso relics. You can simply leave after the 2nd rotation and repeat, or stay for a chance at a mix of Endo, Meso/Neo relics, and Mods
Neo/Axi - Xini, Eris (Interception) the first two rotations drop Neo Relics, the second two rotations drop Axi. Another good spot for these relics is Heiracon, Pluto (Excavation) which has a chance of dropping Endo, Relics, and Mods. Be weary, Neo/Axi relic farming missions AND fissure missions difficulty scales quickly, so come prepared.
If you're leveling a frame, do not take any weapons that are not Mastered(rank 30). As Experience(Affinity) is split among everything you have equipped. Taking multiple items that require Affinity to level will make leveling the frame/weapon longer. If you're leveling melee weapons, find your way to Kappa, Sedna with Loki or Ivara and assassinate everyone(using a charged assassination by holding down the left mouse will increase damage and cause the body to vanish). Stealth kills give an experience multiplier up to 500%. Some primary weapons can be leveled this way too, granted you use Silencing Mods/Frames to give you stealth abilities.
Need Platinum? Plat is mega easy to come by.. Do fissures, open those nifty relics you got, sell the parts(or craft your weapons). Simple as that. Don't forget to check your Void Traces often at lower Mastery Ranks, as you can only hold so many until you level up more. I personally only spend my void traces on making Relics become Radiant by spending 100 traces, and crafting Derelict keys. If you can open enough relics to find whole sets of frames/weapons that can substantially increase your Plat generation.
There are plenty of guides online. Try to find a decent clan to join, as they can be a big help. Some people may even be nice enough to "Taxi" you to places. When googling things, try to stick with "Players Helping Players" Warframe forums and Reddit. Most everything else isn't kept up to date.

(2) Freezes and disk i/o surges when traveling the map on a flyer.
(3) Annoying Dino's added that seem to have no other purpose than to ANNOY; e.g., Ichthyornis and Pegomastax.
(4) Unmodded, the building system (fence supports, foundations, walls, ceilings) is terrible. Structures Plus (S+) solves many problems, but I believe the core building system should not be that bad and one should not have to resort to a mod for a better building system.
(5) Finally, the Primitive Plus DLC should be fully compiled (and may be by release time) so that I can start the game and not have to wait 20 minutes for it to be ready to play.
