TL:DR- Essentially, whats good and bad point by point, use the parts below to help + i have no idea how to do the text formatting so deal with it. If you can't decide on if you want to play the game or not, read below.
Straight up, either you will like the game or you will hate it, it is the nature of the game. So I have played this for 49 hours and I loved it until now, there is some variability in the weapons and gear however most of it is locked behind platinum or end game tier planets. Now with some obvious stuff out of the way;
The good stuff;
1.The not one size fits all idea behind it
2. The variation (what little there is) in the map design
3. Good with or without friends/other players and how seemless it
4. The part where you can set up your own "shop" and trade
The bad stuff;
1. The huge amounts of platinum required for certain in-game items ie. warframes
2. The grinding
3. Some incredibly difficult enemies/bosses
4. That most of the content required to deal with certain things early on, is locked on higher tier planets
Those were the main things I could think of
Now the longer version of the points above
The good stuff;
1. So there is something like 32 different warframes, which is like 32 diffferent classes. This allows players (later on) to change how they play for different mission types however, there are only 3 available to new players (I'll finish this with the paywall part). The weapons seem to me to be highly diverse also promoting different playstyles such as stealth or just really offensive or maybe a hybrid inbetween, whatever you choose to play. Also with every weapon is like 200 different mods for them, all with varying amounts of upgrade space.
2.  With the maps, from what I learned, they bring them out in "tile sets", each with their own enemies and enviroment, which is great. The problem is that there just isn't (imo) enough difference in some maps on planets, as I have done three different types of mission on a single map, some even at the same start point. I can't say much more except that it does get boring after so long.
3. I have played mostly by my self and have done many a co-op mission, and it does help to have more people on certain mission types, such as survival or defense where it can be difficult to defend all sides of the object (such as infestation reactors). Sometimes in missions, if you haven't completed an objective yet, you can invite allies/friends to help you in the mission. I have not experienced the conclave nor random people helping me so I can't say much there but I have experienced the clan (kinda) , it does require alot of resources and usually would be best to set up late game due to most things requiring nano-spores.
4. OMG, I have to say if you have surplus resources (which are rare), you could go into a relay (or Maroo's Bazzar idk) and there is a person you speak to and they allow you to set up a shop, where you can trade for items or grab a bargain on a resource you have been hunting for a while. Not much else to say there
The Bad bits;
1. So to get most items in game, you have to grind your butt off, however there are some resources which can only be obtained either late game or by completing alerts. Warframes are incredibly expensive to craft (still haven't been able to craft one yet :( ) and on the market, they cost near stupid amounts of platinum (the purchasable currency) to buy whole which usually comes to a price of something like £20 (no idea but it is close) for the warframe. Not to mention that colours and decoration for your warframe isn't free, oh no, if you want colours you need to pay, same with changing your armour or helmet.
2. Holy crap, out of my 49 hours played, at least 15 of it has to be grinding due to just doing missions again and again for that rubedo/plastids/gallium/neurodes, it is insane that I had to do a mission at least 20 times to get a single neurode. It is a huge part of the game and unless you are willing to spend hours killing bosses for blueprints or doing random missions for a specific resource, then this isn't your game mate. (don't talk to anyone about grinding if they have the equinox warframe unless they paid for it)
3. The worst by far for me has to be the midgame point at Europa, and the boss that resides there. The raptor/s, which are giant versions of the ospreys, but their gun has a volley of shield devouring aoes followed by precision explosive rounds. I play a volt and I find that I hate shield devouring enemies due to the fact that I am shield (mostly) but this boss takes the biscuit for me, I changed my main weapon twice to combat this boss and my friend managed (somehow) to get a frost warframe and it still proved too much. If you thought that was it, you'd be wrong as a second one follows soon after with 5-6 small drones which never fail to kill me immediatly upon contact because I cannot deal with them as a Volt. Imo, the worst boss so far. About the worst enemies thou, Bursas, they are like tanks with groundpound set to max. My friend who is playing Excalibur, dies to them like a hot knife through butter, but I as a Volt with melee only, wipe the floor with it. This is why I think the game is at somepoints extremely unbalanced.
4. So for an example a weapon called the Drakgoon (or something close) is a fairly good shotgun, but requires a material only known as nano spores, which are on Saturn. Most blueprints for weapons that are useful early on require nano spores, and that I see is the only resource which is locked off but almost everything needs it to be built. Nuf said
Conclusion; If you feel like grinding your fingers and brain to the point where your gloves have more fingers (and brains) than you, then good, play to your heart's content. Whereas the opposite, if you hate grinding, please never touch this game ever. By the way, I am expecting "git gud" comments so I'll say I have gotten good and have been for at least 20 hours now.

Out of all the fururistic space shooting games, I'd have to say Warframe is the best. Though with recent updates, its not as fun as it used to be, it's still an amazing game. The combat is well done and the controls aren't ridiculous or convoluded like in other games. Though the game runs on microtransactions, it isnt 'pay to win'; its more like 'pay to get a larger selection'but most things that aren't cosmetic can still be earned by regular means. But the most important part of Warframe is probably the movement. Warframe offers fluid, easy to use movement, that doesn't just make it fun to play but also to watch.
The game gives you an incredible range of movement that  that ofers way more freedom than most games. Gliding, running up walls, and sliding are only some of the things you can do, but don't worry cause while all these things are available, the game will rarely have parts that will force you to do any of these things. You can take it slow and stealthy, or fast and fluid; you can even just brute your way through things if you really want. There aren't that many games that give you as much freedom as warframe does, so trust me; you won't be disappointed.

Warframe... a Free to Play Game that ACTUALLY reigns true to the name F2P. First off I'll take the time to say this. Take your time with this game's story. Don't rush through (or get rushed) like me. Otherwise you'll be a higher level with no clue what happened in the first 3-4 quests. Anyway Warframe is a third-person space ninja shooter platformer that has randomly generated levels. Warframe has you take control over an amnesiac space ninja on a quest to grind the ever-living ♥♥♥♥ out of the planets you come across. Jokes aside Warframe IS a bit (well more than a bit) of a grindfest. You grind to get a gun, you grind to get a sword, you grind to get parts for a new frame, you grind to get prime stuff that's not even guaranteed. If you do get everything you want you have to wait 1 minute to 3 days for it to finish.
With that aside Warframe has a really great story, solid controls, engaging battles, randomly generated levels (as said before), active and majorly kind community, active devs who livestream future updates, fun and unique classes, strange interesting and downright great weaponry. I highly recommended Warfame if you just want to relax on the weekend after a hellish work day. Just be prepared for a hellish grinding experience.

If you are new to the Steam community and just got your hands on a fresh new gaming pc or if you are broke at the moment to buy some games, I HIGHLY recommend downloading Warframe. Warframe is a free to play game where you can navigate the solar system as a badass space ninja. There are sooo many reasons why I love this game but there are three most popular( I think this goes for everyone that supports the game). These Reasons are:
The variety of things you can do to your warframe is ridiculous from Stances to Modding. You can  equip so many things on your warframes and change their color scheme, armor sets, sigils, synadanas, weapons, skins, and so many other things. Not to mention, you can obtain every single warframe in-game by playing. It will require LOTS of Grinding to obtain the warframes of your choice. Then, modding your warframe requires mods that act like cards with buffs and other skills for your warframe. This is where your creativity comes in to make the ultimate build. This goes along for weapons too.
The gameplay is the core element of the game. It's so fun using the abilities of your warframes to wreak havoc on the toughest enemies. You can also slash and hack your way through a mission using a beast melee weapon you built or a primary weapon to quickly extinguish your enemies. Mostly though, the way your warframe can easily travel and manouver over obstacles really fast makes you feel like a true space ninja by flying in midair and doing flips, climbing walls, and just being a freakin' ninja!
Last, but not least....
The best part about this game is that there are other players willing to help you grind. There are so many things you can do with groups or with friends. You have the ability to trade with one another which makes the grinding a little more easier, making clans to make friends and grind as a whole. Warframe truly is the best free to play game in my opinion and If you are new, please try out this game, give it a go. The veterans and more experienced players are in charge of you and are willing to help you learn how to play the game or help you fight a high level boss. This game is an example of a Free-To-Play done right!
If you made it this far I want to thank you so much for reading and I hope you are at least somewhat interested in getting into Warframe.

Numerous bugs during missions that cause you to lose everything you found.
P2W market with equipment mechanics that make acquiring things without real money objectivly worse than without (Get item instantly vs farm for a day then allow item to craft for up to 72 hours).
Currency used by players IS the premium real money, so not only does paying money get you the character and weapons you want, but allows you to buy everything else that cant be found in the market.
To make the premium currency more appealing, playing the game without it causes you to constantly run into the kinds of timers you see in ♥♥♥♥♥♥ mobile games. Want a new warframe? At very minium (assuming you make all base componants at the same time and instantly craft the warframe when they are done) takes 84 hours. New weapon? 12-24 hours. Why? Literally no reason other than "Putting up arbitrary walls to block player progress then selling the solution makes lots of money".
Its not a bad game, infact its pretty fun. The gunplay is solid and skill based movement speed is great to see in shooters again. But the positives do not outweigh the negatives. This game is build from the ground up to make you pay money or pay by spending every second of your free time playing. I dont take issue with a game selling cosmetics or boosters to help pay for a F2P game, what I do take issue with is being forced to wait 3 full days before I can get something I spent the past week farming the materials for and seeing a little button at the bottom of the crafting window saying to me "Hey, if you get 50 fun bucks you can instantly get the item you want. Dont think about the fact that the crafting timers are only there so I can literally sell you your free time. Just think about how its only a buck to not wait 3 ♥♥♥♥ing days".
I could put up with these terrible game mechanics if I didnt regularly get screwed out of blueprints, materials, and money on missions when they bug out and lock themselves. If you're going to make me wait days tell you allow me to use something I crafted, dont remove about 10% of all the progress and item gathering I do with your horrible netcode and buggy missions that are only slightly more stable than an open world Bethesda game.
This game does not respect your time, therefore it doesnt deserve it either.

Anyhow, Warframe is a game about space ninjas. You will be doing just that. Flying around maps with the unique parkour systems, while weilding firearms and blades. Some weapons are a bit dull or underpowered compared to another weapon, yes, but the number of said weapons is very small plus you might value one of these weapons because you enjoy the way it feels/plays.

I've got over 500 hours in game and STILL get excited about, and look forward to playing this game everyday. There are so many things this game gets right. First thing that I have really come to appreciate is the dinos themselves. they are all unique and serve very different purposes and roles, and display different behavior. they aren't just a different balance of stats with a different skin on them. They may help gather a specific resource, or help tame or level other dinos, they may be a scout mount, or a war mount, even mounts of the same class, like flying mounts, are different, some are fast, some fly longer without rest and can haul more, some are more suited to combat, some aid in survival, or warning you bad weather or preditors are coming. They also drop different resources, so even hunting a variety is necessary. They have done a great job of making the world feel alive with a variety of creatures of all sizes from tiny to huge, they hunt  and attack each other, and all have a place in the world and food chain. they also require different strategy and tactics to tame, making each tame a unique experience.
the second thing they get right is the difficulty curve, you as a little human are definitely a part of that food chain and when you start, you are very near the bottom! they do a great job of teaching you right off the bat it's a big scary world out there, and it gets scarier at night, you survive by wits and sometimes luck rather than brute force... as you level your survivor and get more experienced as a player surviving gets easier, but it never feels like a walk in the park, i've gotten over confident and gotten a wake up call more than once.
the third thing i like is the different DLC's and flavors of the game, vanilla Ark is awesome, but if you don't want the more modern high tech parts, and want a more rustic feel you can do primitive plus, if you aren't challenged enough on the island you can try your hand at the desert in scorched earth, if you want more fantasy elements you have ragnarok... add modding to that and you can get TONS of mileage out of this game and find a game mode that suits your mood that day.
I have not played on a PVP server, but the PVE community has been friendly and helpful, it's online play and the developers are obviously not responsible for any jerks playing of course, but on the whole my experience has been a pleasant one when it comes to interactions with other players.
lastly I like the variety of things you can craft and build... you start with tying together rocks and sticks and can work up to crafting high tech Iron man level Scifi gear, you can build boats, castles, undersea bases, mobile bases on the back of giant dinos on land, sea, and air... even if you go primitive plus and don't have the huge range of different technologies, they make up for it with more variety, different weapons, tools, food/drink, gear, and furniture decor. and no one person can learn it all, so you can try different approaches on different play throughs.
it's not perfect yet, but they seem to be doing a good job of balancing fixing existing issues and adding new content, i haven't experienced anything game breaking or so discouraging i even thought about losing interest. The devs seem really invested in the community and appear to share our passion for the game. In my humble opinion they've been proactive and responsive to players, and deserve a bit more patience than some of the other reviewers have given them.
in short I highly recommend the game and feel it's worth the price tag whether it be the early access price or $60 full release price. It's a quality game that's flexible enough to appeal to different play styles, and has enough depth to keep it interesting for hours on end! All wrapped in a beautiful living world with mighty beasts big and small!

$60 is a joke for an unfinished game. The idea is great, however, execution is horrible. Be ready for weeks of grinding to build any of the more advanced items/base, logging in on daily basis or more often to keep things running (feed dinos, water plants, fix minor damage to the base)... All until you get raided and need to start over. And oh, btw, once you do get raided forget about rebuilding your base and regaining the little bit of power you had. It won't happen. Whoever did destroy your base and killed your dinos (which btw is super fast and easy) won't let you rebuild your base. No matter if you play solo or in a large group. Chances are null.
So, you might be thinking, another frustrated noob player. Then think about it from the winner perspective. Your group (you don't stand a chance solo), your group owns most advanced base and strongest dinos. Possibly all the strongest dinos so that your enemies can't be a match for you. You control access to all most advanced resources (so that your enemies can't be a match for you). You enjoy raiding whoever builds up a little bit. But you still keep everyone in check, not letting them to develop too much. Where is the fun playing a game where no one stands a chance against you? And you don't want anyone to develop a little too much. Why? One bad day, most of your group can't login, someone raids your base and you're done. Oh, and keep in mind you still need to login on daily basis to keep things running. Running = your base having all resources to keep running (yeah, grind, grind, grind) and checking on all opponents basis, raiding them if needed. Not fun. I don't know which side is more miserable.
In short, this game needs some very serious rebalancing to be fun to play. You'll enjoy first few days, maybe a week and then you'll just hate it. Not because of how badly you will be beaten. Because you will know how super fun this game could be, and why in the current state it can not.

If you are new to the Steam community and just got your hands on a fresh new gaming pc or if you are broke at the moment to buy some games, I HIGHLY recommend downloading Warframe. Warframe is a free to play game where you can navigate the solar system as a badass space ninja. There are sooo many reasons why I love this game but there are three most popular( I think this goes for everyone that supports the game). These Reasons are:
The variety of things you can do to your warframe is ridiculous from Stances to Modding. You can  equip so many things on your warframes and change their color scheme, armor sets, sigils, synadanas, weapons, skins, and so many other things. Not to mention, you can obtain every single warframe in-game by playing. It will require LOTS of Grinding to obtain the warframes of your choice. Then, modding your warframe requires mods that act like cards with buffs and other skills for your warframe. This is where your creativity comes in to make the ultimate build. This goes along for weapons too.
The gameplay is the core element of the game. It's so fun using the abilities of your warframes to wreak havoc on the toughest enemies. You can also slash and hack your way through a mission using a beast melee weapon you built or a primary weapon to quickly extinguish your enemies. Mostly though, the way your warframe can easily travel and manouver over obstacles really fast makes you feel like a true space ninja by flying in midair and doing flips, climbing walls, and just being a freakin' ninja!
Last, but not least....
The best part about this game is that there are other players willing to help you grind. There are so many things you can do with groups or with friends. You have the ability to trade with one another which makes the grinding a little more easier, making clans to make friends and grind as a whole. Warframe truly is the best free to play game in my opinion and If you are new, please try out this game, give it a go. The veterans and more experienced players are in charge of you and are willing to help you learn how to play the game or help you fight a high level boss. This game is an example of a Free-To-Play done right!
If you made it this far I want to thank you so much for reading and I hope you are at least somewhat interested in getting into Warframe.

Jokes aside Warframe IS a bit (well more than a bit) of a grindfest. You grind to get a gun, you grind to get a sword, you grind to get parts for a new frame, you grind to get prime stuff that's not even guaranteed. If you do get everything you want you have to wait 1 minute to 3 days for it to finish.
With that aside Warframe has a really great story, solid controls, engaging battles, randomly generated levels (as said before), active and majorly kind community, active devs who livestream future updates, fun and unique classes, strange interesting and downright great weaponry. I highly recommended Warfame if you just want to relax on the weekend after a hellish work day. Just be prepared for a hellish grinding experience.

So, is Clicker Heroes a good game? No, but I wouldn't say otherwise either. It's really addicting and is fun in the beginning, but as you progress it starts to get boring. Really boring. The gameplay is simple: Click monsters until they they die and give you money. Use the money to buy stuff that makes you deal more damage. Repeat.
See why it gets boring? Oh, and it only takes longer to progress the more you play, which might seem obvious but it only makes the game even more repetive and boring.
Well sure, there also some other stuff in the game, such as finding treasures and "ascensions" but neither are very intresting ("ascensions" are essentially like prestiege in CoD, or infamy in Payday 2).
How come I have a couple of hours on this game? Well, I load it up at times and play for ~10min until it gets boring again.

Cons:

- Repetive
- Addicting (I guess this could be positive)

- After you're come to level ~140 upgrading your heroes/buying new ones gets really expensive and it takes ages to afford them (unless you get a autoclicker)

Unlike many people who are giving this game a negative rating in response to the price increase, I'm going to review this based on the actual merits and gameplay. I've played the game off and on since just a few months after it was released. Up until a few months ago it was primarily single player, but that got old after a while. When my friend set up a private server it was like a whole new experience. Being able to craft out a chunk of land to call your own while constantly surrounded by the looming sense of death for doing even the simplest of tasks is a rush. To have to run for your life from a prehistoric chicken wielding steak knives for fingers simply because you wanted to gather wood is enough to get your blood pumping, and dodging dragons on the back of a griffin in an aerial dogfight is an entirely new experience.
The graphics and visuals are top notch and the attention to detail is incredible. The game is not without its flaws, and there are more than a few bugs and optimization issues that need to be fixed. But if you enjoy the open world survial crafting genre and want a new take on it then this is definitely a recommendation. Especially if you have friends to join you.
Bit of a tip though, after trying to utilize a public server it's pretty obvious that most of them are by and large very packed and most of the land is already taken. It's best to go for newer servers or even set up your own if possible.

An awesome pure multiplayer adventure! Anybody who loves fighting with sword and shield but hates the concept of magic, dragons and a crass story is in for a treat. No, campaign, no extensive lore, just fighting! The combat is not too hard to grasp though getting good at it helps, the customizing is good, creating an emblem or changing the pattern on your shield's colours is mostly it, faces change from class to class but you cannot make your own, something, in my opinion, is a bit of shame. The classes are very different to eachother and being able to tailor the weapons to suit your fighting style is very useful, whether you prefer clubbing your enemies with a mace or taking their head off with one fell swoop with a long sword is up to you.
The battles themselves are full of adrenalyn, war cries and steel on steel. Meeting an enemy in combat is exciting a few jabs and one swipe and you fall to the ground. There is of course problems with killing teammates but that's to be expected with the folly of close quarter fighting. The maps are all different some being small areas and others being vast and hilly lands. The different maps mean that you may have to cahnge your class to suit the area, it also means you can gain practice, points and new unlocks for your class. The matches size and time limit vary but all in all any battle your in is going to be fun.
Don't think it's all team-deathmatch, there are many other game modes such as duel, last team standing, king of the hill and many more! Map sizes can even become larger depending on game mode adding areas you may not have guessed were there. There has been no problems with hacks or pure cheating, the only problem is the occasional lag but most of the time it soon stops. There are many things you can do during the games as well as staining your armour with blood, you may remember I refrenced war cries? Well, there are plenty not all are insults some are more tactical for those of you who play serious, you can also type to your teamates as well as the server the only problem is you may not get time to during the battle. All in all, Chivalry: Medevil Warfare is on my must plays for anyone who likes good combat, graphics and teamwork.

Let me preface this by saying I have no problems running this game, as I have a very powerful computer.
The moment I bought ARK and launched it years ago, I was completely blown away. So much beauty, so much content, and so much of the unknown. That's probably my favorite part of this entire game- the unknown. I started with very little knowledge about the game, and it was brutal. The game throws you on a hostile beach with nothing but your bare undies. You cling on to any information you can get your hands on, learning bit by bit how to survive and thrive.
The best times I had in this game were playing with a few friends on a private server. We were constantly struggling and losing everything, but were having insane amounts of fun while doing it. We would always have a big plan or big adventure we would try to accomplish; usually ending in complete disaster. I can't tell you how many times we had to start over on that beach, laughing and learning about our previous catastrophe. Eventually, you manage to get yourself a strong fortress, a fleet of powerful dinos, and a whole lot of resources. But no matter how many you have, it will almost never be enough. There will always be another challenge on the horizon, whether it's something implemented in the game, or something you and your tribemates concocted.
I highly recommend playing on private or unnoficial servers. The official servers are a complete ♥♥♥♥♥how. Don't even bother with PvP servers, unless you want stage ninety billion cancer.
Sure, ARK has its flaws, but just about any other game will too. For a game as ambitious as ARK, I believe many of these flaws can be excused. It's a game with many many hours of adventure, tomfoolery, and fun. I will admit that maybe it should have been completely finished before the price was raised, but it's still a top tier game nonetheless. Highly recommend if you have the computer to run it.

CONS:
- Starting out can be fairly tough
- Does NOT work for old PC's/laptop's
- Requires a lot of memory
- Frequent crashes
- A little bit of a repetitive game (ok, before anyone can literally shoot me for saying this, despite adding new mods and new dinos, it's still the same. Taming is still the same process, drop hunting is still the same thing. Base building, going caving, getting artifacts, defeating bosses, getting loot -- STILL the SAME thing.)
Overall, it's not a bad game, I recommend it. You'll spend hours having a lot of fun --  9/10

Out of all the fururistic space shooting games, I'd have to say Warframe is the best. Though with recent updates, its not as fun as it used to be, it's still an amazing game. The combat is well done and the controls aren't ridiculous or convoluded like in other games. Though the game runs on microtransactions, it isnt 'pay to win'; its more like 'pay to get a larger selection'but most things that aren't cosmetic can still be earned by regular means. But the most important part of Warframe is probably the movement. Warframe offers fluid, easy to use movement, that doesn't just make it fun to play but also to watch.
The game gives you an incredible range of movement that  that ofers way more freedom than most games. Gliding, running up walls, and sliding are only some of the things you can do, but don't worry cause while all these things are available, the game will rarely have parts that will force you to do any of these things. You can take it slow and stealthy, or fast and fluid; you can even just brute your way through things if you really want. There aren't that many games that give you as much freedom as warframe does, so trust me; you won't be disappointed.

I really like this game, but there are some MAJOR flaws.
THE BAD:
My biggest complaint is the weight system & the building system. Make the inventory like they make the Storage Boxes. Lose the current weight system. The more "weight" a player or dinosaur can carry the more inventory slots they get. The reason I am saying this.... lets say you want to build a Behemoth Gateway. You have to make about 10 trips with your materials to the Smithy to craft
.... because it weighs 1800 pounds in materials and most players only spec into 150-200 pounds carry weight.
Want to build a house? Theres only one real way to build without losing your mind. Since the materials weigh a ton, and not the actual foundations, walls, and what not. You must craft what you "think" you're going to need THEN build. There is no build on the fly, because...... YOU CAN'T MOVE "YOURE CARRYING TOO MUCH WEIGHT." Also steal Rust's idea with the building blueprint! I am sick of navigating through the poorly built craft menu to build my house. If you ever did want build as you go.... you'd have to navigate through 2 screens just to get ready to build one time. Imagine if a person is building a 10 man tribe base..... not a good time!
Also make sure you find the flattest place possible or you will be fighting with the building system just to place anything.
Also releasing a expansion pac for a Early Access Game and charging money for it..... that should be illegal.
THE GOOD:
The game is gorgeous.... the dinosaur taming, combat, uniqueness. and customizations are on point! I have a GTX 970 and I after messing with my video options for an hour I got very close to max setting with 45-55 FPS.
The weapons are all unique and work well with the player. (Slingshot could use some updating)
Each armor tier feels like a nice and is a welcomed upgrade.
Game is alot of fun! I went on an exploration once I hit level 30 to find a Gigantopithecus (Big Foot) to try and tame him. Literally was gone with my Triceratops for 5 hours. Got into a huge fight with a level 22 Spinosaur. Found a Gigantopithecus as I was following him around trying to feed him and an Alpha Raptor slaughtered him while I ran away. I fought about 50 Titanboas on my way back home..... (Seriously why so many freaking snakes...) I decided I wanted to make a pack of Dire Wolves... I tamed 3, but my Triceratops died (RIP Cera).... My goal was to get 3 Males and 3 Females so I was staying in the area trying to get decent level Direwolves. I saw some crystals got off my new Direwolf and out of no where a Alpha Carno slaughtered me and my pack of wolves. I had a good time overall.
The game is challenging which I enjoyed. If you are not aware of your surroundings and have a well thought out plan all the time..... more than likely you will die. (in certain areas) Some say the building system is challenging..... it is not.... its just broken.
{{{  7/10  }}}  don't buy it for more than $19.99 IMO. If I could give this a sideways thumb I would, because it doesn't deserve a thumbs up or a thumbs down.

Clicker Heros is a "clicker frenzy" game. You click on monsters to cause damage, once the monster dies (via explosion, evaporation, or falls over and disappear) a shower of gold appears for you to collect. Gold is used to upgrade your clicking or "hire" and "purchase upgrades for" heroes that do damage per second (DPS) so you can lessen your risk of carpel tunnel syndrome. Each level requires you to kill ~10 monsters in order to move to the next level or a "boss fight" which has a high health monster that you have to beat in 30 seconds or less in order to pass the level. Later upgrades include gods you can earn by "sacrificing" your hero souls (which are earned via game resets to level 1).
Snarky character and upgrade descriptions are probably my favorite part.....
For a clicker game it does exactly what it's suppose to do and it's cute, almost childish monsters are visually pleasing to watch get squished to death.

Possessing a lot of potential, ARK: Survival Evolved is a survival game based on a dinosour-filled island, challenging players to survive harsh weather conditions, vicious creatures, and the combatants that are basic health needs.
While I'd like to say this game is a lot of fun, it has a deep and hidden crafting system that is difficult to learn the knowledge of. The game also lacks a thorough tutorial, which has deterred some players.
With a hefty setup of a PC, my computer struggled to render the game at even moderate level graphics, while other games with even more extensive requirements run more smoothly. Built in the otherwise phenomenal Unreal 4 engine, the game features a plethora of graphical settings that can make the game more aesthetically pleasing, but the efficiency  of the game's engine does not suffice for gameplay.
If you can handle cheap graphics, or can afford the setup required, and have the patience to unlock all the game's secrets, I'd say go right ahead. Personally, I dislike this game.

It's hard to really say I reccomend this game as it stands because it needs a LOT of work, so for now, no, I really don't reccomend it.
I enjoy the concept, running around an island and taming creatures, be it extinct dinosaurs, fantasy beasts, or real-life creatures, is something I genuinely enjoy doing. (Tamer class playstyle FTW XD) TMy lite game critizems are:
1: The combat system could use a little bit of work. Sometimes it feels like I'm just spinning my mouse and spamming click while paying to hit something. My only idea to help so far is to add an AOE highlight for attacks so I know what I'm biting/smacking with my dino.
2: Feeding a large amount of dinos quickly becomes a chore and detracts from the enjoyment from the game. My suggestion for this is separating the Wild dino food rate from the Tame dino food rate so that you don't have to constantly stuff bins full of food.
3: The aggression on the dragonflies and vultures REALLY needs to be area-activated by something OTHER than the player being near a corpse. I REALLY don't like being attacked because a raptor decided to maul the nearest dodo and eat it. I heard it was turned down but I still find myself being swarmed by vultures at random points even though I've done nothing more than sit down to regain stamina.
4: Phrasing on the Friendly Fire on/off could be more clear. I have no idea if it's on or off right now TwT
Now, for the real trouble. My biggest issue with Ark as it stands right now is the developers, game balance, and the boldface LIE about it's stage of development.
There are DOZENS of ways you can personalize your game to make it harder, regardless if you play solo or multiplayer- hundreds if not thousands of difficult servers to chose from. So I find it INCREDIBLY frustrating that every update we've gotten from this game is an attempt to make it harder and "more focused on survival." We've had over half a dozen nerfs to dino health and melee because 'oh you shouldn't be able to beat a rex (even a weak rex) with a raptor (even a powerful raptor) that's too easy.' Developers completely removed the ability of flying dinos to gain speed because they were 'overused.' The break rate on weapons, and armor is, quite simply, rediculous. Even high level armor (acendant flak being an example) will only survive an encounter or two if you find yourself removed from a mount, and there are several creatures designed to do EXACTLY that.
It seems that every update is just another excuse to add a 'challange' to the Ark, and really, this isn't Dark Souls: Dinosaur Edition. That's NOT what the game is supposed to be about, that's not how it's advertised, and thats not what most of the players are looking for. Not to be insulting and say you can't do that- again if that's you play style you can STILL find ways to give yourself a challange without forcing the whole gamer community (from dabbler to Gamer God) to play YOUR WAY.
Overall this nerfing and drive to make the game more challanging just serves makes the game GROSSLY imbalanced, and honestly, I don't know if I could consider the official, fully nerfed version playable at this stage- and that's without taking into account the PVP harassment, bullying, ungodly overpowered tribe warfare, and gamers who are only playing to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s to other players (sadly, this is a thing in EVERY PVP community, not just Ark.) All I can see is a constant cycle of taming and dying and retaming and dying because the wild creatures are too strong, tame ones are too weak, and you can't even FLY to get away from them anymore because you're too slow. This paired with the upkeep you're putting in on damaged armor, weapons and tools makes the game SUPER upkeep intensive- more of a chore than a game.
As for seeing change: sometimes the fan base makes any attempt to see a genuine fairness or balancing sound like a challange to God himself. The Hardcore PVP players take it as a literal personal INSULT if you bring up a topic suggesting that a mechanic needs adjusting, even if any game developer in their right mind would never allow you to be one-shot destoryed outside of in-built plot-mechanics or deliberate disregard for your own level (you are a level 1 beginner, do NOT go try to punch a t-rex naked, because DUH XD)
Now, there ARE settings for solo, and un-official servers that can work around these nerfs and difficulties, but these are IMMENSLY unreliable. I say this because I keep loging in to my private game to find them completely reset. I have yet to link it to any particular occasion, but I HAVE noticed that it happens and that once was more than enough, thank you. (I'm currently waiting to see if it coencides with official server events ending) At one point I logged in and found my game of two years had been DELETED (I'd like to note I had a large base of 170+ dinos including SIX GIGAS with a 108 AND 120 KIB TAME.) If I wasn't able to admin spawn and re-make my base, I would have quit playing then and there and demanded a refund, play time be DAMNED. That they claim this is a complete game no longer in Beta is a bold-face LIE.
Here is the designation of a game as it is built:
ALPHA is a game that is still adding content, be new items, new features, new mechanics, and generally not done creating the world.
BETA is when you have COMPLETED adding content and features and are bug-testing, for example- finding out that snakes spawn inside a house is a bug, Beta is the time to fix that.
IDEALLY a FULL RELEASED GAME has tested for as many bugs as they could find and fixed them. In the modern world this isn't as ideal as gamers would like it, and we still see bugs in many full-release games even after testing. (whether this reflexts on beta testing or the increase in players, don't ask me.)
Point being: Ark IS NOT RELEASED. ARK isn't even out of ALPHA yet. The developers haven't even stopped CREATING new content to ADD, they add a new mechanic for almost every creature they release, and they still have more bugs than an entomology lab. (if you don't know what entomology is, it's the study of insects, don't feel bad I had to google it to remember) We've had THREE new biomes added (swamp, snow, redwoods), THREE cave edits (adding new caves, editing exiting caves, and adding underwater caves) SEVEN total map edits (including the biomes, caves, and the recent volcano, which isn't a cave or biome edit exactly) almost ONE HUNDRED creatures (I ain't listing this), HUNDREDS of items (ditto), and DOZENS of new mechanics. and they STILL. AREN'T. FINISHED. This is ALPHA-STAGE game development.
Frankly, I think the developers should be ashamed of themselves for trying so hard to FORCE players to play the way THEY think we should. I think they should be ashamed for lying about the development and de-bugging process. Most of all I think the gamer community deserves better treatment from anyone claiming game design as a profession and expecting to see payment. This isn't a "we pay you-blah blah blah" BS line or anything like that, but we provide feedback to let you know how to really bring your games to life, and having that feedback continually ignored in favor of 'another new game mechanic to make it harder' is getting insulting.
I like the idea of the game, but I'd like it better if it were picked up by someone willing to listen- because if I weren't playing solo under a heavily modified server, I would NOT be playing this game.

With almost 900 hours in game it might be time to ask the questions: Do I still enjoy the game, Do i think it’s worth the hours and do i recommend it?
The Short answer is definitely yes
The long answer is yes, but RNG is king in this game. A follow up question will then be: will you put in the hours and show RNG who is boss, or will you give in and spend money. Examples of RNG will now follow:
* RELICS (how you get all your prime items - somewhat stronger items):
+ Acquiring prime parts requires Relics - Which drops randomly of loot tables in certain areas.
+ Relics drop items on it randomly. You can upgrade the relic to better your chances, but its slightly.
+ Even with fully upgraded relics, RNG can and will still bend you over and...
* RIVEN MODS / SORTIES (semi-end-game missions and mods):
+ Sorties have a random chance of giving you a riven mod (it’s a myth, all drop items are 2000 endo)
+ If you are lucky to get a riven mod, it can either be a shotgun, primary or pistol riven.
+ The random riven has a random mission on it that has to be completed before you can unlock it
+ After unlocking the riven, you have a random chance of getting a random riven for a random weapon with random stats on it.
+ If you got bad stats you can reroll it, to get new random stats that has a random chance of being better or worse (you can revert to the old stats, but it still cost kuva - rare resource - to do a roll)
Other than the above random RNG, there are small amount of RNG in collecting mods, but that just require time.
Now the positives (if you are still reading and didn’t dash for the hills already):
+ The best looking free-2-play 3rd person shooter I’ve ever seen
+ Amazing story quests that does a great job in explaining into history of the game universe
+ A lot of game modes and missions that keeps gameplay fresh
+ Fun game play
+ The devs are very active (a lot of devstreams where they give you insight into upcoming content, quick hotfixes, active in game help and more)
+ The devs are very generous– support charities
+ some Easter eggs in game
+ A lot of gameplay options – warframes and weapons
+ Very helpful community
+ Fequently adds new content for free
+ Everything is obtainable via playing the game (excluding some cosmetics)
+ 2 very well designed raids (with nightmare options)
+ Well rounded bosses (can become easy)
+ Fasionframe is true end game
To conclude: After the update of the star map, sorties, gameplay etc. im definitely still enjoying the game.
I do recommend this game to all, but with a slight warning: Either spend time, or spend money – it is called Farm-frame after all.

This is less of a review for Clicker Heroes, and more a review for my Razer Naga. I am surprised it still works after playing this game for so long.
For how simple the game mechanics are, it is impressive how addicting it can be. Even more fun now that they have added additional mechanics, as well as clans. You can play this game and click furiously, or you can play the game and idle for a while letting your upgrades do the damage for you. You can specialize into specific builds, or you can just make an all around even upgrade path choosing the best of both worlds.
PROS
1. Game can be hardcore or casual. Your choice.
2. Great to play when you have 5 minutes to spare here and there.
3. Something that can be played while multitasking.
4. Interesting art design, and satisfying results from clicking.
5. Good UI design, comfortable controls. Options menu has all you should need.
CONS
1. Mouse company may not continue to honor warranty.
2. Carpal tunnel.
3. Viral. Warn your friends (or don't) before they go to the store page and download it.
4. Like babysitting without getting paid for it. Eventually you will have to focus on the game for periods of time while watching shows.
5. Pay to win. Still, they have to afford food somehow. Understandable.
TL;DR
Do I recommend this game? Yes. No. That is likely the order in which you will give your answer. At first, it is the best thing. Then, you just can't seem to put it down. I just want to play until I can get all the achievements and buy the last hero. Still not there.

So why have I, a founder and player of this game since 2013, recommended Warframe to you? Surely, I have become jaded and detest the approach DE has taken towards this game?
This is a trend I see setting in for a quite a few Warframe veterns. I don't find these impressions of the game without merit. Nor do I think their foundation of what they dislike about Warframe should be easily dismissed. However, I always stand by the idea that at its core, Warframe is an amazing game that almost everyone should at least try.
You see, Warframe is a free to play game, but not just any. It's a free to play with the most amount of love, care, and quality I've ever seen put into one. It's gameplay, the most essential feature, has been refined to an absolute with many ways of playing. Run and gun? You bet. Slash and dash between enemies? It's there. Snipe from afar? Yup. Jump in slow-mo, Max Payne style as you throw your shurikens in the enemies face? Indeed. All within a deadly, fast paced dance, Warframe is no slouch to top notch entertainment. Even its weakest link, Archwing, has also been improved by matching the on-foot fast paced action. I will say however, that Archwing is still the weakest link of the game, but thankfully doesn't overstay its welcome as you progress in the starchart. With so many weapons to collect, your only limitation is both the resources you obtain and the time that pumps inbetween crafting.
You see, Warframe has the foundry. The foundry is a bothersome device that can request either modest amounts of time to complete an item(12 hours, so either wait overnight, or a few game sessions grinding other items later), to absurd amounts of time(3 days for a warframe, so essentially there's a chance you'll probably forget crafting it in the first place). On top of this, newer resources have been linked to limited time missions, or dissolve over time. You can get really lucky and have whatever you need, or unfortunate and will have to grind it out a bunch more to get what you want. To which I have to say, Your mileage may vary. There is a grind in this game. I have personally been at the short end of the stick of RNG compared to my other peers. I even stayed at a MR for a very long time out of pure frustration of the RNG and stuck to one loadout for about half a year. However, that is where my issues with the game ended.
Even the more recent issues won't reach the minds of newer players. The hema, the research weapon that everyone pulls their hair over, is one in a sea of many other weapons that are way easier to obtain. Even the Riven system itself, that claims to break balance, is held back by insane costs and isn't worth putting on weapons that are already powerful. These are issues that, while annoying, doesn't change what Warframe is.
If you are of any relation to a gamer as I am, who's soley interested in playing the game for its insanely fun action spree and enjoy the neat customizations the game has to offer, then I definitely recommend the game to you. With trading being an option these days to acquire free platinum with easy resources such as the warframe market, it won't be long until you get sucked into the hours of just customizing your character and ship, down to the tiniest detail.
The only people I can't recommend this to, are those that play games for instant gratification. With the foundrys wait times, and event weapons all around, those looking to "Catch-em-all" Or there to burst through the games content are in for rough times ahead. For those that are interested in dedicating large amounts of time to a game teeming with customization and entertainment at a slow pace, or for those that are looking to sink their teeth into an adredeline fueled third person shooter one mission per session, I have this to say: Welcome to Warframe.

Best melee combat game I've ever played. The combat is quite deep, but not so complicated that you can't just jump in and start lopping off heads straight away.
There is a good amount of game modes, FFA, Duels, Team death match, capture the flag, last team standing and the best mode, team objective - which has teams competing to attack or defend many varied objectives, like burning a town and killing all the peasants, to dumping corpses into a river, to sieging a castle and killing the king!
There are 6 main weapons and 6 secondary weapons for each of the 4 classes to unlock, which won't take very long but will take a bit of dedication.  The 4 classes all feel very different; archers, man at arms, vanguards and knights. Each has their strengths and weaknesses and varied different attacks.
Very good game. I highly recommend it to everyone, even if you've not really touched the genre of FPS because this is just a breathe of fresh air. I will certainly be playing for a long time to come.

This is less of a review for Clicker Heroes, and more a review for my Razer Naga. I am surprised it still works after playing this game for so long.

You can play this game and click furiously, or you can play the game and idle for a while letting your upgrades do the damage for you. You can specialize into specific builds, or you can just make an all around even upgrade path choosing the best of both worlds.
PROS
1. Game can be hardcore or casual. Your choice.
2. Great to play when you have 5 minutes to spare here and there.
3. Something that can be played while multitasking.
4. Interesting art design, and satisfying results from clicking.
5. Good UI design, comfortable controls. Options menu has all you should need.
CONS
1. Mouse company may not continue to honor warranty.
2. Carpal tunnel.
3. Viral. Warn your friends (or don't) before they go to the store page and download it.
4. Like babysitting without getting paid for it. Eventually you will have to focus on the game for periods of time while watching shows.
5. Pay to win. Still, they have to afford food somehow. Understandable.

Warframe is probably the best experience you never have to pay for.
My journey with warframe began a little under two years ago, and I still love it with all my heart.
It's impossible to sum up warframe in one single genre, I've seen people call it an mmo before, a third person looter shooter, an action rpg, a hack and slash, and in all honesty it's all of those and none of them. Warframe is an unique game that you really will not find the likes of anywhere else. It's in it's truest sense a labor of love from a studio that was supposed to fail but made a bloody gem of a game. If you've ever heard of the story because why the final fantasy series is called final fantasy you'll know the history of warframe.
So what is this game about?
Well it's about warframes, ninjas with super powers in space keeping the balance of power in place and in the process aquiring a lot of shiny new weapons.
So what does warframe do well?
Movement. Warframe without a doubt in my mind has the god damn best movement system ever put in a game, the freedom of movement and playstyle it alone provides you is mind blowing, and you'll have a blast mastering it.
Customization. Want to colour your ship? You got it! Your warframe? You got it! Your weapons? You got it! Your armor?? You got it! Your capes seperately from your armor? You got it! Your dogs and cats? You got it! If it's in the game it can probably be coloured and the colour packs are extensive.
Action. It's fast paced run and gun, hack and slash, kill fest that you can experience solo or with up to four different people,It's very tight and precie and highly skill based. If you get good at warframe it'll very much show.
Weapon variety. This game is full to the brim of guns, pistols, swords, great swords, whips, polearms, energy beam weapons, a spartan laser, shotguns, and so many more. If you want to shoot, slice or blow stuff up this game is perfect for you.
Damage. Most of the damage will come from mod cards, these can be aquired in a wariety of ways. All the drop locations for each mod are listed on the wiki as well as their drop chance. (And you'll be checking the wiki a lot but more on that later). Some of these will drop from your basic units you encounter, some are mission rewards, some are exclusive to some traders, and all are tradable with other players.The modding system is so complicated and intricate I could give a college lecture on it, if you like complexity in your customization this game is for you.
Community. Warframe has one of the best, nicest, most helpful communities I think I've ever come across, there are people always ready to help you beat that one boss you're stuck on, teach you a mechanic you didn't know about, give you an idea what mods to put in a certain weapon, and flat out give you mods, primed parts and other things you may need. Warframes existence is built on this community and the devs know it. The dev team is here for the community, they constantly host weekly streams on their twitch page, where they play the game with the community, discuss the recent updates, future patches, new warframes, reworks and everything, I truly believe after 1700 hours with these people that they're here with and for us, to make us love the game they love.
Clans. Everyone can create a clan for free and join a clan for free. Clans are assigned a clan dojo which they construct decorate and develop to their taste. Clans are built up of different purpose rooms, corridors and halls you can arrange in any way you like. The main purpose of clans is for clan research which includes specific weapons that are "dojo tech" exclusive, as well as some warframes and sentinels that can only be researched in the clan dojo. Dojos also provide an easy place to trade with other players at the trading post and are by in large where most of the trading takes place.
Monetization. Warframe is free to play, which means some content is locked behind premium currency called platinum. I have never felt like I needed to buy it, mostly because you can trade for platinum with other players. If you never want to spend a dime on this game you never have to for anything. The only things that are exclusively pay to use are tennogen warframe skins made by the community, and frankly I think that's fair. Other uses for platinum are to speed up crafting of weapons and warframes, and yeah waiting for something to be built is a pain but it's in real time and you don't have to have the game open for it to progress.
So this all sounds amazing, where does warframe fail?
Explaining itself. While for some people this is a positive warframe just throws you into a world with a rather mediocre tutorial and expects you to find your way. Now the tutorial will tell you how to interact with the world, use weapons, your powers, and such. But there are things intergral to the game that are never explained or flatout never mentioned anywhere like the raids, sorties, nightmare missions, all higher level challenging content that is never explained to you by anyone but the wiki, and that's where you'll spend a lot of your time. Warframe heavily relies on you asking other people, or going to the wiki to find out how to do or find something. Now this is a con in that it's really not new user friendly, but honestly it builds a strong supportive community so take that for what you will.
The grind. Oh yes there's a lot of it, it's an incredibly grindy game and your enjoyment of it will heavily depend on if you like grindy games or not. Honestly though the action is fantastic while you're grinding, and I've never felt like it was unfair what the game asks you to do. But if you hate grindy games turn back now this is not for you you will absolutely hate it.
Bugs. The game has plenty of them, Now are they that common? No I wouldn't say so, you'll actually fairly seldom run into a bug but when you do it'll often be a hard crash, or a forced reset ( you do have to alt f4 sometimes). Bugs mostly occur with new content, and are fairly quickly patched out for the most part. Some annoying little bugs and some major ones too have persisted for years but there are workarounds for them.
PvP. If you're playing warframe for pvp you're playing the wrong game it's not polished, it's poorly implemented in my opinion, most of the community hates it with a passion, and it's desolate for the most part. This is a for all intents and purposes a PvE game and I highly encourage playing it as such.
This review is from the perspecitve of someone who has poured his life into this game over the last few years. You will love it, you will hate it. There are times where you'll think the devs are absolutely genius and there are times you'll think they're utter morons. Warframe has it's ups and downs, it's run by regular people they make mistakes, big deal they'll fix them, It's truly been a lovely experience so far with warframe and I love this game with all my heart. If anything I've written here sounds even a little appealing please do give it a try, it's free so there's no real risk involved.
Now I have miseed out on some things sure, I could write ten books worth of information about warframe, it's a big scary overwhelming game and it just keeps getting bigger. I'm still learning just as much as someone who started an hour ago. Warframe isn't complacent, it keeps evolvoing changing sometimes for the better sometimes for the worse, but trough all of it's ups and downs it has truly been an amazing experience and I'm proud to call myself a tenno.

Ark, as the title suggests, is a survival game in which you start out at a random location with nothing but a gem in your arm. The game came out as early access in 2015 but has since been marketed as a full game, releasing August 8th, 2017. I have over 200 hours on xbox and another account on steam. For a $60 price tag, this game just doesn't feel like a complete AAA game like it should. If an indie game is to charge a full $60, then it must feel like a fully complete game.  Lets compare it with another $60 indie game, No Man's Sky.
NMS art style: In NMS there is a clear art style that Hello games tried to accomplish and at times the game is visually beautiful. Other times the worlds are stale and bland.
Ark art style: Ark does not strive for a "art style" in a sense but its style has remained the same. The game looks good at times, but it is poorly optimised and loads the textures when you are spawing in and while you are playing the game. Playing at higher settings becomes difficult, even with a well built computer. NMS does not have those problems.
Both's gameplay is similar of that to minecraft. Enough said there.
Both were completly overpriced and cost twice as much as they should. Enough said as well.
Both games are constantly updated with Hello Games realeasing major updates at once with new updates like 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3. Ark has major updates but are more spread out. For example, Ark released a small impactful update introducing the otter.
Conclusion: Both games are fun and have some replayability, but both have problems. NMS is overpriced and scratches the surface of opportunity. Ark is also overpriced and has major optimisation issues. Ark also has an overcompicated UI and menu. NMS' UI and Menu is better but has some flaws. But this review isn't about NMS, its about Ark. Ark, as it is right now, just doesn't feel like a complete game like the developers are saying it is. If you want to pay $60 for an INDIE game, go ahead. If you like minecraft-like dinosaur games, this is for you. But if you have just found this game and are considering getting it, I would hold on until a sale or until the developers lower the price, which is possible, but not probable.

I wanted to play Ark so badly when it first came out years ago, but didn't have a computer powerful enough to run the game. I eventually bought a better computer when my old one died on me. The new rig was able to run StarCraft 2 at highest possible setting for days on end without getting tired... it still could only run ARK on the  lowest graphics settings.
I love this game and I think that it has a lot of potential, however, it is one of the worst optimized games I have seen in my entire life and is no where near worth $60. The mechanics are so broken and in need of work that the game without mods is almost unplayable. I play it now and then just for fun, but loose interest extremely quickly each time I return simply because it runs terribly, has horrible mechanics, the AI doesn't exist, and without mods its almost like you're not even playing real game, more like an unfinished sandbox that has no objective or purpose whatsoever. Multiplayer is horrendous, by the way and PVP is unspeakable.
Overall, having played many hundreds of hours... I love the concept, but hate what this game has become. I wish the developers had put more time into making a better overall game, not adding content that no one was asking for and ensuring the graphics were so fantastic and optimized that even most gaming computers can barely handle running it. I'd love to see this game become great, but I don't think the delvers have the capacity to bring it out of the darkness. I'd recommend avoiding buying or playing this game.

I wanted to play Ark so badly when it first came out years ago, but didn't have a computer powerful enough to run the game. I eventually bought a better computer when my old one died on me. The new rig was able to run StarCraft 2 at highest possible setting for days on end without getting tired... it still could only run ARK on the  lowest graphics settings.
I love this game and I think that it has a lot of potential, however, it is one of the worst optimized games I have seen in my entire life and is no where near worth $60. The mechanics are so broken and in need of work that the game without mods is almost unplayable. I play it now and then just for fun, but loose interest extremely quickly each time I return simply because it runs terribly, has horrible mechanics, the AI doesn't exist, and without mods its almost like you're not even playing real game, more like an unfinished sandbox that has no objective or purpose whatsoever. Multiplayer is horrendous, by the way and PVP is unspeakable.
Overall, having played many hundreds of hours... I love the concept, but hate what this game has become. I wish the developers had put more time into making a better overall game, not adding content that no one was asking for and ensuring the graphics were so fantastic and optimized that even most gaming computers can barely handle running it. I'd love to see this game become great, but I don't think the delvers have the capacity to bring it out of the darkness. I'd recommend avoiding buying or playing this game.

Jump in and instantly enjoy; a game that's fun for all the family! If, like me, you're appreciative of blood and guts; you'll get some great laughs from this game. It's multiplayer only, and based around melee combat, with a hint of ranged warfare from archers and medieval artillery. At risk of discrediting the game's quality, I would say that it is like a medieval Call of Duty. Unfortunately, it draws a similar community for that very reason. Even so, there are a majority of less intellectually challenged players, and who are looking purely for a good time. The game offers the opportunity for great creativity in your manic violence, and finding like-minded brutes leads you into to the best fun that games have to offer.

text:
For Starters, I would recommend everyone to give a try to the game early levels, while they don't fully give out all the game is about, the can nevertheless be interesting to look at, before the grind starts.
But where do i find the core of the game enjoyment?  Fantastic Weapon and Character Design, Rewarding Movement Options, Good Customization and Great Free to Play model.
Weapons
Firing a well built gun is satisfying, From The Rocket Launchers, To The Bows and Rifles and everything in between, they all feel just right to use, and you will use a lot of them, since the game exp functions in base of item mastery, instead of player level. Will so weapons take some time to start feeling rewarding to use (Mostly Early Side Arms), They will get better as tou progress.
Warframes
These are your Playable characters. They range widely in general use and apparence, but they aren't just some set of stats to drop your weapons into, Each have a set of 4 abilities, similar to Those found in MOBAs, which vary from AoE Crowd Controls, to Damage Shield.
Movement
The Game is commonly reffered as 'Space Ninjas: The Game' and this is the main reason. Wall Jumps, Super Jumps, Gliding, Rollling, They are all rewarding to use and give de game a good part of it's depth.
Customization
In an MMO, where there are millions of players, One Important aspect is giving the individual a way to differentiate himself from the crowd visually. Personally, I love the ability to change the palette of your weapon and character, as well as other added acessories.
Free-to-Play
Some would say this game is pay-to-win, I would rather call it, Pay-for-Convenience, You can either buy a weapon from the market, or grind it for free. And even then, You can Trade In-Game Items for Premium Currency, making even the more annoying sides of the model (Such as Warframe and Weapon Slots), manageble.

Excellent game. I highly reccomend giving this one a try.
Here are a few of my personal pros and cons. Obviously this is highly subjective so take it for what its worth.
Pros -
Extremely fun core game play mechanics. Visceral combat, fast paced movement system, dynamic maps and loads of monsters to kill.
Wide variety of Warframes to play, most have fairly interesting mechanics.
Very friendly community
The game is open to creative play styles
Performs well on most PCs
Cons -
The lack of truly challenging content. The most challenging and consistent gameplay I seem to encounter have is about 30 minutes into the only tier 4 survival in the game.
Some small but annoyingly frustrating things like gliding while running down a set of stairs or not being able to bullet jump up a wall because a tiny ledge sticking out. Odd things like that which break the otherwise fluid parkour system.
Other than that there is a host of other issues that will make themselve apparent but that doesn't come until you've played for quite some time.
This game is definitely worth a try. I imagine most people could get a solid 60+ enjoyable gameplay hours out of it before dicidng if they want to stick around or not.  It's free so nothing to lose but your time.

Graphics 9.5/10 For a free-to-play game the graphics are very nice.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare is a fast paced FPS (First Person Slasher) that is unique.
The combat is very fun and skill dependant, a single skilled player can kill enemies one after another, with advanced hit detection based on weapon models this allows for a deeper meta, which admittedly can be very odd with moves where you turn your back to your opponent and look at the sky then perform a downward strike which results in an instant strike.
The game's style and art is great, the models may not be of the highest poly count but the general texture work and aesthetic allows for an enjoyable user experience whilst not majorly taxing the hardware of your computer. (On another note the game also supports 2560x1080 [21:9 ratio] natively, good job Torn Banner!)
However the game will occassionaly after a new patch have major balance issues with certain weapons, but many players shun on the use of unbalaced weapons (Feinting is still in the game, why is this?) and some mechanics are unbalanced too, but even though there are balance issues, hopping on this game with some friends and slashing agathian scum makes for an overall enjoyable experience.

A few people are claiming that it is better to just stick with MW but I am happy I have both at my disposal in case one feels to dull I can always switch it up for a different style of close combat multiplayer. One of the main differences between the two games are the classes, in MW you have 4 classes that differ from each other with their stats, weapon selection, and they all have their own unique special ability. While in DW there are 6 different classes that differ from each other in sort of the same way, but it still brings a little more variety. I am playing on a nvidia 780 graphics card and the game play is lag free, the servers that I have played on have not had any lag either and also give me the option to choose hosts with lowest ping which is helpful. I will have to recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a high end computer online multiplayer experience, there are not any games on the market right now that can be easily compared to what this game has to offer.

Warframe is probably the best experience you never have to pay for.
My journey with warframe began a little under two years ago, and I still love it with all my heart.
It's impossible to sum up warframe in one single genre, I've seen people call it an mmo before, a third person looter shooter, an action rpg, a hack and slash, and in all honesty it's all of those and none of them. Warframe is an unique game that you really will not find the likes of anywhere else. It's in it's truest sense a labor of love from a studio that was supposed to fail but made a bloody gem of a game. If you've ever heard of the story because why the final fantasy series is called final fantasy you'll know the history of warframe.
So what is this game about?
Well it's about warframes, ninjas with super powers in space keeping the balance of power in place and in the process aquiring a lot of shiny new weapons.
So what does warframe do well?
Movement. Warframe without a doubt in my mind has the god damn best movement system ever put in a game, the freedom of movement and playstyle it alone provides you is mind blowing, and you'll have a blast mastering it.
Customization. Want to colour your ship? You got it! Your warframe? You got it! Your weapons? You got it! Your armor?? You got it! Your capes seperately from your armor? You got it! Your dogs and cats? You got it! If it's in the game it can probably be coloured and the colour packs are extensive.
Action. It's fast paced run and gun, hack and slash, kill fest that you can experience solo or with up to four different people,It's very tight and precie and highly skill based. If you get good at warframe it'll very much show.
Weapon variety. This game is full to the brim of guns, pistols, swords, great swords, whips, polearms, energy beam weapons, a spartan laser, shotguns, and so many more. If you want to shoot, slice or blow stuff up this game is perfect for you.
Damage. Most of the damage will come from mod cards, these can be aquired in a wariety of ways. All the drop locations for each mod are listed on the wiki as well as their drop chance. (And you'll be checking the wiki a lot but more on that later). Some of these will drop from your basic units you encounter, some are mission rewards, some are exclusive to some traders, and all are tradable with other players.The modding system is so complicated and intricate I could give a college lecture on it, if you like complexity in your customization this game is for you.
Community. Warframe has one of the best, nicest, most helpful communities I think I've ever come across, there are people always ready to help you beat that one boss you're stuck on, teach you a mechanic you didn't know about, give you an idea what mods to put in a certain weapon, and flat out give you mods, primed parts and other things you may need. Warframes existence is built on this community and the devs know it. The dev team is here for the community, they constantly host weekly streams on their twitch page, where they play the game with the community, discuss the recent updates, future patches, new warframes, reworks and everything, I truly believe after 1700 hours with these people that they're here with and for us, to make us love the game they love.
Clans. Everyone can create a clan for free and join a clan for free. Clans are assigned a clan dojo which they construct decorate and develop to their taste. Clans are built up of different purpose rooms, corridors and halls you can arrange in any way you like. The main purpose of clans is for clan research which includes specific weapons that are "dojo tech" exclusive, as well as some warframes and sentinels that can only be researched in the clan dojo. Dojos also provide an easy place to trade with other players at the trading post and are by in large where most of the trading takes place.
Monetization. Warframe is free to play, which means some content is locked behind premium currency called platinum. I have never felt like I needed to buy it, mostly because you can trade for platinum with other players. If you never want to spend a dime on this game you never have to for anything. The only things that are exclusively pay to use are tennogen warframe skins made by the community, and frankly I think that's fair. Other uses for platinum are to speed up crafting of weapons and warframes, and yeah waiting for something to be built is a pain but it's in real time and you don't have to have the game open for it to progress.
So this all sounds amazing, where does warframe fail?
Explaining itself. While for some people this is a positive warframe just throws you into a world with a rather mediocre tutorial and expects you to find your way. Now the tutorial will tell you how to interact with the world, use weapons, your powers, and such. But there are things intergral to the game that are never explained or flatout never mentioned anywhere like the raids, sorties, nightmare missions, all higher level challenging content that is never explained to you by anyone but the wiki, and that's where you'll spend a lot of your time. Warframe heavily relies on you asking other people, or going to the wiki to find out how to do or find something. Now this is a con in that it's really not new user friendly, but honestly it builds a strong supportive community so take that for what you will.
The grind. Oh yes there's a lot of it, it's an incredibly grindy game and your enjoyment of it will heavily depend on if you like grindy games or not. Honestly though the action is fantastic while you're grinding, and I've never felt like it was unfair what the game asks you to do. But if you hate grindy games turn back now this is not for you you will absolutely hate it.
Bugs. The game has plenty of them, Now are they that common? No I wouldn't say so, you'll actually fairly seldom run into a bug but when you do it'll often be a hard crash, or a forced reset ( you do have to alt f4 sometimes). Bugs mostly occur with new content, and are fairly quickly patched out for the most part. Some annoying little bugs and some major ones too have persisted for years but there are workarounds for them.
PvP. If you're playing warframe for pvp you're playing the wrong game it's not polished, it's poorly implemented in my opinion, most of the community hates it with a passion, and it's desolate for the most part. This is a for all intents and purposes a PvE game and I highly encourage playing it as such.
This review is from the perspecitve of someone who has poured his life into this game over the last few years. You will love it, you will hate it. There are times where you'll think the devs are absolutely genius and there are times you'll think they're utter morons. Warframe has it's ups and downs, it's run by regular people they make mistakes, big deal they'll fix them, It's truly been a lovely experience so far with warframe and I love this game with all my heart. If anything I've written here sounds even a little appealing please do give it a try, it's free so there's no real risk involved.
Now I have miseed out on some things sure, I could write ten books worth of information about warframe, it's a big scary overwhelming game and it just keeps getting bigger. I'm still learning just as much as someone who started an hour ago. Warframe isn't complacent, it keeps evolvoing changing sometimes for the better sometimes for the worse, but trough all of it's ups and downs it has truly been an amazing experience and I'm proud to call myself a tenno.
