Chivalry is a first-person fighting game (FFG?) built around close-range melee combat, with a smattering of archery. It never loses sight of the fact that, fancy moves or no, getting personal is a messy business. Heads, legs and arms fly by the dozen in every match, a feature made approximately ten billion times better by the fact that you can further de-limb opponents as they stare in shock at the first mortal blow. There is nothing quite like hacking someone's arm off, then executing a swift and true beheading as they stare open-mouthed at the stump.The gratuitous brutality of knightly melee combat teeters between comedic and cathartic in Chivalry: Medieval Warfare's gory encounters. Well-placed killing blows send limbs and heads flying, accompanied by fountains of blood spewing from drippy stumps that call to mind the iconic Black Knight duel in Monty Python and the Holy Grail. It's hilarious at times and excessively gruesome. Gutting foes has a lot more weight to it here than in other recent entries in the Medieval combat genre like War of the Roses or Mount and Blade: Warband. That alone doesn't make Chivalry the best in its class, but it does incite a certain bloodlust that'll keep you charging into the chaos.

I've played this game for hundreds of hours and had a lot of fun in it so far.
There is a lot of mixed feelings on some scenarios so I will put all Pros and Cons of the game with my personal opinion about it after it.
Hopefully my review will help.
Pros:
*Prehistoric creatures alive, amazing idea, tamable, ridable and even able to build bases on top of them? You got to be kidding me! It is mindblowing actually to find out about all of this. It doesn't only apply for land based animals but flying animals and submerged animals as well. It definitely opens up a whole new world.
*Technological advancement, good but I am personally not much of a "gunner" myself. I've never went further than to use Crossbows and right now with the higher quality Crossbows or Bows they have puts in they definitely become significantly stronger than like a basic gun. Of course a gun of the same quality would be stronger, but for someone like me who doesn't like guns it's great to hear you can still "upgrade" after the Crossbow is unlocked. The unlocking is only a matter of chance and random.
*Maps, even while Scorched Earth needs to be brought, you still have the maps "Ragnarok"-"The Center" and "The Island" besides those two you can generate your own map as well the way you please when poking around with an amount of numbers and percentages, get a hold of that to be able to fully make use of it. So far I haven't much poke around with it, but I've seen maps generated by people which made me see, you can get a hold of how it works. Seen in that perspective you got yourself any map you like.
*Bosses. In case of interest you can always try to defeat the Bosses of the ARK, there are three on the Island, 2 working together on The Center, Ragnarok, no idea and one in Scorched Earth. I advice PvP or PvE to take them on with a tribe unless you are like me, attracted to challenges to figure out how to defeat the Bosses on Single Player. It will be you against the world.
*The challenges, new on ARK and playing on The Island? spawn in the South unless you like to get your♥♥♥♥♥kicked early. As much as a challenge ARK can be when you first start once you get the hang of it you definitely can see yourself growing. From naked with a stone pick to riding a Raptor, Carnotaurus, Tyrannosaurus, Army of creatures all around. -and not just the tames, same goes for your home. From thatch, wood, stone, metal and if you're really good or lucky TEK. Unless you want to be creative and combine the qualities to make an aesthetically pleasing building.
Cons:
*First off the most obvious one.... 68EUR? Seriously? Good thing I brought it during the cheap days with a sale, I had them both for 20. This is insanity. The only person I'd spend this money on to get tis game as well would be for my girlfriend, but a game like this not everybody can effort or even wishes to gift someone, people's pockets aren't made of gold you know. Even while the game definitely is amazing because of the bugs and annoyances that are still in it I'd say, not for this price. Look for a massive discount somewhere or be lucky enough to get it gifted.
*How about the "Running Away" mechanic, of course the running away is logical when a dinosaur gets almost knocked out for taming but to let them run into the water and there they'd swim around in circles until they knock out? Dude, that is not logical or fun anymore! Let them at least AVOID the water by running a different way. I could easily agree on that.
*The "Flyer nerf" of course I think it is pretty logical flying animals had to get nerfed but to completely take away the possibility to upgrade their speed? That is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. Instead what they should have done is letting them 'force land' when it rains /snows. It would be useful taming a flying creature during this period of time but still increases a great risk when to get out and look around, it would still stimulate the players to rather choose for safety and use higher level land based animals instead. But it is what it is and I use "Classic Flyers" you're welcome future ARK players.
*The building.... everything seems to be obstructed, not sure why, not sure why they aren't fixing it either. Good thing there is a mod called "S+ Structures" it works very well, little issues but helps in all terms in all ways. Because of S+ Structures, my base is not only defensive but looks good too.
*Few graphic issues I guess? Well, hot ragdoll action in ARK at times but I'd rather call it hilarious of fun than an issue. It's different for everybody though so if you dislike Ragdolling, well, sorry. Besides that the Transponder nodes.... those are used to track animals that have been putted it on, major issue there. My Beelzebufo as an example has a massive metal node sticking through the half of its body, those things I do find very annoying, please ARK, instead of removing them, fix them.
My opinion:
Not worth buying at this high expense, definitely worth buying cheaper, the game should first be optimized before it can get even anywhere near this prize.
If you're willing to gift someone the game, you sir /miss -are a very generous and good hearted person.
The game itself, the gameplay and what not is amazing. Just make sure to have it modded to increase the gameplay.
-S+ Structures
-Classic Flyers
-Resource Stacks
Those are the mods I play with and I play the game with joy.

Bought this game based on watching gamers play on YouTube... AllShamNoWow, etc.  Only bought it on sale - thankfully didn't play full price.
The game is a joke...
Menu system is atypical and difficult to navigate.  Keybinds show two sets of bindings, which I don't see why, and is confusing - allowing you to bind the same key to multiple actions.  Also, you can reassign all bindings to new keys, but if you click Return to go back a menu, it erases them all and you have to start over.  Only after doing this did I see there's a "Save" on each screen.  :-/
From what I've seen, there's either Arena (Last Man Standing), Team Deathmatch, and Objective (i.e. "push the cart") gametypes.
The gameplay leaves a lot to be desired.  Although there is a "Training" mode (which I could not exit out of once selected, even after already completing it), it is nothing like actual gameplay.  Archers are very difficult to use, and likely require hours and hours of practice to hit more than one shot in a life.  Other classes appear random in their behavior.
Problems I've seen:
- Hit main attack key, but you only HALF swing...
- Block/parry is MUCH more difficult than in training... You can block and aim right at the weaon, and they still cleave your head off.
- Shields appear useless.  I've held up Block, and had swords swing right through me.
- Every server I've joined, all people do is whine and kick players.  Team damage can be hard to avoid, and if you do anything like 10% team damage, they vote-kick.  Never seen such eagerness to vote-kick for such trivial reasons in other games.
Guess I'm glad I got to experience it, based on the videos I watched, but is it worth the purchase?  No.  Even on sale?  No.

(I played this game over 1500 hours.. so maybe time to write a review?)
WARNING: This review might be on the long side but very informative, I'll try to keep it short. (or read only the parts that might be usefull to you)
Q and A will be done at the end.
[NOTE English is not my main language so it might contain typo's]
Gametype:
The game is a 3rd person action PvE shooter, but there is a small area for PvP.
The maximum in PvE is 4 players in a game/match. PvP 4VS4 max.
The game is a grind game what you need to like to keep playing. All "warframes" and weapons can be lvled to lvl30.
There is also a player rank that only can be increased by the amount of weapons and warframes you have done.
Scene:
The genre and scene are placed in the future where you play a ninja kind of warrior called "Tenno". These warriors use the old ways of fighting with gun and blade. (rifles, shotguns, snipers, pistols, swords, hammers and way more)
You'll start out of a pod with no memory of your past. At that point you only know you got 1 enemy and those are the "Grineer". A massive clone army that are trying to get control over the solar system.
This way you have to find, read and listen to any kind of piece you find todiscover what happend in the past with your fellow Tenno's and yourself.
Gameplay:
The starting campaign is a nice introduction to get a bit known to the game. Varius gametypes are being shown at ya, some suit players better then others. This is a good thing to be with more.
After that the campaigns are not that well created and just to pull through and get the rewards. until far later in the solar system where there are suddenly a bunch of campaigns that give you a huge eyeopener.
NOTE: for this you'll have to reach Uranus.. (yeah, ha ha... =.=' planet with the funny name to finally get some action.)
Every Warframe and weapon acts different. Some Warframe got strong powers while others can survive longer under combat conditions.
To navigate over the solar system you'll need to play missions and unlock gates to go from planet to planet. these gates will stay unlocked ones opened. For each gate AKA "junction" you open you'll get rewards, like new campaign and weapons.
The starter weapons can be bought in the market of ingame "credits". Later weapons you can only buy weapon blueprints. These weapons need components to be build. This can take 12 till 24 hours, warframes might take longer sinse you have to build multible parts.
There is also a payed value called "platinum". with this you can buy right away other weapons or warframes.
Then there is a last value called "ducats" but those can only be used at the trader ones every 2 weeks.
Components can be found in every mission. Every planet got different components you need to build your gear.
A good tip is to pick up a much stuff that you'll find lingering on the ground or in crates. This is only benefit for later projects.
Warframes and weapons can be changed in color to what you prefer. Some of them can be changed by style also.
[NOTE all cosmetics can only be bought with platinum. while ALL weapons and most frames can be grinded and be played. It might take longer and more time to get it, but it's not impossible]
Warfame parts can be found defeating bosses. you might have to do it a few times but then you can get the blueprint of that warframe in the market.
Watch out how many times you defeat then though. It might attracted unwanted attention from those that hide in the shadows.
Once you got a weapon or warframe you can mod it to make it even become better. Mods can be found through matchs by killing enemies or as rewards for particular missions. There are hunderds of mods to work with and those mods can be upgraded too!
Community:
The community is really nice especially for those that get started. If you ask in your region chat for info there are most of the time at least 2 or 3 players to help you out.
Although there are also players that might complain about any of the updates (sometimes right, sometimes wrong. every game got those)
Developers and updates:
Developers will keep on their youtube channel and forums you up to date at least one or twise a month. On the youtube channel they also reward/highlight players and artists for anything they created based on the game.
Updates are being added from time to time. These updates bring also bugs with it. The developers most of the time solve these issues within the day or within the week.
Q and A:
Q: can you be revived in a match? A: yes, once you lose your health you'll lay on the ground for a while so other can revive ya. after that time you got 4 revive to respawn per match.
Q: platinum can i only get that by paying money? A: No, you can play a gamemode called void fissures. If you got a relic (what you'll more of eventually) out of those relics come prime parts. These prime parts can be traded. search and ask for correct prices but you'll be able to get platinum that way pretty fast. As long you sell the right parts for the right price.
I suggest to grind the parts and weapons you need. and keep platinum for all kind of cosmetics you want (example a nice color pallet so you can properly give you weapons and frames a nice style)
Q: Can you make clans? A: yes, clans can be created. these clan also get their own base called a "dojo". These dojo's must be build up from scratch though and require a bunch of components to do so.
You can expand your dojo, but that also means parts and research is going to cost more too. The reason all members should help to build it. you got 5 variants of clan sizes.
Ghost: Max 10 players.

TLDR at bottom...
It's a real shame how bad this game has got over the past couple or so years. it is most deserving of its 68/100 score, i would even mark it down from that.
If you want a game whose devs regularly cram more and more grindy garbage quests and pointless requirements nearly every major update that comes out, by all means download this game. I dont so much mind that items take mostly between 12-72 hours irl, it's the fact that most of the new items require a tremendous amount of ultra rare resources that only become available every once in a while (in Alert Quests) that only last for a few minutes to a few hours and randomly occurs (the days that these rare alerts occur isnt pre-scheduled).
the ultra rare resources and their rare quests isnt the only major disappointment. but the star chart that re-locks planets i had before the star chart update, contains lists (called junctions) of new requirements to fulfill in order to unlock those planets. you could have a Neptune Junction with 5-7 things you have to do in order to unlock Neptune, and they arent always as simple as defeat a boss, or acquire a number of common resources. sometimes the items on the list take days and days of grinding. sometimes they require a supremely powerful squad of Warframes to complete. sometimes you have to do it on ur own...
dont even get me started with the new VOID and relic key system.... im not gonna go here, its more of a headache to explain this system than it is to read about it. and speaking of reading about it, the wiki for warframe? also down the drain. if ur gonna play WF, ask ur questions in the region tab of the chat box, bc the wiki for warframe website, forces you to disable adblocker, and if u do that, it will force on you the hair-pullingly annoying auto-play-at-maximum-volume-videos... no thanks.
TLDR: the whole game has been inflated with 5000% more grindy objectives and requirements. in other words, it has become 5000% more boring. which is too bad that i am now quitting this game with so much money put into it, and so much platnum.

After over 100 hours on both the PS4 version then the PC version, I'm re-writing my review into a slightly longer, more accurate one.
Warframe is one of the most played games on Steam, best reviewed on Steam and one of, if not the best, free to play on Steam.
The gameplay is very fun with a lot of different weapons and Warframes (sort of classes) for you to use.
For the most part every single one is different, with 1 or 2 sharing similar abilities (not just copies though). By ranking up you get more powerful and unlock your 3 other abilities, and the max rank is 30. This game's character and weapon progression is mostly with using "mods" which you can find in every mission, with different rarities to them, and can be applied to all the equipment you have (as long as you use the right one, for example you have mods for Warframes, rifles, swords, shotguns, sentinels, ect) and you choose different ones depending on your chosen weapons, Warframe and desired playstyle to go with it. For example some excel at damage, crowd control, support, defensive.
You get to choose out of 3 Warframes at the start of the game for free (which are Excalibur, Mag and Volt)
you can level them up but don't get any kind of upgrades to them, only your mod capacity is increased which is how you will increase how powerful they are. There are lots of different weapons including rifles, shotguns, sniper rifles, bows, beam weapons, launchers and more.
You get to choose out of 2 primary weapons at the start including the MK-1 Braton (assault rifle) or the Paris (bow), as well as 2 secondary weapons; Lato (pistol) or Kunai (throwing daggers).
there are multiple different types like
With each weapon you can equip a
which changes how you attack with the weapon, which includes combos.
Warframe is capable of very fast gameplay because of it's movement system. Things you can do include double jumping, wall running (up and across walls), bullet jumping, sliding and holding onto walls, all while being able to shoot things.
As of now some of the things you can do include defence, survival, exterminate (kill all enemies on the map), capture (capture a certain enemy), spy (hack into terminals to steal data, if you set off the alarms you have a few seconds until the data is destroyed), sabotage (find and destroy objects in the map).
There are also timed alerts which grant rewards for completing them (like mods, resources,
Warframe helmets).
There are invasions where you will have to side with either 2 factions to defeat the other and you get a certain rare resource at the end of it.
Once you get a rank 30 Warframe and complete one of the later quests, you will have access to
which is a series of 3 missions (which change daily) and these have higher level enemies and certain modifiers on them, such as less energy, fire hazards, ect) and you get a random reward after completing all 3.
Archwing is a certain type of mission where you take part in either space or underwater combat. Personally this is the worst thing in the game since it's clunky and boring compared to the normal gameplay but I'm sure the devs will make changes to it eventually. It's not bad to play every so often
This game now has (mostly) optional quests which help further the story of the game, as well as unlock some new stuff.
Some of the quests are good, some are meh, but they are fun to do and the story is interesting.
Yes.
Everything in this game can be aquired without spending money on it at all.
Basically this game is a pay to speed things up. If you don't spend any money on it, you just have to play the game mostly to get the things you want and then craft it. Weapons have between a 8 and 24 hour wait time while Warframes take 3 days to craft.
If you enjoy grinding (playing the missions over and over) then you will love this game even without spending money.
You can sell items you find in-game in the trade chat to get the premium currency (platinum) and even buy the cosmetics or other things. There are daily rewards and one of them is a platinum discount so if you do want to buy platinum, you can get discounts by playing too.
Overall I definitely recommend Warframe if you don't mind grinding.

I'm guessing that being in beta lets them to have the freedom the revamp anything that doesn't seem fit or requires improvement *great I guess*.
As for the newcomers, welcome, as you have a lot to gain from this free game that rivals even AAA titles out there. It might be overwhelming and you might need to invest some time into this in order to even catch a glimpse of what this game has to offer. Being free to play you would expect a pay to win gimmick, you will not find that here.You don't even have to invest money into this game as you can earn platinum(which is in-game real currency) by trading around in the market. Plus it's not even mandatory to use platinum to get cool gear as you can get a lot of the items for free (cosmetics, slots ,colours excluded, but you can pay for it using platinum that you earned by trading.) ; you just have to farm for it *hence why people call this a farming simulator at times*.
Overall it's a great game to come back to once in a while and even better if you're new, I'd highly recommend it.

Hi! I've played this game for about 700 hours, over 2 years and a half (i use the game's launcher mostly). I'll assume you probably watched a few videos already, and know what Warframe is about, so i'll just give you some mildly opinionated pros and cons, in no particular order, followed by a short review.
Pros:
- very good looking graphics at max settings
- decent optimization, can be played on lower end machines while still looking quite ok
- absolutely unique style and atmosphere. Also has a few bits of welcome humor
- more work put into giving it some lore than with most shooters
- frequent updates, with new content, and (much needed) hotfixes
- very large playerbase, there's always someone to play with
- fast, fluid and responsive movement
- hundreds of weapons and dozens of armors (frames)
- interesting semi randomzied maps using well thought out tilesets
- many diverse enemy units and environments
- premium currency can be acquired by trading items you collected with other players (that said, this currency obviously had to be bought with real money by someone at some point)
Cons:
- new gameplay elements often seems to be added randomly, with no coherence
- overly complex weapon mechanics with lots of hidden maths involved
- lack of in-game information means almost mandatory use of an external wiki
- most experienced players tend to use the same 5% of available gear and plays the same 5% of mid-high level missions nodes again and again. Also no real end game.
- more bugs (new and old) than the devs can/want to fix, inevitably it adds up
- crazy amount of grind required for everything, very repetitive and quite unoriginal missions
- few short and not very fleshed out quests. The latest are significantly better though.
- never ending powercreep and nerfs renders what you worked for useless overnight
- unbalanced pvp, zero team play in pve (unless you play with your clan/friends only)
- extreme randomness of rewards means no achievable goals to directly work towards
- almost everything can be bought with premium currency, at insane price point
- some near insulting attempts at sneaky selling tactics. Please DE, we're not blind or dumb!
- pay or be lucky, pay or wait hours or even days, pay or be frustrated, etc. For everything
- in-game player to player trading is horrendously tedious on purpose
- last but not least, juvenile fanboys and wannabe elitists abound. Not the majority of course, but definitely annoying. No blacklist option unfortunately, but you can mute them. Also afk leechers.
______________
To summarize: i'm still not quite sure if i should recommend Warframe, at least in it's current state. Honestly, i must admit i enjoyed it for the most part, and it can even be really adictive. It has many undeniable qualities. But lately, in my opinion, the development became much more erratic and unfocused, the grind even more unreasonable, the cash grabs even more obscene etc... I don't like much where it seems to be heading for. Should you try it? Sure, why not, it's free after all (well somewhat), but keep in mind that it's also VERY time consuming, and the more you'll play, the more its many flaws and shallowness will become obvious and difficult to bear. Invest time (and money) at your own risk!

However I have to give it a bad review... and here is why.
If you're a student with lots of time on his hands and no life this is probably the place for you to be. The game makes such an emphasys on the grind that it is almost P2W. It is true that aside from cosmetics and inventory slots everything can be obtained for free, however you will have to put a ton of time into it. The developers are actively closing grind locations and making new obstacles in front of F2P players and the ingame currency (platinum) is quite expensive 200$ for 4300 plat (the largest pack available and the best price ratio) meaning ~22 plat for 1$. An average weapon bought for plat costs around 200 plat which means ~10$. Well that is if you are willing to take out 200$ from your pocket for this game, otherwise it'll cost you 15$ - 20$.
I say just buy three new AAA game releases and from the rest of the money buy some pizza.

DE outdid themselves in the latest quests by making the players play the same mission over and over again just to add playhours to a questline after which you would get only 1/4 of the reward. Making you grind a stupid new game mode for the other 3/4.
Yeah there's no auction house and no specific price for ingame items. All the trading is done in a trading chat that scrolls at the speed of light. I know this might not be viewed as a negative thing by those who grind a lot since this way the can sell items for double or triple the price of an ingame item. But for the most players it's a rippoff. In the end you'll either buy the item that just doesn't drop for you from the market and get skrewed by DE or from the tradechat for double the price and get screwed by some no life fatso.

It's an FPS... "S" stands for slasher.
Chivalry, is a multiplayer game that focuses on you stabbing, smashing and shooting ( with bow/crossbow ) your oponenets.
Set in the fantasy... sort of... universe, you join can choose to stand with the Agatha Knights, or the Mason Order. Why, for what? Why do you care? STAB PEOPLE!
Lore/story/anything-related is minimal, just giving what is needed and not much else to set the stage for you to fight.
But do not mind my story-seeking side - it's a good multiplayer game that offers much in a way of diversity. DIfferent game modes, 4 classes to choose from, multiple maps, progression system and even customisation of your game character.
Add little things like very clever quick-chat writing and voice-acting, the monty-pythonness feeling and you have a wonderful multiplayer experience.
I find this game a thrill to play, the gore and flying limbs add to it's hilariousity, making me laugh, not swear at my every silly death... unless it's a teamkill from a bugger that just clicks right mouse button all the time... Please, do not do it... Pretty pretty damn please.
The music is what I consider very good, setting the mood, ramping it up. Very good job, though it's not exactly rememberable.
The game looks good, but it takes a good PC to max out. My 2 year old machine mamages at high/mid-high settings to run smoothly at 1920x1080.
Game runs stable, though it rarely crashes on start up. I have nothing to complain about in that department.
It's a good game, simple as that.
UPDATE:
The issue with this game is now simple, developers don't uderstand the saying "If it ain't broke, don't fix it". With every patch this game becomes more cumbersome and annoying to play. UI and HUD changes coming out of nowhere, when nobody asked for them, changes that aren't light or easily passed by.
Performance is getting worse, at least in my case, loading times higher. Bugs appearing with every patch that are not fixed by the next one.
Good game, maybe worth it on a good discount sale. Otherwise, don't bother.

I'll give this a positive review, but I'll tell you this: It's nowhere near s addicting as some people say it is.
True, your first launch, you'll probably play 30 minutes. True, you'l be checking on this every day or two to see how much gold you made and how many upgrades to can get to kill everything brutally fast. That's a given, and really the only reason why this game is even somewhat addicting.
What's not true is spending hours upon hours on this game. You'll spend 30 minutes, an hour tops at a time on this. If you want a more addicting free game, try out AdVenture Capitalist. Another false claim is that this game is a life destroyer. Haha, NO. If you end up destroying your life because of this, that's pretty sad. xD
However, this game has some really good qualities to it. I know, shcocking for a free to play game. It has some really comical bits to it(such as clicking the enemies), it has some pretty funny upgrade descriptions, there are some pretty good enemy sprites, there are a LOT(I am not kidding when I say A LOT) of different heroes to buy, and since most of them have extra upgrades every 25 levels until you get them to level 100, you'll be spending A TON of gold on each hero, trying to level them up until you get that last extra upgrade. Another plus is that some upgrades will just affect one character, some will affect your CDS(Click Damage per Second), and some will affect your total DPS from all other heroes(Damage Per Second), and I like that.
Overall, this is a surprisingly fun free to play game. It's not the best, nor most addicting, however it will get you hooked into checking once or twice a day, for ten minutes spending all your gold you earned overnight or over the day and fighting up to a better boss that gets you more gold per kill. It's pretty cheesy in parts, and there are some cons, but there's not anything too major to point out in this. All in all, this is pretty good. When you're wanting something with at least decent replay value, give this a try. It's likely that you will end up liking it and end up getting pretty hooked. But if you want some REAL hooking, check out AdCap. You'll never go back between this game and AdVenture Capitalist. ;)

"Sorry" the game has finally arrived, get ready for team kills, team damage, and occasionaly a kill!
In all honesty though Chivalry: Medieval Warfare has to be one of the best Medieval first/third person slash and dice em up's I have ever played.  It is incredibly easy to jump into, with only LMB (standard swing) and RMB (block) being good enough for most to start off with, and to feel comfortable with.  However it is in this simplicity where Chivalry shines through, leading to combos etc using just the standard swing.  You also have a stab and an overhead attack for each weapon, which inturn leads to some varied and powerful combo attacks.  There are also kicks and feints which are useful in the right scenarios - leading to a varied and enjoyable fight every time.  As someone who has mastered (did he really type that?) most classes, except that pesky archer class! i can easily say to all newcomers, start with the Vanguard, he's the mid range fighter, and you can't go wrong with the weapon choices and range he posseses, alternatively if you want to really soak up damage and get a feel for a stronger hitting class try the knight to get used to the basic movements/attacks.
And get ready for that "Sorry" message on team chat to get engraved in your retinas guys, as team damage/killing can be a huge turn off for some, however with time, you should hopefully see it less and less.  If you don't rush into someone (friendly) whilst they are attacking, you should be fine, however there are people out there who intentionally seek to annoy others, if thats the case, there is a votekick system, however it is abused badly.  And that is the only gripe i have with Chiv, the constant abuse of team damage, be it intentional or done with intent, although duel servers are a good place to go not only for a good fight/practice (most times!)  but no team mates to blindly swing at, a one on one, intense and incredibly satisfying when you best your foe!

Left my positive review up for a long time, in honour of all the fun this game once gave me - but I recently uninstalled it, because ♥♥♥♥ it. High-level play is simply not fun - it's based around mechanics exploits. Some will argue whether they are "exploits" and that's fine - but the fact remains they are NO FUN. Even when the servers seem well-balanced, 99% of team objective games involve one side completely stomping the other. It's vaguely kind of enjoyable when you are the stomper the first few times, but eventually anyone who actually enjoys gaming will long for the rare *close* matches, whether they win or lose them. Once in a blue moon, you really do get a magnificent match - two skilled teams grinding away at each other, neither one utterly dominated by spinners and clanfolk, slowly giving and losing ground, until it comes down to a frantic 1-minute count on the final objective -- and when that happens, it honestly doesn't matter who wins, the game is so much fun for everyone. But those games have gotten rarer and rarer and rarer as the community has gotten worse and worse and worse (and "better" - in the sense of racking up cheap kills that preclude any of the interesting mid-battle duels that used to happen), and now it's just not worth it anymore.

While I had fun early on, after a while the slog just wore me down and sucked anything interesting out of the game. Add on the fact the developers don't appear to be interested in fixing some of the problematic balance, game issues, and graphical problems and I I eventually bowed out. My plan was to check the game out again after release, but it's become obvious the problems are never going to be fixed as the focus looks like it is solely on more critters and end game raiding.
Riding the dinos is fun as hell, but the grind is tedious.

Besiege castles and raid villages in Chivalry: Medieval Warfare, a fast-paced medieval FPS (Slasher with a Multi-player online focus)
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare is a first-person slasher with a focus on multi-player. Featuring competitive online combat that seeks to capture the experience of truly being on a medieval battlefield. Inspired from the intensity and epicness of swordfighting movies such as 300, Gladiator and Braveheart, Chivalry: Medieval Warfare aims to bring that experience to the hands of a gamer.
The game is skill-based and controls like a FPS, but instead of guns and grenades, players are given swords, shields, maces, battleaxes and longbows. Set in a fictional, yet gritty and realistic world, players will fight in fast paced online battles besieging castles, raiding medieval villages and fighting for glory in the arena with up to 32 players.

By the amount of hours you can see that I have spent quite a lot of time playing this game and it was really fun.
However I have to give it a bad review... and here is why.
If you're a student with lots of time on his hands and no life this is probably the place for you to be. The game makes such an emphasys on the grind that it is almost P2W. It is true that aside from cosmetics and inventory slots everything can be obtained for free, however you will have to put a ton of time into it. The developers are actively closing grind locations and making new obstacles in front of F2P players and the ingame currency (platinum) is quite expensive 200$ for 4300 plat (the largest pack available and the best price ratio) meaning ~22 plat for 1$. An average weapon bought for plat costs around 200 plat which means ~10$. Well that is if you are willing to take out 200$ from your pocket for this game, otherwise it'll cost you 15$ - 20$.
I say just buy three new AAA game releases and from the rest of the money buy some pizza.
By content I mean items that are "vaulted" (locked) only to be brought back after a while for an insane price (50$). Basically reselling the content that already is in the game. A really good approach from the company's point of view but not from yours.
The storyline missions are short and lacking enjoyable content. It seems that the people responsible for the storyline are having an imagination crysis. DE outdid themselves in the latest quests by making the players play the same mission over and over again just to add playhours to a questline after which you would get only 1/4 of the reward. Making you grind a stupid new game mode for the other 3/4.
Yeah there's no auction house and no specific price for ingame items. All the trading is done in a trading chat that scrolls at the speed of light. I know this might not be viewed as a negative thing by those who grind a lot since this way the can sell items for double or triple the price of an ingame item. But for the most players it's a rippoff. In the end you'll either buy the item that just doesn't drop for you from the market and get skrewed by DE or from the tradechat for double the price and get screwed by some no life fatso.
If you're expecting variety from this game then just try something else. There are several mission types in this game and you'll do them over and over.

Warframe is a wonderfully bizarre offering. It's take on the budding "loot shooter" genre is both well executed, and occasionally quite innovative. I don't keep up with the dev updates and live broadcasts, but I can tell you without a shadow of a doubt, that this is a game made by folks who love games, and love the game they make.
What is it? A smooth as silk 3rd person mutiplayer sci-fi action rpg. It's action is fast paced, it's loot and progression systems fascinating, and the sheer amount of crazy ninja movement options will have you gleefully bouncing off of futuristic factory equipment while spraying bullets out of your gigantic arsenal of weaponry.
Cherry on top: It's free. There IS premium currency, however, in-game trading (while clunky) makes any real money purchase competely optional. You can get anything you want just by playing and selling your unwanted loot to others.
If I could levy any actual criticism at this title, it would be it's occasional lack of focus. New systems are lovingly crafted and introduced, only to languish untouched while the devs excitedly add the next big thing. This is really not a big deal though, as most content is already of such high quality.
A grade A quality game. Download. Play. Enjoy.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare is really odd, no story. Training mode, two sides in multiplayer, Agatha Knights and the Mason Order, so its call of duty but medieval weapons? well sorta, But it is more than that.
The mechanics in this game feel new and when you get a kill streak you have shown some serious skill, you're not rewarded, but you have killed 3 enemies with a spear and taken little damge so get back in the fight you damned knight!!!
Its rarly dumb luck when you get a kill in this game. Camping is possible but realative to other shooter. You want be camping with your crossbow for too long as it takes a long realistic time to reload, plenty of time for a knight to come lope your head off. The classes are balanced and the game feels like a genuine challenge, you have to perfect your block or you won't last long, learn to duck to show some fancy skills, feint to♥♥♥♥♥♥me off and then stab me in the side.
As with all great games your skills will develop over time, real skills, not perks or better weapons, you actually learn to fight with a freaking sword and you will have fun doing so. The community is pretty good. Getting into games seems decent at the moment. Something I really enjoy is the Dueling game mode. Its a one on one fight. No risk of backstabbing unless your too slow of course and your enemy gets to your back (its like prison).
The Game is as raw as a first person multiplayer can get at this stage I think, in the sense that you have to get up close and personal for the majority of the classes, (archery is a pain and only for those who have mastered it) you must keep moving otherwise you will be surrounded by the enemy in a good team deathmatch. So with this raw first person swordplay you start thinking of stragety a bit more. You start noticing trends in enemy movement. You antcipate other players whereabouts. After playing for a while go play COD or Battlefield and notice how different you play those games. Its a brilliant game and I have enjoyed it more than the big bullet blockbusters. Long live First Person Swordplay.

This game has some special magic which makes it's first-person perspective melee combat actually work.  It encourages thoughtful positioning as well as quick reflexes.  It balances equipment load outs so that speed, power and defense all have their place on the field.
The environments are well designed and pleasant to take in during momentary breaks from hectic battles.  The objectives vary heavily from death-match, to capture the flag, to bomb delivery, to complex multi-stage siege and defense missions.
Unfortunately, it is online-arena only.  Outside of the tutorial, there is no single player or co-op campaign.  Simply a disparate collection of poorly named, poorly defined user hosted servers; where you can roll the dice and see what you end up with.  As is often the case for online games with no campaign or structure, it simply wasn't able to hold my attention for more than a few hours.  But I would love to see these mechanics transplanted into something more cohesive.

Before you read it : I got 400+ hours, and it's nothing next ot most people who reviewed this game. Just go try it and have fun ok?
Any Warframe fan will tell you : this game is sweet and sour in one package.
Pros are that it's an excellent third person shooter with great mechanics, varied weapons and warframes (that you can consider to be the equivalent of a class/hero/champion with its own kit).
I'll be honest to you by saying that except Vanquish, this is the best TPS game I've played.
If you're looking for a game to pass time, if you like space ninja, if you like one against many kind of games : this game is for you.
But while Warframe got great qualities, it also have cons : the game has rpg mechanics (it's not the con yet).
- And those rpg mechanics involve a whole new level of farming depending of what you want in this game (e.g Equinox or Mesa...Hema...) which sometime just throw you off of it. It is a great feeling to overcome an insane grind and get what you've always desired, but I feel like some middle ground could be found between "one shot this boss 3 times to get a great warframe" and "play a daily mission at least 3 times to have a one coordinate then do it again the day later until you have a shot at one boss to get one piece of a great warframe...bear in mind that the piece you'll get might be a duplicate so hope you have time for that".
- The 2nd problem I and a lot of people are stuck with is : if you like the game and spend a copious amount of time on it, you'll wake up one day and realise there's no closure. No "endgame". You've made your weapons, sentinels, warframes and whatnop stronger and stronger over the time only to realise that you have...nothing that can challenge you. It's a little bit like the feeling Saitama get in One Punch Man : you're just too strong to care about the opposition yet you still are here roaming around trying to find it.
The game is a good game that'll keep you busy for a LONG time, but I wish that once the grind was done people could log in "just to have fun", and from what I've seen I know that DE is more than capable to give this kind of content. I don't know if a lot of people feel like me but this game got a golden mine of untapped potential (Syndicates, Boss, Starchart on hard mode (lvl60-120 ?)), and if this ever get unleashed, this game will just overshadow even the best AAA of the genre : because a lot of people played this game for hundreds of hour, and a lot of them want to just go on playing.
So in conclusion : I recommend this game (of course) while adding that it is possible that it'll only get better. And I really hope it will because it can. it easily can. And if they get it right they'll hit such a jackpot. (I really really hope it goes right...)

Wow, mixed reviews? I've run Ark on a high-end gaming PC and a mid-tier gaming laptop both and have had no real bug issues on either.
This game is good. Really good. SP is kinda meh and gets boring pretty quick, official servers are painfully grindy and not noob friendly. But there are a million unofficial servers to match anyone's taste or gaming style. The majority of my near-1500 hours were spent on three different unofficial servers.
The price point sucks, but only as an early access title. Wildcard's hand was forced to match retailer pre-order pricing. All in all this game is worth the $60 tag. The four incorporated maps total up to about 1000 sq miles of rich and varied terrain, there are hundreds of critters to tame, train, breed, and use, sea, land, and air.
Some tips: Find a server with increased rates. 4-6x rates are fair and balanced. If you don't like PvP but want the OPTION of PvP find a PvPvE server. The Structures Plus (s+ tag) fixes and adjusts snap points and will likely be incorporated into the core game. Always carry an axe and a pick in case you get hung up between a rock or tree and the terrain.
In short, shop around for a server, find a decent community, stay away from official servers until you've really mastered the game.
If you'd rather, server rental prices have come down considerably. For about $15 a month you can run your own server with 40 slots and make your own rules, choose your own mods.
Don't let the negative reviews scare you off. This game is fantastic. One of the best I've ever played. And replayability is endless.

I will be reveiwing "Clicker Heroes" today. Keep in mind that I've played countless hours of this game soley on the browser version and so my current number of hours does not represent my knowledge on the game. However, I admittedly haven't played in a while. I did a quick recap of this game on steam and it hasn't changed much.
Let me start out with stating the fact that there is a bizarely shocking number of people who dislike this game for various reasons. Let me list some common reasons I've seen in the reviews on the Steam version of the game and a short response to each one.
1) The game is basically cookie clicker with microtransactions.
Response: So what? First off - it's completely free to play. If you knew what cookie clicker is and how it did things you know this game is all about grinding gold and such to get upgrades to your clicks. Furthermore, you don't even have to do anything to rack up gold in this game after a certain point. You literally don't need to "play" it. This is achievement grinder 2015.
2) The game has no "skill" or anything involved. "It's just clicking!"
Response: Pull your head out of your♥♥♥♥♥promptly. Please locate the part in the description of this game where it says this is a "Highly skill based game!" and then I'll get back to you. It's as casual as it gets, truly.
3) Pay to Win.
Response: AHAHAHAHAHA oh god. Please! Please!
4) It's easy to just cheat so what's the point?
Response: I don't know. If you feel like breaking a game and finding ways to cheat in it (IE: getting an auto clicker of sorts) that's your own thing. Truly, who gives a damn? This isn't an MMO, this isn't Call of Duty. You're only cheating yourself out of hours upon hours of "riveting" gameplay. This game is meant to be casual in the first place, so do us all a favor and stop your ♥♥♥♥♥ing please and thank you.
--------------------------------------------------------
Now that that's out of the way let me touch on what this game advertizes and offers up front to you, the consumer.
-Ascend to be able to have DPS's of up to " one quadrillion damage per second ".
-Know how " one quadrillion damage per second" feels.
-Click on monsters to kill them and get gold (virtual) for it.
-Hire heroes to deal more damage which in turn will up your kills per minute, which ups your gold per minute in general.
-"Meet" legendary figures such as Athena. 35 unique heroes to hire.
-Make your MMO character's feel like kindergarteners because of their damage per second's.
-Spend your "hard earned loot" to upgrade your heroes and gain special abilities from them.
-Over 100 different monsters, all beautifully drawn and animated, including boss creatures.
-Earn gold while you're idle. No clicking required if you have heroes! Earn while you do the laundrey, etc.
-----------------------------------------------
Now, looking at these features the game seems to offer most of them. To be honest, I haven't put in the play time to verify some of these features but at this point and time I trust the developers on their numbers. I don't think they'd lie to me about what they advertised in their game. 35 unique heroes, I'm sure there are. Over 100 monsters? Great! I'll be counting and I'll compile a list and update this at a later date. I haven't gotten to nearly anywhere near one quadrillion dps but I'm sure it's possible given one of the acheivements for this game is to reach zone 2400 (or something), which would - given my experience - require a "metric f*ck ton" of damage per second to beat anything there.
So far I recommend this game. That may change if I find the features to be lacking compared to what was advertised. Far too often people expect far too much from a game when the developers didn't even advertise it. A game shouldn't be based on anything other than what the developers advertise regarding a rating. That being said, a game can be flat out crap and even broken. However, this game is none of that.
Clicker heroes is a very well done super casual game with all the tools a casual gamer could ever want to use as well as plenty of acheivements to complete and many other things to aquire in game for you collectionists and completionists out there. Even if your interaction with the game is minimal you can still enjoy getting achievements.
Clicker heroes will receive a high rating from me for a few reasons. First off, I genuinely enjoyed it. It's cute, it's a light bit of fun and can be worth the expresso shots to wake you up in the morning after a hard, long night of advancing your quest to get carpel tunnel syndrome from clicking like a mad man with multiple fingers on multiple hands and feet. No one is there to call you a noob, tell you to uninstall or learn to play, because it's not targetted at an audience such as that. So, secondly, it knows who it's marketing to. It doesn't claim to be a "skill based game" or any nonsense like that. It doesn't claim to have great graphics (though it does deliver on it's lovely art style), or have fantastically new and intriguing features or have a world that has you immersed
in it's riveting and in depth storyline and world.
It's just a fun, casual time waster based on clicking the same spot hundreds upon thousands of times, or farming gold from your heroes and making the odd update here and there.
For these reasons I give this game a TEHN AOUTTA TEHN!

With tons of items, non Pay2Win ethics, and excellent gameplay and graphics, Warframe has managed to take my attention for 48 hours (so far), and I love it. The gameplay is fast, fun, and simple, it takes your generic third-person shooter and adds samarai movies and sci-fi, making the combat very unique and a blast to play. The graphics are on par, if not better than AAA games of current day. The vast amount of items to collect and use will keep you hooked for a long time, each gun and Warframe will change your play style completely, and you can earn every one of them for free, the only items you can only buy are cosmetics. Not everything is perfect though, the boss fights seem too bullet spongey, the missions are pretty repetitive, and the grinding can get pretty ridiculous. But the positives overwelmingly outweigh the negatives, and I religously recommend this game to anyone. And why wouldn't you try it? It's free!

So, I've read a lot of the reviews on here lately, and I'm simply amazed how much people cry.
I bought Ark as soon as it came out, and with 2 GTX 690's, I could barely get a tolerable framerate on low. However, I kept playing, and man has this game been optimized compared to launch.
The developer team has put a lot of effort, and during the period I played the most, there were ATLEAST 4 updates a week with content, bug fixes, server performance improvement and client imporvement, SEVERAL times a week.
Then the first negative review wave came, when the devs stated that they were gonna start balancing wild vs tamed dinosaurs, so they nerfed the everliving crap out of tamed dinosaur. This made the game difficult, as you couldn't just faceroll whereever you went, and of course this caused a HUGE outcry. "Oh my god, a survival game that is hard, what a♥♥♥♥♥♥game"......
Next outcry wave, when blood leeches and diseases were added, holy hell, people almost started crying because they had to make an antidote to survive, IN A GOD DAMN SURVIVAL GAME!
Do people even know what games they are getting into?
I've played, and I'm still playing Ark, and I'm having a fantastic time playing it. Animations are good, graphics is gorgous, PvE element is actually relevant (my server has nerfed tamed dinos even more), PvP is scary and gets your heartth pumping as there's actually something hanging in the balance.
Also a thing to mention is that the dev team has been in contact with the community throughout the entire early access, listening to what people want (Scicle for example took like 1 week to implement after being suggested), responding to posts and updating the came constantly.
The game is worth the money for sure, I wouldn't have anything against paying the fee that is now for the game, as I find it a very challenging, in depth, well make, still being worked on title that is worth every penny ( for gods sake, two play modes, 5 HUGE maps where you can start over to get a completely new experience (oh yes, cry me a damn river that one is a paid DLC)).
This game is amazing, and all the people who "hate" it because it won't run smoothly on their 100 Dollar computer or can't handle the fact that the game is in fact a survival game where you're not handed everything you want, you guys, we don't need you.
TLDR; people are crying because the game demands you to actually work for survival, game is super worth the money, and a HUGE thumbs up from me!
To all the haters of the game, go play Rust please...

So, I've read a lot of the reviews on here lately, and I'm simply amazed how much people cry.
I bought Ark as soon as it came out, and with 2 GTX 690's, I could barely get a tolerable framerate on low. However, I kept playing, and man has this game been optimized compared to launch.
The developer team has put a lot of effort, and during the period I played the most, there were ATLEAST 4 updates a week with content, bug fixes, server performance improvement and client imporvement, SEVERAL times a week.
Then the first negative review wave came, when the devs stated that they were gonna start balancing wild vs tamed dinosaurs, so they nerfed the everliving crap out of tamed dinosaur. This made the game difficult, as you couldn't just faceroll whereever you went, and of course this caused a HUGE outcry. "Oh my god, a survival game that is hard, what a♥♥♥♥♥♥game"......
Next outcry wave, when blood leeches and diseases were added, holy hell, people almost started crying because they had to make an antidote to survive, IN A GOD DAMN SURVIVAL GAME!
Do people even know what games they are getting into?
I've played, and I'm still playing Ark, and I'm having a fantastic time playing it. Animations are good, graphics is gorgous, PvE element is actually relevant (my server has nerfed tamed dinos even more), PvP is scary and gets your heartth pumping as there's actually something hanging in the balance.
Also a thing to mention is that the dev team has been in contact with the community throughout the entire early access, listening to what people want (Scicle for example took like 1 week to implement after being suggested), responding to posts and updating the came constantly.
The game is worth the money for sure, I wouldn't have anything against paying the fee that is now for the game, as I find it a very challenging, in depth, well make, still being worked on title that is worth every penny ( for gods sake, two play modes, 5 HUGE maps where you can start over to get a completely new experience (oh yes, cry me a damn river that one is a paid DLC)).
This game is amazing, and all the people who "hate" it because it won't run smoothly on their 100 Dollar computer or can't handle the fact that the game is in fact a survival game where you're not handed everything you want, you guys, we don't need you.
TLDR; people are crying because the game demands you to actually work for survival, game is super worth the money, and a HUGE thumbs up from me!

The vanilla game and concepts revolving around it are intensely flawed both balance-wise and from a technical standpoint due to a massive number of issues from simple visual errors to horrible framerate issues for people with hardware better than what existed when the game first launched.
The developers are hellbent on constantly adding more content of any shape or form without spending the time to refine what they already have, doing haphazard changes to numerical balance and serverside values without actually going any deeper.  This is the entire basis for this negative review:
There's something to get around this, but it doesn't influence my recommendation, and it is as follows:
Private servers are havens for this game, but finding one that fits your niche style is an odyssey.  I'm not exaggerating.  You have to find what LOOKS good, double-check through HTML server browsers in your web browser, try to join, download the mods on it one at a time at an incredibly reduced speed, reconnecting to start the next mod every 60 seconds or so as the connection attempt aborts if the downloads of multiple gigabyte overhauls don't finish in that timeframe, do this an unknown number of times because servers only report a maximum of 4 running mods to server browsing websites when many run much more, finally connect, make your character, jump in and test the waters before realizing the admin screwed up the settings somehow because you're pooping every 5 seconds, there's 5 times as many extremely aggressive dinosaurs on the beach you start on, one of them is glowing and instantly kills you by looking at you and throwing hitscan projectiles (thanks annunaki), the admins are absent and all the buildable terrain has been griefed, a mod is broken and crashes the server, or WHATEVER.  There's so many things that can go wrong and despite being the primary way people play the game nowadays the developers have done nothing to make it easier on people.
You cannot search by mod on the server browser.
You cannot filter on the server browser except by name, password protection, and occupancy.
You cannot see ANY information about mods on the server browser.
You cannot view modified variables of a server using the server browser.
You cannot opt to download all the mods through steam at your leisure on connection since it only queues one at a time and only while attempting a server connection.
You cannot filter out servers using or not using anti-cheat.
You cannot filter out servers that don't match your game version.
Do you get the picture?  The best parts of the game are intentionally neglected to be harder to access.  Why?  Who knows.  There's nothing the devs get by you playing on the official servers.
Now, if they actually fixed the issues with finding a server you like it might actually change my opinion on the game, but it still wouldn't make it run well, it wouldn't fix issues with the game itself that are hardcoded, it wouldn't fix the actual game.  For that, the game gets an easy thumbs down.

Imagine, if you can, Dynasty Warriors with THE most fluid and responsive 3rd person shooter controlls you'll ever play.  I cannot sing enough praise for its movement system.  I can (and have) spent days just surfing through its randomly generated levels.  You and up to 4 friends will be doing flips, rolls, and John Woo styled "bullet jumps/aim glides" as you parkour through (or right past) 100's of enemies that struggle to comprehend that you're a space ninja and there's very little they can do to stop you.
Add that it has a HUGE variety of weapons and characters that you can tinker around with and upgrade to your own personal preferences, I'm always coming back to experiment with one thing or another.  I'd say about 90% of all that stuff can be attained with relatively minimal grinding too.  The remaining 10% of stuff that you'd actually have to grind for?  Mostly gimmick weapons that are outclassed by everything else in the game.
Oh and it's free to play with a shockingly reasonable model.  Want that new gun or character?  Okay, do like 3 or so missions to get the materials, then throw it into the oven to cook for 3 days.  Voila, fresh gun.  Don't want to wait?  Buy it now then I guess.  Or throw it into the oven and get a reduced price for having gathered all the materials already.  The only real constraint is the initial amount of slots you're given for weapons and characters, but for the first 10-15 hours or so of gamplay, you'll probably want to level up your starter gear first (max level of 30, easy to do) before you branch out.
The only thing about this game that legitimately holds me back from recommending it is how much of an unnecessary learning curve the begginning of the game has.  The game takes zero amount of time to explain what mods are most ideal for you when you're just starting out.  It fails to explain which types of damage work well (or don't) against which factions and that elemental mods are outright superior to physical mods.  Because of this, I had a friend who gave up on the game, saying it was too hard, when again, this game is for the most part dynasty warriors level of easy.  It's more about styling on enemies than it is overcoming them.
Not to say the game doesn't have its hard content.  There's all sorts of endless missions where people make it a sport to see how far or long they can go before they need to extract from a mission.  It's there, but you're almost never forced to go there either, so it's got something for everybody.
So yeah, if you actually dig in and figure out how to mod your weapons/characters, maybe rebind some keys here and there for comfort, you might end up addicted like me and 26 million other registered losers.

Warframe is a wonderfully bizarre offering. It's take on the budding "loot shooter" genre is both well executed, and occasionally quite innovative. I don't keep up with the dev updates and live broadcasts, but I can tell you without a shadow of a doubt, that this is a game made by folks who love games, and love the game they make.
What is it? A smooth as silk 3rd person mutiplayer sci-fi action rpg. It's action is fast paced, it's loot and progression systems fascinating, and the sheer amount of crazy ninja movement options will have you gleefully bouncing off of futuristic factory equipment while spraying bullets out of your gigantic arsenal of weaponry.
Cherry on top: It's free. There IS premium currency, however, in-game trading (while clunky) makes any real money purchase competely optional. You can get anything you want just by playing and selling your unwanted loot to others.
If I could levy any actual criticism at this title, it would be it's occasional lack of focus. New systems are lovingly crafted and introduced, only to languish untouched while the devs excitedly add the next big thing. This is really not a big deal though, as most content is already of such high quality.
A grade A quality game. Download. Play. Enjoy.

Warframe used to be a great co-op PvE Game, and while It's constantly updated with new content and features, the developers didn't worked hard enough to ease how the game awards the player. I don't mean the daily award system, I mean the way to earn premium credits to purchase premium only content such as weapons and cosmetics. The only way to obtain premium credits without paying any real money is to endlessly grind on void fussures to obtain a random drop or complete a set and sell it to the trading market. It's not easy at all, it's not like you can list it as a broker and wait if someone actually buys it, you have to announce it to the trading chat and wait for any buyers. Most of the time because the items are really common nobody wishes to buy them.
Even if you pay real money which I spent over 70EUR my Experience wasn't really improved, my Characters may look superior in terms of cosmetics in contrast with the free player but we do actually have the same exact experience. If you really complete the solar missions, all the available quests eventually the game becomes insanely repetitive.
Bottom line, the gameplay is great with fluent controls and intense action, the grinding is very tedious and the game is barricaded with huge pay walls.

Warframe is basically a grinder 3rd person action shooter with some RPG elements where you, the operator, execute (grind) various type of missions throughout the solar system planets and more, wearing one of the "Warframe" special suits that provides protection, incredible acrobatic movements and special powers. On paper this sound like a thrilling concept and can be for some time, but the game has its own problems, some of which it always had and got worse with the time, that can end overshadowing such features.
+ Free to play, if you are good at trading you can get everything you need without spending any rl money.
- However new implemented resources or features are becoming harder and harder to obtain (grind or wait) without spending any rl money. That's somewhat fine, but it is getting gradually worse.
- If you don't have much time to play, you will have issues with the inventory and in gathering resources.
+ You can play solo, or with up to 4 players COOP, or up to 8 players for Raid type missions.
- One of the players pc "host" these missions which can result in severe lag and desync problems and frustration -- depending on who is hosting.
++ Very good game engine, good fps and good detailed graphics.
+ The devs are regularly improving their graphics, lightning and performance technology.
- However i'm not a fan of the overall style, Warframes often have an organic look, and the factions look weird.
+ Fun and fluid gun and run system, allows for a somewhat ninja / matrix'esque style.
+ Plenty of weapons and "warframes" to equip and use (each warframe comes with its own stats and set of powers).
- The vast majority of them will become useless past a certain mission level.
+ Some boss fights and missions can be fun.
- But will eventually become just another boss or grind session with little challenge.
+ You can create, build and decorate your own "dojo" (your clan's base). And use it as a player trading center, for pvp duels or general chilling.
- It takes loads of resources and waiting time to do so though.
- Devs just don't seem to know how to balance their game (mostly regarding pve). And power creep got worse over time.
- Eventually you'll run into bugs or glitches which can potentially ruin a 30-60+ minutes long mission. Every new major content update usually comes with a bunch of new bugs.
+ But usually major bugs are fixed fairly quickly, or they try to.
- The whole game is based on grinding and killing hordes of enemies. That's almost all you are gonna do unless you are into pvp.
- Time limited events and contents. Means if you take a break or don't feel like playing the game, you'll miss that content (special versions of weapons, skins, special mods or cosmetics).
- Updates are usually focused on cosmetic stuff, a couple of weapons to play with and some bug fixes.
- Updates often lacks any interesting idea or significant feature.
-- Most of Warframes and weapons will become useless due to balance and game design (horde style enemies).
It isn't a bad game per se, but I won't recommend it to someone due to the repetitivity and the direction this game has been heading and handled over the years.

The amount of grinding in this game is crazy, but its worth it, once you get away from the begginer phase aka the MR5 curse, you begin to have a completely new look at the game, you've finished the star chart and finally learned how relics work, you've obtained your first Prime and possibly even learned about Lua Drift Mods and the puzzle rooms. There is alot this game hides that you can't see, and it's darn rewarding when you unock those stages of the game.

And one of those things is the Foundry, I honestly hate it when im building cypher's for a spy mission because i suck at hacking corpus coms. Well, starting this game up again after a really long break, i suppose i should give a review of it at this point.
For starters, seeing the amount of hours i have clocked in this game startled me slightly, but im thinking a decent amount of it was AFK or maybe im kidding myself. oh well.
The game itself has moved quite a bit since i initially started playing it, which is to say, that originally there was no help, and everything drop related was pretty much RNG.
Now, you get eased into things, and early missions give you the very basic of things, so you get covered that way, which is kinda nice, considering farming for rare RNG when we are talking common "must have" items was never fun.
Warframe is a nice game, graphics are nice, and the playstyle is fast albeit challenging at times, as it should be.
It is however a farming game, and you will need to do a lot of it, if you want to git gud at it.
Warframe is actually truly
, but it means you will have to sell some things you need, making you, in turn, have to farm some more, to get them yourself.
You can't pay to win here, but rather pay to skip, which is fine, as although it makes some things easier, it's still not viable for the long haul.
In the end, i ended up paying for some ingame currency, to skip some corners, a few times, but considering how much time i've spent on the game, i'd say they deserve it.
TLDR;
Game is good, endgame is weak.
For a Free to Play, it does'nt get much better.
Play with friends, or find some ingame, a good squad makes everything better here.

I had high expectations of this game. Don't take my review as your final answer if you want to buy this game. If you like medieval stuff that's fine. I was expecting a fast-paced FPS version of Counterstrike or Call of Duty, and that's not what I got. I didn't like it because the game seemed unfinished to me. The HUD was overly simple with no option to change it, the textures were pretty gross, and the combat was chaotic at best but very slow at worst. There are multiple ways to kill people like slashing, stabbing and overhead attacks but none of these seem very different from one another and stabbing (the one I thought would take the shortest amount of time) was almost useless because of the time it took to stab someone. On top of that, the tutorial levels glitched up for me so I wasn't able to complete them. I feel that there should have been some sort of actual mission to get you into the game, other than just the option to play with bots. The servers were very laggy for me, and I was not able to play with my friends 9 times out of 10. The textures were also very gross and reminded me of a low-quality Oblivion even when they were at max settings. Overall I'd give the game a 4/10, but I may not have played it long enough to make a decision like this. I'll play it again in the future to see if I like it more, but the community was very rude and the game itself wasn't fun for me.

Before I go over why I like this game, one thing must be made clear: This is one hell of a grind fest. You grind to level up your gear, you grind to upgrade your gear, you grind to get points to upgrade your upgrades with, you grind for resources to build gear from blueprints (which you have to grind for), and then grind that gear also, and so on and so forth. Grindfest.
That said, the core gameplay loop is pretty fun. Drop into mission, kill things, complete objective, repeat. I grew up on things like Unreal Tournament while also being bad at PvP, so this game appeals to me like a vastly superior version of Gears of War horde mode. There is a large variety of weapons to kill things with (after you grind for them, of course), many of which are satisfying to use. The parkour system is enjoyable, despite sometimes being clunky. Also, everything in the game (aside from some cosmetics) can be aquired without spending real money, and there isn't any real reason to spend real money except for impatience (I'll admit, I've spent probably $100 over the past year, but compare that to something like a wow subscription and it's not that unreasonable).
At the time of writing, steam has tracked 334.4 hours of game time, it's surpassed Civilization 5 as my most played  game on steam, and is well on it's way to becoming my most played game ever. Unless the devs do something to break the game such as give me incurable space herpes, I'd be hard pressed not to reccomend this game.

The good
Maps are massive, a huge roster of tameable dinos and monsters including fantasy creatures. The survival aspect is modest, not too in your face but not something you can ignore either. Tons of mod support which is the lifeblood of games like these now a days.
The bad
The game is horridly unoptimized, this game runs like crap on even some modern systems sporting cutting edge hardware. This is due to poor optimization that the devs have said they will be working on before release but at the time of writing this review have yet to see full implimentation. Expect horrid FPS and huge sacrifices to get decent, playable FPS.
Wildcard has been performing some very anti-consumer business practices such as dropping DLC for the game while it's still in 'early access' and hiking the games price before it's even released. This should come as a red flag for anyone dipping into this game, expect more scummy business practices till the community ropes the devs in.
Light end game. The game does have a few bosses for the end game content but only a few now. Said bosses are incredibly well built but few and far between, other then this and a few dungeons loaded with mid-tier creatures.
For now I will set this as a not recommended simply because peoples money matters and for the moment, Wildcards dirty buisness practices outweigh the bonuses for this game and it still runs horridly for a game that is less then a month from release. On the flip side, if you can get it to run for you and find it on sale it's fabulous fun and should distract you for a while. Only time will tell where content and mods take it.

Another great release by Riot Games.
Warframe is a cooperative RTS with shooter elements, set in the future. Whilst Riot Games would have you beleive that this is a dedicated top-down shooter, the game would rather have you nursing pets in your space ship and investing time in menu after menu only to discover you lack resources to proceed with your mandatory crafting. The game is bricked behind numerous paywalls that aim to remove days long waiting periods for crafting.
The focus of Warframe is not well-founded. It tries to be an mmo, promising guild features such as guild halls, and PVP. At the same time it tries to be a pet simulator and something resembling an Arcade shooter from 1989. The story in Warframe has it's charm. You play as a fugitive from Earth who goes by the name Tenno, who recently busted out of prison following an attack from an alien race known as the Lotus. The Lotus are a savage clan of warlords and mercenaries that wear suits of armour known as the Warframes. These Warframes are sent to hunt Tenno, until he befriends a race known as the Grineer, a peaceful race of people who suffer the same attrocities perpetrated by the Lotus.
In a series of long and repetetive quests, you learn from a DNA test that you are in fact Lotus. Upon this realisation you are gifted a Warframe and change sides without any clear motive. The game then devolves into a repetetive, merciless and systematic slaughter of your former Grineer allies without any real resolution to Tenno's prior conflicts. Following this story arc, the game just becomes a series of grind to win missions which become easier if you elect to pay large sums to Riot Games through the in-game store.
Overall, we at Flaming Skull games rate Warframe 3 skulls/10.

Concerned with the direction of the game.
I have played massive amounts of Warframe, I love the game. I love the gameplay. DE has, for a long time, been very good with their monetization model.
Lately, however, with the addition of rivens, and the handling of focus, I am losing confidence in them. Acquiring focus is boring. The benefits of gaining focus is lackluster. Rivens are a literal monetization of game balance. They updated focus by reducing the cost of upgrading nodes, but it's still nowhere near enough. They have done nothing to address how boring it is to grind for focus. I want to have fun while playing a game, not doing a task so mindlessly repetitive it feels like working in an assembly line. They based the entire system around you always paying for an affinity booster, which I have done, and I am quickly realizing they're trying to inch up microtransactions in subtle, indirect ways as much as they possibly can.
Rivens are a good example of indirect monetization. They don't sell them directly to you, they sell you the currency you use to buy rivens from other players. They're still making the money, there's just one extra step involved.
They're inching further and further into a territory that is focused entirely on making money off the players, even if it starts to degrade their experience and enjoyment of the game. I hate to imagine what this game will look like in one or two more years.
Plains of Eidolon was also so buggy the first couple weeks it launched it was clear they did not adequately QA test the missions. Some missions were breaking literally over half the time, like the armored vault for example. Not to mention, they effectively FORCE you to do "gathering" professions like fishing to progress in the game as well. I don't want to go fishing. I don't like fishing in video games. They're just bludgeoning the players of this game over the head with boring, required tasks.
Focus is such a mess I don't even have any desire to progress in that system, leaving me with no desire to continue playing this game, and the rewards for doing teralysts/cetus are similarly so unmotivating I have no desire to do that content either.
