After a thousand hours or so of just letting this thing run, I've come to the conclusion that the addiction is real. Going for that next achievement, going for that next hero, ascension, etc. etc. etc. One thing became clear though, I wasn't doing anything with this at all. It sat in the background doing it's thing while I did everything else but play the game. Sure, I'd flip screens once in a while and click kill a boss or something, but overall, it was the same thing over and over again. The forced ascensions to progress further into the Grind Chain™ simply made the game excruciating after a while. YAY! I hit level 600! Oh, I'm not getting a lot of gold or progressing fast enough, looks like we "reboot" and start over from the beginning. I started ascending at relic gain or 1,000 hero souls, whichever came first. And then doing it all over again and again and again and again...
If you don't mind drooling at a screen for hours on end and clicking like a monkey for it's next hit of crack, get this game. You'll probably enjoy it. If you're curious about clicker games like this and Cookie Clicker, get it, you'll see what they're like and possibly enjoy them.
Me? I'm tired of this game, it has become pointless, like Farmville or Mafia Wars. There is zero risk. There is zero challenge. Only the Grind Chain™ remains. And that, in a nutshell, is pure uselessness to me.
I pushed through the game and enjoyed the graphics (very pretty stuff!) and some of the ideas in this game are kinda cool. Alright, ever since joining this game since 2013 in closed beta and joining back in march 2016 and after 1.5k hours of this game since March 2016 and hearing a lot of negativity, I feel like giving my two cents about this game...
Is it a good game? Yes. Is it perfect? Absolutely not.
First and foremost, the reason why I started playing warframe is because of my interests in fantasy, robots, guns and space age technology stuff, which Warframe absolutely fits all of these. And it lives up to what I expected; large explosions, cool abilities and just lots of dakka. The main gameplay is very fast paced with a huge roster of characters and weapons that spoils players with choices when it comes to playstyle.
But now to the serious things. Is it grindy? Of course it is. But here are my thoughts - the grind isn't that much of an issue. In games like this, I find grind quite essential as there is something to work for and it gives a sense of accomplishment when you emerge from the grind, with shiny primes and♥♥♥♥♥♥ Ever since the new updates, things like resources have become much more easier to find and while the reworked void may have dissapointed some by taking away some fun elements, they certainly made rarer items easier to farm. Because of this, market prices for various items have dropped and this may be a good thing for new comers, being able to buy them easily.
And yes, there is this age old crafting system that creates your weapons in a measure of hours or even days and new players may find progression slow paced at the beginning but once you find something that will carry you on, things can start to progress quicker and the crafting time will seem more and more invisible as you triumph the starchart with your trusty frame and gun.
Yeah, i know. This review up to now seems like I am sucking [DE] off, but don't get me wrong, there are a lot of things that bug me as well. The main problem about Warframe it is extremely volatile, with the developers changing many aspects of the game here and there, some changes for the best, some changes for the good. One example of this is the complete rework of the void system, which♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥a lot of players off and for good reason. (I personally liked the rework) People were used to something they know and love but the developers just take that away just because they can.

Another thing to criticize is not about the Grinding, but shockingly for some of you, the lack thereoff. In many mmos I play in the past, I can get stuck for months and months just because of the grind but for Warframe, my playing have started to reach the end of its life cycle and with all the powerful late game gear I have, everything just seems so easy to do... I really hope the developers do add more challenging and rewarding missions, like more high level survival type missions, which was something they removed from the old void system.
***
All in all, would I reccomend this? If you love sci-fi third person shooters with grindy mmo elements, then absolutely yes! Its a fun game of blowing stuff up and definitely worth a try.
But if you are into a more RPG style game for an MMO, then No.
While I will put a Yes for this review, I can tell you straight off the bat that there are many games that does better.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare is great. The fighting mechanics are really interesting and unique. You have three ways to swing your weapon- LMB, up on the mouse wheel, and down on the mouse wheel. LMB is usually just a standard horizontal swing. Up on the mouse wheel is a stab or poke. And if you scroll down on the mouse wheel, you do an overhead attack. And you also use the right mouse button to block or parry. This makes a really realistic-feeling way of fighting. There's 4 classes, knight, vanguard, man-at-arms, and archer. Each one offering different weapons, armour, and speed. The reason I love this game so much is that you don't really get to experience the fighting as much in other games. It's so suspenseful and fun. There's a few different gamemodes, Team Objective, Team Deathmatch, Free For All, Last Team Standig, and Duel. There's about 14 different maps, all of them are a lot of fun, except Arena, everyone hates that one. The graphics are nice, and all of the maps and lighting look really pretty, until someone gets decapitated on the scene. Furthur on the combat, it's all about timing, when you swing or when you parry is really important. It's way more satisfying to kill someone with a sword and skill, than camping with a gun and shooting someone in CoD. The game's awesome, I've had some really amazing battles in this game that are so epic. That's what this game is, epic.

Warframe is basically a grinder 3rd person action shooter with some RPG elements where you, the operator, execute (grind) various type of missions throughout the solar system planets and more, wearing one of the "Warframe" special suits that provides protection, incredible acrobatic movements and special powers. On paper this sound like a thrilling concept and can be for some time, but the game has its own problems, some of which it always had and got worse with the time, that can end overshadowing such features.
+ Free to play, if you are good at trading you can get everything you need without spending any rl money.
- However new implemented resources or features are becoming harder and harder to obtain (grind or wait) without spending any rl money. That's somewhat fine, but it is getting gradually worse.
- If you don't have much time to play, you will have issues with the inventory and in gathering resources.
+ You can play solo, or with up to 4 players COOP, or up to 8 players for Raid type missions.
- One of the players pc "host" these missions which can result in severe lag and desync problems and frustration -- depending on who is hosting.
++ Very good game engine, good fps and good detailed graphics.
+ The devs are regularly improving their graphics, lightning and performance technology.
- However i'm not a fan of the overall style, Warframes often have an organic look, and the factions look weird.
+ Fun and fluid gun and run system, allows for a somewhat ninja / matrix'esque style.
+ Plenty of weapons and "warframes" to equip and use (each warframe comes with its own stats and set of powers).
- The vast majority of them will become useless past a certain mission level.
+ Some boss fights and missions can be fun.
- But will eventually become just another boss or grind session with little challenge.
+ You can create, build and decorate your own "dojo" (your clan's base). And use it as a player trading center, for pvp duels or general chilling.
- It takes loads of resources and waiting time to do so though.
- Devs just don't seem to know how to balance their game (mostly regarding pve). And power creep got worse over time.
- Eventually you'll run into bugs or glitches which can potentially ruin a 30-60+ minutes long mission. Every new major content update usually comes with a bunch of new bugs.
+ But usually major bugs are fixed fairly quickly, or they try to.
- The whole game is based on grinding and killing hordes of enemies. That's almost all you are gonna do unless you are into pvp.
- Time limited events and contents. Means if you take a break or don't feel like playing the game, you'll miss that content (special versions of weapons, skins, special mods or cosmetics).
- Updates are usually focused on cosmetic stuff, a couple of weapons to play with and some bug fixes.
- Updates often lacks any interesting idea or significant feature.
-- Most of Warframes and weapons will become useless due to balance and game design (horde style enemies).
It isn't a bad game per se, but I won't recommend it to someone due to the repetitivity and the direction this game has been heading and handled over the years.

-Summary at the bottom-
Buggy, unresponsive customer care and what not.
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare looks to be an appealing game from the start. With hilarious ragdoll physics and decapitations that sends you laughing off your seats. However, the game begins to fall apart once you spend some time alone in this game.
THE GAME: The game seems to be have problems with NVIDIA video card users. The framerate absurdly drops to 10fps even on a gaming computer which can run graphic demanding games such as Battlefield 4. I guess I don't have to explain why this is a problem...
UNRESPONSIVE CUSTOMER CARE: Maybe it's because Torn Banners Studios is a fairly new and small team. But even so, it doesn't give them the rights to not reply to a customer's questions. After months of sending in my queries, no replies were received. It seems like they have thrown my message into the junk folder as if it was nothing.
OFFLINE PLAY:
HORRENDOUS AI: Offline play is severely limited. The bots have only one difficulty level and is far too easy. The bots rarely feel threatened by their surroundings and only once or twice showed signs of an intelligent AI. You'll find yourself slashing  your way through the enemy lines in a matter of minutes of gameplay.
CONSOLE DEPENDENT: Everything in offline play depends on the console. From restarting the level to adding bots, it feels as if I have been plunged back to the days of CS1.0. While that is fine for most of us, the console does not even does what it's told to! Once, I tried to use killbot for a quick restart, instead of killing the bots, the game kicked every bot out of the match. Plus, the time between each round change is so unforgiving that if you forgot this is your last round on the map, you'll be plunged into a dreaded Team Objective match.
TEAM OBJECTIVE MATCHES: One of the best modes offered in the game as it requires teamwork, this mode in the offline portion is 2 steps backwards for the game. Offline TO matches are UNPLAYABLE thanks to the stupid AIs the game offers. The AI rarely helps out with the objective so you'll find yourself burning every farm, killing everyone and pushing every cart. In addition, when there are certain levels which requires 2 players to simultaneously complete an objective, there is no way to progress. What is the AI doing you might ask? Well... most of the time they are just standing around at the spawn kicking each other in the stomach, both ally and enemy AI.
ONLINE PLAY:
TOO DIFFICULT FOR BEGINNERS: This is where you'll find the most fun provided you have a friend to come along with you. Most of the time, the lobby is dominated by a few insanely experienced players. So you'll find yourself with high deaths and low kills. This is certainly because of the lackluster training mode and again, the stupid♥♥♥♥♥AIs of offline play.
LAG: The game server sucks. Period. Even on servers where I only have 5 ping, the game lags to hell. In addition to the experienced players, the game becomes unforgivingly difficult to the point of being unplayable.
STILL INSANELY FUN IN THE BEGINNING: Despite these, the game is still insanely fun in the first few hours. After that, only does the problem surfaces.
SUMMARY:
+ Fun in the first few hours
+ Fun with friends
- Stupid AI
- No way to hone your skills
- Online play too difficult for beginners
- Servers unable to handle even the slightest traffic
- Problems with NVIDIA card users.
This game is only recommended if you're really interested in this type of games or if you have a friend to go online with whenever you want. Otherwise if you're playing alone or whatnot, this game is not for you. Recommended to be purchased only during a sale.

I played this game a lot and i had fun, but i really can not recommend it. If you have a very good computer, you can set the game to look gorgeous. There is no real single player mode (last time i checked), you just play online alone, if you get what i mean. This game is best enjoyed with a few mods, so, is that a problem ? The mods exist, right, but the game you pay is the one that needs modifications, so i think it's kind of a drawback. I like when games are good enough as-is.
On the store page, about the early access, developpers claim the following : "We're a veteran team with some major hits behind our leads, and much of the core challenge is already met" which i suppose is wrong. Noone has heard about Wildcards, Instinct Games, Efecto Studios nor Virtual Basement. I am sure they have never developped a big budget video game (maybe DLCs or part of smaller games, that kind of stuff). I don't think they are actual veterans (like Brian Fargo, Chris Roberts or Sid Meier for Instance) and you just need to take a look at how the game is to understand that, i believe.
Collisions are awful, I get stuck in creatures all the time (mostly into the tail). There is no real AI. Animals just wander most of the time, and sometimes they have a special behavior, but it is limited to certain species and under certain conditions, and it quickly become easily predictable. It's not like a realistic behavior, it's more like a scheduled action, and it shows too much for me.
Some game mechanics (or whatever you might called that) doesn't make any sense. Some dinos are designed to be a pain. Of course, it's a survival game, so the player is suppose to struggle, but some things are not done right at all. Some dinos' special ability are really annoying, like being debuffed or even paralyzed for 10 seconds (i think it has been lowered) with no possibility to mitigate the effect with good armor or fortitude. 10 seconds is a really long time when you are being chomped down !
As I said, there is no real singleplayer, and everything takes a lot of time in this game. When you play multiplayer, the timers are going down even when you are offline, but if you play alone, you'll have to be playing and waiting in-game. I have to admit that you can change the time needed for eggs to hatch, for baby to grow, and for parents to mate, but keep in mind that there is no way to do it in game. There is no slider you can move to have this kind of settings changed, you will have to look for a specific .ini file and change or add a few lines into it.
As a conclusion, i could say "Fantastic idea, poor execution", but that sounds a little too bad in my opinion. The game is nice, but still, i could not recommend it. I'm not glad to give this game such a review, but i don't think i'm being unfair.

Before I go over why I like this game, one thing must be made clear: This is one hell of a grind fest. You grind to level up your gear, you grind to upgrade your gear, you grind to get points to upgrade your upgrades with, you grind for resources to build gear from blueprints (which you have to grind for), and then grind that gear also, and so on and so forth. Grindfest.
That said, the core gameplay loop is pretty fun. Drop into mission, kill things, complete objective, repeat. I grew up on things like Unreal Tournament while also being bad at PvP, so this game appeals to me like a vastly superior version of Gears of War horde mode. There is a large variety of weapons to kill things with (after you grind for them, of course), many of which are satisfying to use. The parkour system is enjoyable, despite sometimes being clunky. Also, everything in the game (aside from some cosmetics) can be aquired without spending real money, and there isn't any real reason to spend real money except for impatience (I'll admit, I've spent probably $100 over the past year, but compare that to something like a wow subscription and it's not that unreasonable).
At the time of writing, steam has tracked 334.4 hours of game time, it's surpassed Civilization 5 as my most played  game on steam, and is well on it's way to becoming my most played game ever. Unless the devs do something to break the game such as give me incurable space herpes, I'd be hard pressed not to reccomend this game.

The game about space ninjas without actual ninjas, they're more like gun-blazing killing machines that are extremly fun and addicting to play with. Beautiful art style, interactive devs and a crap tonn of grind.
With multiple ways to do a single mission be it with friends clan mates or by yourself, a game where you can literally play how you like it.
The setting and art desgin is beautiful and one of the primary reasons for me to start playing this game.
The grind is real and can often be frustrating to achive a single target/goal, but it's exremly rewarding and quite satisfying when you finally get it.
Even tho the game lacks a proper story and there is so much potential and it's just so rich with lore. But seeing as the game is still in Beta after +3yrs I'm confident we're not getting a proper story anytime soon.
A game where once you get the hang of it you can truly feel like an OP tank running over obstacles with thousands of ways to kill and wreak havock upon your enemies each of them different and unique from frame to frame.
There is no real "Endgame" to Warframe beside the one true Fashion-frame, thats mostly the reason why most people sink thousands of hours into this game and then feel salty about it because there is no real satisfaction of finishing a game.
The community is one of the more nicer ones I've experienced in online gaming, people are very helpful and the game encourages playing with more people cuz more loot more exp etc. And once you join a clan you can get to know so many people you can learn so much from and get support from time to time.
The trade chat is definatly one of the most intriguing part of this game as we can make plat (in game money) off of it or simply exchange parts for what we need with other players to avoid griding for what we want, it can also be used as a great way to make that ingame money to avoid a lot of grind.
Things often change and it upsets a lot of people *rip ash* but it's a game and honestly what are you gonna do about it, it's not built to make everyone happy it is what it is and some players have a hard time coping to the changes.
Overall it's a beautiful game and possibly one of the best F2P games out there, and the option to pay-2-skip is amazing for those who can't be arsed with the grind or having to deal with RNGesus.

Basic things like the inability to move objects once placed, they must be destroyed. The dinosaur level system is extremely unpredictable and results in wildly variable power levels of anything you come across.  For example, one Tyrannosaurus could be an easy kill while the one right next to it might just eat through you and all your companions. I wanted so very much to like this game, but I had to uninstall it so that I stopped being so disappointed.

This game is phenominal. I'd recomned it a hundred times over so long as your PC is beefy and your connection to the web is good, otherwise avoid it like a plague. It is awsome I get to tame dino's. It is not awesome I have to spend 2 days tamming a dino. Or that I have to spend 2 days imprinting a baby every 3 hours even in the middle of the damn night. I have no idea what the devs of this game were thinking when they decided on some of the mechanix in this game. No one outside of a child on summer vactaion has time for the ungodly grind that was made so familiar with games like World of Warcraft.
The game is not very fluid in the sense that it is not designed for solo play at all. I don't know if the idea was to be a WoW like MMORPG, but the current settings make it impossible to kill a boss without hundreds of hours game play. I don't know about you but that is allot of grinding doing the same stuff and non of it is downing a boss.
Thus the intial experience is captivating, untill you hit 100 and the grind intensifies. Countles hours spent combing the map for the highest level dino to spend 12 hours taming it. And then 48 hours raing its first child that may or may not be any good. The idea for a grind game like this only works when your getting paid a monthly subscription. To expect someont to spend hundreds of hours to make one decent dino, is a little too much.
Even on unofficial server with insane bounus to taming and breeding you will spend a couple hundred hours breeding. Imagine doing this in a official server... It would take a lifetime to achieve that goal. SO this game is NOT for anyone with an Instant gratififcation complex. NO micro transactions (yet) to boost the gind or even make it a tiny bit more balanced.
Lastly the devs of this particular game are morons, to put it mildly. Blizzard is a prime example of how you should impliment PATCHES. Once a week on a scheduled day, a day like Tuesday for instance, when the server population is low. NOT ON A FRIDAY AT 2PM CENTRAL TIME WHEN EVERYONE IS COMING HOME AND WANTING TO PLAY YOUR GAME. Think about the people playing the game for one minute and not what is convienient for you. That is not the way you do business. People expect a useable product not one that has random updates at the worst possible times. I understand its still in development, but get on a damn schedule for the sake of all people who play your game.
This game is still worth your time when you get it on sale., Be warned though that even in the pve culture there are several ways that people can and will give you grief, the most common is pillaring around your base to stop you from building in certian areas. I am going to be honest, despite nearly putting 100 hours into this game, I STILL struggle to like it. I could go into a HUGE rant about this game but I'm going to just lay down some brief points.
Pros:
- Can be a fun experience with friends if you work together building your strongholds owned by your tribe
- Environments look well presented
- Can become competitive and engaging if you're planning to play for tribal wars and dominating territory
- And you can tame and ride a progressively wide range of dinos, depending on your taste
Cons: (more than Pros):
- PRICE. This game I can tell is mostly cobbled together using storebought assets without being created from the ground up by the devs which would otherwise warrant the cost, but at the time of writing this brief review, a price tag of £50? Are you kidding me? Luckily I got this game for cheap, but I also foolishly bought the Scorched Earth Expansion Pack while it was STILL in EARLY ACCESS, and if you are games developer reading this, you NEVER EVER EVER PUBLISH DLC AND EXPANSIONS AND CHARGE FOR THEM WHILE YOUR PRODUCT IS IN EARLY ACCESS. In case you f*** up and don't make the game in the end people are gonna want their money back!
- Performance. This for me is particularly bothering. While some argue it's not entirely possible to optimise this title for what it is, bearing in mind it is CPU intensive because of how much is going on in the world, being in Early Access for roughly 2 years now I would have expected a little more work put into making the game utilise resources more efficiently and effectively and perform better. I have an i7 6850K, 16 gigs (soon to be 32) of 2400mhz DDR4 RAM and admittedly only an Asus 6GB 1060, I still have to run it at a mix of medium, low and only a couple settings on high to make the game at least RELATIVELY smooth and playable. But 2 years of early access again, I would have expected slightly better optimisation. Let alone BEFORE RELEASING IT INTO EARLY ACCESS.
- NPC balancing. I remember my very first death, being mauled to death by a level 90+ giant dragonfly within seconds of joinging the FIRST EVER SERVER I played on. At this point it's not entirely off, but if you find a T-Rex for instance and find it's below Level 60 and possibly lower you'll find yourself disappointed and have to look around for something better, while risking the frequent if not occasional bull**** deaths, having items robbed off you by small land dinos and even airborne NPCs.
- NPC behavoir. More of a minor point at this stage, but even T-Rexes will still attack Dodos instead of dinos their own size as a priority. Let alone some dinos that rob items off you keep coming back to steal more of your stuff and if you try killing the airborne varieties (I keep forgetting what they're exactly called, comparable to Pelicans), they will just keep stealing your stuff and eating your consumables till your inventory is bare and they'll kill you. No point in fighting off vermin, right?
- Development practises. Remember I mentioned publishing and charging for the Expansion Pack when in Early Access? And cobbling the game together mostly from storebought assets and from the Unreal Engine demo? Well because of the screw ups I've heard of, I ALSO heard they've pushed the final release date towards the end of this month (August at the time of writing this). Lets hope more work is put into balancing, optimisation and adding more to the game without charging more than the already shocking £50 price tag.
Overall, yes I KIND of like the game, I play the game for friends and I still have a good time making some very damn funny memories, but if you're thinking of buying into this game, I'm against it because you'll either find it's massively expensive for what it is, poorly made from the start albeit showing signs of improvement, you'll find yourself raging time to time because of BS deaths and more, performance may not be acceptable at all depending on the hardware you have, and not to mention...
... it's ANOTHER survival game with LOTS and LOTS of grinding. You want to pay upwards of £65 into a very grindy, stuttery game? Be my guest.

The game about space ninjas without actual ninjas, they're more like gun-blazing killing machines that are extremly fun and addicting to play with. Beautiful art style, interactive devs and a crap tonn of grind.
With multiple ways to do a single mission be it with friends clan mates or by yourself, a game where you can literally play how you like it.
The setting and art desgin is beautiful and one of the primary reasons for me to start playing this game.
The grind is real and can often be frustrating to achive a single target/goal, but it's exremly rewarding and quite satisfying when you finally get it.
Even tho the game lacks a proper story and there is so much potential and it's just so rich with lore. But seeing as the game is still in Beta after +3yrs I'm confident we're not getting a proper story anytime soon.
A game where once you get the hang of it you can truly feel like an OP tank running over obstacles with thousands of ways to kill and wreak havock upon your enemies each of them different and unique from frame to frame.
There is no real "Endgame" to Warframe beside the one true Fashion-frame, thats mostly the reason why most people sink thousands of hours into this game and then feel salty about it because there is no real satisfaction of finishing a game.

The trade chat is definatly one of the most intriguing part of this game as we can make plat (in game money) off of it or simply exchange parts for what we need with other players to avoid griding for what we want, it can also be used as a great way to make that ingame money to avoid a lot of grind.
Things often change and it upsets a lot of people *rip ash* but it's a game and honestly what are you gonna do about it, it's not built to make everyone happy it is what it is and some players have a hard time coping to the changes.
Overall it's a beautiful game and possibly one of the best F2P games out there, and the option to pay-2-skip is amazing for those who can't be arsed with the grind or having to deal with RNGesus.

My review will be negative until this game is made less grindy, cause this is just unbareable, i need to live outside this game aswell.
Pros:
+ The impressive environments.
+ The general feel of the world of "Warframe". It's all very immersive.
+ Mobility
+ The Randomization of each map. (Each map is build within a specific tileset (Snow, Nature, Ice, Infested, and so on), and whilst they do reach a point where you can recognize each part, they are put together in different ways each time. So you don't entirely feel like you're playing the same map over and over again.)
+ The variety in frames. (There is alot of different frames available in the game at this point, and they do offer a decent change of gameplay. The most fun ones i've played so far have been Escalibur, Hybrid, and Valkyr. Nidus, Inaros and Mesa looks fun aswell, )
+ Pets (I mostly like them as shipmates, just rolling around like dummies, but they can also be useful in battle. But until you grind the proper mods for them, they're mostly just an annoyance as they keep dying, and get weaker everytime they do, and also requires alot more maintenance. To avoid that you could also get a sentinel, which is basically the goldfish equivelant of a dog/cat in this game. They will fly next to your face, often getting in the way of eyesight, but way easier to bring with on a tough mission.)
+ The player market. (The player market allows players to sell certain (hard to obtain) items for the games real money currency (platinum). This not only allows players to get faster acces to certain items (if they buy platinum), but it also allows players to get ingame items without using real money. Aslong as you grind for long enough, you can pretty much get everything in the game. But that is also because you are forced to grind a f**k ton to get that platinum.
+ Decent variation in game modes.
+ The Void. (I freaking love this place, it's so awesome. Full of traps, complicated puzzles, portals, and skill tests that will have you do you're best to speed run through an area before the doors to the treasure room closes. This place is my most favorite thing about the entire game, and in my opinion offers the most gameplay value of any place in the entire game.
+ The Story: (Is really good, and very immersive. Even though some arent incredibly original, they are merged so perfectly well with the general feel of the game, i really enjoyed experiencing the world of "Warframe" through them.)
+ The Mods: (The mods allow for alot of customization, but like most MMO's they also end up with very few viable builds, which defeats the point of having that much freedom with customization, since you might aswell you have a Poison class, and a fire class instead, and make the game something you could actually balance. But if they somehow actually balanced this cluster♥♥♥♥ of god knows how many mods, then they could be a cool way to create a playstyle unique to you.)
+ The Design of everything. (Really cool and different world that they have created.)
+ The Bursa, Juggernaut and Stalker. (These bosses gives a decent challenge, and appears somewhat randomly. They are great for mixing up things, when the general grind gets too boring.)
+ Spy missions. (I like the stealth gameplay in these, and all the traps and puzzles.)
Cons:
- It's simply not fun. (Now this might be subjective, but hear me out. Think of the game, all the time you've spent in it, all the maps you have played over and over again. If you then removed ALL the progression from that, you have every single gun, every single frame, everything is available, and you can just go out and cause mayhem. Would you then play this game for 1/6th of the time that you have already? I am 100% sure that atleast 95% of you will say, no.
Try to be aware of how often this game makes you laugh or smile, and then tell me i'm wrong. This game is work, and you know it.
- The Grind: This usually comes with the territory of free to play MMO's, but none i've ever played has ever felt as grindy as this one. I've been playing for 200+ hours at this point, and i'm just rank 9. I keep telling myself that if i just play a little longer, i will get that weapon, or that frame that will finally make the game fun, but it's just so incredibly repetetive and boring. I find myself just pushing through, because if i get the last resources i need, my next gun/frame will be ready when i wake up the next day. But i still end up getting that one weapon that's suppose to be the game changer "Get the Sonicor, it's hillarious", and it was... for the first hour. It might just have been my favorite gun out of every single one i tried, but i was still left needing something more.
- The Combat: For an MMO, it's decent. But just like every other MMO, it basically just scales by increasing health, armor and dmg of your enemies, and that's where the scaling ends. The syndicates basically just send regular mobs after you, except some of their stats are higher. It's not like "The Stalker", which might be one of my favorite parts of the game. That guy is basically an escalibur on steroids hunting you down everywhere you go, truly an awesome enemy. But rarely will you see a boss of the same caliber, if not that one, ever. Boss battles exist only in the few places where you seek em out to grind for a new frame. Other than that, you will never see them. I personally think they should appear randomly throughout various modes, or atleast the syndicates should have each a boss similar to "The Stalker", that they would send after you. In general this games combat really needs something to mix things up, and an aura or higher stats does not count.
At this moment, Nidus seems like a great frame to play, because his skills are very useful and destructive. His most enjoyable skill is like a ball with octopus arms just grabing everything around it, and throwing it all over the place. It looks really funny, and makes you feel powerful as a frame. I don't get that feeling with most of the frames in this game, rather most of them just feel very harmless, by not really being able to do anything crazy on the battlefield. Hydroid has something similar with his octopus arms appearing all over, but most warframes will not do anything that will make you say "Oh cool!". Mostly they will just have some spell that boosts a stat, or does alot of damage real quick and that's it. More frames like Nidus would make the combat way more enjoyable. When you make the combat pure meat grinder gameplay, atleast make it a crazy f**king meat grinder.
- I'm normally very anti completionist, but this game really brought it out of me, and i kinda hate it for that. Most of these types of games are played until you have unlocked everything, and then never played again. (or atleast not until they release something new, as to take away your 100% complete rating.) I would like to play games for the simple reason that i want to, not because i have to, so that i can unlock everything in the game. I mostly started doing it, because that's what's required to rise in rank, and unlock the best weapons in the game. So therefore i felt more or less forced to do it, so that i could finally start to just enjoy the game, without being locked out of the end game content (which for MMO's is almost always the best content.)
- The game has also been incredibly buggy. Not only because of the Peer to peer system that they got going on, which causes constant host migrations that crash the game. But also because enemies will get stuck outside of the map, automatically making you lose the mission. But you most likely wont realize that until you need to kill that one last enemy, and therefore you're time is almost wasted no matter how aware you try to be.
- Archwing/Space missions. (These are simply horrendous, not enjoyable at all. I don't know why they added these, i hate playing them so much.

Concerned with the direction of the game.
I have played massive amounts of Warframe, I love the game. I love the gameplay. DE has, for a long time, been very good with their monetization model.
Lately, however, with the addition of rivens, and the handling of focus, I am losing confidence in them. Acquiring focus is boring. The benefits of gaining focus is lackluster. Rivens are a literal monetization of game balance. They updated focus by reducing the cost of upgrading nodes, but it's still nowhere near enough. They have done nothing to address how boring it is to grind for focus. I want to have fun while playing a game, not doing a task so mindlessly repetitive it feels like working in an assembly line. They based the entire system around you always paying for an affinity booster, which I have done, and I am quickly realizing they're trying to inch up microtransactions in subtle, indirect ways as much as they possibly can.
Rivens are a good example of indirect monetization. They don't sell them directly to you, they sell you the currency you use to buy rivens from other players. They're still making the money, there's just one extra step involved.
They're inching further and further into a territory that is focused entirely on making money off the players, even if it starts to degrade their experience and enjoyment of the game. I hate to imagine what this game will look like in one or two more years.
Plains of Eidolon was also so buggy the first couple weeks it launched it was clear they did not adequately QA test the missions. Some missions were breaking literally over half the time, like the armored vault for example. Not to mention, they effectively FORCE you to do "gathering" professions like fishing to progress in the game as well. I don't want to go fishing. I don't like fishing in video games. They're just bludgeoning the players of this game over the head with boring, required tasks.
Focus is such a mess I don't even have any desire to progress in that system, leaving me with no desire to continue playing this game, and the rewards for doing teralysts/cetus are similarly so unmotivating I have no desire to do that content either.

Warframe is by far one of the best games I've ever played, and I would freely recommend it to anyone while telling them to keep these considerations in mind:
1. This game is not by any means a Pay to Win title, while the option exists, no money whatsoever needs to be put into Warframe. Any items aside from cosmetics can be farmed and built in game. Even then, the games hard currency can be obtained without buying it.
2. Don't expect to master the game quickly, there's a lot of details to every aspect of the game to learn. From leveling to mod builds, farming locations, and even the intricacies of the trade system, there is a tremendous learning curve.
3. Warframe is very grind heavy. You will find youself running the same mission to obtain things for days at a time every once in awhile, the RNG system is very much luck-based.
4. The community, while not perfect, is still one of the best you will find, there is a low amount of toxic players and it's very noob friendly.
5. If you're looking for PvP, look elsewhere. The main focus of Warframe, and indeed it's true strengths, is in it's PvE content, as such, the PvP (called the Conclave) is very much underdeveloped and unbalenced.
In short, while Warframe is by no means a perfect game, and certainly not for everyone, it is worth trying at least.

I bought it in EA and as of now I think you would be wise to not spend your money on this. It is riddled with bugs, the performance is a joke (like really, really bad) and it simply did not deliver what it promised.
Survival: the usual chores, eat drink and so on. Hunger and thirst are just filler stats that have you push a button once in a while.
Taming: The game gates you into a taming-chain by only making dinos tameable in a realistic time (can still be up to 12 hours, imagine sitting by your dino 12 hours and feeding it narcotics) with the food made from eggs of a dino previous in the chain. To advance you need to tame, but it's boring and just takes ages.
Combat: The worst part of the game. It's all about dinos. As a human you basically have no chance to prevail. It's simple combat about beating or biting and beating one another until one is dead. The outcome is mostly decided by the stats your dino has, there's just spamming attack 1 until someone dies. This also applies to the world-boss fights that simply need you spending resources for ammo and taming armies of dinos, it's not really about skill and tactics used are basic.
AI: Still horrible. They promised to give dinos pack dynamics, create an ecosystem, but as of now it's just a giant island stuffed with stupid as hell dinos that spawn at random locations in their biome. Not only is the population way to dense, they also have introduced so many dinos that they don't know where to with them. As previously said, they are dumb as hell and behave like AI puppets with some basic functions, it's just immersion-breaking.
Building: Actually quite well done, it can be hard to gather the mats on your own, but there's something for everyone. You can event build a house-boat and go out to live in the seas. In PvP however, be prepared to get wiped if you're not playing 16 hours a day.
Progression: Not much to say here, you level up by doing stuff and unlock new engrams for weapons or building. The last tier of items, the so-called tek-tier items are all a big letdown. They need lots of a certain resource you just get from wold bosses, but do not really provide anything useful apart from a replicator structure. You can't even use your high-tek stuff in the bossfights.
Summing it all up, ARK: Survival Evolved did not evolve at all. The barebones game mechanics all are still the same while they just stupidly added content drop after content drop. It fell under that category of game with incredibly much potential but failed to deliver in terms of depth. You will have fun at first, but as you get into it more and more it will just prove unimmersive and with too many chores to keep going.

Picked this up for 5 euro on the Steam sale - Wouldn't advise getting it for much more than that.
The combat is fun and hitting people over the head with a sword is cathartic - It's especially satisfying if you do it right and it all comes out in your favour. There are a lot of FPS games which claim to include close combat, but none feel as visceral or as strong as the central combat of Chivalry. The game has simple Battlefield-esque rules in multiplayer (Or just plain free-for-all) which seems fair enough. The plot also stands up in the sense that it doesn't over-complicate.
The thing is, it looks like a game that was intended to be single player but at some point someone realise that the AI was too bad to roll out with a single player campaign, and it became entirely multiplayer dependant. Which seems great now, but for all I know a few weeks down the line nobody else will be playing or the servers will fill up with people flaming. For now the multi-player stands up, but that doesn't change the fact that when I want to play single player, I end up with a wide open space with the two teams sitting on opposite ends, facing the wall and twitching. There are also more than a few corners in which one can get trapped by jumping at the wrong angle.
Then there's the fact that it's a 15 euro indie title which appears to have paid DLC for different helmets (Which at best you will only see from behind anyway). For a game that's already startlingly incomplete given its lack of decent AI and relatively small variety of maps to choose from. To me, this is Torn Banner getting a bit too big in their pantaloons.They need to make sure everything runs smoothly before they can think about releasing DLC.
So in short it's a really strong, fun game mechanic which doesn't seem to know quite what to do with itself, and it suffers from a sense of feeling a bit small, a bit unimmersive and not nearly as epic as the tralier intended.

After playing this game for one year and half and still counting i felt the need to review it:
In a nutshell: Warframe is a TPS featuring space ninjas jumping around killing and bringing balance to a chaotic universe.
Pros:
F2P not P2W:
You just need time to grind and anything (except third party skins) can be bought by trading in-game currency with other players instead of buying it.
Continuously updated:
Developers costantly release new content refreshing the mechanics, game modes, visual effects and stuff.
Yes they might not be the best on their job and they actually make mistakes from time to time but still they supply free content for all
Funny alone, even funnier with friends:
You can't possibily face real challenges without good team/clan/alliance/friends so you have to pick one, the friends are obviously the most important but if you dont have any you can always get some in-game.
Can be pretty much endless if done right:
I'm referring to the whole game longevity
Community is mostly open to chat/help/discuss in a civil way
Cons:
The grind can be horrendously hard:      ( ONLY FEW TIMES AND IT HAS BEEN REDUCED A LOT RECENTLY )
You aren't forced to grind but if you want to master the game few heavy grinds are unavoidable unless you spend in game currency.
The game can be repetitive:
Maps are generated by putting together previously generated rooms but the whole outcome isnt oppressignly the same, the high count of different rooms do a great job in hiding this problem.
Hard to understand and even harder to master:
The first time i played i was amazed and confused,
The first week passed and i installed few modifications and upgrades without knowing what i was doing,
The first month i understood what i was doing but still i missed few core concepts in the game,
The first 3 months i was able to get most of the items i wanted and started to grind more,
After 6 months i farmed a lot and still couldn't find a few of the endless amount of parts i needed,
After a year i had everything or almost and the game started to evolve,
After a year and half i still have many things to do and the farm has been greatly reduced.
I would rate the game a solid 70/100.

So, with over 2,000 hours, I would have to say that ARK is my favorite game of all time.  That being said, please read this review with the following in mind:
1) I am not a huge gamer.  I'm a casual player.
2) I'm 40+ years old, and my hands are bad due to carpal tunnel, so I don't have the best reaction time.
3) I don't generally play on official servers, because I do not have that kind of patience.  (I mean, I have played on them a little, but generally, I steer clear.)
4) I mostly play PVE or PVPVE.
So most people will say "you're not a real gamer".  But I think there are people out there like me who just kind of want to have casual fun.  So, that being said:  I love this game.  Sure, it has problems.  But, the problems are well worth the experience.  I've played on more than a dozen great servers, and...some not-so-great servers.
So, Pros and Cons:
1) Steep learning curve.  You're going to die like 3984579843 times when you start.  A raptor is going to kill you.  A megapirana is going to kill you.  You're going to freeze.  You're going to die of thirst.  Something is going to destroy your house.  Something is going to destroy your bed.  You're going to fall off of your pteradon into  the water and drown.  You're going to lose all your stuff and have to start over again, and again, and again.  As a person who mostly played MMORPGs before this, that really upset me at first.  Now, I take it much more in stride, because anything I lose, I know how to make again.  And once you kind of know what you're doing, you know how to avoid a lot of this stuff pretty easily.
2) Game instability/lag.  I don't know about official servers but on the unofficial ones, you will hit lag spikes.  Bad ones.  And on the really over-filled servers (especially ones on non-official maps that aren't optimized well) you're going to experience crashes.  The only thing I can tell you there is to shop around for a server that has a good balance of mods, not too high of a harvest rate, and a dino limit per person or tribe.
3) Character customization.  You basically look like everyone else, or you make your character look like an incredible abomination.  There's only like ten sets of armor in the game, though you can paint it, so I guess that's cool.
OK!  ON to the reasons I love this game.
1) DINOS!!!  Okay I don't know about you, but this brings back some wonderful aspect of my childhood.  There are so many dinos to discover, and each one has its own special abilities and uses.  Instead of you getting powers, you tame the dinos so that you can use their powers.  One dino might help you harvest wood at a higher rate.  And some dinos are for battling.  Some for traveling.  Some even for things like helping to level other dinos or assisting you in farming.  Taming dinos is hard, but you feel a real sense of accomplishment when you manage to get a good one tamed.
2) Building stuff!  Okay, I like building.  I like creating my own little village, or a castle, or just a really cool house on a cliff.  With building mods like S+ or Keeps and Castles, you can do some truly amazing stuff.
3) Crafting system.  So, basically you harvest stuff in the world, grow in your greenhouse, or have your dinos create materials.  And then you use them to make the stuff you need.  This does lead to some grinding at times, but like mentioned before, grinding is cut down once you have the appropriate dino to help you gather what you need.  Then you make everything from walls to generators.
4) Exploring.  I like exploring.  And with ARK releasing new maps regularly, there are always new places to explore.  Sometimes I will just fly around just to look at stuff and watch dinos fight each other.  There's battles going on in the world all the time, independent of you being there, with carnivores attacking herbivores, and herbivores fleeing...  Always something going on.
5) Excitement because you never know what is going to happen.  It's always something new.  And you always have to be on your toes.  The other day, a t-rex started eating my house when I was low level on a new server, and I had to find a way to lure him away without dying.  But it was just that sudden moment of turning around in my house and seeing a t-rex head sticking through the wall that made me jump.
6) "ARK Science".  Now here is what I really like, so called "ARK Science".  That's experimenting with the elements at hand to see how you can conquer your environment.  Such as figuring out how to make traps and taming pens to tame things safely.  Or how best to optimize your pipe system to irrigate all of your crops.   It's not even stuff that they've put in the game to be sciencey most of the time.  It's more an a-ha moment of "Oh man, if I do this, and then this...then this will happen!"  There's no tutorial when you start this game.  You learn as you go, and learning ARK is a blast.
7) PVP?  I don't know.  I don't PVP but I've watched some PVP videos and they are super interesting.  Your tribe has to work like a well-oiled machine in PVP.
8) Breeding.  Breeding is also a thing I haven't really gotten into.  But some people are super into it, and into breeding for cool color mutations and stuff.  I wish you could get real mutations like...I don't know, a direwolf with three tails or something, but that would be difficult, I guess, to make.
So more than reviewing, I thought I'd also include a short guide about how to get started in ARK if you want to play on unofficial/modded servers, how to choose a server, etc.
1) Rates.  Some servers jack up their rates to an insane level.  Like 1000x.  And while that sounds cool, those servers are usually super laggy.  Look for a server with something more reasonable.  I like 5x, usually -- which means 5 times as much harvesting, taming, and XP as official servers.  It makes ARK very playable as a solo level without going too overboard.
2) Number of mods.  The more mods you have on a server, the longer it is going to take to log in.  Right now I am playing on a server with 44 mods.  And while that means there's a lot of cool stuff on the server, it also means it takes like 20 minutes to log in.  I think the optimal number of mods is around 10.
3) Dino limit.  PVE servers can get laggy because people tame 3049385309458 dinos.  A per-person or per-tribe dino limit is good.  This forces people to get rid of their older, more lower level dinos when they get better ones, instead of having them stand around, taking up room and making things lag.
4) "Conversion" mods.  I don't know what else to call them, but these are the big package mods like Annunaki, Pugnacia, Ark Eternal, etc.  They're fun, because they add a new level of complexity to the game, often with newish dinos or powers, etc.  But they will also make the server more dangerous often, so if you are new, it might be a harder start.
5) Maps! TheIsland is the original map, pretty small but probably the most optimized/developed.  TheCenter has some cool ruins features that are great to build in, and a floating island at, you guessed it, the center of the map.  Ragnarok is the newest official map, and may not be completely finished?  Scorched Earth is....all desert, basically.  It requires different skills, building materials, etc.  And it has a different set of dinos, but many of them are very unique. For unofficial maps I've played Thieves (lots of floating islands), very large map.  And I've also played Crystal Isles.  I love Crystal Isles, it's beautiful and vibrant and very wow, but is still very much under production and needs more optimization.  It probably has the best newbie starting area though.
So it looks like I am running out of room.  If you got this far, congrats, and I hope this helped or at least convinced someone to start a great journey in ARK.  It's very worth it.

I have put nearly 1500 hours into this game so I believe that I can give a rather fair impartial review for any would be buyers of this game. Is ARK: Survival Evolved fun? Yes, yes it is fun, is it worth sixty dollars? No, no it is most certainly not.
I got onto the hype train that is ARK WAY back in the day, back when it was a flat thirty dollars for an early access game. I wasn't here since day one, but I was around since the first major tamed dinosaur nerf, where dinos had so many stats that it was basically impossible to die while riding one, back when carcasses of dinos you killed were likely to fly a good hundred feet into the air and freeze, making you waste time. Back when you expected♥♥♥♥♥♥to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥, As an early access game, they were levied some time for all the bugs they had, you bought into the experience knowing how bad it was and it was still fun. Time consuming as all hell, but fun. Everything takes ages and still does, but when you finally tame that one dino, when you get that one drop, you find that perfect tribe to play with and everything cleans, the game truly feels amazing, it feels like the sandbox it was made to be and feels actually fun.
However, while that is fun, there are just so many problems this game has to this day that I can't forgive it anymore. Let's start with problem number one, the paid DLC in an early access game. Now, I'm a massive fan of DLC, but only when it is done right. Had they released this down the line, a good year or so after its initial release, I would have been ok with it. But releasing well in the middle of its early access lifetime when they still had a pleothora of mechanics and dinos to release, it was just a slap in the community's face, especially into a community that paid expecting their money to go into fixing the base game. To this day, I still refuse to buy it out of disgust for such a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ practice.
Bugs and technical issues that would make Ubisoft seem like a patron saint. Once again, while in early access, fair enough, I can give you some slack. But now, they are releasing it for sixty dollars and expecting us to just be ok with the♥♥♥♥♥♥tons of issues, some tiny, some massive? Really? On the bug side, you can just randomly fall into the world at some places in the map, it has gotten better then in its early days, but not fully polished up enough to be ok for a full sixty dollar release. Technical issues too, dinos legs splaying in weird directions when they are on uneven surfaces, sinking into the ground a bit when on ceilings, which you have to use for flooring because there isn't a better alternative when there is even a slight dip in elevation, dinos spazzing out as their bodies jitter after murdering them. Seeing them ragdoll is one thing, but seeing them melt into polygons as their forms shoot in random directions, once again, not something I want to see or expect in a sixty dollar game.
The official servers are an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥how. I HIGHLY suggest that you don't even look at them at all, period, just don't. One of a few things will happen, you will be utterly subjugated by the alpha to the point where you don't get to play, spawns blocked, not allowed to have dinos over a certain level and just annoyances. If do happen upon a server that either doesn't have an alpha or the alpha isn't♥♥♥♥♥♥ you still have to deal with the bugs. There was a major update that brought in a new item called the industrial cooker. As a solo player, I had happened upon a server that luckily didn't have a♥♥♥♥♥♥alpha on top of everyone liking me so I was able to just play, but once again, solo player, it is difficult to get things as said kind of player but with a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of work, I finally managed to make such an item. Problem was, something was wrong with the patch, it got rewound, and my work, just up in smoke, no one to fix it. Other problems include servers with a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of people also having to deal with lag, so things will take exponetially longer on them. Tames that should only take an hour taking two, rubberbanding, and a host of other problems, the server I played on got so bad, that raptors couldn't hit you, they rubberbanding themselves too hard with their own speed. It has gotten better over the years, but it is still annoying, your best bet is playing on a private server where an admin can auto fix those problems OR playing single player where you can admin fix those problems.
There is also a cheating problem on official servers were players have aimbots, radars, and have found ways to glitch under the map and break your stuff from below. Days to Months work of progress can just be wiped away at the drop of a hat simply because someone cheated, and if you are on an official server, you are up♥♥♥♥♥♥s creek without a paddle.
All and all, when it was 30 dollars and didn't have ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t DLC tied to it, I could recommend this game to anyone with a lot of time on their hands that enjoyed power fantasy of riding dinosaurs, but right now, the game is far too unpolished and far too buggy for its sixty dollar asking price, hell, they just released a new map and it isn't even finished yet, like come on.
Pros: Power Fantasy and childhood wish fulfillment, you wanted to ride a T Rex, you can ride a T Rex.
Playing with friends and finding a good community to play around it enjoyable.
The sense of fufillment when you start taming lots of dinos and you build a base is amazing.
A lot of options to play how you want and a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of options for what kind of dinos you want to use.
Private servers heavily allievate a lot of the problems the official servers have.
Gray area between players: EVERYTHING takes a long time, unless you are playing on a private server with the rates expontially higher, the wait for everything is insane. Chivalry is the best game to do the whole medieval multiplayer combat thing. It's immensely satisfying and extremely fun to play. Though it can be frustrating at times, it will provide you with hours upon hours of fun which makes it well worth the price of admission.
It's a good-looking game. Based on the Unreal 3 engine, it runs well and looks good. It stays reasonably grounded in its portrayal of medieval weapon, armor and terrain and looks good doing it. It's graphically competent and it won't get in the way of the gameplay, but it won't be something you remember.
Gameplay is probably the most important thing to look at, and it's done well. There's a wide range of weapons and 4 classes to chose from. Combat is fun and realistic. Slicing someone up with a broadsword is extremely satisfying and the game just feels very "medieval". It's hard to put into words, but it is good, believe me.
Like with many online games, it can get very frustrating when lag comes into play. Balance is ok for the most part, but sometimes unrealistic, for example: How can that puny archer parry my giant warhammer with his tiny dagger? Frustration can also come in the form of scumbag players who do mean things like teamkill, but that's really the community's fault.
You can get a lot of playtime out of the game. I found it to be significantly more fun with friends, and being able to air out your frustration with lag to someone can help relieve the stress and make the game more enjoyable, so be sure to buy it together if you have someone to play with. I recommend this game if you've got even the slightest interest in medieval combat.
P.S. I am a person that can get easily frustrated when games "misbehave", so do take my notes about frustration with a grain of salt. If you're the kind of person that doesn't get upset at videogame logic, scumbag players and lag in games, it won't upset you in this one either.

Don't let it consume your life, as it has mine.
Nearly 3000 hours of doing nothing but grinding resources.  That is all that I feel I’ve accomplished.  If I could go back in time and tell myself not to pick up Ark, I would in a heartbeat.  With very few exceptions, most particularly the good friends I've made in Ark over the last 3 years, I regret ever launching the game.
Real-time survival games are a novel idea, but Ark is a black hole that can take over your life and never let you go.  The massive amount of content and logical systems working in the background is staggering, but seldom are you allowed to enjoy any of those for long if you play official servers.  After nearly 3 years of Early Access, the developer Wildcard did very little to alleviate the issues official PvP players had with being raided offline and issues official PvE players had with being greifed.
The only praise I can make for Ark is that it has extremely talented art and coding departments.  The atmosphere they’ve created is stunning and passionate, with breathtakingly detailed landscapes and lifelike creatures that roam them.  That and the semi-intuitive building system is enough to keep many players coming back to the game, but not enough to justify the massive amount of time you will invest into daily tasks that feel more like work than fun.
I was enticed back to Ark twice to check out new content and get back together with old friends, but every time resulted in regrets and the wish that I had never started to begin with.  Overall, my advice to anyone browsing this game is to pass it by, and never look back.  You will potentially save yourself years of frustration, stress, and disappointment.

I have more than 1100 hours in this game mostly unrecorded hours due to steam being offline most of the time (maybe 1800 hrs). See the negative issues addressed in the reviews are all 100% valid. But, they don't really become applicable until you either finish the story line (loosely speaking) or reach Mastery Rank 8. The former takes 3-4 weeks. The latter takes roughly 2-3 weeks. The roughest experiences I have had were when I started out and when I was finally crashing. The middle portion or about 80% of the time I spent on this game were well spent. Some people claim grinding is difficult and while it is there were other means that I sometimes used. I'll be honest (no hacks or cheats) i made somewhere around $600 worth of platinum without inputting any amount of my own money on this game. Just depends on how well you utilize the market chat. Also, compared to games I have played like CS:GO, League of Legends, Overwatch, etc the warframe community + devs made the game super welcoming.
Five things I loved:
1. Combat + Parkour (Best update + removing stamina)
2. Solar Rails (Disabled due to monopolization by Alliances I was part of one)
3. New content every week sometimes twice a week/Events (LOVE EVENTS)
4. Graphics for F2P game
5. Clans/Alliances (Research material and recognition)
Five things I hated:
1. Trade market (players have no idea what they are doing, scammers, toxicity)
2. Prime Frame drop locations and ABC rotation (had to play intervals of 40 minutes of T3 Survival for 1 piece which had 0.01% drop rate)
3. Viability of frames, I hate playing solely healer but trinity is loved for grinding yet no one wants to play it sadly oberon healing not very viable
4. Baro Ki Teer (items are overpriced to hell)
5. Resources drop rate (have like million of alloy plates after 10 hours of grinding but 3 neural sensors LOL)
I would recommend playing this game and enjoying the game staying away from trade market, prime frames, and the meta. Just ignore that stuff. Don't do what I did. I would grind my gear up to top tier and solo Tier 4 Survival for 60 minutes on several different frames. It burned me out and all the aspects of the game that were fun for me are somewhat gone (solar rails, recognition for being in a clan, addition of more chance in drops). If you take a break from the game its pretty hard to get back into it because of how quickly content gets added. However, if you listen to the things I say to ignore, then you will enjoy the game assuming you can get over the initial entrance hurdle for about 1-2 months.

This game is actually rather simple. There is no storyline and all you do is click to kill different monsters in order to collect money to level up and buy more heroes to get more money. Every once in a while, you start over though you get a ‘Hero Soul’ that can be used to summon an Ancient. These ancients will help you do various things and are sort of similar to idols that you can ‘worship’ to gain things like extra DPS points or gold when fighting monsters. Every 5th level there is a boss you have to fight in a certain time frame and if you can’t, you just can’t get to the next level for a bit.
The controls are actually really simple, just click. That’s it, you don’t have to remember arrow keys or what to type, you just use your mouse and a finger. You also only need one button on the mouse too. A little kid could do it or someone half asleep. I play it on the computer but I’m thinking that if you play on Android, you just use a finger and tap the screen. Then the game gets to a point where it can play itself, no thinking needed. If you want to start a new game, you just have to get up to a point where you can ascend and you can do it.
The artwork is actually really good with colorful monsters and actually rather creative. As for the heroes, you don’t really see much of them; they are just standing to the side and have different looks and feels to them. I wish that they would play more with the element thing as some characters themes are elemental based. For example, one character has all ice looking armor while another has fire based look to them. That will do nothing to the attack; the character only adds DPS to your attack.
The music is… um… well I have a confession to make. I don’t normally play the game with music as I have it running in the background mostly. It’s alright but not note worthy. It’s one song that loops over and over again and though it’s a bit epic, it gets old after a while. It also is a bit annoying when hearing the clicks and coin sounds going on. When something dies, it does a little sound depending on what it is and then as the gold is added to your stash, you get the sound of a coin dropping. Over and over again, it just is a bit annoying. Some enemy’s sounds don’t really seem like they match anyway, for example an oversized Ratty dieing makes a sound as though a sheep is going baa or something.
Other then the music and sound, it is not a bad mindless game to play with and you can easily just close it and come back to later since it will collect coins in real time depending on where you leave it. I like to leave the game on a level where it only takes a second to kill a creature on its own and then close it and come back to it the next day to buy and upgrade.
I would reccomend this game to anyone i know. The gameplay is something I have never seen from another game and I enjoy the creators vision to take hand to hand combat into the realm of fps

Warframe is by far one of the best games I've ever played, and I would freely recommend it to anyone while telling them to keep these considerations in mind:
1. This game is not by any means a Pay to Win title, while the option exists, no money whatsoever needs to be put into Warframe. Any items aside from cosmetics can be farmed and built in game. Even then, the games hard currency can be obtained without buying it.
2. Don't expect to master the game quickly, there's a lot of details to every aspect of the game to learn. From leveling to mod builds, farming locations, and even the intricacies of the trade system, there is a tremendous learning curve.
3. Warframe is very grind heavy. You will find youself running the same mission to obtain things for days at a time every once in awhile, the RNG system is very much luck-based.
4. The community, while not perfect, is still one of the best you will find, there is a low amount of toxic players and it's very noob friendly.
5. If you're looking for PvP, look elsewhere. The main focus of Warframe, and indeed it's true strengths, is in it's PvE content, as such, the PvP (called the Conclave) is very much underdeveloped and unbalenced.
In short, while Warframe is by no means a perfect game, and certainly not for everyone, it is worth trying at least.

Overall its not a bad game by any stretch, especially for a free to play title. Just dont expect to be able to dip in for short blasts of fun every now and then. If you're not in it for the long haul then expect to drop real cash to get the things you want.

I think I've played enough Warframe to understand how it works and whether or not it's worth the space it takes on your storage.
The short answer is that it is.
Warframe is currently regarded as one of the better Free-to-Play games on the market right now. It allows players to fight in many styles, and allows enough customization for them to both bend those classes to their own needs, and appear different from the thousands of players romping around.
The game looks nice in general, especially since it was released a few years ago. It's held up well thanks to constant development from the team, who releases content regularly (relative term).
Combat and movement is very fast-paced and fluid, with a variety of weapons and ways to attack your foes. The enemies themselves aren't very bright, but they can be strong, often come in large numbers, and have many attacks of their own. Missions take place on procedural tiles, which adds to the replayability factor of Warframe. Playing the same mission twice will not yield the same results. Space combat is a bit lackluster, but has been improved greatly since I started playing.
Additionally, there are more environments in Warframe than in other shooter games, such as Destiny. While some planets  use the same tile-sets as others, there is still more variation than Destiny.
Another large part of Warframe is trade, and while I have enjoyed my time buying and selling the parts I need, I highly recommend that new players seek out a veteran merchant who is willing to explain what parts are worth more, and how to find them. I've had instances where I can sell a fairly common, unfinished Prime set for 100 platinum (the game's paid currency), when that particular weapon is barely worth 20 as a full set. Platinum itself is extremely important to the game, as it is not only used for purchasing cosmetic items. Many things essential to the game such as Weapon Slots have to be bought using Platinum.
It should be noted that Platinum can be earned without purchasing it with real money (although that is an option). I have spent exactly 0 dollars on this game, but have accrued many things that must be bought with Plat.
Overall, if you're a fan of the modern Free-to-Play model, Warframe is an absolute must. It will likely keep you entertained for at least 100 hours. As of the time I'm writing this, I've played nearly 3 times that amount, and have no intention of stopping.

The storyline, vast number of weapons and warframes, the graphics,the combat system, even the ideea that it was based upon "ninjas in space" was very good. We all know it was about grinding and farming from the beggining..but most of us loved it anyway. The updates were mostly good in the first year and a half since it came out. However...slowly, things started to go bad. Every single time they released a good weapon and could clearly see that a lot of players were using it, they nerfed it right away.
Also the requirements for building weapons and frames are incomparably higher than they used to be...wich of course means more and more grinding. Now..if you want to build a certain weapon, you have to build two more ,each with a 12hrs duration.
It's obvious that the greed for more and more money turned this game into what is is today...where for a prime frame and two prime weapons you have to pay almost as much as for 2 AAA Titles just released. And of course, they make it harder and harder to obtain those items for free...just by grinding.
There a few changes they made to Warframe that made me give up on this game.
*Prime Vault - A new way to make money...mostly from the new players wich don't have the prime frames like Frost Prime, Ember prime, Mag prime and so on.
*The changes to the Void..are horrible.Another change that requires more and more grinding. I loved farming the void with my friends before..it was fun, now it's the complete opposite.
*The complete removal of fusion cores. I had 6k rare 5 fusion cores, and several other thousands of uncommon 5,common and only to wake up one morning to see everything changed to a simple number called Endo.
*The game simply gets boring when you have a high mastery rank and posses almost everything in game
*Riven Mods
*The market changes
An advice from a player that invested over 3k hours and a lot of money into this game , would be to try to play without investing any money into it. But..that's only my opinion !

Warframe is a free to play game that does almost everything right when it comes to the free to play model.
It is NOT a pay to win game, despite what anyone has ever told you. Every single warframe in the game can be unlocked without paying a cent.
You want Frost? Go kill Lech Kril a few times on Mars
You want Chroma? Complete a quest, progress through the planets/story
You want Nezha or Zephyr? Join a clan and make them
You want a Soma? Buy its blueprints with credits and gather the materials
I think you get the point..
This game is awesome you should give it a shot if you haven't already, but be warned, Warframe is not for everybody. If you cannot stand the grind, then you should just quit.

In my Opinion, Clicker Heroes is the best idle game out there and I have played alot of them. The game is very easy to understand, yet, there's deep strategy involved. You click to deal damage, you buy heroes (and upgrades) to deal damage over time and you buy (and level up) ancients to improve your damage, your gold gains or even reduce the amount of monsters you have to kill to progress.
There are tons of ways you can play the game, just by the way you build your ancients. You can focus on having your skills last for a long time, you can focus on dealing as much damage over time as possible without clicking or you can make it so your clicks are extremely strong. Of course, with a lot of time and effort, you can buy and level up any ancients, but the amount of time it takes to get there depends on how good your strategy is.
Also, they are always adding new content to the game and improving it, so if you ever get bored, come back 3-6 months later and you will have new heroes, ancients and/ or features that will have been implemented!
PROs:
-It's free.
-It's fun.
-It's easy to play.
-The game is being updated every few months.
-You can leave the game closed and you keep progressing.
-You can play this game while waiting for multiplayer games to start or when you have 5 minutes of free-time at work.
-The achievements are great and there are many to unlock (most of them are also Steam Achievements).
-The replayability of this game is endless...
-The monsters and backgrounds are really cool.
CONs:
-There's only 1 music in the game.
-It does get repetitive, but starting over or waiting for updates usually does the trick.
