I used to think Warframe was a MMORPG.  That's what it's advertised as.  Superficially it has all the trappings of a MMORPG.  But it doesn't play like one.
Let's pick an example of a well known MMORPG.  I'll use Guild Wars 2.  The quest line is very long and forks a lot.  You can get all the way to level cap doing quests, always doing something new, and then, if 2-3 months of solid playing wasn't enough for you, start a fresh character and play a very different game.
Warframe isn't like that at all.  The entire ranking system is based on getting every piece of gear (warframes and weapons) in the game and giving them XP to "rank" them up.  Plus taking a silly test at each tier.  That's it.  And some of that gear is extremely rare; either it can only be gotten from Baro Ki'Teer once in a blue moon (and that's no exaggeration), or you have to collect its component parts from extremely rare "alert" mission rewards.  The whole scheme is designed to keep you coming back to the game for 1-2
to finally reach Nirvana (a.k.a. MR23).
But it gets worse.
The runaway power scaling in the game is
.  Through alert, invasion, nightmare, fissure, and syndicate missions, all of which you need to do to get that all important gear, the game actively rewards high level players for playing lower level content.  The problem is, in certain mission types, a high level player can just sit in one place spamming an ability and instakill every enemy on the map.  Or, with their mods and arcanes, they can move so fast that a lower level player can't keep up with them.  For the whole mission.  This isn't fun to do, and it's certainly not fun for other players who pretty much don't get to do anything at all.  It's the worst power scaling I've ever seen in a MMO.
And then there's the itsy little problem that you can't really learn the game from either the tutorial or playing it.  Sure, there are tutorials on movement and a bunch of other things.  But does the game describe all the different types of mods?  All the myriad ways you acquire that gear you need to rank up?  How to use multiple syndicates to your advantage?  Even how to trade?  And especially the drop rotation system, which you
to know to get some gear?  There is a huge number of orthogonal mechanics in the game, all of which eventually feed into that mastery rank, but most of which you'll only learn about from reading a third party wiki.
Let's briefly explore another major problem, namely that it's a coop game and yet many of the mechanics used by different equipment conflict with each other.  For example, there are numerous melee weapons that have low base stats but become very good with stacking mods, because they have high crit and status chance.  This works great if you're soloing.  But as soon as you enter a mission with someone using Ember, or Zarr, or even a ridiculously modded Tigris, it can become nigh impossible to keep the stacks up.  So you have a coop game where other players can have a severe negative effect on your abilities.  That makes sense... not.
I have special hate for the so called Prime Vault, a system that has effectively become a Disney style artifical scarcity to coerce players to pay hard cash for gear.  Which, you may remember, you need to rank up.  Oh, sure, the vault might be open once every year or two, so you can spend a month farming relics and hope to get that special piece.  Good luck.  See you next year when it might be open again, if you're lucky.
Now there are plenty of grindy MMOs, that's part of the genre.  But as I mentioned earlier by example, in most MMOs the grind is just plain more interesting.  A big quest line.  Some kind of unique boss mechanics.  Something to break up the monotony.  In Warframe, there are a handful of maps ("tilesets"), and they play the same every time.  Sure, they rearrange the map slightly and different routes into vaults and prisons might be open, but it's 99.44% the same mission every time.  And you're going to run that mission hundreds, if not thousands, of times.  Also, most bosses just amount to "oh, this one has a weak spot
".
If all that wasn't enough to turn stomachs, they literally added a social disease in the latest content.  This is no joke; you touch another character and get a cyst, which you're stuck with semi-permanently.  (You can "drain" it after a week to make a certain pet, but you'll just get another one because the players do it intentionally.)  Whoever thought this was a good idea was unbelievably out of touch.
By the way, if you've ever thought that watching a game on stream will you give an idea what it's like, Warframe is a great example of how this fails.  Most of the popular streamers are late gamers; they already have the cool gear and mods, and are mostly just farming for items to sell or trade.  Furthermore, both their followers and DE shower them with gifts, including plat and new frames.  In many cases you won't even see the RPG mechanics, because they do all the "maintenance" off stream.  You can't get a representative view of the game this way; in a sense, they're not even playing the same game.
If you have the stomach for a highly monotonous game that only starts to be "fun" when you reach end game and can trounce all the plebs, go for it.  If you're obsessive enough that getting 348 pieces of gear from grindy, repetitive missions is something you would be driven to do, go for it.  Otherwise, do yourself a favor and play a different game.
To be fair, the visual effects are quite good.  It's not all bad.

I bought this game when it was in early access on day 1. Back then, it ran pretty badly, like, slideshow badly. But i was optimistic, they were a pretty small studio looking to make something of triple A grade in size and scope, i was on board to support that. They put out fairly frequent updates too, adding new content all the time which was great. And in the beginning, they seemed to be doing their best to try and make the game run better and get it into an actually playable state. If you watched any video's from when the game released on Early access initally, unless you had a super rig, this was a frame by frame game. Even with a monster PC it still ran abysmally. The optimization it needed was provided for a handful of months, after which got it to a playable state, but it still didn't run great.
Now, about 2 years later, we are still waiting on the optimization and en-mass bug fixes that the game so desperately needs. It always seems to be pushed off further and further in favor of adding new content. Now, I could get on board with more and more content added to the game if the game was able to at least sub consistently run smoothly and reasonably, but it just doesn't. In my experience, framerates are variable at best, with some of my friends who played this game with better computers than me barely managing to scrap 40-60 frames in still settings, i.E. if they aren't really doing anything and just watching things happen. For me, i can manage 30-40, until i start needing to do things, and by do things, i mean harvest resources, engage in combat, or load terrain. In these times ill scrape 20-30, and will frequently freeze up briefly as resources are collected or a rock breaks/tree falls.
This kind of constant frame dips and freezing might have been acceptable and understandable when the game opened to early access, hell even for several months after the game went out on early access, but its not acceptable anymore. Its been too long with too little improvement in that department.
The developers have also failed to address community feedback time and time again. From things like the aformentioned optimization and bugfixes that the game needs, to balance issues such ad rafts getting nerfed, and flying mounts getting essentially grounded as they were deemed overpowered. I would agree certain things about them needed to be changed, but instead of looking for a creative or nuance solution to the issues, rafts for many were essentially broken, and fliers went from strong to near useless for much more than light transportation overnight. More often than not, i found changes and nerfs to things to be in the favor of what the developer wanted them to be used for rather than leaving them open as options that had many creative uses.
And that leads me to the third thing that has soured this game in my mind, the release and early access DLC. Now, apparently scorched earth was released as DLC to help keep the company afloat in the face of a lawsuit earlier in the cycle, which might have been annoying for the consumer then, but was at least somewhat understandable. Where it becomes unacceptable to me, is when the game bumped its pricepoint to a 60 USD pricepoint for price parity on 'full release' when honestly, the game is not ready for a full release, and it just feels like a slap to the face after charging 20USD for a DLC in early access. If the game was much better optimized, less buggy, and the studio had listened better to its fanbase who so desperately wanted this game to only improve, as i have, and wanted it to get better, i could understand the price hike.
But to not even shift the extra map to be included in the base game (which would still be 10USD less in total for those who puchased both prior to full release) on top of all the previous grievences, i just cant support the game anymore. As much as i enjoyed this game before, as much as i wanted it to get better, and as much as i want to give it a recommendation, i just cant. Its sad, as ive had some great times with friends in this game, but it has deteriorated from the poor handling of it by the developer, and i cant be more sad about it. ARK: Surival Evolved, is not a game worth your time and money, unless you are fine with being disappointed with a Dev who doesn't handle their game well, and who wont be listening to you unless you agree with them.

This is one of those games that is far more than meets the eye.
You get in, and right away, you're reminded of Cookie Clicker, "Oh, it's one of those", you say, but give it a shot anyway because this is a cute new reskin with epic music and a fantasy theme.
Then you start buying heroes. Cid is a good enough gal, but she just makes one click equal two, no big deal. But the moment you get your first DPS hero, Treebeast, you find yourself leaping off into a game of far more mechanics and bonus numbers than you anticipated not too long ago from this Cookie Clicker "clone".
You get these heroes, all different, unique, with their own different upgrades. Most of them give that hero straight DPS, but others give you more gold, or boost your friends, or grant you special abilities to really shake up your screen. You push the limits of how far you can go, until it seems like each monster takes an hour and you simply don't have the gold to get stronger... Reset time - You reset, and suddenly the world is like new, but you're much stronger now. You might even enlist the help of the gods to follow you between resets, making each new game faster and stronger than the last.
This is your standard idle-game... with so much more.

Original review:
I used to love this game, but I dont anymore for many reasons. I have played since launch on PC (my account wasnt connected to steam at the time, which explains the hours), but a majority of my hours have been on Xbox One. Warframe has improved many ways since launch, but has made MANY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ changes and decisions, namely greed caused this. Here is a few negatives:
1. The endless grind for Warframe's, also many are locked away by microtransactions (Platinum)
2. No Console-to-PC account transfer. I spent alot of hours on console and when I came to PC, I was disappointed to find out that my account could never be transferred.
3. It takes more time crafting than it takes getting parts
4. Some parts are ridiculous difficult to grind (such as Neural Sensors), which you also cannot buy from the market
5. PvP is dead
6. When you start over, you will feel like you never want to play the game again due to the insane amount of time you spent grinding and barely progressing after HOURS of gameplay.
7. Spending more time keeping your pet alive that playing with it killed the pet system for me
8. Many mods are useless (on Warframes at least)
9. Trade system is still trash
10. Being in a clan is required for quite a few essential things, which I despise because I want the single-player challenge.
11. After about 80 hours of gameplay, the game becomes a chore instead of having fun.
12. DE shifting away from the consumer (player) and is more focused on profit, censoring anyone that disagrees.
Now some positives:
1. Decent looking graphics for a F2P game
2. Playerbase is helpful and somewhat active
3. Constant updates and stuff to do
4. Customable stuff
5. Pets and Warframes look cool
6. Credits can get SOME blueprints for things you want (but you have to grind the materials)
7. Very small chance you could get Platinum during gameplay
8. Mod system has improved since launch
9. Many events allow players to get resources
10. Chat is civilized

As a person, I tend to jump around from game to game, generally putting no more than 48 hours into one. I currently have around 600 mission hours in Warframe, and it's been one of those consistent games in my life. It's got really nice atmosphere and the various suits and weapons you can use all feel very different from each other. If you're one of those who plays only the most efficient sets on the most efficient runs, you might get bored quickly, since balance isn't quite this game's forte, but if you're like me, you can easily spend hours looking at your gear and still finding things you haven't used in a while. The only downside is if you want as many things as I have, you have to pay for extra slots, but even that can be circumvented because the premium currency, "Platinum" can be traded among people. There are also various factions you can fight against, but unfortunately the actual uniqueness of mobs can sometimes get a bit dull.
TL;DR: Pros and Cons
Pros:
- Huge variety in personal customization
- Fantastic environments and scenery
- Premium currency is tradeable
Cons:
- Can get grindy if you don't pay money
- Mobs could be a little more unique
- Where did my life go?

I like the concept of this type of game, but there is just nothing that special about Clicker Heros. There was a real missed opportunity here, as a stand-alone clicking/upgrade game, to outdo other games like this that exist. Maybe this is still possible in the future but it would require one or more overhauls.
Pros:
*Game looks quite nice and plays smoothly.
*You can farm gold when the game isn't running, but you need to check in to get upgrades and kill frequent bosses.
*The game lasts a long time, I'm not even sure if there is any end to the damage and levels you get to.
*The few abilities you can activate are useful and can be applied when needed.
*Actually clicking continues to be useful when using abilities, even late into the game.
Cons:
*Unlike other click games, you can basically forget about upgrading most of your stuff once you unlock the abililies from each tier. There is no thought involved; Only the 1st tier upgrade for clicking, and whatever your last 2 unlocked damage tiers are seem to matter at all.
*Nothing exciting or funny ever happens. There are no suprises, nor any significant changes in gameplay.
*Enemies dont do anything other than bounce up and down and wait to die.
*There is only one enemy at a time, and all enemies are exactly the same except for their graphic.
*There are no threats or even any status negative status affects. The only thing that can happen is you not having enough DPS to kill an enemy in the 30 second time limit.
*There are no strengths or weaknesses, only one bland type of DPS.
TL;DR Game is boring, even for a clicking/DPS game.

A good, fun, gory first person melee action game, Chivalry sticks you right in the armour of a medieval knight as you fight on vast battlefields, hacking each other to pieces as you spar with your opponents for domination. With four classes each working in their own way, and a plethora of weapons to use, you can truly make the knight you wish to be, whether a nimble man at arms, dodging strikes then counteracting with a flurry of blows, the reckless vanguard charging into battle with powerful running attacks, the unstoppable knight with his thick armour, or the ranged archer, bringing foes down from a distance. With a mix of game modes and some incredibly enjoyable objective gametypes that focus around some pretty gritty depictions of warfare (such as plaguing cities with corpse wagons, or pillaging cities and murdering the peasants) as well as your general free for all matches, there's something for everyone in this game.
And if you fancy a hand at a chivalry with more combat variety, look no further than the Deadliest Warrior expansion, pitting some of history's greatest warriors to battle against each other with all new weapons and abilities. With six completely different character classes from the blunderbuss-wielding pirate to honourable samurai and the vicious viking berserkers, deadliest warrior provides a fun, senseless murder-fest with these figures of history to see which was strongest.

Okay. I've played almost 600 hours of ARK- I suppose it's time that I wrote a review.
First off, I love ARK. I've had a lot of fun with it, and I've found that it's best heavily modded and played on a private server with a group of friends. It is absolutely not a singleplayer game and isn't entertaining at all in singleplayer unless I'm using console commands to run some tests and experiment with various creatures.
Let's talk about a few of my favorite and least favorite things about ARK.
Favorite things:
-The number of creatures. There is no lack of biodiversity in any of the maps, and it keeps things interesting.
-The modding community. There are no end to the wonderful maps and mods made by the community that inject hundreds of hours more into ARK's playtime.
-Mounted combat. Especially aerial combat can get intense and I find myself with a pounding heart and tons of adrenaline in my system. Nothing gives you a rush like diving into the World Scar on the Scorched Earth map and stealing a wyvern egg, only to fly out with dozens of furious wyverns right on your tail and seconds away from death at any time.
-The cooperation. This might seem like a weird thing to put here, but I love the cooperation required to do a lot of things (such as taming most of the larger and more dangerous creatures in the game) and it leads to a lot of trust between friends. Sometimes this goes awry (I didn't MEAN to drop him into the giga's mouth but, well, things happen) but other times it works out brilliantly and you feel like you own the world.
-The graphics. ARK can be a stunning game- IF your computer can handle it. If you don't have 16gb of RAM and a good graphics card, don't bother getting it for the graphics. If you're at the bottom range of graphical settings, ARK looks and runs terribly and you won't enjoy yourself. The bloom effect can get annoying but you can shut it off via the console.
-HAVING AN ARMY OF DINOSAURS. Hello? Who wouldn't want that? I personally lean more towards the fantasy creatures (particularly the wyverns) but I was definitely a dinosaur kid as a child and I guess that's bled over into now.
Least favorite things:
-The terrible optimization. The last few updates have improved this a lot, but ARK has long loading times and crashes inexplicably. It can get very laggy and overloads slower computers very easily. I said this before and I'll say it again- do NOT bother if you don't have 16GB+ of RAM. 8GB is simply not enough to run ARK with any consistency or quality.
-How damn DIFFICULT it is to do some things. It's nearly impossible to kill the bosses if you have a small tribe and with each update they "fix" the exploits my tribe uses to DO things that you normally need 20+ people to accomplish regularly. ARK feels more and more elitest with every update and it's very frustrating for a casual player on a private server with three friends. If you like things like this, then good for you, but it's just not my thing.
-So many bugs. ARK is coming out of Early Access next month as I write this, and let me tell you, a lot of the bugs that were in the game originally are still very present. Most of the gamebreaking ones are gone, but some new ones are still here and while you learn to deal with/avoid them it's annoying. The graphical glitches are frustrating and persistent, although not everyone has them.
-All the bizarre ways to tame creatures. Most are simple- knock them out, feed them, keep them out until they're tamed. A lot of creatures have been added lately with bizarre and difficult taming methods, and while it keeps the game interesting, it makes it very annoying for someone who can't remember every animal name and taming method. Having a bookmark to the wiki is a must.
Overall, I really enjoy ARK and would recommend it if it appeals to you. It's very difficult in places and I'd really recommend installing mods to fix a lot of the things in the game that you don't like.

A great game for those that are into the medieval age and who LOVE first-person sword fighting.
Although it has some bugs and not-so-good animations, it can do for one of the best medieval games out there. It has a huge learning curve though, so do not (or atleast try not to) get frustrated.
The melee weapons can range from daggers, maces, swords (like the Zweihänder), flails, spears, to polearms. There's also throwing weapons (Knives, Hatchets), bows, crossbows, smoke bombs and firebombs.
There are four classes in this game: The Archer, Man-At-Arms, Vanguard and Knight.
can use both bows and crossbows, and they can only use daggers or shortswords as melee weapons. They have no special mechanics.
(shortened as MAA) use daggers and shortswords too, they can wear small shields and they have a very fast attacking speed, movement and a higher stamina.
are sort of the balanced class in the game, where they aren't too slow, nor too fast. They use swords, longswords, maces, shields, polearms and spears, and they have a sprint attack mechanic where if you sprint for long enough, you will be able to leap forward for a powerful, although very predictable (and can be blocked), side slash.
are the strongest, slowest and healthiest class in the game. They have no special mechanics, and they are relatively weaker to blunt weapons. They can use swords, longswords, greatswords, shields, tower shields, maces and flails.
The graphics are quite nice and fitting, and Knights specifically look really good. It's an Unreal Engine game, so expect shiny (but a little unstable) graphics.
The gameplay involves, especially, slashing in three different ways: Side slashing (Left click), Thrusting/Stabbing (M. Wheel Up) and Overhead swings (M. Wheel Down). All buttons can be re-binded, that I know. You have to use the right attacks at the proper situations, and since there is Friendly Fire too, a side slash could end up decapitating your ally. You can kick enemies that are too close to you, staggering them and making an opening for your attacks. There is also the Feint mechanic, which is rather risky to use at first, but it can turn the tide of a 1v1 duel completely. A lot of tactics can (reccommended, but not necessary) be devised if you wish to be successful along with your team.
To put things into a short list, here are the ups and downs of this game:
Pros:
- Nice graphics
- Great combat
- It's somewhat balanced
- Can be silly in a good way sometimes
- Lets you be creative with your playstyle
- Could be one of the best Medieval era games
Cons:
- Huge learning curve, to the point it might scare some players away
- A lot of teamkillers
- Lag can be a big issue for those with slow connections
Overral, I think this is totally worth to buy even if it may, or may not be on sale. My rating is 8/10, not 9 or 10 because the fact my internet isn't too good made me have trouble fighting or even playing as MAAs, which is a bit disappointing.

-The terrible optimization. The last few updates have improved this a lot, but ARK has long loading times and crashes inexplicably. It can get very laggy and overloads slower computers very easily. I said this before and I'll say it again- do NOT bother if you don't have 16GB+ of RAM. 8GB is simply not enough to run ARK with any consistency or quality.
-How damn DIFFICULT it is to do some things. It's nearly impossible to kill the bosses if you have a small tribe and with each update they "fix" the exploits my tribe uses to DO things that you normally need 20+ people to accomplish regularly. ARK feels more and more elitest with every update and it's very frustrating for a casual player on a private server with three friends. If you like things like this, then good for you, but it's just not my thing.
-So many bugs. ARK is coming out of Early Access next month as I write this, and let me tell you, a lot of the bugs that were in the game originally are still very present. Most of the gamebreaking ones are gone, but some new ones are still here and while you learn to deal with/avoid them it's annoying. The graphical glitches are frustrating and persistent, although not everyone has them.
-All the bizarre ways to tame creatures. Most are simple- knock them out, feed them, keep them out until they're tamed. A lot of creatures have been added lately with bizarre and difficult taming methods, and while it keeps the game interesting, it makes it very annoying for someone who can't remember every animal name and taming method. Having a bookmark to the wiki is a must.
Overall, I really enjoy ARK and would recommend it if it appeals to you. It's very difficult in places and I'd really recommend installing mods to fix a lot of the things in the game that you don't like.

So, as someone who played the Beta for both PC and PS4 with a combined total of maybe 1.5k hours on both platforms, I can safely say that I have fallen out of love with this game, and here's why.
Ah yes, the grind. The main focus in Warframe is collecting resources to build new items like weapons, new warframes, consumables, etc. The problem is that recently the grind has become about 1000x as grindy. DigitalExtremes (aka DE, the developers of Warframe) have added/changed a load of features to make getting the newest content as tedious as possible. For instance, Nitain, a resource that has 5 spawns at day for about an hour, the problem is that the spawn times are completely random, and you need A LOT of this stuff, for instance, the Vauban Prime warframe ALONE costs 20 nitain, and you can imagine how long that would take for casual players who have jobs and can't constantly be checking on warframe just to see if a new nitain alert is availible. Or the fact that much of the games content is locked behind things known as Junctions, pretty much a gate to a new planet. Junctions each have their own set of requirements before they can be taken on to unlock a new problem. For veteran players, like myself and many others, who have already done much of the starchart/solar system we already have these planets unlocked and thus don't have to do the junctions. The problem is that quests like The War Within require these junctions to be completed, and any progress you could've previously made on the junction requirements are not retroactively counted, meaning that if, say, you defeated Vay Hek on Earth, Defeated 10 Sentient enemies on Lua, Collected 3 of the Challenge mods on Lua and Crafted a Mastery Rank 5 weapon before the Junctions were added, you have to do that all over again to actually allow you to access the junction. And for me personally, those challenge mods were ridiculously hard to farm, taking me over 50 runs on Lua to get one challenge room that can be done solo, for
, and that is if you don't fail the challenge room and if the junctions were already implemented.
Warframe's community is one of the most vibrant, also one of the most defensive. If you look on pretty much any forum thread on the Official forums about someone complaining about an actual problem with the game (I.E. The Balancing issues, the Pay-2-Skip, The Grindiness, etc.) you will also find someone defending DE, usually with a "It's Free to Play, so you can't compain" argument, or "You should've looked on the forums before the update". These types of people never actually give decent counter-arguments, and are usually just really scummy fan boys who look past every actual issue with the game. Not to mention the in-game community isn't that great, most players are only interested in helping themselves and/or are super spiteful and bigoted, atleast on PS4; I cant speak for PC's community, but it seems to be worse from what I've seen lately.
So, I think I have to talk about DE themselves, because a surprising amount of people don't want to. In my honest opinion, the entire DE team has turned into a greedy corporation that flat out refuses to listen to the complaints and concerns from players. Things are costing more and more platinum (the microtransition currency) like the Frost Harka Deluxe Skin Bundle costing as much as previous Deluxe Skin Bundles, but for less items; or Prime Access being worthless now, especially the accessory packs, $60 for remodel of your ship and your operator, things that you only see on occasion, or $80 for the newest primed warframes and weapons. They also don't listen to the community about broken/op weapons or about how dumb Riven mods are. Riven mods, for those of you who don't know, are mods you have a chance of obtaining at the end of the daily "sorties", pretty much a set of 3 extremely high level missions that reset daily. Riven mods were introduced to make weaker weapons more powerful and give players more customization. The problem is that they aren't needed; a simple number change can turn a terrible weapon into something reliable atleast, like they did with the Sicarus Prime, after they added rivens.
DE seem to just care about money and putting out things that they want, not what the community wants. Who ever said that Warframe needs more invincible enemies or mods that can buff already ridiculous weapons like the Tonkor or Soma Prime into a tier that can't even be called a god tier because of how powerful they are? Nobody. DE simply does what they want because they know that players are just going to complain and not actually stop playing the game or buying platinum.

This is my first review. I don't normally write reviews but felt compelled to by the huge amount of negative reviews here. To be honest I'm surprised by the amount of negativity for which I feel is unfair for what I believe is an amazing game. Much of the negativity appears to be due to the games development taking a direction some don't approve of. The other seems to be down to the games performance. I must make it clear that I only play single player or multiplayer with my children so true multiplayer is something I hold no interest in & cannot comment on. This review is aimed at my single player experience of the game.
I came into the early access early in this game & have seen the game mature over the past 18 months or so & have seen the game mature, I've also seen the upset caused when major changes have been made within the game which seemed to upset many players where some even now seem to be bitter about those changes. The game was in early development & the whole point of that is to build the game making changes, trying things out, removing things that didn't work out as the developers intended. All are part of the EA process so nothing to become upset about, after all that's the reason why us EA buyers paid much less than full retail price for the game.
What some reviewers don't seem to take onboard is that the game was in development so bugs, non-optimisation & changes are there all the time. In fact some seem to be on a crusade to vote down the game because changes have been made which they don't agree with, which I feel is a little unfair on such a great game. Take note of the bad reviews & you will be missing out on what I feel is the best game available - full stop! Look at the videos & the screenshots & yes, that's how the game is!!
The game during early access could be purchased very cheap, in fact I paid the full EA price of £23.99 for the game & £14.99 for the dlc which I feel is a real bargain as I have spent well over 1000 hours playing & still intend playing many many more hours. This is something I cannot understand, I see many negative reviews where the poster has spent hundreds or even thousands of hours within the game.  If the game is negative in their opinion then why have they spent so many hours playing it??? Some are complaining because the price for the released game will be £49.99, yes I agree £49.99 is a ridiculous price for many games, but not Ark, this game has so much to offer & will keep you amused for weekss/months/even years as I have found.
I have a high end PC so I experience no optimisation issues I can run the game on Epic settings & get very good fps, previously I had a low-end AMD processor system built in 2010 but with a reasonable video card & the game was still comfortably playable, settings were around mid-range & still playable. Remember though that I am talking about single player here, multiplayer maybe different?
The point of this review is to try & be honest here without the bitterness some seem to have towards the developers & the direction the game has gone which clearly doesn't sit well with some reviewers. My advice is, don't sit on the fence wondering, buy the game, try it, if you don't like it then refund it! If you pass this by then you are missing out on the greatest game that's ever been created in my opinion!
If you have a high end system then the game will run fine, if you have a low end system then be prepared to do some research within the forum & guides & you should be ok. The game is highly customisable, you can literally change anything to suit your style of play making it easier or harder depending on what you want. Start the game easy, pick an area that is marked as easy. Be aware of what is going on around you all the time, try to tame up some creatues to help protect you as soon as you are able. At first don't stray too far away from your chosen spot until you are able to defend or outrun predators (of which there are many) At first you will die a lot but each time you learn from that death. Over time you will learn to survive, when that happens you are hooked for life! My advice is to start off playing alone in single player until you have learned the game before venturing into multiplayer which I again will say that I have no experience of apart from playing locally with family.
Buy this game, if you don't you will be missing out on something very special! - be warned though, the game is huge so be prepared for a long wait for it to download. The game will also swallow up the hours so be prepared for it to take up much of your free time.
This is my first & only review, I am no fanboy nor do I have any links with the developers.  I am just a normal games player who has been compelled to write this (honest) review of which I see as a fantastic game which should not be passed by. This is my experience of this great game, I'm not saying others may not have had issues but I feel with over 1000 hours playtime I am qualified to give an honest review as I see it - I have had none of what others have posted negatively about apart from the normal hiccups of an early access game which one expects when going into an alpha version of a game.
I can't wait for the full release version of this which I'm sure will hold some nice surprises :) hopefull there will still be 1000 more hours of gameplay awaiting me.

As a person, I tend to jump around from game to game, generally putting no more than 48 hours into one. I currently have around 600 mission hours in Warframe, and it's been one of those consistent games in my life. It's got really nice atmosphere and the various suits and weapons you can use all feel very different from each other. If you're one of those who plays only the most efficient sets on the most efficient runs, you might get bored quickly, since balance isn't quite this game's forte, but if you're like me, you can easily spend hours looking at your gear and still finding things you haven't used in a while. The only downside is if you want as many things as I have, you have to pay for extra slots, but even that can be circumvented because the premium currency, "Platinum" can be traded among people. There are also various factions you can fight against, but unfortunately the actual uniqueness of mobs can sometimes get a bit dull.
TL;DR: Pros and Cons
Pros:
- Huge variety in personal customization
- Fantastic environments and scenery
- Premium currency is tradeable
Cons:
- Can get grindy if you don't pay money
- Mobs could be a little more unique
- Where did my life go?

Well I can honestly say Warframe is really good at making you want to spend some money. Which in my opinion is a good thing, keeps the economy moving.
You don't need that weapon now, you can wait 12 hours for it to be built.
You can get that Catalyst or Reactor by waiting out the alerts and invasions.
But you can get that faster by paying some money, even worse you can get up to 75% off ingame currency, tempting you to buy some before the offer goes away.
Look I would say Warframe is worth the download, if you have a decent download speed and expansive hard drive space, I would strongly recommend downloading.
Some points in it's favor...
Everything is achievable through gameplay (GRINDING). Some of which is only avaiable through gameplay (capes...).
If you want ingame currency, you can trade with the less RNG blessed players on trade chat.
Gameplay is fun, better with friends though.
Make new friends, the commmunity is usually quite nice.

GRINDING
Download size is ever expanding
Weapon and Warframe (suits you play in) start with limited quantity, like garage slots or such in other games you must purchase them with ingame currency.

I enjoyed this game for the most part, but i only paid $40 w/ the expansion. The gameplay itself is far from perfect, but in progress. It is still bugged to all hell (i.e. get stuck in rocks, dinos get stuck on trees, spawn inside a rock,etc.). The concept of this game is magnificient, would doesn't want to feed a triceratops (Trike in the game) a bunch of berries, throw a saddle on it, and wreck all havock with it's horns. The maps are beautifully designed, the biomes are separated in such a way that you dont go from volcanic wasteland to showy tundra riddles with moose and mammoths (I said moose and mammoths in the same sentence) in just a few steps. The creatures are by far my favorite part of the game, there's such a diverse cast, that are at your disposal to tame and ride, and each one is useful for gathering certain materials and accessing certain areas diffficult to get to on foot. Now, my least favorite part of the game, YOU NEED A SUPER COMPUTER TO RUN THIS GAME WITH QUALITY GRAPHICS. I have a fairly high performance computer and it seemed like it was constantly struggling to keep up with the game. Most games I can run at the highest quality of graphics flawlessly, but this one, i had to run on the lowest and it was still very low fps, constantly having to stop what i was doing in game to allow the game to catch up,crashing, freezing, etc. The reason I am recommending this game is because I have a belief that the developers will patch and fix the game to run smoothly without bugs and glitches upon release. It's a common misbelief that a game is supposed to get fixed in the early access stages when that's not the case, early access is to help the devleopers see how the game can be fixed and release a near perfected game on it's official release date.

The best way to describe this game is "could be great". I have played it for the whole year it's been out now, and that's exactly the same thing I said about it when I tried it out for the first time. Why "could be"? Because this game is held back from achieving its full potential by the multitudes of bugs that plague it. A year ago I was hoping it would be fixed. But here I am, a year later, still experiencing the game in a state that could only be excusable for a beta, or a game in its first month of release.
That's not to say it isn't fun. The combat mechanics are simple to grasp and easy to start, yet offer loads of room for improvement. There's a decent variety of choice. Between the game's four classes and lots of weapons to pick from for each, everyone is bound to find the playstyle and loadout that fits him. And the visual customization system allows you to add a personal touch to your warrior. The graphics are pretty, if you've got the system to see them, because the optimization is some of the worst I've seen in any video game ever. There's a variety of game modes to choose from, and while there aren't many maps, most of them being recycled for different modes, the existing ones are well made, albeit with the occasional enviromental bug here and there. The sound is absolutely superb, especially the voice acting, which, coming from a non professional cast, makes it all the more impressive.
In short, you probably won't regret buying this game. It may not be perfect, but it offers the best immersive medieval combat experience for multiple players currently on the market. Just be prepared to experience some deaths that are entirely not your fault, but rather, atributed to the game's flawed state. But as long as you can look past that, the overall fun you get from this game will sure compensate for it.

I have been playing Warframe for a good while, a friend hooked me into the game a little over a year ago and I still play to this day. I do love this game, I really do. This game is literally everything Destiny should have been in my opinion. Raids, Surivial modes, a compelling and great add ons with amazing customization.
The game gives you insane amounts of choices, especially for a free to play. And I want to stress that factor, IT IS A FREE TO PLAY GAME! The payment system is what I like to call a "Pay to Advance Faster" or P2AF system. You are not required to purchase anything in this game, especially with the in game trading system. This game honestly you cannot go wrong. It's an MMO, RPG, Shooter all put into one. There is a Warframe for everyone's playstyle. You love to be the meat shield of the team? Play Rhino, Chroma or Atlas. You like to be an Assassin? Play Ivara (My personal Favorite), Loki or Ash. Do you love to just go balls deep, all in, and killing everything in your way? Play Valkyr (Another favorite who just got a Prime Frame), Excalibur or even Inaros. Are you the support main of your friend group or like saving lives? play Trinity, Oberon or even Nekros. There is so much choice, so much potential. And with the game constantly expanding. This game is beautiful and I can't wait to see the constant advances it'll make.
**MY ONE QUIRK WITH THE GAME**
There is a major connection issue that makes it difficult to connect to a different host on multiplayer if you do a Public Match. I notice that this happens on computers with lower end specs, so it makes it diffciult to play with friends when I'm not using my PC.  I hope to see this fixed one day.
Other than that, I never see any true breaking issues. I recommend this game to anyone and everyone who wants something free to play that can be very addictive.

(Reader's Notice: This is a rather long review; I wanted to be in-depth.)
I couldn't tell you exactly when, or how, I heard about Warframe. I joined shortly after "The Mad Cephalon" update, and haven't been able to put the game down in the years since. Warframe is a fast and furious journey of gunplay, gore, and gathering. Let me tell you about it.
To say Warframe seems uninviting to new players is a bit of an understatement. After a thrilling introduction to the game's core mechanics (gunplay, acrobatics, melee, etc.), the player and their chosen Warframe are whisked up into orbit aboard their Orbiter, a personal space station where you'll spend time between missions. Within the Orbiter lay all the crucial systems to your play; loadout management, crafting, navigation, and so on. Virtually none of these systems are explained to you as a new player, and their explanation relies largely on either helpful players (which are plentiful in the community) or the reliably-maintained Warframe Wikia.
The newly-revamped Starchart is, admittedly, easier to navigate than its predecessor; completing every mission on a given planet will give the player the opportunity to complete tasks at a "Junction". Doing so will face the player with a short boss fight, rewarded with progression to the next planet. Each of the game's myriad of environments is, to the say the least, beautiful. From filthy shipyards to colossal forests, Warframe's worlds certainly aim to please.
Inhabiting those environments, of course, are your enemies. The endless, vicious armies of the Grineer generally inhabit both the innermost and outermost worlds of the solar system; presenting simultaneously the easiest and greatest adversaries, depending on where you travel. The Grineer have a distinct chem-punk, industrial vibe to every unit and map, and prefer brute ballistic force.  Inhabiting the worlds between the Grineer's dominion lay the Corpus; a corporate conglomerate of space capitalists that prefer energy weapons and robotic proxies. The futuristic, digital style the Corpus prefer contrasts (but does not clash) with the industrial motif of the Grineer; the two factions frequently come into territorial conflict. And lastly, in the dark nooks and crannies of the solar system lay the Infested; a Flood-like contagion of viral monstrosities that seek only to assimilate and spread.
All these factions, in essence, are your enemy. As a Tenno, you are hated and hunted by the Grineer, Corpus and Infested in turn. Luckily, as a Tenno, your Warframe is also exponentially more powerful than even the mightiest Grineer soldier, Corpus crewman, or Infested monster. Speaking of Warframes:
There are dozens of them. Each harboring a uniquely destructive (or supportive) playstyle; from the impenetrable Rhino to the elusive Ivara. Acquiring these new Warframes, however, will not be easy: For most frames, their component parts (Neuroptics, Systems, and Chassis) are dropped as rewards from specific bosses, i.e. Equinox's component parts are dropped as potential rewards from Tyl Regor, the boss at Uranus. After crafting of the component parts, the base blueprint for the "final" craft can be acquired from the Market aboard your Orbiter, and, as the community says, "put in the oven."
But if only it were so easy. Unfortunately, Warframe, being a Free-To-Play game, follows the according model of microtransactions, specifically for the currency of Platinum. However, this cannot be stressed enough:
Every weapon, frame, companion and auxiliary item can be acquired through gameplay. Platinum is used primarily for cosmetics and as a "rush" tool; any item that is "in-progress" in the crafting Foundry can be rushed via the use of Platinum. Need to play that new Warframe right away? Rush it. Don't want to wait until tomorrow to use that new shotgun? Rush it. While by no means a necessary means to an end, Platinum has proved helpful to many a player in upgrading their arsenal that much quicker. Further cementing its presence in the game is the fact that Platinum can be traded; generating a rich and diverse economy of trading that can enable players to acquire Platinum without spending a dime.
In fact, many weapons and Warframes (specifically, Prime gear) are
to acquire from the Market, and can only be acquired through gameplay or trading.Prime items present one of the most unique features Warframe has to offer. Should a player find themselves wanting a Prime Warframe (say, Nova Prime), the acquirement of said gear becomes what could best be described as a personalized scavenger hunt. While not difficult, the quest for a Prime item is certainly tedious, if not rewarding.
With the advent of the "War Within" update, Warframe's high-level daily "Sortie" missions became a feature reserved for relatively experienced players to the game, who had completed the War Within quest (reaching this point is, by itself, an odyssey). Sorties pit players against extremely high-level adversaries under special conditions (enhanced enemies, rampant radiation, etc.) and generally present the greatest challenge the game has to offer outside of
Raids. Alongside Sorties, of course, reside Warframe's two Raid missions; "The Law of Retribution" and "The Jordas Verdict". Only the former is played extensively, however, so keep this in mind as you launch yourself into Warframe's endgame scene.
For all my praise, you'd imagine I have nothing bad to say about Warframe. You'd be wrong. While I won't pollute a positive review with criticism, I will certainly caution incoming players about the game's downfalls. To put it lightly, RNG is absolutely rampant in many sectors of the game. Loot tables can occasionally be either cluttered with junk (for an example of this, see the community's reaction to Nidus' drop table) or flat-out ridiculous in their percentages. Alongside RNG lays the constant push to purchase Platinum. While not inescapable, it's made quite clear to the fledgling Tenno that the developers would very much like them to purchase Platinum. While not necessarily done maliciously, it can occasionally become anxiety-producing for the newly-minted player with little to no direction. And, last but certainly not least, lays the matter of grind. In Warframe, you will be doing
of grinding. I temper this criticism with the reminder that, alongside Warframe's grind lays incredibly engaging and enjoyable gameplay that will make this trek worthwhile.
To encapsulate it, Warframe is not a perfect game; in fact, it is very far from it. However, beneath its cold, uninviting exterior lays a rich, immersive game populated by a thriving and welcoming community. Being unable to find a squad to fill is nearly impossible, and if you're seeking out a specific item or objective, you will almost always be able to find someone else to join you on your journey.
Come, Tenno. It is time for you to join the war.

This game in all it's greatness, is broken. A game based around medieval tactics used in old warfare, it has great potential and uses it.. most of it.
Although, if you are going to make a game, don't break what the gameplay is crucially based around. The blocking mechanic, and the leveling system.
The blocking system does what it's name dubbs it to do, block. But if you block, and someone else hits you [and you take damage] while you're blocking, something is going wrong. Blocking is meant to stop the weapon from hitting you, if you and an enemy are facing eachother, you're blocking and they're swinging, that should be an effective block, right? Most of the time that mechanic doesn't work in Chivalry.
The leveling system is based on getting enough kills in order to unlock the next weapon. When you take the time to level up for a highly-desired weapon, naturally you'd aspire to keep this weapon. In Chivalry, every once in a while your new weapon gets deleted and you have to work from the ground up all over again. Me and other people I know have had this problem and it has yet to get fixed.
Chivalry has some horrid optimising problems with it's server browser. Most of the time, refreshing the server list takes away all of the servers. If you get too spacific with the server filter, it breaks and you don't get anything, even though there are obviously servers out there for what you have searched.
Want to join a friend? They have to tell you the server's name and you have to pain-stakingly search for the server that may not even show up on your list. Join them via Steam? Steam will say you cant join the server your friend is currently in.
Sometimes servers will allow you to join, other times, you won't be able to join and it will be stuck on the loading screen until you cancel it.
Chivalry can be a nice game to play at times, but due to these issues, I wouldn't stick with it.

Alright, time to write my first ever review...
I have been playing Warframe for almost four years now as you can probably see from my hours played. I have seen so much amazing content added to this game that I don't even know how to start complimenting the 3D Modelers.
BUT.
I have also seen the most volatile fan base since I stopped played Halo and Call of Duty. Vitriolic ideals of "what should and shouldn't be in the game" fly everywhere without a moment's hesitation. Many point out that the developers "just want our money."
Yes... They do.
That's how a company works. You think Dota 2 or League of Legends stays up because of a player base alone? Those employees need money to live and go to their job to work on said game. Almost no player I have met in-game has actually considered this fact and continue to spew hateful speeches against other players and the developers because they don't want to grind or pay real money.
As for the Beta argument I have seen...
It's how they can continue to keep releasing content the way they do. Sure, there are glitches. Nearly EVERY game in the current generation of consoles AND PCs ships with glitches. And they get patched after release. Warframe is no different. Being a Beta release allows them to stamp out bugs as they form, preventing a full-release nightmare like many games in the past. I don't want to name names for fear of♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off THOSE fan bases...
Probably already irritating most of these players from my first few paragraphs now...
As I said earlier, I have played this game for a long time. And while I do have to agree that some of the new content has RIDICULOUS costs for casual players, people have to remember that they only release content every week or so. Usually, bug fixes above all else. It's honestly a miracle they release as much stuff as they do compared to other companies. I don't see many other games release so many new characters and weapons that add new systems to the game without massive update packs that cost outrageous sums of money to purchase.
But I digress.
Players should remember that this is also in a similar vein to an MMO, meaning they need to have things for players to do so they don't get bored. Let's face it, grinding has been in video games since their inception. Castlevaina 2... Final Fantasy... Heck, any shooter is grinding just to level up to unlock the next tier of guns.
Is it right?
Maybe not...
But the player isn't the developer.
Try looking up a class in Game Design or Coding and see how quickly you get overwhelmed with the amount of stuff to make sure works ABSOLUTELY PERFECTLY in order for a game to work. Coding alone must be hell for this game due to so many different characters and combinations between weapons and frames. And don't even get me started on the graphical side...
TennoGen content creators alone have a hard time getting to see their dreams and concepts put into the game. Copyrights, similar designs, and many other factors can get that idea scrapped before it even hits the cutting room floor for fear of being sued or accused of imitating something else. The fact that Warframe looks NOTHING like other games in terms of design truly speaks to the developers as creators and it should with every player.
Instead, many whine about the fact that they have to spend more than five minutes to unlock a weapon they want...
And to put it out there... I haven't even gotten to play the recent content!
That's right!
I'm sitting in limbo as I write this review.
I had to transfer my email over to a new account due to my ancient ISP finally shutting down its email service.
Do I hate the devs for "forgetting about me as a player?"
No. Because I have faith in them.
And though that faith has been dwindling since it started to take a lot longer than expected to transfer my email so I can play again, I still keep that ember of hope alive in my hands that I will get to play this amazing, albeit flawed at times, game created by amazing people who only wish to see their dream come true on the small screen.
All in all, Warframe may not be perfect, but it still beats the heck out of other games I have played through the years. I have met the kindest and most helpful players I have ever met in my sessions of endless fun and entertainment.
And before anyone asks, yes I have spent quite a bit of money on this game. Because I have a job and  it's nice to receive that paycheck that allows you to continue doing what you love. And I will continue to spend money on this game so it can continue to flourish and change, evolving with the player base as the developers, and players, learn from their mistakes.

Are you looking through the reviews to help you decide if you should try this game? Then let me help you if that is the case. To save time, I will list down the pros and cons.
Pros
- A F2P game that ISN'T P2W
- Great graphics for a game that's free
- Gameplay is fun and fast paced
- Customization galore
- Frequently updated
- Multiple playstyles
_____________
Cons
- Waiting for crafted items
- No end-game
- Holy hell is the grind real
_____________
Neutral
- Community can be amazing and horrible at the same time.
______________________________________
Only proceed if you have more time to read
______________________________________
If you want more explanation, let me provide it here:
Not P2W: Yeah, you don't exactly win by buying the most expensive item in the game (which by the way are cosmetics). You get better with your builds, not with your guns. PvP is ridiculously balanced, no one becomes a powerhouse.
Community: Man this one is important. Any game can be great with the community's influence. But just like all communities, Warframe has it's fair share. I've played with a lot of great people in this game, but I've also encountered a lot of people who can turn any new person off. Especially the elitists, screw those players.
Waiting game: Yeah, this is as close as P2W as you'll get. Everytime you craft an item, there's a waiting time. And depending on your item(s), they have varied wait times. (i.e Consumables are 60sec , Weapons are 6-12hrs , Warframes 3 days)
GRIND: Oh yeah, this is the biggest topic here. With almost every major update, the game becomes harder and harder to grind. It was a simple RNG luck back then, that was okay. But now, things got more grind. Relics are, to me, a huge step backwards. Back then you had T1 - T4 , simple enough to remember, wasn't complicated. Now you got Lith, Meso, Neo, Axi that has their own sub-categories like Lith N1 or Neo N3 and so on. With every new "prime" items that get out, more of these things come out as well.
No end-game: Yeah, this one hits hard too. Once you've gotten almost everything, there's not much point in going back asides from the major updates. That's it, game over and wait for next update.
Quests: OOH, these are my favorites. With each major update, the game gets a new storyline quest. The ones with cinematics are absolutely amazing ( See the Second Dream, and why the community went crazy when they played it), and of course you get side quests. Not as interesting, but most are still fun.
Overall, I've had a wild ride with Warframe. And I thoroughly enjoyed my time with the game. Sure there's no end-game, but I sure as hell enjoyed my ride getting there.

This game is one of the best first person fighters I've played. Actually scratch that, it is THE best first person fighter I've played! Some people call it a hack and slash, that's more because first person fighters don't really exist. The fighting mechanics are top notch. Once you get deeper and deeper into the mechanics, the more you want to play.
It has some trouble because there are a good number of bugs. Leveling up can take a while because the game frequently forgets what weapons you've leveled up and how much experience you have. It's a minor thing considering most of the better class weapons are the starting ones. It comes down to preference at higher levels of weapons.
The greatest strength the game has is that it feels closer to real combat than most games do. The weapons are fairly balanced, there are some notable weapons, that perform less than expected. However, it plays into the game, because people will think you're not very skilled for choosing them, so they get cocky. Once they think they have the upper hand, they will be more prone to mistakes.
I recommend this game to anyone (maybe not little kids, it's kind of violent), It's unique and worth the cost. For its asking price, it's a bargain. I give this game a 9/10, I'd give it a perfect, but there are the leveling bugs. Once those are fixed, this is a perfect tournament fighter. It's gaining in popularity, so give it a try.

I have been playing Warframe for a good while, a friend hooked me into the game a little over a year ago and I still play to this day. I do love this game, I really do. This game is literally everything Destiny should have been in my opinion. Raids, Surivial modes, a compelling and great add ons with amazing customization.
The game gives you insane amounts of choices, especially for a free to play. And I want to stress that factor, IT IS A FREE TO PLAY GAME! The payment system is what I like to call a "Pay to Advance Faster" or P2AF system. You are not required to purchase anything in this game, especially with the in game trading system. This game honestly you cannot go wrong. It's an MMO, RPG, Shooter all put into one. There is a Warframe for everyone's playstyle. You love to be the meat shield of the team? Play Rhino, Chroma or Atlas. You like to be an Assassin? Play Ivara (My personal Favorite), Loki or Ash. Do you love to just go balls deep, all in, and killing everything in your way? Play Valkyr (Another favorite who just got a Prime Frame), Excalibur or even Inaros. Are you the support main of your friend group or like saving lives? play Trinity, Oberon or even Nekros. There is so much choice, so much potential. And with the game constantly expanding. This game is beautiful and I can't wait to see the constant advances it'll make.
**MY ONE QUIRK WITH THE GAME**
There is a major connection issue that makes it difficult to connect to a different host on multiplayer if you do a Public Match. I notice that this happens on computers with lower end specs, so it makes it diffciult to play with friends when I'm not using my PC.  I hope to see this fixed one day.
Other than that, I never see any true breaking issues. I recommend this game to anyone and everyone who wants something free to play that can be very addictive.

Clicker heroes is a free to play idle clicker game in which you click to kill monsters. This game has microtransactions but it is completely playable without them. Clicker heroes has consumed a large amount of my time; I'd say that I'd really recomend you play clicker heroes if you like the idle clicker genre. A nice feature of the game is that your monsters will grind gold for you even while you don't have the game opened! So when you come back the next day you have a nice pile of gold waiting for you.
Along with the idle clicking mechanics there are additional things that make the game a lot more complex than just clicking monsters. As you progress and unlock attributes from your heroes you will unlock special abilities. These abilties can be activated for a limited amount of time and provide you with bonus benefits such as: Producing more gold, more damage, more critical hits, and so forth.
For the complex part of the game there are these things called hero souls. These hero souls are obtained by killing boss monsters, and leveling up your heroes. These hero souls are not usable until you ascension and reset your progress. You will keep your hero souls but you will lose all of your heroes and levels and have to start from level 1 again. These hero souls can be used to purchase and level up statues which will provide you with passive attributes which will stay with you even after ascensioning.

By far one of the most addicting games to play with friends.  While it does have numerous flaws, I must say that as an overall game, Ark is one of my favorites.
Pros:
Ark has a strange way of forcing you to adapt.  You're never fully safe and can die at any moment, forcing the player to learn quickly or fall trying.
The game's dinosaur taming is both good and bad, but I'll get to the bad later.  When you finally tame that rex or mosasaur or quetzal, you feel a rush that doesn't exist in a lot of the other survival games.
It's very fun to play with friends, though larger groups of friends make it easier than smaller groups.
Cons:
It's very easy to get salty in this game, and more experienced players rarely help newbies wirnhout expecting something in return that they know the newbies can't return.  The community overall is a 50/50.
Taming dinos at higher levels can take forever, and that isn't ideal when you're short on time.  This game is time intensive and isn't for those looking for a quick game to play.  At least on public servers.
You can die at any time and anywhere.  This can be very rage inducing when you first start out and don't have the means to recover your corpse.
Dino's sometimes glitch out.  As well as your dead body if you aren't lucky.
Most f what I've said has been experienced on an official PvE server.  I don't have any experience with raiders an the like, so I can't say anything about PvP servers.
Like I said earlier, it's a great game to play with friends, but otherwise it can be droll and can take an incredibly long time to progress in since many of those higher level dinos can take around nine hours to tame.  And you have to pay attention to them or they'll die or wake up when you aren't there.
Buy at your own discretion and after lots of research to make sure you want this game.

I cannot recommend this title, and here's why:
There's mainly 2 ways to play the game, actively or passively. Pursuing the game actively highly involves clicking the enemy target for as long as your fingers, toes, and other creative means allow you to go on. Do take note, that even if you decided on taking the active route because it may seem like you'll progress faster in the short future, in the long run, the difference isn't as huge as one might think.
Passive gameplay involves opening the game, leaving a few tweaks on upgrades and then closing the game again. The main aspect of this gameplay is what it does while the game is shut down, as it also fights passively for you once you get your very first few upgrades.
For both gameplay types there's a later game strategy, as you decide between which skills you use and which special supportive powers called Ancients you invest in (by spending hero souls, the currency of the game). These can highly change the speed of your progression throughout the game. However, sooner or later you'll hit a wall where your damage is simply no longer enough for progressing with your current upgrades. This will force you to start the game countless times back at stage 1 in order to earn more hero souls for upgrades. So, you'll have to gear yourself with remarkable amounts of patience (if you can call it that) if you plan on getting anywhere in this game, as it won't change an inch beyond selecting upgrades.
My main objective when I started the game was to get its achievements, which I at first thought would've been a breeze considering the lack of any requirements beyond clicking. It's even capable of idling and playing itself while you're gone. How hard can it be? The plan was to only spend small amounts of time on the game, which didn't happen, as the game also rewards you for actively playing. Hoping to rush through the game quicker for the achievements, I continued.
Would I recommend people to play this game? No, I really can't say that there's anything to come here for, other than a quick fix of satisfaction for a few minutes for the active player, just to realise later that you'll be that bit more disappointed that you even spent your time on it in the first place. And as a passive player, you're in for a long wait consisting of tiny upgrading and no variation.
Through all this, I've learnt that clicker games don't work for me, even though I had thought they might've at first! At least not when it's executed in the way that Clicker Heroes had. Perhaps I would've been better prepared for it in the beginning had it been called Passive Heroes. And maybe by removing the clicking feature alltogether, and making it a passive waiting game would've made the experience very different.
tldr;
It gets tedius very, very fast and you should probably be spending your gaming time elsewhere. I wouldn't want to recommend such an experience to anyone. It feels like a human experiment. The princess is in another castle~
Overall, if you insist and MUST play it, I would recommend the passive route a lot more and think of the game as passive heroes instead of clicker heroes, as the reward vs investment in active gameplay is just not there.

ARK is a game about surviving and taming dinosaurs.  The general approach is to tame small, weak dinosaurs, then use those dinosaurs to tame bigger and better dinosaurs, before branching out into all sorts of foraging, farming, and exploring.  You likely already know what ARK is - The screenshots tell enough of a story alone.
Disclaimer; Most of my time playing has been on Unofficial PvP servers.
It seems like many of the reviews lately have been overly negative because of the issues with Official servers and the price change. Private/Unofficial servers fix a great deal of these issues.  Rules can be enforced better, exploits more directly monitored, etc.  It can take time to find a quality Unofficial, but I have found it to be well worth it.  We knew about the price change long in advance, though most long-time ARK players will agree that the game is not ready for release, and thus the price hike seems...abrupt.  Having bought at early access price and invested additional money in running a server, I have found the experience to be well worth every cent.
ARK does a lot of things right and a lot of things wrong.  I would be hesitant to recommend it to anyone because of the extremely time-intensive nature of the game, but it fills a niche extremely well.  ARK is a game that can make hours and days disappear if you let it - There is always work to be done.  And make no mistake, ARK is often work.  That being said, I find that the slow build over time leads to an overall very satisfying experience.
Pros;
Dinosaurs.  This is why you should play ARK.
Robust mod availability for customization of experience.
Wide spectrum of gameplay from hellish dungeons to peaceful farming.
Long-term efforts with satisfying payoffs.
Great to play with friends.
Plenty of tense, panic-inducing moments, particularly in caves and deep water.
Cons;
Difficult vanilla game experience.
Extremely poorly optimized + Insane disk space usage.
Extreme time consumption depending on server settings.
Can tend toward boring/grindy at times.
Often very buggy in ways that range from annoying to rage-inducing.
tl;dr - Hesitant recommendation.  Play Unofficial servers.  Not ready for release.

So I haven't played ARK for very long in comparison to some of the other people giving reviews on here but I feel it has been enough time to be able to sum up the experience in general.
The idea behind ARK is brilliant, everyone loves dinosaurs and everyone loves shooting/stabbing/knocking out other players whilst buiding bases and exploring a huge open and beautiful sandbox. The first compliment I will give this game is that it is B.E.A.U.T.I.F.U.L on epic graphics with everything turned to the max. It's a shame then that the vast majority of people cannot play on this level of detail without frying their system.
The game performs poorly on all but the beefiest systems (And according to the fanboys on some systems that apparently contain core 2 duo's and a GTX 660.....) although in fairness it does still look good on high and medium settings whilst running fairly well.
On to my main gripe with this game and why I will not be reccomending it.
It is IMPOSSIBLE to play on any of the official servers for more than a day without being wiped when you go to sleep, this review is being written after I have joined the 4th tribe in 3 days to be wiped (2 on the first day and then one for each day after I have woken up and turned on the computer to be met with XXXX killed you). It just isn't fun anymore and the fact of the matter is that a tribe of 60 people being able to transfer their characters and all of their stuff accross to any other official server and wipe it within a matter of hours is gamebreaking for PvP and is turning this game into another RUST where the only way that you can viably play is by joining some huge clan of people that expect you to be able to play 24/7. This point segways us nicely into my next problem, do not even bother buying this game unless you are a shut in nerd who only plays video games or you are unemployed because it is a vortex that sucks you in and requires hours of uninterupted play time to be able to actually get anywhere.
All in all then ARK is a game that was good as a concept but has been ruined by bad gameplay mechanics in some vital areas, poor performance on everything but a £1500 or more rig and the fact that any progress you do make on official servers is wiped daily rendering the whole experience pretty ♥♥♥♥ing pointless.

Alright, time to write my first ever review...
I have been playing Warframe for almost four years now as you can probably see from my hours played. I have seen so much amazing content added to this game that I don't even know how to start complimenting the 3D Modelers.
BUT.
I have also seen the most volatile fan base since I stopped played Halo and Call of Duty. Vitriolic ideals of "what should and shouldn't be in the game" fly everywhere without a moment's hesitation. Many point out that the developers "just want our money."
Yes... They do.
That's how a company works. You think Dota 2 or League of Legends stays up because of a player base alone? Those employees need money to live and go to their job to work on said game. Almost no player I have met in-game has actually considered this fact and continue to spew hateful speeches against other players and the developers because they don't want to grind or pay real money.
As for the Beta argument I have seen...
It's how they can continue to keep releasing content the way they do. Sure, there are glitches. Nearly EVERY game in the current generation of consoles AND PCs ships with glitches. And they get patched after release. Warframe is no different. Being a Beta release allows them to stamp out bugs as they form, preventing a full-release nightmare like many games in the past. I don't want to name names for fear of♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off THOSE fan bases...
Probably already irritating most of these players from my first few paragraphs now...
As I said earlier, I have played this game for a long time. And while I do have to agree that some of the new content has RIDICULOUS costs for casual players, people have to remember that they only release content every week or so. Usually, bug fixes above all else. It's honestly a miracle they release as much stuff as they do compared to other companies. I don't see many other games release so many new characters and weapons that add new systems to the game without massive update packs that cost outrageous sums of money to purchase.
But I digress.
Players should remember that this is also in a similar vein to an MMO, meaning they need to have things for players to do so they don't get bored. Let's face it, grinding has been in video games since their inception. Castlevaina 2... Final Fantasy... Heck, any shooter is grinding just to level up to unlock the next tier of guns.
Is it right?
Maybe not...
But the player isn't the developer.
Try looking up a class in Game Design or Coding and see how quickly you get overwhelmed with the amount of stuff to make sure works ABSOLUTELY PERFECTLY in order for a game to work. Coding alone must be hell for this game due to so many different characters and combinations between weapons and frames. And don't even get me started on the graphical side...
TennoGen content creators alone have a hard time getting to see their dreams and concepts put into the game. Copyrights, similar designs, and many other factors can get that idea scrapped before it even hits the cutting room floor for fear of being sued or accused of imitating something else. The fact that Warframe looks NOTHING like other games in terms of design truly speaks to the developers as creators and it should with every player.
Instead, many whine about the fact that they have to spend more than five minutes to unlock a weapon they want...
And to put it out there... I haven't even gotten to play the recent content!
That's right!
I'm sitting in limbo as I write this review.
I had to transfer my email over to a new account due to my ancient ISP finally shutting down its email service.
Do I hate the devs for "forgetting about me as a player?"
No. Because I have faith in them.
And though that faith has been dwindling since it started to take a lot longer than expected to transfer my email so I can play again, I still keep that ember of hope alive in my hands that I will get to play this amazing, albeit flawed at times, game created by amazing people who only wish to see their dream come true on the small screen.
All in all, Warframe may not be perfect, but it still beats the heck out of other games I have played through the years. I have met the kindest and most helpful players I have ever met in my sessions of endless fun and entertainment.
And before anyone asks, yes I have spent quite a bit of money on this game. Because I have a job and  it's nice to receive that paycheck that allows you to continue doing what you love. And I will continue to spend money on this game so it can continue to flourish and change, evolving with the player base as the developers, and players, learn from their mistakes.
