First off, let me say that this review will be two-in-one: one for Chivalry: Medieval Warfare (CMW) and Chivalry: Deadliest Warrior (CDW).
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare: Chivalry is an amazingly fun and rewarding game that can seem intimidating for the new player. When you first start out and pick the tutorial you will feel out of place and in over your head. You're given numerous commands to practice and master, with a variety of key strokes and combos being thrown at you early on. When you move on to the core MP, you begin as a untrained whelp, flailing and swinging wildly while more skilled opponents beat you down. But slowly you recognize the patterns and develop strategies to deal with your enemies. The sense of reward you get upon beating an opponent in a one-on-one duel is immensely satisfying.
While your standard game modes like FFA, TDM, and CTF are there, the real joy comes from the "Team Objective" game mode. These matches can last up to 30 minutes but are arguably the best of all the game-modes. Combat in Chivalry is visceral and addictive. Even the frustration of death is lessened by the hilariously over-the-top depictions of violence.
While initially intimidating and slightly frustrating, Chivalry offers a rewarding experience for those that stick with it, and those who enjoy team-based games will get many hours of enjoyment from the Team Objective mode.
Chivalry: Deadliest Warrior: I really wanted to like CDW. It seems amazing, offering you the chance to play as a Samurai, Knight, Spartan, Viking, Ninja, or Pirate. The settings are pulled from each warriors respective civilizations and there is quite a bit of detail in the landscapes. Weapons and bonuses are easier to unlock than in CMW. Those positives aside, the real enjoyment out of Chivalry is the combat and the teamwork, both of which are lacking in CDW.
There is no Team Objective mode in CDW as of this writing. Game modes revolve around Last Team Standing, Free for All, or Team Death Match. The maps, while detailed, are enormous. This poses problems when trying to find enemies to fight, and Last Team Standing matches usually end up with two teams camping in their spawns while others fight and weaken their numbers. While a respectable strategy, games drag out longer than necessary, exacerbated by the scale of the battlefield. Gameplay is much faster paced, but seems to favor "twitch" gameplay over strategy. At first, I thought this was due to my trying to apply my CMW tactics to CDW, but after hours of playing I found that other players were having similar problems. Parrying and counter-striking rarely proves effective while hit detection is severely off. More than once I've swung at an enemy at close range only to not hit him, while other hits connected when I thought they would be misses. LMB spam tends to win out far more than in CMW. CDW seems to just try to copy the basic mechanics of CMW without any of the strategy or feeling of accomplishment of the original.
I wholeheartedly suggest players give CMW a shot and stick with it for a little bit to give it a good shot. I wouldn't recommend CDW if you are a huge fan of CMW, but would suggest it if you find CMW's combat/speed to be too slow for your tastes, though I might recommend waiting for further patches to be released.

You play as Isaac (before you unlock more characters), a young child who has fled to the basement after his mother tried to kill him. As you explore the basement you will encounter all kinds of enemies, from poop to floating skulls this game has everything.
+Lovely pixel art style
+Fantastic design, that includes levels, characters, enemies, items and more
+A vast number of items including 160 more than the original
+A vast number of enemies to face
+Ten characters to unlock and play as
+Loads of different bosses each with their own combat style and unique design
+Tons of secrets to discover
+New rooms sizes and layouts
+New and improved UI including a better minimap
+If you quit during a run the game saves your progress
+Local Co-Op
+Full controller support though I think the game is best enjoyed with KB controls
+Runs a whole lot better than the original due to a new engine and it's now in full HD
+Immensely replayable
+A vast number of achievements for you to unlock
+/-Most of the other characters are very difficult to unlock
-Great soundtrack but it just doesn't stand up to the original game's soundtrack
-There's no way to check what items you have and what effect they have (you can however see a list of the items without descriptions)

9

Now that the pricing has become more reasonable I am cautiously changing my thumbs down to a thumbs up.  I say cautiosly because I really love the solo and "with friends" gameplay.  The open servers are a mess to be avoided at all costs and the game still hase plenty of glitches and bugs.
The good:  A very challenging survival game.  You are going to die a lot at first. It seems like everything can eat you when you first spawn in.  Once you have acheived the basic level of survival there is plenty of exploring, crafting and base building  to keep you entertained for a few hundred hours. The graphics are beautiful with great lighting effects.  Eventually though, like all survival games, you reach a "what now" point.
The bad:  Life on the servers is extremely rough.  The key appears to remain well hidden until you have advanced your skills and base to a considerably high level  The difference in firepower between a new starter character and a month old veteran is huge.  The month old veterans will be entertaining themselves at your expense.  You will be raided hard and often.  Your grass/wood/stone walls will fall easily to rocket launchers and large dino armies.  Your base will be raided over and over again until the will to live leaves you.  If you are unfortunate enough to have chosen an open server, bored alpha tribes from other servers will port in with their massive dino armies and wipe the server clean.  If you are not first on the server you will be food and playthings for the earlier settlers.  And yes, a player corpse can be harvested not only for the loot they were carrying but for their meat.  Oh, and logging out means nothing as your character always remains in game- asleep and when you are logged off everyone that finds you will have a look at what you have and probably kill you for sport.
PVE servers: Griefing is still a thing and every day a new way to make you want to cry is invented.
I enjoyed my solo game time and time spent with RL friends on private servers.  The game is very challenging. and provided a lot of laughs, - Trying to survive on a public server ranks up to some of the most miserable gaming experiences I have ever experienced.  Because of this, I can't wholeheartedly recommend the game.  For solo play  sure.  But if you are looking to survive on one of the public servers expect to be ridden hard and often.  If you are into that sort of thing then this is definitely the game for you.

Chivalry is a first (or third) person slasher game which consists of 2 teams: Agatha Knights and Mason Order. There are 4 classes to choose from: Archer (long range, low hp), Man at Arms (ability to dodge, low hp), Vanguard (uses heavy weapons and can execute a sprint attack with high damage, medium hp) and Knight (uses high damaging weapons at the cost of speed, high hp).
The game has a variety of game modes including: Free-for-all, Team Deathmatch, Team objective (best mode), Last Team Standing and King of the Hill. These game modes are very fun and can keep you entertained for hours. Just to note that Team Objective and King of the Hill matches can last a long time (30+ minutes).
The combat is satisfying with a variety of attacks to choose: slash, stab and overhead. You are able to parry (block) but at the cost of stamina. You will also loose stamina if you miss an attack or kick (breaks an enemies block). These mechanics do work well but could do with some tweaking.
Overall I do really like this game and can easily spend a few hours playing. I very much reccomend this game, although it can be a bit buggy. Make sure your PC is capable of running it, as laptops will suffer even at lower settings (but can still be playable).

The goal of warframe is to grind.
If you want playstyle variety you need to grind for weapons/warframes (or you can buy them with premium currency).
Weapons and frames need to be constructed from resources and parts that drop from bosses (or you can buy them with premium currency).
You need to grind the bosses that drop the parts (or you can buy them from other players with premium currency).
Have the parts? Great!  Now you need to construct the weapons/warframes in real time, for 12-72 hours (or you can rush build queues with premium currency).
Oh wait, do you have the proper mastery level to use that item? If you don't you need to grind up levels on other, worse gear first (can't buy that with currency lol).
The easiest way to level your gear is to, you guessed it, GRIND on enemies for hours at a time! There are booster packs in the shop for a very small fee if you want to speed that up though.
Ahh good, now you finally have your new item. Now you need to upgrade it with modules to bring out its full potential! Wait, do you have enough Endo to level up those modules? And can your new toy even fit what you want without needing an Orokin Reactor?
--------
Warframe has a very critical problem: the entire game, from start to finish, is a grind. If you buy weapons, frames and consumables with real money you end up depriving yourself of content, but the alternative is slogging through the same maps trying to reach the edge of the power creep. I only play it out of a tired habit. Avoid this game.

Like the name says, you click it. And keep clicking. Yes, it's one of those time wasters.
Contrary to, for example, AdVenture Capitalist and in similarity to Cookie Clicker, your clicking will have impact for a good amount of the game (where in the first you literally only have to click a few times, manage your angels, and the game will do the rest for you, different games, really), but it felt a bit grindy for me. The heroes are okay, the abilities aswell and I also like the ancients idea, adds a bit more of control to how you play (though also a tad more randomness).
Unfortunately, that is also the cause of trouble.
Well to get more DPS you need hero souls, which you get 1 for every 2000 levels you have of your total heroes, after ascending(nothing wrong about that, fair enough), and every soul is worth +10% DPS.
To get even more DPS, you should get ancients. There are some that increase abilities' durations, the DPS while idle (no clicks for 60 secs), more gold found, less monsters per stage, less boss HP, etc, etc.
Though if you buy ancients (cost of the first = 1 soul, 2nd = 2, 3rd = 4, 4th = 8, etc and you can select 1 from random 4, but you can get a new selection with a cost of half the souls needed to get another ancients), you lose the +10%DPS for each soul. So, pretty much, your objective is to grind as much souls as you can, then buy ancients, keep grinding, buy more ancients, keep grinding, up to a point where leveling up ancients are too much of a waste on DPS.
There's also a forge system which I haven't explored yet though, so sorry for that.
To be fair, the game is good. It has lots of potential, it is very well made.
But somehow, it just doesn't do it for me. I liked the simplicity in Cookie Clicker, the humour and minimalistic interaction of AdVenture Capitalist, Tap Titans is a somewhat good which I've been hooked and lately, I've been playing Time Clickers, which is quite awesome.
Final opinion: You want to try the game? Go ahead. Do it. You might enjoy it and be glad you ever did ^^ I don't honestly like it, but we all have different tastes, so we can't all like the same games :P

Hello my names Carl and this is my review of clicker heroes. Clicker heroes is great free to play clicker! It has a beautiful and cartoony art style however it still keeps a profesional look (It generely also has a great frame-rate). The gameplay of the game is its main point, very addicting and although its just another clicker, it has something unique wich is hard to point out. The main point of the game is to collect an army of heroes and become powerful by upgrading them and giving them buffs and powers. Each hero comes with a type of attack- clicking and DPS. however to my dismay so far in my playthrough only one character is a clicker, and it also took me a short while to understand the mechanics of the game. So a fun little tutorial would have been useful. However despite lacking in a few ereas this game is one of the best indies around! A fantastic art style to addicting gameplay i rate this game 8 out of 10!

Overall the game fun. Like most sandbox games, it is really up to you on how you find the fun in it. I can suggest private small groups, or PvE servers. As the power curve is too dramatic if you do not know what is going on or if you do not have a tribe. Unless PvP is what you like, I can then suggest un official servers for a better first experience.
At $60 Idk if I would say it is worth it. I would say sit tight there will be a sale sooner or later.

I bought this game 1 day before the price hike. How lucky!
This game has good progression from early to late game and is fairly addictive (see my gametime). I really enjoyed the 100+ hours I've put into this game, but the number of shortcomings for this game are plenty.
1) Very poorly optimised; I'm not too picky about my FPS but it seems like the devs have ignored this for far too long..
2) Late-End game is mostly about luck; because of the long arduous process to get to late-end game, although fun and somewhat rewarding, suddenly there's a wall halting your progress because you just don't have better equipment or dinos to fight the bosses. These rare gears/blueprints can only be found from loot crates (which is uncommon/rare), and breeding dinos just takes too much dedication.
3) It took my tribe on a private server about 80 - 100 hours to achieve late-end game, and while it was fun for the first time, I doubt I'll ever go through this crazy process again. Without mods the game is not really replayable.
4) Given the scale of this game, there are many bugs that exist (which is fine if attended to) but they seem to be ignored or forgotten by the devs. What's the point of churning out more content but not fixing the core of the game?
I would have given it a thumbs-up if the price remained the same, but at $55, it's really not worth the money. Maybe you could buy it during a sale..? Or perhaps they could just lower the price? If not I can only foresee this game slowly sinking into the game graveyard.

This is ridiculous. Any clicker game is ridiculous. All you do is slay a monster, buy heroes to slay more for you; they are able to slay more powerful ones, thus you gather more gold and buy more powerful heroes to slay more powerful mosters for more gold and... until it is not possible for you to mathematically achieve the next level. Played this game when it came out. Took a break for a couple years and came back, still a great game.
If you found yourself loving the Mass Effect series, here's the cooperative version!
Pros / Cons
Pros
- Seems the developers are doing all they can to initiate new content. Over 3 years the game has completely changed.
- They adapt the game to fit a desirable yet challenging experience.
- There always seems to be a decent amount to do, things to shoot for, etc.
- If you have a friend that wants to play and you're already deep in the game, it won't necessarily take long for them to be able to accompany you and be effective. YET they still have nice rewarding aspects for progressing in the game.
- There is generally NO NEED to purchase in game currency. Everything can be achieved in the free-to-play fashion.
- In game currency is obtainable without using real cash. This is huge IMO.
Cons
- Can be repetitive.
- If you're more of a die hard PvP player, this MAY not be for you. Though they have PvP it's not as extensive as its PvE
- Though the story is good, I found it hard to emerse myself in it. Which is the usual tell tale of any MMO style game.
- If you're the First Person Shooter type and can't have it any other way. This won't be for you. I prefer the third-person.
- "Crafting" can take a decent amount of time. 3 literal days for frames to complete. This may discourage casual players.
All in all, this game is pretty epic for being free. I'd say support the developers and grab some in game currency. They've worked hard to get this game to the Top 5 Played Games on steam. (As of 12/27/16)  Not to mention updates and expansion are frequent and content seems to be never ending. Good game.

I know, I know. Another negative Warframe review from a salty player with lots of hours in the game. How original.
Look, you've probably heard plenty of crap about this game from other negative reviews, but this is just my two cents:
For the amount of time you put into this game to earn things, you could achieve so much more in other games.
For the amount of money you put into this game, you could gain so much more from other free-to-play titles.
But what is it recently that made me quit?
Well, a fair few months ago, when Vauban Prime came out, I took a ~8 month break from the game, because of how unbelievably grindy it got. DE (the developers) increased the resource cost of things astronomically - like how some resources can only be obtained during rare, limited-time missions (nitain extract) or rare resources that remove themselves from your inventory after just 24 hours (Argon Crystals).
But it's okay, because DE releases fresh new content sometimes, right? Well, every time DE implements something, it's terribly implemented. Atrociously so. But sometimes DE comes back and revisits this content, sticks "2.0" at the end of the name, and treat it like a whole new thing. They might fix some issues, but introduce a slew of new problems.
An example of this is the "focus" system. Basically, without spoilers, you get certain types of XP for certain types of skill trees by using weapons or gear with a certain attatchment on them. When this was introduced, gaining "focus" points was ridiculously slow. After a while, DE responded to community complaints by advertising that they'd introduce a consumable that would appear on the map after certain time intervals, and give all players a 6x multiplier on their focus gains. Awesome, right?
What they really did was nerf how much Focus you get by making it an absolutely tiny fraction of what people were initially complaining about - then the 6x multiplier would only make up for the nerf. This is in the same update, mind you. And DE didn't communicate this at all.
And now they've moved on again, forgetting about the focus system, just like every other previously implemented system in the game.
Update 18.13 introduced nerfs to warframes (exoskeletons that are essentially interchangable classes) that didn't deserve a nerf. Many warframes that previously filled niche purposes were suddenly completely useless or outdone by other warframes. Certain builds people had on their warframes were now irrelevant. It was a♥♥♥♥♥♥show. And DE left it like that.
But for the longest time, people had been asking DE to balance all weapons in the game. Because there are hundreds of them - and it's a mess. Some can instantly wipe out all high level enemies in the vicinity, others require constant firing for minutes on end just to take down the same enemy. It is the worst I've ever seen in any game.
But that's okay, because DE created a fix that came with update 19, otherwise known as The War Within. This fix would be known as...
Riven mods. Basically, these are meant to be how DE rebalances the weapons of Warframe. And it is just the worst thing I've ever seen be added to the game.
Basically, Riven mods are mods for your gear that make them better. And they can make them way better. The problem? This didn't just apply to the terrible weapons that needed rebalancing - this applied to all weapons. And this is meant to be the fix that rebalanced weapons. I cannot fathom the stupidity behind this decision. It's laziness and stupidity.
Want to rebalance all weapons in the game, just like the players asked for? Sweet! Players will now have to grind against a time-locked grind on sortie (daily) missions for a small chance at obtaining a Riven mod, which then requires player to complete another arbitrary task just to "unveil" the Riven mod and make it usable, and then the player is left in the hands of RNG on what weapon the Riven mod worked with.
That's right, Riven mods are locked to only working with ONE weapon. Just one. Out of hundreds. It could be something you don't even own. It could be for a useless weapon, and still not make it good enough to compete with the high-tier weapons, or just be further nerfs to what are already the best weapons in the game.
So what do these Riven mods do?
These mods can do anything from giving a flat-out boost to damage, coming with useless buffs (adding additional % slash damage on a weapon that only 1% of it's damage as slash) or even nerfs, such as decreased damage and increased recoil.
Didn't like the way your Riven mod came out? You can reroll the traits it has with a whole new resource that requires a constant, conscious effort to grind, all while the cost for re-rolling your Rivens increases with every re-roll.
However, DE did make two fixes: they capped the resource increase for re-rolling Rivens to 3500 kuva, and made it so lesser-used weapons gain stronger buffs from Riven mods. But only after community outcry. Because the devs are so lazy, oblivious and moronic that it took the players say "umm, buffing
with rare mods doesn't fix the weapon balance issues" for them to change anything. And when they did "fix" it, it barely made a difference.
The Glast Gambit came out a few days before I wrote this review. With it, a new weapon was introduced - the Hema, and a new warframe - Nidus.
Now, what's great about some warframes is that you can get their parts in quests. Sure, these quests were super grindy, but it was better than the alternative - many warframes in the game can only be obtained by having boss enemies drop CERTAIN PARTS of CERTAIN WARFRAMES which requires credits, resources and TWELVE HOURS EACH TO BUIILD and THEN you may construct the warframe with the final stage of crafting - actually constructing the warframe. Which takes SEVENTY-TWO HOURS.
In quests, as you complete each grindy objective, you're rewarded with a part, which you craft - for credits, resources, and and a twelve hour wait. But it's better than having the part drop from a boss - where there is only an obscure chance that you get the part you want. This was the case with the warframe known as Chroma.
DE decided Chroma was clearly too easy to get, after a while, and decided to split up the pieces and making rewards for clearing different systems, sets of levels, and side objectives. Yep.
Now, the Glast Gambit rewards you with one piece of the Nidus warframe - the blueprint. Not other part. The other parts can only be obtained from a LOW DROP RATE from only EVERY FOURTH ROUND from a
That's right. You have a low chance every foruth round after much repitition on just one level - the only level to contain this new game mode - and play it over and over and over and over again until you get the warframe parts. Which then require twelve hours, some credits and some resources to complete. And then you may build the warframe - requiring a 72 hour wait.
Well, that's♥♥♥♥♥♥ So what about the new weapon, the Hema?
It requires mutagen samples. A lot. Mutagen samples are a very uncommon resource that can only be found in certain areas of the game, and
Now, you see, weapon research gets a bit cheaper when your clan has less players. So those clans dedicated to helping out new players? ♥♥♥♥ them. DE just♥♥♥♥♥♥on them. And you can only be in one clan at a time. So people are being mass-kicked from clans, and it's anarchy. And DE doesn't care. They want people spending real money to buy gear from them, and will encourage players to stab each other in the back to make a buck. What scum.

TL:DR. The game MAY one day be worth buying, but WC Studios is just breaking the game more and more with every day as the "official" launch closes in. I would NOT recommend it in its current state. Maybe talk someone else into wasting $60 and gift it to you? ;)
I bought this game back when it first came out, for quite cheap, and I understood it was early access and would have bugs; this didn't bother me as I've beta tested before and this game appeared promising. Key word - APPEARED.
While I do have 390 hours on record as of this review, I've found the vanilla game severely lacking without mods, and on top of it, the game is not properly balanced whatsoever (hence the mods, some of them rebalance it). If you want to play this on single player or maybe with just a couple friends, you will have to make major adjustments to nearly every single variable in the serer settings to make the resistance/damage/experience/harvesting/etc more playable. This game is NOT intended for single-player nor just a few people in its current state. [You'd think they would come up with an adaptive system like other games that knows how many people are playing and adjusts accordingly automatically]
The game is awesome in a lot of ways, such as the crafting of your items and weapons, being smart about your hunting so you don't aggro the wrong dinos, needing shelter and food to survive, etc. But there are a lot of dynamics that are broken and every time WC Studios releases a new update as they get ready for the official launch on Aug 8, they break twice as much as they fix. (They honestly think they're going to get $60 for a half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥broken game?! They were lucky to get $30 while it was EA)
I've personally mentioned issues to WC Studios and I've seen many others bring up glitches or broken aspects, ways to improve on things. But they completely ignore their customer base. They do things how THEY want, when THEY want. This is why the vast majority of ARK gamers mod their servers - the vanilla game is very boring and linear because WC Studios won't give us gamers what we want and expect to see.
Maybe one day the game will be totally fixed and worth buying but as of right now, there are so many bugs and broken things in the game, it's definitely not worth $60, it's not worth $30 anymore even.
Oh and before I forget, those that do mod their dedicated servers, we have to use third-party software because the built in mod updating system WC Studios created doesn't function whatsoever. It's intended to erase existing mods, download all mods [again even if theres no updates] and then install the mods. What it actually does is erase all mods and proceed to crash, and if you should start your server without mods when it was modded....congrats, you just corrupted your world and will need to restore from a backup. Luckily, ARK does keep about 10-15 backup copies of previous saves for every single world (if you do unique save locations for each world/server).

This game could be described pretty easily: Robot ninjas in space. But to be fair, there is much more to it.
In Warframe you play the titular characters, also known as Frames. There are a lot of different frames, all with their own abilities, and minor stat differences. With a ton of different primary weapons, like bows or shotguns, secondary weapons like kunai or simple pistols, and melee weapons, like swords, even more swords, and scythes, you can as such individualize your playstyle to suit you the most. Do you want to rush in and just wreak havoc? Or do you prefer a slow and stealthy kind of approach? Both are very much possible.
The graphics are good, although I sometimes either find them to blinding (some of the light effects are very bright) or too dark, but those are just my personal tastes. The controls are easy to learn, and the game isn't too hard for beginners, with a natural progression curve.
Different missiontypes, and even PvP help keeping the game with it's variance, but that doesn't mean the game doesn't have problems...
As with many free to play games, there is a very obvious catch. You either have to pay for stuff you want, OR you have to grind for it. And grinding for the good stuff can take quite a while. Now, it is definitely not necessary, and enjoying the game without so called Prime weapons or frames is very much possible...but sometimes even getting normal Frames can be a hassle. Grinding for stuff can be really annoying, as many of the good things have a low drop chance, making it necessary to do multiple runs of the same mission. Sometimes over and over again, and even after hours, you are no closer to what you want. And even IF you have the bleuprints for the parts together, you still need to build them, which normally takes 84 hours at least for a frame (12 hours for a part, of which you normally have three, and then 72 hours for the frame itself). And after that is done, you can claim your Frame. That is...if you have a free slot in your inventory.
You only have a limited amount of slots for weapons (all together, Melee, Primary, Secondary), and a limited amount for frames. To get more, you have to pay Platinum, the currency you get for real money. So if you are a collector like me, you might find yourself with a problem.
However, there is a silver lining. You can trade Some items with other players, especially prime parts and blueprints, and they can give you platinum in return. So if you don't mind the grind, you will never have to pay real money for anything.
In the end, I would recommend the game for anyone who likes hack and slash games combined with third person shooters. Sure, it's grindy and getting things you want can take a long time with seeing the same stuff over and over again, but it is a good game to just pick up, and play for an hour.

So, allow me to preface this with the following: I recently reviewed Warframe after it's release of the Glast Gambit update. Since then, I have gone back and taken a third look at the game as a whole. So let me be frank, I still cannot suggest this game to anyone looking in from the outside, having never touched it previously. I do not believe it is worth the time that I have sunk into it, for various reasons I will touch upon in this review. But first, allow me to justify this quickly. Digital Extremes, Warframe's developer, is fraught with controversy and shady bussiness practices that go beyond status-quo. I will not go into them for the sake of keeping this under the size of a college essay, but I will say this much. They repeatedly disregard the betterment of the community and game, be it the lack of acknowledgment of problems the game has had for extended periods of time, or hostility towards several members of the community over the lifespan of this game. This kind of behavior is not something I can excuse, and is one of the many reasons I cannot suggest this game. Now, into the more detailed explanation of my reasoning.
-- First and foremost I will touch upon the gameplay itself.
-Pros - Snappy, responsive, and highly addicting gameplay makes even menial or mechanically simple challenges enjoyable to some extent.
-- Varied game types allow for more dynamic gameplay, dependant on your personal preference.
-- Frequent and impactful live events give the game a shifting and ever-changing roster of activities to choose from.
-- Several different roles or classes exist within the game, in addition to hundreds of mostly unique weapons and stances for said weapons. You will never be the exact same as the person next to you, unless you actively try and model your own builds off of somone else's.
-- Stellar community.
-- High levels of progression.
-Cons - Repetitive, tedious tasks are, oddly enough, often given priority over the more interesting or dynamic gametypes. For example, the simple horde modes, Defense and Survival, are currenly some of the easier ways to farm the highest tier of gear available in the game.
-- Dear lord the grind. Nothing in this game can be acheived in a short amount of time. Though, if you are used to MMO's this wont be as daunting. If you are looking for a game that grants you immediate reward for completing objectives, turn around now and don't look back.
-- Poorly laid out loot systems. The methods for getting Primed gear in this current period of time within the game is a little convoluted at best, and heavily reliant and extreme amounts of RNG at worst. Getting Primed gear takes long stretches of time, not for sake of getting the necessary materials to build it, or even waiting for a mission or objective to become active, but simply because of the slim chances of receiving the proper piece to what you need.
-- Pay to progress. The game allows players to buy their way through a severe portion of the games 'early' stages, or even purchase the most powerful gear in the game during limited time access packs. If this is a pay-model you do not wish to participate in, turn around now.
The game, however, has many details that are both good and bad, so I'll touch on these here.
-- Warframe is constantly evolving, changing. Thus, what is effective today may not work at all tomorrow. The game always shifts and morphs, meaning you have to pay attention to what works and what doesn't every time you engage into a mission, whether or not the build you are using is old or new.
-- The story is vague, largely hidden in Codex, or lore, text dumps. The more recent main story quests have been intruiging and done well, but they expect you to have already grasped at the bases of what this world was built on. This left several of those I play with lost, as they neither cared to read through thousands of item descriptions to see the story, nor did they have the time. Coming from someone who's play the Souls series frequently, this game's story seems like a slightly less polished execution of that same storytelling format. There is a large disconect between the gameplay and story, and that has caused some awkward moments in some of the quests that feel stilted or awkward. Otherwise, however, the delivery is often well done and quite unique in comparison to other MMOs.
-- Warframe takes a lot of time to play. Though it can be picked up and set down thirty minutes at a time, the game requires you to dump around 50-100 hours in before things truly pick up and become interesting. That time commitment may not seem like an issue to some, but for those of us with jobs, school, or families, possibly even all three, I figured I'd let you all know. This game will eat your time away.
-- This is community driven game. No beating around the bush, if you don't plan on playing with people, do not play Warframe. It is not worth it.
I'd like to say a few words before setting this review to rest. As mentioned earlier, I have reviewed this game three times. Once, at around 400 hours combined between my xbox and PC accounts, I gave it a glowing review. Then, recently, around 1000 combined hours, I gave my negetive review, largely in part due to the massive annoyance of the Glast Gambit's changes. Now, I will say this once more. Warframe, though a good game, has major flaws. These faults include and extend past what I touched on, but even with all this game's cracks and broken pieces, it is still a good game. It could easily be much better, should DE choose to acknowledge some of the game's longstanding issues. If you are someone who has not picked up this game yet, turn around and do not look back. Do not try this game. It is not worth the time you inevitably sink into it. If you are looking to return to the game, and are hoping my review may have some insight to the game's current standing, I will say this much. Things are improving, but not quickly enough. Thank you for reading, I hope my review assisted your decision making.

Overall score: 8.75/10 Would reccomend to anyone who enjoys action games, and saving money.

I like how it looks, it's beautiful looking, yet it doesn't need the newest possbile computer. And anyhow, in the midst of battle, you're not going to be looking at the textures anyway.

The combat is well done aswell, you have different attacks (swing, overhead and stab) which are useful for different situations. You can only block for a second or so, but you don't need to choose the direction of your block, like you do in Mount & Blade and War of the Roses.
There's also 4 classes, each with their own specialty. Archer for ranged fighting, Man-at-arms is quick and can dodge, the Vanguard can do a sprint attack and the Knight is slow but powerful, and can also wield two handed swords with a shield. Personally, I love the Man-at-Arms.
Last but not least, the setting is great. As a Mount & Blade fan, medieval games always catch my eye. This one looked like it had caught the Medieval feeling (dismemberment and blood!) very well.
If you're planning to buy this, go ahead. It's great fun!
And remember to choose your side wisely...

This game is a mixed bag. It does offer a far more precise and fluid control scheme than say, Mount and Blade or War of the Roses, and as such was more skill-based than its competitors. However, while CMW started out as a competitive PvP game, it has since been heavily dumbed down to make it more accessible to a wider audience. In addition to this the game has suffered from crippling bugs and glitches that TBS does not seem capable of fixing. Each time they resolve one issue, they introduce two new ones. Some of these problems can also be exploited to gain unfair advantages, such as attacks that hit instantly and broken animations that hide one's attacks from one's opponents, allowing the player to get around their target's defenses in a cheap way.
Thus, while the game is still fun to play in a casual manner, the competitive aspect has been ruined. If you want to compete with the best, you have to cheat, as almost all highly ranked players happily abuse any exploit available to them with no regards to fair play or sportsmanship. As a result, the community is one of the most toxic you will find.

This review is about my experience with Ark: Survival Evolved, and why I reccomend it to anyone who enjoys survival genre games. I see tons of flak over the recent price changes, or the fact that some bugs are still a problem. However these things happen with nearly every game being developed, and are not the sole problem of Ark alone. The fact is there are weekly bug fixes and optimizations being done, as well as regular updates. There will always be bugs, most will be fixed and some will not, some things considered to be bugs by the community are not bugs at all. Does that make it okay? no but thats just how it is with all games.
I have played Ark since it first launched in early access. (not all the time but over 1000 hours so far and still having fun.) I have experienced the good and the bad, the poor decisions and the overwhelmingly fun times I've had in game. So here are some pro's and con's of my experience with Ark.
Pro's:  - Vast open worlds to explore -
- Plethora of creatures to tame, kill, or breed-
- Fantastic modding comunity-
- Seperate official PVE and PVP servers for those who do not want to worry about being raided-
- User created custom servers for those who dislike, or do not have time to grind.-
- Ability to make long standing friendships, or endless bitter rivalries.-
- The ability to build your own foward operating base, or just a simple cottage in the woods.-
- Feeling of progression without linear quest experiences-
- Downright beautiful landscapes and visuals-
Con's: - Graphically demanding- If you do not meet minumum specs, I suggest playing on console-
- Load times & D/C's- although they have improved dramatically, load times can still be quite long to the point of
battle eye disconnecting user from the host.-
- BUGs - An ongoing problem as with any game. While many have been resolved, still quite a few remain that have
been aparent since launch. Nothing that has outright stopped myself from being able to play.-
- Quirky and sometimes frustrating AI.-
- Frustrating standard building mechanics- Since they have adopted S+ as a soon to be official mod, hopefully a
thing of the past.-
- Extremely time oriented and grindy on stock servers.- I almost exclusivly play on custom unnoficial servers for
this reason, I just do not have time to tame a beast for 5 or more hours, let alone days.-
- Poor development choices- This is mostly in regards to their launching of paid DLC to a title that is still
developing(allbeit worth the money, still a poor choice.) as well as their call to raise the price so far away from
launch. I understand from a business standpoint why the price raise was necessary, and they had been talking
about it for some time, the timing however was terrible.
- A 2 sided somewhat toxic community- It sems as though there are very few people like myself, who take both
sides of an argument into consideration. For the most part, you will see people who love this game, or hate it
completely. Myself, I have had over a thousand hours played in Ark, well worth even a $60.00 price tag, and I am
still having a blast. I do realize there are problems and not all of them will be adressed.
However In my honest opinion If you enjoy this genre, you will have fun in Ark: Survival Evolved. Yes there will be
frustrating times, yes you may D/C or crash, you may even have everything you have built wiped out in an instant
due to an update ( only happened to me once because of a mod i was using)...But in the end, for myself anyway,
there are far more good times than bad. That is why I can honestly and whole heartedly recommend this game!

Great concept, rubbish implementation.
The core ideas of Warframe are ace, get a load of powers and guns, smash weird enemies in varied environments, all the while getting stronger. Add onto this a solid movement system as well as an initially rewarding progression system and Warframe should have the strength of core gameplay to barrel right through minor flaws of balancing or uneven progression mechanics.
Unfortunately, Warframe doesn't have minor issues with progression, it's infested with them. While most of the epynomous Warframes are all if not balanced then at least varied, the vast majority of the game's massive arrray of weapons exist only to level so that you can progress the weird and clunky Mastery mechanic whereby you get to take a series of uninteresting tests to unlock some, but only a few of the more advanced weapons. The mechanic does provide some advantages to levelling new weapons, but only once you're long past the point of painfully grinding a progression of dull nondescript weapons instead of getting to play with whatever your favourite is.
Compounding the issue, newer stuff is almost always better, and rather than spending any effort on balance, the devs created a system of random powerups, the variance of which is so massive that it will make weapons either embarassingly overpowered or actually provide bonuses to stats that the weapon does not posess. It's a mess of a system, and only the most extreme signal that Digital Extremes haven't got the faintest idea what to do with their game.
Recommendation? Play it for a bit, it's free, and the core gameplay isn't bad, but be very aware that you're far better off waiting a long time before spending anything on the game's ridiculously overpriced RMT offerings. further, this is no Blizzard or Riot game, don't expect well thought out development in tndem with the ridiculously priced monthly RMT content packs.

Chivalry, a short but powerful name for a game. But what exactly is it and what can you expect from it? I'll tell you all about it while I split up every element in its own section so its easier to read.
Chivalry is a Multiplayer First Person Melee game. When I say Melee then I actually mean that you'll get to fight with swords, axes, polearms, clubs and much much more. This game is pretty fast paced once it comes to close combat. There is also the ability to use distance weapons such as bows, spears, crossbows and throwing weapons. The main objective of every game is kill, kill, kill some more, and kill everyone else. Objective game modes are also availible but ofcourse you'd need to kill a lot there too. You have a HP bar and a Stamina bar, HP ofcourse lowers if someone hits you. There are some rare occasions that you'll get one-hit but that takes lots of skill and luck. The stamina bar lowers with every swing or block that you do, once your stamina hits 0 then you'll be stunned for about 2 seconds and open to every attack. Stamina regenerates if you dont move at all, so does HP very slowly but that isnt really worth it. Other than that its just hit and block. There are 4 classes you can play with. Man-at-Arms who is a light fighter with low defense but generally faster and lighter hits and has the ability to dodge an attack if timed right. An Archer who mainly uses distance weapons who also deals double damage if he hits someone in the back. The Knight has the most armor and strength but is also the slowest in game thus fairly easy to hit. Vanguards have the most reach ingame with a decent amount of defense. They can build up a charging attack while running. The game is pretty easy to understand, but also quite frustrating, I'll get to that later.
There is a very small story, maybe 5 lines in total that you'll only get to see if you play the Tutorial, and it doesnt even covers everything. There is no Singleplayer mode whatsoever, only Multiplayer.
The graphics of this game are based on the Unreal Engine 3. It also supports nVIDIA's PhysX feature and seems quite realistic. Pretty much every system of today will be able to run this game in atleast 50-60 fps. I've seen minor graphical glitches where the ragdoll body was all acting up, and shortly after the beta release there was also a cloud bug in the game but that got fixed very quickly. Other than that the graphics are still decent on this game, but nothing to bloat about.
The sounds are crystal clear and the voice messages are randomized in 5-8 messages for every option you choose or repeat. The music on the other hand is pretty repetative, I could only distinguish 3 different tracks that just loop over and over again. As far as I know there is no sound customization at all but seeing that they added the Steam Workshop a while back, it might change soon.
There is an ingame chat function where people can communicate. Usually not much will be said there except for some few insults and some rare compliments on occasions. Most of the time when you ask people something they might react positively depending on what server you'll be in. Next to that there is also a kick function, which is actually abused a lot by losing players who cant stand to be killed over and over. Like I said earier this game is pretty frustrating because you can die pretty quickly if you dont watch out, and usually end up raging or insulting people if you keep losing over and over.
Since this is a multiplayer only game, you'll get the same gameplay over and over but just with different situations and/or maps. Generally it can be very fun to replay this game everytime you connect to a server and i've seen entire clans doing clan wars with eachother which can be great fun too. Replaying a lot of maps can be more positive than negative because you'll know the best spots and where to expect enemies.
This game is loads of fun, but also quite frustrating. Especially if you have a short fuse. I find myself getting pretty angry at most times because of the players im up against but I always tend to come back and play this again after a few days. It's really been worth my money so far and there is an interesting DLC for this as well. I love replaying this game from time to time

Gone are the days where you could sit in a Defense and go 40+ waves for Prime parts. Gone are the days where the Void even matters. Now it's a normal map you can visit to farm for Argon Crystal you'll rarely need. A whole group of tiles, completely useless now.

THE Medi-Mom frame that heals everything and keeps your squad in enough Energy to spam your stupid kill-frame ability as much as possible. "Rework" being code for "nerf".

Half the trade chat will try and scam you for premium currency, the other half will try and scam you for the item at a lower cost than it is "worth. TL;DR I used to love this game, but the staff and community have turned it into a heaping♥♥♥♥♥♥pile that I'll probably never play again.

V: Visually this game looks great, but at times it seems like it could be optimized a little better. Being able to customize your knight is a lot of fun in its own right.
A: AAAAAGAAAATHAAAA! Seriously you're going to hear tons of yelling and dying but it's all in great fun. The weapons sound amazing and the wounds sound real. Well done on that part. With a pair of headphones it's even better.
G: Gameplay? I'd put the depth of the combat somewhere just shy of Mount and Blade. The learning curve is great, easy to get into but difficult to master, though someone who's really good will run circles around newbs. It's pretty bug free in this stage, and you rarely feel cheated when killed, unless you're a sore loser.
